“Sirius come back!” Marlene wailed as she made to follow him, but the moment she reached the door it slammed in her face and she threw her arms up, letting her torch sail across the room in terror as she fled back to Remus’ side.

“Wait! Do you hear that?” He gasped.

“No,” Lily moaned, still scrambling away from the deer.

But there was no mistaking it; another scream, this one coming from directly above.

“Sirius! Remus! Help! Lily, help me!”

“It’s James!” Remus said. “He needs help!”

“We need help! What the fuck did that?” Marlene cried, pointing her torch at the deer. It was positively the most swearing Remus had ever heard her do.

“James, I’m coming!” Lily shouted. Just as impulsive as Sirius in her own panic, she threw herself up the stairs after his voice and Remus followed, eager to reach the climax of their prank.

“Don’t leave me!” Marlene shrieked, dragging herself up after them.

“Lily, you’re going to break an ankle!” Remus warned, following the light of her torch as she took the stairs two at a time. Rounding the second floor's landing, she slipped on something and fell back into him with a yelp.

“Lily!” He gasped, as she stared down in horror at the blood oozing down every stair. It’d been Peter’s idea to drop a huge bucket down them from the third floor, but now as they slipped and slid across the slick wood, Remus was starting to regret everything.

“Someone help me!” James wailed again. “Oh god!”

“James!” Lily shouted again. “We’re here!”

“Please help me! Aughhh!”

“Potter, please! Just shut up!” Marlene screamed.

Pushing free of Remus, Lily climbed the stairs even faster, slipping in the waterfall of fake gore a handful of times before finally emerging on the top floor. Another grisly moan echoed down the hall as Lily whipped her head around, lashing the air with her red plaits.

“Over there,” Remus pointed, half-panting; “It came from over there.”

All three of them crept down the hallway toward the last door, reaching it with their hearts in their throats. Both girls scanned doorway leading inside with their torches until finally they converged on a single spot across the room’s black abyss, where they found James lying in the dust, his wrestler’s costume all torn up in the front and covered from toe to throat in blood.

It actually looks pretty damn convincing, Remus thought, as Lily burst into tears.

“What the fuck?” Marlene bleated.

Lily skidded across the room and sank down to her knees next to James, her trembling hands hovering over him as she cried. Her tears were so real that Remus instantly felt guilty.

“James? James Potter, talk to me!” Lily begged, reaching out to cup him around the neck and lightly pat his face. Her fingers came away red and Marlene clamped a hand over her mouth like she really was going to hurl.

“Potter, wake up!” Lily ordered again, gingerly tracing her shaking hands over his chest. “Oh god.”

“Lily…?” James’ groan was more than convincing, but the little gurgled gasp he gave after whilst also spitting up blood would’ve made anyone freak out.

“I’m here, we’re here!”

“Oh my god,” Marlene whimpered. She turned and threw herself into Remus’ shoulder once more, nearly taking both of them to the ground. Lily was still half-lying over James, clearly in distress with her dress and stockings slathered in blood and grime. She’d sucked back her tears to stay calm for him, but it was obvious she was about four seconds away from a mental breakdown.

“Lily…” James breathed again, wheezing like he was dying. (He wasn’t.) “Lily I…”

“It’s okay!” She whimpered, hands stroking James’ face gently. “We’re gonna get help. We’re gonna get a teacher—Sirius has gone to get a teacher! You’re going to be okay, just—just keep talking!”

“Lily… I…”

“Yes, James?”

“I…”

With a great exhale, James slumped back on the floor, head lolling upward with closed eyes as blood continued to leak from the corners of his mouth. Lily gave a strangled gasp and threw herself over his body, clutching the front of James’ shirt so fiercely she’d ripped another hole in it for each of her fingers.

“James, wake up!” She shouted. “Wake up!”

Marlene smacked her palms into her eyes, staggering backward and hissing, ‘fuck—fuck—fuck—fuck’ over and over again.

Remus just stood there. How long did one actually pretend to be dead for? They’d never discussed it, and he certainly hadn’t expected such a visceral reaction. If anything, he’d assumed Lily would’ve caught on by now, but seeing James so torn-up had clearly shaken her.

James must’ve agreed, because before Remus could even contend with kicking him in the shoulder and calling the whole thing off, he opened one eye and shot upright.

“HAH!”

Lily flew backward instantly, shrieking and scrambling across the filthy floorboards. Marlene was screaming before she’d even taken her hands away from her eyes and she dove back into Remus, knocking them both over in one big heap.

“Gotcha Evans!” James shouted gleefully. “S’all fake! I’m actually fine!”

There was a moment of stunned silence, before Lily—arms, face, and hands now covered in the syrupy blood—snapped out of her shock.

“James Potter!” She roared. “You absolute DICKHEAD!” With a great hiss she threw herself forward and began to beat James in the centre of the chest with her fists.

“Ow!” He laughed. “You’d hit an injured man?”

“I’ll show you injured!” Lily screeched. “You let me think you were dead! Are you fucking mental?”

“Ooof! Evans!”

“I’ll kill you myself, YOU TWAT!”

Having recovered from her shock, Marlene sat up and whirled on Remus, who had finally let the facade fall and was grinning with an open mouth at the sight of Lily’s anger. “You guys are the worst!” She growled, hitting him fiercely with both hands.

“Ow—c’mon! It was kind of funny,” he said, making her hit him again.

“It was not!” Lily whimpered, losing her anger and beginning to cry again. Instantly sobered of his laughter, James frowned and gathered her into a tight hug right there in the middle of the room.

“I’m sorry. Don’t cry, Daisy, please don’t cry.”

“I hate you!” Lily sobbed, but she hugged back fiercely, and Marlene and Remus were left to watch on in the dark. Eventually Marlene raised an eyebrow in question and glanced up at Remus, who shrugged, completely bewildered. A moment later the pair finally broke apart and Lily gave James another sharp shove.

“Piss off.” Sniffling, she stood up and snatched her torch off the floor before storming out of the room while James called after them.

“Oh c’mon, Daisy, it was just a bit of spooky fun!”

“You don’t get to call me that!” Lily shouted back, her torchlight disappearing down the hall. Remus made to sit up only to be shoved by Marlene as well, who set off after her with a sharp grunt. James stared after them, sighing wistfully like a man in love.

“Ah, man, she’s going to be pissed off for weeks.”

“Don’t stop there, how about a whole year?” Remus sniggered.

“No, she wouldn’t.” James’ face fell a bit. “Would she?”

“Dunno. If you hadn’t broken character she’d still be busy mourning you rather than hating your guts.”

“Nah, she’d hate me just for dying in the first place.”

“You’re probably right, but perhaps next time you should magically revive yourself rather than scare the pants off her?”

“It’s called comedic timing, Lupin, look it up. You got my shoe?”

“Sirius has it, I think.”

“Buggar.” James looked down and wiggled his foot. His sock was stained with mud and damp. Shaking his head, he stood up and held out a hand for Remus and together they followed the girls out, eager to be out of the dingy shack.

“Oh c’mon girls, wait for us!” James called down the stairs.

“Fat fucking chance!” Marlene hollered back.

Being careful of the blood, they managed to catch up with the girls on the ground floor. James loped in front of Lily just ahead of the front door, making her slam to a stop. He dodged the torch she swung at him but not the second slap to the shoulder.

“Piss off before I give you detention until you’re balding!” She spat.

“Potter men don’t bald," James snickered.

“Ugh! I knew I should’ve trusted my gut!” Lily rounded on Remus, blinding him with her torch as he fell into step next to them. “Where’s Black? He waiting to play dead too?”

“I don’t know where he went!”

“You’re all dickheads!” She declared, using her arm to wipe some of the blood from her cheeks. Unfortunately the sugary muck only smeared more. James reached over and flicked a finger over the blood, tasting it with a cheeky grin.

“Oh get out of my way!” Lily hissed, shoving him away from the door.

“And don’t you dare follow us!” Marlene ordered.

“Where else would we go?”

“Try Hell, Potter!”

“You have the torches, though,” Remus said, and she flipped him off just as Lily reached the door and threw it open—only to come face to face with a terrified Mary and Lottie.

“WAAAAAH—!” Mary clamped her hand over her mouth to stifle her scream as Lily and Marlene fell back from the door, clutching the front of their shirts in shock.

“Enough!” Marlene wailed. “I’m so tired!”

Mary and Lottie fled into the Shack, slamming the door after themselves and bending over and heaving for air as Lily kept her light concentrated on them. “Why’d you sneak up on us?” She demanded.

“We didn’t!” Mary wheezed. “We came to look for you, and then Black, he—he—!” Mary waved a hand vigorously as though it would finish her sentence for her. In her other hand she was brandishing Marlene’s witches’ broom like a sword. Next to her, Lottie was clutching the gin bottle tightly to her chest, blonde ringlets hanging limply around her head.

“Try announcing your presence a little earlier next time then,” Marlene moaned.

“What happened to Black, Mary?” James asked smugly.

“He was dragged off! He came to find us and them something just fucking took him!”

“Ugh!” Lily growled. “He was just playing! The bloody liar—it’s all a big gag!”

“What?! How do you know? You weren’t even there!”

“Ask this tosser,” Lily snapped, reaching back to tug James forward by his torn-up shirt. Mary and Lottie took them in with gaping mouths, eyeing the blood that coated both James and the front of Lily’s previously spotless dress.

“Great!” Mary scoffed, dropping the broom and clapping her arms to her sides; “So it was just some big bloody joke to fucking scare us!”

“I wasn’t scared,” Lottie said, sipping her gin.

“Oh bullshit.”

Pushing past James, Marlene went straight to Lottie and snagged the bottle, taking a deep gulp. Lottie let her and turned back to the rest of them pointedly.

“Where’s the other two idiots then?”

“They were supposed to be back at the fire with you,” Remus said, and Lily instantly had him by the ear, tugging him down to her height with a nasty glare.

“Enough!”

“Bloody—ow, Evans!”

“Where are they?”

“Let the poor man go, Daisy,” James said, “they really were supposed to meet us.”

“Well they weren’t at the fire pit,” Mary said. “Sirius led us back here saying all of your were hurt!”

Grudgingly, Lily released Remus’ ear and let him step back to rub it with a small pout. “Well Peter was supposed to be with you,” she said to Mary, “so where is he?”

“I don’t know,” Mary shot back. “He said he needed to wee.”

“That was AGES ago!”

“And he never came back!”

“Theen why were you screaming?” Marlene asked.

“We weren’t the ones screaming, were we Lot?”

“Nope.”

“Then it was Peter!” Lily said, exasperated. “If you hadn’t let him walk off—”

“ME? You were there too! And he said he needed to piss! Figured he had that covered on his own! You guys were the ones actually screaming—we heard you in the woods!”

“Only because of the trees!”

“The TREES?”

“And the deer!”

“What DEER?”

“That deer!” Lily thrust her finger out at the spot the stag’s head had once been, but it had vanished. As she faltered over its absence, Mary fumed.

“You screamed your head off over some dead animal?”

Lily whirled back around. “Well did you see the dead animal? Because it was covered in blood!”

“So are you!”

“I’M AWARE!”

“Okay, okay,” Marlene sighed, stepping between them and pushing the gin into Mary’s hands and picking up her broom. “Let’s just get back to the fire and get our stuff. I think we’re all tired of being in the bloody woods.”

“Good idea,” James said, and Marlene whirled around to smack him in the shins with her broom.

“You two, we’re roasting over a spit before we leave,” she threatened.

“Fine, leave Black to the bugs. I’m done,” Mary said, hiking up her frilly skirts and throwing open the front door without a hint of fear.

With a dopey grin on his face, James nodded amicably and the six of them filed one by one out of the Shack. At the end of the cobbled path they found Peter lying there, covered in blood and playing dead just as James had.

Lottie marched right up to him, either fist clenched at her sides. “If you don’t stand up right now I’ll finally have a birthday to myself,” she snarled, before drawing back her leg and slamming it into Peter’s side.

Both James and Remus winced as Peter rolled over with a groan. “What the fuck?” He demanded, before sitting up to find all of the girls glaring at him. “James?” He hissed. “You broke character?”

“Sorry Pete,” James shrugged. “Couldn’t be helped.”

Sorely, Peter climbed to his feet and Lottie shoved him forward through the trees back the way they’d come. There was very little talking on the return trip, as most of the girls were still seething with rage, and when they’d finally made it back to their little camp they found an empty ring of logs and no Sirius.

“Fuck him,” Mary lashed. “Nice knowing you, Black.”

The fire had died down without any tending, leaving only a small huddle of burning ash with their things scattered around the clearing. Lily and Marlene used their torches to scan the ground for any rubbish before noticing a single discarded antler abandoned in the middle of the camp. Lily bent down and scooped it up, turning to Mary and holding it out to her.

“A-HA! Look, Mary, I told you. I swear to god, those—”

“What are you swearing at me for?” Mary snapped.

“I’m not actually swearing at you!”

“So you’re just being dramatic again?”

“Dramatic?”

“Yeah—dramatic! Like with this supposedly dead deer and the blood and the—!”

“Oh, that’s real rich coming from you, Mary.”

“What’s that supposed to mean?”

“Guys—” Marlene tried, but Lily wasn’t done.

“You were the one too afraid to even check on your friend,” she shot and Mary drew back, offended.

“We came after you didn’t we? In the dark no less!”

“But not Potter, and he was lying dead in some creepy house in the woods!”

“How’s that my fucking fault?”

“Well what if it was real? He could be seriously injured one day and you wouldn’t even know it!”

“Then how ‘bout next time you put a damn leash on him!”

“You’re impossible!”

“And you think you’re everyone’s bloody mother! Just admit you were scared!”

“I wasn’t!”

“You were screaming!”

“You try finding your boyfriend dead on the floor!”

A single collective gasp went up between the entire group. Instantly Lily’s hands flew to her mouth. She whirled on James, who appeared slack-jawed and petrified, but before any of them could say anything, a body rushed at them from behind—half human and half deer.

“WHAT THE FUCK, JAMES?” It roared.

With screams that could’ve curdled milk, Lottie and Marlene flew backward over a log as Peter threw himself back into the trees for cover and Lily dove into James, knocking him to the ground. Frozen in place with her own shrill yelp, Mary instinctively pushed Remus ahead of her and he sprawled, taking their attacker down with him.

“FUCK!” The monster wailed. “My spleen!”

It was Marlene who recovered first, flashing her torch across Remus’ back and revealing Sirius—still dressed in his black skeleton costume, only with the horrid make-shift deer mask dropped over his head.

“BLACK!” Lily screeched, sitting up on James’ chest and pushing her blood and dirt-matted hair out of her face.

“What the hell?” Sirius moaned again, blinded inside the mask. “Whoever you are—get off me!”

“I think you re-broke some of my ribs,” Remus grunted.

“LUPIN?!”

“Oooh, you shut up!” Mary snarled, kneeling down beside Sirius and yanking the stag’s head away only to slap him hard on the forehead.

“AUGH! It was just a joke, Macdonald!”

“What the hell—WHY?” Marlene wailed.

Remus made to sit up but Mary only shoved him down again stubbornly, making both him and Sirius moan with the weight.

“Oh my god,” Sirius wheezed, then; “Potter, I’m gonna kill you…”

“Me?” James demanded, sitting up in the dirt.

“Yes! You! God—Lupin, get off me!” Sirius lifted his head and pointed at Lily and James furiously. “Explain yourselves now! Since when have you two been secretly on the pull?”

Every head turned in James and Lily’s direction.

“Is it true, Lils?” Mary demanded.

“No!” Lily shouted, at the same time as James said; “Kinda.”

She whirled around and smacked his shoulder. “We—”

“Haven’t been lying about all those trips to the library?” Marlene said, incredulously.

“And how about all that extra time on the football pitch, James?” Peter demanded, emerging from the bushes with several twigs in his hair.

“Well, we—”

“Oh, give it up already!” Sirius grunted, sitting upright and pushing Remus off. “Spit it out—how long have you been shagging behind our backs?”

Lily gasped, mortified, but Marlene and Mary just came together, shouting in unison; “HOW LONG?”

“Since summer!” She moaned.

“But James was with me all summer,” Peter gasped, horrified.

“She means we've been talking on the phone,” James hissed.

Sirius laughed incredulously. “Oh, so while you two were giving each other the bell all summer you just thought ‘hey no need to tell my best mates anything, let them figure it out’!”

“You did, didn’t you?”

“Actually Lily confessed just now,” Remus said. “I’m just mad I didn’t call it.”

“You knew, Remus?” Marlene gaped.

“No, he didn’t!” Lily said. “None of you did because we knew you’d react like this!”

“Well, maybe if you’d told us over breakfast rather than Halloween in the woods we would’ve reacted a bit differently,” Lottie added sarcastically.

“Yeah,” Mary agreed, snatching up a discarded booze bottle, “but I am curious, where is it you two have been bunking off together?”

“Yeah, which dorm?” Sirius taunted. “Or does the gym storage room get more action than I thought?”

“Oh fucking hell, Black,” James scoffed, while Lily covered her face and jumped up, immediately racing up the path back toward House Lane.

“Lily!” James shouted, scrambling after her. “Lily, come back! You might get lost!”

Sirius was up in a second; “Oh no you don’t, Potter!”

He shot forward but unfortunately for him, Mary was faster. She stuck her foot out, tripping Sirius and leaving him sprawled in the dirt once more with a stiff grunt. “Cowards!” He coughed, as the other girls took off after Lily and James in the night.

Gingerly, Remus stepped up to look down over Sirius as Peter began to sputter with laughter behind them. His makeup was smeared with blood and dirt, but when he looked up at Remus he sighed and smiled.

“What, got something on my face?”

“Just a smug look.” Remus glanced at the discarded stag. “We gonna have to start calling you ‘Prongs’ too?”

Before Sirius could answer, a faint wailing called out from the trees, much more distant and haunting than any of their screams had been.

“What was the hell that?” Peter squeaked. "Reckon it was the Shack?"

“Nah, Pete, don’t worry," Sirius said, "s’just my mother after finding out I skipped my last chemistry test.”

Remus shook his head, too stupidly happy. “Happy Halloween, you dickhead.”



Chapter End Notes

'Twee' means dainty or overly cutesy.

Midges are these horrible little flies that infest the summer and autumn of Scotland.

‘Giving the bell’ is the same as ‘giving someone a ring’ on the phone.

Being 'on the pull' means to be looking for sex.

'Bunking off' means to skip out on something for school or work, but in this case Mary's alluding to James and Lily skipping out on them to be together.





Chapter 37: Sirius Turns Seventeen


Chapter Summary

Happy birthday to Sirius, love Salazar <3



Chapter Notes

CW: Smoking & drinking, but I suppose you're getting used to that, lol. Also references to sexual themes/activities.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



You are the dancing queen,

Young and sweet;

Only seventeen,

Dancing queen,

Feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah!

- “Dancing Queen” ABBA, 1976



Wednesday 3rd November 1976

As surprising as the James and Lily relationship reveal had been, the fact that the girls remained livid over the Halloween gag did not come as a shock. None of them so much as glanced in the direction of any 4A boy in the three days that followed, which for Sirius could only mean that the prank must’ve been successful.

It was a bit startling for Remus to think of his friends as being ‘together’ together, but the more he thought about it the less weird it felt. James and Lily had both had feelings for one another for so long—even if one was more quick to admit it than the other—and regardless of how mad she was now, Remus hadn’t missed the way Lily had been looking at James since the beginning of term. Really the most surprising thing was how long they’d been able to hide it, and how none of them had connected the dots. Tonya would’ve been killing herself over their blissful ignorance. He couldn't wait to tell her.

Before it all came back Remus thought he must have been dreaming, which he didn’t do very often. He was flying maybe, or weightless somewhere, just floating along. It wasn’t like being in water; in water you were still able to feel the weight of your arms and legs as they fought to keep you upright. Instead he felt like air—complete nothingness. He’d come apart at the seams, breaking up into little bits of matter until he was nothingness itself. He’d think later how that should’ve scared him—the thought of becoming nothing—but when you were so used to being everything at once, being nothing didn’t seem all that bad.

He remembered his mother’s trunk during that dreaded hour of night that was too unreasonably late to be up, but too horrifyingly early to be awake. Remus called this time of night the ‘shit hour’, because you could do shit-all during it and shit-all about it. Couldn’t talk, couldn’t play music, couldn’t turn on a light, could only sit and think; mostly about things you could do shit-all about. It was all-around shit. You could always worry though, since worrying was shit too.

His heart had leapt into his throat as he threw off his covers, dropping to his knees and reaching beneath the bed to find it. For the first few seconds his fingers fell upon only empty air, and he briefly wondered if the trunk had also disappeared into nothingness, but then his palm collided with the familiar leather surface of one of its corners and he fought to reach the handle. Dragging it out as quietly as he could so as to not disturb his roommates, Remus smoothed trembling fingers along the outside. The leather was damp, moisture already seeping into the cracks along its seams where it would eventually break it apart from the inside-out like a cancer.

Not entirely a masochist, Remus didn’t stop to wonder if the water had made its way inside. Using the tiny luggage key, he popped the trunk’s top and breathed out as he stared down at its contents.

They were fine.

The trunk’s exterior had held the test of time and prank. There was no hint of damp or mistreatment, not even along the delicate silk lining. The records were still pristine, albeit slightly dusty from six years of neglect. Perhaps it would’ve been better if they were ruined—the covers left soggy so he’d have no choice to throw them out or risk mold. It’d be half the hurdle, gone. But Remus had never been very lucky.

Oh, where have you been, my blue-eyed son?

And where have you been, my darling young one?

“Shit,” he mumbled. Told himself.

He shut the trunk.





* * *





Friday 5th November 1976

The Hawkings rumour mill could’ve rivalled the BBC with how well it collected and carried news. It took all of one day for word of their ‘late-night dip in the Dubh’ to spread across the entire campus, though at the behest of Regulus and his cronies or Mary and her beautifully big mouth, no one could be sure. Up until that moment Remus had been certain there wasn’t a single thing about the school that could surprise him anymore, but the prestige that running around freezing and naked in nothing but their knickers brought really threw him for a loop.

“ ‘Course we did it,” Sirius had boasted to a crowd of kids in their next forms, “cold water’s supposed to be good for you. Tightens everything up and all that. Lupin would know, he’s got abs.”

“Oh shut up, you dickhead,” Remus snapped, making everyone laugh. He could have lived in the weight training room and would still never pass for more than a bulky noodle, but he’d already resigned himself to suffer the cheeky questions and prodding until Sirius inevitably gave everyone something else to talk about.

Too bad not everyone was under the same impression.

“You need to stop telling everyone you ran around school naked, it’s not funny,” Kimmy lashed as she clutched tightly to Sirius’ arm on the common room couch. It was almost rare to see them sitting so solitary. Kimmy usually preferred to have an audience, parading Sirius around like he was an expensive broach on her shirt.

“We weren’t actually naked,” Sirius reasoned, “I told you we—”

“It doesn’t matter what actually happened if everyone thinks something else. Presence matters—public image matters! Really Sirius, I thought you’d understand that.”

Sirius said nothing, just turned away with a stubborn look as though he were pretending to count the books that lined the common room’s walls. Finally Kimmy reached for his chin and gently drew his gaze back to her as she traced a line around his perfect cupid’s bow.

“I don’t mean to be harsh, darling. You know I can’t stand the embarrassment—not after what Daddy did to Mummy, leaving us like he did. You understand, don’t you?”

Sirius nodded coolly and Kimmy’s face split into a smile as she began brushing her fingers through his hair. A moment later and they were made-up; kissing and sinking into the sofa with the fireplace blazing at their backs. Sirius’ hand slid up to cup Kimmy’s neck but she tugged it down across her collarbone and then even lower, right out there in the open for all to see. Still kissing her, Sirius’ eyes opened and flitted across the room. It took Remus a split-second to realise he was looking at him—that he’d noticed him staring.

Horrified, Remus ripped his eyes away, heart thrumming in his ears with embarrassment.

“Moony, it’s your turn,” Peter said.

Swallowing the lump in throat, Remus straightened up in his seat and turned back to their game of chess. He couldn’t stop thinking about Kimmy and her sickly-sweet voice—she never spoke quietly, not even while fighting with her boyfriend—and Sirius with those stormy eyes of his. Remus moved a pawn just to do something, and instantly Peter was grinning in delight.

“That’s checkmate, Lupin.”

“Fuck.” Remus flopped back in his seat. He should’ve known; he could’ve been in the best form he’d ever been in and still wouldn’t be able to beat Peter in chess.

“Do you want to have another round?”

Remus glanced at the clock. “No, sorry, I should really get that assignment done for Flitwick. I haven’t even started.”

“I thought you finished it yesterday,” Peter said, gathering up the game pieces.

Remus pursed his lips. He’d meant to finish the homework yesterday, but Sirius had inexplicably showed up in the library with a gang of Kimmy’s friends and he’d fled before he could be tortured by any more of his girlfriend’s unbearable giggling. It was getting ridiculous really—everywhere he went, there they were. As though Sirius were determined to make him into their own personal voyeur. Hawkings College existed on over five hectares of land—it was bigger than Windsor Castle for Christ’s sakes—and still there was no relief. Remus figured that he’d have to start sleeping in a tree soon just to avoid Sirius and James’ late-night conversations about how it felt to touch Kimmy’s boobs.

Peter eventually left him to find Moira and after collecting his things, Remus made his way out of the common room and toward the stairs. As went he allowed himself one final glance back, but this time Sirius wasn’t looking at him. Instead his eyes were trained on the fire while Kimmy snuggled into his chest and traced circles across his chest.

Remus returned upstairs.





* * *





Wednesday 10th November 1976

According to the Hawkings student handbook, students were to be responsible for their own laundry to 'help reinforce proper etiquette and value in the small chores of life'. Remus didn’t mind much, though the amount of teenagers who were too posh to know how much laundry detergent to put in with their bed sheets really stupefied him. He tended to wait until late in the evenings to do his laundry, that way he could sit and relax with a cigarette and a book and not have to worry about a prefect strolling along and giving him detention for smoking out of bounds. Too bad he had his own personal prefect to contend with.

Lily checked the remaining time on her washer and came to join him on the laundrette’s bench as they waited. Mary had also joined them, propped up on top of one of the dryers and musing over her current fascination, which also happened to be Sirius’ relationship status. Remus had no escape from it.

“I heard she hooked up with a student teacher in her tenth year,” Mary said, sipping the hot chocolate she’d brought with her from the dorms.

“Mary! I thought we agreed that we weren’t going to badmouth other women anymore,” Lily huffed; “There’s enough ingrained societal misogyny without us adding to it! Men are constantly tearing us down—there’s literally no use in us doing it to one another when we have them to do it for us. No offence, Remus.”

He waved her off, indifferent.

“What about the fact that you’re always whinging about Chastity?” Mary pointed out snidely.

“You mean Chastity Bell from history?” Remus asked, interest suddenly peeked.

“You gossips, that’s different,” Lily shot. “I don’t dislike her because she’s a woman, I dislike her because she’s an air-bag.”

Remus snorted as Mary gave Lily a ‘whatever you say’ sort of look.

“Hey Remus,” Mary started, “is Buchanan a good teacher?”

“Uh—yeah. She’s great actually, why?”

“I thought I might consider taking voice lessons with her next year. I’ve been doing the math and I’ll have a free period so I figured I might as well do something that’ll be fun before we leave school and start preparing to work until we die.”

“I thought your life goal was to move to Paris and become a rich widower,” Lily teased.

“Well, that too. But imagine how many attractive Parisian men will be knocking down my door when they discover I’m rich, with a dead husband, and the voice of an angel.”

“I didn’t know you could sing,” Remus said.

“Oh yes,” Lily giggled. “The shower’s her opera.”

Mary just pressed her hands to her cheeks and smiled humbly. “It was just a thought. My mum had a beautiful voice. Daddy used to say it was one of the reasons he fell in love with her.”

Remus looked down at the ground. He appreciated the fond way Mary could talk about her mother. It was clear she loved her a lot.

“Petunia expects her boyfriend’ll propose soon,” Lily blurted suddenly. “I’ve never even met the guy, but she told me yesterday on the phone.”

“Isn’t she still in school?” Mary asked, scandalised.

“Yeah, but she wants to get married the second she’s done. Says she doesn’t want to wait like Mummy did, but our mum wasn’t even old when she and dad got married. She just wanted a career first.”

“So she’s not going to university then?” Remus asked.

“Our parents want her to consider a polytechnic or a vocational program but she’s pretty stubborn.”

“God,” Mary scoffed; “I couldn’t imagine getting married at our age. There’s too many things I want to do first and having a man hanging around that often would be awful. No offence, Remus.”

“Isn’t this ‘no offence’ stuff getting a bit old?”

“Nope,” Lily grinned.

“Could you imagine if one of us got married?” Mary said, lifting her hot chocolate back to her lips before gasping. “I wouldn’t put it past Kimmy. Think she could convince Sirius to propose before Christmas? Bet she’d demand some tacky ring that’s been passed down through his family for ages and then complain that it’s ugly.”

“They’ve barely been dating for two weeks,” Remus said.

“Like that means anything. She’s got claws like a saber-toothed tiger, and Sirius has money.”

“His family has money—he doesn’t want any of it.”

“Well, that’ll change if Kimmy’s got anything to say about it. And she seems very fond of him. I heard her call him ‘Loveykins’ the other day.”

“I think I’m gonna hurl.”

A ding sounded, Lily’s washing machine, and she popped up to begin pulling her sheets out and transferring them to the dryer Mary was currently sitting on. “Stop teasing poor Remus, Mary, his sensitive heart can’t take it.”

“I’m not sensitive,” Remus objected.

“Sure you are. You’ve been moping ever since Black started dating the girl.”

“I have not.”

“Are you lonely, Remus?” Mary asked. “I’m still seeing Ken Thomas but if you’re really hurting I can put that on hold and take you out myself.”

“Thanks for the offer, Mary, but I’d rather be single and lonely than dating and pitiful.”

“Then you’re the only one.”

Lily shut the dryer and reached past Mary, hitting the start button. It jarred her so fantastically that she split hot chocolate across her skirt and slid off the dryer to scowl down at the fresh stain.

“Boo, you hag,” she huffed at Lily, who only smiled.

“We are in the laundry room—want to throw your skirt in with Remus’ stuff?”

Mary glanced playfully at Remus before reaching for her zipper.

“Oh, you guys are ridiculous,” he wailed, covering his eyes as both girls giggled at him.

Eventually Lily got Mary a towel to wear around her waist and they all moved on to the next topic of business, but Remus’ mind couldn’t avoid veering back into Sirius-territory.

No! Stop it, you bloody idiot. Stop thinking about it!

He pinched himself, squeezing until the dull ache turned into a throbbing and the pain had occupied at least some of his thoughts of Sirius Black.

That’s it. Every time you think of it, you can just pinch yourself.

Remus sighed. He’d definitely gone mental. But maybe it would just work. It could work. After all, no one else was telling him to make Sirius a priority, it was all in his head. If he could just turn it off then everything would be alright again. They were just friends—Remus shouldn’t care so much.

And so he wouldn’t. That was that.

“Remus, did Sirius ever say if he had my Runaways tape still? I couldn’t find it yesterday,” Mary said.

“Uh, yeah he and Kimmy were listening to it… yesterday.”

“Oh, okay. I’ll get it back from him later then.”

In the cover of his lap, Remus pinched the inside of his wrist.

This was going to take some getting used to.





* * *

Remus Lupin was a weak, weak man.

Sirius’ problems are not your problems, he told himself over and over again like a mantra. I bet if you asked Sirius he wouldn’t even call them problems in the first place!

The voice taunted him, as did the faint bruises decorating the inside of his arm. He’d given the habit up only a few days into it after realising that both the act of pinching and the bruises it left only made him think of Sirius more. He’d tried snapping an elastic around his wrist instead, but that wasn’t any better. And so there they were, nearly halfway into November, and it was still impossible to put Sirius or Kimmy from his mind. Perhaps it was because they liked to fight so much—publicly too, to the point where daily relationship updates might as well have been posted on the school’s main noticeboard.

THIS JUST IN: Sirius Black only loves Kim Bishop’s purple miniskirt this much, rather than THIS much.

HOT OFF THE PRESSES: Kim Bishop’s boyfriend thinks she should really get a sense of humour! One joke about bowel movements every other blue moon shouldn’t be such a world-ending event!

TALK OF THE DAY: Year 12 students should be able to accompany their year 13 girlfriends off campus during free-days and if the faculty says they can’t, well then it must be the boyfriend’s fault! HA!

Really, he should’ve been grateful. Early on Sirius had discovered he wasn’t likely to get the same sort of ego-boosting reaction out of Remus as he did with James or Peter. Apparently it was supposed to be quite thrilling to be regaled with how it felt to snog Kimmy between the shelves of the library where they could be drawn and quartered by Ms. Pince at any moment, but thankfully Sirius had quickly learned to stop trying where Remus was concerned. That didn’t mean however, that he wasn’t going to complain to him.

“Sometimes it’s like talking to a bird—like an actual bird, Moony—just chirp-chirp-chirp-chirp-chirp. It never ends. And the whining—ugh.”

“Then break up with her,” Remus suggested for the tenth time, trying hard to concentrate on his geography text. He had a free period and was trying to study in one of the empty halls, but Sirius had tracked him down after bunking off from Modern Languages.

“Ah,” Sirius smirked, “but see where’s the fun in that?”

Fun? How about relief? Relief and a bit of repose for the rest of us!

“I don’t get the upside,” Remus grumbled. “All you do is fight.”

“But she’s hot.”

Oh my god.

Sirius sighed wistfully, doodling stars on Remus’ open notebook. “Kimmy's pretty fun too, you know. She’s always willing to try new things—did I tell you she went with me to the Shrieking Shack?”

“Did I tell you that Lily went to the library and found out that it was actually where they housed tuberculosis patients in the thirties?”

“So you mean to say that people have actually died there? Cool.”

Remus resisted a groan. “You’re so thick sometimes.”

“Maybe, but Kimmy’s not. She’s actually really smart. In that sort of untrying way. And she’s very loyal to her friends—you should come and hang out with them sometime! Bet we’d all have a party.”

Fat chance.

“—And she likes my music too! She lets me put on whatever I want and always has a good opinion on it.”

“So she’s you.” And yet somehow so much worse.

“Oh damn,” Sirius laughed; “You might be onto something, Moons. Potter’s always saying I’m likely to fall in love with my own reflection. Ha, Kimmy’s gonna love that.”

Fall in love?!

“Well, why don’t you just marry her then!” Remus snapped, making Sirius shift uncomfortably in his seat.

“Woah, marry her? Where’s this coming from?”

“Nowhere,” he huffed, glancing away quickly. “Just something Mary said… It was a stupid joke.”

Sirius leaned in. “You’re not jealous by any chance, are you Moons?”

Remus looked back, fully ready to explode on him—No, I’m not jealous, your girlfriend’s just the worst thing since The Beatles breaking up!—but the expression on Sirius’ face was not his usual teasing. It was open and honest, seeking the truth. If Remus wanted to, he could’ve made his feelings clear right then and there. But even he didn’t know what those were and a part of him was afraid Sirius would try to ask.

So, because he was young and stupid just like Sirius, and because he wanted to punish them both, Remus said;

“No, I’m not jealous. You’re just an idiot.”

Sirius’ honest look was instantly replaced with bitter anger, which no one could’ve really blamed him for. “Fine,” he lashed, pushing up to his feet and letting his chair skid backwards. “Call me when you’re done having your little fit or whatever.”

“Call me you’re done being a selfish twat!” Remus shouted back, as Sirius stormed from the room, flipping him off over his shoulder.

After that they started avoiding each other at all costs. Remus was determined to never be alone in the same room with Sirius, or else risk having to talk about it. It drew any musical practice of theirs to an immediate halt, but it was a sacrifice Remus had to make for his sanity. As long as someone else was around then the subject of Kimmy could be avoided and Sirius couldn’t ask why Remus was acting so nasty about everything all of a sudden.

It isn’t all of sudden, he would tell the imaginary Sirius in his head, it’s always been like this with you!

And yet he had no explanation. The realisation that Sirius had always ignited this jealous part of him hurt a little bit—no one liked thinking of themselves as a complete cad—but even the green-eyed monster within him didn’t prevent the buzzing couple from showing up wherever he went.

“What are they even doing here?” He ground out, turning around on the bench at the edge of the football field to scowl at Sirius and Kimmy. They were sitting amongst the sports stands along with a handful of Kimmy’s friends, all of them drinking warm hot chocolate from the dining hall and sharing cigarettes between themselves. Remus thought haughtily that they didn’t look nearly as fun or thrilling as Simeon and his friends. At least their hot chocolate would’ve been likely spiked with Amaretto.

James lowered his water bottle and pulled the hem of his sports jacket away from his body to fan himself. It was the team’s last practice outdoors before they all moved into the indoor pitch for the winter and Remus was more chilled sitting on the bench than he’d hoped he’d be. Despite James’ eagerness when he’d asked to accompany him to the field that morning, Remus was only there because Sirius had told them that morning that he was planning on bringing Kimmy back to the dorm. Guess he’d changed his mind. Bloody prick.

“They always hang out here,” James advised with indifference. “They’re friends with Keith and he’s on the team. Dunno why Kimmy still stays to watch though.”

“What do you mean?”

“Keith’s her ex. He’s just like Kim so naturally the whole team heard about their break-up. I just sorta figured they wouldn’t want to be around one another so much since it was apparently pretty messy, but I guess that’s what happens if you share a friend group.”

As James loped away to join the team’s practice match, Remus couldn’t help but look back. Kimmy and Sirius were bundled up next to each other on the stands, laughing and passing a spliff back and forth.

I rolled that, he wanted to shout, I know him better than you.

But it didn’t make any sense, so he just turned back around on the bench and read his book.

Remus knew he could only avoid Sirius for so long. Whether it be because of his inability to remain consistent in his emotions or Sirius’ general lack of commitment, he could already feel them softening toward each other. In the beginning it’d been snide quips that left James and Peter to look between them awkwardly, but eventually their energy was spent and it took everything Remus had just to ignore the problem that shouldn’t have even been a problem in the first place.

The day he was confronted about it came on a particularly cold Friday in late November, after everyone had spent the school day complaining about the drafty conditions of the classrooms and quickly retired to the warmth of the dorms. The girls had joined them in camping out around their common room fireplace and they were all watching some game show on the telly. Remus was only half-paying attention, draped back against one of the sofas and trying not to fall asleep. On one side of him was Lily and James, curled up next to one another under a knitted blanket, and on the other was Marlene, her toes tucked under his thigh for warmth. Sirius sat sprawled ahead of them on a bed of cushions Mary had made up, no Kimmy in sight. None of them asked where she was of course, and Remus was grateful. It felt like just saying her name would will her into existence.

‘Next category: Name that Tune! Remember, there are no lyrics, just that funky beat! Here’s the first ten seconds,’ the host rattled. A moment later the soul-beat music spilled from the television speakers and Mary shot upright.

“Ooh! Oh! ‘Shining Star’ by Earth Wind and Fire!” She declared. “Or—or it’s The Temptations!”

“No, it’s gotta be like James Brown or something,” Sirius said. “I say ‘Sex Machine’.”

“You really think they’d put a song called ‘Sex Machine’ on television?” Marlene gaped.

“If they can put ‘You Sexy Thing’ and ‘My Ding-A-Ling’ on ‘Top of the Pops’ then these game show hosts can do whatever they want.”

“You’re all wrong anyway,” Remus murmured. “It’s ‘I Want to Take You Higher’. Sly and the Family Stone.”

‘And that was “I Want to Take You Higher” by Sly and the Family Stone!’

“Wow Remus,” Lily smiled, “good job.”

He shrugged, cheeks burning as he tried to avoid the look Sirius was giving him. It didn’t work. “Something on my face?” He drawled finally.

“Just surprised is all.”

“Me too. Thought you were supposed to have a perfect memory?”

Sirius gave him a little smile. “Guess it’s more subjective than I thought.”

Breathing in, Remus busied himself by picking at the fuzz on Lily’s blanket. He knew the next song too but didn’t bother showing off and Mary got it, grinning at Sirius smugly.

“Lucky guess,” he grumbled, shouldering her good-naturedly.

“Do you want a cuppa?” Remus asked Marlene as the show went to commercial break.

“Sure,” she nodded.

After taking stock of the rest of his friends’ tea orders, Remus pulled himself free from the couch and turned to make his way into the kitchenette across the hall.

“Hold on, I’ll come help you,” Sirius said, popping to his feet and immediately coming after him. Remus stubbornly didn’t bother waiting but Sirius paid no mind, padding in after him and leaning against the countertop as Remus gathered everything for tea.

“So James and I were going to have a little practice sesh tomorrow if you were interested,” Sirius said, passing him the kettle without being asked.

Remus lit the burner on the hob and shook out the match. “Sorry, got homework,” he mumbled.

“Oh, how about something the next day then? Kimmy’s having a little get-together.”

“You’re inviting me to one of Kimmy’s parties?”

“Yeah, don’t worry, It’s totally casual. You should come, really.”

Remus squeezed his eyes shut. Why, oh why, do you insist on having me around?

“That’s the day before Bilshin’s next test,” he said eventually, “I think I should probably study.”

“You don’t need to study anymore,” Sirius scoffed. “You have that test in the bag already.”

“Easy for you to say, Mr. ‘I threw my final exams and still got better marks than ninety-percent of the school’.”

“You’re still hung up on that?”

Remus glared at him.

“Okay, how ‘bout we study together first! Thennnn… we hang out?”

“Sirius, I’m not really interested in hanging out.”

“Why not?” He whined. “It’s like you’ve become a ghost or something—can’t nail you down anywhere!”

The metaphor only made Remus more unnerved. “I—I don’t need you to ‘nail me down’!”

“Well I didn’t mean it like that,” he snorted. “But please, Moons. I’m tired of fighting—not that we were fighting, of course. Everyone has spats, just—I miss you.”

Oh fucking hell. Fuck you and everything you stand for you stupid fucking supermodel of a tosser!

Remus rubbed awkwardly at the back of his neck. It would’ve felt better to hit something, but then he’d be the loon. He just wished the water would boil faster. “I wouldn’t fit in.”

“I wouldn’t want you to,” Sirius said, honestly. “I just want to hang out with my mate.”

“And your girlfriend.”

“Well, yeah duh? But Kimmy’s got friends. Yvonne mentioned she might have a thing for you actually.”

“Which one’s Yvonne?”

“Short—blonde—got all those freckles. Cute enough, I suppose,” Sirius shrugged. “You should come! It’s been a while since it’s just been you and me.”

“But it won’t just be you and me.”

“I know, but—please?”

Remus knew he wasn’t interested, but as Sirius stood there and begged him, he could feel his weakness creep back into his bones like a cancer.

“Fine, but I’m not gonna be nice.”

“Oh no, that would be asking far too much,” Sirius snickered, lifting himself up on the edge of the countertop and casually resting his hands on his thighs. From that angle he was finally taller than him, and as Remus looked up he felt a tug just behind his navel. It scared him and so he stepped back, accidentally brushing his hand across the side of the hot kettle.

“Shit!” He hissed, bringing his finger to his mouth to suck on.

“You okay, Moons?” Sirius asked, leaning forward.

Oh how I hate you sometimes. Wish I knew why.

“Pretty prick,” Remus mumbled around his wound.

Sirius smirked. “What was that?”

“I said you still owe me for the last two rounds of baccy from Xeno.”

“Oh.” Sirius’ face split into another grin. “Don’t worry, I’ll make it up to you. Promise.”

You’d better.





* * *





Sunday 21st November 1976

When James and Peter asked where they were going, Sirius said ‘a party’. He invited them too, but they both had club activities. Apparently Professor Slughorn was planning on letting students start construction on their own homemade rockets.

“Wouldn’t that mean you also have Slug Club stuff?” Remus asked, surprised Sirius wasn't more interested in the idea of shooting off his own personal explosion.

“Nah,” Sirius shrugged, “I only go when I feel like it.”

“And how often do you feel like it?”

Sirius just winked at him.

After bundling up to ward-off the cold, they met Kimmy and her friends camped out in a small crop of trees by the lakeside, surrounding an illegal bonfire of their own.

“I would’ve asked the girls to come too, but I think they’d be suspicious of another fire,” Sirius said to him, arm wrapped around his neck as they approached the clearing.

Kimmy stood up when she spotted them coming, eagerly racing over and combing her sandy waves to one side so as to show off her long neck.

“Hi Loveykins,” she beamed, kissing Sirius and making Remus pull away immediately. “Where’s your friend—James?”

“James isn’t coming,” Sirius said. Remus noted with a bit of satisfaction that he’d winced at the nickname too.

“But you said he was gonna be here,” Kimmy frowned; “I told Yvonne and everything.”

“I said I’d bring a friend,” Sirius said, eyeing Remus pointedly.

“Oh.” Kimmy looked him up and down appraisingly. “That’s fine then. I’ll go let Yvonne know.”

She scuttled back to the group and Sirius gently bumped his fist against Remus’ shoulder. “Sorry,” he winced, “she really only said to bring my ‘friend’.”

“Believe it or not, Black, I did not have the time to fall head-over-heels for ‘Yvonne’ in the last day and a half. I think I’ll be alright.”

“Oh good,” Sirius wrapped his arm around his neck again as he dragged him toward the fire; “not sure I could handle a broken-hearted Moony.”

Someone had brought a wireless radio at least, and as they settled in on a log next to Kimmy, Remus found himself drifting with the quiet music. It was a Showaddywaddy song, one that had been hogging the radio waves since its release and probably would until everyone hated it enough to change the channel whenever it came on.

‘Let’s go for a little walk,

Under the moon of love;

Let’s sit down and talk,

Under the moon of love;

I want to tell ya,

That I love ya,

And I want you to be my girl;

Little darling let’s walk,

Let’s talk,

Under the moon of love!’

“Guys, this is my best mate, Remus,” Sirius said, introducing him to the circle of about a dozen kids, all of them huddled close to the fire and each other. Remus waved back shyly and turned to Sirius.

“Who’s wireless is that?”

“Keith’s,” Sirius answered, cracking the tab of a beer and passing it to him. “Isn’t it cool? He just got it so it can reach stations even further away than anything Pete’s got in that AV club of his. We finally have more to listen to than just church hymns and disco!”

Suddenly it made a lot more sense as to why Sirius liked hanging out with them so much. “So you like Keith then?"

"Sure, he's an alright bloke."

"But isn’t he Kimmy's—?”

He never got to finish his sentence. Kimmy leaned over and pat Remus on the knee while pulling her puffer coat up tightly around her neck. “Remus take this end of the blanket!” She said. “That way we can all snuggle.”

He might’ve objected, but Sirius was already passing the fuzzy pink monstrosity over his shoulders and he’d forgotten to double-up on jumpers.

“Sirius,” Kimmy said suddenly, her bubbly-tone replaced with that of disappointment; “I thought we talked about this?”

Remus glanced over to see Kimmy staring at Sirius’ painted nails.

“It’s black though,” Sirius reasoned, examining his fingers.

“It’s still nail polish—not very manly.”

“So what, you’re not going to hold my hand if my nails have a bit of colour on ‘em?”

Kimmy gave him a sour look but Sirius just leaned in and whispered something in her ear that made her smile and she finally took his hand. “Alright, as long as you take it off by tomorrow.”

Remus had to bite his tongue to keep from saying anything, and Sirius just shrugged indifferently. As Remus sipped his beer, waiting desperately for the buzz to set in and dull his irritated nerves, Sirius went around the circle of teens and rattled off their names like racehorses on a track.

“And that’s Stanford and Jaz, they’re together but Jaz was with David before. Now David’s casually seeing Kiki but Kiki’s also on-again, off-again with Anwar who dated Erica before that but is now basically with Stacy. And then that there’s Yvonne and she’s sitting next to Monica and Luke—they’re step-siblings—and next to them is Keith who dated—”

“Let me guess, Kimmy?”

“Yeah!”

“We’re all very comfortable with one another,” Kimmy said, leaning in again and sliding one hand up Sirius’ thigh. From an objective point, Remus knew she was pretty, but even her current friendliness made him want to tear his hair out.

“So have you dated David, Kiki, and Anwar too, Kim?” He asked.

“Oh don’t be silly, David’s like my brother.”

Remus downed the rest of his beer.

Watching Kimmy’s friends play around the fire was a lot like how it felt to see politicians and bureaucrats play nice at Lyall's dinner parties. Remus had never really been to very many of them beyond the few his father made him squeeze into an uncomfortable monkey-suit for, but he’d spied on more than one of the galas held at the Lupin Estate. He’d been younger then, but he could still remember how the officials would weave their way through the crowds, and stopping to talk to people less important than they were but never daring to interrupt a conversation of someone above their station. The upper class had never really changed that way, and it occurred to him as he watched the kids interact, that they were those same future elites. One day they would be feigning laughter with an American congressman or some heir to a booming investment firm, rather than just pretending to ignore one another over a fire.

It made Remus miss Audrey with her unsolicited socio-economical commentary, and Renata and Deacon with their almost grandparent-like way of asking how your day was. They could always find something to be glad about. He wished Cass were there with his guitar—he’d have been a ‘beginner’ on it for three years now. He craved the floaty, nonsensical feeling of Alice’s drugs and most of all, he wished Simeon were there to call everyone on their bullshit. At least Sirius would’ve listened to him.

“Moony,” Sirius said, nudging him with a half-smoked spliff. Remus took it and nearly brought it to his lips before passing it onto the kid on the log next to them. Stanford or Stanley or something.

“You okay?” Sirius asked, eyeing him. “You don’t seem like you’re having much fun.”

Because Kimmy had moved away to join Keith and another girl on the other side of the fire, Remus answered honestly. “I’m not.”

“Why? Are you cold?”

“Yes, but it’s not that.”

“Then what is it?”

He sighed. “They’re like a commune.”

“I know right?” Sirius beamed. “Isn’t it great?”

“No, it’s not great. They aren’t actually about ‘peace and love’, they’re just glorifying everything. You really think Kimmy with her thousand pound-sterling, mink-lined coat would be caught dead sharing beans and alfalfa in some dingy co-op with a bunch of hippies? All this is, is some weird incestuous friend group who doesn’t actually like being friends with one another.”

“It’s not incestuous.”

“Are you sure about that? Because those step-siblings are sitting mighty close to one another.”

Sirius scoffed. “You think you can see through everyone, don’t you?”

“I see enough. Are you really going to stop wearing things like nail polish just because Kimmy says she doesn’t like it?”

“She doesn’t mean anything by it, she’s just got a strict family. They wouldn’t think it’s proper for a bloke to show up with nancy nails and all that.”

“When were you planning on meeting her bloody family?”

“I wasn’t!”

“Then I don’t get it.”

“Well, that’s a first.” Sirius opened another beer. It was his third or fourth. Remus tried hard to rein-in his temper.

“I don’t mean to insult your new friends. I’m just happy with ours.”

“I am too, nothing could replace you guys. It’s just… nothing wrong with branching out a bit right? Unless you… have something else to say about it?”

Remus drew back. “Like what?”

Sirius gave him a long look. “Nevermind, I was just kidding. Go on then, how is it these guys are any different from us?”

“Well for one thing we don’t all sleep with each other.”

“We could.” Sirius wiggled his eyebrows.

“Don’t be gross. At least we all actually like each other.”

“Fine, so we like each other. Anything else?”

“I just don’t get how this couldn’t bother you. Look at your girlfriend—” Remus threw out a hand before remembering other people were around. Setting his jaw, he lowered his voice; “She’s practically sitting in her ex-boyfriend’s lap, doesn’t that bother you?”

“No, why should it? I dated Mary and we’re still friends.”

“Oh, right. Glad to know that a three-week relationship didn’t totally decimate your friendship.” Remus sighed. “I just don’t want you to be upset if this doesn’t turn out how you want.”

“Aw, are you worried for me?”

“Don’t make me drown you in the lake.”

Sirius smiled, setting his head on Remus’ shoulder playfully. “Don’t worry, Moons, nothing can break my heart.”

Remus wanted to push him away, but he found he was frozen in place. Chalking it up to the cold, he kept still until finally Sirius pulled away and untucked himself from the blanket. “Be right back,” he said, “gotta wiz.”

Watching him go, Remus picked up Sirius’ fresh beer and took a swig for himself. “Tosser,” he grumbled, as Kimmy picked up the edge of the blanket and sat down in Sirius’ spot herself.

“Uh—sorry Kim, Sirius just went to the toilet.”

“That’s okay,” she said, snuggling into his side, “I don’t mind waiting.”

Remus tried to ease away, but Kimmy just slid closer, a dozy smile on her face. “I wanted to say I wasn’t actually disappointed when he brought you along,” she said.

“Oh yeah…?”

“It was just Yvonne. She has a thing for athletes.”

“James has a girlfriend anyway.”

“Mhm, Sirius told me, but Deedee’s good at getting what she wants. I still think she’s crazy though. Athletes are all wrong—learned that the hard way with Keith. We never saw eye-to-eye on things. He’s much too tame. Who you should want are the ones you really shouldn’t. The wild ones.”

On ‘shouldn’t’ a shiver ran up Remus’ spine.

“It’s why I go for the artists,” Kimmy said. “Sirius said you play music with him.”

“Sometimes.”

“Bass, right?”

“Yeah…”

“Well, I think that’s very hot.”

The gall of a woman with a drink in her hand.

“I think I’m gonna go have a smoke,” Remus said, attempting to untangle himself from the blanket.

“Oh no, have it here. In fact, have one of mine.”

Kimmy produced a box of menthol cigarettes and pulled one free, offering it to him between two fingers. “I got them from in town. They taste great compared to those ugly rolled ones Sirius is always smoking.”

“No, I think I’m okay.”

“Oh c’mon, here.” She took the non-filter end between her teeth and cheekily tried to pass it to him that way, but when he didn’t take it, she just plucked it from her lips and turned it around, lighting and blowing smoke up into the night air. The minty smell hit Remus’ eyes and made them twinge, but Kimmy didn’t seem to notice.

Across the fire, the wireless continued to play, this song more unwelcome than the last;

‘ —at a church,

Were people saying, My God, that’s tough;

She stood him up,

No point in us remaining;

We may as well go home,

As I did on my own;

Alone again, naturally…’

Remus was about to get up and ask Keith to flip the channel himself when Kimmy turned to him, lips pursed quizzically.

“Has Sirius talked about me much?” She asked.

It felt like a trick question. “Well yeah, of course.”

“Oh good. That makes me happy to hear. What sort of things has he said?”

“Kim, I don’t think I should—”

“I don’t care if it was dirty, in fact that might be more fun. At least in regards to what I wanted to ask you.”

“Ask me?”

She turned to him suddenly and got even closer, holding the burning menthol between them. “Look, I’m no slag, but I thought it might be fun if the three of us… you know.”

“Hooked up?” The words came out before he could stop them, and instant regret surged as Kimmy’s face lit up.

“Yeah. I was talking to Sirius about it and neither of us have ever—”

“You talked to Sirius about this?”

“No,” Kimmy said fondly, setting her hand on his thigh and stroking it gently, “but I’m sure he wouldn’t mind.”

“Actually I think he would.”

“Why? Was he lying when he said he’d never done it before?”

Remus’ face felt hot. “No, I just—maybe I mind!”

“Oh, don’t worry about that.” Kimmy laughed and pinched his thigh lightly, making Remus straighten up on the log. “It’ll be fun,” she told him in an alluring voice, before moving her hand up and taking his. She raised it toward herself—toward her chest.

“No,” Remus chirped, pulling his hand back sharply. It knocked the cigarette from Kimmy’s hand and she stared down at it sorely before snapping her face back to his as he stood up. “I don’t think this is a good idea,” he said.

“Remus, sit down back down,” Kimmy hissed, “the others are looking.”

“Oh I forgot, you only like people watching when you want them to, right?”

A nerve jumped in her jaw. “Sit down and I’ll forget you said that.”

It felt like an ultimatum, and instantly Remus was that same hoodlum kid again, who was always running away from school to chase his friends around dodgy alleys and throw beer bottles at cars. Posh public school prats like Kimmy didn't know what it was to really be intimidating.

“No," he snarled viciously. "In fact, I was right. I’m not interested. You're like a leech hanging on to my best friend. Someday someone's gonna burn you off."

Kimmy’s mouth dropped open in disbelief but Remus held his ground. “You can tell Sirius that I went back to our room," he growled. "Oh and by the way, your menthols smell cheap.”

Turning, he marched away from the circle of kids, almost trembling to his very core and not because of the cold. Kimmy had more than surprised him, but it wasn’t the idea of sleeping with her that had thrown him. It was the fact that she might’ve brought it up to Sirius first.

“Fuck,” Remus hissed, hugging himself as the sound of Keith’s radio fell away.

‘And when she passed away,

I cried and cried all day;

Alone again, naturally,

Alone again, naturally…’



Chapter End Notes

The two songs that were playing around the fire were "Under the Moon of Love" by Showaddywaddy (1976) and "Alone Again" by Gilbert O'Sullivan (1972).





Chapter 39: November (Part 2)


Chapter Summary

Remus wonders what it is that's missing.



Chapter Notes

CW: Remus has a bit of a melt-down here. Just in case that’s triggering for anyone <3



See the end of the chapter for more notes



I’m singing this note ‘cause it fits in well,

With the chords I’m playing;

I can’t pretend there’s any meaning here,

Or in the things I’m saying;

But I’m in tune,

Right in tune;

I’m in tune,

And I’m gonna tune,

Right in on you…



- “Getting in Tune” The Who, 1971



Remus could not, under any circumstances, ever look Sirius in the eye again.

And that pissed him off, because it wasn’t even his fault!

Sirius had demanded to know of course, what it was that had made him flee so quickly from the bonfire. Apparently Kimmy had done just as he’d asked and told Sirius that he’d gone back to his room, but the aloof attitude with which she’d spent the rest of the night in had been more than cause for alarm.

“I just started feeling bad,” Remus said the next morning, trying to rush into the toilet while Sirius got in his way.

“Did Kimmy say something to you?”

“God, no! Can I just piss, please?”

“Sorry, Lupin!” Peter said, slipping into the bathroom behind Sirius.

Remus swerved around Sirius in anger and pounded a fist on the door. “Ugh—Pete, get your sorry arse out here now!”

“You’ve been moodier than a girl on the blob—if you want me to break up with her just say so!” Sirius said from behind him.

“I don’t care what you do, Sirius! Just leave me out of it!”

“Fine!”

“Fine!”

“Smashing,” James declared, walking into the room with four cups of tea. “Now can you two numpties stop yelling? It’s seven in the morning.”

They didn’t exactly make up after that, but there wasn’t any need to. Remus had already resolved for perhaps the millionth time to put Sirius and Kimmy as far from his mind as possible, and now that they were both suitably pissed off at him, it was easier. While Sirius threw himself into his relationship, Remus threw himself into the books, spending every moment he could out of their dorm and in the library. He still missed practising with Sirius, and his music marks were suffering slightly as a result, but he couldn’t bring himself to ask him. Every time Sirius so much as glanced at him he assumed that that was it; that he knew what Kimmy had asked him and they’d finally have to talk about it, and Remus couldn't have that.

But he did want to talk about it—just not with Sirius. But who could he go to? Peter and Lottie couldn’t keep a secret to save their lives, and Mary would’ve been just as unable to keep something so juicy to herself. Lily wouldn’t tell anyone—except for maybe James, and James knowing felt about as world-ending as Sirius knowing. It left Marlene, who could certainly be trusted but he didn’t want her judgement either.

It was all such a mess.

Then it hit him; Tomny and Tonya.

Of course! They knew him, they’d believe him when he said he wanted nothing to do with the girl—that she’d come on to him.

When he finally got the nerve to phone the flat, only Tonya was around. It was almost a relief actually, not to have to explain to Tomny why he was so pissed over another bloke’s girlfriend. He wasn’t mad because Sirius had a girlfriend, he was mad because that girlfriend was Kimmy. At least, that's what he hoped.

“She sounds like a right bitch,” Tonya said.

“God, yes. Finally someone gets it.”

“So what are you gonna do?”

“Huh?”

“You turned down her offer. Would you have accepted it if your friend had been the one to ask?”

“N-no! I—I don’t have any interest in other guys’ girlfriends.”

“Oh, I know,” Tonya laughed, “couldn’t get you to make a real move on me if I tried.”

“Not funny, Ton.”

“It’s a little funny.”

Remus sighed into the phone. “I don’t know what I’m gonna do. I’m tired of fighting with him.”

“Then maybe you should be honest, tell him you think his girlfriend’s a miserable cow.”

“Can you do it for me?”

“Yes.”

“… That was a rhetorical question, but thanks anyway.”

“Always here to help, love.”

Talking with Tonya had made him feel better, but it did little in the long run. Remus still couldn’t bring himself to admit that what he needed wasn’t more distractions, but an honest answer.

That he still did not have.

The fact of the matter was that Sirius Black was a rare enigma he didn’t know what to do with, and that meant less time spent at his side, and more time spent at the library.

“Hey Scarface,” Barty hollered down the library’s centre aisle, “take any more naked trips to the lake? How's those pale cheeks of yours?” Before he could so much as begin to laugh though, Ms. Pince appeared and hauled him out by the ear.

“Didn’t think Barty even knew this school had a library,” Remus grumbled, grinding his pencil down to the nub in the middle of his notebook.

“I don’t know why you don’t just tell people it never happened,” Lily said, innocently flipping through her history text.

“Because it did—or were you suddenly not there?”

“Oh I was there alright. And you do have pale cheeks, you know.”

“That’s a blatant lie—you never saw them!”

She looked away with a smug expression but neither confirmed nor denied. At least being with Lily was easy. She never brought up Kimmy and any griping about James usually came about because it was impossible to grip with him. Lily had said more than once that if their relationship failed it would be because James was too nice to point out when she was being an absolute nutcase.

Clearing her throat, Lily flipped a flash card, quizzing him to pass the time. “On what Mediterranean island was Napoleon Bonaparte born?”

What ever happened to the #1 pencil? Remus wondered, zoning out.

“Remus?"

“Huh? Oh… longitude?”

“We’re studying history.”

“What,” he paused to yawn, “they didn’t use longitude in the old days?”

With a sigh, Lily finally set the flashcards down and glanced at the wall clock. “Where is she? We agreed to meet at four-thirty.”

“Maybe you scared her off by suggesting we do the project on the 'decline of feudalism during the French Revolution'.”

“I'm trying to be nice,” she huffed impatiently, “but between this and prefect stuff, I’m about ready to snap.”

“Does this mean Snape’s still ditching you to be Slughorn’s hound?”

Lily nodded grimly. “Yesterday was the fourth time this month that he’s left me alone to prefect work with Chastity. Figures I would get grouped with her in class too.”

“Does he know about you and James yet?”

“No! God, I don’t even want to know how he’d react. They hate each other.”

“For good reason.”

“You’re not going to say anything are you?”

Remus shook his head adamantly. He didn’t need to go around spilling other people’s secrets, he had enough of his own. “No, never. You and James already made all of us promise to keep it hush.” A thought suddenly occurred to him, and he squinted at her. “Wait, don’t tell me this is all because of Snape?”

“I just don’t want there to be any arguments,” Lily reasoned.

“But you’re dating! How does James feel about all of this?”

“He’s fine with it.”

“Really?”

“Yes, ask him yourself if you don’t believe me.”

Remus sat back in his chair. It wasn’t hard to believe that James wouldn't do just about anything to make Lily happy, but resisting rubbing his successful relationship in Snape’s face every time they crossed paths? That was a feat.

“Remus,” Lily started again, drawing his gaze, “is there something else you’d rather be doing? Because you’ve spent half the morning daydreaming and the other half making it snow inside.”

She was right of course. Since they arrived he’d successfully shredded the first several pages of his study guide into tiny pieces. “No, sorry,” he mumbled, scooping the scraps into a pile with his palms.

“Are you feeling okay? You look really tired.”

“Well it is a Saturday morning, Lils.”

“So you’re tired because it’s early, not because you barely slept last night?”

Remus just grunted in response and Lily frowned.

“Have you gone to see Ms. Pomfrey? She might be able to give you something that’ll help.”

“The nurse can’t do anything. I’m not a restless baby you can give opium to, Lily.”

“And she’s not going to give you opium, Remus, but maybe she’s got a tea or something.”

“Blimey, you’re right, how could I have never thought of chamomile before?”

Lily scowled, unimpressed, and closed her history text. “Will you tell me why it’s so bad then? Why you can’t sleep?”

To avoid her gaze, Remus began patting at his mountain of paper bits. “No reason. Always been a shit sleeper.”

“So it’s chronic?”

“Guess so.”

“Insomnia’s supposed to be triggered by stress, you know.”

“Is it really? Fascinating.”

She threw a flashcard at him.

“Sorry,” he said over a light laugh, “it’s nothing.”

“It can’t be nothing,” she pressed. “Is it exams that have you so distressed? Because you know those aren’t for a few weeks.”

“I’m not distressed.”

“And you’re going to pass all of them with flying colours so—”

“Lily, it’s not exams!”

“Okay…” Lily bit her lip. “Is it something else then? Like maybe… someone else?”

“Oh my god,” Remus moaned, pressing his fingers into his eye sockets, instantly mortified that she had somehow been able to read his mind. “Please stop.”

“I know, I know. But Peter’s got Moira and Lottie’s with Mickey and Mary just started seeing that Bryan guy from the year above—”

“I thought his name was Ken?”

“Different guy—but I know we’ve been busy and Sirius has been spending a lot of time with other people, so I figured if you’re feeling a little neglected—”

“I have you and James.”

Lily raised her eyebrows pointedly. “Not that I’m not flattered, Remus—truly—but… my point? Me and James?”

“Oh…”

“It’s not like I want you to feel as though you can’t—”

“No, I get it,” Remus said, raising a hand to stop her.

“Yes, well,” Lily cleared her throat a bit, “I’ve been thinking…”

“Shocker.”

“Oh so snide—I meant I’ve been thinking about you. You and… other people…”

That got his attention. “What are you on about now, Evans?”

“Nothing! Just that Marlene really clung to you on Halloween, so I thought that maybe…”

“Here’s the pot calling the kettle black if I’ve ever seen it! What about you and Potter? You were hugging and kissing and—”

“We did not kiss!”

“Only because you were too busy trying not to knock his head off.”

“Yours too, actually. And you both would’ve deserved it.”

Remus smirked. “Bet you liked tricking him out of his clothes on Sirius’ birthday.”

“Oh shut it, you.”

Remus sat back, satisfied. But he couldn’t deny the odd feeling that came over him when Lily brought up Marlene. They were friends, right?

“I swear to god…” Lily sighed, looking to the clock again. “She must think this all some joke. If our marks suffer because we had to drag her along—”

“Well I think we should consider ourselves lucky. Sirius and Lottie got stuck with Snape.”

“Or Sev got stuck with Sirius.”

Remus groaned. “How much does that git pay you to buy such loyalty?”

Lily stuck her tongue out at him and he reached over to poke the back of her hand with his pen in retaliation. She gasped before doing the same to him, leaving a mark on his wrist and igniting a pen-war that only ended when Chastity Bell finally dropped her book bag down onto the table across from them.

“Hi-ya,” Chastity said coolly, pulling her long brown hair over her shoulder. She raised an eyebrow when she noticed the ink, now decorating them up to their elbows.

“Hi, Chastity,” Lily said, straightening up and reaching for her books. “Glad you could make it. I don’t know if you got the chance to look over my notes but we—”

“Look I don’t mean to be rude or anything, but is there any way we can make this quick?” Chastity started, untucking her chair from the table and sitting down. “I’ve just got some things to do today.”

Lily gave a vinegary smile. “Yeah, that’s fine. How about we go over the project’s rubric to assign roles, that way we can do them separately.”

“Sounds perfect.”

Stiffly, Lily set about organising her notes as Remus stretched and draped one arm over the back of his chair. Chastity hadn’t bothered to unpack any of her things, and instead was simply staring at him like he was a puzzle she’d yet to work out. It made him slightly nervous and he licked his lips, keeping his eyes focused on Lily’s papers as well.

“There, that one,” Remus said, pointing at the rubric. Lily slid it out of her paper stack and tapped them straight again before clearing her throat.

“Right, so, I figured—”

“You’re from London, Remus, yeah?” Chastity interrupted.

“Er, yeah.”

“What part?”

“Greenwich,” he answered, suddenly aware of how moist his palms had become. Some girls just did that to you—it had been the same way with Tonya until he’d gotten to know her better. Kimmy, thankfully, did not have the same effect.

“Oh really?” Chastity began twirling a lock of hair around her finger. “Someone told me it was Chelsea. I’m from Kensington. Where’d you go to school?”

“Just some boys’ school.”

“Well why’d you switch to Hawkings? It’s terribly dreary up here. Not that we don’t appreciate having you, of course.” Chastity propped her chin on her hand and batted her eyelashes.

“Doesn’t rain anymore than it does in London,” he murmured.

“Was it because of the school’s reputation then?”

“Not exactly.”

“I bet it must’ve been terribly lonely at an all boys school.”

“Er…” Remus glanced to his right where Lily was sitting and quietly fuming under the guise of a tight-lipped smile. “Chastity, I really don’t think—”

“Oh, call me Chas. Everyone does.” Chastity smiled broadly and leaned in a bit. “Say, would you be willing to tell me how you got—” She tapped her nose over the spot where Remus had his scar. Before he could react, Lily reached across the table to slap the project rubric down in front of her along with a list of books.

“Chas,” she said sweetly, “would you mind asking Ms. Pince which of these books are available? I know they’ll be useful for the project.”

Chastity picked up the list with two fingers as though Lily had just handed her a dead rat. “We’ll need all of these?”

“Don’t worry, if you can check them out for us, Remus and I will compile whichever ones seem most useful for your half of the work.”

“So you want me to—”

“If you mind terribly, Remus can always go look and you and I can stay here and start sorting through Professor Binns’ extended reading list.”

Chastity’s eyes became narrow like a cat’s, but rather than begin hissing, she proudly got up from her seat and began stalking toward the librarian’s desk, her school skirt swishing behind her and the reading list clutched tightly in her fist.

“I thought you already checked out the books we needed,” Remus said, nudging Lily’s elbow with his own.

“I did. I just needed her to go away. I can’t believe what she said to you.”

Remus looked up again, watching Chastity at the librarian’s desk. She caught him staring and waved and he swallowed thickly. “She isn’t any worse than Kimmy. In fact I’d rather Black date her. At least she didn’t ask anything anybody else hasn’t already wondered.”

“Ugh, boys,” Lily scoffed, scribbling in her day-timer. “You just think she’s hot.”

“I do not!”

“No?”

“No!”

Lily just smirked, making Remus roll his eyes. “Want to work on this Tuesday night after English?” He asked, attempting to change the subject. “We don’t need to invite Chastity.”

“Can’t, I have a Slug Club meeting.”

“Oh. You’re still in that? Sirius never goes.”

“Mhm. Black only comes to about every second or third meeting, but Professor Slughorn still thinks he’s some unfulfilled genius and won’t bother kicking him out. Potter goes, though. How about tomorrow?”

“No, sorry, I told Marlene I’d help her with something.”

“With what?”

“Dunno, I only half heard her when she was running to class this morning. More homework, I guess. ”

Lily clicked her tongue and gave a sly smile. “You guess?”

“Yeah, I mean what else?”
