“Oh, nothing.”

Remus narrowed his eyes. “What are you smirking at?”

“Come on, Remus. I know you’re not that thick—Marlene?”

“What about her?”

Lily dropped her head back and gave a great groan. “Fine, what… colour would you say her hair is?”

“… Is this a trick question?”

“No, you dimbo! What colour?!”

“Blonde...?"

Lily held out her hands as though she were presenting him with an idea. “I think it’s more like this beautiful golden colour. Like daisies or sunshine. See, now it’s your turn. You read, try for something more romantic than just ‘blonde’.”

Remus looked around like an explanation for his friend’s sudden insanity would appear out of thin air. “What does romance have to do with a hair colour?”

“Now you’re asking me the trick question!”

He snorted and Lily smiled back at him wistfully. A moment passed, then she asked; “Have you ever been on a date, Remus?”

He blinked. “What? No.”

“Would you like to—if we weren’t at school?”

Remus looked up briefly, eyeing Chastity, before pushing the thought away and giving a short chuckle. “Wow, Evans, I’m almost inclined to accept your proposal if I didn’t worry about James sucker-punching me for it.”

“Actually I think you’re about the only one he wouldn’t sucker punch,” Lily replied gleefully, “but nice try. You know I meant Marlene.”

“Well that’s all right and good, but I’m not dating Marlene.”

“But would you?”

“If we weren’t at school?”

“No—anywhere. Like right now?”

“You’re trying to set us up, aren’t you?”

“And apparently I’m failing miserably at it, since both of you are about as observant as Professor Binns.”

Remus balked. “You mean you’ve talked to Marlene about this?”

Lily just looked at him. “Duh.”

“And what did she say?”

“I’m not going to tell you unless you’re interested.”

“So that means she’s interested?”

Lily rolled her eyes and flipped open her textbook, letting Remus slump back into a bout of thoughtful silence. Marlene was a good friend, but a girlfriend? That was news. Marlene was pretty enough of course, and her taste in music wasn’t all that bad—almost pleasant if you took away the amount of church hymns she had committed to memory.

He thought of his friends, Peter who’d been in what could only be considered a long-term relationship in teenage years, and James who’d been pining after the same girl for most of his waking memory. Sirius was nowhere close to their level, but seemed to have enough fun on his own if his and James’ late-night conversations were anything to go by. And of course there was Tomny and Tonya, who both seemed to exist in the same way that the ocean met the shore, separate but moving together as though one couldn’t exist without the other. They were all happy in their own way and he’d never felt jealous over it until recently. Perhaps getting a girlfriend would mean he could finally start worrying about his own relationship status and not Sirius’.

As Lily continued writing and rewriting her study notes, Remus bit his lip, strumming his fingers on the table as though he were playing his bass. It was the first few chords to “You’re My Best Friend”.

He sighed, pausing his fingers. “Marlene likes the Bee Gees right?”

Lily looked up and beamed at him just as Chastity returned to the table in a huff, slapping the book list back down on its surface.

“This is the suggested reading list for psychology.”

“Ooh, sorry Chas,” Lily frowned, “my mistake.”





* * *



Later that night…

Remus winced as he hit the wrong cord and his flow was instantly obliterated, ruining his run-through of “In the Hall of the Mountain King”. He might’ve felt less disappointed, had Sheila not been sitting right in front of him on the piano bench. Asking his teacher for a bit of extra help practising had seemed like a good idea before, but now he was just embarrassed.

“You’re going for speed, but what we really want is accuracy," Sheila told him. “Try keeping your hand locked on those four frets that way you can use your third finger rather than tripping over everything with your first and second.”

He nodded and tried again. This time the flourish sounded better, but he still messed up the rests.

“Here.” Sheila turned back to the piano and played each note staccato so he could hear them clearly. “You hear that?” She teased, hitting a high G several times; ding-ding-ding-ding! “That’s where you rest and begin the reprise.”

Taking a deep breath, Remus tried once more, but again he hit the wrong cord and immediately froze. “Shit. I sound terrible.”

Sheila turned around on the piano bench, her hands folded neatly in her lap. “Remus, you sound wonderful.”

“But I still can’t get it,” he huffed.

“You’re learning. It’s alright to make mistakes. Rome wasn’t built in a day.”

“And yet Sirius gets to be born a Mozart.”

Sheila smiled like she knew exactly what was going on, and he immediately regretted the snide remark.

“I’ve noticed you and Sirius have been sitting apart these last few weeks,” she said, casually smoothing out her skirt. “Do you want to talk about it?” Remus went to open his mouth but she cut him off; “Let me guess—no.”

He scowled at her and looked down at the Fender stubbornly.

“Well,” Sheila started, “I may be your teacher, but I’m certainly not a counsellor. I can’t tell you what you should or shouldn’t do to magically solve all your problems, but I can assure you that taking it out on that bass guitar isn’t going to make you feel any better.”

Remus plucked a harsh fret pointedly. “I disagree.”

Sheila laughed at him and turned back to the piano. “That’s right, not a counsellor, just a music teacher,” she said, loudly, as though she were talking to the room itself. “I wonder though, if I were to play really loudly, you wouldn’t be able to hear much, would you? Not even if someone were to shout out all of their problems. They wouldn’t even have to be talking to me, they could just be saying words. Like, how they’re feeling or how they wish they were feeling. Hmm, I wonder.”

Without letting him object, Sheila immediately started up a piece with a brisk tempo, starting as vivace and quickly transforming into vivacissimo. As promised, she played each note with such fervent vigour that the piano drowned out even the incessant noise of the room’s radiator as it blared down at them from the ceiling.

“Nope!” She hollered. “Can’t hear a thing! Anyone could be saying anything and no one would know!”

This is stupid, Remus thought. She’s insane.

“Did you say something, Remus?” Sheila called.

“N—”

“Sorry, can’t hear you!”

He growled in the back of his throat. “This is stupid!”

Sheila kept on, her back to him and swaying with every excited note.

“I said it’s STUPID!” He yelled again, with no reaction. “It’s stupid and I want to smack him!”

Remus had blurted the words out so suddenly that it surprised him, but their meaning was instantly lost in the noise of Sheila’s music anyway, leaving him stunned and almost overwhelmed.

“I want to tell him he’s being an idiot and hear it when he says the same thing to me!” He picked up, clutching tightly to the neck of his bass while Sheila practically danced to the rhythm of the piece. “I want to stop being jealous of everything! But what isn’t there to be jealous about?! He’s talented and popular and good-looking and—and people like him better and I do too so I don’t understand what the PROBLEM IS!”

“That’s it, Remus!”

He could’ve choked on the music. It was diving down his throat and pulling out his words as though it could throw them to the wind. If he were in a movie, he’d be whipping around in a tornado, waiting to be dropped in the Land of Oz to squish his own Wicked Witch.

“I want to understand but it’s impossible,” he wailed. “I want to be there and not there at the same time and I want him to just understand without me saying it! I want to be here and I want to be home and I want to pass my exams but I also want to be able to say ‘FUCK IT’ like I used to! I want to play guitar with James and watch stupid movies with Peter and read wonderful books with Lily and listen to amazing music with him! I want to throw bottles at walls with Lee and wrestle with Doss and see Flaky again but I can’t! And I want to be with Tomny! I want to see Tonya—I want to do all of it right NOW! And I’m so tired of caring—I just don’t want to care anymore but I do! AND THAT MAKES ME TIRED!”

As he finished his breathless rant, Sheila’s song slowly came to a filtered end, dropping in tempo and volume until she was just tapping her fingers against the keys.

Any way the wind blows…

“I’m very proud of you, Remus,” Sheila said, slowly turning around on the piano bench as he heaved in his chair. Remus sniffed, wiping his face, but her eyes were kind. Without judgement. It nearly killed him.

“But remember," she told him; "you’re only sixteen, dear. It’s okay to be upset, to be unsure. And it’s certainly okay to be tired.”

Remus bit down hard on his bottom lip to keep it from trembling. Maybe that was just it. Maybe he needed someone to say it was okay.

Something across the room drew Sheila’s attention and she turned toward it with a brighter smile on her face. “You’re late for your detention, Mr. Black.”

Remus shot upright in his chair and spun around to find Sirius standing there, arms pressed up behind his head awkwardly.

“I didn’t want to interrupt your song,” Sirius murmured, not meeting either of their gazes.

Sheila popped up from the piano bench and began smoothing out her skirts, completely nonchalant. “Well, I was going to make us some tea before I set you to work, but I’m afraid I just ran out of sugar this morning. I’ve been meaning to make a run to the faculty office to pick some up, but I haven’t had the time. Perhaps I’ll go now. Provided you can promise you’ll still be here when I return?”

Sirius nodded slowly and Sheila let her eyes pass over him to Remus. “Alright then,” she hummed. “I’ll be right back. Just in case anyone needs anything.”

She left the room in the same brisk manner with which she played, stopping only to put a comforting hand on Sirius’ shoulder. Remus tried not to pay attention, wiping his reddened cheeks as he turned back to the Fender and attempted to recall what Sheila had said about his fretting. Impossible.

“How do you do it?” Sirius asked, crossing the room and taking a spot back up on the piano bench. He didn’t so much as glance at the piano, just clasped his slender hands in his lap.

“Don’t ask vague questions, they only waste time,” Remus mumbled.

“But it’s like our thing. I ask ‘how do you do it’ and you say ‘do what’ and I say ‘make everyone like you’.”

“Not everyone likes me.”

“I like you.”

“Stop that.”

“See, it is our thing—stop what?”

“Stop throwing words around! You’re like a walking sudoku puzzle.”

“That’s funny, except sudoku uses numbers,” Sirius snorted. “D’you mean words like ‘I like you’ then? ‘Cause I’m not throwing it around, I do like you.”

“Fine. Do you also like Kimmy?”

“Well I should, shouldn’t I? She’s my girlfriend, and she says she likes me.”

Remus bit down hard on his bottom lip. “Is that why you date her then? Because she says she likes you?”

“You say that like it’s odd or something.”

“Well, maybe I’m just odd.”

Sirius raised his chin. “Alright, so you’re odd. Would it be so bad if I were odd too? I wouldn’t like you if you weren’t.”

“You always know just what to say,” Remus said with sarcasm.

“I know, it’s a gift.” Smiling, Sirius spun around on the bench and faced the piano. He just stared down at it as though it were stone rather than a tool for excellence. “You’re odd, Lupin… sort of like a cuckoo clock.”

“… What?”

“You are! You exist in this sort of shell that only ever venture out of at certain times of the day. And when you do, no one ever ignores you. You make yourself heard, but then you’re quick to snap yourself back up again. You’re consistent at least, I’ll give you that. But you know, every time you pop up, I sort of get this little thrill, like ‘oh there he is again’—there’s that Moony! God, he sure is surprising!”

“You’re insane,” Remus mumbled, pressing his chin to his shoulder out of embarrassment.

“Insane, odd—they’re all just synonyms for one another. As far as I’m concerned, that makes us the same.” He looked at him. “And I want to be the same. I do.”

Remus licked his lips. I wish I could make you understand.

“Sirius… did you hear what I was saying when… when Sheila was playing the piano?”

“No. Would it have been better or worse if I did?”

“I don’t know.” He took a deep breath. “But I don’t want to fight anymore.”

Sirius’ shoulders sagged with relief. “Me neither. Does this mean… that you’re not mad anymore?”

“No—or yeah, I'm not mad. Lily—she… she gave me some stuff to think about.”

“Oh…” Sirius looked down at his hands. “That’s good then.”

“Yeah, so… friends again?”

With a tight smile, Sirius nodded. “Always.”

It felt like a weight had been lifted off Remus’ shoulders. He still wasn’t sure what it was about Sirius that cut him so deeply, but if he could at least learn to not be so jealous then just maybe things would go back to the way they were.

“Do you want to practice something?” He asked, making Sirius nod enthusiastically.

“I thought you’d never ask! My god, you should hear James, he’s brilliant! Might be a prodigy himself! C’mon, I left my guitar back at the dorm.”

As Sirius bounded away from the piano and to the door, Remus began to scramble to pack up his things. “I thought you had detention? Sheila told you to be here when she got back,” he said, setting the Fender back into its case and shoving his music sheets back into his bag.

“Eh,” Sirius shrugged, “I’ll give her an I-owe-you or bribe Evans to make her a batch of cookies or something.”

Remus sighed happily as he came to join Sirius by the door. “You think the world bends to you.”

“Au contraire, Lupin, I make the world bend to me. It’s an exhausting task really, perhaps you should try it sometime—give me a break.”

“I’ll get right on that.”

Sirius bounced up and down in place in excitement. “Can’t wait to see it.”

He turned to lead them away, but Remus reached out and grabbed his wrist at the last second, making his own heart jump in surprise.

“Sirius,” he tried as the dark-haired boy whipped back around to look at him; “Are we… Are we missing each other? Like… messing something up? I just feel like maybe something’s been… lost.”

Sirius laughed gently. “How can you have lost me? I’m right here.”

Oh.

Nodding, Remus dropped his arm. “You’re right. I was being odd again. Sorry.”

“S’okay. Now c’mon, let’s go make James and Pete be odd with us.”

“Okay.”

Together they shot out of the Bellchant building, narrowly avoiding Sheila as she made her way back up the street. Remus tried hard to reassure himself; Sirius had said they weren’t missing, so that must’ve meant they were whole.

He wanted to trust him in that, at least.



Chapter End Notes

A 'girl on the blob’ is a girl on her period.

'Vivace' is the musical direction for a fast-paced piece and 'vivacissimo' is just faster than that.

We go through a lot of emotions in this fic, don't we?





Chapter 40: Marlene


Chapter Summary

Remus gets to see a new side of Marlene. Revenge is plotted.



Chapter Notes

CW: Smoking, pining, and organised sports (though that might only be a trigger for Remus, lol)



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Sunshine, lollipops and rainbows,

Everything that’s wonderful is what I feel when we’re together;

Brighter than a lucky penny,

When you’re near the rain goes, disappears, dear;

And I feel so fine,

Just to know that you are mine!

- “Sunshine, Lollipops and Rainbows” Lesley Gore, 1963



Wednesday 1st December 1976

With the spat with Sirius behind him, Remus could finally move forward. There was still Kimmy to contend with of course, but it was at least clear now thanks to her general disdain for him that she’d told Sirius nothing of her proposition. Remus didn’t mind, let her pride save him from further embarrassment. He was just happy to have his friend back, even if it came with a few unsavoury conditions.

On Wednesdays the ninth years had free-rein of the library for study hour, and so Remus met his friends in one of the large private study halls in the Flamel Block. He’d expected they’d all sit and study together as usual, but apparently Lily had other plans. A cheeky smile on her face, she’d secluded him and Marlene at their own table and made it clear to everyone else that he was ‘helping’ Marlene with homework and they ‘were not to be disturbed’.

“She’s just being silly,” Marlene said, “we’re only studying—we always do it together.”

“Mm.”

“Did you hear her going on about how I asked for help with the English homework—what English homework? Professor Flitwick agreed not to assign anything while we read the next novel. She’s just having us on. I only asked for your help to—Remus, are you listening?”

“Mm?”

Marlene followed his gaze and rolled her eyes. “Really, do they have to be so public about it? We actually do have exams to prepare for.”

“ ‘If life’s a stage…’,” Remus murmured, before blinking as he forced himself to look away. Of course he agreed with Marlene; the one time Sirius shows up for private study and all he can do is sit back with Kimmy practically in his lap, their faces stuck together in the middle. Every time a teacher came by James reached over and thumped him in the shoulder, and the pair would separate long enough for the threat to pass before sniggering and returning to their revolting show of public affection.

But, as he was getting better at reminding himself, Sirius’ relationship wasn’t any of his business.

“Honestly, I’m a bit surprised they’ve made it this long,” Marlene went on. “I didn’t think Sirius was Kim’s type. He wears more makeup than she does.”

“He’s not wearing it anymore,” he said simply, reaching for his pen as it rolled away from him across the table.

“He’s not?”

Remus shook his head. It probably would’ve taken a world-ending event for him to admit it aloud, but he secretly missed zoning out on Sirius’ colourful nails as he strummed his Rickenbacker during class or practice. But it didn’t matter, they were talking again, even if Kimmy was now making it plain that she hated him. Not that that mattered—the feeling was mutual, but he was at least thankful that she was subtle about it. Dinner the night before had been one of the first meals they’d shared together since the bonfire, and after another failed project-meeting with Chastity, he and Lily had arrived together at the dining hall to find their table already crowded with friends. While Lily immediately began sharing her woes of Chastity with James, who already had a cup of tea prepared for her which he pushed across the table with a smile, Remus took a seat between her and Moira. It had been almost startling to see their table so full, but as he’d dug into dinner, Remus found he didn’t mind all that much. In fact, he’d missed it.

“You should’ve seen Miss Pince’s face when Remus returned the books and said he’d re-shelve them himself,” Lily started over her chicken and rice.

“I know the cataloging system! Only because of detention…”

“But I’ve never even seen her smile. It was like you’d cast a spell on her or something.”

“A regular casanova,” James chuckled. “Next you’ll have the teachers swooning for you, Lupin.”

“He already does!” Sirius exclaimed, appearing behind Remus and throwing his arms around his shoulders in a great bear-hug. “Pretty sure Sheila’s in love with the handsome prick.”

“Get off,” Remus moaned, and Sirius obeyed, turning to Moira and Peter.

“Oi guys, budge up a bit?” They did so and Sirius slid in next to him along with Kimmy.

“Thanks,” she told Moira lightly, who nodded at the popular sixth former with slightly widened eyes.

“So what’d you decide to play?” Sirius asked, meaning their upcoming performance test in music. He leaned in a bit to hear over the dining hall’s chatter, blocking Remus’ view of Kimmy.

“Sheila suggested I adapt a cello étude to show off technique, but I think I’m just going to find something simpler.”

“Not that that isn’t terribly boring, but why would you want to do something simpler? You’re so good, Moony.”

“Easy for you to say,” Remus shot tamely.

“Well I agree with Remus,” Kimmy started, her voice tight and snooty. “I mean, you’ll be there, Sirius, and who would want to play piano in front of Mozart? Honestly I’d be embarrassed.”

Remus had bitterly thought that it was a stupid analogy—Sirius didn’t even like playing the piano—but Sirius only smiled.

“You give me way too much credit, Kimmy,” he’d said, and then he kissed her and Remus turned to James sharply, interrupting his and Lily’s conversation. As he finished his dinner he felt Sirius’ thigh continuously brush his on the bench and grew even antsier. Being conscious of Sirius Black was a lot like realising your body needed to breathe to survive. Most of the time it was so automatic that there was no reason to question it, but then there were those dreadful moments of self-awareness that you found yourself overthinking—nervous and short of breath as you counted every inhale and exhale and longed to rewind time to thirty seconds before, when you were so blissfully ignorant to it all.

Inhale.

Exhale.

“Remus?”

Inhale.

Exhale.

“Remus are you listening?”

Inhale—

“Remus!”

He straightened up in his chair, fumbling his pen and sending it skittering across the table. “Yeah, I’m listening,” he murmured, fetching it from the floor as he came back to reality.

“Then what did I just say?” Marlene asked.

“You yelled at me for no reason.”

“Ha.” Shaking her head, Marlene went back to her books and Remus watched her. That was one of the things he liked best about Marlene, she never pestered for more. She took exactly what was given and accepted it as fact—there was no digging for extra evidence or emotions. She didn’t pry. It made her the perfect person to tell a secret to, really.

“Hey Marls, if I tell you something, you promise to keep it to yourself?”

Marlene’s head popped up. “Sure, unless you’re asking me to help you hide a body, which in that case I’ll have to at least tell my therapist about it.”

He smiled, before wincing uncomfortably. How did one say ‘my best friend’s girlfriend tried to come onto me’?

“Kimmy… sort of asked me to hook up.”

Well, like that I guess.

Marlene’s jaw dropped. “Oh my god, really? Holy crap, I-I mean—Jesus…”

“Halloween really changed you, didn’t it?” Remus snorted.

“Shut up. I can take the Lord’s name in vain sometimes too. And this, well this bloody deserves it. What did you even say?”

“I said no, obviously! I’m not that insane…”

“Okay, but like, she actually asked you to cheat on Sirius?”

“Well I think in this situation she’d be the cheater not me, but I get your point. And no, not exactly. She sort of suggested that we… all do it.”

He didn’t think Marlene’s eyes could get any bigger. “Woah. I knew Kimmy was like that but damn, that’s ruthless. What’d Sirius have to say?”

“I don’t know!" He squirmed. "She said she hadn’t brought it up to him yet, and I didn’t exactly turn her down lightly, so… I doubt she’d ever admit it now.”

“Well, that’s good then. Problem solved.”

“Just like that...?"

“You said no, right? And Sirius doesn’t know so there’s no weirdness there, unless you think there is…?”

Remus began tapping his pen against his notebook awkwardly. “No, I don’t think so. We had a few spats but I think it’s over with now.”

“Then I guess the only thing left to do is wait for them to break up.”

Marlene’s startling nonchalance might’ve once made him want to crawl inside his own skin with worry, but as he glanced back across the study hall, he found himself more relaxed.

“You’re pretty good at this,” he told her. “But you still can’t tell anybody.”

Marlene smirked. “Give me your dessert at supper and my lips are sealed.”

“Ha, deal.”

Suddenly the low ding of the school bell chimed above their heads, signalling the end of study period. Marlene was out of her chair in an instant, bag swung over one shoulder. “I asked earlier if you brought your stuff with you for today—did you?”

Reaching down, she began to help him gather his books and things, as Remus blinked in confusion. “Er, what stuff?”

“It’s fine if you didn’t, we can just swing by your dorm and get it,” she said, checking her watch.

“Marlene, what stuff?”

“For football. You promised to help me with the team today.”

“I did what? WHEN?”

“The other day—I passed you in the hall and you said, ‘yeah sure’. I figured that meant yes.” Snapping her fingers, Marlene gestured for him to stand and practically pushed him into his winter coat, roughly shoving his knit cap on his head and dropping his bag over his arm. “C’mon,” she said as he dragged his hat up over his eyes, “we only get the pitch before dinner, then we lose it to the boys.”

Grinning, she slapped him on the shoulder playfully and turned, letting her long legs carry her out of the room.

“Marlene, hold on a second!” Remus called, streaking after her. Just as he left, Lily flashed him a beaming smile and a thumbs up.

Marlene was tall and a fast walker, and despite his long stride Remus had to half-jog just to keep up with her. By the time they were marching back up House Lane he’d already passed the initial stages of shock and denial and went straight for bargaining. Marlene, it seemed, would have none of it.

“I know you don’t like football,” she started reasonably, passing Finch House and waving at another girl, “but I couldn’t ask James, he’s already so busy with his own team, and he helps out enough as is. Plus, half of the other boys are just as likely to laugh in my face if I'd asked them to play with us.”

“Why not Sirius then? He's loads better than me at sports.”

“I think he’s also a little tied up sticking his tongue down Kim Bishop’s throat.”

“And Peter?”

“Are you serious?”

“C’mon Marls, anyone but me! You have a whole school to choose from.”

“But you promised.”

“And you tricked me! Stopping someone to ask for a favour and then rushing off to class before you tell them what it is they’re agreeing to isn’t fair.”

“Life’s not fair, Remus. If it were, I’d have been born with looks like Mary, brains like Lily, and confidence like Lottie’s.”

“You’ve already got all those things and then some.”

“Ha, you’re sweet,” Marlene said, marching away. As she did, it struck Remus that her quip was more than just sarcasm—she really didn’t believe he thought she was just as good as the rest of their friends. Without letting himself think, he reached forward and grasped Marlene’s wrist, pulling her to a stop in the middle of the path. She whipped around, nearly lashing him in the face with her ponytail.

“I meant it,” he said firmly, before quickly releasing her wrist. Marlene glanced down before smiling reluctantly.

“Sure, Remus.”

“I did.”

“Okay.”

“I did!”

“Alright, I believe you!”

Remus shoved his hands in his pockets awkwardly, embarrassed by his outburst. “Well… good. You’re smart and pretty and tough—people should envy you, really. I do, when you're not dragging me to football practice, that is.”

Marlene began gnawing on her bottom lip before a smile finally peeked through. “Thanks, Remus.”

“Mhm,” he nodded gently, before noticing a small leaf had gotten caught in her hair. Reaching up, he plucked it out and twirled it in between his fingers in front of her nose. Marlene’s smile widened and for a moment it was contagious, until they were interrupted.

“I know chavs are generally too stupid to remember where they are half the time, but some of us actually have places to be.”

Remus turned to find Snape standing behind them, rucksack over one shoulder, rumpled sneer on his face. Unfortunately the dorm he’d chosen to stop and reinforce Marlene’s self-esteem in front of was not neutral ground. Just behind Snape, the great grey stone of Salazar House loomed, its serpentine insignia highlighting every surface.

Remus sighed, instantly irritated as he stepped back from Marlene. “Snape, has anyone ever told you that you have a special talent for magic? You make smiles disappear.”

“I’d almost believe that were clever if it weren’t coming from you, Scarface,” Snape said, standing comfortably on the end of his House’s stone walkway. He was clearly enjoying what he thought was a home-field advantage.

“Oh shove off, Snape,” Marlene hissed. “No one asked for your opinion anyway.”

Snape curled his lip, unfazed. “That’s right, don’t mind me, I’m just on my way to dinner. I really hope passing this much rubbish on the way doesn't ruin my appetite.”

Remus crossed his arms over his chest. “I would’ve thought you’d have an iron stomach, what with all the foul crap you regurgitate on a daily basis.”

“You’re right, I’m being completely unrealistic. You’re not rubbish, you’re scum.”

“Stop talking to us like that!” Marlene shouted.

“You were barely tolerable before, McKinnon, and now you’re hanging around with low-rents like him. Kill any more cops lately, Lupin?”

Remus scowled but it was Marlene who stepped forward first. “As if your family comes from royalty!” She shot.

“Better than the gutter.”

“Which is where, Severus? In Liverpool? Where your father is no doubt having to lay off dock workers left and right? Where they’re considering a strike that would leave your family with nothing? Tell me, how lucrative is a shipping dock no one can use?”

Snape turned a deep shade of red, a blood vessel threatening to burst in his forehead. “You don’t know what you’re talking about.”

“Then enlighten me! You’re the one who picked the fight, so how is it you’re so much better than us when your position at this school is more precarious than anyone’s? Remus is miles better than you, and you’re just jealous.”

“Fuck off.” Going around them, Snape began to march off, but Marlene wasn’t finished, shouting after him;

“You’re a coward Snape! You have nothing better to do than rag on anyone who dares have a good day in your presence because you wouldn’t know goodness if it smacked you upside the head! You’re just bitter because people like Remus are smarter, richer, kinder, more handsome, and better in every way—while you’re just pathetic.”

Slamming to a halt, Snape spun back around and advanced on them, lip lifted in a snarl. But Remus was also bigger, and he stepped between them before Snape even got close, armed with a deadly look of his own. “Just try it,” he dared him, and Snape’s nostrils flared as he pulled back.

“You’ll get yours eventually, you skiver. I know people who could make that scar look like a paper cut.”

Remus casually rubbed his nose to mock him. “If you reckon you can do any better, you’re welcome to try.”

Straightening up, Snape clutched at his bag strap and glared at them both, finally muttering another quick; ‘fuck off,’ before retreated back up the path away from them.

Unfortunately that merciless force also extended to those same friends as well.

He supposed he could do that much.

“Means they’re gonna fight you for the ball,” she answered. “Try to keep it from them, and do stay strong, Lupin.”

“Oi,” he started, “Marlene—!”

“Her middle name's Grace if that helps!” Nicole called innocently.

“Er—Marlene Grace McKinnon—!”

Defeated, he shut his mouth and the entire team giggled. A moment later Michelle’s whistle blew and the first of them raced forward.

“C’mon, Remus,” Michelle shouted encouragingly, “don’t make it too easy on them.”

“Now that’s just sad!” Marlene sighed dramatically, making everyone snigger again.

“You can do it, Remus!” Nicole added kindly, just before high-fiving Anna as she returned to the drill line-up.

The next girl also had no trouble snatching the ball from him, but by the third Remus at least sort of understood the point of the drill. He did his best to keep the ball between his heels, awkwardly dancing around each player until they inevitably took it from him. Thankfully, the longer they went at it the easier it got and eventually he was able to keep the ball away from them for a considerable length of time, creating a clog in the drill’s line-up.

“You’re getting cocky, Remus,” Nicole laughed, just as she used the side of her foot to knock it from between his legs.

“So he can run?” Marlene shouted tauntingly.

“He can!” Remus declared. “He can also—”

Marlene never got to hear what it was that Remus could also do, as the moment he reached the ball again she was there, sliding—actually sliding, on her side and everything—beneath him to knock the football away. Remus tripped over her and turned mid-air, slamming onto his side on the green turf and rolling onto his back with a low moan to stare up at the gym roof. “You okay, Rem?” She asked. “I didn’t damage you too badly, did I?” Her ponytail slipped over her head to dangle down above him and he stared at her, slightly transfixed, although that might’ve just been a repercussion of being knocked on his arse.

“I guess you hit your head after all.”

“Nah. I’m fine.” Reaching out, Remus took her outstretched hand and climbed to his feet next to her, dusting off his shorts. “Thanks.”

Marlene nodded, sheepishly pressing her knuckles to her cheeks and muttering; “Don’t mention it.”

Instantly the rest of the team, who had abandoned their other drills to watch, began erupting into ‘oohs’ and whistles that had her looking up, redder than before. “Okay, cut that out!” She ordered, but the girls only grinned guiltily.

“You’re blushing, Marlene!”

“Nicole!”

“You are!”

Marlene began marching toward her and Nicole jumped away, dancing around the crowd of girls to keep the distance between herself and the team captain. It was amusing to note that he wasn’t the only person at Hawkings who had their own ‘Sirius Black’ to contend with.

“Look, it’s the boys!” One of the girls called suddenly, and the entire team turned as a single unit, crowding into one another as the Hawkings’ boys team emerged on the field in their pads and football boots, dispersing to the benches to drop down their bags and towels. With an irritated sigh, Marlene gave up chasing Nicole and walked up to the boys, who were of course led by their own captain, James. They knocked knuckles, a gesture Remus had never seen Marlene reciprocate off the field, and Marlene began flapping the front of her uniform for air.

“Sorry Potter, didn’t mean to run long. We’ll clean up now.”

“S’fine McKinnon. You can stay if you want even, we’re just running drills today too.” James looked up and casually tossed Remus a wave when he noticed him. “Hey, Lupin.”

“Hey, Potter. Thought you had Slug Club stuff tonight?”

“Nah, that's tomorrow,” James said with a friendly nod. Casually, he looked back to Marlene before his smile abruptly fell and he snapped back to Remus. “Lupin?! On the football field? YOU TRAITOR!”





* * *





It was rather hard to detach himself from James, who didn’t seem to believe that he’d been forced onto the field against his will, but Remus managed to duck out before he could call him a ‘seditious Judas’ and ended up joining the girls for a late dinner in the dining hall. They were as rowdy as any boys team, tossing napkins this way and that, but off the field Marlene easily relinquished her hold as captain overseer and let Michelle turn into the mother hen, making sure that each girl had drunk enough water to drown a small mammal.

“We’re going to watch a movie together in the theatre room after if you’re interested,” Marlene said, polishing off Remus' chocolate pudding.

Both Anna and Nicole had overheard and stared at him with expectant eyes until he’d finally given in.

“What movie?” He asked, defeated. Marlene shrugged, but Anna intercepted easily.

“Penny got a hold of a copy of ‘Rosemary’s Baby’ from her older sister. We can set it up on the projector.”

“That sounds nice,” Marlene said. “What is it, like a romantic comedy?”

The American ‘R’ rated film was certainly not a romantic comedy. Marlene spent most of it hiding behind her hands or with her face pressed into his or Nicole’s shoulder, squirming at the more gruesome parts as the other girls shrieked with terror or delight.

“You’re never picking the movie again,” Marlene told Penny when it was over.

Remus waited until her back was turned to shuffle over to Penny and nudge her. "I thought it was great," he whispered, giving her a sly high-five.

He said his goodbyes to the girls outside his own dorm. On his way inside he was stopped by another boy who told him he’d missed a call and when Remus checked the hallway board where they took messages and posted school notices he found not Giles’ name but Tomny’s (well—‘Tommy’, but still). Elated, Remus fumbled for one of the phones and eagerly dialled the flat’s number, biting his lip as the call went long-distance and began to ring. Since their first call in October Tomny had reached out a small handful of times, but the conversations were unpredictable and often shorter than he would’ve liked. They didn’t talk about the weather again though, and Tomny seemed generally upbeat (Tonya was always upbeat) which probably meant that the ‘holistic healing’ thing was now old hat.

It was Doss who picked up the phone, which made Remus a bit uneasy, mostly because he hadn’t spoken to the older boy since Tomny had told him Doss was the only other person that knew he’d been lying about his family. But of course Doss was as friendly as ever, asking him “How’s tricks?” and filling him in on every stupid and ingenious thing Lee had done since they’d seen each other.

Eventually Doss passed the phone along and he got his familiar “hey Lu” and “hello, sweet love”. Tomny and Tonya seemed alright, though all the flowers that Tonya had been cultivating on their balcony had died as soon as the winter air had rolled in and she was disappointed over it. As per usual the call became a three-way conversation, with both Tonya and Tomny speaking over each other but never getting irritated by it. Remus pictured them cuddled together on the couch or Tomny’s patchwork recliner with the receiver tucked between their heads. They laughed when he told them about Marlene and her team (“Thought you hated football, Lu?”) and Tonya talked music for a bit, excited by the new album Queen was supposed to drop later that month.

Through it all they did not talk about Christmas, as they hadn’t since Tonya had planted the seed in Remus’ head just before Halloween. Their silence on the matter seemed so loud that Remus found himself unable to even bridge the topic, just as he had every other phone call since, and after they’d said goodbye to one another he set the receiver down and snatched Tomny’s name off the message board, crumpling the note in the palm of his hand.

The following evening while Peter entertained Moira in their dorm room (“Oh, piss off Black, we’re only playing cards. And even if we weren’t it’s none of your business!”) and the rest of his friends attended Slughorn’s club to let him lecture on about the fascinations of chemical reactions or otherwise, Remus took it upon himself to retire to the astronomy building for a bit of alone time. He’d only visited his favourite spot a few times since the start of the term, and it remained the only portion of his map he had yet to share with his friends. It was peaceful, and he took his bass and a bit of the weed they’d procured from Xeno and sat with the door cracked just enough for the smoke to escape. The telescope’s vast, empty room felt like the perfect place to write songs—not that Remus was, but he imagined that Sirius would find it utterly inspirational to listen to the way every note seemed to reverberate off the domed walls.

Since returning to school Sirius’ songwriting had taken a strong up-turn. No longer was he obsessing over angry metaphors or bitter wishes, and instead he wrote whatever he wanted, whenever he wanted. Remus’ favourite so far was this short composition Sirius was calling “Backtrack Children”. It only had a chorus, but it reminded him of his boys back home—especially the line 'Skid Row’s regular Romeo'. It felt romantic in a heavy way, like the dirty sort of rock ‘n’ roll Sirius so desperately wanted to embody, despite growing up a proper, high-class English boy.

“It’s like writing a letter,” Sirius had told him one evening, chin pressed to the side of Andy’s acoustic guitar. “You just gotta decide who you’re writing to.”

“Yeah well, not all of us can speak in lyrics, Black.”

Sirius had said nothing to that, only bit his lip and scribbled something in his notebook.

It felt good to inspire him at least. They may have only been playing at starting a band—a joke which James had encouraged since he’d agreed to let Sirius teach him the guitar—but Sirius was the only one of them that was actually interested in pursuing music, and if Remus could contribute at all to any of it, even just a single note or lyric, that would be enough.

Just before curfew, he gathered his things and made his way back to the dorm. Unlocking the door he walked in to find his roommates surrounding James’ bed and staring down at the same textbook.

“Not sure that’s what they mean when they call it ‘group study’,” Remus said, as his friends glanced up.

“Moony! You gotta—” Peter started, before Sirius reached over him and snatched the book up from the covers.

“Moony! Moony! Moony! Moony! Come look at this!”

Setting down his instrument case, Remus crossed the room and Sirius shoved the textbook into his hands. “Chemistry? Uh, hate to break it to you, but I don’t take chem.”

“It’s Snape’s,” James sniggered. “Sirius lifted it out of his bag during tonight’s club meeting.”

“No way.” One by one Remus began flipping through the pages, finding scribbles in every other margin of different equations or notes on chemical properties and the like.

“He carries the thing around like a bible,” Peter grinned, “ten quid he notices it missing immediately and throws a historic fit.”

“Well, that would be something,” Remus said, snapping the book closed and handing it back.

“You’re missing the best part though,” Sirius insisted, taking the book and flipping it back open. “I only thought it would inconvenience him, but I think the slimy git just handed us the key to our revenge against my darling baby brother.”

“What do you mean?”

Turning the book around for Remus to see, he pointed to a single scribble Snape had left in a margin next to a list of chemical reactions and stood back, locking his arms behind him like an innocent bystander.

“Moony, my dear, have you ever heard of a thiol?”

Chapter 41: A Rather Rancid Revenge


Chapter Summary

Ah, the classic stink bomb. Yes, good.



Chapter Notes

CW: Light homophobic language.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



See the years roll on by,

Such a senseless waste of time;

What a way to reform,

Call out your number;

Who’s a non-conformer,

Not me baby, oh yeah!

- “Borstal Boys” Faces, 1973



Friday 3rd December 1976

It had taken a few days of study but eventually they’d worked out how they were going to return Sirius’ birthday favour to Reg and his friends. Of course though, it hadn’t been enough to consider only pranking the four of them. After some eager propaganda from Sirius, it was now looking like all of Salazar House was to bear the brunt of their rancid revenge. That was if Professor Slughorn ever stopped talking.

“So you see Lumby, every hydrogen atom in your body is likely over thirteen billion years old because every hydrogen atom was created at the very beginning of the universe.”

“Uh-huh.”

“And even that had to wait another three hundred and eighty years for the universe to cool after the Big Bang.”

“Cool…”

“Yes, very cool! Cool enough for hydrogen and helium to form. The very first elements!”

Professor Slughorn beamed at him, and Remus just blinked back. He thought agreeing to keep watch would mean he’d have to think less about the prank, which involved several chemicals and accelerants (of the non-poisonous kind—they checked) that he could barely pronounce, but he hadn’t counted on Hawkings’ chemistry teacher paying a evening visit to his classroom when everyone was supposed to be at dinner. The others had had just enough time to throw themselves into a classroom storage closet as Remus had scrambled to pull his lock-picks from the supply cupboard when Slughorn had strode in. He’d been initially surprised to find him there alone, but after some quick excuses on Remus’ part, was all too willing to launch into a lecture on the differences between hydrogen sulphate and hydrogen sulphide.

“I’m sorry, Lumby,” Professor Slughorn started, dropping his deep-set brow, “was there something you wanted to ask? I don’t believe I have you in any of my classes, do I?”

“Oh no,” Remus tried, wetting his lips, “I was just trying to come up with an interesting research topic for my end of term history paper, but after our chat I’m confident that I wouldn’t be able to do the universe much justice.”

“Nonsense, you seem to be a good listener. How are those notes going?”

Remus snapped down to the notepad he’d been pretending to scribble on. “Oh I…”

Slughorn checked his watch. “Great snakes, is that the time? Best be getting on now, else you’ll miss curfew.”

Remus nodded and let himself be guided out of the classroom, down the hallway, and into the chilly night. After saying goodbye to Slughorn, he walked down the pavement a bit and hid in the bushes until his friends spilled out after them into the dark, all of them giggling like school girls.

“Now where was that acting on Halloween?” Sirius demanded, spotting Remus as he stepped into the light of a street lamp with his hands in his pockets.

“Up your arse.”

“You tell him, Lumby,” James grinned.

Remus scowled. “You get everything?”

“Oh yeah,” James said, as he and Peter showed off the boxes they were carrying. Inside were dozens of empty glass or plastic bottles gathered from the kitchen’s rubbish bins, balloons, duct tape, bicarb soda—everything they would need for the prank, at least according to the Snape’s notes.

“Think we should test it?” Peter asked, looking down into the box.

James nodded. “Yeah, but not in our bedroom. As long as Snivellus hasn’t led us astray then the smell is going to stick around for a while.”

“Only if we do it right,” Sirius said. “But really, how bad could it stink?”

The answer was fucking bad.

Together they had made their way back inside the Galilei Block, up to the third floor and down the furthest hallway to a girls toilet. The bathroom was always empty thanks to a rumour that it was haunted—one Sirius was all too willing to embellish.

“Apparently some year ten girl literally gave up the ghost in here,” he sniggered. “A snake crawled up the toilet pipes and bit her right on the arse.”

“We’re on the third floor,” Remus scoffed.

“Snakes can climb.”

After James had reassured Peter that Sirius was full of shit and there were no snakes hiding in the pipes waiting to bite his nob off, they got to work on a bit of trouble-shooting and were able to come up with a device that appeared as little more than a plastic water bottle with a balloon duct taped to its top. The ammonium sulphide that would make the bomb stink had been put in the bottle’s base along with the other liquid ingredients, while the bicarb soda—effectively the ignition to the prank—was stuffed into the top of the balloon and left to hang down over the rim to keep the two separated.

They tested it three times, escaping out into the hall to avoid the stench as each balloon burst with a sharp bang that echoed throughout the building. They were eyeballing the ingredients for the most part, which meant every bomb had a varying time limit before the gas build-up would cause the balloon to burst. Each one smelled absolutely horrid and by round three Remus was convinced he’d never be able to smell anything pleasant again. Naturally, they were all thrilled.

With several dozen of the bombs in hand, they packed up the rest of their supplies and loped back to the dorms, sticking the shadows to avoid getting caught out after hours. They had to move agonisingly slow so as to not risk upsetting any of their monstrous concoctions early and by the time they were making their way down House Lane it was getting mighty close to midnight.

“Lucky Kenny isn’t as much of a curfew stickler as Benjy was,” Peter said, checking his watch for the dozenth time.

Sirius gasped; “Imagine if one of us became dorm monitor next year—think of the pranking opportunities! You should do it, Potter.”

“Why me? I’m already spending all my free time with you and that bloody guitar, where would I possibly fit in looking after a whole dorm of nobs?”

“Maybe you’d be able to do it if you weren’t putting so many extra hours in at the library. Who’d have known dating Evans would come with a lifetime subscription of ‘shhh’.”

James puckered. “Mind your business.”

“Hmph.”

“Are we doing this or do you girls need more time to have it out?” Remus asked. They’d made it to Salazar House, where most of the lights were dim and quiet.

“No, we’re doing this,” Sirius said. “Everyone remember the plan?”

They all nodded; Sirius and James would take the upper hallways, starting at the second floor and working their way up to the fourth while Remus and Peter filled the kitchenette and common room with enough bombs to fumigate Australia. Fifteen minutes later, at exactly midnight, they’d start tipping the bicarb soda filled balloons into each bottle and leg it out of the dorm. No one was to escape unscathed; if any of them were caught before then they’d hoot twice like a barn owl (according to James this sounded a lot like a ‘HOOOOOHHH-HOOOOOHHH’) and once like a screech owl (‘REEAAAAHHH’) and trigger any bomb within reach. James did admit afterwards that he had no idea what sound either animal actually sounded like but his impressions had them in stitches anyway.

Once they’d stopped killing themselves with laughter, it was time to go to work. Carefully they carried the boxes up Salazar’s front steps and slipped inside, checking that the coast was clear before they crossed the main hallway and split off at the staircase, eager to exact their revenge.

“You cover the kitchen,” Remus said, “I’ve got the common.”

“Hope the boys in green enjoy the smell of rotten eggs and arse,” Peter murmured giddily before slipping away into the dark with his stink bombs in hand while Remus carried the rest of the box into the common room. The space felt distinctly un-cozy compared to Godric, decorated with cold wooden flooring, dark leather couches, and emerald-green curtains that reminded him of the window coverings in his bedroom back in London. He set a bomb behind each, knowing that the horrible smell would cling to the heavy fabric for ages and left more under the couches and tables, as well as tucked in behind plant pots (sulphur didn’t kill plants right?), and even one inside the chest cavity of a tacky suit of armour. By the time he was finished there were more than a dozen bottles scattered throughout the Salazar common room. They’d be airing the place out for weeks.

“Pete?” Remus called quietly into the hall. He found Peter setting up a row of bombs just outside the entryway to the kitchenette, barely a shape in the darkness.

“Almost done,” Peter said. “You set it all up?”

“Yeah. What time is it?”

Peter checked his watch. “Oh shit, it’s midnight now.”

“Already? Damn it, okay, just start—”

Before he could finish Peter was already tipping the first balloon’s worth of bicarb soda into the bottle ahead of him. There was a fizzing sound, and the balloon slowly started to inflate. Remus turned and dashed back into the common room, doing his best to remember where he’d left each of the bombs. He ended up accidentally punting one across the room when he missed it in the darkness and flinched at the sharp sound of the glass bottle shattering somewhere, but managed to get to the rest. As he carefully skirted back into the hallway to meet Peter, his heart was hammering so loudly in his ears it sounded like a bass beat.

“Where are they?” Peter demanded, practically dancing in place as he eyed the filling balloons in the hallway around them. The bombs looked incredibly stupid, like tiny hot-air balloons made by toddlers, but they already knew better than to underestimate their power.

“They should be making their way down by now,” Remus said, equally as antsy.

“Maybe they got caught?”

“Didn’t hear James’ hoot. Let’s go get them and get out of here.”

Chapter 42: Winter Aches


Chapter Summary

The boys have made up... just in time for another problem to present itself. And present it does.



Chapter Notes

CW: Implied sexual references.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Have pity on the young man,

They ain’t got nothin’ in the world these days, I said;

They ain’t got nothin’!

They got sweet fuck-all!



- “Young Man Blues” The Who, 1970



There was no denying it: he’d utterly wasted November. The prank with the lads had been proof of that. The time Remus had spent being mad at Sirius could’ve been put towards putting shits like Snape and Barty in their place. They could’ve been spent on music, or actually studying for his exams like he’d meant for. In reality, Remus had spent more time in the library than ever and yet between his constant worrying and bad mood, none of it had sunk in. It was the greatest waste of his sixteen years of life.

And so, as the November chill gave way to the fluffy snowfalls of December, Remus told himself he’d do better. He’d get some real studying done, hang out with his friends like he was meant to, not just because he was avoiding one of them. Except, the final month of term came with a few more unforeseen circumstances, one of which being the revelation that while he’d been off being bitter and snarly, James Potter had proved himself a more than capable guitarist. In fact, their first real practice session in the dorm had left Remus’ jaw on the floor.

“I know right?!” Sirius said, practically vibrating with delight.

Remus could hardly believe it. Where Sirius’ playing ranged from delicate and bewitching to furious and erratic, James had found a home right in the middle. He was charming and humble and yet his careful fingers danced up and down the strings as gracefully as a ballerina. It would’ve been captivating without any sound at all.

“Wow,” Remus had said when James had drawn his song to a finish. “That was… amazing.”

“Thanks, Moony,” James smiled shyly.

Remus looked down at his lap, where the Fender sat abandoned between his legs. He suddenly felt the need to busy his fingers with anything other than playing.

“I think your E-string sounds a bit out of tune though,” he said, gesturing to the acoustic, “how ‘bout I—”

“Oh, no it’s okay, I got it,” James said, flipping the head toward himself and fiddling with the tuning keys.

“He picked that up fast too,” Sirius said. “Looks like we’ll have a real band soon!”

He hated himself for it, but the next time either of them asked him to play, Remus made up an excuse and escaped down to the common room.

This is what you wanted. If you’re missing out, it’s your own fault, a nasty voice would ring. Your fault! Your fault! La-la! La-la!

But he’d already missed out. When Andy’s guitar had first shown up in the mail and James agreed to learn a few chords, he’d been just as excited as Sirius; they’d found yet another addition to the bolshie cult that was rock and roll. He had no idea at the time how their dynamic would shift. Now why that would bother him so badly in the first place, Remus still wasn’t sure. What he was sure of, was the exact moment it became apparent that he no longer needed Sirius’ extra tutelage with the bass.

After the stink-bomb incident, the school’s supply of tomato juice, paste, pie—anything that could get the smell out—had been exhausted and the only four non-Salazar students who smelt of steaming rubbish had been effectively pinned for the prank. Sadly for those like Snape who were praying for a more public downfall, the Hawkings’ statute of limitations had played in their favour. Rather than being hung from Castle Hall by their thumbs, each of them served a light two-week detention sentence with their forms teachers before they were freed to ensure they still had plenty of time to study for their examinations.

Come their final weekend of indentured servitude, Mrs. Buchanan was promptly absent and her place had been filled by some flighty secretary who was more than content to leave them alone in the music room while she smoked and read gossip rags down the hall. He and Sirius were supposed to be polishing the brass instruments, but the moment the secretary popped her gum and strode away they’d both reached for their guitars. It was the first time they’d been alone with their music since before Sirius’ birthday, and Remus was so elated by this fact that his fingers played every note like a reflex. They managed “While My Guitar Gently Weeps” all the way through perfectly on their first try and on top of it all, they sounded good.

Rickenbacker in hand, Sirius danced up and down the orchestra risers with his tie unlaced and his shirt open to the third button. “That was bloody brilliant!” He’d declared when they finished.

“It did sound cool, didn’t it?” Remus bragged, suddenly desperate for Sirius’ praise.

“You’re a dab hand—a real musician! Now just imagine how cool it’ll sound with another guitar.”

And that was that.

As long as Remus was a real musician, Sirius was free to throw himself into teaching James, which he did whole-heartedly and with enough vigour even Peter was tempted to join in—though he still refused to admit it. By the time exams were upon them their private practices had become virtually nonexistent, traded instead for studying that left Remus’ brain more sore than ever. Often he would return to the room after studying with the girls to find the two of them practising, and though they would always welcome him, he had begun to see a wall go up between them, brick by invisible brick. Sirius had found a new hobby-project in James, and Remus, though now more advanced as a musician, had lost his place as musical confidant.

During the moments he felt most reasonable, Remus thought to himself that it was only natural; Sirius and James were best friends and had known each other as long as they could remember—brothers in almost every sense. They deserved to find pleasure in each other's talent. It helped some to remind himself that after Kimmy’s oh-so-public dumping Sirius had been left more than a bit rattled—people didn’t just dump guys like him—and was just looking for the next best distraction, but still it stung. Stung worse even than the times Sirius had skipped out and disappeared with Stacy, his brief fancy after Kim that hadn’t lasted more than a week and a half but succeeded in propelling his cheeky reputation even further into the school’s stratosphere. Since after all, Stacy had been one of Kim’s best friends. Apparently dating one's ex was club-exclusive.

Not that it mattered—Mary had already generously informed him and anyone who'd stop to listen that Sirius and another girl named Vivian had been caught snogging behind the football stands.

With nothing else to do Remus threw himself back into school work, determined that he would at least be able to get Sirius to look his way when they received their exam results. He told himself that the competition he’d constructed in his head was to make up for Sirius making a fool out of him the year before, but he couldn’t deny the part of him that missed the connection that had originally belonged to only the two of them. If cigarettes had gotten him in the door with Tomny, the key to Sirius was music.

He was suddenly aware of how chapped his lips were, and his stomach felt weird, and—

Oh no… no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no!

Remus squeezed his eyes shut.

Stomach.

He opened them, trying his hardest to recall anything even moderately disgusting. The stink-bomb stench, the way Snape’s nose hairs curled at the ends, kissing McGonagall’s bare feet—

“I’m definitely going to make you sing this time,” Sirius called, looping the Rickenbacker’s strap over his shoulder and turning around with a pick in his mouth. “Even if it’s just the ‘oooh’ bit. And you gotta do the high note—like your balls haven’t dropped.”

Balls. Nob. Skin. Stomach?

“Fuck.”

Sirius looked up from his guitar. “Moons?”

“Yeah! Sorry! I’m just gonna—I-I’m gonna go to the loo first.”

Keeping his back to Sirius, Remus waddled into their bathroom, slamming the door behind him and throwing the bolt into place. He had only a few seconds to breathe before Sirius knocked.

“Yeah—yeah, fine!”

“No, just give me a minute…" He needed noise. "Er—play the record maybe? I think I’ve forgotten the bridge bit. Just need to hear it and I’ll be good.”

He looked around desperately, just as a record scratch sounded from outside the bathroom door and Queen began playing in their bedroom, followed by a great 'ooooh!'

Dropping his head back against the door, Remus let out a short groan. “Please, please don’t. Just shut up you idiot…”

But there it was. Sirius began to sing along, possibly even louder than usual to ensure that he’d hear it from inside the bathroom.

“Ooh, you make me live! Whatever this world can give to me, it’s you, you’re all I see! Ooh, you make me live now, honey! Ooh, you make me live!”

Fuck it, Remus thought in frustration; He can wait then, the bastard.

Thursday, 16th December 1976

Any problem could be avoided if one tried hard enough. Unfortunately, Sirius Black wasn’t just a simple problem, he was a personified predicament.

A second ‘incident’ popped up during their geography exam, leaving not only Remus’ sanity to suffer as a result, but surely his marks as well. It was freezing in the Great Hall, but he’d still had to remove his jumper midway through the test to cover his lap after an essay question pertaining to the ‘rolling plains of East Africa’ had left him unable to think about anything other than the curve and dip of Sirius’ pale stomach. It wasn't even the boners themselves that had him frazzled—he'd been insatiable at fourteen, once popping a woody after a school matron had praised him for being so good about his yearly check-up—it was the fact that they'd been spurned by none other than one of his bestest friends.

Everyone has a stomach, this doesn't mean it's about HIS stomach, he tried telling himself. But then, no one's stomach looks like his.

It was so stupid. Remus was positive that if Sirius ever caught wind of it he'd pitch himself off the roof of the astronomy building.

As always Sirius had finished the exam first and was waiting around outside when Remus marched out, his cheeks already splotched with red.

“There’s my little bookworm,” Sirius called, tucking his chilled hands under his armpits as he fell into step next to him. “How’d it go?”

“Fine,” Remus mumbled gruffly, keeping his eyes on the ground.

“So you reckon you’ve got this one bagged then? I know you’re trying to beat me, and I swear I won’t hold back. That’d just hurt your pride, hey?”

“Great. See you later.”

“Woah, hold on. What’s the rush?” Sirius grabbed his arm, and Remus flinched back sharply.

“I’ve just got something to do, okay!” He snapped, and Sirius stared at him until the red spread further down his neck. “Sorry. I—I really gotta return this book to Lily, so you should… wait for James.”

It felt wrong to blame Sirius for a problem that was so clearly his, but even when he managed to avoid the more physical reactions, Remus was unable to concentrate. He laid awake at night drowning in intrusive thoughts he normally would’ve been able to read or study through. Music might’ve helped, but there was no way he was going to cross their bedroom in the middle of the night and camp out mere inches from Sirius’ bed.

Things had only got worse the more Sirius tried to get his attention. He’d become awfully handsy since dating Kimmy, which made sense since they’d hardly kept their hands off one another, and every time he came close to touching him Remus had to resist the urge to pull away. Then, as if everything else weren’t enough, Sirius would play the most distracting songs he could think of every chance he got; as though he was unknowingly trying to punish Remus for his indiscretions. On the same evening of their failed practice session, he’d played “Why Don’t We Do It in the Road?” on repeat under the guise that the cassette got stuck in the tape deck. That did not go over so well with James, who like Remus, had been suitably anxious over his exams—though he doubted he had to worry about rolling plains in Africa and stiff peaks elsewhere. The reality was that Remus needed a distraction from his distraction or he was going to fail every test he took.

After abandoning Sirius on the front steps of the Great Hall, he trudged down the snowy lane to the girls’ dorm and began tossing small pebbles at their window until Marlene’s face appeared and she stuck her head out into the cold.

“Just bringing back Lily’s study guide for MFL,” Remus said, holding up the booklet.

“Okay, bring it up,” Marlene said, and he hopped on the slick electrical box to stretch up to the edge of the window. They were almost nose-to-nose.

“Lily not in?”

“No, it’s just me actually,” Marlene said with a tone of disappointment. “Mary was supposed to be around, but she said this morning that Laurence MacGregor had been eyeing her up during their exam. I doubt she’ll be back any time soon.”

“Oh.”

“Mhm.” She took the notes, and sheepishly traced her finger along the binding. “So… Do you want to come in?”

Remus immediately thought of Sirius. A distraction from his distraction.

“Yup, sure.”

Smiling, Marlene drew back and let him pull himself inside. He knocked the snow off his boots on the ledge and she carried them into the bathroom before they could drip across the carpet while he slid the window closed after himself. It was nice and warm inside the girls’ rooms, trunks already open and lined up against the wall in preparation for Christmas holiday.

“Tea?” Marlene offered. “I made it for Mary, but she’s not gonna drink it. Should still be warm. I can put some music on too if you’d like.”

“Please.” Shucking off his coat, Remus looked around before deciding to settle down on the floor between Marlene and Lottie’s beds, leaning his back up against one of the hutches.

“I’ll spare you from any ABBA,” Marlene said, setting an album on Mary’s turntable. Remus smiled a bit, and a second later Joni Mitchell was playing.

“This okay?”

“Yeah sure, s’great,” Remus said, as she tucked herself up onto her bed and passed him a cup of tea. “Joni Mitchell’s… cool.”

“I think so too,” Marlene gushed. “I like ‘Ladies of the Canyon’ best… I think listening to her is what falling in love must feel like.”

“That sap, he never told me that.”

“It’s cute to think they can finally say how much they like each other.”

“Mhm.” Remus raised his cup to his lips.

“You don’t have to pay any attention to what Lily’s been saying, you know,” Marlene said suddenly, making him pause.

“You mean like the—”

“Yeah, she… she’s just being silly. She’s got it in her head that you and I… well, I dunno. Don’t worry about it if it makes you uncomfortable.”

“I’m not uncomfortable,” Remus said, choosing his next words carefully; “I… like you, Marlene.”

“Oh.”

“I mean, you’re a great friend.”

“Oh, yeah you too.”

He resisted the urge to smack himself in the forehead. Idiot.

While Marlene lifted her cup to her lips, looking anywhere but at him, Remus did the same and instantly frowned at the tea’s bitter taste. No sugar.

“Oh that’s right,” Marlene chuckled lightly, “I forgot you preferred your tea as sweet as lemonade in summer. You’d probably be able to tell me exactly how much sugar is in each cup down to the gram.”

“Ha, probably..."

With a funny look, Marlene stood up from her bed and plucked his teacup from his hand. “I’ll be back with something sweeter,” she said, lifting the tray and making for the door.

“No Marls, it’s fine, really.”

“It’s not a bother, you just sit tight.”

As the door fell closed behind her, Remus relaxed against the hutch and listened.

‘Oh honey you turn me on,

I’m a radio;

I’m a country station,

I’m a little bit corny;

I’m a wildwood flower,

Waving for you—’

He closed his eyes, smiling to himself. “Oh Potter, you’re so getting bullied for this one.”

When Marlene finally returned, he was in the middle of changing the album, sorting through the girls’ collection after being pleasantly surprised. “Who’s got the Genesis album?” He asked, turning around to find Marlene standing there with enough tea mugs for an entire party. “What are you doing?”

“An experiment! Come sit down.”

“It’s a blind taste-test,” she said, gesturing to the cups. “Close your eyes and see if you can guess how many teaspoons of sugar I put in each one.”

“Why?”

“Oh, indulge me, we’ve got nothing better to do. Unless you wanted to study some more?”

He didn’t, so he closed his eyes and let Marlene push the first cup into his hand. This one tasted how James usually took his tea. “Two.”

“Good job.”

The next one was a little sweeter, but not by much.

“Three teaspoons—no, two and half.”

“Damn, I thought I’d had you. Okay, next.”

The third cup made him gag and his eyes flew open as he stared down at it. “Oh my god—you put the whole damn tin in here?”

“Close. That one has nine scoops.”

Remus shook his head. Most of the sugar hadn’t even dissolved, just sat at the bottom collecting into a tiny white mountain.

“Last cup,” Marlene smiled, handing it to him. Remus sipped it and sighed. Perfect.

“Four scoops.”

“Ding-ding-ding! We have a winner.”

“Now you have to try the one with nine scoops.”

“No way! It’ll go straight to my waist. You’re the only one who can afford it, you twig.”

“Ow, my twig-feelings.”

Laughing, Marlene set the tray aside and picked up her own tea. They sat there facing each other on the bed, sipping it in easy silence. Marlene watched him with her blue eyes and he found himself wondering if Lily really was right after all. If he could like Marlene, then maybe he could put all this nonsense with Sirius behind him.

“Marleeeeene, my looooove!” Mary sang as she burst into the bedroom. “You’ll never guess who I snogged under the stairs—oh, hi Remus!”

Saturday 18th December 1976

Despite Lily’s vote of confidence, Remus was not excited to receive his end of term marks. He hadn’t exactly failed, per say, but the results were certainly less than anticipated.

“What happened?” She gasped, flipping through his school report with green eyes the size of dinner plates. “I-I mean they're fine, but what the heck? You studied so much!”

“I know,” he said sorely. “Guess I just tripped at the finish line.”

Lily frowned sympathetically and passed his report back, adjusting her bag as they made their way down House Lane. “There’s always next term.”

“Yup.”

“Aw, cheer up, Remus. If Black has anything to say about it just tell me and I’ll give him detention for being an arse.”

He half-smiled, kicking a stone out of his path. “Lily Evans, my knight in shining armour.”

“And don’t forget, light of your life.”

“Of course. It’s a wonder James hasn’t gotten jealous.”

Lily locked her hands behind her back, smiling shyly. “He’s odd that way—I think he loves too much. Couldn’t be angry at his friends if he tried.”

Remus was suddenly reminded of his conversation with Marlene in her dorm room. “Speaking of love…” He glanced sideways at her, eyebrows raised. “Have you two, you know, said it yet?”

“You mean have we said ‘it’ yet?” Lily bit her lip. “No. Feels a bit heavy, I think. James said it once, but I think it was just sort of on an impulse. It surprised me, and I... didn’t say it back. He said it didn't bother him and that we should take our time, but... I think I’m worried that once we do say it one of us will realise it’s not true.”

“You’ve got to be joking me,” Remus replied automatically. “That’s such bollocks, Lils. You and James are—”

“Are what—an expectation? Well have any of you ever stopped to consider how that might feel? The pressure it might come with? I know I’m right—James loves too much, and I don’t want to be the thing that stops that.”

“So you don’t love him?”

“No—or I mean, I think I do, but I don’t want to be wrong either. Everyone says that you just know when you love someone, like a lightbulb going off in your head. But how can you tell a regular lightbulb from a love lightbulb? I don’t want to get it wrong and regret it, not when James is… you know, James.”

“I get it,” Remus said. “But you should know that James only has love lightbulbs, and if you asked him to, he’d happily share.”

Lily laughed. “What a dumb metaphor.”

“Bet James would find it funny.”

“Ha, probably.”

“You should ask him tonight, at the party.”

“That’s still happening?”

Remus nodded as they stopped outside Godric House. “James and Sirius somehow convinced Kenny to let us have the whole common room to ourselves. He wouldn’t let them throw an actual party, so it’ll just be us. But it’s something before we all go home for the holidays.”

“Sounds nice. I should go on ahead then. I’ve still got some packing to do before we leave tomorrow.”

“You’re coming on our train right?”

She nodded. “I’ll get off midway at Doncaster and transfer onto Lime Street’s line from there.”

“And how’s Snape feel knowing he’ll be taking the other train alone?”

Lily bit her lip and scuffed her shoes on the sidewalk. “I haven’t told him yet actually…”

“You’re just full of secrets this year, aren’t you?”

“Must be contagious.” Lily looked him up and down pointedly before stepping down the sidewalk. “I’ll see you later, then. Make sure you get all your packing done so you’re not scrambling tomorrow.”

“Yeah okay, see you.”

With a wave, Lily left him outside of his dorm and Remus ducked inside. He checked the message board—a missed call from Giles, probably just organising his trip home; and there!

A call from Tomny.

Eagerly, Remus dropped his bag to the floor in front of one of the phones and dialled the flat. A voice answered after a few rings, one he didn’t recognise.

“ 'Ello, whatcha want?”

“Is Tomny around? It’s Remus.”

“Oh blimey,” the voice said, before distantly calling, “s'Remus!”

There was some shuffling of the receiver on the other end and Lee’s voice came through, bright and cheery; “Lupin! Hey! Long time no chat, mate. How’s tricks?”

“Good,” Remus answered, “how you been?”

“Oh, just hunky-dory. You lookin’ for Tomny?”

“Yeah.”

“Sorry, he’s not actually around at the moment—Tonya somehow convinced him to take her out for the night. Right now it’s jus' me and Ian—my lil' bro. You jus' heard him there—Ian say hi.” In the background, Remus heard Ian call out a friendly ‘ello’.

“Hey, Ian,” Remus replied, “I don’t think he and I've met.”

“Ah yeah, nah,” Lee said. “He’s new fish around here. We finally found someone to replace you, Lu!”

Remus swallowed, and took a moment to switch his receiver to the other ear. “Oh yeah?”

“Oh don’t worry, the nob’s not nearly as tall or cheeky.”

“Glad to hear it. Well, I got a message that Tomny called but I must’ve missed him. I’ll be on the train back to London tomorrow, so I guess I’ll try him from home.”

“Oh yeah,” Lee started, “can’t wait to see you. When you droppin' in?”

Remus paused. “Oh, uh, I’m not sure.”

“Tom said you’d be comin' around. S'been too long—bet that school makes you want to tear yer hair out at the roots, yeah?”

Lee laughed, but Remus blazed right past it. “Tomny told you I was coming? He—he said I could come?”

“Mm-hm.”

“When?”

“I dunno, yesterday maybe? Tonya hasn’t shut up about it—did you know they never fight unless it’s about you? Most of us have money on which of them gets you in the divorce.”

It felt as though Remus’ entire body was humming. “I’ll come,” he promised. “When I get back—you can tell Tomny I’m coming.”

“Brilliant. Should be good. I’ll see you then.”

“Absolutely.”

Lee hung up and Remus squeezed the phone tightly in both hands, almost bouncing up and down on the spot. He could hardly believe it, Tomny was letting him come back. He wasn’t going to spend his entire holiday at the estate with only Giles, the dogs, and a few nameless servants for company. Everything else felt like pointless chatter—his jealousy, avoiding Sirius, bombing his exams. Screw his poor marks, nothing could ruin his good mood.

“Alright there, Moony?”

Remus turned around to find Sirius standing in the middle of the main hall, a piece of poster board tucked under one arm.

“Yeah, brilliant! You?”

Sirius looked him up and down and smiled. “Champion. Look.” He lifted the board up for Remus to see; in big block letters it read, PRIVATE PARTY—MESSERS ONLY!

“That for tonight?” He asked, and Sirius nodded eagerly.

“We get one final hurrah before we all return to our own shitty realities, so might as well make a show of it, right?”



Chapter End Notes

Lots of songs referenced in this chapter:

The opening song by The Who was originally written and performed by jazz artist Mose Allison (1957) and covered by The Who on their 1970’s "Live at Leeds" album. Both versions kick ass.

The song Remus and Sirius play is George Harrison's “While My Guitar Gently Weeps” (1968).

"Sweet Emotion" is by Aerosmith (1975).

"Stone Cold Crazy" is by Queen (1974).

The song Sirius sings is "You're My Best Friend" by Queen (1976).

“Why Don’t We Do It in the Road?” is by the Beatles (1968).

‘A dab hand’ is slang for being an expert in something.

A 'breve' is the UK term for a double whole note. 'Quavers' are eighth notes.

'MFL' is just an acronym for Modern Foreign Languages.

A 'school report' or just 'report' is the same thing as a 'report card'.

Lime Street is a large train station in Liverpool.

Chapter 43: Cherry


Chapter Summary

Final night at Hawkings before Christmas holiday. Friendships are changed and tested.



Chapter Notes

CW: Drinking and homophobic language.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Man has always wanted a woman by his side to keep him company,

Women always knew that it takes a man to get matrimony and harmony;

Everybody knows that a man who’s feeling down wants some female sympathy,

Gotta have love to carry on living,

Gotta have love ‘til eternity...

- “People Need Love” ABBA, 1972



Really it was kind of Kenny to hand over the common room for their last night at school. Remus doubted it made him or any of his friends very popular, but other kids stayed away for the most part, deterred by Sirius’ sign and the threat that any party-crashers would receive detention and in the very least, a nasty wedgie.

All of them piled in together and turned the couches into a single ring the way Simeon and his friends had done the year before. The fire burning in the grate was doing its job of keeping them warm with the windows cracked, though they had more than enough booze for that anyway. Invites had been extended to all of their closest friends, including a few plus ones. It had seemed like a good and fair idea at the beginning, but unfortunately Mary’s choice of company couldn’t have been worse. Remus thought he could see the interest—Bryan had wavy brown hair with baby blue eyes and chiselled jaw to boot—but it only took about ten minutes for the rest of them to figure out he had the personality of sour milk.

“Yes. They’re a rock band.”

Mary’s mouth dropped open into a little ‘o’. “You really want me to?”
