Their favourite spot for privacy had quickly become a quiet hallway on the second floor of the Flamel Block, just across the way from the languages department. It wasn’t uncommon for couples to be found camping out in various spots across the school; the outdoor bleachers were commonplace, or the private study rooms at the back of the library—though one did run the risk of getting caught by Ms. Pince, who seemed to disappear and reappear throughout the extensive library as though she could teleport. James wouldn’t admit where it was that he was always taking Lily, but Sirius had his money on the sports equipment room and Remus was inclined to agree with him.

He’d entertained the idea of taking Marlene to the astronomy building, but that was always dark and he was worried she’d think he was trying to pressure her or something. In contrast the hallway she’d shown him was brightly lit and boasted several window seats that overlooked the campus gardens and wildflower fields. Much of the grounds were still covered in a thin layer of snow and frost, but the view was always picturesque. Other students rarely came down that far unless they were heading to lessons and each seat had just enough room for the both of them to sit with their legs stretched out, ankles resting on top of one another in the middle.

These were the moments Remus appreciated most about being with Marlene. Together they’d discovered a new sort of quiet that brought comfort, and that comfort always included her, their window, and a good book. He also liked watching her from that spot, seeing the way her blue eyes flitted across the page while she read.

Marlene glanced up from her book and caught him staring. “You finish the chapter already?”

“Yeah,” he nodded.

“Okay, just give me a second, I’m almost done mine.”

She looked back down at the book in her lap and he leaned his head back against the wall behind him, gently picking at the peeling paint on the window’s edge. A few spaced-out minutes later, and Marlene finally clapped her novel shut and sat up excitedly.

“Okay, chapter summary—twenty words or less. Go.”

Remus drew his knees up and held up his fingers to count. “Lorrie skips out… leaves Jack to clean up pub… they end up at the Christening… Montgomery gives shitty apology.”

“Nice.”

“Thanks. Your turn.”

Marlene cleared her throat. “Beatrice meets lighthouse keeper… daydreams about her ex-husband’s farmhouse… hurts ankle falling off wagon… rescued by handsome keeper… storm hits.”

“That was a lot of compound words just now, Cherry.”

“Well, get on my level,” Marlene sniggered. He smiled and they leaned forward, exchanging novels. It was all part of a little game they'd constructed—switching back and forth until the words began to blur together or they both agreed the book was dry as the paper it was printed on.

“I expect a scandalous twenty-word review of whatever Beatrice and that lighthouse keeper get up to during the storm, just so you know," Marlene warned.

He waved the novel at her. “I’m on the job.”

Marlene giggled again and began flipping through the pages of her book. Remus watched her, zoning out on her hands for a moment before he lifted his arm and checked his watch. “Oh shit,” he said, sitting up right and swinging his feet down to the floor.

“What’s the matter?”

“It’s past eight.”

“Really?” Marlene clicked her tongue. “I hate winter sometimes. The sun disappears and it’s just night all the time. Oh well, curfew isn’t until nine anyway.”

Remus stood and reached for his bag. “Actually, I promised the lads I’d meet them.”

Marlene raised an eyebrow. “For what?”

“Nothing—music stuff.”

“Ha, that’s rubbish.”

“I’ll walk you back?” He tried, smiling guiltily.

“Fine.” She sighed good-naturedly, getting down from the window bench and reaching for her jacket.

“Thank youuu…” Remus sang, tugging on his own. Marlene picked up his scarf and looped it over his neck, tugging him down for a little peck before releasing him.

“This better not be anything too insane,” she warned.

“Oh no, in fact I think everyone will find it pretty relaxing.”

A man of his word, he walked Marlene back to Rowena House and they said goodnight on the dorm's front steps. He was properly late by the time he made it back to his own dorm, only to find that the room was empty and the others must've gone on without him. Unwilling to miss out on the prank that had been his idea in the first place, Remus tossed his bag aside and set off across campus toward the church, only stopping once to avoid a pair of passing teachers on their way out for the night. He was just crossing the church courtyard when a hand grabbed him by the back of his jacket. Remus sent up a silent prayer for his eardrums, readying himself for Filch’s horrendous curfew-breaking lecture, only to receive a light hissing from Sirius instead.

“Where have you been?”

Remus sighed in relief. “With Marlene. Sorry, lost track of time.

“That’s all right and good but while you were shoving your tongue down McKinnon’s throat, we were here putting moves on your prank.”

Remus glanced around the empty courtyard. “Yeah, ball really seems to be rolling.”

“Guess this is what they mean by new year, new priorities.”

“Is that jealousy I detect, Black? And here I thought green was Salazar’s colour.”

“Yeah, bet you’d look real good in black and blue too.” Sirius raised both fists tauntingly.

“Lay off him, Sirius,” James said, appearing out of a bush behind him and dusting the frost and leaves from his wild hair. “Pete’s not here either.”

“Yes, I am!” Peter wheezed, rushing up to James’ side from the road and stopping, bent over while he caught his breath.

“Hope you two at least had fun shagging your girlfriends while we waited here freezing our bits off,” Sirius grumbled.

“When you find someone who can put up with you for more than ten minutes it can be your turn to be late,” Remus said.

“Why bother? I’ve already got you as a captive audience.”

James grinned and socked Sirius in the shoulder with a large baggie of weed. “Okay, drama queen, let’s get this show on the road.”

Shooting another disapproving look in Remus’ direction, Sirius snatched the weed—courtesy of Seesaw—and began marching toward the church. The hash was mostly seeds and stems and not all that good for smoking, but would still smoke and smell strongly enough to peak a few sinful noses during the following morning’s service.

“Wait, we’re just walking right in?” Peter asked, as they went up the steps and James reached for the front door.

“We already scoped the place,” James said. “It’s Father Minsin on confessional duty tonight and he’s already fallen asleep in the booth.”

“You still sweating over what Francis told you, Pete?” Sirius asked disdainfully.

“He said one more problem and I’ll lose my spot as club treasurer," Peter whined. "We couldn’t meet for almost two weeks after the stink bombs because half of us smelled to high heaven!”

“Well, what would you rather be known as? The guy who turned his church into the Jimi Hendrix Experience or the guy who sits around watching telly in some dark clubroom, tugging on his nob?”

Peter glowered like he’d swallowed a lemon. “Whatever, get on with it then.”

Sirius nodded to James and he opened the door wide enough for all of them to slip inside. Most of the church’s lights were off, but they scooted along the wall closest to them anyway, avoiding the hallway of confessionals and ducking toward the church offices.

“One of us should be keeping watch,” James said, and Sirius immediately turned to Peter.

“You heard him, Pete. You were the late one after all.”

“So was Remus!”

“Watch the volume,” James winced.

“Last in, first out,” Sirius said firmly. “And it’s Lupin’s weed.”

Peter huffed, but unable to argue, finally turned and trudged back the way they’d come.

“You are certainly losing the popular vote tonight,” Remus said, earning himself a threatening finger in the face from Sirius.

“Best learn some loyalty or you’ll be next.”

Remus yanked the weed bag from his hand and hit him with it, still sniggering. They followed each other into the ministers’ offices and found themselves in a large room with a long meeting table taking up most of its middle. They left the lights off, and the room remained blue-cast thanks to the winter moonlight drifting through the sheer window coverings. Someone had left a set of vestments draped over the back of one of the chairs, and Remus held it up to James, who was busy snacking on a box of sacramental bread he’d found.

“Next Halloween costume—Father Potter?”

“I’d do it,” James said around a mouthful of wafers.

Sirius turned around from the front of the room. “If you’re done stuffing your face with the body of Christ, I found the incense box.”

Remus tossed the robes down and together they joined Sirius by a heavy wooden hutch on the other side of the room. “You sure you’re feeling okay, Black? You’re not normally so cranky while laughing in the face of God.”

“And you’re not normally so flipping oblivious,” Sirius grumbled. Remus exchanged a look with James, who only shrugged and offered to share the wafers. He turned it down with a small smile as Sirius opened the incense box and they were met with the instant smell of frankincense and myrrh.

“I don’t think we should replace all of it,” James said, “or they’re bound to notice the change in smell.”

“A fifty-fifty mix then?” Remus suggested. Sirius nodded in agreement.

“Find me something to put the rest of the incense in.”

Remus looked around. There was a large array of silver and gold chalices along one wall of the office, the same ones that the ministers used in their service. He went to them and plucked one with a lid off the shelf and brought it back to Sirius, who began scooping incense into it with his hands.

“You figure anyone’s actually going to get high ‘cause of this?” Asked James.

“Nah,” Sirius scoffed, “but in the very least the church is going to be needing some airing out, just like our friends in Salazar.”

“And we get out of church early,” Remus smirked.

Suddenly the office’s overhead lights blazed to life and left each of them momentarily blinded as they spun round to find Father Minsin standing in the doorway, hands clasped in front of him. “Good evening boys,” he smiled, and Sirius visibly deflated, one hand still in the incense box.

“Fuck.”

"No need for foul language, Mr. Black," the priest said. "I believe we're in plenty enough trouble already."

Completely caught, Father Minsin made them wait on the front steps of the church until Filch showed up. The groundkeeper and self-appointed child-torturer looked about as happy as kid on Christmas as he held the bag of hash aloft like a trophy.

“Caught breaking and entering with illicit substances, eh?”

“No, Mr. Filch, we were going to smoke it all but then the voice of God came to us and we ran straight here to repent.” Despite the excuse, Sirius’ delivery read as rather unenthusiastic, and Filch only smacked him upside the head before ordering them to start the long march toward Castle Hall.

“What happened to Pete?” James whispered sorely, his breath coming out as hazy puffs in the cold night air.

“The little worm must’ve ran off with his tail between his legs, the bloody coward,” Sirius growled. “All for his fucking knob-jockey AV club. That little rat!”

“Quiet!” Filch barked.

Remus pulled his winter cap further down over his ears in silent protest. The street was dark but Filch marched just behind them with his torch. He could see someone else making their way toward them from the Bellchant building, and as he watched they slipped on the icy pavement and went down with a spectacular shriek. Filch straightened up and squinted into the dark.

“You three don’t move,” he ordered, before wobbling across the street to help.

“I’m freezing,” Sirius said, “maybe we should just make a break for it.”

“He literally knows where we sleep,” Remus scoffed.

“Hey," James started, nudging Remus with his shoulder; "isn’t that your guys’ music teacher?”

Remus and Sirius followed James’ gaze to find that he was right. Filch was helping Sheila gather up a stack of books she’d dropped in her fall, all while chattering and pointing his torch in their direction. Sheila looked to them in the dark and Remus straightened up a bit before she smiled and crossed the street ahead of of the sour old man.

“Evening gentlemen,” she said. “Mr. Filch has just told me some very interesting news. Can you guess what it is?”

“It’s all a lie, Sheila,” Sirius said.

“Church is a very serious thing.”

“So am I—‘what’s in a name’, right?”

“You watch your mouth,” Filch snapped, appearing at Sheila’s side with a stack of her books in hand. Their teacher smiled anyway and turned to him.

“Mr. Filch, I’m sorry to say I have a bit of bad news myself. You see, just earlier when I was leaving the Bellchant building I could’ve sworn I heard a noise coming from one of the storage closets. I think it was Mrs. Norris.”

Filch’s eyes shot wide. “M-Mrs. Norris?”

“Yes, but I’m afraid I didn’t have the right key on me. I was going to ring your office when I’d gotten home but good thing we ran into one another here. It was such an awful yowling. If you are worried, I won’t mind walking the boys back to Castle Hall myself so you can go and check on her. In fact, I’ll make good use of them while carrying these books.”

“But ma’am—”

“Oh,” Sheila sighed suddenly, “I just realised it was the same closet with all the bass drums stacked in it. I do hope she didn’t knock them over and get trapped underneath.”

That was enough of a push for the caretaker. He practically threw Sheila’s books at them before taking off up the street.

“It was storage closet number seven!” Sheila shouted after him. “At the very back of the building!”

All three boys gaped up at her. “Was all of that true?” Remus asked, after Filch had legged it all the way up the street.

Sheila sighed wistfully. “He never really was very pleasant, even when I was a girl.”

“You went to school here?” Sirius demanded.

Sheila looked back to him and winked. “Okay, time to go home. It’s freezing and we all have class in the morning.”

They deflated slightly and turned to start up the street toward Castle Hall. Suddenly Sheila whistled at them from behind. “Boys, where are you going?”

“To the Headmistress’s office?” James said dumbly.

“Professor McGonagall is not in her office at this time,” Sheila said, “and unless you’d like to draw her from her warm bed, I suggest we go this way. Now c’mon.”

All three of their jaws dropped and it took another friendly wave from Sheila to get them going again. “This is insane,” James whispered as she led them back toward House Lane. “Isn’t she going to punish us at all?”

“Shh!” Sirius snapped quietly; “Don’t tempt her.”

They walked silently behind the music teacher’s clacking boot heels until they reached Godric. “Brrrr!” Sheila said, stopping just shy of the dorm’s front lawn. “I don’t know about you boys but I am ready for spring.”

She smiled and Remus looked from her to the dorm. “Mrs. Buchanan, are you actually letting us off?”

“Yes, Remus, I am,” she said simply, “but only on one condition—no more pranks in church. We have enough silliness at Hawkings without you three parading around in the middle of the night like a little band of marauders. So I want you to swear to me, no more issues with the church.”

“Absolutely,” Sirius agreed automatically; “We promise to be on our best behaviour from here on out. You’ll not find any witches to burn among us.”

“You swear to me?”

“We swear!” They said together.

“Good. Oh and boys, one more thing—don’t go wasting perfectly good hash on some gag. Filch just smokes it himself, you know.”

If Remus’ jaw were any looser it would’ve fallen off. “You—?”

“If you tell anyone I said that I’ll deny it,” Sheila said firmly. “Now give me my books and get your sorry butts inside. If I catch you out again tonight I’ll let Mr. Filch hang you by your thumbs from the gym’s rafters.”

“You heard her, Lupin!” Sirius scooped the books from his arms and handed them over to their teacher before yanking him up the path to Godric’s front doors. Remus stumbled after him in the dark, and when he looked back Sheila was already walking away from them down the street.

“I cannot believe that just happened,” James half-laughed as they fell through the doors. “You two get to have the coolest forms teacher in the entire world, and I get stuck with Bilshin?”

“Now who’s jealous?" Sirius cackled. "But listen—who cares, we got off the hook! And Sheila thinks we swore off pranks.” Grinning spectacularly, he lifted one hand to reveal crossed fingers and James—matching his expression—revealed the same. They both looked at Remus expectantly, but he only stared back dumbly, still a little stunned by Sheila’s entire spiel.

“Oh Lupin,” Sirius sighed, “so smart and yet still so slow on the uptake.”

“Who cares, two out of three marauders ain’t bad!” James declared, locking his arms around both of his friend’s necks and leading them toward the staircase. “I think I like this new moniker too. Much better than ‘messers’ anyway. Just wait until Pete hears!”

“Wherever he went," Sirius said. "But hey—Marauders? You don't think Sheila’s already copyrighted it, do you? Because I think we just found the perfect name for our band.”





* * *





Remus was awoken early the next morning by hushed voices and short clatters. He turned over, groaning, and drew back his bed curtains to peer out. James and Sirius were standing by Peter’s bed and had somehow dragged Sirius’ entire stereo over with them. James had the Rickenbacker strung around his neck, its cord plugged into the stereo like an amp, while Sirius leaned over Peter’s snoring form with a metal baking tray.

“Wha...? What are you doing?” Remus called groggily.

“Shhh,” Sirius hissed, while James held a finger to his lips. Eyebrows shooting upwards, Remus laid back down to watch as James raised his hand in the air and the pair of them began to silently count down;

‘Three—two—’

On one, James’ hand came down and he strummed an intense note on the guitar, which was then amplified ten-fold by the stereo. Immediately Peter flew upright in bed and slammed his forehead into the baking tray, before collapsing back into his sheets with a yowl. Victorious in their scheme, Sirius and James erupted into laughter and fell back, killing themselves as the guitar’s reverb echoed around the room.

“What the hell?” Peter moaned, clutching his face.

“S-Sorry Pete!” James crowed between his laughter.

“My nose!”

“Don't—Don’t worry!” Sirius wheezed. “It’s just a little payback—Wormtail!”



Chapter End Notes

'Polyfidelity' is an earlier coined term for ‘polyamory’.

This was a comforting chapter, I feel :') And finally! A NAME—MARAUDERS! And not just that—three out of four now have their nicknames, cheers babes!





Chapter 48: Horribly Brilliant


Chapter Summary

An upset in a string of relationships leaves Remus with a rather 'boring' problem on his hands.



Chapter Notes

CW: Violence? Or really, just a few punches to the noggin. Ends well <3



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Treat him well, he is your brother,

You might need his help one day;

We depend on one another,

Love him that’s the only way…

- “He is Your Brother” ABBA, 1973



Tuesday 25th January 1977

Sirius gave a great groan as he stretched his arms above his head. His shoulder popped and he let out a sigh of relief as he rubbed it. “I swear to bleedin' Christ, Binns gets more and more boring the older we get. The old dinosaur would probably explode into to dust if you so much as threw a pencil at him.”

James wrinkled his nose in amusement. “I’ll bet he doesn’t even know how boring he is. He probably lost his hearing in ‘69 and has just been rambling ever since.”

“Sight too,” Peter added over a yawn, stretching as Sirius had. Both of them had elected to take a nap during the second half of the lecture.

Remus didn’t mind Professor Binns’ class as much. They all had it together and he was already ahead of the assigned reading, which gave him time to work on other, more trying things.

“So how’s that novel coming along, Lupin?” Sirius asked, nudging Remus in the side as they made their way down the hall.

“I told you I’m not writing a novel,” Remus dismissed. Ahead of them, James spun around next to Peter and began to walk backwards.

“What is it you’re always scribbling in that diary of yours then?” He asked.

“It’s not a diary, it’s a journal.”

“Love notes for McKinnon, perhaps?”

Sirius clapped his hands over his ears. “Please, spare me.”

“They’re not love notes!”

“ 'Course not. They’re love songs aren’t they, Moony?” Peter smiled.

Sirius’ yanked his hands down. “Songs? You’re writing songs and you haven’t told me?”

“I’m going to ask Binns for a new seat partner if you keep spying over my shoulder, Pete,” Remus threatened bitterly.

“Don’t change the subject!” Sirius snapped. “C’mon, pull the diary out, I want to see them.”

“No way! Nothing’s finished yet.”

“I don’t care if they’re finished. Art's best in its rawest form anyway.”

“I’m not giving them up so you best just give it a rest.”

"Fine." Sirius reached out and grabbed Peter by the shoulders. “Wormtail, my main man, c'mon, fess up now—what’d you see? Were they any good? Did they even rhyme?”

“Don’t even try it Pete!”

“I’m not telling you anything while you’re still calling me ‘Wormtail’,” Peter rebuffed, shaking Sirius off. Sirius glowered and James slung an arm across his shoulders as they all started down the staircase toward the ground floor.

"Should'a known you were fightin' a losin' war, Black. It is Moony."

“We’re supposed to be a band," Sirius complained. "Brothers in arms—Marauders! How can we do that if we’re holding back from one another?”

James lifted a hand off Sirius’ shoulder and pinched his nose between two knuckles. “Didn’t realise there was such a rush.”

“There isn’t,” Sirius said in a nasally tone, before ripping his nose free, “unless you want to leave school and head straight for Law like your dad wants.”

James rolled his eyes and Sirius pinched him back smugly, before wheeling on Remus. “C’mon Moony, let us see the songs?”

“No.”

“Come on! I’ve shown you mine, so you show me yours!”

“I really hope I heard that out of context,” Mary said, appearing above them and taking the stairs two at a time until she'd caught up.

“Oh don’t be jealous, Macdonald,” Sirius said as they all stopped to wait for her, “not everyone can woo someone as stoic as Moony.”

Uncharacteristically, Mary ignored the quip and looked straight at James, her dark eyes hard and serious. “Potter, can you bench someone from the football team for being an utter cunt?”

James blinked at her foul language. “Maybe. Why?”

“It’s about Lottie,” she sighed. “Yesterday she... Well, she found out that Mickey’s been cheating on her.”

“Oh fuck,” James and Sirius said together.

“Mickey?” Peter echoed, the picture of surprise. “Mickey cheated on her?”

Mary rubbed her arm sorely. “I wasn’t supposed to tell you, but Lottie won’t do anything about it and Mickey's walking over her like rubbish. You should've heard him! The prick deserves something after what he did.”

“What'd he do?” Asked Sirius. "I mean, aside from the cheating part."

Mary looked around the crowded hallway sorely before beckoning them all over to a quieter corner next to the seminar halls. “You know she went to visit him before school, right?"

All four of them nodded, leaning in very close.

"Well... when we came back she said she felt as though something were off. She’d found another girl’s underwear in his bedroom.”

They all balked a bit at that, and Sirius murmured ‘yikes’ under his breath while Peter just shifted uncomfortably.

"What'd she do then?" James prodded.

“She confronted him, of course! But Mickey just denied the whole thing. Said the underwear belonged to his sister.”

“ ‘Cause that’s any better,” Sirius shuddered.

“Yeah, so yesterday they got into a fight and Lottie brought it up again—because it was complete and utter bollocks—and he totally fessed up! Said a whole bunch of nasty crap too.”

“Like what?”

“I... can’t tell you that.”

James and Sirius exchanged a sorry glance, and Remus suddenly felt very grim. He hated gossip on the best of days, but if Lottie's relationship was really in such shambles and she didn't want anyone to know, then... "Maybe we shouldn't be talking—"

It was Peter, of all people, who cut him off. "Where’s Lottie?” He demanded, looking like a shaken fizzy drink ready to burst.

“Should be downstairs somewhere," Mary answered. "I think she and Lily just had psychology.”

Like a tin soldier, Peter did a full turn and started down the staircase again. His urgency was infectious, and suddenly the rest of them where chasing after him as well. After a bit of rambunctious searching, they eventually found the two girls sitting alone in one of the break rooms, both looking rather forlorn. Lily noticed them first and leaned down to whisper something to Lottie, who was hunched over the table with a tin of chocolate biscuits open in front of her. When she looked up her eyes were rimmed red and purple from crying, and her face was bare of all makeup, making her look startlingly young. Remus wasn't sure he'd ever seen her without painted eyelids and lipgloss, and it was the first time he could really see the resemblance between her and Peter.

“Hi guys,” she mumbled, through a mouthful of sweets. Mary smiled warmly and pat her head as she pulled out a chair to sit down. James sat next to Lily, who elbowed him pointedly.

“Oh—hey Lottie,” he said awkwardly. “How was psych—”

“Why didn’t you tell me about Mickey?” Peter blurted. Instantly Lottie’s blue eyes shot wide and she swallowed before spinning on Mary, expression furious.

“You told them?”

Mary shrunk in her chair slightly. “Sorry Lot, but Mickey—”

“I can’t believe you! I told you I didn’t want anyone to know! This is mine and Mickey's business to work out, no one else's!”

"Then you shouldn't have told everyone!" Peter barked.

"I didn't!" Lottie howled. "I told MARY! Which was clearly a mistake!"

Wincing, Lily leaned in closely and reached to stroke Lottie's hand as a comfort. “Lottie, you can’t really expect to just work it out with him, can you?”

“It’s no one else’s business!” Lottie shrieked again, pulling away.

Undeterred, Peter leaned in over Lottie's chair. “You want to forgive him?” He demanded. “Are you mental?!”

Lottie spun around to glare at her brother. “It’s especially not your business!”

“Why not—why couldn't you tell me? I'm your brother!”

“Exactly! Which means you're practically useless!"

“I am not! I could—Well, I could talk to Mickey!”

“I don’t want anyone to talk to Mickey! I don’t even want to hear his name! Now will all of you just PISS OFF?!”

Peter bristled at his twin's harsh dismissal. “You—You would’ve told Sim!”

“Who says?" Lottie hissed. "Even if I did, Simeon would be able to do something about it! At least he could kick Mickey's ass or something!"

"Who says?" Peter lashed back, a perfect mirror.

"Okaaaay," Sirius tried, grabbing Peter by the shoulders; "Maybe we should take this down a notch, hm?"

"Oh, piss off, Black!" Lottie snarled. "You'd just as soon cheat on me too!"

"Ouch." Sirius released Peter and turned to Remus, sniffling sardonically. "Moons, she hurt my feelings."

"You're a troublemaker, Black, not a peacemaker. Can’t fight nature," Remus chuckled wryly, putting a consoling hand on Sirius' shoulder.

"You're such a bag!” Peter ground out, as he and Lottie continued their face-off. "We're just trying to help."

With a terrible growl, Lottie launched herself to her feet, nearly knocking Peter with the chair as it clattered backwards. "And since when do you even care? God, you're infuriating! It's always 'Sim this', 'Sim that'. Newsflash, baby brother—you’re not Simeon so stop trying to act like it!”

“I’m—I'm not!" Peter sputtered. "Why would I even want to act like Simeon?”

“You’re asking me that? Oh, that’s rich.”

Peter huffed, looking about as red as a tomato. “I’m telling you now, I could do something about it. I will do something about it!”

“What will you do Petey—call him a prick? Tell him that he’s a horrible asshole and a sorry excuse for a boyfriend? Well, I’ve already covered that! Now if you’re done, I’m going back to my dorm.” She shot a venomous look at Mary. “Alone.”

Pausing long enough only to shove a final biscuit in her mouth, Lottie snatched up her bag and sweet tin and pushed past her brother, stomping out of the student break room and down the hall. They all watched her go, and Remus cleared his throat awkwardly. “Well, that went well,” he mumbled, earning an ironic smile from Sirius that he then had to swallow.

"Screw her, she's gone mental," Peter grumbled, taking up his sister’s now-empty spot at the table. Next to him, Remus pulled out another chair and Sirius promptly threw himself into it, grinning like he was having a grand ol' time.

"Thanks, Moons, you're such a gentleman."

"Stop making a joke out of this!" Mary snapped, making Sirius flinch.

"Alright, alright. Far from me for trying to defuse the tension. You could cut it with a bloody spoon. Though, I think Lot should go out for acting. She'd win an Oscar with a performance like that."

"Oh, shut it. Lupin, sit!"

Shooting a 'thanks for that' look at Sirius, Remus sat too, and a stilted silence came over all of them. Luckily they had Lily to break it for them; “You guys couldn’t have done that in a calmer manner?” She sighed, taking James’ hand.

“Was she actually considering forgiving him for cheating on her?” He asked, forehead creased with worry.

Lily frowned. “I don’t know, she’s out of sorts. Her and Mickey have been dating for over a year."

"That's like a decade in teenage-girl years," Mary interjected.

"Yes, well... The whole thing really caught her by surprise," Lily amended with another deep sigh.

“That’s generally how cheating on someone goes,” Sirius said, having moved on to picking at the dark polish on his nails. Mary noticed and swatted his hand for it, making him jump. “Alright fine, but what I want to know is what he said to her after.”

“No, it was so mean!” Lily said immediately.

“Not to mention vulgar,” Mary added.

Peter, who had been utterly silent ever since his sister's prompt exit, slapped both hands against the table top. “James, you and Sirius have gym with Mickey next, yeah?”

“Er—yeah.” He checked his watch. “In a few minutes, actually.”

Wordlessly, Peter stood up from the table with his bag and started away.

“Wormy?” Sirius called, looking around. “Where’s he going?”

“Pete? Pete, we got class! We—ah shit,” James said, getting up to follow him.

“I’ve got to go get Lottie,” Lily moaned, doing the same.

Mary, Remus, and Sirius were left to stare at one another. “Well, I’m not missing this,” Sirius declared.

“Me neither!” Mary agreed, as they all shot from the table after their friends. Peter didn't bother to wait for them as he marched from the main building and out onto the frosty lawn. They were a decent walk from the gym, but he was moving so swiftly that even Remus had to jog slightly to keep up. Despite Sirius and Mary's initial enthusiasm, a knot of dread had taken up residence in his stomach. Remus had known fighters, and Peter with his below average height and only moderate athleticism did not make par. He wished Lily had come with them and not gone after Lottie, at least she might've been able to frighten some sense into him. For now all they had was mild, tender-hearted James.

“C’mon Pete, do you really want to go after Mickey? Lottie’s already pissed at you," James reasoned, surely doing his best to sounding sympathetic without being condescending.

“Shut up, Potter, this is the coolest thing he’s ever done,” Sirius hissed, holding onto Peter’s shoulders as he strode across the grass toward the gym. "You can do this, Wormy. Mickey's all talk and no balls. I'll be he runs away at first sign of trouble. Otherwise just give him a sharp right hook! Don't let him talk too much or he'll one up you."

James pulled his muffler away from his face. “He says as if he's ever actually been in a fight."

"I've been in a fight before! Remember year nine? I went three rounds with Nick Durbey! And he was a year above us!"

"That was gym class, we were wrestling on sponge mats, and you still barely touched each other! Hooch had to push you into the middle of the ring herself!"

Sirius leaned into Peter's ear like a devil on his shoulder. "C'mon Wormy, who you gonna listen to? Me, or the guy whipped by a ginger?"

James crossed his arms over his chest with a scowl. "You’re actually the worst sometimes, Black.”

“Pete wants to be a Marauder,” Sirius announced, “it’s time he proves he can keep up!”

“Mary, tell him he’s acting like a lunatic!”

"No way," Mary answered, fingers tucking up tight in her arm pits. "I say kill the bastard. Guillotine, castration—something."

"Moony—!" James whirled around. "You make them listen!"

Trying not to huff too loudly as he kept up with them, Remus took a moment to consider. Lottie had gone for the low-blow mentioning Simeon, though he supposed Peter had brought him up first. Perhaps this could be the thing that mended that chip on his unbrotherly-shoulder. Then again, Remus had never had siblings. Honestly, James was just asking for the impossible.

“Though I rarely agree with his methods—and he is being a total nob—I think... I might actually with Sirius on this one,” he said, making Sirius practically punch the air in glee.

"HA! Take that, Potter! Moony agrees with me!"

James nearly tripped along the path in his shock. "Moony! You can't be serious?"

“Mickey... deserves whatever’s coming to him," Remus said, trying to ignore the squirmy feeling in his gut.

"That's right!" Sirius said, clapping Peter's shoulders again as they made their way up to the gym doors. "It's only right we rough the prat up a bit."

"You're gonna get our best friend killed, you daft—oh! N-Not that I don't believe in you, Pete!"

"Nice save, Potter," Sirius sniggered, while James punched him in the arm. "Ow—fuck! Save it for Mickey, mate!"

“Are you girls fucking finished?” Peter growled.

"Sorry, Pete. Didn't mean to 'take the mick'. Heh."

Peter shrugged Sirius off, who turned to grin at James, looking a little too satisfied with their friend's newfound virility. Afterwards all four of them, along with Mary, emerged in the gym's foyer.

“We’re definitely going to be late for biology, Remus,” Mary chittered, though she didn’t look anything less than entertained. Next to her, Peter was already scanning the room for any sign of Mickey.

“Anyone see him?”

“There,” Remus answered, pointing to a group of boys across the gym sitting on the second row of stands. Peter took off instantly and they all followed, though his strides did slow the closer they got to Mickey and his friends.

"C'mon, Wormy, you can do it," Sirius hissed quietly, midway across the floor. "Call him out on it!"

“Mick—” Peter’s voice cracked and he had to try again; “Mickey!”

Mickey glanced up lazily and Sirius gave Peter a comforting smack on the back. “There you go—give 'em a piece of your mind!”

“Yeah?” Mickey called, staring them down from his seat on the benches. “Whatchu want?”

Peter cleared his throat a bit. “I need to talk to you, er… prick.”

Oh dear, Remus thought, as James pressed his lips together to stifle a moan.

Across from them, still lounging casually, Mickey set his jaw. “Let me guess, this about your sister?”

“Yeah it’s about my sister!" Peter yelped; "Who do you think you are, cheating on her, you barmy dickhead?!”

“Oh good, insult number two’s got a bit more bite to it,” Sirius whispered to Remus.

“Oh get off it,” Mickey scoffed, “it’s none of your business, Puny-grew. This is between me and Lot, so you can butt-out.”

“You don’t get to call her ‘Lot’ anymore!” Peter seethed. “And it is my business, she’s my sister!”

“Hmph. I’m surprised she even told you anything. You two aren’t exactly close, right?”

Peter balked a bit. “A-As if you know anything!”

“I know enough. You always were royally gassed over not being the favourite brother, even when we were kids. You’d think things would be better now that Sim’s gone, ‘cept you’re still the bottom of the food chain with this lot.” Mickey gestured lazily at all of them, and next to Remus, James bristled.

“Oi, watch your mouth, Mick,” he warned.

Mickey shrugged, uncaring. "Not my fault you collect friends like it's a contest in charity, Potter."

Ready for his own fight, Remus had yanked it out and was about to throw it right back before Sheila appeared to give Barty hell and he'd hidden the stick behind his back. “Mm?”

“Do you have a few minutes after class? I wanted to show you something.”

“What’s a musician?” Remus scoffed. “I say it’s anyone who makes sound with an instrument. Who says everyone’s got to be a Tchaikovsky or a Rachmaninoff.” Those were Tonya's words, he remembered. They felt right then, suddenly.

“Here.” Remus set up a music stand with a simple beginners tablature next to the kit and Peter squinted at it while he gestured to the first bar. “I know you know the notes. This is beat one and it’s a crotchet falling on the bass drum and the hi-hat—the hi-hat's got a pedal there, but you're supposed to tap it with the sticks. Then beat two’s the snare and hi-hat, and beat three’s—!”

“Yeah!” Remus exclaimed. “You already got it, see! You know what you're doing.”

“Well, we won’t know that until you try, yeah?”

Biting his lip, Remus waited in silence, and for a while it seemed as though none of it had worked and he’d just pushed Peter into something he had no real interest in—but then the faintest sound of a bass pedal thumped from the kit, and Remus suddenly found himself holding his breath.

Peter played and no, it wasn’t good. Any rhythm he might’ve had was sacrificed for nerves, and he had that same stilted playing that came with paying too much attention to the music sheet and not enough to the instrument, but it wasn’t about sounding good anyway. It was never about sounding good, not really. They were rewarded when the drums got louder, and the longer Peter played, the more the sound filled up the space; just up and up, building and building. Like a hot air balloon rising into the sky, or a sunrise cresting the very tops of the trees.

Nearly off his arse with happiness, Remus was left to stare up at the ceiling with a dopey smile on his face. “I sounded horrible,” Peter said.

“Yup,” Remus agreed, standing, “and it was bloody brilliant.”

“It’s brilliant to be horrible?”

“You’ll get better,” he shrugged, “and eventually you could be horribly brilliant.”

Peter set both drumsticks on the music stand. “Right. Peter ‘horribly brilliant’ Pettigrew. Dad’ll be so proud.”

Peter sighed again and Remus bit his lip. “Pete, did you know not a single member of The Beatles could read or write music?”

“None of them?”

“Nope, not one. But you can—so you know what that means right? That you’re already on your way to being a better musician than any of ‘em.”

Peter looked down and smiled and Remus felt warm victory rise in his chest.

“You’re not boring Peter,” he said quickly. “I just wanted you to know that.”

Glancing down at himself, Peter palmed his stomach anxiously. Finally, he raised his head.

“Thanks, Remus.”

“Don’t mention it. Now I know I should probably let you go find Moira. Sorry this took a bit longer than expected.”

Peter stood up and stretched a bit. “Well actually, Moira’s meeting her roommate Candace for a project, and I was just really going to tag-along. I don’t think she’d miss me for one study hour, so… would you maybe want to go smoke a spliff or something?”

Remus’ eyes widened in surprise. Then he smiled. “Yeah, absolutely. Let’s go get baked.”

Peter grinned again and together they crossed the room, back to their things. Tossing on their jackets, they left the music room and made their way back outside. It was snowing again, but the sun had finally come out, lighting up the gold in Peter’s hair and leaving their cheeks and noses warm.

"Hey, Remus?" Peter asked as they skirted the pavement. "Are you serious about this music stuff? About being better than the Beatles?"

Remus looked down at his boots. "Well, you know Pete, crazier things have happened."



Chapter End Notes

'Take the mick/[mickey]' is slang for teasing someone.

'Ledge' is slang for 'you're a legend'.

John Bonham was the drummer for Led Zeppelin until his death in 1980. Ginger Baker was a legendary drummer and the co-founder of the band Cream.

A ‘crotchet’ is the UK term for a quarter note.

A ‘quaver’ is the UK term for an eighth note.

A ‘hi-hat’ is a type of cymbal on a drum kit.

This chapter feels like a deviant from the 'wolfstar' romance plotline, but in the best way :') It has a special place in my heart, yk? xo loves.

Chapter 49: Well Fitted in Arts, Glorious in Arms


Chapter Summary

Valentine's Day has come to Hawkings. Remus struggles with more than one kind of relationship.



Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes



A teenager’s romance is fickled or true,

A teenager’s romance is red hot or blue;

You’re either in misery or high on a crest,

A teenager’s romance is like all the rest…

- “A Teenager’s Romance” Ricky Nelson, 1957



Saturday 12th February 1977

Getting a girlfriend was supposed to solve everything. It was supposed to help things make sense, and most of all, it was supposed to take his mind off of Sirius Black’s bloody stomach. Stomach, stomach, stomach—ugh! WHY stomachs?! He had no clue. And yet, all it had taken was for Sirius to roll out of bed all bleary-eyed and shaggy-haired with his pyjama shirt unbuttoned to his navel to cause another incident. Remus had stayed up late with a regular bout of restlessness and forgotten to close his curtains again, so when James’ alarm clock went off early that Saturday morning he turned over to throw a pillow at him, only to catch Sirius upside the head with it as he crossed the room.

“Woah, bit early to be declaring war innit, Moony?” Sirius moaned, tossing the pillow back with a grunt. Remus caught it and didn’t miss the way Sirius casually reached beneath the hem of his shirt to scratch his stomach, yawning as he continued on to the bathroom.

Finished with their warm-up, Marlene’s team of girls rushed the bench together and flopped down among their water bottles.

“I think it’s ‘shoot the shit’ actually,” Remus said.

“Try participating in practice first,” Marlene said, playfully shoving Nicole by the shoulder. Nicole grinned back and snatched Marlene’s hand out of the air, kissing it lightly before giving a playful shriek and shooting away across the pitch.

“Honestly, where do you get off being so cheeky?!” Marlene lashed, streaking after her. Content to watch, Remus leaned back against the bench as Anna sat down next to him.

“They’ll never change,” she sighed wistfully. “I swear, if one of them had been born a boy—”

“Oh! I didn’t mean anything by that, Remus…”

He chuckled. “No, it’s okay.” There was a level of girl-friendship that Remus was never going to be able to understand. And frankly, that was just fine with him.

Beyond the pitch-line Marlene had given up the chase and was now being taunted by Nicole as she ran backwards around her in circles. Finally, Marlene stuck her foot out and Nicole sprawled, grabbing onto her at the last second and taking them both to the ground. They came up laughing and Remus couldn't help but feel a twinge of envy, but as he sat there observing them, he couldn’t quite put his finger on what it was he was so jealous of.

Remus could’ve sworn he’d avoided the whole Valentine’s debacle, and had been quite content to join his friends for dinner that evening only to learn that he wasn’t out of the woods at all. In fact, James and Peter had just about lost their minds the moment he told them of Marlene’s reaction.

Sirius turned over onto his stomach. “But I’m not—”

The bedroom door creaked open and a hand slipped in, waving a white dish rag in surrender. “Is it safe to come in?”

“Don’t be idiots,” Remus answered and both James and Peter appeared in the doorway, grinning and holding a tea tray between them.

“Oh good, you’re listening to music!” Peter said. “Must mean you’re done fighting.”

“Never,” Sirius announced, shooting a smirk in Remus’ direction.

James and Peter came forward, abandoning the tea by the door and squeezing in between the two beds beside them. “What we listening to?”

“Queen,” Remus and Sirius said together.

“Great,” James said, tucking his hands behind his head. “S’pose we should tuck in then, Pete—those guys never write a song shorter than six minutes.”

Monday 14th February 1977

Marlene took the flowers with a slightly furrowed brow. They were a bit droopy after having been picked nearly two days before, but still better than nothing.

“Thank you?” She said, looking them over with a small smile. “Where’d you even get them?”

“It was a special order.”

She held out her hand and he helped her down the icy steps before tucking both his and hers back into his pocket for some warmth. Together they made their way up House Lane, toward the dining hall.

“How are your friends back home doing?” Marlene asked. “You heard from them much?”

Marlene's curiosity over Tomny and the others had been piqued ever since the beginning of their relationship, when he’d called her from the flat. “They’re good,” Remus said. “I talked to them the other day. A few of them had this nasty cold but they’re still good.”

“That’s nice. Maybe I should meet them when we go home for Easter. Could be fun?"

Marlene looked up. “Why wouldn’t I?”

“Yup.”

“Cool.”

They kept on, until a voice called out to them from across the berm and Michelle, Marlene’s vice-captain, raced up to them, half-panting. “Oh my gosh, you two! I can’t believe it—did you actually do that Remus?!”

“Oh my god,” Marlene moaned, and Remus dropped his hands to blink in the daylight. Hanging from the roof of the hall and at least thirty feet across was a ginormous white banner bearing the words;





MY DEAREST MARLENE, WILL YOU MARRY ME?

- YOURS IN UNEQUIVOCAL ADORATION, REMUS LUPIN



“I’m gonna fucking kill him,” Remus promised.

Like a brick wall, the Headmistress had hardly flinched even as Sirius bounced off of her, and afterwards simply crossed both hands ahead of herself, thin mouth drawn into a tight line.

“… Tosser.”

Friday 18 th February 1977

How—oh how—had he failed so spectacularly to learn his lesson? James had repeated it like a mantra their first year; never underestimate a Black. All their other classmates started giggling as Sirius scowled down at the slip and Bilshin walked away. * * *

He shook his head. Nightmares required a certain level of deep sleep, which he was half sure he never got, and besides, no nightmare could be as shitty as the things he couldn’t forget during the daytime anyway. He'd take a zombie or a murderous prom queen over one of those any day.

“Hey,” she smiled.

The silence was abrupt and startling. They did, making their way outside the wall and skipping across the road until they'd made it into the endless pastures and some of the giddiness that came with sneaking out had been replaced with the crisp reality of the chilly night air. In the dark, and with only three torches to split amongst the ten of them they were risking twisted ankles and the occasional cowpat, so they walked behind one another in pairs. Everywhere they stepped was damp and spongy since it was still that part of the year where the ground melted during the day only to refreeze at night. “Thought I smelled something funny. Don’t tell me it’s you, Macdonald?”

“No!”

“Can we get on with this?” Remus said, feeling as haggard as the rest of them. “Where’s this pub?”

“It’s this way,” James said, taking a shivering Lily by the arm and shooting off down the street. It only took a short while longer for the little brick cottages to give way to shut-up shops and quiet street corners. Along the way they passed a closed corner shop (“Sorry, Moony. I’ll ask Xeno to bring you some brand-name fags next time.”) and a small bakery that still smelt mouth-watering despite its darkened windows. Tired and half-frozen, they made their way inside The Three Broomsticks and took a seat at one of the big round booths near the back where they could avoid any curious eyes. It was a tight squeeze with ten of them, but James was able to pull up a few extra chairs and they all settled in. It didn’t take long for the pub's landlady to notice. She strolled over to the table, wiping her hands on her apron.

“Hello there. Don’t think I recognize you lot.”

“We’re from out of town,” Mary replied boldly.

“If you say so.”

“Say, I remember you,” Sirius said, flourishing his hand as if to flatter. “Madam Rosetta, wasn’t it?”

“Rosmerta,” she corrected, “but everyone just calls me Rosie. This is my pub, so what’ll it be?”

“A round of pints,” Sirius said.

“And some tea,” Marlene added. Sirius looked at her, appalled.

“What? It’s freezing.”

“How about some warm ciders then?” Rosmerta offered. “I’ve got some steaming wassail in the back.”

“That sounds great,” James nodded, and she tossed a few napkins on the table and strode away.

“That was too easy,” Lily said.

“I told you,” Sirius said smugly, “they don’t care that we’re here as long as we can pay up afterwards.”

After the landlady had returned with their tray of drinks, they distributed the pints and cider amongst themselves and drank deeply until their insides were warm and a light flush had come to each of their cheeks. The last of them had just finished shrugging out of their winter coats when Mary pointed across the room.

“Oh my god, is that Greyson Kent?”

All ten of them strained their heads to get a look. On the other side of the pub, a group of year 13 boys were crowded into a corner.

“Yep, it is,” James said. He and Greyson were on the football team together. After some prodding from Mary, he called Greyson’s name and they exchanged a friendly wave.

“Over there, it’s Holly,” Lily said, pointing to another small group of students. “I can’t believe she’s here. She’s a prefect, you know.”

“Oh good. Now you’re not the only one breaking the rules,” Chastity said. James nodded as if to agree with her, making Lily scoff while pinching him on the arm.

“Right, that’s enough then,” Mary said, before unceremoniously downing half her pint. “I’m going to say hello.”

“To Greyson?” Marlene said. “But we just got here.”

“Exactly, which means I won’t be buying any more of my own drinks. C’mon, Lot, let’s go.”

Eagerly the two girls wiggled out from the booth and strolled across the room, stopping behind Greyson and his friends and smiling until the boys ultimately pulled up a few chairs for them.

“Gotta hand it to her. She knows what she wants and she goes for it,” Chastity said.

“Reminds me of someone else I know,” Sirius added keenly. He and Chastity exchanged a flirtatious look, while Remus glared hard at the bottom of his pint glass.

“I see Rachelle. She lives next door,” Moira said, nudging her boyfriend. “I want to say hi too. Petey, are you coming?”

“Yeah, alright.” Peter gathered their drinks and together they got up from the table.

“Don’t let those girls eat you alive, Wormy,” Sirius called after them. Minus the four extra bums at the table, there was finally enough room to shimmy around the booth. Remus and Marlene found themselves at its centre, with James and Lily to their left and Sirius and Chastity across from them.

“I can’t believe there’s so many other students here,” Lily said.

“I can’t believe you’ve really never been,” Chastity replied.

Lily bristled. “Not everyone’s so keen on breaking the rules for a bit of fun.”

“Right.” Chastity sipped her pint. “So how’d Potter know the way?”

As if the thought hadn’t occurred to her, Lily turned to James, who quickly busied himself by swishing his drink around. Finally he caved.

“It was that time with Simeon. After the… you know… party.”

“You told us that the party was in some dirty old barn,” Marlene said.

“We came to the pub after,” Sirius amended. “Sim’s idea.”

A sudden consideration came over Lily, as though she’d suddenly found the bottom of her cider glass very interesting. “Oh. Well, that’s fine, I suppose.”

It was clear to the rest of them that she was merely swallowing her pride, and the sour memory that came with it. Too bad Chastity wasn't in the loop.

“You should’ve seen how sloshed Potter was,” she giggled. “Had to practically drag his arse out, didn’t you?”

“You were there?” Marlene gaped, while James looked very guilty.

“ ‘Course. I knew Simeon. He dated my cousin Bethany when they were our age.”

“I don’t actually remember seeing you,” Sirius said to her.

“I remember seeing you,” Chastity smirked. “I can see why you wouldn’t remember. You were pretty busy. You know, with that girl’s hand down—”

“Rosie!” Remus chirped, raising his glass as the barmaid passed. “Another round please!”





* * *





Remus didn’t know what time it was, but so far he’d downed two full pints, half of Marlene’s pale ale, and a warm cider. He’d been pushed and squeezed and shoved as other students came and went from their table, visiting and exchanging pleasantries like they weren’t all breaking over a dozen school rules just by being there. Unluckily for Remus, he’d found himself sucked into a conversation with Chastity that had no way out. Sirius was still planted starkly on her other side, while Marlene had slid over to Lily and was refusing to speak to him.

"Piss off, you called me drunk," she snubbed.

"I didn't," Remus tried reasoning. "I just said you were being a bit silly."

Marlene just stuck her tongue out at him.

So, he was left with Sirius and Chastity, and it occurred to Remus that never had he so strongly wished that women came with an off switch. Chastity talked like she was on a late-night talk show and everyone else was merely there to listen or entertain her. “Your fingers are so long,” Chastity giggled, busy holding her hand up against Sirius’ in comparison. “I guess what they say about musicians is true—you are mutants.”

“You should see Moony’s,” Sirius said. Face lighting up, Chasity turned eagerly and grabbed Remus’ wrist just as he was about to polish off his third ale. She pressed both his and Sirius’ hands together in front of her, examining them as though she’d just discovered a new species.

“Wow, Sirius,” she exclaimed, “your hand looks like a baby’s next to his!”

“An elegant baby’s!”

Remus pulled his hand back. It was clammy from holding Marlene’s hand under the table and he didn’t want Sirius to feel it.

"Remus' fingers totally dwarf yours," Chastity teased, but Sirius just leaned across her toward Remus.

“Your hands are so bloody soft, Moony,” he said. “You gotta build up those calluses more.”

“Oh, haven’t you heard?” Sirius grinned, sitting back. They made eye contact over Chastity's head and Remus prepared himself for the incoming embarrassment, but Sirius only paused and ran his tongue over his top lip.

“Sometimes this guy has trouble sleeping,” he said lowly, so only the three of them could hear, “and he sneaks over to my side of the room to listen to music.” Sirius mimicked putting on headphones. “But I have the window, so when he’s sitting down on the floor and we’ve forgotten to shut the curtains the moon comes through the glass and reflects off the top of his head like a little halo. So he’s Moony.”

Remus didn’t know what to say, the story was so ridiculous, it was laughable. Not that Chastity minded.

“That’s so cute,” she declared. “I want a nickname.”

“Stick around long enough and you’ll get one,” Sirius confirmed, before reaching across the table to nab Remus’ hand again. “Though maybe we should be calling this one mutant fingers, ha!”

“Gerroff,” Remus slurred, shaking himself free. Chastity giggled (Christ, did she ever stop giggling?) and turned her shoulder into Sirius’ chest again—she’d been doing it all night, sidling closer to him until she was practically in his lap. Sirius didn’t seem to mind. All it took was one sly upwards glance from her and they were kissing.

Instantly apprehensive, Remus slid toward Marlene. “I’m gonna go have a smoke.”

“Okay,” she said, “just don’t stay out long. We still gotta walk back and it’s cold out.”

He nodded, and she and Lily slid down to let him out of the booth. After a quick pit stop at the loo, Remus shrugged his jacket on and stepped out into the cool air.

Moving past the small crowd of local smokers, he skirted down the lane until he’d stopped beneath one of the pub’s windows. It was cracked slightly, allowing warm air and the faint sound of a radio to drift out into the night. Only slightly comforted, Remus lit a cigarette and inhaled deeply. He held that first golden puff inside, mind drifting to Sirius and Chastity. By then his lungs were screaming for air. When he finally exhaled, he coughed until his eyes watered.

“Need me to get you another pint to help wash that down?” Sirius asked, appearing beside him in the dark.

“Shit. What—you doing—out here?” Remus said, in between hacking.

“I came to join you.”

Recovered, Remus cleared his throat, refusing to meet Sirius' gaze. “You looked pretty busy before.”

“Lost mine,” Remus lied, because he felt like it. The weak joke didn't seem to go over well with Sirius, who glanced up at him sharply before reaching out to grab the front of his jacket. They were so close Remus could see the faint orange glow of the cigarettes reflected in Sirius’ eyes.

Entirely rattled, Remus imagined himself grabbing Sirius by the front of his coat and shaking him. How does that not freak you out? He'd demand. How can you just do that?!

Like this, the imaginary Sirius would say, and then he'd... Well, who knows what he would do. Sirius was weird like that. Entirely unexpected.

Someone had graffitied across its brick, but the paint was so faded he couldn’t make out what it said. It reminded him of his friends back home. How many hours had he spent running around the End with the boys, tagging everything from cars doors to street signs? It’d been so long now, before he came to Hawkings, and Tomny didn’t even bother with that stuff anymore anyway. Maybe their tags were faded now too.

“No, I told him to cheat off of James. I told him to cheat off you in history. Where’d you get those fags? Xeno always says he only brings in loose baccy.”

“Dunno. Dad, maybe. You actually like Lily, right?”

“I dunno. You're always on her arse about something.”

Sirius rolled his eyes. “Of course I like her. Evans and I might not always see eye to eye on everything, but she makes James happy. And I like seeing James happy. Do you like Lily?”

“Maybe, but I had to check. Now go on, it’s your turn," Sirius smiled, patting him on the arm. The touch was gentle enough that Remus found himself staring down at his arm afterwards as his next question materialised in his mind.

Why is it so easy for you to touch me?

He almost said it out loud, but then it occurred to him that there was a chance Sirius would ask him to explain the question—which felt impossible, because he wasn't entire sure where it'd come from in the first place. They were a friendly group, them Marauders—especially James and Sirius—but Remus had always felt a bit on the outside. Touching Sirius never felt like it did with Tomny or Lee or Doss. It was always different somehow, like he was too aware of him. And that frightened him.

"Earth to space cadet," Sirius called. "I said it was your turn."

"I..." Remus sighed. "I can't think of anything. You go."

"Can't. S'against the rules. You gotta ask something."

"Fuckin' hell, fine. What's your... er... favourite colour?"

If he thought the question was stupid, Sirius didn’t say it. Instead he just smiled, acting almost shy, and in a small voice he said, "Brown."

"Brown?" Remus echoed. "Why brown?" He'd expected Sirius' favourite colour to be something as loud and obnoxious as he was, like electric blue or fandango purple.

"Dunno," Sirius said, "I just like it."

"Oh. Er, alright. Your turn, I suppose."

"Do you trust me?”

“Blue—” Remus stopped himself, and Sirius' face began to crease with laughter.

"Did you think I was going to ask your favourite colour, Moony?"

"Shove off. That would be the normal thing to do, wouldn't it?"

"Ha, you're funny. I can ask your favourite colour anytime. What I want to know, is if you trust me."

Still a bit caught off guard, Remus’ eyebrows knit together in puzzlement. “Yes,” he said finally, “I think so. Do you trust me...?”

“Always." And then Sirius stared at him, hard and genuine. "How old were you the first time your dad hit you?”

Oh.

So it was like that then.

Remus shuffled awkwardly on the spot, rolling his cigarette between two fingers. “Lyall—or... My dad, he... He’s never hit me.”

“Never...?”

“No. How old were you?”

“Can’t remember. How about your mum?”

Remus felt his jaw tighten. “Dunno, can’t really remember either. She probably didn’t. At least I don't think she did. How’d you get your burn scars?”

Sirius took the question in stride. He’d been expecting it. “Boiling water. I was eleven. How’d you get yours?”

Almost immediately a phantom ache split across Remus' nose and he reached up to rub it. “Broke my face on some guy’s fist. Do yours hurt?”

“Not anymore. At least yours sounds more badass. Why’d you lie about it?”

“It was easier. Why do you hide them?”

“It’s easier. Do they scare you?”

Remus’ expression turned resolute. He was still buzzed, but his answer would’ve been the same drunk or not. “No.”

“Good,” Sirius said, looking down. Still watching him—as if he could do anything else—Remus brought his cigarette back to his lips.

“Why’d you jump out that window—hurt your arm?” He asked, inhaling.

“Wanted to get away," Sirius exhaled. "Who told you I jumped out a window?”

He blew out the smoke. “Regulus. Why don’t the two of you get along?”

“It’s complicated.”

“That’s not an answer.”

“Sure it is. What happened with your mum?”

“It’s complicated.”

Sirius sighed again. “Right.”

“Right,” Remus said. “Why won’t you go near the piano?”

“I do go near it—”

“Why won’t you play the piano?”

“You know why.”

“No, all I know is that it has something to do with your mum. Which is why I'm asking.”

“Fine. It’s ‘cause it’s always for her. Or for someone else,” Sirius said, voice tight. “The guitar’s for me. And for you.”

Remus glanced down, digging the toe of his boot into the pavement. “Your turn,” he mumbled.

“Why won’t you show us the songs you’ve been writing?” Sirius asked.

“Because they’re not finished.”

“Will you ever show us?”

“Maybe." He looked up again. "Will you ever play the piano again?”

“Maybe. Dunno what it’s gonna take.”

“You gotta find a new reason to play,” Remus said without thinking. “I mean—make it for you, right? Someone told me that.”

“Sheila,” he lied, surprising himself again. Tonya wasn't a secret... right?

“Huh,” Sirius said, biting his thumb as though lost in thought, before indicating for Remus to ask another question.

So, he did.

“What happened with Miles?”

Instantly Sirius’ lips parted in shock and he dropped his hand. “What?”

“I asked what happened with Miles.”

“I… how…?” As if suddenly lost on the spot, Sirius looked down but drew back slightly and raised his cigarette, which had burned down to nothing and gone cold in the night. “Damn,” he said quietly, “I guess time’s up. You’re pretty good at this game, Moony.”

Remus couldn’t help it. The disappointment washed over him like a wave. “You cheated.”

“No, I definitely played by the rules," Sirius said.

"So you're not gonna answer my question?"

"Can't. Time ran out. That would be cheating."

Bitterly, Remus flicked his cigarette stub away and Sirius did the same, before ultimately smiling and throwing an arm up around his shoulders. “Aw, don't be angry, Moons."

"You're a prick."

"Naturally, but still, it feels good to get some information out of you for once.”

“That makes one of us,” Remus grumbled. He let Sirius turn him around so they could make their way back toward the pub’s entrance.

“I was perfectly forthcoming,” Sirius said.

“You’re a manipulative bastard, Black.”

“Put that in a song and I’ll believe it. Until then, good game.”

And that was that. They walked back inside together as if nothing more than a cigarette had been exchanged between them.

But Remus could already feel the shift.

Sirius was now the keeper of the most secrets he’d ever revealed—maybe even more than Tomny—all because of some silly little game.

He wondered if it was the same for Sirius. Did Remus now carry more of him than James did? No, there was no way. Competing like that would only mean a loss, and Remus didn’t feel like playing loser again. If he was alone he might’ve entertained the thought more, but that wasn’t Sirius. Sirius lived like emotions were just part-time work. Like they were a simple nine-to-five, and could be shut off at the the end of the day in favour of easier, more light-hearted fun. It was a form of resilience, he knew, and one of the things Remus would always admire most about him. He envied it too, and very secretly, feared it.

He nodded and left her at the end of the canteen line, crossing the dining hall to scoop a few napkins and two sets of utensils onto their trays. As he did, he noticed Chastity and Sirius sitting a few tables down. Reaching across the table, Chastity spoon-fed Sirius a bite and he stole her fork before holding it out of her reach and making her come around to his side to get it back. She slid onto the bench beside him and they kissed for a bit, before Sirius noticed him watching and tried to flag him down.

“Ready?” Marlene asked, appearing at his side with two cups in hand.

“Yeah,” he mumbled, flashing a weak wave in Sirius' direction before following Marlene out of the dining hall. Trays in hand, they made their way one building over, to their secret spot on the second floor of the Flamel Block. It’d become a habit of theirs to sit at the window and eat, and they always did so while reading or else talking about their day. Today though, Marlene did not bring a book, nor did she seem very talkative. Instead they sat together, staring out their window as the late-winter sun dipped down over the trees.

“We could you know,” Marlene said eventually. “I mean, just to get it over with. It doesn’t have to be a big deal.”

Remus didn’t have to ask what she meant. “Wasn’t it a big deal to you before?”

Marlene puckered a bit. “I’m not a little kid.”

“I wasn’t saying that.”

“I know.” She sighed, biting down on her fork. “It’s just, I do like you, Remus. I do.”

“I like you, too.”

“And I would rather it be you than anyone else.”

Remus pressed his lips together. “I’ve never done anything either,” he confessed. This seemed to be the correct thing to say, because Marlene nodded earnestly.

“So we’d be each other’s firsts then?”

He nearly winced—how did people just talk about this stuff?—but Marlene was staring at him expectantly, and Remus didn't want to seem lame.

“Alright," he swallowed. "We’ll just do it then.”

“Okay," Marlene agreed. "I mean, the first time should be a little—you know—but all first times are, right? At least this way we could stop worrying about it. I’d rather get it over with and move on.”

“I don’t know,” he confessed. “Does it feel weird?”

“A bit.”

“Well… we don’t have to tell anybody.”

“That’s right!” She straightened up. “It’s just for us anyway. And everyone does it, right?”

“Er… yeah.”

Marlene nodded. “Brilliant, then.”

To their credit, they did not fold under sheer nerves. The air felt awkward, and without even realising it they’d spent the days before avoiding being alone together, probably because that would mean having to talk about it. Remus had half-expected Marlene to show up at any given moment and tell him that she’d changed her mind, but as always her will was resolute, and come Wednesday evening he told all his friends they were studying and that he’d see them later. On his way out he'd secretly raided the small trove of condoms Sirius had piled into their bathroom cabinet as a joke. He wasn’t sure how many to take so he ended up stuffing a handful in his back pocket and shooting out of the room as though he’d just lifted from a corner shop.

When he got to the girls' room Remus found Marlene waiting for him in a pretty skirt she'd borrowed from Lily. She'd even put on some make-up, which he nearly said she didn't need before realising that that was probably not the smartest move. He called her pretty instead, and Marlene seemed pleased. There were candles lit that left the entire room smelling of vanilla and also made Remus' nose itch, but it went away when Marlene broke out a small bottle of rum, which they downed to calm their frenzied nerves. Remus kissed her first, because that was what he thought he should do, and thankfully Marlene followed his lead, curling into him on her Rowena-blue covers with slow and anxious fingers.

The beginning bit was really what took some finessing. He’d never seen a bra before—at least not one being worn—and the little hooks were really the bitches Lee was always saying they were. Up until that moment the most he’d ever felt of Marlene was her hands, neck, and face, and it surprised him how soft she was all over. But that was just girls. It was exciting—of course it was exciting—even if Remus spent the entire time feeling like his head was in an oven. When they finally started ridding themselves of the rest of their clothes, he pulled his shirt over his head and Marlene eyed the necklace Sirius had given him, thumbing it lightly before kissing him again. She was good at not dwelling on the awkward, at least, and eventually they got the motions down.

Sometime during the middle of it all, Marlene tapped him on the back lightly; “Um, Remus?”

He froze. “Are you okay? I'm not hurting you, am I?”

“I'm fine, but you’re leaning on my hair.”

“Oh, sorry!”

Afterwards they sort of just laid there, staring up at the top of Marlene’s four-poster. He didn’t think either of them had been good at it—really ‘it’ was just a jumble of sweaty limbs that’d only lasted for about fifteen minutes from start to finish—but the whole thing still made his heart race in an umcomfortable sort of way. Remus kept waiting for the feeling to disappate, but when it didn’t he just accepted that that was how things went your first time. It felt easier.

“Well…” Marlene said finally; “that was…”

“Sweaty,” Remus finished.

She laughed—thank god—and took his hand, bringing it up to her mouth. “I’m sure next time’ll be better, right?” She whispered, lips just barely grazing his knuckles.

“Yeah. Next time.”

And so Remus dressed, kissed his girlfriend goodbye, and made the trek home. His stomach still felt funny, and the entire way all he could think of was how badly he wanted to talk to Tomny, but when he made it back to Godric and dialled the flat, there was no answer. Frustrated, Remus slammed the receiver down on the machine, and turned for the stairs. It made him bitter to be ignored; enough so that he didn’t even notice he wasn’t alone when he walked into his own dorm room. It took until someone deliberately cleared their throat for him to whirl around, where he got an eye-full of Chastity's bare back as she straddled a half-naked Sirius over the covers.

“Well, I didn’t actually mean ‘homework’, you dimbo,” Sirius said cheekily, making Chastity giggle. “But don’t worry, it’s a natural progression after health class. Even Evans has seemed more frisky lately.”

“C’mon, don’t be too angry, I’m pretty sure she and Potter got stuck with the sports equipment room.”

“Leaving!”

“Can you at least bring a light when you come back?” Sirius called after him. “Can’t find mine!”

He escaped down to the common room, where everyone else was mercifully going about the rest of their evening in complete and utter normalcy. After his heart had stopped hammering—he’d already given up on trying to eject the image of Sirius and Chasity in bed together from his mind—Remus pulled a random book from the common room’s shelves and slumped down on one of the empty couches. Did it bother him that Sirius and Chastity had been dating for less than a week and already she’d seen his scars, while Sirius had felt the need to hide them from him for over a year? Probably. But that was normal, right? It was normal to be worried about his friend and also annoyed with him when he invited girls back to their room without saying anything.

So why was it Remus couldn't bring himself to concentrate long enough to read more than a page in his book?

It was agony, actually, just trying, and eventually he gave up entirely, leaving the book open over his face as he slouched back on one of the common room sofas. He was almost asleep when he felt a nudge on the bottom of his foot. Lifting the book, Remus found Sirius standing at the end of the settee, smiling shyly.

“You can come up now,” he said. “Chas’s gone home.”

“You sure? Might want to air out the room first.”

Sirius snorted and stepped up, snatching up the book and tossing it aside. “Come upstairs with me. I’ve got the stereo going, and there’s weed and tea. We can snuggle too, if that’s still not enough.”

“You know,” Remus started, sitting up, “you think you’re so bold, but really you’re just foul.”

Sirius’ eyes glittered. “Am I?”

”Yeah, you are. And I'm getting real sick of your shit.”

“Aw, Moony,” he grinned, “you're so cute when you lie. Now c'mon, tea's getting cold."

Taking a moment to lean down and pat him on the thigh, Sirius turned and strolled away with his hands in his pockets. Conflicted by his anger and the desire to follow him, Remus paused long enough to watch him go. His mouth had suddenly gone dry, and his heart was racing again as though he were back in Marlene's bedroom. But he wasn't in Marlene's bedroom at all, and as Sirius stopped in the common room's doorway to beckon him forward with another one of his cheeky smiles, Remus began to feel nervous all over again.



Chapter End Notes

A jacket potato is like a baked potato.

Idk if it's necessary to add, but 'outstanding work' just means overdue homework.

'Up the duff' is slang for pregnant.

Sommmmmme people might disagree with me, but I believe in stories like this that it's really important that Remus and Sirius find love and intimacy outside of one another too. In my experience, couples who've only ever had each other lack that quintessential portion of comparison when it comes to physical and emotional issues. If you've only ever been with one person (at whatever capacity), who do you have to compare yourselves to when things go awry? How do you know when things HAVE gone awry?

Anyway, that's just my explanation for this chapter. I hope you can see the tension I'm trying to build here, hehe. 'Til next time, loves! <3

Friday 25th February 1977

Tonya had opened a door for him over Christmas, introducing him to the gruesome genre he had no hope of satisfying among Hawkings' bland library pickings.

Marlene just turned her nose up. “The opening was traumatic. I felt so bad for the poor girl!”

Remus winced. “I know—but she gets revenge!”

“Doesn’t her own mother try to kill her?”

“Yeah, but she kills her first.”

“How is that any better? It’s just miserable.”

“It’s horror.”

“Oh yeah, hor—ri—ble!”

“Better me than Carrie.”

"What's so bad about that? You bug me all the time," Remus said, opting to hide his embarrassment with a jab. Again, Sirius took it in stride and leaned his head against one hand, looking up as though he were a cat and Remus was his favourite ball of yarn.

"It's a thing—they do it on the telly programs all the time."

Yes well, Remus imagined asking Lily to hang out with Chastity outside of class or prefect duties would’ve gone over like a ton of bricks anyway.

Remus felt a warm feeling rise in his chest. “No, go ahead. It’s really thrilling.”

“Tell me about it on the walk back to class?” Sirius turned to go, looking handsome in the early-afternoon sun, and Remus hurried after him.

“Okay, so I won’t spoil it but there’s this girl Carrie, and she’s being bullied in school but she finds out she has these crazy psychic powers and…”
