She nodded and they sat down together, drawn close to putter over each other’s notes as they always did. Despite the girls’ nasty row, it didn’t take them long to find their groove again, but the entire time Remus held Chastity’s words in the back of his mind.

When they finally broke for the afternoon, he walked back to his dorm to find Sirius lying upside down on his bed. He had Remus’ teashades on, with a spliff between his lips. The stereo was going—T. Rex to match his mopey mood—but he turned it down when Remus walked in.

“Wanna smoke?” Sirius asked, offering the half-finished joint. Glancing at it, Remus dropped his bag by his bed and walked over, before sitting down on the floor next to James’ bed and accepting the weed. He took a long draw, exhaling and resting his head back against James’ maroon bed covers.

“Why’d you say the study-date was Chastity’s idea?”

Sirius visibly winced, like he was hoping Remus would avoid the jugular for more than thirty seconds. “Dunno,” he muttered lightly, eyes hidden behind the sunglasses.

“Did you want them to fight?”

“No! I just, dunno… Wasn’t thinking, I guess.”

Remus examined the joint. “Liar.”

Sirius huffed and turned over onto his front, lifting the shades up onto his head. “So what do you want me to say?”

“How ‘bout the truth?”

“The truth?” He echoed. “The truth was, was that you’re spending all of your damn time studying and reading, and reading and studying—and it’s always with your bloody girlfriend!”

Remus was partly stunned. “That’s what you’re supposed to do with a girlfriend, innit?”

“No—well, yeah—but not all the time! Not so much that you forget your friends!”

“I haven’t forgotten anyone!”

“James and Pete have noticed it too. You know, they wanted to tell you that story with the incense themselves, but you were nowhere to be found.”

“I was just eating breakfast with—”

“With Marlene!”

Remus ground his teeth together, feeling heat spark in his cheeks. Had he really been avoiding his friends? No, not consciously of course, but between the need to beat Sirius in school and prove to himself that he was good enough to have a girlfriend it’d just been easier to play pretend-study with Marlene. They were so alike, but had enough differences to keep it interesting. Just like him and Sirius, he supposed.

Seemingly irritated by his silence, Sirius sat up and reached across the gap, plucking the joint from his fingers. Remus watched as he inhaled, those sharp cheekbones turning concave before he blew the smoke out the corner of his mouth and reached up and behind himself to tap the ash out into an ashtray he’d left on top of the stereo.

“Why didn’t you just tell me all this?” Remus asked.

Sirius thumbed the joint’s paper filter. “I don’t know. Felt weird.”

“It isn’t.”

Sirius glanced at him, eyes scanning him from head to toe. “It isn't...?”

“No. I didn’t mean to ignore you, Sirius.”

“I know.” Sirius dropped the teashades down over his eyes and took a drag. “Don’t flatter yourself—you’re incapable of ignoring me on purpose.”

He could’ve shot back a witty retort, he always had one, but instead Remus just smiled, because Sirius was right. “Next time you want to hang out, just tell me.”

Sirius lifted the shades again; “Yeah?”

“Yeah.”

“Okay, I want to hang out.”

Remus blinked. “Like… right now?”

“Yeah!”

“O-okay. What do you want to do?”

Sirius stopped, like he hadn’t considered getting this far. Finally he flopped back onto his stomach and held his hands out, waving them as he spoke; “You know that book thing with McKinnon that you're always doing?”

It took Remus a moment to understand; he'd forgotten he'd told Sirius about it. “The chapter-reading thing?”

“Yeah! I want to do that.”

“Oh, you’d probably just find it boring though.”

“No, I want to, really!”

“Okay… got a book?”

Sirius grinned and held Carrie aloft. “I’ve already read the first few chapters. It’s… interesting.”

Remus smiled and stood, crossing to his side of the room to pick up a book of his own from the ever-growing pile next to his bed. “You’re going to have to apologise to Marlene, too, by the way.”

Sirius slid down onto the floor and stretched his legs out. “Yeah, I know. Chas was a bit out of line.”

“A bit? Anyway, it’s not just that. Pince overheard the two of them arguing. We’re banned from using the study rooms for a month.”

“Aw, fuck. Reckon she’s likely to beat me now.”

“You do sort of deserve it.” Remus dropped down across from him, placing his legs just on the outside of Sirius’.

“So, what now?” Sirius asked, smacking his book on the ground lightly.

“Well, we read a chapter and then summarise it in twenty words or less, and then we trade and read the next chapter.”

“Doesn’t that get confusing?”

“You get the hang of it. It’s really only something Marlene and I do for fun.”

Sirius smirked. “Swot.”

“Git.”

They matched grins and each opened their books. It only took about ten pages for Remus to come to the conclusion that the book he’d picked, which had seemed a promising horror story, turned out to be a mere mash-up of cheap clichés and the odd sexual taboo or two, but he didn’t get much further than that anyway. Two minutes in Sirius had begun to bob his leg incessantly, and Remus ended up staring at it more often than he did the page.

“Are you done yet?” Sirius asked eventually.

“You’ve finished the chapter already?”

“No, but… ‘Pops’ is showing a rerun tonight. Supposed to be Jethro Tull, 10cc, and Smokie.”

Remus squinted at him, before shutting his book. “Okay, go on then.”

“Yes!” Sirius jumped up, setting the book aside and gently tapping out the second spliff they’d lit before grabbing his jumper. “Say,” he chirped, just as Remus got his boots on, “so long as we’re being honest, I have got this other question.”

“Shoot.”

“Why is it McKinnon’s always calling you ‘Rem’? I just mean, what’s that about?”

Remus stood up and shrugged innocently. “It’s a sports thing, I think. Like how the guys sometimes call James 'Pot'?”

“It’s weird.”

“That’s rich, coming from the guy who came up with ‘Moony’, ‘Wormtail’, and ‘Prongs’.”

Sirius threw the door open and clicked his tongue. “Aw, it’s cute of you to pretend you don’t totally love it. Now c’mon, I’ve been missing you and we’re not going to waste this evening by sitting together in utter fucking silence.”

“Heaven forbid.”



Chapter End Notes

Short, innocent little chapter, mostly because I've been so busy! Hope you guys still liked it, and happy Halloween. I think it's actually so fitting that Remus is a horror fan, even if I'm a big wuss myself, hehe.

In case you were unaware, a 'mondegreen' is a misunderstood or misinterpreted word or phrase resulting from mishearing of the lyrics of a song. Felt fitting somehow, since Remus and Sirius keep misunderstanding one another. (Things change soon though, I swear it!)

Chapter 53: People's Parties


Chapter Summary

March passes. Remus' comfort comes with a surprising confession.



Chapter Notes

CW: Allusions to child abuse, mostly manipulation and neglect. Smoking and drinking.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



On the dry and dusty road,

The nights we spend apart alone;

I need to get back home to cool, cool rain,

I can’t sleep, and I lay, and I think;

The night is hot and black as ink,

Woo, oh God, I need a drink of cool, cool, rain…

- “Love Reign O’er Me” The Who, 1973



March 1977

Remus knew his friends meant well, but his birthday had never really been of much interest to him. In fact, he loathed it. The whole thing made his stomach twist with uneasy memories and having to pretend that he was having an even-moderately good time was exhausting. The year before the girls had all but tricked him into having a party, but even then it was more about James and Lily getting over their spat. And seeing as how the pair were only more in love than ever, a sudden break up seemed unlikely.

Stubbornly, Remus had already flat-out refused to let Sirius use his birthday as an excuse to throw a party in the common room, which he acquiesced to—bitterly—perhaps only because James’ seventeenth was a few weeks away and on a weekend anyway. It was a small mercy, and afterwards even the girls gave up pestering him. Suddenly all talk of his birthday became null. Remus could hardly believe it—they were actually listening to him.

Ha, complete bullshit. Sure, Remus didn’t want to hear about any chatter over his birthday, so what did his namby, over-achieving friends do? They planned a surprise party of course.

Now, with surprise parties, the ‘surprise’ bit tended to be crucial; but none of his friends were known for being particularly proficient at lying, and they all talked too much anyway. The real shock came when Lily was the first one to give up the ghost. Her agenda had mysteriously disappeared (it turned up later in James’ bag) and she was scrambling to remember her meticulously planned school week on a piece of scrap paper.

“When did we say we were going to compare history essays again?” She asked, her face flushed with worry.

“Wednesday night?” Remus supplied.

"Uh-uh, I've prefect stuff!"

"Thursday?"

“No, that’s the night of your party!”

Lily had immediately shot upright and Remus sighed, already tired. “Party?”

“Oh, don’t tell anyone I told you!" She moaned. "It was supposed to be a surprise.”

“I thought we agreed no parties.”

“It’s just a small one! We were gonna do it in your guys’ room. We have to do something, Remus, it’s your birthday!”

He was irritated, but Lily just batted those big green eyes of hers and he caved. “Fine, but I’m not going to pretend to be surprised or anything.”

Lily had to accept that, but her accidental confession got the gears turning in his head. If it was that easy to get Lily Evans to fess up, how would his other friends fare?

Peter and Lottie were easy of course. Neither of the twins could keep a secret to save their life, but James had been slightly tougher. He’d finally broken when Remus turned the tables, making it sound as though he was sad his friends were willing to forget his birthday all together.

“Yeah, I dunno. I guess I’m just a little bummed, but my birthday is on a Thursday and we’re all so busy, so I get it.”

“No, Moony!” James tried. “I swear we haven’t forgotten!”

“Oh I know, it’s just…” he sighed, “but it’s okay, we’ll do something real grand for your birthday.”

“We’re doing something for yours too!”

“Oh… really?”

“Yeah! It was supposed to be a surprise, I swear!”

“A surprise?”

“Mhm! So you don’t have to… worry…” James stopped, because he’d noticed the evil grin on Remus’ face. “You dick,” he hissed immediately. “Who told you?”

“You did, just now.”

James put his head in his hands. “Don’t tell Lily,” he mumbled.

And he didn’t, because it was so funny that they all thought they’d spilled the beans on their own. The last one he managed to get to fess up was Mary, who did so with little effort on his behalf, as she was too busy defending her favourite pop group to notice.

“There’s an ABBA song for everything,” she'd declared.

“Even funerals?” Remus had sassed.

“Sure. Send off your grandma with ‘Hasta Mañana’ and I guarantee there won’t be a dry eye in the room.”

“And yet I remain unconvinced.”

“Fine, I’ll just have to prove it to you tomorrow.”

“Hmm, can’t. I’m busy tomorrow actually.”

“No you’re not, you’ll be with us celebrating your—fuck.”

It was funny, but the only ones who refused to crack were Sirius and Marlene. They’d been considerably good at dancing around the subject of his birthday, even when he got weepy over it like he had with James. Remus was fully prepared to call them on their icy hearts, only he hadn’t planned for the significant derailment. If he had, things would’ve gone a lot differently.

On the morning of his seventeenth birthday Remus woke up to a friendly dog-pile and a delicious breakfast organised by James and his favourite lunch lady. He was sung to, congratulated, and then afterwards, guided around by an unsuspecting Marlene.

“I still don’t see why I can’t go back to my room and get my other coat,” he pushed cheekily. "It's freezing out here."

“Here, you can have mine,” she offered quickly, shrugging off her oversized leather jacket and draping it around his shoulders. She did her best not to look chilly without it, but they were on a walk around the lake to undoubtedly kill time and it was already getting dark.

“I know, you know,” Remus said, taking off the jacket and passing it back. Marlene took it, her mouth dropping open into a sour ‘o’.

“How—who told you?”

“All of them,” he smirked. “ ‘Cept Sirius.”

Marlene moaned and checked her watch. “Fine, whatever, it’s about time we got back anyway.”

“I promise to act surprised,” he told her as they turned around.

“You’d better!" Marlene said, jabbing him in the arm with her finger. "I was counting on it being funny, Lily was going to snap a picture!”

“Well how’s this?” He threw up his hands. “ ‘Oh my god, I had no idea—you guys really got me’!”

“Try for a little less sarcasm.”

“Now you’re just asking for the impossible.”

They took the evening trolley back to the dorms, where Marlene stopped him, checking her watch once more. “Just do us a favour and hang out in the common room for a bit. Black’s got detention and he wanted to be there when you came up, and considering he’s the only one who didn’t blow the gaff, I think he deserves to be in on it.”

“Of course he does,” Remus smiled. “It’s fine, I was gonna make a call anyway.”

She beamed. “To your friends back home? Say hi for me.”

“Kay.”

Stretching up onto her tiptoes, Marlene gave him a quick kiss on the cheek before escaping up the stairs to their dorm, shrugging off her jacket as she went. Remus watched her go before he crossed the hall to the phones, where he picked up the receiver and pounded the flat’s number. It’d been over two weeks since he’d heard from Tomny or Tonya, but today was his birthday, dammit! And he was determined to keep calling until someone bloody well picked up.

The phone rang once in his ear, then clicked on and Remus huffed, ready to give his friend a piece of his mind.

“Tom! Hey! Why you been ignoring—”

‘We’re sorry, the number you have reached is not in service, or is temporarily disconnected. The number you have reached is not in service at this time. This is a recording.’

Remus’ stomach dropped to the floor as the intercept message droned on in his ear.

‘If you feel you have reached this recording in error, please check the number and try your call again. Goodbye.'

The line clicked dead, and Remus faltered. It was a mistake, had to be—he’d just entered the number wrong. The number he’d had memorised ever since Tomny had given it to him. He'd just entered it too fast. That was it. He dialled again.

‘We’re sorry, the number you have reached is not—’

His hands were shaky that time. Again.

‘We’re sorry, the number—’

Again.

‘We’re sorry—’

“No!” Remus wailed, slamming his fist against the wall beside the phone. He couldn’t listen to the message anymore, so finally he set the receiver down, jaw clenched so tightly his teeth ached. There were plenty of reasons why the phone wasn’t working; maybe Tomny had forgotten to pay the bill—he did that sometimes with the gas or electric, but it hadn’t happened since Tonya had come. Maybe they’d gotten drunk and busted the phone, or maybe they were having issues with the telephone company. There were so many unexciting, mundane reasons why he shouldn’t be worrying, and yet, there were just as many horrible excuses to do just that. Problems with money, a fallout with Burrin, a break-in at the flat, a fight amongst themselves. All were just as probable as the mundane, but none scared him as much as the thought that they were all gone—that the flat was sitting empty or now had new tenants. That they’d said nothing and left him behind. That someone had...

Marlene would’ve told him he was jumping to conclusions—worrying himself for no reason, but at least she knew something about it—not a lot, but something. She and her family understood what it was like to live near the bottom. They’d struggled to make ends meet before, followed the politics that affected the little people. She’d understand. He just needed to talk to Marlene.

Practically running, Remus threw himself up the stairs to the fourth floor, arriving wide-eyed and out of breath. He only stopped—right before his bedroom door—when it occurred to him that six of his friends were just on the other side, waiting to shout and cheer and have a good time. He could hear the girls’ laughter as ABBA seeped out from beneath the door like a poor joke;

‘Knowing me, knowing you,

There is nothing we can do;

Knowing me, knowing you,

We just have to face it, this time we’re through;

Breaking up is never easy, I know but I have to go,

Knowing me, knowing you,

It’s the best I can do …’

Remus was instantly sobered. Mary was right; there was an ABBA song for everything.

“You gonna stand there all day or are you going in?” Sirius asked, a merry ring in his voice. Remus looked up to see him walking toward him, hands in his pockets and a happy smile on his face. “Did ya lose your key? I got mine right here, just say the word.”

Deadly quiet, Remus stepped back from the door and marched down the hallway, blazing past Sirius and reaching the stairs in an instant.

“Woah,” Sirius called; "Where are you going? We—there’s something—”

“I know about the party, and I’m not going in there,” Remus snapped, slamming to a halt on the top stair.

“A-Alright…” Sirius pulled his hands out of his pockets, “but you know we didn’t mean to upset you or anything.”

“You didn’t!”

“So you’re pissed off for no reason…?”

“No!” Remus grunted. He felt like he might explode if he stayed any longer. “I just can’t go in there.”

Sirius bit his lip. “Okay… What do you want to do?”

“I don’t know—go. I need to get out of here.”

“Well, do you mind if I come with you? You just… no one should be alone on their birthday, right?”

Remus was a little stunned, but he turned away sharply and took a few more stairs down. Finally he looked back. Sirius was still standing in the middle of the hall, rubbing the back of his neck sorely. “Well?” He demanded. “You coming or not?”

Eyes wide, Sirius sprung forward. Together they wordlessly continued down and out, marching across campus one behind the other. They walked aimlessly at first, Remus sharply changing directions every few minutes to keep his mind from wandering back to the flat. Sirius never questioned it, and didn’t speak either, which he was grateful for. Finally, Remus figured out where it was he wanted to be, and started toward the right building with long, purposeful strides. Sirius had no trouble keeping up.

When they made it to the astronomy building, Remus popped the lock. The cool air inside was a relief. He’d felt stifled in the dorm, but the openness of the night sky had made him feel as though he were going to drift right up into open space. He needed something to ground him, and the dark, wide space of the telescope hub did just that.

Sirius gawked up at the domed ceiling of the circular room. “Bloody hell, Moony, you’ve really scoped out every hiding spot on campus, haven’t you? I never saw this place on that map of yours.”

Partly ignoring him, Remus crossed the room to the far wall and collapsed against it. “Shut the door,” he said, and Sirius did so, leaving them in near-complete darkness apart from the faint glow of a single desk lamp spilling through the glass window of the research room next door. Remus withdrew the couple of spliffs he’d been keeping in his pocket for the party and lit one. A moment later Sirius came to join him against the wall and after a long drag, he passed the joint along.

“That’s a big telescope,” Sirius said, observing the ginormous device that took up most of the centre of the room. He held the spliff to his lips before speaking around it; “Maybe I should take astronomy next year.”

“Would’a thought you Blacks knew enough about stars,” Remus quipped. There was no humour behind it, but Sirius laughed anyway.

“You’re probably right. Every time I cracked a book to study I’d be reminded of some horrible second cousin or something.”

“As if you study.”

“Touché.” Sirius passed the joint back. “So do you want to talk about what’s got you so wound up?”

“No,” Remus answered, leaning his head back against the wall. “I just… want to be quiet for a bit.”

“Alright then.” Sirius leaned his chin on his hand and began bobbing one foot, but he was quiet.

“Tell me a story,” Remus said suddenly.

“Thought you wanted quiet? You’re being contradictory.”

“I’m a contradictory guy.”

Sirius sat up a bit. “Do you want to ask each other questions again?”

“No, I just want to hear you talk.”

“Okay,” Sirius breathed, taking a second to think. “Did I ever tell you about Gisela?”

“Who’s she, another girlfriend?”

Sirius chuckled. “No, she was mine and Reg’s governess when we were kids. She watched us before we went away for school and again whenever we came home for holiday. We adored her. She would always hide sweets under our pillows for when we woke up and sometimes in the summer they’d melt and just make this horrible mess but she still did it. And she used to let us use the maps in the drawing room as play mats and we’d make little army men out of sticks and bits of rubbish and argue over who took over what country. Mum hated it of course, but Gisela thought it was ‘good for our development’. Made us resourceful or whatever.”

“And what happened to her?”

“Dunno.” Sirius pulled his knees up to his chest. “When I was about seven or eight she and the gardener disappeared.”

“It’s always the gardener.”

“Yeah," Sirius chuckled. "And they took with them the twenty-thousand pounds they’d stolen from my father’s safe.”

Remus paused, joint halfway to his lips. “She robbed you?”

Sirius shrugged. “Didn’t feel like she was robbing me. Dad maybe, but Dad's pockets always felt like black holes. I was smart but I didn’t have any real concept of money.”

“Wow. Just when you think you know someone…”

“Oh, I knew. I was the one who gave her the code.”

Remus blinked. “Hold on, you helped her rob you?”

“Guess it was a big thing back then, but obviously it didn’t put much of a dent in the Black family fortune. And I didn't care. I just wanted to make her happy.” Pausing, Sirius bit his lip. “You know, I’ve never told anyone that…”

Sirius began scratching at the floor with his fingernails and Remus stared down at the joint, before offering it. “I used to go on these treasure hunts for my mum," he said quietly. "That’s what she called ‘em anyway.”

Looking up, Sirius raised a brow and took the spliff. “Treasure hunts? What sort of treasure?”

“Not the kind that would excite a kid. It was medicine—pills mostly. I don’t think Dad wanted her to have ‘em. These men—sometimes they were ‘doctors’ other times they were other ‘buccaneers’—they’d come 'round the house when he was away and leave packages in the mailbox or hide them in the bushes.” Remus chuckled darkly, shaking his head at the ridiculousness of it all. “I’d go down and get them and sneak them back inside for her. Eventually I had to start hiding them under my shirt or Giles would take them. I didn’t always know what was inside but I didn’t really care.”

“So why’d you do it then?”

“I guess... because I wanted to make her happy.”

Sirius took a deep breath. “It’s fucked up, man.”

“Yeah. But we turned out alright in the end, right? You’re a genius, albeit a lazy one—”

Sirius’ arm shot out, wagging a finger at him. “And you’re the only person on planet earth, Remus Lupin, that can make someone feel better about themselves by making them feel worse!”

Smirking, Remus lit another spliff and held it aloft. “Cheers to that, Black.”

Sirius shook his head. “Oi, toss your lighter here.”

He did so and Sirius stuck his hand in his pocket, withdrawing something. Remus had to squint in the low light to see what it was, but when he realised he couldn’t help his surprise. “Is that one of Bob’s firecrackers?”

“Yup,” Sirius smirked. “I was gonna freak the girls out by playing at putting it on top of your cake, but guess since we don’t have one of those around…”

He jumped up to his feet and Remus followed suit, stepping in close as Sirius lit the fuse and it sputtered to life. “Make a wish,” he said, before chucking the little firework across the room. It cleared the whole space and bounced off the other side of the circular walls at least twenty feet from them before going off with a noise so loud it reverberated around the room like trapped thunder. Sirius whooped, punching the air as dots of light covered Remus’ vision.

“Yes!” He shouted. “Fuck silence!”

Remus coughed out his laughter and Sirius was right there, pushing a second firecracker into his palm. “Do it, Moony,” he said. He passed him the lighter, their fingers fumbling against one another in the dark, and Remus flicked the flame to life, bringing the fuse toward it. He held the firecracker for a few long seconds, entranced by the way the flame desperately licked down the wick toward its inevitable doom. In it he pictured Tomny, running in a life that would only lead to rougher and rougher landscapes. He pictured Tonya, a born traveller who’d willingly locked herself up inside a flat she hated and for what—love? He saw his father and the misery he’d embraced as his everyday, and his mother who’d gone and left him instead.

Remus threw the firecracker. It exploded above their heads, without even making it to the other-side of the room. The noise was deafening and wonderful.

“Fuck yeah!” Sirius screamed.

“Fuck!” Remus wailed. “Fuck you!”

“Yeah, fuck you!”

“FUCK YOU!”

Sirius clapped him on the back, grinning sadly. “Fuck them.”

“Do you have another?” Remus breathed.

“No, sorry. That’s it, mate.”

He sagged against the wall, half in disappointment and half in relief. “It’s alright. I just… I needed that.”

“I know.” Sirius came to join him at the wall, tucking his hands behind him. Remus scooped the joint he’d dropped up off the floor and relit it, sucking in and passing it along to him. Sirius held it to his lips, before pausing; “Have you ever just wanted to get something off your chest so desperately it feels as though you’re drowning?”

“Yes,” Remus said, truthfully.

“Do you remember the last question you asked me outside the pub?”

Remus’ heart jumped. “ ‘What happened with Miles’.”

“He was... sick,” Sirius said after a long pause; “That wasn’t a lie, but there was other stuff too. He and I… we used to write each other these letters. We’d write all the things we couldn’t bring ourselves to say out loud and then trade. It was like a game at first. 'You couldn’t say it but you could write it down'. It made stuff feel… I don’t know—safer.”

“Like Gisela.”

“Yeah, and other stuff too. Anyway, one day when he was home for Christmas I guess his grandparents found one of the letters or something. They almost didn’t let him come back to school, but he did and we… man, I really liked Miles.”

Sirius brought the spliff to his lips sharply and breathed in. His hand—his perfectly steady musician’s hand—was trembling.

“I get it,” Remus said.

“You do?” Sirius’ gaze snapped to him.

“Well, yeah. He was your friend.”

Sirius deflated. “Then you don’t get it. I liked him—and he liked me too. That was the problem, don’t you see?”

Remus felt something twist in his gut. “So that means you… oh.”

“Yeah.”

“With… boys?”

“And girls.” Sirius crossed his arms haughtily. “So you get it now, why I couldn’t tell the others?”

Remus was stunned into silence. Never before had he considered… Sirius was a boy, and Miles was a boy, and… Jesus.

“Well say something!” Sirius pushed.

Remus scrambled; “I… Wow. I just didn’t expect that… I mean, you date a lot of girls, Sirius.”

Sirius scoffed. “What about you? You mean to say that there’s nothing going on between you and that ‘Tom’ guy?”

“What? Tomny—no! He’s dating Tonya.”

“You’re always on the phone with him.”

“Not always.”

Sirius knocked the ash off the end of the spliff. He handed it back, not looking at him. “Oh.”

Remus stared down at the weed before taking it. Sirius’ fingers were warm.

“Their phone’s down,” he confessed. “I was… I am worried. It’s never happened before and they’re—they’re not like you and me. I think they’re part of a gang now.”

Sirius’ mouth pinched together like he wasn’t sure if he should be impressed or apologetic. “A gang? That’s who you’re friends with?”

“They weren’t into all of it when we met. It was just fun, then.”

“Well, guess that explains a lot about you,” Sirius said. Remus looked at him questioningly and he tapped his own nose so he understood.

“Oh, yeah." Remus reached up to run his fingers across his scar. "It was awful. Tomny blamed himself for it.”

“I hope he at least killed the guy who did it. It’s such a shame—marking up your face like that.”

“You saying I’m ugly now?”

“Nope, not saying that at all. Handsomest Lupin around.”

“I’m the only Lupin around.”

“That’s convienent, isn’t it?”

Remus tipped his head forward to hide a smile. Sirius watched him and when their eyes met again he bit his lip. “I won’t tell anyone about you and Miles. I swear.”

“Didn’t think you would, but thanks,” Sirius said, crossing his ankles. “I mean it’s cool right? You’re with McKinnon and I’ve got Chas, so… it’s cool. All of it.”

“Yeah… cool.”

“And I trust you, you know,” Sirius said, knocking him on the thigh, “I do.”

“I trust you too.”

“Good. Oh, and Remus?”

He looked up in earnest. “Yeah?”

“Happy birthday.”

“Thanks, Sirius.”

They sat together for a long time and when they’d run out of weed and the darkness began to feel stifling they walked. All over the campus they went, killing time until midnight had come and gone and rather than being Remus' birthday, it was just any other early morning in late winter. When they finally returned to the dorm during those wee hours, they found their friends waiting for them. None of them were happy, but his and Sirius’ quiet moods were enough to cue in on, and each of the girls simply kissed him on the cheek and left.

"Sorry guys. Didn't mean to ruin the night," Remus said, while his friends slipped into bed. James turned around, shaking his head kindly.

"Don't be. We're just glad you're okay."

"Yeah," Peter yawned. "Besides, we got to eat all your cake."

Everyone snorted, and James took off his glasses while Peter pulled his bed curtains shut. Sirius, who had been reclining on his bed, sat up and reached for his own curtains. Catching Remus' eye, he raised his chin and winked before shutting out the light. A second later a chorus went up; "Happy birthday, Moons."

"Yeah, happy birthday to Moony."

"Happy birthday, mate!"

Remus laid down in his bed. His voice was a whisper; "Thanks guys."

He tried the flat several more times after that. The line was never reconnected.

Eventually Remus stopped calling.





* * *





On the day of James Potter’s seventeenth birthday, the sky over Hawkings opened up and poured like the heavens themselves were in mourning. The water came down in sheets so heavy that the moment you stepped outside you were soaked to the bone. And it just kept coming. All day it rained, battering the windows of their dorm with the ferocity of a thousand Big Bad Wolves. The rain was so incessant that it would end up washing out the bit of road behind the science building, forcing the trolley routes to change for the remainder of term while also flooding the football pitch so badly players were slipping around in mud for weeks afterwards. It was a Sunday, which meant no classes at least, but the trek to breakfast was miserable and by the time they reached the hall their wellies were filled up from the top down.

“If April showers bring May flowers, what do bloody March downpours bring?” Peter asked dolefully.

“Good luck,” James answered, shaking out his soaked curls and beaming all the while.

James truly was brilliant, Remus knew. The rain would’ve ruined anyone else’s mood—and it did—but not his. No rain could dampen James Potter’s tenor, not even on his own birthday.

Like the rest of them, Sirius had been less excited about the weather, thinking mostly about how it would dull the affairs they had planned for the evening, but by the time they were loping back across campus after class, he’d given up the bad mood and tipped his head back to feel the water spatter him on his cheeks and eyelids. He’d waited until they were outside Godric to stop and do this, and each of his friends yelled at him from the front steps to come inside.

“No!” He called. “You have to feel this! It's like—like rebirth! This is what it means to start over, I know it! To get another chance!”

“The only thing you're gonna get is a cold!” Remus reasoned.

“I don’t believe in coincidences! What song were we just playing yesterday—‘The Rain Song’! ‘Upon us all a little rain must fall—just a little rain’!”

“He’s finally gone mental,” Peter moaned over the noise of the rain. “He’s quoting Zeppelin in the middle of a storm.”

“No, I think I get it,” James said, shucking off his coat and skipping down the dorm’s steps to join his best friend in the rain. Sirius jumped when he saw him, throwing his own jacket aside and taking James’ hand as he let loose a war-cry of pure exhilaration. James matched it, and they swung each other around through the lawn’s grassy puddles until they were both sprawling and laughing.

“Oi,” Kenny said, sticking his head out the front door; “What are they doing? They’re not drunk already are they?”

“No,” Remus answered, “they’re being reborn.”

Kenny shook his head like they were all crazy and ducked back inside as a shivering Peter did the same. Remus stayed, and eventually he sat down on the steps, pulling off his jacket hood and leaning his chin on his arms. They probably were mental, but if Remus understood anything, it was that what Sirius and James were experiencing at that very moment was as close as any of them would ever get to feeling like gods.

So he watched, and he thought the same thought he’d been thinking for the past three weeks, because it was impossible not to think about. It was a revelation that he hadn’t seen coming and yet after a month of thinking, he was still unable to comprehend how he’d missed it. Sirius must’ve done it on purpose just to mess with him. Just to make it so the few hours of sleep he got a night were plagued with wild thoughts and even wilder dreams. So that wherever he went, whether it be alone or in the company of others, he was always thinking about him. And it worked.

Sirius Black liked girls.

And boys.

And apart from the mysterious roommate who’d disappeared late their tenth year, he was the only person on earth who knew.

Fucking hell.

Remus had never put much stock in being gay. He’d never known anyone who was—probably. It was an out-of-sight, out-of-mind sort of thing, wasn’t it? He’d thought once that maybe Lyall was a bit buggered, after all he’d never remarried, but at the time it was just another way to slander his father in his head. Now it made him feel guilty—he would never have said anything like that to Sirius, though he supposed that Sirius wasn’t gay, not as long as he liked both guys and girls. He wondered if there was a way you could be both, but he couldn't fathom how that would work. Tomny had had a girlfriend once named Viola who claimed to go both ways, but she only ever kissed other girls while drunk. It seemed to him at the time that she only did it to show off to other guys, but Tomny never seemed to care and he’d only dated Viola for a few months anyway.

Remus tried not to think about Tomny much. He’d told himself after the third week of zero contact that Tomny had moved on, or was gone—anything to keep from dwelling, but that too, was impossible. There were too many unanswered questions, too many unknown variables. Several times he’d almost considered just up and leaving—hitch-hike to the nearest train station and catch a ride back to London to see for himself what had happened, but eventually he’d started confessing these ideas to Sirius who was always somehow able to talk him down. Perhaps it was because Sirius claimed they were moments of strength.

“They should be grateful for your loyalty,” he’d always say. And afterwards Remus would be able to sleep, for a little while.

It was a strange dynamic. By day Sirius was his worst nightmare—a plague of cheeky remarks and grudgingly handsome looks—and by night he was his saviour. He’d tell more stories about Gisela or things that had happened to him and the boys as they grew up at school, and for once he did not dance around the mention of Miles. Remus learned that things between them hadn’t changed until their tenth year. Before then they’d been best friends like anyone else, but unlike James or Pete, Miles understood what it was like to not enjoy going home for the holidays. Sirius had grappled onto that.

In exchange for his honesty, Remus told him bits of what it was like living at the flat. Sometimes it was hard—just getting the words out felt like he was regurgitating glass—but other times it was easy. He mostly talked about Lee and Doss and Seesaw, and also Flacky who’d died too young. He mentioned little about Tomny or Tonya, perhaps only because they confused him the most now, but also because he blamed them more than the others.

Soon it became clear that they’d unintentionally become each other’s secret-keepers. It wasn’t as though James, Lily, Marlene, or any of the rest of them weren’t trustworthy, but in the early hours of the morning when he couldn’t sleep, the only one he wanted to talk to was Sirius. Because, as he was coming to realise, Sirius understood. He knew what it was like to be left behind, to ache in the absence of someone. But where he now had Sirius, Sirius had had no one. It made Remus want to swear undying loyalty to him, and so he did—silently. He promised himself that girls or boys, he would always be there for Sirius, because that’s what a good friend would do.

“C’mon, Moony! You have to feel this!” Sirius shouted. His voice carried across the heavy rain, aided thanks to James, who had lifted him onto his shoulders in a great hurrah. Seeing them so happy together didn’t require much more convincing, and a moment later Remus had peeled out of his coat (it was already soaked through anyway) and joined them on the squelching grass. James high-fived him and Sirius tipped forward, sprawling off his friend’s shoulders and forcing Remus to catch him, which he did, badly. They went down onto the muddy lawn in a heap and James piled on top of them. It was exhilarating.

It made him wonder if maybe he didn’t hate the rain so much after all.





* * *





Walking into their room, Remus found James adjusting their waterlogged shoes over the radiator to ensure that they were all drying as efficiently as possible. He’d been confined to the bedroom since they’d returned from breakfast while the rest of them set up downstairs. They’d done a spectacular job, if Remus said so himself. Red and white streamers in honour of James’ favourite football team had been taped to every surface and various banners had been constructed bearing the words ‘Congratulations on completing rehab!’ and ‘So glad you beat the blow!’ There were a few obligatory happy birthday’s too, but those were much smaller.

The girls on the other hand had enlisted the help of the baking club to bake not one, not two, but seventeen birthday cakes—which was just as well, really, since Sirius seemed to have invited half the school. Remus had taken it upon himself to organise the music, hauling Sirius’ stereo down to the common room along with his vinyls and impressive collection of 8-track tapes. He’d meticulously organised the albums in order of playability—starting off strong with Exile on Main St. and following it up with James’ favourite, the Kinks’ Face to Face . After that he’d allowed himself a little wiggle room to read the crowd’s vibes, but all in all it was a strong lineup.

“Can I bloody well come down now?” James grinned when he spotted him. “We all know today’s just an excuse to party.”

“No, we’re celebrating the birth of our dearest friend,” Remus said, feigning distress.

“Well this ‘dearest friend’ is going stir-crazy. All I can hear is rain pattering the roof and you took all the music.”

“Alright, you can come down, but there’s one more thing.” From behind his back Remus pulled a party hat, lovingly constructed by Peter with a pair of paper antlers extending from either side. James looked at the thing with a mixture of shock and disappointment before sighing and holding out his hand.

“You really are such a good sport, Prongs,” Remus snorted, coming forward and looping the hat and string around James’ chin himself. He reached up to bat playfully at one of his antlers, a joke he knew no one else apart from the four of them would get, and James shook his head hopelessly.

When they made their way downstairs, past the tower of rain boots and coats, everyone was waiting. They exploded with a huge rally of ‘HAPPY BIRTHDAY JAMES!’ to which James responded by throwing his arms up in the air and screaming back with equal amounts of energy. Sirius bounded forward, punching him in the arm affectionately and everyone else followed up with pats and congratulations of their own. The record player started, and Marlene appeared at Remus’ side with a drink for him and they cheersed before downing the entire thing in one go. Marlene belched immediately, embarrassed, but Remus only pulled her close and blew a raspberry on her cheek.

If the rain did anything, it dulled the noise. From the outside the dorm looked almost average, with hardly any indication that there were over a hundred kids inside, smoking, drinking, and behaving in a rather non-religious manner. A dance floor had opened up in the middle of the common room and at one point Sirius and Peter began aggressively shaking a beer can each, before cracking the tabs to let the foam spray out over the heads of everyone within ten feet of them. Lottie, who’d supposedly spent hours taming her curls against the humid rain, just about throttled her brother in the middle of the dance floor. Around them people cracked windows to let out the smoke and younger kids weaved in and out, stealing booze and smokes as though they were pick-pockets on the street. When the girls brought out the cakes James nearly passed out at the sheer number of them, each one decorated with seventeen candles each. He blew them out one by one and everyone cheered, crowding around to get a slice.

“Remus!” Lily called over the guffaw. “We have something for you!”

He turned to find her and Marlene standing together, holding a chocolate cake between them. “Another cake?” He asked. “I think you’re immensely overestimating James’ sweet tooth.”

“This one’s not for James,” Marlene amended. “It’s yours, to make up for the birthday you skipped out on.”

Remus laughed awkwardly. “Oh, thanks. You didn't have to do that.”

"We know," Marlene grinned.

“And don’t thank us just yet,” Lily said. It sounded like a warning, but before anything could be done, she and Marlene grabbed hold of the back of his head and yanked him forward, slamming the cake into his face. Remus moaned, temporarily blinded by icing while plenty of people turned to laugh.

“So how’s it taste?” Marlene sniggered. Remus dug the chocolate from his eyes and sighed before sucking even more off of his thumb.

“Delicious. Want to try some?” He surged forward for a kiss and Marlene shrieked, shooting away with Lily.

“Need a towel?” A high-voice chimed, and Remus turned to find Pandora of all people. The towel in question was in fact not a towel, but a crochet doily, which he took anyway and thanked her for. She smiled and handed him a drink, knocking her own against it before flouncing back to a set of maroon couches where Xeno was sitting amongst a group of kids, looking even more hippy-ish than normal in an open-chested poet’s shirt.

As he cleaned himself up best he could, Mary passed him on the arm of some guy—Grayson Kent, he realised. “Oi, Remus, your tape’s skippin’!” She shouted, and he strained his ears to find that she was right. Picking his away across the room, he finished his drink and passed off the empty cup before crouching down in front of the hi-fi. He found, irritatingly, that his carefully curated album piles had been messed with, throwing everything out of whack. Unable and unwilling to reorganise everything in his inebriated state, he instead began searching for one of the LPs Andy had gotten Sirius for Christmas, but couldn’t find anything among the mess anyway.

“MOONY! PSST—OI, MOONY!” Sirius wailed from the corner of the room, where he and Chastity were tucked up against an open window, sharing a cigarette. “PLAY SOME RAINBOW!” Sirius continued, making Chastity giggle and whisper something in his ear. “S’a rock band!” He slurred back. “Their guitarist was in Deep Purple!”

Suddenly disinterested, Remus grabbed a random tape from the piles that he thought belonged to the Doors, and slammed it into the stereo, hitting play. He was about four steps away when the first moan cut through the air, making him and everyone around him slam to an utter halt.

“What in the Black Sabbath insanity is this?” Another kid said aloud, but it was too late, the sex tape picked up mid-shag—exactly where it’d left off all those months ago in their eleventh year, when they’d discovered it inside the borrowed hi-fi while hiding away within the guts of the church’s organ balcony.

Remus scrambled back to the stereo as the whole room burst into staggered laughter and slammed his finger on the eject button, yanking out the tape like it was a bomb about to go off.

“Blimey!” Sirius announced. “I thought I’d lost that!”

Chastity gaped; “That’s yours?”

“What? No! I just—Moony tell her!”

Remus threw the tape at him and Sirius scrambled to catch it.

“C’mon Black, if you’re going to engage in such filthy hobbies you should really keep them to yourself.”

Remus turned away, cuing up another album while feeling mightily pleased with himself. As Sirius did his best to convince Chastity that it wasn’t his sex tape (“Look at the tape’s date, Chas—1972!”) Remus scanned the room for Marlene. He spotted her on one of the sofas, tucked up between Nicole and Anna. The entire team had been invited—James’ orders—and Remus was glad for it as he bent over the back of the sofa and dangled a joint between the girls’ heads.

“Ladies, care to partake in some of the 'devil's lettuce'?”

“Oooh, yes please,” Nicole said eagerly. Marlene looked sceptical—she wasn’t usually one for weed—but nodded along with Anna and the four of them stood, making their way out into the hall. Remus realised halfway to the back door that he’d leant Sirius his lighter and turned around to get it, only to come to an abrupt halt as a drunken James stood up on a chair, shouting over the crowd.

“HELLO! YES! EVER’ONE SHUT UP I HAVE SUMTHIN’ I WANNA SAY!”

The record scratched off, courtesy of Sirius, and James cleared his throat; “Firs' of all, thank yeh to my idiot friends, wherever you may be, for the wonderful decor. I’m sure my mum's so proud I kicked that nasty blow habit—and I know nunn'of yeh will tell 'er about the drinkin' problem because we all got one!”

Plenty of kids snickered and held up drinks—'Hear! Hear!’

“Thank yeh to the girls for the many, many cakes! And of course thank you tah ever’one for showin’ up!” James continued, nearly tripping off the chair. “Now n'gonna play you all a song, and I want to dedicate it to my beautiful girlfriend, Lily!”

“Oh my god,” someone nearby moaned. Remus looked to his left to find Lily, a drink in one hand and the other pressed to her pink cheek. She was wearing James’ party hat.

He smirked and sidled up next to her, bending over to obstruct her view. “You’re looking a little redder than usual, Evans.”

“Buzz off,” Lily chuckled weakly.

“Maestro, the music please!” James called.

“Yes, sir!” Sirius announced, before hitting play on the hi-fi. Remus wasn’t sure what he was expecting, but it certainly wasn’t “Let’s Get It On”.

“WRONG SONG, SIRIUS!” James threw himself down from the chair while everyone laughed and Remus put his arm around Lily as she just about folded in on herself from embarrassment.

“Those idiots,” she moaned.

“Could always be worse,” Remus reasoned; “He could be playing you a song on the guitar himself in front of everyone.”

Lily dropped her hand from her cheek and held her heart instead. “Oh thank Lord he’s not. I couldn’t take it. I’m already so embarrassed, I knew I should’ve waited to tell him.”

“Tell him what?”

Lily pressed her lips together before blurting out; “I told him I loved him.”

Remus gasped. “You did not!”

“He was so happy—and I wanted it to be special so I thought I’d do it on his birthday—ah! It’s so embarrassing.”

The song shifted and James got back up onto his chair, holding a hand over his eyes and scanning the room until he ultimately spotted the two of them. “DAISY! This one’s for you!” He pointed at Lily with his beer. “I love you too, babe!”

James had chosen a Fleetwood Mac song, and it floated out around the room;

‘Sweet wonderful you,

You make me happy with the things you do;

Oh, can it be so,

This feeling follows me wherever I go…’

Listening like the rest of them, Lily sighed, too happy and too embarrassed.

“You’re gonna marry him, right?” Remus asked teasingly. “ ‘Cause he might die of heartbreak if you don’t.”

“Only if I don’t kill him first. It’s a good thing he’s cute.”

They shared a cheeky look while Sirius raised his drink in the air; “To Daisy!” He shouted. James did the same and everyone cheered; “TO DAISY!”

Sportingly, Lily held her drink aloft before downing it all as Fleetwood Mac sang directly to her;

‘I never did believe in miracles,

But I’ve a feeling it’s time to try;

I never did believe in the ways of magic,

But I’m beginning to wonder why…’

James launched himself off the chair, streaking toward them. Other kids parted automatically to let him through and when he made it to Lily he scooped her up so she could wrap her legs around his waist and kiss him.

Lifting his fingers to his mouth, Remus whistled and Lily broke apart from James to swat the air in front of his face. Undeterred, James peppered her cheek with kisses instead, the complete and utter embodiment of a man in love.

The rest of the night went off without a hitch. The rain continued to pour, and Remus did not think of Tomny or London even once.



Chapter End Notes

To ‘give up the ghost’ means to give up or stop working.

‘Blow the gaff’ means to reveal a secret.

Sorry if it feels like I'm teasing you, but I did say this chapter would rock your socks. Next one is gonna be... fun :^)





Chapter 54: Charity Case


Chapter Summary

Baby cows! Bad friends! unBelievable realisations!



Chapter Notes

CW: Discussions of classism and bullying.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Oh, you’re the best friend that I ever had,

I’ve been with you such a long time;

You’re my sunshine and I want you to know,

That my feelings are true;

I really love you,

Oh, you’re my best friend…

- “You’re My Best Friend” Queen, 1975



Monday 4th April 1977

Calving season had come early to Hawkings. Just a few days before they were all scheduled to head home for the week-long Easter holiday, it was announced that Professor Kettleburn had invited all the twelfth year biology classes down to the Agricultural barn for the chance to witness a calf being born.

“I think Loughty just wants to push us off onto someone else for an entire afternoon,” Mary commented, as she, Remus, and Marlene marched across campus to collect their packed lunches from the dining hall and then down to the school farm. As they got close the smell of manure wafted up on the spring breeze and Mary covered her nose, lining up behind a row of students while an older student wrote a number on the back of their hands in marker.

“That’s your group,” he explained. “You’ll be going into the barn only a few at a time so the animals don’t get spooked.”

“Wonderful,” Mary grumbled, examining the crudely drawn ‘4’ on her hand.

They found their other friends waiting by one of the fences, all scattered around a flattened patch of grass. Lottie, Peter, and Moira were a few feet away, petting a goat through the fence, while Sirius and James sat on top of it, swinging their legs back and forth. When he spotted them, Sirius jumped down from the fence to compare group numbers, only to be soured upon finding out that his ‘5’ did not match Remus’ ‘2’.

“Charlie and Erik J. are taking bets on which group’s gonna catch the calf being born,” Sirius said. “Guess I have to change my bet to group two now.”

“Bet on your own group,” Remus said, stepping past him to swing himself up on the fence beside James.

Sirius leaned on the fence post next to him. “But you’re our lucky charm!”

“Never been lucky a day in my life,” Remus corrected, stifling a yawn. He’d slept more poorly than usual the night before and after tossing and turning for hours he’d finally slunk across the room and set a vinyl on the turntable. That was all it took to wake Sirius up these days, and as always they ended up on the floor with their backs against the hutch, sharing the headphones between them until that fateful shit-all hour of the morning became a little less shitty.

“Lily’s in group two,” James said, glancing at his hand, a '3' to match Marlene. Next to him, Remus put a hand over his eyes, scanning out over the rest of the kids.

“Where is she?”

“There.” James pointed across the grass, to where Lily was standing next to Snape, looking rather ruffled. “She’s trying to convince him to take our train home for the holiday.”

“God, why can’t she just give it up?” Sirius blagged. Remus smacked him lightly on the shoulder with the back of his hand.

“No friendship-shaming,” he said. "Lily means well. Even if it is Snape."

Sirius gave him a hard look but then nodded reluctantly and turned around to lean against the fence. “Well, it doesn’t look like she’s being very convincing.”

That at least, appeared to be true. Snape had his arms crossed haughtily while Lily stared up at him, using her hands to illustrate whatever point she was making. As they watched, another agricultural student shouted across the small field that group two was on deck and would be heading into the barn in a few minutes.

“Guess I should go get her,” Remus sighed, sliding off the fence.

“Godspeed, soldier,” Sirius said, saluting him.

He trudged across the yard, stopping a few feet from the pair, who were still arguing quietly. “Lily?” Remus called. “It’s almost group two’s turn to go in.”

Surprised by his appearance, Lily looked back. “I’ll be right there!” She said, before turning back to Severus, who was only glaring at him over her shoulder.

“If you were just willing to work it out, Sev—”

“As long as you’re hanging around them, I don’t want anything to do with it,” Snape snarled, “so leave me alone.”

Turning, Snape stalked off, leaving Lily looking deflated and haggard. Remus walked up to her side and scowled after him. “Did you really think it was going to work?” He asked softly.

“Let’s just go,” she sighed, turning toward the barn.

Lily was quiet for the most part, even as Professor Kettleburn gave an ecstatic lecture on the miracles of calf-birth. The air inside the barn was slightly too warm to be comfortable and Remus found himself stifling yawn after yawn. If Lily noticed his fatigue she didn’t say anything. He knew the Snape-thing still bothered her and had ever since Snape had given up his role as a prefect at the start of term. His departure left not only a hole in the ranks, but also meant that Lily had no choice but to flounder with other undesirable partners like Chastity. Remus would’ve thought that that would’ve finally marked the end between them, but something about Snape ignited the righteous part of her, and no matter what anyone tried to say, she refused to let herself be hated by the boy she’d known most of her life.

When their twenty minutes of observation was up and no calf had been born they emerged out into the mid-morning sun once more to trade places with the next group.

“I’m gonna go to the bathroom,” Lily said placidly, turning toward the school buildings. Remus continued on and passed Mary, Lottie, and Peter on their way into the barn, flashing them an unenthusiastic thumbs-up. When he arrived back on the patch of grass with his friends he found James and Sirius ripping open their packed lunches as well as his, peeling sandwiches apart like some field experiment.

“Er… What are you doing with my lunch?” He asked.

“I tried, Lupin!” James snapped. “I bloody well tried, but whatever maniac thought that fucking toff up really went to town on the ‘audacity’ and the ‘dickheadishness’!”

“Anybody got something to say that makes sense?”

“He tried to talk to Snape for Lily,” Marlene said, observing the boys from her spot on top of the fence. “It didn’t go well.”

“I swear to god that asshole won’t be happy until we break up!” James growled.

“Yes,” Remus said, “that’s exactly right.”

James stood up. “Well tough nuts 'cause it ain’t happening!”

“I would hope not. You only just openly declared your love for her in front of half the school last week.”

James shrank back slightly, still embarrassed by his drunken birthday proclamation, but Sirius only popped to his feet, grinning as he held up a baggy of peanut butter they’d scraped off the sandwiches.

“Snivelly told James to eat shit, and now he’s going to know how it feels,” he announced. “Good thing you prefer your jam sandwiches with enough peanut butter to choke a horse, Moony.”

Remus was unimpressed. “I was gonna eat that.”

“You and your grumbling stomach are just going to have to forgive us,” Sirius said, patting him on the shoulder and tossing the baggy to James, who continued filling it with handfuls of grass and mud. He passed it back to Sirius when it was full, nearly bursting at the seams with muck.

“What is the goal here?” Remus asked, slightly unnerved.

“We’re gonna trick Snivellus into thinking he’s really stepped in it,” James told him. “We considered using a real cowpat, but decided it would be funny enough to watch him dance around with peanut butter on his head instead."

"You're so merciful," Marlene said sarcastically.

"I know, right? Ready, Black?”

“I await your signal, Prongs,” Sirius grinned, before he disappeared across the field with his cow-bomb in hand.

“You sure this is a good idea?” Remus asked. James glanced at him, mouth pursed.

“I’ll give him one last chance,” he said. “He can either get over himself and accept that Lily and I are together, or he can eat muddy peanut butter.”

“I think you’re asking for a little much. Snape’s not just going to start being tolerable because you want him to—or because you played some stupid prank on him.”

“Then he’s made his own bed.” Decisively, James set off toward the pig pen where Snape and a couple other Salazar boys were leaning over the fence, taunting the animals or poking them with sticks.

Remus looked back to Marlene. “I can’t believe you’re just sitting back.”

“You didn’t hear what he said,” she told him. “I say, let him eat shit.”

“Well are you coming then? I’ll give you a ride.”

Marlene looked him up and down. "You sure you can carry me?"

"I'm skinny not entirely useless," he scoffed.

She smirked lightly and reached out for him, and Remus pulled her up onto his back, smiling as he took off after their friends. They caught up to James just has he stopped to face the pig pen, clearing his throat. “Snape,” he called, drawing the other boys' attention away from the pigs, “I changed my mind. We've still got stuff to talk about.”

Snape sneered; “You never know when to give up, do you, Potter?”

“Lily wants us to get along.”

“And I told you—never gonna happen. I'd rather be drowned in the lake than pretend to be friends with the likes of you.”

That can be arranged," Remus said, letting Marlene slide from his back.

“Gonna hit me too, Loony, like you did Mick Truman?" Snape leered. "Go ahead, try it, there are enough teachers around. Maybe they’ll lock you up for good, you lunatic.”

The other boys laughed like some maniacal audience and Marlene bristled; “The only one who deserves to be locked up is you!”

“Ugh. Do us a favour and muzzle your bitch, Loony.”

Only Snape could make anger bloom so quickly. Remus stepped forward again, stopping only when Marlene grabbed his arm. “Don't. Just look up,” she muttered lowly, and he did, instantly spotting Sirius, who was lying on his stomach on the pig pen’s roof. In his hands he held the bag of mud and peanut butter, extended out over Snape’s head.

Seemingly unruffled, James crossed his arms over his chest. “I used to think everyone was worthy of forgiveness, Snape, but then I met you and I’m just not so sure anymore.” He sighed as if disappointed. “Can’t have everything, I suppose.”

“Are you finished?" The nasty boy snarled. "If I wanted to listen to bullshit all day I’d ask for your opinion.”

“It never gets any easier,” James groaned. “Okay, that’s it. Black, bombs away!”

“James?”

They all turned to find Lily standing there, her expression worried. Unfortunately, there was no stopping what came next. At the same moment, Sirius threw down the bag and it promptly exploded over Snape’s head in a great mucky mess, spattering him, his friends, and the pig fence to boot. In impact, Lily’s hands flew to her mouth while Snape let out a wail of disgust.

“What the fuck?!”

Rolling off the pig’s roof, Sirius dropped down next to James and both of them stared in a mixture of shock and victory. “This feels familiar somehow,” Sirius grinned; “The cow shit’s new though.”

Realisation dawned on the Salazar boys’ faces and Snape immediately began to gag, whirling away to resist hurling.

“James!” Lily shouted, streaking forward. “What are you doing?”

“Don’t worry,” he said, trying not to laugh, “it’s not real cow dung.”

“It’s only mud and peanut butter, Lils,” Marlene said.

“Peanut butter?” Lily shrieked. At her words, Snape straightened and pulled a handful of muck off his head, holding it up to his face. He turned an ashen colour and then began to hyperventilate as though he couldn’t breathe. It looked almost comical, even as Lily shot toward him and grabbed his arm. Snape tried to throw her off, but she only withdrew her prefect’s help whistle from her pocket and blew it hard, making everyone around them turn and look. A moment later, one of Professor Kettleburn's students appeared, staring at them in shock.

“Er—What’s the matter?”

“He needs to go to the medical room,” she explained, while Snape wheezed next to her.

“What’s that all over him?”

“Peanut butter—he’s allergic!”

“Oh fuck,” James winced.

The older student took Snape’s arm and began quickly leading him away as he heaved-in breaths like a popped balloon. Lily started after the pair before whirling on the rest of them, her face a mask of vexation. “What were you THINKING?” She roared.

“We didn’t know he was allergic!” Sirius tried.

"Don't you DARE try and act like this wasn't on purpose! This was premeditated! You three can't handle it when someone else wants to do things their way! You always have to have the last word!"

James suddenly looked very nervous. None of them had seen Lily so angry since Remus' birthday the year before. "Daisy, I swear," he sputtered; "we didn't mean to—"

"You never mean to! And yet you DO! You must have cow dung for brains! Why can't everyone just get along?" With that, Lily threw her arms down and raced after Snape, her wellies squelching in the mud. The rest of them were left stunned into guilty silence, while every other student looked on in uncomfortable bewilderment. Remus was pretty sure none of them had cow dung for brains, but after listening to Lily scream it for all to hear, he was almost convinced.

“Did we just kill Snape?” Sirius asked, making Marlene seize up and smack him sharply on the arm.

“Don’t say that!” She wailed.

Shoulders slumped, James stepped forward and stared after Lily like a broken man—or in the very least, one that knew exactly how badly he’d messed up. “I am such a fucking idiot,” he moaned. No one seemed quick to correct him.

“Hey!” Peter shouted, appearing from the barn's direction and skidding happily into Sirius’ side. “You guys missed it—the calf was just born!”

“She’s so cute!” Lottie gushed next to him in a baby voice. “All wittle and tiny!”

Mary strolled up to them, arms crossed and looking almost as ashen as Snape had. “I swear I’m never having children. All slimy and disgusting, eugh!”

“It was just a baby cow, Mary,” Lottie insisted.

“It came out in a grey sack—they had to cut it out! It’s not a cow, it’s an alien.” She shivered lightly then looked them all up and down; “What’s wrong with you guys? Not like you just had to watch a live birth.”

“Pretty sure we just killed Snape,” Sirius repeated blandly, making Marlene shriek in horror and cover her face.

Mary crossed her arms. “Well, sounds like you had a much more productive afternoon then.”





* * *





They did not (thankfully—regretfully? Debatable) kill Snape. Having not actually ingested the peanuts, the wanker wasn't ever in any real trouble, though he'd put on quite a show on his way to the medical room. The school nurse, Ms. Pomfrey, did give him a shot of adrenaline just in case, but by mid-afternoon it'd become clear that Snape was going to be just fine.

James and Sirius were not so fortunate.

They were marched down to the Headmistress’s office where the severity of their actions were outlined with an unmerciful punishment consisting of four week’s detentions as well as James’ removal from the football team for twice that. Really he was lucky not to be kicked off the team all together, but tournaments began in June, and Hawkings still needed its star player. Snape, of course, wasn’t satisfied with this. In his eyes every one of them were just as culpable and deserved punishment, most of all James, who'd plead guilty to inciting the prank. Snape wasn’t convinced of his regret, but according to Sirius, McGonagall couldn’t reach his parents to discuss proper punishment and refused to take his bias or anger into consideration when punishing another student. They were, however, to write Snape a letter of apology each, which they were to read aloud in front of him and the Headmistress.

Neither James nor Sirius fought the punishments, both too guilty or too afraid of Lily’s wrath to even consider it. A creature of habit, she ignored them for a short while until James had worried himself into a frenzy thinking she was simply going to break up him; but rather than that, Lily took the incident as an opportunity to make amends. With only a day left at school before everyone returned home for the Easter holiday, she gathered all four 4A boys to her and ordered that they march down to Salazar House with her and formally apologise to Snape.

“But why do Remus and I need to go?” Peter whinged. “We had nothing to do with it.”

“You’re doing it to clear the air!” Lily shot back. Next to her, Sirius sighed dramatically.

“It’ll never work. There’s too much bad blood between us. He hates us, we hate him, it’s just the way things are.”

Bitterly, Lily smacked him in the shoulder. “And I’ve had enough of it, so we’re all going to apologise and you better bloody well mean it!”

“We will,” James promised eagerly, shouldering his best friend in poor attempts to get him to shut up.

“Snape’s not so innocent just because he’s got a shitty immune system,” Sirius started indignantly, “James might be willing to forgive him for you but he’s still a shit-eating wanker and you’re making a mistake trying to stay friends with him, Evans.”

Lily gave Sirius a look that either meant she was about to explode or burst into tears and James reached forward to grab him firmly by the shoulder this time. “I’m willing to be the bigger person,” he reasoned. “And I do regret pranking Snape. I wouldn’t have done had I known he was allergic, and neither would you, Sirius.”

Sirius looked away, but it was obvious James was right. Together they made their way up the street toward Snape’s dorm, dragging their feet over the freshly-mowed lawn while Lily pestered another boy sitting on the front steps to go and fetch him. Snape emerged along with an entire brigade of boys that included the two he’d been standing next to at the farm (Remus had learned their names were Drake and Ainsley after they testified to McGonagall on Snape’s behalf) and even Barty Crouch, who was never one to miss out on drama.

“You made a mistake coming here,” Crouch called, like a cheesy TV villain.

“Sev,” Lily started, ignoring the other boys with all the prefect courage she could muster, “we’ve come to apologise. James and Sirius regret what they did, we all do.”

“I don’t,” Snape said, “from what I heard they’re going to be mucking barn stalls for the next month.”

“I think I can smell them already,” Drake answered. “Yeah, that’s it—eau de shit.”

Laughter echoed and all four boys flexed their hands agonisingly at their sides. Remus heard James take a deep breath while Sirius cleared his throat, no doubt itching to throw a snarky response right back.

“We’re not here to argue,” Lily pushed, “we’ve come to apologise.”

“But why? I’ve already got your apologies right here!” From his pocket, Snape produced the letters James and Sirius had been forced to write and began reading them off while those around him grinned and sniggered; “ ‘To Severus, I’m so, so sorry we attacked you with peanut butter—there is absolutely no way things would’ve turned out that way had we known you were allergic. We feel most awful for what we did, and if you’d just consider forgiving us, we swear to spend the rest of our days seeking repentance for our most heinous sins—”

“I think you’re skipping the part about using jam instead next time,” Sirius said blandly. "Can you not read sarcasm?"

“Oh shut up, Black,” Snape sneered. “I haven’t even gotten to the part where you grovel to McGonagall.”

“Sev, please!” Lily begged.

“No!” From his place atop of the dorm’s stairs, Snape threw the letters in the air and Lily flinched as they fluttered down around her. “I don't give a shit about some stupid apology! Your shitty boyfriend almost poisoned me and you expect me to forgive them?”

James stepped up to Lily’s side and grasped her arm, a gesture that only made Snape appear more livid. “You don’t need to forgive us,” he said, “but we don’t need to fight anymore either.”

“Easy for you to say,” Snape snarled, “you got the last laugh!”

Lily pulled away from James; “No one was laughing, Sev! We’ve said so many nasty things to one another, don’t you think this is finally the time to put it all to rest?”

“Put it to rest?! He almost put me in a grave! And you’re still defending him! Honestly, isn't the righteous act getting a bit old, Lily? I wouldn’t be his friend for all the money in the world, and you’re doing it for free even though you can’t even afford the tuition here!”

Lily snapped back like she’d been slapped but Snape wasn’t finished. He pushed in front of the others and stepped down a stair, eyes wild.

“I’ve kept your secret for years and you repay me by dating and befriending the most intolerable pieces of crap imaginable! I was on your side when they were still pulling your hair and calling you a swot all day long! I didn’t care if your family had no money or you could only get into Hawkings on a stupid scholarship! I was the one who told you about it in the first place so we could go to school together but the moment you got here you decided that popularity was more important!”

“Sev…” Lily’s lower lip had begun to tremble.

“Don’t you do that!” Snape lashed. “You always cry when things don’t go your way, but not this time! You’re just embarrassed that everyone else here comes from proper stock and you’re just a middle-class nobody who couldn’t get anywhere if you didn’t sleep with your bloody textbooks open!”

The silence was staggering. Snape’s admission had taken all of them by surprise, most of all Lily, who obviously hadn’t counted on him being so vicious. Snape was insufferable at the best of times and spiteful the rest, but he’d never turned his poison on her.

Almost panting from all the shouting, Snape drew himself up to his full height. “Well there then,” he hissed. “Maybe everyone else can keep your secret now too, you pitiful charity case.”

Like lightning, Lily turned and took off across the grass toward her dorm, eyes covered and already crying. James was the first of them to react—shooting toward Snape with one fist outstretched; “YOU—!”

“Now!” Barty wailed, and a second later all four of them were being bludgeoned with bags of peanut butter, which without the added mud and grass, mostly bounced off of them like lumpy rocks. Shocked and instantly sore, they all staggered back while Snape dove for cover.

“You little shits!” Sirius cursed, covering his head. “You’re gonna pay for this!”

“Hope none of you are allergic!” Someone shouted.

As they began to retreat, fresh peanut butter now staining their school clothes, the Salazar boys chased them right off the lawn, hooting in victory. Remus was almost glad Snape hadn't given them the chance to properly apologise; none of them deserved it.

“Ow…” Peter groaned, once they’d made it two dorms over and were no longer being pursued. “What’d they do—freeze the peanuts first?”

“Fucking dicks,” Sirius sighed, wiping muck from his jumper. Next to him, James was quiet, bent over with his hands on his knees and staring at the ground like it might crack open and swallow him.

“You okay, Prongs?” Remus asked, and James looked up.

“Did you know Lily was a scholarship student?”

Remus shook his head, but he would’ve been lying if things didn’t suddenly make much more sense. One of the first times he’d ever hung out with Lily on their own, she’d asked him if he’d come to Hawkings with ‘help’. At the time he’d rebuffed her, thinking she was pitying him for being poor, but now he knew she was just trying to see if they had another thing in common. If he had said yes, or at least explained himself better, maybe she would’ve trusted him with the secret; but instead he’d reacted like any other snob. It meant Lily had been left with only Snape, her childhood best friend who no matter what she did, would never be able to assimilate into the life she’d built for herself at school.

“She never told me…” James murmured. The shock on his face was clear as day. He and Lily had been dating going on seven months, not counting the whole summer they’d spent talking over the phone. “How many times did I invite her to the summer house… or—or to London to see the sights. I even offered to buy her train ticket! And for Christmas I sent all these books mum got as first editions and—and I got her that stupid bracelet for her birthday—but what if—what if she thought I was rubbing it all in her face?”

Sirius set his hand on James’ shoulder. “She didn’t, mate.”

“Then why wouldn’t she tell me? I’m her boyfriend.”

“I get what you're saying, Prongs, I do. But I think right now what she needs is a friend. So let’s be upset later, kay?”

It was the most reasonable thing Remus had ever heard Sirius say, and it was enough to leave James speechless.

"Sirius is right," Remus said. "Worrying about why she didn't say anything won't make her feel better. She probably just didn't want to ask for help."

"Yeah, Evans is stubborn like that," Peter shrugged. "Though, I dunno why 'cause she's always helping us. I'd have failed every maths class I've ever taken if not for her."

Slowly, James nodded, his mouth drawn together in a tight line. “Yeah, yeah, you’re right. We just gotta tell her it’s okay.”

With a comforting smile, Sirius indicated down the street in the direction of Rowena House; “C’mon then, before her eyes get all red and puffy from too much crying.”

They started forward together and Remus fell into step next to Peter, who had started staring down at the ground like he it was a puzzle he'd yet to sort out. “Moira isn’t a scholarship kid,” he murmured, “I don’t think, at least.”

“Thought you said her family was in real estate?” Remus asked.

Peter visibly relaxed. “Yeah, that’s right, they are.”

Remus pat him on the back.

Once they reached the girls dorm they went around the side and threw rocks at the girls’ window until Marlene appeared, opening it and sticking her head out. "What happened? I thought Lily went out with you—why's she so upset?"

Before they could answer, Mary appeared at her shoulder. “What the bloody fuck happened? Lily's in here balling her eyes out. Potter you better have not dumped her."

"I didn't!" James insisted. "Just let me—"

"You must've done something! Haven't seen her cry like this since eighth year Christmas when she—"

“I can hear you!” Lily wailed from somewhere inside the dorm. Flinching, Mary immediately buggered it out the window, dropping down onto the electric box beneath and then onto the lawn, Marlene not far behind her.

“Spit it out,” Mary lashed; “She’s in there crying like Sirius if Jagger died.”

“That bad?” Sirius asked, clicking his tongue.

“Snape said some stuff…” Remus started. Passing the girls, James climbed onto the dorm’s electrical box.

“I’m gonna go talk to her,” he said, “will you guys stick around for a bit?”

Sirius waved him on; “Yeah no problem, mate. Holler if you guys need anything.”

James nodded and hauled himself up onto the window ledge, closing it after he slipped inside.

“What happened?” Marlene asked again, and they all settled down on the grass while Sirius retold the story of the affair. He handled the topic of Lily’s scholarship carefully, but it still came as a shock when they realised that not even the girls knew. Lily had somehow managed to keep her mysterious scholarship a secret from everyone, including her closest friends. Marlene and Mary kept sharing the same look, communicating telepathically the way Remus knew girls could, but they let Sirius finish his story. The ending and the details about Snape came with more venom, but that was to be expected.

“That fucking wanker,” Mary growled from behind her teeth. “Maybe we should put peanuts in his food for real.”

“Killing Snape’s not going to make Lily feel any better,” Peter pointed out.

“It’d make me feel better," Marlene added woefully.

As they all lapsed into uncomfortable silence, Remus leaned back on his arms and continued picking grass to pass the time. Eventually, as the sun was beginning to dip down toward the trees, Lottie appeared, having spotted them under her window from her walk up the road. She flopped down on the grass and they relayed the same story, though this time Mary and Marlene interjected with their own tidbits until they all trickled back into silence once more. Remus hoped James was at least getting somewhere with Lily, but he had no way of knowing since he’d shut the window.

“It’s freezing out here,” Lottie said eventually. The street lights had turned on behind them and James had yet to emerge.

“Here, Lot, take my jacket,” Sirius said, shrugging out of his coat.

“Thanks Sirius, but you’re really not my type.”

“I literally just offered you my coat.”

“Hm. Okay then.” Lottie took the jacket and snuggled into it. “Ooh, you do smell good though. Not like eau de shit at all.”

“Hmph. Thanks.”
