Chapter 59: James Potter’s Technicolour Dream World


Chapter Summary

Remus meets with his forms teacher to discuss his plans for his future. The Marauders discover something surprising about James' connection to music.



Chapter Notes

No CWs for this chapter. See end notes for an update on my posting schedule!



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Oh God, life is strange,

Some are fast and some are slow;

Some believe me, don’t even know,

No, no, no, no, no;

Strange, life is strange,

Life is strange,

Oh, my life is strange…

- “Life is Strange” T. Rex, 1973



Sunday 24th April 1977

Once a year, all sixth form students were required to meet with their forms teacher to discuss what it was they wanted to do with the rest of their lives. Being a rather prestigious place, most Hawkings students had their entire life plotted out by year 7, either by their families or someone their family hired. Those students who didn’t commit to upper sixth (and there were some, even at Hawkings) would leave school and take over whatever business or lordship from their parents. Naturally, anyone who stayed would aim for the most reputable university that would admit them and from there head into politics or business or whatnot, and if they didn’t do that it was probably because they had a diamond mine in Botswana to inherit. Remus’ friends were no exception.

For most of his life James had resigned himself to simply following in his father’s footsteps. Shortly before his first and only child was born, Fleamont Potter, an already in-demand corporate lawyer, opened his own law firm and was quickly propelled into London’s legal stratosphere. A child of immigrants, Fleamont was determined that his own son have every opportunity available to him, though he was distinctly under the impression that taking pre-law classes at school and actual law in university was the best way for James to secure that opportunistic future. James didn’t seem to refute this. As long as he had enough free time to play his sports and hang out with his friends then he was content.

Peter was a little more vague about his future. Like James, his father expected him to head into the family business, supporting Simeon as he ran the newspaper until their sons could inherit it from them. For the most part, Peter appeared agreeable to this, despite the fact that working under his brother seemed to be the last thing that he would ever want to do. Remus had never said it, but he’d always sort of pictured Peter doing something with his art. Every time he saw his friend complete another sketch it struck him that it was better than the last. And the last had always been very good so… but Peter was not a risk-taker, and he was always saying how his father didn’t believe in the arts—a great source of contention between his and James’ families, since Euphemia Potter, a highly educated woman in her own right, was a curator at the National Gallery in London.

“The world will always need news!” Peter would say, puffing up his shoulders to imitate his father.

“And the world will always worship art!” James would say, wagging a finger to imitate his mother.

And then, because he was Sirius, Sirius would chime in with; “Mum’s right! Ars longa, vita brevis—‘art is long, life is short’!”

‘Life is short’ became Sirius’ mantra in the weeks leading up to the teacher/student meetings. He'd read it off-hand in one of their textbooks and always said it with conviction, but somehow it still felt as though he were trying to reassure himself that art was worthwhile, rather than convince the rest of them. Under normal circumstances Sirius would have had absolutely no cause to worry about his future. The Black family was so old and esteemed that if Sirius were to trace his roots back more than three generations he’d probably have found that he was cousin to not only the British royal family, but at least four other monarchies as well. Sirius could’ve lived the rest of his life without lifting a pinky and still have been richer than any sorry sod that crossed his path and yet, he wanted none of it. To him it was blood money—paid for but never earned. Yes, Sirius was determined to make his own way—with Uncle Alphard’s inheritance as a comfortable subsidy, of course. After his meeting had finished, he left Sheila’s office looking cool and collected. Not much worried Sirius Black, and certainly not the future. When he dropped down on the bench where Remus was waiting for his turn, he was still smiling. Even played at lighting one of his cigarettes, but put the pack away when Remus gave him the stink-eye.

“What’d she ask you?” Remus asked, as Sirius untucked his hands from his jacket pockets and lifted them up behind his head casually.

“Oh, you know, the usual—what university I want to go to, what I’m gonna study, what goals I have in life. All boring stuff.”

“And what’d you say?”

Sirius tilted his head toward him and raised an eyebrow. “What do you think I said?”

Remus looked away, fingers knotted in his lap. It’d been hard to look at Sirius these last few weeks, but beyond breaking up with Chastity, Sirius had done little to provoke such a reaction, which meant it was all on him. Embarrassing, really.

“I at least hope you weren’t a dick about it,” Remus said snidely.

“Me? Never.”

A smile tugged at the corner of Remus’ lips, but a moment later the office door opened and Sheila stuck her head out. She was wearing a long hair scarf covered in daisies, and when she leaned over to peek out the doorway the tips of the scarf hung almost to the ground.

“Remus, you can come in now,” she said fondly.

“Good luck, lover boy,” Sirius teased, jamming him in the ribs with his elbow before hopping off the bench and starting down the hall. Remus glared after him, wondering if this was what it meant to really like someone.

“Can I get you a cup of tea?” Sheila asked after he’d followed her into the office. “I was just about to have one myself.”

“Sure—I mean yes, please.”

She smiled and gestured for him to sit while crossing to a small coffee counter. Being in less demand than those found throughout the school’s other buildings, Sheila’s office in the music hall was of a decent size, but was made tighter by the mountains of papers and books she had piled on every shelf and in every corner. There were binders upon binders and instruments upon instruments scattered about the room and enough boxes of old records to get Remus' heart racing, but still it managed to feel like a sort of organised chaos. This was proven when she pulled a small sugar tin out of a cupboard filled to the brim with miniature, multicoloured maracas.

“I’m afraid I don’t keep any milk in the office,” she apologised, while carrying two mugs of steaming tea back to her desk, “but there’s plenty of sugar.”

She handed him a small spoon and set the tin in between them, which Remus appreciated, before scooping three generous spoonfuls into her own cup, which Remus appreciated more.

“I’ve a bit of a sweet tooth,” she amended shyly. “Colin always says it’ll be the death of me.”

“Who’s Colin?” Remus asked, stirring plenty of sugar into his own tea.

“My husband.”

Remus stirred a little slower. Of course Mrs. Buchanan had to have a husband, but the way she’d said it so casually had surprised him. “Is he who you’re always going to visit when you leave school?”

Sheila tipped her head forward. “Yes, in fact. Colin lives in Glasgow. It's where our home is, actually.”

"Why teach all the way up here then? Surely there are jobs in Glasgow."

"You'd think, but I'm afraid our government hasn't been so helpful on the job front as of late. Anyway, I like Hawkings. It's like my second home. And I really don't mind the travelling, I get to do most of my marking on the train. It's great to pass the time."

“Why aren't you there now?" Remus asked.

"Because we're having your meeting, silly. A teacher's work is never done, after all. But don't worry, I actually do like hearing about my students’ plans for the future. Makes me excited to think about what they might accomplish. And besides, Colin's at the hospital this week, so no one'll be home anyway."

"Oh..." Remus tapped his spoon on the rim of his cup. He’d never really given much thought to accomplishing anything. "He a doctor then?"

"Hm, something like that."

Her answer felt a bit dismissive, as though he were nothing more than a child, but then again he had been asking a lot of questions. Remus would've never admitted it, but just hearing Sheila talk made him feel... well, better, probably.

“Now, I do believe I'm the one who's supposed to be interviewing you, so shall we get started?” Sipping her tea with one hand, Sheila used the other to flip open a folder with his file in it. She looked it over for a moment, drawing her finger up and down each page as she read. “Mhm. Yes, good marks—”

“Decent marks,” Remus mumbled. Sheila gave him a sly smile and glanced back to the file.

“Good marks, good health, suspected interests in literature, history, and—” she looked up again coyly, “music.”

Suddenly shy, Remus lifted his tea cup to his lips.

“Your father still works in government, yes?”

“Yeah.”

“And do you have any desire to enter a position such as his?”

“No.”

“So that's a no to politics or law?”

He shook his head firmly.

“And is it your intention to return school next year for upper sixth or do you have plans to pursue your education elsewhere?”

“I want to come back,” Remus said without a moment’s hesitation.

“You do?”

“Yeah.” What was there at home anyway—Giles and the dogs. His friends were at school.

“That’s wonderful then,” Sheila grinned, “we have a goal. Have you given any thought to the classes you might take next year? Most students coming back chose a single subject to work toward before going on to university. There’s law, philosophy, ethics, history, fine arts, human biology, music—”

“I haven’t given it much thought.”

“Well, you still have time to decide. The school doesn’t ask you to confirm re-enrollment until the end of summer.”

Remus nodded, picking at the rim of his cup. It was handmade with a sunflower painted on the side. A closer look revealed a small engraving near the bottom; ‘To Mrs. Buchanan, made with love—Elsie, 1973’.

Watching him, Sheila flipped his file shut. “How is it you’re feeling today, Remus?”

“Fine,” he murmured.

“I want something a little more than ‘fine’,” she said, clicking her tongue; “Remember it’s not just a solo, it’s a cadenza, and music isn’t played as ‘cheerful’ it’s played as ‘allegro’.”

“I’m very fine, then. I'm andante.”

Sheila smirked. “Alright, you cheeky thing, might as well spit it out then. What is it you want to do with your life, Remus?”

He squirmed a bit. Of course he’d been expecting the question—dreading it really—but he had no answer for her.

“What did Sirius say?” He asked.

Sheila shook her head lightly. “I’m sorry dear, that’s confidential. I couldn’t tell you what Sirius said in his meeting any more than I could tell him what you say in yours. It might influence your decisions.”

“Not all kids are so easily influenced, you know.”

“I know,” she smiled, “but I just want to make sure that they’re all doing what it is they want to do. Are there any universities you have your eye on?”

“Not really.”

“How about a goal for after you leave school, or even this summer?”

He shrugged. “Gonna learn how to drive.”

“Brilliant. And where is it you want to drive?”

“Anywhere, really. Away.”

“Away, where?”

“Dunno…”

Sheila sipped her tea again. “Well, it’s okay to not know right now. Sometimes the best trips we take have no real destination. Will you tell me where it is when you figure it out?”

“Do I have to?” Asking that felt better than just saying no.

“Of course not,” Sheila said, before placing a hand to the side of her mouth to whisper; “but I would like to know where your band is playing so I could come watch one day. I’ll bet you and Mr. Black could put on quite the show.”

Remus perked up. “I thought you said you couldn’t—”

“Now, shall we talk about your maths for a bit?”





* * *





Remus slid in next to Sirius at the dinner table. “You told Sheila about the band.”

Sirius smiled deviously over a bite of stew. “Gossips.”

“You told her we were planning an actual band.”

“Aren't we? Really, this dancing around our future is getting a bit old, Moons. Don’t tell me you actually told her that you’re going to be a flippin’ rice farmer.”

Remus shook his head, then, too curious; “What’d she say?”

“She congratulated me actually,” Sirius said smugly, “said if anyone could do it, we could.”

“Really?”

“Well, good as.”

“You’re so full of shit.”

“Vita brevis, Lupin.”

“Yeah and ‘carpe diem’ and the other bit,” James finished, joining them at the table along with Lily. “How were your guys’ meetings?”

“Peachy. Yours?”

“Long,” James yawned. “I swear, Bilshin lives to exhaust us.”

“Yours go long too, then?” Remus asked Lily, who had begun to pick at her dinner like she was lost in a daze.

“Oh? Yeah, good.”

Remus exchanged glances with James who immediately tightened hold of his fork. “Everything okay, Lils?”

Lily said nothing at first, until James nudged her pointedly. “It’s nothing to worry about,” she persisted. “Barty’s young and stupid, that’s all.”

“But he said something again, didn’t he?” Sirius glowered.

“Yes! And he’s not the only one,” James lashed. “Snape—”

“Tried to apologise,” Lily interrupted.

Remus’ jaw practically hit the floor. “You didn’t accept, did you?”

“No, of course not! Severus can apologise until he’s blue in the face. He did as much while we were home for Easter—it doesn’t mean I’m just going to forgive him, but I don’t have to hate him either.”

“Well can I finally hate him freely then?” Sirius scoffed.

Lily rolled her eyes, but James was not finished. He leaned toward her; “If you would just let me say something to them then they wouldn’t bother you—”

She slapped her fork down. “You’re obviously all cut from the same bloody cloth so I’ll say to you what I’ve already said to Remus: I refuse to let it bother me. Start reacting and they’ll just keep at it even more.”

“So we pretend like you’re not being bullied?” Sirius demanded.

“If that’s how you want to put it, then yes.”

“No!” All three boys said together.

“Do you want me to find somewhere else to eat? Because I will,” she threatened. “Now I’ve said my piece, and that’s that. If I hear that any of you are going around threatening people or getting yourselves in more trouble I’ll put you in detention for the rest of the year myself!”

Sirius leaned in. “How about we just prank them with—”

“No pranks!”

“Kay, fine,” James grumbled, “but I don’t understand why you can’t turn that wrath of yours on little shits like Barty.”

“It’s not effective on Barty,” Lily said through her teeth. “Now eat your damn dinner.”

None of them were satisfied, but Lily refused to say any more on the matter and they knew better than to argue. Remus did have to hand it to her though, she was holding out for much longer than anyone else he knew would’ve been able to. It wasn’t as if she took everything lying down—anyone who might be ballsy enough to say something snide in her presence were promptly handed a detention slip, but that only seemed to make things worse. Eventually kids started to turn and flee from her in the halls, shrieking things like ‘here comes the penniless prefect’ while waving pink-slips she’d already given them in her face. James just about throttled Barty every time they were in the same room together, but the real surprise was Sirius’ reaction. The following Monday, after Lily had lambasted them over dinner, Sirius got into a fist fight in the middle of history class with some pig-faced kid named Jason Mueller.

It was the middle of silent study, and Professor Binns was lightly dozing at his desk like normal. A faint noise drew his attention and Remus looked up from his textbook to find that Jason had dropped his pencil, but when Lily went to pass it back to him, he only sneered;

“Oh, keep it. I’m sure you need it more than me.”

Temporarily stupefied, Lily just sort of blinked at him for a while, but before she could turn away and hide the red blooming in her cheeks, Sirius, her seat partner, stood up and plucked the pencil from her hand, pointing it sharp-end first at Jason’s nose.

“Here,” he snarled lightly, “you dropped this."

"No, I didn't," the pig-faced boy contested.

"Yes, you did. And Evans was nice enough to pick it up for you. Now take. It. Back.”

At that, Jason looked from Sirius’ face to the pencil, to Lily. “No thanks," he laughed finally, "wouldn’t want to catch anything. I hear poor-people rats have all sorts of nasty diseases. You understand, right Black?”

Sirius raised both eyebrows, then pressed the pencil’s eraser to his lip in feigned consideration. “Sure, Jake, I understand. But would you do me a favour? Catch this.”

Before Jason could react, Sirius had tossed the pencil straight toward him, but while Jason fumbled to catch it Sirius’ fist came down, socking him in the cheek hard enough to leave the other boy sprawling from his seat. Several other students shrieked in shock and Lily leapt up, completely horror-stricken, but before anyone could do anything, Jason sat up and threw himself at Sirius' middle with a great cry.

While their classmates hooted and hollered, the two scrapped on the ground until Remus managed to pull both of them apart. It was enough to get Professor Binns’ attention and Sirius was quickly shuffled out of the classroom, holding his punching-hand to his chest. Remus knew he’d be hurting—it was a rookie shot, he’d squeezed his thumb on the inside of his fist—but something about watching Sirius come to Lily’s aid like that had made him incredibly proud... among other things.

Unfortunately for Sirius, Lily did not share the same sentiment.

After using her prefect status to escort both boys to the nurse and then detention, she spent an entire evening lecturing not only Sirius, but all four Marauders on the importance of rising above their tormentors. To his credit, James tried his damndest to make her see reason, but Lily was adamant. Any issues stemming from Snape or her scholarship were hers to deal with, and everyone else should respect that. Remus didn’t agree, but she wouldn’t allow him a word in edgewise anyway.

Still riding the high of socking Jason, Sirius once again milked his injury for all that it was worth, taking the opportunity to sit back in art class and play model, as they continued their unit on oil portraits. Remus loathed the class but the girls had convinced him that taking it would mean an easy A, except according to their teacher, Madame Aubert, he painted like he’d already ‘jeter l’éponge’. Thanks to Sirius he was half sure he knew what it meant, but if ‘jetering’ the ‘ponge’ meant he’d never have to pick up another bloody crayon again, he’d do it.

“You’re such a nob,” Remus complained, doing his best to mix a colour that looked even slightly akin to Lily’s copper waves. Peter was the one painting Sirius, and was doing a significantly better job of capturing the blue tones in his dark hair.

“It’s my right wrist, Lupin,” Sirius complained, waving his wrapped hand at him. “My strumming hand!”

"He's just worried he won't be able to wank anymore," Peter teased.

"Correct," Sirius said crudely, "but I'm a musician first, a masterbater second."

They all laughed, except for Lily, who was trying her best to hold still for Remus while Sirius tossed this way and that on his stool.

“Does that mean your dreams of being a musician are shattered, Sirius?” She asked.

“Of course not. Lead singers hardly even have to play instruments these days anyway.”

“You’re a lazy nob then,” Remus corrected, looking up from his portrait. It made Lily look more like some hair-raising evil witch than a girl, but he wasn’t about to tell her that.

“Ah, what do I care,” Sirius waved, “I got Potter."

"To wank for you?" Remus suggested, making Lily groan.

"Yes, as a matter of fact. Didn't you know—I get off vicariously though others. You couldn't imagine the time it saves me. Speaking of which, I got us some more sheet music for tonight. Pete, think you can pass it onto Prongs next period so he can look it over for our practice tonight? Don't want him lagging behind.”

“Dunno what help that’s gonna be,” Peter mumbled, staring down at his painting with a concentrated expression.

Sirius rocked forward on his stool. “What do you mean?”

“Stop moving,” Peter huffed, wetting his brush, “I mean James can’t read the music so what’s the point?”

“Sure he can. I taught him myself.”

Peter snorted. “That’s what you think.”

Remus shared a glance with both Lily and Sirius. “Mind extrapolating a bit, Wormtail?”

“It’s not that big ‘a deal,” Peter sighed, glancing from Sirius to the canvas. “I mean, he still sounds great right? He just can’t read it. I'm surprised neither of you have noticed. Now stop bloody moving."

"But he never has any issues during practice," Sirius said.

"Well yeah, it's because he always gets you to play it first."

"... What?"

Peter let out an irritated sigh and lowered his paint palette. "Okay, read my lips—James. Can't. Read. Music. I quizzed him myself last practice. He knows all the notes, and if you ask for a G or B-sharp or whatever he'll play it, but the moment you point to it on the page he's lost. You've never noticed because you're only ever listening to him, but that's it exactly—he’s listening too. James plays by ear.”

Sirius’ mouth dropped open. “No fucking way. By ear? He’s moved on to bloody Hendrix now and you’re telling me he’s playing that all by ear?!”

“I don’t understand, is that uncommon?” Lily asked.

“Plenty of musicians can’t read music,” Remus shrugged, also shocked, “but memorising every note just by what it sounds like isn’t exactly the most efficient way to learn an instrument. They have to have perfect pitch, and yeah, that’s pretty rare. Most people just start with memorising a few chords and work their way out from there, but I guess if James has been doing it from the beginning then…”

“Then he’s also a genius!” Sirius finished.

Remus nodded. “Even with your memory, hearing an entire song and copying every note by ear should be impossible.”

“It basically is,” Sirius said smugly. “And he was holding out on us this entire time. Wow. I’m gonna kick his arse.”

“Try sitting still for a second first,” Peter grumbled, setting his paintbrush down just as their teacher strolled by, clutching a fistful of fresh parchment. She stopped at his shoulder and beamed as she took in his portrait.

“Ah, Pierre,” she sighed in that thick, French accent of hers, “c’est magnifique. You’ve captured Monsieur Black’s likeness exquisitely.”

“You hear that,” Sirius said to Lily, “she called me ‘exquisite’.”

“What is it you are calling this piece, have you decided?” Madame Aubert asked.

Casting a look at Sirius, Peter smirked shyly. “I have. I think I'll call it, ‘A Narcissist's Mirror’.”

Both Remus and Lily began to snicker and Sirius crossed his arms with an unimpressed expression, but Madame Aubert just clapped her hands together in enthusiasm. “Très bon! Monsieur Lupin, et toi? What about your portrait of Mademoiselle Evans?"

Holding up his wicked painting (wickedly bad, that was), Remus considered. “Er... ‘Smudged Ginger’?”

Sirius snorted and Lily gave a little gasp before playfully whipping his own paint rag at him. Madame Aubert just clicked her tongue.

“Je vois… Maybe keep thinking, yes?”

“Yes, ma'am.”

Their teacher strolled away, shouting to the class that it was time to start cleaning up, and Peter began looking between his and Remus’ paintings pointedly.

“Oi!” Remus snapped, pulling his portrait back when he noticed.

“What? It’s nothing to be ashamed of, Moony. You said it yourself, it's abstract.”

“Yes, and it’s still a work in progress!”

“Whatever you say,” Peter said, smiling smugly.

Remus scoffed and dipped his fingers in his water jar before flicking them at Peter, who flinched away.

“Watch the masterpiece, Lupin!”

“C’mon, it’s already time to clean up,” Lily said, hopping off her stool as Remus set her portrait aside and collected his brushes.

“Sirius hang on, I just want to finish this bit,” Peter insisted, keeping him sitting while the rest of the class fluttered around, trying to finish up before the final bell rang. When it did, Sirius launched himself up from his stool.

“Are you done yet, Pete? ‘Cause I’m starving,” he declared.

Peter nibbled on the end of his paintbrush in consideration, still teetering his stout legs on the bottom rung of his stool. “You guys go on ahead, I wanna finish this bit here before the paint starts to thicken. I’ll just catch a late dinner.”

“Alright, but remember we’re practising in the music room tonight. Room two. I wanna see for myself if your ear-tingling assessment of James’ abilities are for real or just rubbish.”

“Fine, fine,” Peter waved, turning back to his painting.

Saluted his friend goodbye, Sirius met Remus and Lily by the door and joined them as they left the classroom.

“What’re they serving for dinner, again?” Lily asked, dodging other students as they shuffled up and down the hall.

Letting the sea of bodies part naturally around him, Sirius opened his mouth and spoke through a yawn; “Pot pie again. With corn and the little cups of jelly that are great for throwing—”

“Lily?”

Snape appeared behind them unannounced, so close that he might as well have been breathing down the back of their necks. At the interruption, Sirius jumped nearly a foot into the air and spun around with the rest of them. “Fuck—! You should come with a warning bell!” He hissed.

“And you should come with a muzzle,” Snape shot back. "I'm here to talk to Lily, so why don't you just get back to whatever ridiculous scheme you're sure to be planning and leave us alone."

"Ha, joke's on you, Snivelly," Sirius shot, "it's a Thursday and Thursdays are for initiating ridiculous schemes, not planning them."

"I'm surprised you can plan anything at all, what with hot air where a brain should be," Snape seethed. Remus might’ve congratulated him on the good quip if Lily hadn’t immediately sighed and stepped between them.

“Severus, that’s enough," she sighed. "Now what do you want?”

Snape eyed Remus and Sirius, who had both drawn themselves up to their full height, fully prepared to defend Lily’s already degraded honour. “I want to talk to you,” he grumbled.

“We already talked,” Lily said tiredly, “there’s nothing else to say.”

“Yes, there is. There's plenty more to say if you'd just listen, and if we could have five minutes to ourselves—"

"You're lucky you're still standing here," Remus scoffed. "If it weren't for Lily, I'd have already—"

"Flunked out? Been arrested for assault? Trust me, I know your type, Lupin."

"You don't know anything about me, Snivellus."

"I know enough. Like how your—"

"Enough!" Lily shouted. "I'm so done with this! Severus, if all you're interested in is fighting then I don't want to hear—!"

"—I want to apologise!" Snape cried hurriedly. "I'm sorry! I don't want us to fight anymore."

While Remus and Sirius suppressed a string of irritated moans, Lily's shoulders slumped in worry. “Sev, you’ve apologised plenty, and I already told you that I'm not angry anymore... but that doesn’t mean everything’s just fixed. I think that... Well, that maybe we've just outgrown each other."

Snape's screwed up his face so tightly it began to turn red. "That's a stupid answer."

Before any of her friends could jump to her defence, Lily threw a hand out to stop them. "I understand if that's how you feel, but I've made up my mind. I'm sorry.”

"Is this about the charity case thing?"

"No, it's about trust. Trust you broke."

“Everything can be fixed.”

“Not everything,” Remus ground out.

Snape snapped his eyes toward him, but Lily just shook her head. “I’m sorry, Severus, but we’re not friends anymore. I’ve made my decision.”

“You can’t just do that!” Snape snapped. “We've known each other longer than anyone here. Now I've apologised, and I already told everyone to stop calling you a charity case!”

“Don’t think they heard you,” Sirius scoffed. “Now you’ve got her answer so buzz off.”

"Go paint your bloody nails, why don't you, Black! You're the one poisoning Lily. You and the rest of your scummy, low-life group. Band—what band? You're going to fail before you even get your feet off the ground! Lily's mental for thinking that hanging around you will bring anything but failure!"

Pushing up his sleeves to ready himself for another fight, Sirius took a step forward. "Come here and say that, you fucking worm!"

Lily spun around, grabbing onto him; “No! Sirius, it’s alright.”

“No, it ain't! Real friends don't talk to one another like that."

“Fuck you, Black! This’s got nothing to do with you anyway!”

At Snape's reply, Sirius let out an incredulous laugh and crossed his arms over his chest;

“Actually it does! You see, we were there when you revealed your true colours and permanently revoked your own ‘Lily Evans’ friendship card’. Rather spectacularly, I might add—no offence, Evans—and you’ve already given your shitty excuse for an apology, that Evans has been so gracious to accept—good on you, Evans—which leads me to believe only one thing...” Next thing they knew, Sirius had gotten between Snape and Lily, tipping his head in Snape’s direction; “You didn’t come here today to apologise, you came here to guilt Lily into being your friend again. Well, let me be the one to tell you that that’s not how the world works—that’s not how people work! You don’t get to just decide that you’re important to someone, especially after you’ve fucked up so royally—people aren’t things. So if you’re so hurting for friends, why don’t you go find your little chemistry set and build a new one?!”

Snape drew back, a look of utter loathing on his face. “You’re making a mistake,” he warned Lily. “One day these freaks are gonna end up in jail—or worse! Then you'll know I'm right. Mark my words, Lily, they’ll just disappoint you.”

“I’m used to disappointing people,” Sirius said, almost smiling; “the shock wears off after a while. Now too-da-fucking-loo, Snivelly.”

Scorned and embarrassed, Snape finally turned and left them in the middle of the hall, stalking away for what Remus hoped, but knew, wouldn’t be the last time. Still, as he watched him go, he couldn’t deny the giddy feeling he’d gotten watching Sirius verbally thrash one of his greatest enemies.

“You were too mean,” Lily sighed sadly, “and yet somehow I’m still grateful.”

Sirius turned around and took Lily’s hand in his, actually dropping down into a bow and kissing her freckled knuckles. Remus felt his mouth go dry just watching and had to clear his throat as Lily’s eyes turned to saucers.

“I am sorry for every nasty thing I have ever said, thought, or even briefly wondered about you. And—" Sirius beamed at her; "I am grateful to be your friend.”

“Oh, well, I—” Lily also cleared her throat; “Thank you, Sirius. Really.”

Sirius winked up at her. “Anytime, Evans.”

“You’ve never said that you’re grateful to be my friend.” The comment slipped out before Remus could stop it.

With any and all bad mojo dispersed, Sirius dropped Lily’s hand and straightened up. “Ah, well you’re not just my friend Moony, you’re the apple of my eye—my fair-haired boy!”

Unable to help it, Remus opened his mouth to tease him some more; “Actually that sounds more like Peter to me."

“The yin to my yang then!”

“James.”

“Alright—you're the light of my bloody life then!”

“Nuh-uh!” Lily jumped in spectacularly. “I’m the light of Remus’ life! And he’s my object of dearest affections!”

Sirius sighed dramatically, sagging against the row of school lockers behind him. “I am running out of metaphors here people! Keep it up and I’ll make you, Evans, my gentlemanly caller, and Moony here—honey bunch!”

“Why wouldn’t Remus be the gentlemanly caller?” Lily snorted.

Sirius covered his mouth with his hand as though he were scandalised. “Oh, because we’re much more intimate than that. What you and I have is still just puppy love, but Moony—us together is like a burning flame of wanton eroticism.”

“Keep it up and I’m going to smack you with your own thesaurus!” Remus swore. He could hardly function anymore as friends. One spark of eroticism and he might actually keel over. Though, Sirius would probably pay to see that, he expected.

“Careful, he might like it,” Lily smirked, confirming Remus' suspicions.

“Maybe I will. We’ll never know unless we try—” Already puckering up for a kiss, Sirius made to straighten up, only to gag a little when his school shirt got caught on the edge of the locker, pinning him in place. “Oh hell—Moony, be a dear and come free me.”

Remus turned to Lily. “Lily, are you hungry?”

Lily turned to him. “Why yes, Remus, I believe I am.”

Remus offered his arm. “May I escort you to dinner, oh light of my life?”

She took it. “Yes, oh object of my dearest affections, I would simply love that.”

“Wait!” Sirius wailed as they turned and started down the hall. “Evans! Moony! You can’t just leave me, I’m gonna tear my shirt here! C’mon guys, I’ll keep trying! How ‘bout 'my angel'? Dear paramour? Sweetheart?! Honey bunch!? C'mon guys, don’t leave me behind!”





* * *





Peter wasn’t much of a liar. In fact, Remus could’ve sworn that keeping a secret caused him physical pain, so it made sense that he hadn’t been lying about James. Completely amazed by his best friend's unsung talent, Sirius leapt up from his spot on the music room’s risers, swinging the acoustic around his back and grinning like a madman. “You jammy bastard! If I’d have known that this was what you were capable of when McGonagall kicked you off the football team, then I would’ve poisoned Snape ages ago!”

“Poisoned him? I'd have put him in the ground already,” Remus said from his seat on the risers.

James waved them off before slinging the Rickenbacker off his shoulders and setting it down on the guitar stand. “Man, my arms feel like rubber,” he huffed.

“You might feel better if you don’t hold your breath for the entire solo,” Peter supplied from his spot behind the drum kit.

“Yeah, I think you’re right, Pete,” James smiled. "Honestly I’m glad you noticed. Pretending I understood what you were on about with those silly little lines and dots was really starting to suck. Just gotta work on my endurance, I guess."

“Endurance—smurance! I still cannot BELIEVE you just casually picked up ‘All Along the Watchtower’ by EAR!” Sirius gushed, still shaking his head in disbelief.

James rubbed his neck. “I'm sure it’s not that big a’deal."

"No, it is,” Remus said. “You’ve got perfect pitch, Potter. Not even Black has that.”

“Oi. I don't need perfect pitch. I have range." Sirius illustrated his claim by launching into a bit of Led Zeppelin. " 'And I'm buying a stairway to heaveeeeen'!"

"You always have to steal the show," Remus sniggered, balling up some scrap sheet music and pelting Sirius upside the head with it.

Again, James tried to wave them off. "Okay, fine, so I have perfect pitch. What, like three out of four Beatles must've had it too?”

“Try none of them," Peter said, and when they all glanced at him in surprise, he balked a bit. "What? So I did some research over Easter. Sue me..."

"C'mon Potter, how do you do it? Now, don't be shy, spit it out!" Sirius demanded, grabbing his friend by the shoulders and shaking him across the music room floor.

"I don't know!" James pleaded. "I just hear the notes and match the right colours together, alright?!"

Sirius stopped his incessant shaking immediately. "Colours?"

"Yeah! I just figured out which colours go with what sound. Makes things easy, that way."

Remus squinted at Sirius, then Peter. "Prongs, what do you mean by 'colours'?"

"You know, like the colours you see when you hear certain stuff? Like... a dog barking is this weird orangey-brown colour, but a trolley honk is like more rusty? You can just see it, yeah?"

They all blinked at him, and finally Sirius leaned forward, slowly shaking his head. "We... don't see colour when we hear a dog bark, mate. We hear a dog. Barking. That's it."

James frowned. "Are you pulling my leg?"

"Honestly, think we should be asking you that," Remus said. "You really just like... see colour when you hear shit?"

"Not everything has a colour," James babbled. "Just like—specific sounds. And names. And... notes. It's how I remember 'em! Been doing it since I was a kid... You sure you guys don't see anything? Like at all?"

They all shook their heads.

James' entire body relaxed, as though a thought were just occurring to him for the very first time. "Wow. Shit."

"Wait, I think I've heard of this," Peter said excitedly. "Mozart had it. They said he could see specific words and colours in his mind while he was playing. It helped him write. That happens for you, yeah James?" At his question, James nodded dumbly, and Peter used one of his drumsticks to point at Remus. "Moony, go on and pluck a string for him. See if we're right."

Perking up, Remus readjusted his seat on the risers and plucked a single chord off his bass. They all turned straight for James, who licked his lips and nodded again, this time a little more sure of himself.

"That's an E. It's purple. Not like bright purple, but more soft. Like a lavender."

"And this one?" Remus plucked a D-sharp.

"Definitely green."

"But what note is it?"

"D-sharp."

Remus looked to Sirius, who's mouth was hanging open. "Wow, alright. And this note?"

At the sound, James nearly smiled. "That's an A. A's are always yellow."

"Holy shit!" Sirius gasped. "You mean you really just see that? He plays an A and you see yellow?"

"I thought it happened for everyone," James said, looking just as shocked. "My mum used to joke that my gran would make this egg casserole that tasted like the colour of day-old rubbish so she hated eating it. Made perfect sense at the time."

"Maybe he doesn't have perfect pitch," Peter said. "Maybe he's just a mutant."

"More like superhero! That shit's like magic!" Sirius grinned, picking up the Rickenbacker himself and sliding the strap over his shoulders. "I'm gonna play something—you say what it looks like."

“Sure,” James chuckled, appearing more than happy to play along.

Excitedly, Sirius ripped into one of his favourite Zeppelin licks, which had them all leaning forward to get a better listen. When he was done, James arched a single eyebrow and crossed his arms over his chest. "You're gonna play Jimmy Page and tell me that it don't sound exactly like bright red? It was just one big swirl of it. Like a tornado."

"Amazing!" Sirius cried. "This is so cool, imagine what we could do with your superpower. We're gonna writing songs that sound and look like masterpieces! C'mon, we could start right now. I have that that little diddle I did up in our room yesterday—you know the one, goes like—” Sirius began plucking away at a fun selection of notes. “Hey? Hey?!”

"Alright," Remus said, unslinging his bass and standing up for a stretch. "You guys can start without me, but I'm gonna go get a drink from the fountain. Be right back."

"Actually me too," James said, slipping over to Remus' side.

"Look at him," Sirius pouted, "he's already running."

"I'll be right back," James assured him. "While we're gone, why don’t you do the band a favour and break in our dear drummer boy a little bit more? Oh and—that 'little diddle' of yours was hot fucking pink.”

Grinning happily, Sirius arched a cheeky brow and turned to Peter, who was busy yawning and rubbing the sleep from his eyes with a drumstick in each hand. “Aw dammit,” he mumbled after, which only made Sirius cackle as he crossed the risers to him.

“C’mon, Wormy, Pot’s right. You’ve been doing an awful lot of ' just watching' at these practices of ours—now it's time we see what you’re really made of. Got any wicked drum fills to show off? No weird brain-colours necessary, honest."

"Don't bother me," Peter whined. "I'm happy going at my own pace."

"Aw, but I already know you’ve been practising in secret—perfect time to fess up! Now let's hear that talent!”

“We’re lucky that teacher of yours lets us practice here after class and weekends,” James said, “don’t think we could get away with having a drum kit in the dorms.”

“It’s gonna be hell trying to find someplace to rent in London,” Remus said snidely. “Can you imagine drums in a flat? Ha.”

“So you’re serious then—about moving back home and being in a band together?”

Remus felt suddenly self-conscious. “Well, it’s a funny thought, sure, but there’s not much else I wanna do right now. And with you and Sirius, how can we go wrong?”

James looked down shyly, before reaching out to let his hand trail along the cinder block wall of the hallway. “So you don’t want to go into politics like your dad then?”

“Fuck no.”

“Ha. Fair.”

“Do you want to be a lawyer like your dad?”

Stopping next to the water fountain, James leaned up against the wall and rubbed his arm. “Not really,” he confessed, “but if I go to university I’ll get to play football on an official team. In our meeting the other day, Bilshin told me he figures I have a chance at a scholarship actually—s’long as I don’t bollix it up and get myself tossed off the team next year.”

Remus cracked a smile. “Better put out a restraining order on Black then, just to be safe.”

“I better,” James said, matching it.

“So you want to play sports professionally?”

“Maybe,” James shrugged. “I did when I was a kid, but it never really felt like the best thing. Dad loves football but didn’t like the idea of me pining over it. Says you break your body before you’re thirty—and then what, live as a cripple?”

“A filthy rich cripple.”

“Only if you’re good.”

“Trust me, Prongs, you’re good. Even I know that.”

“Even you?”

Remus sighed. “You finally gonna make me say it? I fucking hate football, mate.”

“I know,” James laughed. “It’s such a shame really. I’d kill for your legs.”

“Thanks, ‘Legs’, I’ll take that as a compliment.” Smirking, Remus bent forward and took a drink from the fountain.

“So what was it Sirius said to Snape again?” James asked, and Remus drew back up, wiping his mouth.

“He not tell you?”

“Nope, heard it from Lily actually. Surprising right? Sounds like just the thing he’d brag about.”

“Maybe he’s maturing.”

“Don’t bet on it.” James replaced him at the water fountain, speaking between gulps; “So what’d he say?”

“Told him off for Lily’s sake mostly. There was something about Snape literally making new friends like Frankenstein, but then Sirius apologised.”

James straightened up, water dripping down his chin. “To Snape?”

“No,” Remus answered in amusement, “to Lily. For ‘every bad thing he’s ever said, thought, or briefly wondered’.”

James wiped his mouth on his sleeve to reveal a curious smile. “Wonder what’s brought that on. Maybe she’s got something on him.”

“I told you, it’s maturation.”

“You really believe that?”

“No, but they say if you say things out loud enough times eventually they’ll come true.”

“And who’s ‘they’?”

“You know—them—people.”

“I see. Could you also ask them who’s gonna win the Cup this year? Pretty sure Dad’s bet most of my inheritance on Manchester.”

Remus’ smile broadened. “Ah, but what do you need that for when you’re gonna be a famous rock star?”

James surged forward and slung an arm around his shoulders. “Oh, Moony, I like the you that comes out when Sirius isn’t in the room. He’s so playful, that one.”

“Oh stuff it.”

They walked back together, following the paintings of various instruments that led back to the music rooms. “What even is that?” James asked, pointing at the image of a boxy string instrument.

“A crwth,” Remus answered smugly. "What—your superpower not tell you that?"

"It has its limits," James said. Then he sighed, but like with most things concerning him, it was a happy sigh. “You know, I do sorta wish we could just say we were gonna be in a band. Might make things feel less—I dunno—uncertain.”

“Which things?”

“You know—things—” He echoed Remus teasingly; "the future. Boring stuff.”

“Maybe we’re just going about it wrong,” Remus offered lightly. “Maybe we gotta stop saying we’re ‘gonna’ be in a band, and just say that we ‘are’ a band. Sirius’ll at least be happy about that.”

“Hm. You know you’re so smart, Moony. You better kick his ass come exams.”

Remus bit his lip to hide a smile, and offered his fist. “Count on it.”

James returned the fist bump and they rounded the corner toward the music room. As they approached, the sound of drums drifted toward them, uneasy and staggered at first, but eventually dropping into a cool and gentle beat.

“ ‘Little Wing’,” James said, recognising the song, “he’s playing Hendrix, too.”

Remus pushed the doors open to find Peter across the room, playing with his eyes closed while Sirius stood behind them. When he noticed them, Sirius waved his hands in the air and pointed vigorously to Peter, mouthing; ‘This guy, man!’

Finishing the drum fill, Peter let the notes filtered off at the end before opening his eyes and slowly looking back at Sirius. “So?”

“It was GREAT!” Sirius shouted.

“Pete!” James called immediately after; “Were you actually playing with your bloody eyes closed?”

Peter clutched the drumsticks nervously. “Well I—”

“It was great,” Remus said quickly, as James practically vibrated at his side.

“It was,” he agreed, before throwing his hands up in the air. “And guess what, Moony says we’re in a band!”

“WE ARE?!” Peter said, at the same moment Sirius shouted; “HE DID?!”

James nudged Remus in the side. “Tell ‘em, Moony!”

Remus looked to James, rolling his eyes over a smile, before throwing his arms up too, albeit a little less enthusiastically. He had to save face somehow.

“Guess we’re in a band, lads.”

Sirius’ arms immediately shot skyward to mirror his. “FUCK YEAH WE’RE IN A BAND!” He wailed, streaking down the bleachers until he met them at the doors. “This is fucking brilliant! It's vita brevis! Oi Pete—get your mousy butt down here and join our band already!”

As Peter scrambled down from his kit, Sirius looped an arm around both James and Remus' necks. “This is gonna be great,” he swore, “we’re gonna be great.”

Peter reached them and James loped an arm around him to gather him into the circle, but Remus couldn’t look anywhere but at Sirius. He could feel the ghost of Sirius’ thumb as it stroked the side of his jaw and sent shivers down his entire back.

I like you so much, he wanted to tell him—wanted to scream it. He’d been so distracted since they’d gotten back, but how could he have been when Sirius was always the most distracting thing in the room? He wanted to drown in it—to satiate the need or stop it, he wasn’t sure. And now Sirius’ eyes, which were never not alight with cheeky mischief or mad passion, were filled with promise. In them, Remus saw what might’ve been a glint of their future and when Sirius finally looked back to him, smiling like he’d just been handed the key to Heaven, he knew he’d found his answer. And just like Tonya, it wasn’t in London.

It was right there.



Chapter End Notes

'Upper sixth' refers to year 13, which would equate to the 12th grade in North America. Lower sixth is therefore year 12/11th grade.

'Jeter l’éponge' literally means 'throw the sponge' but it's a French idiom meaning 'to give up'.

What James has is a form of synesthesia (specifically 'chromesthesia' or sound-to-colour synesthesia) which means that sound invokes an involuntary visual representation in the user's mind when they experience a certain thing or feeling. Synesthesia is different for everyone who has it, and not much is known even today about how it is caused. It makes sense that James would've gone his whole life without realising he was different, as testing for this sort of thing did not exist and information on it was slim to none.

Chapter 60: Paws Off, Padfoot

Trying to make some sense of it all,

But I see it makes no sense at all;

Is it cool to go to sleep on the floor?

I don’t think that I can take anymore;

Clowns to the left of me!

Jokers to the right!

Here I am, stuck in the middle with you…

“Stuck in the Middle with You” Stealers Wheel, 1972



In a lot of ways, dating Marlene had been easier than not dating her at all. Back then Remus could be trusted to better hold himself in check, but without a girlfriend to procure notions of guilt over, his feelings for Sirius had begun to run rampant. He'd remembered what it was like to be jealous of James whenever he and Sirius went off together, or began talking about anything moderately close to music—which was more often than not, now that they'd actually agreed to make their 'band' official. He caught himself glaring at the girls that stared at him when he walked past, and laughing a little louder at his jokes just to be sure that Sirius heard him over the others. Remus didn't want to laugh. He felt more like crying, and the jokes were usually shite anyway.

He tried to keep everything at bay by edging himself into denial—meditating on pensive thoughts such as how his feelings could just be that of those forged in friendship, now blown out of proportion due to his failed relationship, boredom at school, or general disinterest in his current reality. Surely he was just mistaking 'like' for something more substantial, and the turn-around period for such ridiculous things was simply much longer than anticipated. It even occurred to him that he could be mistaking his ideas of Sirius as leftover affection for Tonya. After all, the likeness was uncanny. From the inexplicable desire to have drama follow them from room to room, down to their inky-black tresses, the similarities were almost endless. Perhaps he was simply feeling this way because Sirius was there and Tonya was not. Every time he thought he'd begun to miss her again, Sirius was by his side, offering him smiles and distractions by the armful. But it would never work, Remus would tell himself. No matter how guilty he'd felt while dating Marlene, it was nothing compared to the guilt he now faced alone. The Twelfth of Never would fall upon Tibb's Eve before the two of them could ever be anything more than friends.

And why's that? That devil on his shoulder would say, whenever he thought he'd made peace with it. Sirius said it himself, he likes blokes. And he ain't dating that love-sick, primrose Chastity Bell anymore. What's a'matter, chap—afraid you might like it?

Yes, Remus thought back a million times. Some might deny it, but 'like' and envy went hand in hand. There were plenty of people who didn't like Sirius Black, but they certainly envied him. Whether for his looks or his smarts or his money, or that bewitching devil-may-care attitude of his. Sirius was bold and daring and Remus, he... wasn't. He was just Remus. He was happy being the tag-along, the sarcastic friend with a fag and a half-decent music recommendation in his back pocket, the kid with a crappy dad because nine out of ten dads were crappy anyway. He could be 'Remus and his books'—'Remus and his fags'—'Remus and GODDAMMIT WOULD YOU ALL JUST LEAVE ME ALONE?!'

Maybe it was a hard realisation, but it would've been worse to lie to himself. He just wasn't willing to risk it all like Sirius was, and if he were being truly honest with himself, he was afraid. Afraid that Sirius would ask him to.

Though... that didn't mean he couldn't look, right? Sirius made that part easy, what with his, well—everything. Between Remus' own romancing and the way things had gone down with Tomny, he'd somehow missed it, but where Sirius had been handsome before, the shape he was growing into now was downright stunning. He had a side-profile that made Remus want to punch him if just to add a dent to the perfect ridge of his nose. Unlike so many other musicians, his fingers were long and delicate—a realisation that had come after they'd received a lecture in art class about the Sistine Chapel. Remus had thought crudely that compared to Sirius, Michelangelo's depiction of Adam's hands were rather ugly. And then because it was so embarrassing, Remus rushed back to the dorm for an ice-cold shower.

I must be going insane, he thought, while drowning himself under the showerhead. No sane person thinks about someone else this much. Maybe I should just tape a bag over his head—see him try and look so bloody fit then. Bastard.

Oh, he blamed Sirius, alright. Not just for his looks or his inability to be missed in any crowd he was ever in, but for his kindness. And for keeping his secrets.

A full month had passed since that phone call with Tomny. More often than not it hung over Remus' head like a dark cloud, but thanks to his friends' goodwill, he was finally starting to feel okay again. He dreaded summer, but at least he would have James and Peter. Mary and Marlene too, if he could put up with their primping and preening. He was more worried for Sirius, who'd had such a horrible time over Christmas, but they would both find ways to distract themselves. Sirius was wreak his havoc, and Remus would read his books, maybe even venture out on occasion. Not to the End, no—he refused to obsess over people who had no interest in him, no matter how many pretty words they used to justify it. Even now, Remus wasn’t sure what Sirius had done with Tonya’s letter, and he didn’t ask. He’d been right to hand it over. Secrets like that only made him and Sirius closer, and when he was ignoring his more ludicrous emotions, he supposed it only made them better friends too.

You have my everything, he thought, each and every time he found himself staring at Sirius from across their bedroom, classroom, or dinner table. It didn’t matter how much distance was between them, or how stupid he knew he was for doing it, Remus was always staring at Sirius. It as though he put him in a trance. It happened so often that some of the others had even taken notice, and Remus had had to make up a few imaginary bees just to get himself out of it. But it was okay now—he was okay—except he still wasn't sure how he was going to keep himself from ruining a friendship that meant everything when a single glance from Sirius left him thrumming from top to bottom. It made him apprehensive to let Sirius come close, but he also couldn’t bear to let him drift away. It was like some horrible game of cat and mouse, without knowing who was playing what. Remus had never fancied himself a wolf, but playing cat and reaching for the stars didn't sound all that more pleasant.

Thursday 19th May 1977

After several weeks of practice, Hawkings’ first (and likely only) rock band, 'The Marauders', were finally starting to sound half-decent. James and Sirius found it rather difficult not playing over one another every other song and Peter still dragged behind in tempo sometimes, forcing Remus to make up for the lost rhythm with his bass lines, but for a couple of wannabe rock stars with only Sirius' formal training to split amongst them, they'd certainly done alright.

Tuesdays and Thursdays had become unofficial practice nights, along with the occasional Sunday if they were feeling up to it. With the incident involving Snape long behind them, James eight-week ban from the football team was about to be lifted, which would probably change how often they could get together, but Remus had Sirius had already been assured: this was for real. All for one and one for all, those Marauders. Remus couldn't wait until they were making music of their own.

For now though, it was just any other Thursday. Remus was supposed to be meeting the guys for another practice, except he was running late after getting sucked into a conversation with his new biology partner, Jillian, who seemed a bit too eager to get a jump start on their project. He’d made the mistake of using the band as an excuse to try and leave, which had only opened up an opportunity for Jillian to pepper him with more questions. It’d taken a while to shake her, and he doubted his friends would’ve found it as interesting a conversation as Jillian seemed to. They’d probably have just made fun of him for not being able to say no to the girl—but it didn’t matter much anyway, as the moment Remus rounded the corner leading up to the music building's front doors, he was drawn to an immediate halt.

All thoughts of biology and Jillian evaporating instantly, Remus watched as Sirius leaned out of door, one foot crossed in front of the other at the ankle. He was talking to a girl—just chatting really, but he was leaning back against the open door so casually that not even a blind man would have mistaken it for anything other than flirting. A moment of pathetic doubt flitted across his mind—Maybe they're also talking about a... biology... project—but then Sirius smiled and touched his thumb to the side of his mouth and Remus knew he was right.

Uncomfortable with the idea of walking right between the two of them, he skirted to the side of the pavement and bent down, pretending as though he was riffling through his guitar case and having to retie his shoelaces. Half of him wanted to crane his ear just to catch a snippet of their conversation, but that jealous Moony that had been living under his skin for who knows how long wanted nothing to do with it.

It took far too long for the conversation to end for it be anything innocent, and by then Remus’ ankles were beginning to ache from the three-dozen times he'd tied and untied his shoes. When the pair finally said goodbye and Sirius slipped back inside the music hall, he stood and stiffly made his way to the front doors, bass guitar in hand. He passed the girl, whose uniform was made up of Rowena House colours just like Lily and the other girls'. For a split-second Remus was so caught up by the navy blue of her skirt that he'd nearly missed the little wave she gave him. Not that it wouldn't have mattered—he did not return the gesture.

Throwing open the doors to the music hall, he muscled his bass inside and took a deep breath. Sirius was just ahead of him down the hall, walking with his hands in his pockets and—was he whistling?

“Oi! Black!"

The cherry tune cut out immediately as Sirius turned around, a wide grin on his face. “Oi, yourself, Moony. Thought we were gonna be waiting on your sorry arse all night.”

Feeling strangely apprehensive after the quip, Remus approached Sirius, who’d stopped to wait for him, and swallowed the lump in his throat.

“Who was that?” He asked, indicating to the doors with a jerk of his head.

Sirius looked around him before scratching his nose. “Oh, you mean Tess? She’s in English with James and I. Was just asking me about the homework.”

“Just homework? Nothing else?”

Sirius gave him a funny look, which was ironic because Remus felt anything but funny.

“We talked about the band too," he said. "Can you believe it? Guess word’s getting around. We’re already famous.” Sirius stepped forward and clapped him on the shoulder in a friendly manner, but Remus hardly noticed.

“You were flirting,” he said sharply.

Sirius' funny look returned, this time accompanied by a self-satisfied smirk that made Remus want to punch his lights in.

“Was I?”

“Yeah, you were. So what, you gonna date her?”

“Would it be a problem if I did?”

Remus’ mouth opened, temporarily dazed by Sirius’ brazen response. “N-No. You just—might as well fess up to it if you’re interested.”

“Why, you got a thing for Tess?”

Say no, a voice screamed.

“Would it be a problem if I did?”

Idiot.

Sirius glanced down and then shoved his hands back into his pockets. “No… no problem. Didn’t realise you and Tess knew each other all that well, that’s all. But yeah, I’ll back off. Not worth risking your best mate for some girl, right?”

Remus felt his stomach sink.

You fucking idiot.

“I don’t have a thing for Tess,” he confessed. Sirius squinted at him.

“You don’t? Then why the grumpiness?”

“Jus'... in a bad mood. Sorry. Date her if you want.”

“You're so weird. I never actually said I was gonna date her,” Sirius said, trading his confused look for a smile.

Great, now he thinks you're weird, Remus thought.

You ARE weird, jealous Moony said.

The thought was enough to leave Remus panicking.

"You think I'm weird?" He demanded.

"Uh—yes?" Sirius looked him up and down. "Or no. Actually, I'm not really sure what the right answer is here. Can you give me a hint?"

Mortified at his own lunacy, Remus forced a smile. "…Was only joking. We both know Potter's the biggest weirdo anyway, right? I mean, I don't know any other seventeen year-olds ready for marriage, do you?"

Satisfied by the response, Sirius laughed in agreement. "Nope. Now who'd have thought it—the only tosser among us with a well-adjusted family and he's the weirdo."

They laughed together, albeit awkwardly, and Remus rocked back on his heels until his fried nerves gave way.

“Wanna get to practice then?” He suggested.

“Sure, Moony. We were waiting for you.”

Sirius turned and motion for him to follow, and Remus did, feeling horribly stupid. Who was he to police those Sirius did and didn’t date? Best friends didn’t do that. He had to get control of these embarrassing outbursts.

Back in music room #2, their friends were waiting for them. Peter was already tucked up behind the drum kit, licking his thumb as he flipped through a book on music theory. James sat next to him on a stool, spinning haphazardly in circles while holding the 1964 Strat Sheila had so graciously lent out to him for practice. As the door clattered shut behind them, James looked up.

“About time Cinderella arrived for the ball,” he called; “Clock’s just about to strike midnight, you know.”

“Yes, and he’s broken a glass slipper so don’t test him,” Sirius cheeked.

“I’m fine, let’s just play,” Remus grumbled loosely.

James exchanged a wary look with Peter, who just shrugged and added his own sound effect with the drums; ba-dum-tsss!

Remus ignored it, setting the Fender's case down and popping the lid. "Black, you got those music sheets?"

"Right here," Sirius said, dropping a paper folder down on a music stand.

“Hell yes, what we playing tonight, Maestro?” James asked.

“Maestro is not an acceptable nickname,” Sirius scoffed, shoving the sheet music into his chest. James took the paper—which they all knew now he couldn't read anyway—and began toddling after Sirius with a coddling smile.

“Ah, c’mon—you were just complaining yesterday that you don't have one. I’m really trying here.”

Sirius handed Peter his music sheets. “Try harder.”

“I think it’s fine,” Remus said, from across the room.

“That’s ‘cause you’re a shit.”

"Since when are you supposed to like a nickname? You were the one who forced those stupid names onto us in the first place."

"My nicknames are art!" Sirius cried, balling up Remus' sheet music and throwing it at him. "You're an arse."

“So you don’t want one?” Peter asked, while Remus chased his paper ball down the music stand.

“Never said that,” Sirius said haughtily. "But honestly—who are we right now? We got Moony, Wormtail, Prongs, and Black. What the fuck—that’s so lame!”

“I'll remind you again that you're the one who came up with all of that crap in the first place,” James added snidely. "If you don't like any of our suggestions, just give yourself one."

Lifting his guitar strap over his head, Sirius paused long enough to flip James the bird. “I can’t just give myself a nickname. That’s worse than lame, that’s bottom of the fucking barrel-level embarrassing.”

“Okay I got it, how about Moony, Prongs, Wormtail and ‘that other asshole’?”

“I appreciate the menial effort but that’s not exactly snappy enough.”

“How about ‘The Hair’?” Peter suggested.

“Oooh—! I like that one!” James grinned, while Sirius scoffed.

“Fuck you guys, you’re not taking this seriously at all.”

“We could always call you ‘Trouble’! Or how ‘bout ‘Starboy’?”

“That sounds like the name of a cheesy superhero," Remus called.

“Exactly!" James shouted gleefully; "He could be the sidekick to Bowie’s ‘Starman’, eh?”

“Fuck you, not a chance," Sirius hissed. "I ain't anybody's sidekick, so let’s just get going on 'Honky Tonk Woman' before you're kicked out of the band for being absolutely useless."

Sighing wistfully, James returned to his stool, rumpled music sheet in hand.

“It's okay, Prongs, I liked that one,” Peter said out of the corner of his mouth.

“Thank you, Wormtail. Wanna walk me through the rhythm?"

Peter rolled his eyes. "Honestly, when you gonna actually learn to read music? What good's a super power if you can't read?"

"Meh, reading's for you normal blokes. Call me when your dad's voice starts sounding like the colour of chocolate chip cookies."

As James scooted in closer to the drum kit, Remus walked himself and his bass back across the orchestra risers, setting his paper down on the stand next to Sirius' and picking up the Fender. Sirius watched him out of the corner of eye, while tuning the Rickenbacker.

“You’ve been awfully quiet," he said to Remus. "What, no stupid nickname jokes?”

“Nope,” Remus shrugged, picking out the notes of the song's chorus.

“Nothing? What happened to that creative mind of yours?”

“I don't work for free.”

“Stingy arsehole. Your D's out of tune by the way.”

One corner of Remus’ mouth curled upwards and he tucked his pick between his lips. "Maybe you have perfect pitch," he muttered, but before he could even look up to gauge Sirius' reaction, the other boy appeared in front of him, nose only a few millimetres from his. Almost spitting out his pick, Remus jumped backward on the stands. “What the—back off, you idiot!”

“Not until you suggest something,” Sirius pushed, pushing way beyond the limits of personal space.

“I don't care, tell James you're flippin' Maestro and let's call it a day!”

“Ha—Try again.”

“Fucking—I don’t know!”

Sirius reached out and grabbed Remus’ face on either side, practically shaking his head back and forth. “I’m gonna rattle your snarky gob until something decent falls out!”

“Get off me!” Remus hissed, pushing him off. “God, you’re incessant—like a bloody dog!”

“Good, keep it going!” Sirius encouraged.

“You want me to call you a dog?!”

“I want you to suggest something! Join the club already, Moony! It's only been two years!”

"Oh, fuck off," Remus bristled.

Sirius didn't seem to care. "C'mon, we know you've got dogs. You name them—now name me!"

“Fine!" He threw his arms up. "Zenyatta, Seabiscuit, Padfoot—"

"Padfoot and Zenyatta?" Sirius grimaced. "Those are terrible names."

"UGH! Take your pick, I don’t care, just don't—”

Remus drew up short, his breath leaving him all at once.

Just don't touch me.

A beat passed and then Sirius huffed, clearly unsatisfied. “Guess it’s true, you can’t force perfection—or a half-way decent nickname.”

“Dogs this, dogs that—there was so clearly a bitch joke in there,” James said to Peter, almost as though he were trying to diffuse the sudden tension.

"I thought 'Padfoot' was kinda cute," Peter returned.

Ignoring them, Remus bent over to pick up his dropped pick and wipe it off on his shirt before returning it to the corner of his mouth.

“Bloody lunatic, it's just a nickname. Have mine if you’re so pressed,” he grumbled to Sirius, who’d turned away to plug his guitar into an amp.

“You can’t just recycle a nickname," Sirius lashed, "that’s horse-shit.”

“Given this enough thought, have you?”

“Blame Lottie. She was the one who brought the utter lack of equality among this group of lads to my attention in the first place.”

“You’ve gotta be kidding me,” Peter scoffed.

“I’m sure he isn’t,” James sang, “but if you two are done with your little spat, I actually want to make it in time for dinner, so let’s just shut up and start playing, yeah?”

Remus stood up and pulled the pick from his lips. “Yes, let's."

They all dispersed a bit to ready themselves, and Remus did his best to ignore Sirius' presence. Despite this, he could tell Sirius was watching him again; his gaze felt like a million tiny little pin pricks staring him in the back. Too stubborn to give him a reaction and too rattled to call him on it, Remus walked over to his own amp and tested the volume. He made sure to bring his music sheet with him, so he didn't have to be next to Sirius while they practiced.

You never make things any easier, he told him telepathically. Just for Christ sakes, stay away.

"You got the basics already, Potter?" Sirius called, still eyeing Remus as though he was the toy he’d wanted and hadn't got.

"Basically," James shrugged. "You guys just give it go. I'll follow you."

"Alright. Moony, you good?"

"Let's just play," Remus muttered.

"Fine. Pete, count us in.”

Peter squinted at the sheet music. “Okay, but I don’t have a cowbell..."





* * *





Friday 20th May 1977 — The Next Day

They didn't always fight. Some days were good—like the Monday before when they'd taken all the freshly-dissected frogs from the biology lab and hid them in Professor Flitwick's desk just before class. The shriek he'd given when he opened his drawer while looking for a pencil had been enough to leave Remus and Sirius in stitches for hours. It'd been ages since they'd pulled a proper prank, and Sirius seemed eager to bring one to fruition, even if it wasn't on such a grand scale as those they'd managed to pull off before. If Sirius had known what was coming, he probably wouldn’t have been so eager. But that was the fun of practical jokes, Remus supposed; full of surprises. Though, he wasn’t sure what cow-tipping had to do with pranking.

“Well, it’s not really a prank, we’ve just never done it,” James amended, as they made their way down the lane in the dark, one half-drunk bottle of whisky in hand. Skipping out on curfew had been his and Sirius' idea, but with a little liquid-courage, Remus and Peter had been just as eager to join in.

“You sound pretty lax for someone who is not only counting on getting back onto the football team, but also wants to be dorm monitor next year,” Remus said, never one to let his friends off easy. Smirking around the rim of his gin bottle, he threw back a final gulp before passing it to Peter, who finished it off and tossed it into a bin along the side of the road.

“I’m not counting on anything—I’m on the team! And I told you, I’m only considering it,” James insisted.

“Nah, he’ll do it,” Sirius started, punching James lightly in the shoulder. “Imagine the parties—and he can declare his undying love for Evans at every one. Don’t that sound great, Prongsy?”

“That sounds like a surefire way to get fired,” Peter added.

“Really, Wormtail, do you think he’ll be the first dorm head in history to throw a party? It’s time you started thinking bigger and better, my friend.”

“Hmph.”

"How did you even come up with this 'cow-tipping' thing anyway?" Remus asked. "Thought they only do shit like this in dumb American television."

"As a matter of fact, that's exactly how we found out," Sirius said, before going on to explain how he and James had been forced to watch some horrible 'coming of age' movie in their Classics class. "There's always cows in that field just around the eastern lip of campus, right? James and I saw them this morning from the top floor of the science block."

"We did," James confirmed. "They're there."

"Don't cows bite?" Peter asked.

"Sure, they got teeth," Sirius shrugged, "but I'd be more worried about getting trampled. Cows and buffalo aren't that distantly related, you know."

"I'm gonna tip the most," James said, before hiccupping. "I shall be the—" HIC! "—King of cows!"

"Now that's a nickname," Sirius said.

Remus was sceptical, and didn't fancy dragging any of his friends back to the medical room when they got trampled, but after emerging through 'Moony's glory hole' (“Sirius I will murder you.”) there was no going back anyway. Their only real regret was that James’ torch had turned up dead and they were left with only a single torchlight to guide them.

“What, why aren’t we tipping the school’s cows?” Remus asked, squinting ahead of them down the dark dirt road that followed along the outside of the school wall.

“Kettleburn never leaves them in the field overnight,” James explained. “Probably for this exact—" HIC! "—reason.”

"Prongs, try holding your breath."

"Okay—" HIC! "—Moony."

“I wouldn’t try messing with the school’s herd anyway,” Peter supplied, flashing the torch around. “They’re all hairy and have horns that look like they could disembowel a grown man. Talk about buffalo.”

“Yeah, but not these guys,” Sirius said, “they’re dairy cattle. Now c’mon, it’s this way.”

Nudging James, who had just managed to stop hiccupping, Sirius took off across the road toward a barbed wire fence and carefully placed his hands and feet along the wire. Making sure to go slow, he stretched it out for each of them to slip through and let James trade with him so he could do the same. Afterwards they were all left standing on the soft ground of the Highland field, staring out with nay a cow in sight.

“Why are we here again?” Remus asked, only because he felt like complaining. It was pitch black and all he could smell was cow dung. At least they'd all worn boots.

“ ‘Cause Moony,” Sirius sighed, “when you think back to your school days ten years from now, you’re not going to remember sitting in class getting lectured by Binns, or the papers you wrote, or even the people you liked and the people you loathed—but cow-tipping with your favourite lads? That you’re gonna remember.”

It was a good argument, so Remus resolved himself to stop complaining and just gestured for Sirius to go on. He did so, winking at him and grinning in that shameless way of his that left Remus feeling exhilarated and tired all at once.

No, you’re already over this, you toff. He’s your friend.

Then why does he have to look like that? And look at me like that? It’s not fair.

Life’s not fair, idiot.

Remus pinched his forehead. He needed to stop having imaginary arguments over Sirius in his head or he really was going to lose it.

“I don’t mean to be the voice of reason or anything,” Peter said as they walked, “but I don’t actually see any cows.”

“They’re here!” Sirius insisted. “We just saw them today, you were Prongs.”

“Is this the right field?” James asked, sounding sceptical himself now.

Sirius began turning around, searching desperately. “Yeah—I mean, I think so..."

“You think so?” Remus echoed.

“Well all fields look the same, don’t they? And it’s bloody Scotland—there’s fields everywhere! All I know is the cows were out behind the science buildings on the opposite side of the fence and now so are we.”

“Cows do have feet, you know—they can move.”

“Thank you for that startling revelation, Lupin.”

“We know they were here because we can still smell them,” James said, pinching his nose for dramatic effect. “How ‘bout we just walk a bit more? Who knows, maybe we’ll find some sleepy sheep instead and we can tip them.”

“I think sneaking up on a sheep might be a little harder,” Peter said, but because they were lightly buzzed and without anything else to do other than return home and head to bed (which was totally unacceptable and totally not cool) they kept walking. Eventually James and Sirius fell into step with one another, sharing the last bottle of whisky and surging on ahead while Remus hung back with Peter and his torch, not interested in breaking an ankle in some stray foxhole. As a result, Peter had taken the chance to share with him his most pressing dilemma: what he was going to get Moira for her upcoming birthday.

“I could always call mum and she could send something, but that almost sounds a bit lazy, don't you think? I was supposed to look over Easter, but she came to visit so I didn't have to time to sneak off, and Moira wouldn't be impressed if it weren't a surprise. You didn't have to buy Marlene a birthday gift while you were dating, did you?”

“Uh-huh... sure...”

Sirius' hair looks a bit blue in the dark. It's the moon. The moon must make it blue.

“Are you even listening, Moony?”

Remus blinked several times. “Oh yeah, sorry Pete. Why don’t you just make her something then?”

“Like what?”

“Mhm.” Remus drifted off again, unable to help himself only because it was nighttime and Sirius was still ahead of him and Sirius always looked best under the moonlight. It made every inch of him light up like real star-shine. He had his back to him, but Remus knew without looking that his stormy eyes would have turned clear, and his smile—just absolutely blinding.

“He’s your friend…” Remus told himself under his breath. “He’s your friend.”

“Oh yeah,” Peter said sorely, before biting his lip.

“Gifts don’t have to be expensive to be meaningful,” Remus told him, quietly. “Just get her something you know she’ll like.”

“Gross!” He wailed, before letting loose a string of horrible retching noises.

Unfortunately, the tug was a little too good, and his foot shot up right out of his boot, leaving him to sprawl backward in the muck before finally catching himself with one more horrible squelch.

All colour drained from Sirius’ face, and he looked down to find that he’d stepped in a second cow pat, only this time, with his bare foot.

“Oh fuck,” James gasped, “you didn’t actually step in another one, did you? That's prime comedy, mate!”

Sirius gave a wail so loud he could’ve been heard from Castle Hall. Holding a hand to his forehead, Remus fought back a smile. Seeing the normally composed Sirius dance around like a chicken with its head cut off was almost too much.

“It’s just a little cow pat,” he started, barely holding back laughter now. “Could you be any more of a prissy prat?”

Sirius gaped at him, horrible offended; “Would you like to try it?! Because there is cow shit between my toes!”

That was it for Remus, who broke down with laughter so hearty it brought real tears to his eyes while Sirius waddled around, desperately wiping his bare foot on any bit of clean grass he could find. James and Peter joined him, laughing at the whole thing but mostly Sirius, before James shot upright in realisation.

“Cow pat—oh my god, Moony, what was it you called Sirius in the music room yesterday? Pat-foot?”

Sirius’ head turned to them so quickly it almost looked like he gave himself whiplash. “No way,” he hissed.

“Oh hell yeah!” Peter gasped. “That’s it—that’s your nickname! Patty-foot!”

“No fucking way!”

Remus crossed his arms with a shit-eating grin on his face (pun intended); “Oh c’mon, I know you don’t take being the butt of the joke so well, but you didn’t actually think we’d let you pick your own nickname, hm… Pat-foot?”

“That is your DOG'S NAME!" Sirius roared.

“No—he's 'Padfoot'. Though I suppose we could call you that instead on the days where we're feeling generous,” Remus said smugly.

"You dicks! You vicious, betraying les roi des fille de putes! Je t'emmerde!"

"You're right, Pat-foot, the name does have its own sort of 'je ne sais quoi'."

“HA!" James howled. "So good!”

Fuming, Sirius stopped forward and grabbed hold of his boot, yanking it free with one hand and pushing his hair up over his eyes with the other. As he did so, he raised the boot high, primed for throwing.

“Oh fuck,” Peter yelped, already turning to run.

James did the same, shouting; “Run, Moony! He’s gone mad!” And Remus turned, cackling as raced away, a single shit-covered boot arcing over his head while Sirius screamed after him.

“Your accent is ABYSMAL AND YOU’RE ALL DICKHEADS!”

“Watch your step on the way home, Padfoot!” James answered. “Wouldn’t want to become ‘Padfeet’ now would we?”

“AUGHHHH!!!”
