Chapter 62: Loyalty


Chapter Summary

The Marauders plan pranks. Barty loses his teddy bear. Remus worries for Sirius.



Chapter Notes

I think I might've fucked up and posted this too early, but I'm not sure because I panicked and immediately deleted it, lol. This version is a RE-POST. Sorry if you got two notifs.

CW: Smoking, references to abuse. Take care of yourselves first <3



See the end of the chapter for more notes



And these children that you spit on,

As they try to change their worlds;

Their immune to your consultations,

They’re quite aware of what they’re going through;

Ch-ch-ch-ch-changes!

- “Changes” David Bowie, 1971



Sunday 29th May 1977

Remus could tell his friends felt guilty after the incident with Barty. Even after he’d forgiven them, they still insisted on catering to him as though he were some wilted daisy. It was frustrating, but Remus didn't dare snap at them again. Not after what Sirius had said about his scars... And in the days that followed, Barty and the other boys stayed clear, which quickly became the sliver-lining of the whole thing. That, and the undeniable wake-up call that it'd given him. With everything finally out in the open, Remus was forced to reevaluate the way he’d been treating his mother when it came to his other relationships. He realised that not only had she become a skeleton in his closet, but a roadblock when it came to trusting his friends. They believed the rumour because he’d given them absolutely no reason not to, and it left him feeling ill. These were the people he trusted the most, and if he couldn’t be honest with them, then who could he be honest with?

Marlene threw a legendary fit when she found out the truth, spending several hours begging Remus to forgive her for all the things she’d thought and—even worse—told her family. He forgave her on the first apology, but she cried until her voice turned hoarse anyway. In the end he was able to distract her with talk of her most recent read, some science fiction novel she’d devoured in less than a day. He was getting good at distractions these days, it seemed.

The boys, on the other hand, opted for a more stoic approach. Remus knew without asking that they wouldn’t just accept his forgiveness and move on. Something needed to be proven—their loyalty, their support, their hatred for any and all things Barty. He let them only because it meant pranks—less time spent 'coddling Moony' and more time hiding out in their dorm room, pitching ideas back and forth while music played in the background. Remus had to admit, the plans they laid were some of their best yet; a whole week of exams interlaced with merciless pranks on not just Barty, but his roommates as well, who Sirius had generously declared guilty by association. It might’ve just been his way of punishing Regulus, who it turned out he’d had a nasty row with over Easter, but the pranks were harmless enough, so no one said anything.

No one except Lily of course.

“You guys are insane,” she huffed, after arriving at their dorm to collect the maths notes she'd leant Peter.

"Not insane—sensible," Sirius told her, while draped out over James' bed like a cat. "These things have to be nipped in the arse quickly. Can't let Barty think he got away with messing with Moony with only a small bruise to show for it, can we?”

“There is no way you have this much time to mess around while studying. You're going to fail everything at this rate.”

“Au contraire, Evans, it’s only lower sixth. Which means just a few AS-levels lay between us and sweet, sweet payback."

Lily pointed at him viciously. “AS-levels are important! Some of these tests help decide what uni’s you can apply for next year! They’re meant to set up your entire future!”

“Only if you dream of intellectual labour—which I do not."

“Well, what about you?” She demanded of James. “You've only just gotten back on the football team, I thought you were spending every waking moment whipping those guys into shape?”

“I am,” James said, from his place next to Sirius, the same cheeky look on his face, “we planned this stuff instead of sleeping.”

“And you?! I thought you didn’t want to retaliate.” Lily whirled on Remus, who had his back leaned up against the side of Sirius' bed.

“I never said that..." he said, suddenly finding the stack of albums sitting to his left very interesting; "And besides... they’re good pranks.”

“... Ugh. Peter, at least tell me that you’re taking this seriously?”

Peter held up his hands in surrender; “I’m just worried about my maths.”

Shaking her head with a final moan of exasperation, Lily opened her bag and shoved her notebook inside. “Fine, do what you want, but I don’t want to hear about any of it—from any of you!”

“Rest assured,” Sirius promised; “it won’t be us you’ll be hearing it from.”

She scowled lightly; “Alright, to hell with all of you then. I’m late for a prefect meeting anyway.”

“See you at dinner?” James called, and Lily tossed him an irritated wave and shut the door behind herself.

“Ah, I don’t blame her for being mad, I’d lash someone too if I was taking like, six A-levels in my twelfth year,” Sirius said, snatching a piece of notepaper from the stack of school books at the foot of James' bed, and rolling onto his back. Crumpling the paper up, he began tossing the ball up and down methodically.

“She's only taking three," James amended proudly. "And she's working hard! She wants to get into Oxford."

Sirius whistled. "Shooting high, our little swot is. Couldn't be me. How 'bout you, Moons?"

Remus shook his head. Lyall probably would've bent himself in half just to get Remus' name on the applicants list, but fuck him if he thought he was ever going to be some 'scholar'.

“Wait..." Peter said, sitting up on his bed; "Does that mean you guys aren't thinking of university at all?"

"No," Remus said, at the same moment that Sirius snorted; "Of course not."

They shared a glance, and Sirius gave a wink that left Remus slightly weak in the knees. To distract himself, he cleared his throat and turned to Peter. "What about you, Pete? Does this mean you have plans?"

Peter shrugged and looked down at his hands. “Not really. Probably just end up doing business stuff like Dad.”

Catching his paper ball out of the air, Sirius gave a dramatic groan; “Dear fucking lord, I don’t know who’s worse—you or Potter. It’s always, dad’s this, dad’s that. Law or business, business or law—it’s all the same boring crap, and somehow we're still not getting the big picture here!"

"Which is what?" Asked Remus.

"Duh—our band!"

"We can be in a band and be educated, can't we?" James chuckled.

"Sure, but all of the best artists were drop-outs. Like Hendrix and Springsteen."

"So you're not even going to consider it?"

"Nope."

"But what about..." Remus licked his lips. "Going for something like... music?"

"There's an idea," James agreed; "You could find some conservatory—probably go for classical guitar if you really wanted. Or music theory—then you'd be just like all those composers you're always name-droppin'."

"No thanks. Don't care much for being the next Schumann." Sirius kept tossing the paper ball; up and down, up and down. "Besides, already been there, done that."

“What are you on about now?” Peter asked.

“Royal Academy of Music,” Sirius answered, sounding almost bored. “I auditioned for a spot in their piano department at the end of our tenth year. Turned it down.”

Reaching over, James snatched Sirius' paper ball straight out of the air. “You never told us that!”

“Yeah, well, I said no so what's it matter?”

“You mean, your mum didn’t try and make you go?” Peter demanded, finally scuttling off of his bed and coming to sit next to Remus.

“She tried a'course, but she couldn’t make me. I threw the audition. Ruined it before she had the chance.”

“Wow." Remus squinted up at him. "You mean you didn’t want to go at all?”

“Nope. In fact, not going was one of the few sweet victories of my life. Those poor sods are like robots. They live and breathe for music until they don't even like it anymore. Couldn't imagine a worse way to live. Definitely not for me...” Already withdrawn, Sirius turned over onto his stomach on the bed and began picking at the dark blue polish on his fingernails.

Not just any school, Remus thought while watching him; but the Royal Academy of Music... They wanted Sirius, and he turned them down. Wow.

Sometimes it was easy to forget that Sirius was a piano prodigy. Occasionally Remus would try to envision what it might look like to watch Sirius' elegant fingers drift up and down the keys. To listen to their sound and know that it wasn't pouring out of just any soul, but Sirius'—that it once had! Blimey, it must've been amazing, but all he could do was wonder, since Sirius refused to play.

Not that he blamed him.

Near the end of their first year together, Sirius had confessed that his mother had been his piano teacher. While people called him a prodigy outwardly, Sirius had dealt with hours of excruciating practice, playing until his joints locked together and his fingertips bled from the quick. He'd had nails split down the middle on him or else fall off completely, and still Walburga forced him to play. Sirius only confessed these things when he knew he could get away with framing them as a joke. Sometimes it would take Remus days to come to the realisation of what had actually been said, and then he was left with the guilt of it because he hadn't known how to probably comfort him. Maybe it would be different if Sirius had just said things like "she used to make me slam my own fingers in the fallboard when I played out of time", but instead it was always, Mum used to think it was hilarious to shut my fingers in the key cover whenever I cocked things up. It's how I learned to keep time. Who needs a metronome when ya got punishment and reform?

Remus had never met Walburga Black, but he hated her. Viscerally. She'd left Sirius with scars inside and out, and still expected a thank you for granting him such talent. It was vile, and Remus doubted that anybody—not even James—would ever truly know the full extent of what went on inside the walls of the Black home. He couldn't even imagine being there—feeling so terrible all of the time, while simultaneously being forced to play such beautiful music. It was the sort of thing that rewired your brain; what should be beautiful, became a nightmare. If it were Remus, he probably would've never touched an instrument again; but Sirius was stronger. He never let his mother ruin the one thing he truly loved in this world.

"What's everyone gone so quiet for?" Sirius said eventually, eyeing the rest of them. "Thought you'd be happier. If I'd have gone to that poncy place, you would've had to deal with two new roommates. And you don't just get lucky with a Moony twice."

Yes, Remus thought, I'm happy you turned it down.

What was life without a Sirius Black? He wasn't even sure anymore.

"You're right," James said, "I, for one, am happy you chose to stay, Padfoot. If you'd have gone, I'd have a long life as lawyer to look forward to, just like me dad. All of it—the big house, the happy family, the nice cars. And now look at me—with only a life as a musical degenerate in the cards. Not everyone can say that."

"No they cannot," Sirius grinned.

"What a thing to look forward to," Peter ragged shaking his head. It made Sirius laugh, until he glanced back and began eyeing Remus up again. "What about you, Moons? You've been awful quiet about your own plans—thinking about getting yerself a degree in music then?"

"Nah," Remus said with a small smile, "what do I need that for? I'm already in a band."

"Oh really?"

"Mhm, yeah. S’just a little thing right now, so you might not have heard of us, but I expect that eventually I’ll be too busy playing to thousands for normal, boring things like going to college.”

Sirius’ smile doubled, and he extended a fist for Remus to bump. “Let’s make it hundreds of thousands.”

“Alright.”

Peter surged forward, clapping his hands over their fists. “Hey, I’m in this band too, aren’t I? I don’t actually want to do business, you know.”

“Right you are, Wormtail.” Sirius raised an eyebrow at James. “And you?”

James chuckled. “Fine, but if our first record’s only got your face on the cover, I’ll riot.”

“Perish the thought of hiding your handsome gob from the rest of the world,” Sirius said, pinching James on the cheek. James accepted, only because it meant Sirius was close enough for him to grab his cheeks in retaliation and stretch them out like playdough.

“AUGH—” Sirius clapped his hands to his cheeks before batting him off; “Okay,” he laughed, “tomorrow might kick off exams for everyone else, but I solemnly swear that by the end of this week, everyone’s going to think twice before messing with a Marauder.”



* * *





Careful to save some time for studying so as not to incur the wrath of a certain Oxford-bound ginger-girl, they spread the pranks out on several days. On Monday, while Remus and Peter were sitting in on their first exam, James and Sirius managed to convince some seventh year Salazar kid to get a hold of Barty’s shower bag for them. With it hand, they committed what might’ve been Sirius’ worst nightmare—putting hair removal cream into Barty's shampoo. Remus wasn't even sure where they'd gotten the stuff on such short notice, but unfortunately it didn't matter much. The next morning when Barty appeared in the dining room for breakfast he was still sporting a full head of hair, and they had no choice but to declare the prank a failure.

“Maybe the git just never showers,” Peter offered; “you know, like Snape.”

James and Sirius began to grumble, already plotting their rebound revenge when Barty pulled his jumper over his head and tufts hair shot off him like a dandelion. It took several seconds for anyone to notice, but eventually a clump of chemically-fried hair ended up in Yaxley’s cereal, and the boys finally picked up on something being very not-right. A few confused and panicked moments later, Barty had nearly fainted in the middle of the hall and the Marauders got their first taste of sweet revenge as his friends helped him hobble to the nurse, hair breaking off in big clumps as he frantically ran his fingers through it.

On Wednesday, while the year eleven boys were in gym, Remus, James, and Peter snuck into the change rooms and picked the locks on Yaxley and Traver’s lockers. Inspired by the girls’ prank on Sirius’ birthday, they took everything but their shoes and left behind bed sheets they’d painted to read “Godric Pride”. Watching the two boys scuttle back to their dorms in red togas was certainly the highlight of their day.

Thursday they all found themselves busy with exams, but unlike the term before when all he’d had was Sirius-on-the-brain, Remus finished his day feeling rather victorious. So far he felt good about all of his exams, but whenever he asked Sirius how he thought he did, Sirius would give only sly or vague answers. It was enough for now, but Remus was just itching to get his fingers on their final marks.

“So what we doing tomorrow?” James asked, shouldering his bag as they all made their way back to their dorm from the Great Hall. “We could plant some weed in their room and tip off their dorm monitor?”

“I was thinking something else actually,” Sirius said. “Something more... sweet. After all, tomorrow’s Reg’s birthday.”

“Really?” Remus asked.

“Yeah. So maybe the little sod deserves a treat. Prongs, that tin of sweets from your mum still under your bed?”

“Should be. I haven’t touched it.”

They all looked to Peter, who pulled a face.

“Oh, fuck you guys. I didn’t touch it either, James can keep his lava chocolate.”

“Good,” Sirius smirked. “Hope the boys are feeling hungry.”

Waking up early the next morning, they got themselves sorted and left the tin on Regulus’ regular table, lying in wait across the room as the four Salazar boys filed into the hall. While his roommates opened the tin, Regulus paused to pick up the card they’d planted, reading it over before scanning the room with a suspicious look. Immediately they all turned away, innocently picking at their breakfast.

“What’d you end up writing on the card?” James asked quietly, nudging Sirius with his elbow.

“ ‘To Regulus, my jewel-eyed prince. Happy Birthday, love from your secret admirer. Kisses. Hugs. Have my babies'—you name it.”

“Cruel bastard.”

“Look, they’re eating them!” Peter said, and Remus turned around on his bench to watch as Barty—now sporting a severely short number 2 buzz-cut—Yaxley, and Travers began stuffing their faces. Regulus remained more sceptical, and got up from the table without so much as a taste, leaving them be.

“That little git, is he really not gonna eat it?” Sirius hissed.

"Maybe he hates chocolate?" Peter suggested.

"Nobody hates chocolate," Remus scoffed.

“Looks like he’s getting himself a cuppa,” James said. He was right too, and by the time Regulus returned to his table with his tea the other three boys were red in the face and rasping for breath. Half-screaming, Barty flew from his chair and downed a neighbouring girl’s glass of milk, but it wasn’t enough apparently, and he scrambled to find another while Yaxley and Travers made a beeline for the drink table, disrupting the line up of students and throwing themselves under the beverage dispensers to guzzle directly from the spigots. A horrified lunch lady came out from behind her counter to scream at them, but Regulus remained unperturbed, sitting quietly at his table and flipping through a textbook.

“That’s it!” Sirius snarled, standing up and marching across the room. Exchanging worried looks, James, Peter, and Remus quickly followed, stopping next to Sirius while Regulus casually sipped his tea.

“Come to wish me a happy birthday, ‘secret admirer’?” Regulus asked calmly.

“You knew it was us,” Sirius said.

“Of course I knew it was you. You’ve been pranking them all week.”

“And today was supposed to be your turn."

Regulus' mouth curved upwards haughtily. “Too bad your thinly-veiled gag was about as clever as a monkey holding a dull hammer.”

Sirius fumed; “You cheeky little git! You didn’t even tell your mates it was us, you just let them stuff their faces without saying a thing!”

“They’re the ones who fell for it,” Regulus shrugged; “Let them figure it out.”

“I think they did,” Peter mumbled, watching as Yaxley and Travers scraped their tongues with napkins on the other side of the hall, moaning and crying while other kids laughed.

Furiously, Sirius slammed his hands down on the table; “Don’t you have any sense of loyalty—any at all?”

"As if you know anything about loyalty."

"More than you. What kind of bastard lets his friends take a fall for him and isn't even sorry for it?"

Unmoved, Regulus just flipped a page in his text. “If you’re done, I have an exam to study for. Not that you would know what that's like either.”

Like a steaming bull, Sirius scoffed, but did not lash out. Instead he turned away and stormed back to their table, cursing his brother under his breath. Peter followed, but James stayed a moment longer, smiling genuinely.

“If it’s any consolation, happy birthday, Reg.”

Glaring, but admittedly more pink-cheeked than before, Regulus said to them, “It’s not.”

James waved awkwardly. “Er—cool… See you... around then…”

“That was really lame,” Remus whispered as they crossed back the way they'd come.

“Shut up.”

“Change of plans,” Sirius announced as they sat, “plant the weed. Throw a stink bomb into his gym bag. Leave a jar of bees in their bathroom. We can switch their water bottles out for pickle juice, and cut the hot water line and steal their towels and—" Sirius suddenly lit up. "Yeah that's it, let’s just steal everything!”

“And do what with it?” Peter demanded, looking quite uneasy at the daunting list.

Sirius smirked. “I hear the Dubh’s pretty nice this time of year. Reg’s always hated anything to do with water. He’d probably avoid bathing if he weren't such a priss. Maybe we should help him out—give him a reason to go for a little dip.”

Remus wasn’t really a fan of Lake Dubh either, but stealing stuff from their room seemed a lot more preferable than the charge of manslaughter that Sirius was bridging on. The prank also proved to involve very little water acrobatics on his part, with the hardest bit being breaking into their dorm and sneaking everything out without getting caught. They waited until later that evening while everyone was off eating dinner, and then strode right in the front doors.

"Shouldn't we trying to be more inconspicuous?" Peter winced, after they'd passed several boys on the stairway.

"Nah," Sirius said, "I want them to know it was us."

No one seemed too inclined to argue.

They followed each other up to the third floor, where Remus got to work on the lock with the others practically breathing down his neck. When the door finally gave way, they all slipped inside and found themselves in an incredibly average dorm room. A stray sock here, an empty tea mug there, three messy beds and one neat.

“I’ll give you one guess which bed belongs to my control-freak brother,” Sirius blagged, purposely snatching up Regulus' pillow and throwing it across the room.

"Okay, but I gotta be honest, I was sorta expecting something more... horrible?" James said. "Like, I dunno, maybe a few dead cats or a dartboard with our faces pinned to it."

"No, that'd be far too clever," Remus answered.

They got to work next, moving about the room and gathering up whatever they could find that would inconvenience the boys the most; a left shoe, the bathroom light bulb, the window curtains, every third issue in Yaxley’s comic book collection. Eventually Remus uncovered a nasty-looking switchblade from Traver’s side table, and James also lifted the small jar of poorly-rolled spliffs he'd discovered in the back of the bathroom cupboard, but the real treasure was actually the worn teddy bear Peter had found hidden in between the wall and headboard of Barty Crouch's bed.

“What do you reckon his name is?” Peter asked, dangling the bear by one arm. “Mr. Cuddles? Sgt. Squishy?”

“No way, it’s definitely something distinguished like ‘Mr. Weatherby’ or ‘Sir Rutherford’,” James snickered.

“Eh, my money’s on ‘Teddy’,” Remus finished, taking the bear and shoving it into one of the pillow cases they were using as bags.

“What’s your bet, Padfoot? You're the best with names, after all,” James called, turning around just in time to see Sirius ducking his head under Regulus’ bed. “Ooh, I wouldn’t try that if I were you, mate. I only found dirty magazines under Yaxley’s and half the pages were stuck together.”

“Maybe he was just playing target practice,” Remus offered snidely.

“Nasty,” Peter laughed, but Sirius remained quiet, until finally he withdrew, bringing with him a small black case, which he flipped open to reveal Regulus' prized violin.

“Yes! Found it!”

“I'm not sure leaving an instrument like that to float in the middle of the lake is such a good idea,” James winced, but Sirius just got to his feet, grinning victoriously.

“That little git values nothing more than this bloody squeak-box. If you want to get a reaction out of him, this is the way to do it. The dickheads should be grateful we’re not flooding their room like they did ours.”

James reached up to rub the back of his neck. “Whatever you say.”

“Hurry up then, we’ve stayed long enough as it is,” Remus said, grabbing a full pillow case and heading toward the door.

It took some time and even more whining and whinging, but together they managed to lug everything down to the lake side, where they tossed it into the nearest canoe and pushed the entire thing out into the middle of the Dubh. It floated nicely, barely even weighed down by the stolen goods, but despite being successful, none of them were jumping for joy.

“Feels a bit anticlimactic,” James observed.

“Well 'course, they're not here yet,” Sirius said proudly, crossing his arms over his chest. "But don't worry, I left a map."

“A map?”

“Yeah, got the idea from Moony, actually.” Sirius glanced in Remus’ direction. “After his map of hiding spots.”

“Copycat,” Remus said, digging the toes of his boots into the rocky shore.

"Anyone for a celebratory spliff? It's on Barty," James said, holding up the jar of joints from the bathroom.

They all appeared eager to partake, but when it began clear that James wasn't going to be able to get the lid off of the jar, Remus took it and threw it against the rocks, instantly satisfied when it shattered to pieces.

"That's our delinquent," James cheesed, as he and Peter went to work picking the crappy rolls out of the glass and rocks. Picking out one of his own, Remus checked it over for any shards before setting it to his lips and lighting it. He'd just gotten his first decent drag when he turned around to find Sirius a few feet away, staring out over the lake at the canoe, which was drifting quietly along on its own.

Careful not to slip on the shifting stones, Remus strode up to his side and took another short puff before offering it. "Wanna try?"

"Cheers," Sirius said, taking the spliff with two fingers and examining it. "Wow, this is shit. Doesn't even have a filter. Maybe you offer to teach Barty how to roll a decent joint, Moons."

"Maybe he'd hate me less then," Remus chuckled, before glancing at the canoe, now at least a hundred yards away. "You satisfied now?"

With the joint between his lips, Sirius breathed in deeply and exhaled smoke through his nose. "I will be. Once I know we've really gotten them. What about you? You're the one they came after."

"It's whatever," Remus dismissed, squinting over his shoulder at James and Peter to avoid meeting Sirius' eyes. "I was angry, but Barty's just an idiot. What's he really gonna do to me in the grand scheme of things."

"You let them off too easy," Sirius sighed. "Sometimes a little revenge is needed."

"Maybe... but don't that mean that Barty wins again? If all I do is worry about getting him back, when will have time to make myself feel better?"

"Getting him back is how you make yourself feel better," Sirius said, gesturing at the canoe with the joint.

"You don't really believe that," Remus said.

Sirius shrugged. "Sure I do." He took another drag and went to pass the joint back, but Remus got caught staring at his fingers. How was it that everything somebody did became beautiful when you realised what they meant to you?

"Moony?" Sirius waved the joint. "Want some more?"

"No," Remus said. "Don't want to green out before we see the end of this prank of yours." And I'd rather not touch you right now.

"Suit yourself." Sirius raised the weed to his mouth again.

"GUYS!" James called suddenly. Both Sirius and Remus turned just in time to spot Regulus, Barty, Yaxley, and Travers crest the top of the shore. All of them were breathing heavily, no doubt from running all the way from their dorm, but they all managed to appear livid as well. Regulus was at the helm, looking more alarmed than Remus had ever seen him.

Instantly giddy, Sirius flicked the joint away and clapped his hands together. “Hey lads! You found our note then?”

“You!” Yaxley shouted. “Our—our stuff!”

“I knew something was up when you were all mysteriously missing from dinner!” Barty snarled.

Peter began a clap, smug and slow, and James gave a snide whistle while Sirius only laughed; “I’m impressed boys, you’re a lot quicker on the uptake than we would'a thought.”

“What did you do with it?” Regulus barked, a vision of rage.

“Oh, you mean—” Mockingly, Sirius played a quick air-violin 'wah-wah' before clicking his tongue and pointing behind him at the lake. "Happy birthday, bro."

Realisation dawned on Regulus’ face, and he turned sheet-white and began skidding down the rocks to the very edge of the shore. With his shoes just barely grazing the water, he stared out over the Dubh as though his entire life was crumbling before him.

“You actually put our stuff in the lake?!” Travers bellowed.

“It’s safe in a canoe,” Peter promised; “You just gotta go get it.”

“Yeah, go on, Reg, it’s just a little swim,” Sirius said smugly.

"YOU BASTARDS!" Barty howled. "We'll get you for this! You better start sleeping with one eye open, all of you!"

"Big words from someone who looks like a chewed toothbrush," Sirius keened. "If you're so desperate for a proper row though, you could always try going a round or two with Lupin! Though, I'm not sure how eager I'd be if I had a bruise like that."

Barty hesitated, before wiping his hand across the dark bruise that had flowered along the top of his cheek. Perhaps the smartest decision he'd ever made, he did not take a running charge at Remus. Instead he surprised them all by showing actual control as he called out to his friend; "C'mon, Reg. We'll get it later."

Still utterly quiet, Barty's call was enough to prompt Regulus to turn back around and face his brother. His hands squeezed were at his sides, fingers tapping together as though he were timing something or counting down.

"What?" Sirius drawled at him. "You wanna fight then? Alright, I'll entertain it. Go ahead, have a go. Come at me!"

But Regulus did not fight. Instead he remained stoic, glaring with such venom that Remus could've believed that he might've had a real chance of winning said fight, should he actually attempt to rush one of them. Remus could tell it was making Sirius antsy; he wanted a reaction, something that told him without a doubt that he'd won.

"Got nothing to say then?" He demanded. "Mummy's favourite boy lost his favourite toy and he just stands there—really?"

The goading did nothing. Regulus gave him nothing.

"Man, what a disappointment this is," Sirius scoffed. "You must have no feelings at all. Like an empty doll."

"Shut up!" Barty hissed.

"Oh! Look at that, your mate's defending you, Reg! Too bad you wouldn't do the same for him!"

Regulus gave the barest breath of a scoff, before finally turning away and marching off, back up the embankment. He did not stop and wait for his friends, but kept going back the way he’d come, leaving his roommates to stare after him.

"Where you going?" Sirius cried. "Violin's this way!"

"Sirius," James said, coming in close. "C'mon, man, it's done."

"Bloody coward," Sirius swore, ignoring him as he threw a dismissive hand at Barty and the rest. "Well? You gonna just stand there or you gonna follow him? Bloody sheep!"

“Fuck you!” Barty snarled, flashing them a double-bird as the other three boys turned and following Regulus off.

"Mission accomplished?" Peter said slowly, obviously relieved when James turned and high-fived him.

"Yeah, we did it," he said, smiling and nudging Sirius pointedly. "Don't gimmie that face Black, the prank was successful."

Sirius did not reciprocate the gesture. “The little buggar didn’t even try,” he said. “He just stood there—didn’t even get his socks wet.”

Peter reached over and gave Sirius’ shoulder a pat. “But their stuff’s still in the middle of the lake. We did it!”

“Yeah, sure… we did it,” Sirius said, obviously unsatisfied.

“So… how should we celebrate?” Remus asked, watching Sirius closely. “Maybe we hold a band practice?”

“That’s a great idea, Moony!” James agreed. “Between exams and pranking we haven't had any time, and I’ve got the tournament next week. So what do you think, Padfoot? A nice evening of noise to lighten your unappreciative mood?”

Sirius blinked himself out of his daze. “Sounds great,” he answered, and James gave a firm nod, gathering Sirius in by the shoulder and starting up the shore with him.

“C’mon, Moony, Wormtail—we’re gonna finish this night off right!”

“Hell yeah!” Peter called, chasing after them. Remus followed, because what else was there to do, yet he couldn’t shake the knowledge that Sirius obviously hadn’t gotten what he wanted.

Ignoring the stilted atmosphere, James managed to wait until they’d made it back to House Lane before clapping Sirius on the shoulder. “Oh, that’s right! Forgot to mention it before, but you’re not gonna believe it. Yesterday, while you and Moony were taking your English exam? Yeah well, Pete and I were just waiting around for you and we sorta got to messing and guess what—we wrote something!”

“Like a song?” Remus asked, surprised.

“Yeah!”

“He means he composed it. I wrote it down,” Peter said to Remus as they walked. “You should’ve heard him—‘and then it could go, da-nah-nah-nah, da-dum-duh-nah-nah!’ It was almost painful."

James scoffed; "I still don’t understand why I would need to know the difference between a 'breve' and a 'quiver' when I have you three.”

“It’s a quaver. Not quiver."

“Yeah, well, tomayto-tomahto, pina colada, and the other bit.”

Remus couldn’t help his smile. "What colour is this new song of yours?"



"It's a giant mash, but it's got this real soft melody that's mostly blue. Padfoot's favourite colour, even!"

"Yeah sure," Sirius said, obviously not paying attention.

"You told me your favourite colour was brown," Remus said. Sirius looked at him very sharply, and he nearly baulked.

"Brown?" James grimaced next to them. "Like what kind of brown?"

Sirius' eyes dipped, as though he were trying to scan Remus from head to toe. Finally they came to rest on his face again, looking him right in the eye.

"A very specific kind..."





* * *





Sunday 5th June 1977

Remus could hardly believe it. It was end of term, marks were finally out and after he'd managed to get his hands on his end of term report, he practically raced back to his dorm. There was little audience to be had, what with James off at final football practice ahead of her year-end tournament and Peter visiting with Moira for her birthday, for which he'd prepared a lovely portrait of her as a gift. But none of that mattered; all Remus had needed was Sirius.

Sirius and his final report, that was.

As he sat in the middle of their dorm room, scanning their reports from top to bottom, he found himself practically vibrating out of happiness. He’d really only been aiming for one, but there it was, printed in solid black and plain as day.

“Three?” He echoed. “I beat you in three classes?”

Sirius shrugged, acting startlingly fine. “It would seem so, my good Moons.”

Remus lowered the reports. “Oh my god—three!”

“Congratulations.” Smiling, Sirius held out his hand. “You’re either a certifiable genius, or a slave to your textbooks.”

“It’s called hard work, Black. You should try it sometime,” Remus gloated, before taking his hand and shaking it firmly. "Thanks."

“You did good," he told him again. "And as luck would have it, I've already prepared the perfect reward for you.”

Remus felt his heart jump. “And what’s that?”

Taking a second to tuck the cigarette he’d been fiddling with behind his ear, Sirius plucked his marks from Remus’ hands and began folding them up into a paper airplane. “You get to play the part of the most crucial piece in our final pièce de résistance. And all you have to do to succeed is distract my dear little brother for a few measly minutes.”

Remus sighed. “You mean you actually want to do that?"

“Of course.”

"I thought we were over this. It's almost end of school, why bother?"

"Because it's the end of school!" Sirius cried. "We can't just leave without pulling the greatest prank this school's ever seen!"

"We didn't pull one last year?!"

"We were busy last year. We found the Shrieking Shack and then fancied ourselves a killer concert—but since there's nothing halfway decent going on right now..." Letting the paper plane fly, Sirius watched as it soared across the room toward his bed, and by an inexplicable chance, flew straight out the open window. “Aw man, did you see that?” He cried in delight, rushing the window and sticking his head out.

Remus didn’t bother to join him, thinking back to the way Sirius had returned to their dorm after the lake and declared that Regulus’ stoic reaction to the prank still wasn’t enough. To appease him, they’d come up with the same sort of stunt they’d pulled on Snape the year before—only this time the plan was to rig a bucket of water above the stairs of Salazar House and soak Regulus on his way out. It was Peter’s idea to dye the water Godric red with food colouring, which Sirius had loved, naturally. But they hadn’t talked about the prank since that night, and as a result Remus had stupidly let himself believe that Sirius was over it.

“Wouldn’t you be the best one to distract Reg?” He asked, as Sirius leaned back from the window.

“Nah, he’ll never give me the time of day, but you—you’re more neutral.”

“So you want me to be the one to lure him under the bucket?”

“Yup. And that’s not all.” Smirking, Sirius turned toward the bathroom, disappearing inside and reappearing a few moments later with a large mop bucket in his hands. “ We may have made a few upgrades to the plan. Ta-da!”

Remus looked into the bucket, but instead of water like they’d agreed upon, he found the same syrupy blood they’d used back on Halloween. It'd been innocent enough then, since the only people they'd chosen to soak in it were each other, but pouring a bucket of fake blood on someone who wasn't expecting it...

“You gave me the idea actually,” Sirius grinned, “or should I say, our dear friend Stephen King did. 'Carrie' was full of prime pranking ideas.”

“You can’t be serious..." Remus snapped his head up; “You can’t dump fake blood on your little brother—this isn’t a horror novel!”

Staring at him like he’d been slapped, Sirius stepped back and set the bucket down. “Oh c’mon, don't be such a wuss. It’s just a step up from the food colouring. I thought you would’ve loved it.”

“This is definitely more than a step up! We agreed on water! The was that he would get wet, not scarred for life!”

“Yeah—was! And then we decided that hosing the tosser down wasn’t enough!”

“We?”

“Yes, we! James and Pete agreed—this is funnier. Imagine the reaction.”

“It’s not funny,” Remus told him sternly; “Did you even read the book?”

Sirius rolled his eyes. “As if my brother had suddenly gained the supernatural ability to snap all our necks with a flick of his wrist. Just think of it, Moony—this’ll be legendary!”

“This is mean.”

“No, mean was telling everyone your mum killed herself and that you’re next.”

“Barty did that.”

“And Reg just sat back and let him. Didn't say a single word. Know who does that? Cowards.”

Remus couldn’t believe his ears. “You’re taking this too far, Sirius. You’re becoming obsessed with hurting them even worse than they hurt you.”

“They hurt you, Moony!"

"And I told you, I'm over it! Barty couldn't make me feel any worse than I make myself feel! Soon it won't even matter anyway, it'll be summer and we'll be all be going away. Barty can't touch us then."

"You mean you'll be away. I'll be going there."

Oh... damn it.

"Sirius... if this is about all of us going home... then maybe—"

"It's not!" Sirius snapped. "It’s about the pranks—the fun! Watching ‘em squirm! We do something big at the end of year so we’re remembered the next—that's how it works! And you’re either in or out.”

Remus’ blood ran cold. “In or out, huh? That easy?”

“It can be. That depends on you.”

“You don’t mean that.”

“Stop telling me what I do and don't mean. You're not my fucking conscience. You're supposed to be my friend.”

"I am your friend!"

"You're not acting like it! You're supposed to be on my side, not theirs."

Remus bit down hard on his bottom lip. “I am on your side, Sirius, but why does it have to be this?”

“You just don’t get it.”

“Then explain it to me!”

“I can’t!”

“Why not? Since when can we not talk to one another?”

Pausing, a nerve jumped in Sirius’ jaw as he ground his teeth together. “Look, I know you’re still new here and all—”

“Fuck you, Black,” Remus snarled.

“Fine, you don’t get it then. You want out, that it?”

“No, but—”

“Brilliant, then we finish this tomorrow and the little brat learns his lesson.”

“Which is what, Sirius?”

“That not picking a side makes you just as guilty as the rest of ‘em!”

“Why can’t he learn that lesson with water?!”

Sirius stepped back, shaking his head, but Remus wasn’t finished. He reached out, grabbing his friend by the shoulders and forcing him to look at him. “Sirius, please. I’ll help you and it’ll be enough, I promise.”

“Why aren’t you angrier?” Sirius asked, eyes cold and grey.

“I’m always angry,” Remus confessed, “but that’s not anyone else’s problem but mine.”

“That can’t be true. You deserve someone to blame.” His words felt like a confession.

“I know you’re angry too, but... things won’t be like this forever.”

“How do you know?” Sirius spat. “They’ve stayed the same for the last seventeen years, why would tomorrow be any different?”

Now Remus knew it was a confession.

“Because," he told him, "we get to choose what tomorrow means. Not anyone else.”

Sirius turned his head, looking at Remus’ hands as they clutched his shoulder. For a split second Remus thought he might pull away and that would be the end, but thankfully, all he did was sigh, deep and heavy, and close his eyes.

“Alright. Fine Moony, we’ll do it your way.”

Remus slumped in relief, and squeezed tighter. “Okay... Thank you, Sirius.”

“Don’t thank me, idiot,” Sirius scoffed, rolling his shoulders and pulling away. Remus instantly cracked a smirk.

“Oh, I’m the idiot? You forget I’ve seen your marks—they’re abysmal. You might be losing your touch, Black.”

It was the spark they needed to bring them back. At his words, Sirius’ eyes flashed devilishly. “You sure about that, Lupin? That I'm losing my touch? Mm, no... I’m pretty sure I know at least a few ways to convince you otherwise.”

For a split second Remus forgot how to breathe. A muscle jumped in his neck and he forced a laugh before clearing his throat and picking up the bucket of fake blood, glancing down at his murky reflection. “I’ll… get—get rid of this then...”

Saying nothing, Sirius turned away. He crossed the room to his bed, plucking the cigarette from behind his ear and pulling his zippo from his pocket.

Remus couldn’t help it; he called after him.

“Sirius?”

Sirius turned around instantly. “Yeah?”

“You… You said it yourself, right? It’s about fun?”

Usually Remus was able to discern what people were thinking by their expressions, but the look that Sirius gave him next was both vague and all too open. Licking his lips first, Sirius set the cigarette between his teeth and clicked his lighter to life, breathing in deeply and then out, filling the air in front of his faze with a soft haze.

“Yeah, Moony. Fun...”



Chapter End Notes
