Chapter 63: Memory


Chapter Summary

The bucket tips.



Chapter Notes

CW: Swearing, mentions of child abuse. Sad times, but happier endings!

(also lmk if you spot any glaring mistakes. I'm posting this while sleep-deprived xx)



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Oh no, not me,

I never lost control;

You’re face to face,

With the man who sold the world…

- “The Man Who Sold the World” David Bowie, 1971



He probably should've been angrier with Sirius. Much angrier. It should've been easy—Remus was an angry person after all. For the last several years of his life, his anger had left him feeling as though he were on an ever-revolving merry-go-round with no way to get off. Every now and then he would fool himself into thinking that he had escaped it—that the memories had finally stopped chasing and hounding his sleep—but then he'd go home again, or get a letter, or someone would say things like his mother had killed herself, and the entire thing would start up again; round and round.

Out of all of it, the one thing Remus could never allow himself to be, was angry with his friends. It just didn't come naturally. He was annoyed by them often, sometimes livid even, but anger... true anger... now that was something reserved for people far worse than friends.

It was probably the reason why he'd believed Sirius would never not be true to his word. Stupid. Sirius was just as angry as he was, he simply... showed it in different ways. Remus had used to believe that James and Sirius were two different sides of the same coin, but even as close as they were, all it would've taken was the slightest bit of foresight to realise how wrong he'd been. There was no room on a coin like that for someone as good as James.

"Shall we flip a coin, eh Moony?" Sirius had suggested once. "Heads you, tails me."

It was over something stupid, like who got the last fag in the box, but as the ten pence glittered through the air in slow motion, Remus found himself praying that it would turn up heads. He'd still share the fag of course, but it would be his and that would be more than enough reason to gloat.

Heads. Heads. Let it be me. Me. Me. Me. Me. Me.

He'd felt the same way as he watched their final prank unfold—after agreeing to play the key piece in the plan, granting him a front-row seat to Sirius' revenge. Just... me. Me. Me. Me. Let it be me. Look at me—watch me! But then reality finally dawned.

Sirius wasn't looking at him at all. He couldn't. There wasn't the space for him. Sirius was lost in his own memories—busy with a never-ending merry-go-round of his own. He had no time to think of Remus, or anyone else for that matter. In Sirius' mind it was the exact same. Me. Me. Me. Please, let it be me.

And really... who could hardly blame him for that?





* * *





“Sirius, I still don’t understand what I’m supposed to say to him!”

“Anything! Tell him you want violin lessons."

Remus gaped at him; “Violin lessons? Are you insane?!”

“You could always challenge him to a duel instead.”

“Could you try not being an utter dickhead for two seconds?!”

“Just say you wanna talk,” James supplied, looking quite giddy—a far cry from how nervous he’d been after they’d hauled themselves out of bed early to set everything up. James had always been an early-bird, but between football and pranking, he looked about ready to pass out on his feet most days.

“And then what?” Remus demanded. "Shall I suggest knitting to pass the time?"

“If you really want,” Sirius shrugged. "But c'mon, Moons, you’re smart—get creative with him. Just make sure he's on target before the first bell goes. And don’t worry, we’ll give ya a little whistle right before so you have time to get out of the way.”

Remus glowered. Lure Regulus away from his friends and breakfast with little-to-no bait—no small feat then.

“We’ll be around the side of the building with Pete,” James said, checking his watch. “It’s on you now, Moony. You got five minutes.”

While Sirius raised an enthusiastic thumbs-up, James gave Remus' shoulder a final comforting squeeze and then the both of them slipped out the dining hall's backdoors. Remus tried not to immediately throw in the towel, but his confidence was weaning. It was easy for the rest of them to be optimistic—they'd given themselves the easy job. They'd left him with the task of remaining inconspicuous and yet intriguing enough to guide Regulus into the very heart of their prank, which knowing the eternal stubbornness of the Blacks, was certainly easier said than done. Remus was starting to think that it was just as much a punishment for him as it was Regulus.

But ah well, not much else to do but get to work then.

As he made his way across the dining hall, he noticed the girls waving at him from their usual table, but instead of going to meet them, Remus rubbed his clammy palms against his trousers and strode straight toward Regulus with a stern expression. He gave the boys no time to be surprised by his presence, shutting down their breakfast conversation with a severe; “I need to talk to you.”

Looking unnervingly unsurprised to see him, Regulus looked up with a dismissive glare. “I really hope this ‘I need to talk’ business doesn’t become a habit of yours. Because I. Don’t. Care.”

Remus swallowed. “You—You might if you heard what I had to say.”

“Oh Reg, you’re really so popular,” Barty started, “even dogs chase you now.”

Remus had been expecting this. Intervention from friends was Sirius' reason #2 factor in letting the prank fail (the first being the stick Regulus had stuffed a mile up his arse—fuddy-duddy) which meant it was important to get them to fuck off.

“Hey Bart, didn’t see you there," he sneered; "How’s the teddy bear? Not too waterlogged I hope?”

Barty scowled, but Remus looked past him, bending down toward Regulus slightly. “I need to talk to you,” he said again; “it’s about…erm... Sirius.”

Regulus made a frustrated face, like he wanted to tell him to stuff it and fuck off, but finally, after much teeth-grinding, he pushed back from the table and stood.

“Reg!” Barty called; “What are you doing? Don't listen to this wanker—he's mental!”

“I’ll be right back,” Regulus said. “Just wait here.”

Yes, success! It'd been easier than he thought even. Perhaps he was cut out for this. Insides positively buzzing, Remus led Regulus from the dining room and into the hall. He kept walking, his pace perhaps a little too quick in his desperation to make it outside, and finally Regulus snapped at him.

“Where are you going, Lupin? I thought you wanted to talk!”

“Uhm... Too many people—this way!”

He heard Regulus give a huff, but he was still following so the plan hadn’t failed yet. Though that didn't mean the universe was letting him off that easy.

Almost to the front doors, Remus rounded a corner and nearly ran head-long into somebody, only to realise at the last second that it was his biology partner, Jillian. As he fell back, she gave gave a little squeak of surprise which quickly became a beaming grin, showing off her braces and a deep pair of dimples.

“Oh—! It's just you, Remus. Hello!"

"Er... hey Jill. Sorry for almost running into you. Was in a bit a bit of a hurry."

"That's alright." She peeked past him. "You and your friend on your way somewhere then?"

"Yeah, actually we—"

"We're not friends," Regulus cut-in.

Jillian smiled awkwardly. "Oh, well I was just looking for you actually, Remus. Are you all ready for our final presentation today? The wonders of cell mitosis, right?”

“Yeah, totally!” Remus scrambled. "It's just, right now I'm a bit—"

“Oh, good! I was thinking we could go over our parts at breakfast together, that is if you're not too busy...?" Jillian’s gaze turned to Regulus again, who was standing a few feet behind them, arms crossed and glaring like the devil.

"Lupin, are we talking or are you going on your date?" He snapped impatiently.

Remus' heart gave a little start; "Ah—no! We're definitely not—"

"Date," Jillian giggled, biting her lip as she tucked her hair behind her ear; "Remus and I aren't—heh!—dating."

Simultaneously tired of being talked over and also worried about the prank, Remus cleared his throat and Jillian's attention whipped back to him. “Sorry, Jill, I got something going on right now. Maybe we could chat about the presentation during next break?”

“Oh yeah, sure. Biology isn't until last period anyway. Shall I meet you ‘the spot’ then?”

Remus hated how she’d dubbed the back row of the biology room ‘the spot’, but she’d already winked clumsily at him and judging by Regulus’ expression, he had about four seconds to get moving again.

“Sure, see you.”

Slipping around her, Remus looked back only to make sure Regulus was with him before finally emerging out onto the front steps of the dining hall. He glanced around, but found no sight of his friends, only the plastic bucket looming several feet over their heads. There'd been no way to disguise it, but Sirius hadn't wanted to just wait for Regulus to come walking out on his own and risk missing him—therefore: Remus, distraction-extraordinaire.

“Okay, spit it out. And this better not be another stupid prank,” Regulus snapped.

Remus couldn't help it; he laughed.

"What's so damn funny?"

Quickly he clapped a hand over his mouth. "Nothing! Just... thanks for agreeing to meet with me."

"I'm not meeting with you," Regulus scowled, "you're interrupting my breakfast. Now spit it out before you actually start acting like the lunatic everyone says you are."

It was hard not to rise to the bait and react, but doing so would just ruin the prank. Regulus had stopped just in front of the doors, several feet off-target, and with no time or patience left to scramble for something to say, Remus took Sirius’ advice and rattled off the first thing that came to mind;

“Er—the violin!”

Regulus pulled back, nearly affronted. “Pardon me?”

“You play the violin!”

“Are you trying to be funny or are you actually this stupid?”

Remus gave a nervous laugh. “Ha—funny. No, I only meant that you play the violin well. And so I… thought that maybe you could… teach me?”

“You brought me out here to ask me that?”

“I guess so…?”

Regulus turned back to the door.

“Wait!” Remus cried. “You’re right, I was just playing—I really do have to talk to you though.”

“I’ve already entertained enough rubbish to do with my brother,” Regulus spat scathingly. A pair of students passed them, walking into the hall all while quizzically murmuring to each other and pointing up at the sky. Regulus stepped aside for them and went to look up, but before he could spot the bucket, Remus threw his hands up.

“But you still followed me!” He half-shouted. The freakish gesture at least got Regulus’ attention again. He straightened up to his full height, which was not much shorter than Sirius’ these days, and drew back from the door, crossing his arms. Remus watched him, keenly aware of the few feet between him and the chalk 'x' marker Peter had left on the ground.

“I’m not going to help you,” Regulus said. “Sirius has made his own bed. Even if he doesn’t know it yet.”

The vague statement caught Remus by surprise. “What are you talking about?”

“Well, I assume he’s figured it out and told you, but it was only a matter of time before she did it anyway.”

“Do what? You mean your mum?”

“Who else?”

“I don’t… What do you—”

Regulus took a step forward, almost menacing. “I told him to stop pushing her, that it was just gonna make things worse, but he never listens. Did he even tell you about Easter?"

"Only that you had a row," Remus shot. "How hard could it be to get along as brothers for one week?"

"We didn't have the row," Regulus hissed. "All he was supposed to do was give one stupid concert, and he couldn't even do that!"

Concert?

"It's just a bloody piano!"

Piano?

"He could've refused—ran off somewhere and avoided the entire thing, but no—what does he do? He smashes an entire bottle of vodka on it and lights the whole thing on fire in the middle of the bloody ballroom! Our entire family was there! Plus half of the British parliament and a member from every affluent family from here to Australia—and he burns an eighteenth century heirloom right in front of them! What did you idiots think she would do?!"

For a moment Remus was without words. Regulus' explosion had surprised him, not because Sirius had done, but because he'd neglected to mention it at all. Remus was pretty sure arson was on Sirius' bucket list for Christ's sake. And his mother... What was Regulus even saying?

"You're saying he did this, because they... tried to force him to play?"

Regulus puckered. "One song wouldn't have killed him. But he always has to make a scene. It’s impossible for him to keep his head down, and he’s not the only one who pays for it.”

It was as though a boxing bell had gone off inside Remus' mind. Regulus’ words had driven a spark down his throat, and instantly his hackles were up, gearing for a fight.

“ ‘Not the only one’?” He snarled. “You’re always on him for fighting back but I’ve seen his scars, you little coward! The ones he got when you were in the way—when he was defending you!”

A horrified look came over Regulus, and he faltered immediately, gritting his teeth as though he too were feeling the leftover burn of Sirius’ injury. “He’s not the only one who doesn’t always want to go home,” Regulus ground out, “but if he just shut up for a little while longer, then maybe things would be fine!”

"I—" Remus drew up short. It was at that moment that he began to realise just how similar the two Black brothers were. Both of them had put up a wall, but where Sirius’ was sarcastic and aloof, Regulus’ was withdrawn and stoic. They were both dealing with their pain the only way they knew how. For as long as Remus had known him, Sirius had been counting down the seconds until the day he’d be free from his family, and maybe Regulus was doing the same.

“I don’t think you want to hate your brother,” Remus said quietly. He shot a quick glance around the corner, where the lads would be waiting. Can you hear this, Sirius?

"I do hate him," Regulus said bitterly.

“No... No, you don't. In fact, I don’t think any piece of you hates him, not really.”

“You don’t know anything about me."

“You're right," Remus agreed. "I don't know you at all, Regulus. I have no idea what it's like being you. I can tell you don't like that place though—home. Neither does Sirius. And that's just one thing in common, but I'll bet there are more. You are brothers, and if you just agreed to talk to one another, then I think you could be on the same side.”

“And what side is that?" Regulus sneered. "You don’t exactly look like winners to me.”

Remus almost laughed. “That might be true, and I may not have any brothers, but I can tell you one thing—being on a side with friends feels a whole lot better than one without.”

Regulus looked down at the ground. It felt dismissive at first, but the longer Remus watched him, the softer his expression became.

“You should talk to Sirius, Reg," Remus pleaded. "This back and forth doesn’t have to go on forever. It can end.”

“He won’t talk to me," Regulus said in a small voice.

“Then we’ll make him talk. We could find some common ground and get it all out in the open. It’ll feel better, I promise. And hey, if he doesn’t want to listen, then we can tie him to a tree—and if he tries to talk over us, we can muzzle him. We have options.”

A smile flickered across Regulus’ face. It was so quick Remus almost thought he’d imagined it. “Stupid,” he murmured, “ 'common ground', what pish…”

"Better than a battle ground."

Absent-mindedly, Regulus began dragging the toe of his shoe ahead of him, blurring the chalked 'x' on the ground until it was little more than a smudge. Remus stared at it, and suddenly the reality of their situation came back to him.

Oh no.

Then, with all the terror of an air-raid siren, a single whistle cut through the air.

No... No, no, no, no, no, no—no!

Regulus glanced up; “Okay, Lupin, where’s my brother?”

Remus surged forward. “REGULUS, WATCH OUT!”

Overhead, the first bell of the morning blared above them, drowning out his desperate cry. He grabbed onto Regulus’ surprised shoulders just as the bucket tipped—yanked furiously and with sure glee. He had tried, but not fast enough, and down came their revenge to splatter over the both of them. Only it was much thicker than water.

Sirius, you damn liar.

The blood was in his hair, his eyes—everywhere—it was as thick and warm as though it’d been drained from a real animal only moments before. It was all he could taste and see and smell. He scooped the red cornstarch from his eyes and shook it from his hands, spattering the front steps even more. The space around him was a crime scene, the front doors and stone steps soaked with gore, deep rivers running down into the grass. Dancing around it, Remus' friends emerged from around the side of the building, whooping with victory and only stopping to gape in horror once they’d spotted him.

“Moony, you were supposed to get out of the way!” Sirius wailed. "Didn't you hear the whistle?!"

Remus had no words. It only took a few seconds for students on their way out of the dining hall to begin gathering. They appeared at the doors behind them, whipping the open and going cross-eyed with shock as others crowded around to get a look. He felt disgusted and horrified, but not because of the blood. Watching Regulus was like taking a punch to the gut from an elephant. He simply stood there on the front steps, mouth open and breathing shakily as though he were afraid to move. Blood soaked his dark hair, dripping down the side of his face and staining his fine features. Seeing him stunned and covered head-to-toe in gore was a million times worse than watching Carrie.

“Christ—out of the way already!” Remus heard someone shout, and a moment later Lily had muscled her way to the front of the crowd, stopping just shy of the puddled blood. Marlene was with her, and as they came to sudden halt, both girls whipped their heads up, having gone as white as sheets.

“Oh my god,” Lily shrieked. “Remus!”

“Don’t worry,” Peter called, maybe more for the crowd’s benefit; “it’s not real blood!”

Looking past them, Lily gaped at the three boys. “You lunatics!”

Sirius bent down and stuck his fingers into the blood dripping down the hall’s steps, sticking them back into his mouth. “S’just sugar,” he grinned, teeth stained red.

Some kids laughed, but a few moaned in disgust, hardly believing the truth. Sirius didn’t care—the prank had worked. Remus wanted to scream at him—You promised!—but there wasn’t time.

“Is this what you meant?” Regulus asked in the barest whisper, one only Remus could hear. “Is this what you meant by ‘finding a common ground’?”

“Reg..."

“You’re all the same,” he spat, his voice a mixture of anger and betrayal. "And I hate you both."

Turning away, Regulus tore down the cafeteria's steps. He passed Sirius, who spun around to watch him go, leaving behind bloody footprints in his wake.

"Just back up, don't step in it!" Lily was shouting, trying her best to usher students back into the dining hall. Some would not be deterred, and as they began skirting around the muck, Sirius started up the steps, walking right through it until he reached Remus’ side.

“Sorry, Moons, didn’t mean to sacrifice you! But you didn’t get out of the splash zone fast enough.”

Smiling, Sirius clapped a hand over Remus' back before withdrawing it, grimacing at the sight of the sticky blood now staining his palm. Remus was too numb to yell at him; he was still watching Regulus. As the youngest Black brother turned a corner and disappeared out of sight, it occurred to him that Sirius had sacrificed a lot more than just a friend.





* * *





It took longer than expected for Remus to scrub the fake blood from his skin. Longer even, to rid it from his hair. The sugar soaked into his scalp and stained his face, leaving him red-washed like some sad circus clown. He supposed that for someone who’d been in on the prank in the first place, he’d almost gotten off easy. While Lily had ordered the other three to stay behind and clean up their mess, he’d staggered back to their dorm room like a true victim. Though generally victims weren’t supposed to feel so guilty. Even if Sirius hadn’t broken his promise, and the bucket had been filled with water, it still would’ve ruined everything. He couldn’t help but think that Regulus must’ve hated him even more than his brother now. After all, he was expecting a stunt like that from Sirius, but Remus had lulled him into a sense of security and then betrayed his trust. It really was the epitome of a mess.

As Remus made his way out of the bathroom, scrubbing his hair with a towel, he found Sirius waiting for him on his bed. Up until that moment it’d been easy to ignore all other feelings thanks to the guilt he felt over Regulus, but as Sirius sat up and smiled ruefully at him, Remus began to sense a heedless rage well up within him.

“Glad to see the dye came off your face,” Sirius said, as Remus pulled the towel from his head and stiffly marched to his wardrobe.

“What are you doing here?” He ground out.

“Evans ordered the other tossers back to class, but I thought one of us ought to check in on you so I snuck away. Good thing too—looks like you missed a spot.”

Getting up, Sirius reached for the side of his face and Remus ripped away, startling the both of them. “Don’t!” He snarled.

Sirius' smile waned, and he bit his lip. “Ah, Moons, I’m sorry. I didn’t mean for you to get covered in muck. I’ll buy you new clothes.”

Remus couldn’t help his huff of incredulous laughter; “That’s what you’re sorry for—that I got hit too? You lied, Sirius! You said it’d just be water!”

“I know, and we filled it with that first. Just—didn’t feel like enough.”

“It never does, does it, you stupid wanker?!” Remus spat. “Nothing’s ever enough for you! You always have to take it too far!”

Sirius stepped away, looking sore. “Look, I know you’re mad but—”

“Actually, I’m furious! You should’ve heard what Regulus was saying, if you had you never would’ve pulled that rope!”

“Well, whatever it was must've been real eye-opening if it's prompted this sort of reaction.”

“You prompted this reaction, Sirius! You did when you decided to lie to me! Regulus was ready to try and make up—he was gonna talk to you and you ruined it!”

“Oh I did, did I?” Sirius barked. “That’s funny ‘cause I was totally trying to fix things in the first place!”

Remus flung his towel at the wall with an angry cry. “AUGH—You’re insane!”

“Fine—I’m insane, whatever! But I was only doing this for you!”

Remus rounded on him. “Oh my god—are you actually for real?”

“Friends don’t let friends get utterly walked over!" Sirius hollered. "We were protecting you! No one else—just us! Those shits deserved everything they got! And we did it for you!”

“I NEVER BLOODY ASKED YOU TO!”

Sirius drew back, a vein bulging in his neck. Remus returned his glare, almost panting. He waited for Sirius to whip out another stinging response—one that would leave him feeling raw for days on end—but instead Sirius just walked out of their bedroom, slamming the door behind himself.





* * *





Remus did not see Sirius in forms. Remus did not see Sirius in first period. Remus did not see Sirius at break or lunch or even biology, which he’d promised not to skip only to ensure that he’d get to watch him squirm during the song Jillian had written for their presentation on cell mitosis; If you fall down and scrap your knee, if your nails grow long and strong inexplicably, if you wake up in the morning as tall as a tree, have no fear, that's just cell mitosis, baby!

Because they deserved some punishment too, Remus avoided James and Peter as well. They tried to keep up, apologised profusely every chance they got, but Remus told himself that it wasn't enough. Freezing out his friends made him feel bad, but not that bad. After all, they only thought they were apologising for dousing him in fake gore. He doubted that even Sirius, despite their argument, understood what had really happened.

Arguing with Sirius always felt good in the moment—well, not good, more like a release—it was the bit that came after that was harder. In the absence of others all he could think about was how things could’ve gone differently—gone better—just like Sheila had said. He'd resented plenty of people: his parents, teachers, doctors, anyone dumb enough to think they had a hope in hell of "changing him for the better"—but those were all different. Sirius was his friend. Tomny was his friend too, and though he still held some sense of a grudge, really he just missed him. And now that they were so close to going home for the summer, he couldn’t afford to miss Sirius too.

He tried the astronomy building first, then a few other hiding spots, but still no Sirius. He hadn’t shown up for any of his other classes either, and none of the girls had any idea, though Lily was trying to track him down herself to slap him with a detention slip. Even James and Peter didn’t know where he was, and Remus refused to let them help look.

Finding him in the music room had been a coincidence. He’d left one of his books under the risers that morning and was returning to fetch it when he stumbled upon Sirius in a place he hadn’t seen him in a very long time—sitting at Sheila’s grand piano. He hadn’t noticed him yet, and unable to help himself, Remus paused in the doorway, waiting to see what he’d do. But Sirius just sat.

Sat and stared, in utter silence.

“Fuck man—just make it for you already,” Remus said finally, making Sirius spin around as though he’d been caught doing something he shouldn’t. When he saw it was only him, he deflated, turning back to the instrument.

“What are you doing here?” Sirius asked, hunched over on the piano bench. Remus could see the entire shape of his shoulder blade outlined underneath his school shirt.

"Just... looking around," he mumbled from the doorway.

“We don’t even have class today.”

“Classes are over anyway. And I forgot my book in forms.”

“Oh.” Sirius began rubbing his fingers like an arthritic old man. “Want to... Want to sit?”

At the offer, a sliver of hope lodged itself in Remus’ chest and he shuffled into the room. Sirius made room for him on the bench and he sat, though it felt awkward; his legs stuck out past the pedals and the keys felt too low to the ground to be within comfortable reach. Next to him, Sirius was the picture of a perfect musician. He sat with his back straight and his hands neatly tucked into his lap like it’d been drilled into him, which of course it had. For a while they just existed there, staring down at the open piano without a word. Sirius regarded the ivory keys like they were the fangs of a cobra ready to strike, but to Remus they were only ghosts.

“Are you… still mad, Moony?”

Remus looked to his right, where Sirius was watching him with tepid eyes.

“I should be, shouldn't I?” He said; then, “But no, not really... You?”

Sirius shook his head. “No. I’m mostly just sorry for lying. And for breaking my promise.”

“Well, I’m mostly sorry for yelling.”

"And I'm mostly sorry for upsetting you."

"I'm mostly sorry for calling you a stupid wanker."

“Nah... I deserved it.”

“You’re right, you did.”

Chuckling half-heartedly, Sirius looked down at his lap. Remus wanted so badly to take his hand—to trace the soft pads of his palm, the ridges of his knuckles—but there were things unsaid between them.

“I’m not mad,” he said again, “but that doesn't mean I've forgiven you.”

“Okay,” Sirius murmured.

“What you did was…" Remus sighed. "It just made things harder.”

“Seems to be all I’m good at.”

“That’s not true. You set a piano on fire in front of your entire family—that takes real talent.”

Another smile touched Sirius' lips. "I'd been saving that one. It felt good to watch that hunk of wood burn—worth every punishment that witch could come up with. I just wanted it to feel like a husk. Like everything else in that house..."

Looking down at the piano keys, Remus swallowed thickly. “Do you remember last year when I picked that fight and you threw out that list of everything you knew about me?”

Sirius nodded in recognition; “Yeah why? Looking for volume two?”

“No, wanker. I only meant to say that I never told you that I have a list too.”

“Oh? For me?”

“Mhm. It’s alphabetised, even.” Remus held his hands out and spread them apart as though he were reading off a giant billboard. “Starts with, ‘absolute dickhead’. Shitty wanker's a bit further down.”

“Ha. You know me so well.”

Lowering his hands, Remus nudged Sirius with his shoulder. “Seriously though. I do know you. You can cause bad, but you also do good sometimes too."

"Nah. I like to deny it, but I'm a Black through and through, Moony. I'm stained black, even in here." Sirius tapped his chest.

"No," Remus shook his head. "Could a stained person, make people smile even on their worse days? Could they start a conversation with a stranger and end it with a friend? No one's good all the time, Padfoot, but that doesn't mean you don't have good parts. Like... how you always give everyone your undivided attention when you’re talking to them, even if it’s just to be a sarcastic asshole."

"I have a reputation to protect," Sirius supplied cheekily.

"Yeah, well you’re loyal to a fucking fault too—don't I know it—and you can't sleep when you know others might be crying. You say you hate school, but you come anyway and you still manage to get all the teachers to like you."

"Mm, some more than others."

"You hate reading for class but secretly enjoy reading for yourself—"

"I like the 'happily ever afters' what can I say?"

Remus smiled. "I know you’re really good at crosswords and that you work hard, even if you’d prefer to pretend that you don’t. You whistle when you think nobody’s around and sing when you know they are—you're a wicked-hot musician. And you call James’ parents ‘mum and dad’ because you know he likes hearing it!”

Sirius chuckled a bit at that. “I like it too.”

“I know. I also know you don’t let anyone tell you off for the nail polish or make up or jewelry, and I admire that, and…” Remus smiled lazily down at the piano keys; “and you do care about school. You like school.”

“I like my friends,” Sirius amended. “I can like anywhere, as long as we’re together.”

“Anywhere, huh?”

“Anywhere.”

“Am I your friend?”

Sirius’ head shot up. “You actually need to ask me that?”

Yes, Remus thought, but am I only your friend?

“Sorry…” He murmured, coming back to himself; “I was being stupid.”

“You’re never stupid,” Sirius said. He looked away, back to the keys that might bite him, and Remus began to feel the familiar hammering of his heart in his ears.

“My mum used to play the piano, you know,” he said plainly, to drown out the noise. “She was really good—classically trained like you. Before she got sick, she was always saying how she would teach me, but I don't think I would've made a very good piano player anyway. My posture’s too shit.”

Out of the corner of his eye, Remus saw Sirius crack another smile. “We should’ve got you on something long, like the bassoon. Put your lanky git body to good use.”

“In that case I’m getting you a ukulele.”

“Do it. I’ll bash ya in the knees with it, you giant.”

Remus chuckled weakly, and his eyes caught his own reflection in the piano's silky surface. “Sometimes at night... it's as though I can hear her playing.”

“Like... in a dream?”

“Must be. I don’t think I have any real memories of hearing her play, even though I know she must’ve. She got tired easily, and the pills made her hands shake. It was hard for her so she sort of just… sat by the window of the music room. She used to just watch the piano for hours, staring at it like it was some sort of living thing that might come alive and, I dunno… hurt her." He looked back at Sirius. "Kind of like you’re doing right now...”

Sirius tightened hold of his hands, crushing his fingers in his lap until they went white. "I know it shouldn't be this hard, it's just..."

"You don't want to play?"

"I dunno... It hurts in a way. Remembering."

"I understand," Remus told him. "It hurts because it was their job, but instead they put all their shit on us, didn't they?"

Sirius ran a nervous hand through his hair. "You're... You're startlingly self-aware sometimes, Moony."

"It's part of the guilt-complex."

"God. Not the guilt-complex..."

Remus smiled again. It was easy around Sirius. “You can play if you want, Padfoot,” he told him, “you just have to make it for you.”

Sirius released his strangled fingers and for a moment it looked as though he might stretch them toward the piano keys, but he choked, hesitating long enough to let out a frustrated sigh.

“I can’t.”

Sighing softly, Remus reached up to rub the back of his neck. As his hands came down, he stopped to stare at them, and then glanced back at his friend. “Well, do you trust me then?”

“Yes,” Sirius said, without hesitation.

Nodding, Remus took a nervous breath and set his own fingers on the keys. He pressed the first note, a high little ding that echoed out around them like a cry, and looked to Sirius for approval, but Sirius was only staring at his hands on the keys, forehead creased in concern. So, Remus kept going.

He pressed another key, then another, until his fingers were clumsily hopping across them one at a time. When he reached the last he hit it several times; dun-dun-dun-dun-dun-dun-dun-dun and then proceeded to fly back up to the other end, reaching past Sirius with a cheeky grin. Eventually te was slapping the keys—hammering them—drawing noise from the instrument in every unfathomable way he could. Beethoven would’ve been appalled, Mozart would’ve had him drawn and quartered—he didn’t care. It was noise and neither of them could bear silence—never could, never would.

“Okay, okay! I get it, you really can’t play!” Sirius laughed eventually, catching him by the wrists and choking out his sinner’s symphony.

“Guess you’re going to have to teach me!” Remus grinned, pushing past him to reach a few more notes.

“I can’t!”

DUH-DUN; “You must!”

"No, I really can't!"

DUH-DUH-DUNNN! "Then we suffer!"

“You’re such an idiot, Moony!”

Yes, oh yes, Remus thought, his face overtaken by a grin. “I think my fingers are possessed, Padfoot! I need an idiot’s instruction!”

Sirius laughed some more, and it was more beautiful than any song. The best composer in the world couldn’t have matched it.

“Bloody—Alright!” he said finally. “Give the ivories a chance to breathe first!”

With a final; DUH-DUH! Remus sagged against him, laughing as he drew back. Sirius shoved him lightly.

“That was a total train-wreck.”

“I’m a beginner,” he said shamelessly, “I’ve never been shown what to do.”

“Clearly.” Sirius licked his lips and raised his hands, actually letting them hover over the keys. If Remus looked close enough he could see his own muddled face reflected in their polished ivory shine. He wondered what Sirius saw.

“Hey,” Remus said, leaning in until he could see both of Sirius’ eyes. “Do you trust me?”

Sirius looked to him, jaw clenched, and nodded.

“Okay then.” Slowly he drew up off the bench, giving Sirius enough room to stretch out and reach every key. He stood behind him, holding his breath, and Sirius did the same, almost frozen. “You can do it, Padfoot,” he urged him. “You don’t have to be the Sirius that played before. You can start anew.”

Looking back at him, Sirius opened his mouth. It would’ve been so easy for Remus to lean forward and kiss him.

“Okay,” Sirius breathed quietly, before straightening up on the bench. Even his back looked beautiful, and Remus was nearly lost in the image of him alone, but the moment Sirius began to play, he was truly transported.

Sirius needed no sheet music, instead the notes flew out of him by either muscle memory or pure invention. The song was beautiful and terrifying all at once. Light and airy like a summer breeze blowing through sheer white curtains, but just beyond that, distant thunder clouds rolled closer and closer. It made goosebumps rise over his entire body. It made Remus want to flee the room. It made him remember the sound of his mother crying when she could no longer get out of bed on her own. The clatter of pill bottles as her shaky hands spilled them across the floor. The emotion that came with seeing her blue eyes well up with frustrated tears.

But it was also those nights Hope would leave the radio on, and they’d dance around the parlour until they were laughing so hard they had to sit down. Of sitting in Giles’ lap and watching him turn the paper and pointing out the pictures. Of hearing Tonya say I love you. Of being hugged by Tomny. Of seeing James and Peter smile. Of hearing the girls laugh.

Of Sirius' everything.

Remus wasn’t sure what the song was named—probably something French—but if he'd have gotten to choose, it would've been 'Memory'.

He was still miles away by the time Sirius finished the song, and he came back to himself to find his friend breathing so hard his shoulders were trembling. Remus heard a sniffle, and swallowed, afraid that he’d made a mistake in pushing him.

“Sirius…”

“God,” Sirius said, “I fucking hate Bach. Mum used to make me play the Partitas for hours, yelling or hitting me with this fucking stick—a real narrow one, like a whip—every time I played too fast or hit the wrong key. Sometimes I would do it on purpose too, just to have a real reason to glare at her—then she’d scold me again because, ‘how dare I look at her that way’. But she looked at me, Moony! She looked at me and it was never enough—it’ll never be enough. Why can’t I play for myself? For only me?”

Sirius sagged inwards like he was trying to make himself appear very small and Remus surged forward, sliding onto the end of the bench and catching him as he began to break down. He squeezed, so tight that he could feel Sirius’ trembling in his own bones. “I hear you,” he told him, “I hear you.”

“It just fucking sucks,” Sirius whimpered. “I hate all of it. It was horrible. I sounded horrible.”

“No, it was beautiful. You were so beautiful.”

“Not beautiful enough.”

“What’s enough?" Remus swore. "Who decides when anything’s enough?”

Through his choked sobs, Sirius laughed bitterly. “The audience, I suppose.”

“Well fine, but right now I’m your only audience and I say it was enough, Sirius.”

Sirius reached up and clung to him, holding his arm so tightly it should’ve hurt. Remus barely felt it.

“I won’t play for her anymore. Not any of them,” Sirius told him, head hung. “But I’ll play for you.”

Remus squeezed even tighter. “I’d like that.”

Neither of them said anything for a while, and slowly Sirius' breathing began to even out again. He sniffled a few times, and Remus didn't even mind if he was wiping snot on his shirt.

“Remus...?”

Chills. Sirius hardly ever called him by name.

“Yes, Sirius?”

“I meant it, you know—what I said before... You’re glorious.”

“… I’m just happy you’re here, Sirius.”

With his face pressed into Sirius’ shoulder Remus couldn’t be sure, but he thought that Sirius just might be smiling. They hugged one another for a long time still, an awkward jumble of limbs that were too long and yet not long enough. Briefly Remus began to wonder what it was he was doing—you're too close! Get away now before it ends badly!—but the thoughts left him the moment Sirius shifted and he let go. They turned to look at one another, grey eyes and brown, and for a moment the world almost made sense, but then Sirius looked away.

“That was embarrassing,” he murmured, wiping his face on his sleeve.

Remus tipped his head back to look at the roof of the music room—anywhere but Sirius’ mouth—and shrugged. “Not as embarrassing as watching you hop around with cow shit stuck to the bottom of your foot.”

“Or showing your bare arse off to the entire school.”

“And just how does our gym class equate to the entire school?” Remus demanded, looking back to him. Sirius grinned guiltily. Remus sighed happily.

Then for a split-second, Sirius’ eyes darted downwards. Remus didn’t miss it. An explosion could’ve been happening right over his shoulder and he still wouldn’t have looked away. He didn’t, not even to see for himself how Sirius’ pinky was now brushing up against the side of his hand as it rested on the piano bench. He almost shivered, but then Sirius bit his lip and leaned in ever-so-slightly. Remus did the same, and suddenly they were closer than they’d ever been...

No! We can’t!

Fuck that—yes! Yes! Yes! Yes! Ye—

“YES!" James shouted from the music room doorway. "Told you we’d find ‘em, Pete!”

Sirius whipped around so fast the ends of his hair swatted Remus in the face as he flew backward, nearly toppling off the piano bench. He caught himself on the keys, making a dreadful twang of noise as James and Peter skipped into the room.

“You jammy bastards!” Sirius cried, forcing a stilted laugh. “You just about scared the living daylights out of us!”

“Not as if we were sneaking,” James said. “What were you even doing?”

“Playing piano,” Remus answered quickly. Sirius glanced at him, and he noted with relief that his cheeks were also red.

“You were actually playing the piano? I thought you hated the thing, Sirius,” Peter said in surprise.

Sirius stretched his arms out sheepishly. “Yeah, well... someone convinced me to give it another go.”

Remus blushed harder. Fuck me, really.

“That’s great news, mate!” James cried. A second later he was bouncing across the room and grappling Sirius in a hug from behind. It almost made Remus jealous to see James do it so easily.

“We totally missed hearing you play,” Peter agreed, coming to join them.

Lightly shoving his best friend off, Sirius spun around on the bench. “So what are you two doing here—come to practice?”

“Nah,” James waved, “we were looking for you actually.” He looked at Remus pointedly, brows raised. “Does thisss... erhm... mean you and Moony have made up then?”

“Well—”

“Yes,” Remus answered. Sirius turned to him, looking hopeful, and bit his lip over a smile. It was irrational, but in that moment Remus had never resented James and Peter more. Curse their eternal friendship. Curse their horrible timing more.

James clapped his hands together. “Brilliant, now we can tell you our good news!”

“What good news?” Sirius asked.

Peter cleared his throat. “We talked to McGonagall about our schedules for next term, and she approved it. We're gonna switch a few classes around.”

“You can do that?” Remus frowned. “They made us choose weeks ago.”

“Yeah, well, we sorta realised that next year’s our last year at school—all of us in the same place—and who knows what’s gonna happen after,” James said kindly; “So Pete and I figured, might as well make the most of the time we’ve got left.”

“You make it sound as though we’re all gonna hop the twig the moment we leave school,” Sirius smirked.

“No, nothing like that—but life is unexpected right, so we thought that—”

“That we’d switch into music with you!” Peter announced.

Both Remus and Sirius were stunned. “Like take music with Sheila?” Sirius eventually echoed. “In class? With us? The two of you?”

“No,” James grinned, “the four of us.”

“It’s just a spare. Might as well make it fun,” Peter shrugged.

Remus was utterly slack-mouthed; “But Pete, what about your art lessons?”

“Meh, not like I was gonna do anything with it anyway. I can still draw on my own time, and Madame Aubert's already said I can use the art room whenever I want.”

He whirled on James. “And you, you’re just gonna give up gym?”

“I can run during breaks. S’not as if I’m gonna suddenly lose all athleticism by sitting in here for a few hours a week. Who knows, maybe I'll learn something.”

"Like how to read sheet music," Peter snorted.

While James shouldered his friend, Sirius shot to his feet, almost glowing with excitement. “This is brilliant! Albeit a bit unexpected, I'll give ya that—but still, absolutely fantastic!”

“Thought you’d be happy!” James cried.

“Of course I’m happy!” He grabbed his best friend by the shoulders. “This is a real chance—we can actually make something out of Marauders now! We could even perform!”

Peter blanched a bit. “Hold on, we’re hardly the Hawkings’ Philharmonic Orchestra."

“Bah, orchestras are just glorified cover bands anyway.” Sirius turned back to the piano, almost breathless. The look he gave Remus was pure happiness. “This is amazing, isn’t it, Moony?”

“Yeah,” Remus said, “it really is.”

Chapter 64: Crescendo


Chapter Summary

It the Marauders' final day of the 1976-1977 school term, and they're going to celebrate.



Chapter Notes

You guys were literally so sweet in the comments on last chapter. I actually cried while reading some of them *cries again*. Thank you so much for enjoying this story. Hearing that people want to read these words is truly the best motivator.

Now, without further ado... on with the show!

CW: Drinking. Cringing. Friendship and... more?



See the end of the chapter for more notes



I don’t mind other guys dancing with my girl,

That’s fine, I know them all pretty well;

But I know sometimes I must get out in the light,

Better leave her behind with the kids, they’re alright…

- “The Kids Are Alright” The Who, 1966



Thursday 16th June 1977

When Professor McGonagall asked him to come to her office on the eve of their last night at school, Remus assumed it was because she’d finally decided on his punishment for almost sending Barty to an early grave. After two weeks with no word on the matter, he'd almost let himself believe that she'd forgotten the whole thing, which was laughable. Their Headmistress had a memory like an elephant and a penchant for justice much stronger than any London police officer. That, combined with her calling him in to the main office so close to summer holiday could mean only one thing: that he was not going to be returning to Hawkings Independent School next term.

It was pleasing at least, to look up at the glass cabinet behind McGonagall’s desk and see the shiny new first place trophy the boys' football team had earned at their end-of-year tournament. James had been ecstatic over the win and arrived back at school the day before, waving the thing over his head while the whole team cheered. He'd spent the rest of the day touring the grounds with it and accepting praise from all the teachers before promptly passing out for a nap that was now going on eighteen hours long. Peter had stopped packing a few times just to make sure James was still breathing and afterwards Sirius had gotten the bright idea of sticking a pair of tampons up his nose to see if they'd make him snore even louder. (Where he'd gotten the tampons, Remus had no idea, but his hypotheses was correct; by the time Remus had left the dorm, James was snoring like a chainsaw.)

In the time since, Remus had started his walk over to Castle Hall, resolving not to tell any of his friends about his sure-to-be expulsion while they were still at school. He didn’t want to be the one to ruin their last night together; instead he’d write them each a letter once he was home. At least that way they’d have the summer to forget about him. Only, Remus hadn't been counting on McGonagall’s personal peculiarities, and unbeknownst to him, was walking into a much stranger conversation.

“You want me to do what?” He demanded.

Professor McGonagall gave him a tight-lipped smile. “It’s very simple, Mr. Lupin. I want you to spend your final year at Hawkings as a school prefect.”

Oh Christ.

Remus slapped his forehead. “You’ve got to be joking.”

“Oh, but I assure you, I am not.”

“But I thought you were going to expel me—I punched a kid!” Two, if he were being honest.

“Do you still wish to be expelled, Remus?”

Quickly, he shut his mouth. “No…”

“Then I assume this is an arrangement that works for both parties.”

“But I am not prefect material!" Remus blabbed. "Prefects are—are—smart!”

McGonagall cracked another smile, this one of the snide sort that said she knew everything. “You are very intelligent, if your marks this term are anything to go by. In fact I believe congratulations are even in order, good show. Are there any other prefect-like qualities you don't claim to adhere to?"

“Yes! They care about things like—like extracurriculars, which I do not—no offence. They're like professional babysitters, and I'd probably kill a baby as soon as it looked at me."

"I assure you, there will be no babies," McGonagall chuckled. "Only your fellow classmates."

"Okay, but—but prefects are just so uncool—and they're also stuck-up and bossy!”

“Is Ms. Evans stuck-up and bossy?”

“Well, she’s certainly bossy but she…” Remus trailed off, caught up in his own web. With nothing left to do, he let out a heavy sigh and leaned forward to beg. “Please, Professor McGonagall, can’t you just give me detention? Or assign me lines to do over the summer? I'll post them to you and everything!”

“I could, though I’m not sure the message would sink in properly come September, but if you were to have something constructive to fill your time, like becoming an acting prefect, where you’ll be expected to uphold the school rules rather than break them—then I’m sure it’ll stick.”

Remus used to think that all gym teachers were sadists. Now he was coming to the conclusion that the assumption extended to Headmistresses as well.

“Mr. Lupin,” McGonagall started again, “I stand by what I told you when you arrived here nearly two years ago, we here at Hawkings do not admit lost causes. You are a prime example of a student who has flourished under proper tutelage and the creation strong bonds between yourself and your peers. Now I implore you to use your final year at school to think on what it is you’d like to do with yourself in the future, and how you might best go about it. You have had many successes here—even if those successes were dotted with a few brow-raising complications.” She punctuated the statement with a brow-raise of her own, and Remus avoided her gaze guiltily. “But... I expect that you will have many more to come."

“Complications?”

“Successes.”

“... As a prefect.”

McGonagall nodded, a clever smirk on her face, and Remus let out another long sigh.

“Fine...”

“Excellent. As you may know, you will be required to arrive at school on August thirty-first in preparation for the other incoming students to arrive the following day, but apart from that, I hope you have a very happy summer, Remus.”

“Thank you professor,” he said, standing, “... you too.”

Remus left the office feeling conflicted. He didn't want to be a prefect, he wanted to be left in peace. Okay, so maybe the prefects weren't all of the things he'd said they were, but they certainly weren't made up of kids like him! Ugh, it was all so messed up.

By the time he'd made it back to House Lane, Remus had moved past the 'denial' stage and had gone straight to bargaining, attempting to look on the bright side, of which there were three main points:

1. His friends were going to have a heyday when they heard the news, but at least he wasn't going to be expelled.

2. As a prefect, he would be able to give them detention for said heyday.

3. He would at least have Lily. Having her by his side would be better than nothing, and with Snape finally out of the picture, perhaps they could even be prefect partners.

By happenstance, Remus ended up stumbling upon Lily first, as she was just getting out of her end-of-year prefect party. She'd been making her way up the lane toward the boys' dorm when they met up, and was wearing a pretty violet dress with matching ribbons in her hair.

“You look nice,” he said, and she beamed at him.

“Thank you! The dress is actually from James’ mum. She made it for me for Christmas—apparently there isn’t anything that woman can’t do.”

She gave a little twirl and he clapped for her, before shoving his hands into his pockets as they finished making their way back to the dorms.

“I met with McGonagall today," he confessed. Better to tell Lily first than anyone else. "She's decided on my punishment for hammering Barty."

"Oh no. What'd she say?"

"She's asked me to be a prefect."

Lily gasped; “She did?”

“Well, more like told me.”

“That’s brilliant! You’ll be so good at it!”

“You’re mental. She only wants me to do it so she can claim that I’ve been ‘reformed’. The shitty kid with a bad track record and facial scars is now top of the school—'imagine what the board’ll have to say'.”

Lily smacked his arm playfully, practically bouncing up and down on the pavement next to him. “Who cares what the school board will think—this is a big deal, Remus! It’s recognition for all your hard work.”

“Feels more like an unpaid job I don’t want.”

“But it is paid.”

Remus’ head shot up. “It is?”

“Just a small stipend,” Lily amended. “But still, it’s something. And you’ll get an extra period in your timetable to study for A-levels.”

“Oh sure, that is when I’m not busy with me ‘prefectly duties’.”

“Those aren’t all the time. If you're lucky they'll give you a permeant position somewhere, like the library! I did that my first year, and I got to study all I wanted during the down-time."

"Yippee..."

"Just think of the other benefits though—you can give Black a detention every time he pisses you off!”

He had thought of that, but it was funny to hear Lily try to sway him. “In that case he'll have so many detentions, you’ll never see him again.”

Lily giggled. “I’m going to miss that free period actually. Did I tell you I switched some classes around?”

“Oh? Did you suddenly find an interest in music too?”

“No, law actually. To prepare for university.”

“I thought you wanted to do psychology in university," he said, clearly surprised.

Shyly, Lily began staring down at her shoes as they walked. “Hm, yes, well, I’ve been thinking about it for a long time now, and there are plenty of ways to help people within the field of psychology, but none that really call to me. For so long I thought being a lawyer was unrealistic, but now I feel as though it might be something that I could actually be good at. You know... helping others when the law won’t.”

Remus looked up at the great expanse of blue sky above them, and suddenly felt very thoughtful. “You’d make an amazing lawyer, Lils.”

“You think?”

“I know.” He glanced at her. “You win almost every argument.”

Lily took his arm affectionately. “Almost every argument. I know a few stubborn jerks who are hard to crack.” She pinched him, and he jumped but didn’t shake her off. Instead they kept walking, arm in arm.

“So what kind of law?” Remus asked, when they were almost back at Godric.

“Civil litigation I think. I’d like to defend labour workers and women—maybe even medical malpractice. Somewhere I can really make a difference for those who might otherwise get walked over.”

Remus gave an impressed whistle. “You and James just gonna take over his dad’s firm together then?”

“I don’t know about that. Let’s just get into university first.”

“Ah, but you gotta aim high, Evans. Sirius’ll need all the help he can get, springing himself from whatever lockup he ends up in.”

“You’re all hopeless,” Lily sighed happily, shaking her head. They’d made it back to his dorm, and were walking up the front path together when Remus spotted Jillian waiting by the front steps. She perked up immediately and waved at him, making Lily cock her head curiously, a cheeky look on her face.

“What’s going—”

“Don’t say a word,” Remus ground out, as Jillian raced up to them.

“Hi ya, Remus!” She smiled.

“Oh, h-hey Jillian...”

“I was hoping to catch you! Do you have a moment or are you… busy?”

Jillian looked pointedly at the way Lily was holding his arm, but Lily just dropped it innocently. “ ‘Course he has time!” She trilled. “I was just on my way in to see the lads. He’s all yours, Jill. I’ll see you inside, Remus.”

Remus watched as Lily shot him a pair of finger-guns before flouncing up the dorm’s front steps in her purple dress, utterly abandoning him to his fate.

“Maybe you should give corporate law some thought,” he called after her, “I’m sure with your icy heart it’d be a walk in the park!”

Lily only waved, while Jillian gave a little giggle. “You’re so funny, Remus. I get why Lily likes you.”

“Ah. Thanks...”

“Are the two of you… I mean, she’s still dating James Potter, right?”

“ ‘Course,” Remus frowned. “Why, has anyone said otherwise?”

“No, of course not! I just…” Jillian bit her lip over a smile. “Remus, I was wondering if you wanted to exchange phone numbers to, you know, keep in contact over the summer?”

Remus’ stomach tightened. No, no, please no.

“Ah, well—you see Jill, I—uhm... I don’t actually have… a… p-phone…”

“You don’t... have a phone?”

“We—Well I-I do, it’s just I… erm... took a vow of silence?”

“Wouldn’t that mean you’re not supposed to talk at all?” Jillian asked, blinking at him.

“It’s er—well, it doesn’t start until the summer, actually. Yeah, that's right—not a single word the moment we arrive home. All us guys are doing it, in fact. It's... a political thing—sociopolitical! You know—fight the power and all that...?”

“So what’s your stance? Starving kids in Africa or something? Poor factory workers' conditions?”

He felt bad for lying to the poor girl, but they only had one day of school left—there was no way that whatever this was, was going to persist throughout an entire summer, so he winced and gave another crappy excuse. “Sorry, it’s kind of a personal thing so... it’s hard to explain.”

“Oh, alright,” Jillian said kindly; “In that case, could I write to you instead—like a pen pal? Or does your vow of silence extend to letters, too?”

Remus forced a laugh. “Ha... ha... Don’t be silly," he said through his teeth, "of course you can write.”

“Brilliant. What’s your address?”

With no other excuses left in the vault, he gave it to her, regretting every choice that had led him to that point.

Ha! You're so weak.

Shut up.

Can't even say no to a girl. It's your funeral, mate.

With his address tightly fisted in her grip, Jillian finally left him on the dorm’s front steps, waving goodbye and hurrying up the lane as though she were afraid he would turn around and snatch it back again. Feeling like an utter idiot, he watched her go before dragging his feet the rest of the way inside, only to find that Lily had been watching them through the door’s window the entire time.

“You’re evil!” He wailed, as she burst into laughter in the dorm's foyer.

“But Remus, it was so cute!”

“It wasn’t cute, she’s bloody everywhere! I swear to god, yesterday she was waiting for me outside the toilet!”

Lily bent forward, howling and cradling her stomach. “Why haven’t you just told her you’re not interested then?"

“It’s not that easy!”

“Of course it is, you’re just a chicken!”

Groaning, Remus turned away and leaned his head against the public post board next to the phone lines. “She has my address now—what if she actually looks me up over the summer? Oh god, what if she shows up at my house?”

Finished with her laughter, Lily wiped the tears from her eyes and pat him on the shoulder. “She's only a girl, Remus. You may be popular, but you’ll have to work a bit harder than that if you want to claim you have your own stalker.”

“I’m not popular,” he grumbled, “James and Sirius are popular.”

Lily gave a great sigh. “Oh Remus, sometimes you can be so thick.”

Baby, I’m amazed at the way you love me all the time,

And maybe I’m afraid of the way I love you;

Maybe I’m amazed at the way you pulled me out of time,

You hung me on the line,

Maybe I’m amazed at the way I really need you…

- “Maybe I’m Amazed” Paul McCartney, 1970



Their last night at school was finally upon them, and being the loud, obnoxious seventeen year-old’s they were, they’d tried pushing for an end of the year party, but Kenny was adamant. After an entire keg of mulberry wine had split over the common room rug on James’ birthday, the dorm monitor had sworn off all partying for the rest of the school year.

“He’s such a nark,” Sirius complained, hauling his packed trunk toward the door in preparation for their early departure the next morning. “The carpet was already red, it barely stained!”

“What about the clogged toilets on the first and second floor?” Lily asked from James’ bed.

"And the mattresses that ended up on the front lawn?" Remus pushed.

“And the curtains those eighth years set on fire!” Peter added.

“It was just the trim,” Sirius scoffed, ignoring the rest of them, “and they were god-ugly anyway. Glad someone finally did it.”

“Well,” James started, from his place next to the record player, the only thing Sirius had yet to pack up, “you’ll be glad to know that I don’t have anything against a bit of split wine—or arson.”

A gasp went up around the room.

“Does that mean you got it, Prongs?” Remus asked, still busy peeling his Queen posters down off the wall. To answer him, James turned around, rubbing his hands together.

“That’s right, lads—and lady—you’re looking at the next Godric dorm monitor. McGonagall sent the notice over this morning.”

“Fuck yeah!” Sirius cried, ditching his trunks to smack his hand against James’ in congratulations.

"The Headmistress is definitely going to regret that one!" Peter snorted.

“That's not all, Remus got prefect too,” Lily added, because she absolutely couldn’t help it.

All three of his friends turned their wide eyes on him, and Remus groaned inwardly.

“Moony, you didn’t!” James exclaimed.

“It’s my punishment for laying out Barty,” he said quickly. “It was either that or she’d probably have had me expelled.”

“This is so great!” Sirius proclaimed. “A dorm monitor and a prefect under one roof—who's gonna stop us now?”

“Maybe I will,” Remus said smugly, “if you continue to annoy me, that is.”

“Ha.”

The bedroom door opened and Mary stuck her head in. “We come bearing gifts!” She sang, before opening the door and revealing the several bottles of booze she’d hidden under her shirt on the way up. Marlene and Lottie came after, all of them wearing big smiles and casual clothes instead of their usual uniforms. They quickly made themselves comfortable, falling across the boys’ beds as Sirius and James popped the top of every bottle they'd managed to sneak in.

"Dorm monitors say no parties, so fine," Mary declared, "we'll just have our own."

While Sirius set an album on the turntable, Remus quickly finished putting his posters away and shut his trunk before accepting his first drink of the evening from Lottie. After pushing the beds aside, they made a large circle on the floor and fit in together, each of them simply content to spend their final night in each other's presence. James had laid back on the rug with his head in Lily’s lap and she began curling her fingers through his dark hair while Sirius sat next to them, Andy’s guitar propped up on one knee. Remus found himself tucked in between him and Lottie, who’d begun to draw on his arm in pen. He let her, slightly bemused by the skull and crossbones she'd already doodled on the inside of his forearm. It was almost sad to see their room looking so barren, but with eight bodies filling it up it didn’t feel nearly so empty.

Eventually word of his and James’ promotions came to light and afterwards Marlene announced that she had news of her own. Apparently her summer plans included spending the entire month of August away in Morocco, where she’d be volunteering with a non-profit charity organisation to feed homeless women and children. This came to a great surprise to all of them, most of all Mary, who’d been banking on having Marlene come stay with her in Paris so she could avoid her family.

“I told you about it,” Marlene reasoned.

“Yes, but you never said you were actually gonna apply!” She whined.

“Well, I didn’t think I would be accepted either. You should’ve heard how long it took to convince Mum and Dad to let me go.”

“Why Morocco?” Remus asked.

Marlene grinned, the excitement clear on her face. “Mr. Durrin has a friend who teaches English there and he connected me with a recruiter in London.”

“So they speak English?” Lottie interjected.

“Some do, but it’s mostly Arabic and French.”

“That’s insane,” Sirius said. “You’re gonna fly there—on a real plane?”

“Yeah, but I’ll still be around for a while. We don't leave until mid-July.” She looked at Mary, who had puckered and turned away, picking at the rug. “Don’t be like that, Mary. I thought you’d be happy for me.”

“You didn’t even mention it…” Mary pouted. “You don’t even speak French!”

Reaching over, Marlene took her hand. “Guess you have the next four weeks to teach me, then.”

Mary glanced down at their interlaced fingers, and sighed before squeezing back tightly and leaning her head on Marlene’s shoulder sadly. Remus knew exactly how it felt, anticipating how much she would miss her best friend after her departure.

“Now I suppose our summer plans pale in comparison, huh, Pete?” James said, nudging Peter with his foot.

“I believe you’re coming to visit me this summer,” Lily said, pulling her fingers out of James’ hair.

“Oh—not that! I just meant the summer house in Devon. I told you we were going there after I visited you, yeah?”

Lily smirked and bent down to kiss him on the forehead. “Yes, you did.”

“Jesus—get a room!” Lottie teased, finishing up several swirling lines on the inside of Remus’ wrist. He watched her, lifting a mug of whisky to his lips before glancing to his left and catching Sirius’ eye.

“You want one?” He smirked. “I warn you though, my tattoo artist is in very high demand right now.”

Lottie giggled but Sirius only gave a quiet smile. He had a drink in one hand and was quietly fiddling the guitar's tuning keys with the other. “What are your plans for the holiday then?”

“Got none,” Remus answered. “Unless you count avoiding my dad. I figure it’ll just be me, Giles, and the dogs mostly.”

“And us!” James chirped. “Nice try, but you’re not getting away this summer, Lupin. Mum says you can still come to Devon too—there's plenty of room!”

“Okay, Prongs,” Remus smiled, before looking back at Sirius. “I promise to write, though," he told him.

“Oh really?” Sirius casually sipped his own drink. “Songs or letters?”

“Dunno yet. Maybe both if you’re lucky.”

Sirius chuckled, before tucking his pick between his teeth and looking down again, strumming lightly on the guitar’s strings. He was wearing both nail polish and eyeliner today, probably because he knew he wasn’t going to have either while at home. The thought suddenly struck Remus, and he felt bad all over again. He'd tried more than once to bring up the odd things Regulus had been ranting about outside the dining hall, but ever since that day in the music room, Sirius had been dismissing any and all mention of his mother. Remus supposed it was because he didn't want to ruin the time he had left by discussing her, but it was still worth worrying.

“Sirius..." he started lowly, so only the two of them could hear over the stereo's music; "about that thing Reg said to me...?"

Instantly Sirius’ smile was gone. "I thought I told you not to worry about it."

"You did—twice. But if you could just tell me what Regulus meant, then maybe..."

"I told you already, I don't know what Reg was on about. He was probably just spewing shit because he was pissed off."

"No, no—it was before the prank. I think it was a warning. And after, that's when he was ready to make up with you."

"Yeah right. I think hell will freeze over first."

"Sirius."

"Remus."

Remus sighed. "Alright. But you're absolutely sure everything's gonna be fine?"

"No," Sirius snorted. "I'm going home—it's never fine. That's what makes it all so 'exciting'. Heh."

“You jackass—doesn’t that worry you at all?”

"Nope."

"Why not?"

With suddenly finality, Sirius clapped a hand over the strings, looking up at him. “ 'Cause Lupin... if I stopped to worry about every little threat my mum spat out, I’d never feel brave again.”

Remus' throat suddenly felt very tight. He held Sirius' cool gaze a moment longer, before finally breaking eye-contact and looking down at his lap. “Oh. I’m… sorry.”

“Don’t be. You worry too much, Moons. And you’re so much cuter when you’re smiling.” Reaching out, Sirius clapped him gently on the back before returning to the guitar. If he noticed the way Remus’ eyes were watering in embarrassment, he didn't say anything. Finally Remus let out a heavy breath; unable to look at Sirius anymore, and turned to Lottie.

“Lottie... why is there a cartoon dinosaur on my arm?”

Lottie beamed down at her handiwork. “Because it’s cute and you’re cute!” She bopped him on the nose with her finger, but in comparison to Sirius, his reaction was rather null.

Still tucked up between his friends, Remus focused on polishing off his drink—and then a second—until the turntable finally clicked off, giving him an excuse to leave the circle and change the album.

“Remus put on ‘Goodbye Yellow Brick Road’!” Mary called as he stood.

“No, that’s way too sappy,” James said, “go for ‘Moondance’ instead.”

“Try reading the room guys.” Sirius turned around and pointed to his bed. “Moony, I left ‘Electric Warrior’ right there.”

“The one who gets up off his sorry arse gets to pick the music,” Remus answered, before picking up A Day at the Races and showing it off. Sirius smirked, obviously satisfied, but Mary gave a moan.

“This is blatant favouritism.”

Setting the needle down, he joined the circle once more while the album’s long intro gave way to one of his favourite guitar riffs of all time.

‘Ooh, ooh yeah, ooooh yeah,

Get your party gown;

Get your pigtail down,

Get your heart beatin’ baby;

Got my timin’ right,

Got my act all tight;

It’s gonna be tonight, my little school babe!’

As Remus rejoined the circle, Sirius reached an arm out and looped it around his neck, drawing him so close he could smell the whisky on his breath. “Favouritism or no, you gotta admit, Moony has taste.”

"I wish there was actual room to dance," Lottie complained. "Potter when you're dorm monitor, I expect at least one party every week."

"You can't afford a party every week, what with the way you drink," Peter said.

"Ugh. Really, do you always have to be such a milksop, Petey?"

“I know what we can do! We should play a game!” Mary announced, before covering her mouth to hide a rather unladylike belch.

“Noooo,” Remus laughed immediately. "Please, not again. I can't play another silly truth or dare game."

“I don’t see why not,” Marlene teased, “after all, it is our last night together.”

"Yeah, c'mon Moons," James pushed. "Just one round."

“It doesn’t have to be truth or dare,” Lottie said comfortingly.
