“The trick! The trick!” Sirius urged. “That one you showed me once! Remember, back in the astronomy building?”

It took Remus several seconds to understand what Sirius was going on about. When it finally clicked, he nodded and raised his fist. Every kid around them seemed to lean in out of anticipation, but Remus had seen the trick loads of times. It’d been Lee who’d taught him.

Taking the zippo in his other hand, he formed a small chamber with his fist and held the button down so the gas could build up in the small space.

“Watch this, this is the cool bit,” Sirius said to the guy next to him.

After a few seconds, Remus struck the lighter and opened his fist. What followed was a small burst of flame like a tiny fireball, right there in the centre of his palm. Every zooted kid within ten feet gave a loud ‘OOOH!’ and then suddenly they were all clapping.

“Yes! That’s my Moony!” Sirius cried, as Remus wiped his palm on his shirt, just thankful he didn’t light himself on fire. “Moony’s so cool, ‘e’s like magic. Just love ‘im, don’t you love ‘im?” He nudged the same guy as earlier, who gave a torpid nod, clearly high on his own shit. “Hey, Moony! I love ya!”

Remus’ heartbeat suddenly filled his ears. He began to feel itchy, like ants were crawling up his spine. “Sirius—”

“OH DAMN!”

The cry had gone up from the other side of the pool, where a group of guys were laughing and hollering, all of them pointing in the same direction. “FUCK YEAH, MATE!” They shouted. “JUMP!”

As much as Remus wanted to pause everything and peel out of his own skin, there wasn’t time. As a crowd quickly formed, he looked up to find James standing on the roof of the pool shed. Peter, when Remus chanced a look, was still playing poker.

“It’s like I can fly,” James said, much to the glee of his audience.

“You can’t fly, James!” Remus replied, trying his best in his muddled state to calculate the distance between the roof of the shed and the pool edge. Several feet, at least.

“No, I can do it. I’m sure I can fly.”

The crowd immediately took up a chant; “FLY! FLY!”

“YEAH, FLY!” Sirius yelled. Remus smacked him for it.

“Are you crazy? He’s gonna die.”

Sirius glanced between James and Remus like he was just seeing them for the first time. “Uh… Don’t jump, Prongs. Moony says not to jump.”

“Moony says to jump?”

“No! Don’t jump!” Remus shouted.

But the crowd was against him. “JUMP! JUMP!” It cried, fists beating the air with eager want. It didn’t matter if James ran the risk of splattering himself on the pool deck, they wanted a show. Remus wished he knew where Simeon was, but he didn’t, so instead he just began shoving his way through the gathered bodies, until his rubber legs had carried him up to the side of the tall shed.

“James, come down.”

James squinted down at him in the dark. He was missing his glasses. “That you, Moons?”

“Yes, it’s me. Now get down here.”

“JUMP! JUMP!”

“I dunno… I think I’m supposed to jump, Moons. They want me to jump.”

“JUMP! JUMP!”

“Think of Lily,” Remus pushed. “Would she want you to jump?”

“Don’t listen to him,” someone heckled. “Jump already.”

But James was hesitating. “I really miss Lily,” he moaned.

“Alright, then come down and we can call her.”

“Really?” James lit up. “You’d let me call her?”

“Yes, just come down now and we’ll phone ‘er up! I swear.” Remus reached up, itching his shoulders. The winking stars had returned, and he felt hot and cold all at once.

“JUMP! JUMP!” The crowd continued to chant. James was looking all around, like he couldn’t decide where the noise was coming from. He was so close to the edge of the shed now, and Remus didn’t think he’d be able to catch him if he fell.

“James don’t—”

“JUMP!”

“Just come—”

“I’M COMING, LILY!”

And then, with all the stupidity granted to him at birth and that collected along the way, James Potter launched himself off of the roof of the shed.

Remus almost covered his eyes, except he couldn’t feel his arms. Overhead, James soared, carried by the roaring cheers of his fans, and straight into the deep end of the pool. He’d cleared the edge with several feet to spare, but as his dark form sunk to the bottom and did not immediately resurface, everyone began to crowd in.

“He alive?” Someone asked.

“I dunno… you check.”

There were a few mumbled responses, all of them equally as unsure, and Remus felt his chest twinge. He’d forgotten to breathe. Luckily, Sirius was still his ever-loyal self, even when high.

“I’ll save ya, Prongs!” He declared, before letting out a victory cry and throwing himself into the pool. This of course ignited a rallying cry, and suddenly dozens of kids were throwing themselves into the water, clothes and all.

Remus waited with baited breath until Sirius and James finally emerged. When they did, he found them laughing, and suddenly furious, he picked up another discarded beer can and tossed it at James’ head before muttering under his breath that he needed to piss.

It turned out that for all the party’s expensive sound equipment and endless booze, they did not have anywhere to take a leak. “Try the woods,” a guy told him when he’d asked. Feeling irritable, Remus turned and made for the clearest crop of trees.

“Bloody friends… fuckers…” he grumbled to himself; “What’s the point of ‘em… keep ‘em around to… to give ya heart attacks! … Fucking idiots…”

Stopping before a suitable tree, Remus steadied himself and unzipped his trousers. He’d just gotten down to business when a snapping sound filled his ears. At first he thought he was just hearing things—a common side effect when one was dropping LSD—but then the sound came again, followed by the muffled sound of voices.

Almost sputtering, Remus scrambled to do up his trousers and flee, except his legs had gone rubbery again, and when he stepped back he caught his ankle on a tree root and went down hard on his side. Wincing, he looked up, and just a few short feet away he found a couple in various states of undress, both of them rushing to adjust their clothes. It was dark amongst the trees, but Remus hadn’t really gone that far in, and when his eyes finally focused, he found not just a regular couple, but a couple of men. And not only that, one of them was Simeon.

“Oh shit,” Simeon said, when he realised who had caught them.

“Who’s he?!” The other guy demanded. It was Guy… or Hugh. Remus still couldn’t tell.

“Relax. I’ll handle it,” Simeon replied cuttingly. He’d only just managed to get his flared trousers back on, and his shirt hung open revealing his entire chest.

“Here, Remus, let me help you up,” Simeon said, coming forward and grabbing Remus under one arm. Without bothering to wait for his friend, Simeon began leading him back toward the house. “Wow… You sure gave us a fright,” Simeon said, forcing a chuckle.

“Didn’t mean to… Only taking a piss,” Remus murmured. He wanted to pull away; Simeon’s touch felt like pins and needles, but he was holding onto his bicep with an iron grip. “Didn’t see anythin’ really…”

“Sure you didn’t. But that’s alright.” Simeon was smiling, but it didn’t reach his eyes. Just as they reached the start of the lawn, he stopped and made Remus face him. “Remus, I know you might be thinking that—”

“I didn’t know you were gay,” Remus flubbed, stupidly.

Simeon’s gave a light chuff, like an almost-laugh. “I’m… not, but…”

That’s what they all say, Remus thought. He let his head rock back, blinking at the stars that winked for him. Puddles, puddles…

“Remus, this is a sensitive thing,” Simeon started. “People really can’t know that Hugh and I… hold on, Remus are you alright?”

“I drank from the blue cup.”

He began popping his lips, creating that little sound of a bursting bubble. He did it in time with the winking stars. Bop, bop, bop…

“Fucking hell…” Simeon shook his head, but he was smiling genuinely now. “Remus—Remus, look at me.”

Remus did.

“You can’t tell anyone. This has to be our little secret, alright? Maybe if it were someone else and not Hugh it could be different, but it’s not so… you can’t tell anyone. Do you understand?”

Bop, bop, bop…

“Remus? Did you hear me?”

“Yup,” he replied, popping the ‘p’. “Ourrrrr little secret…”

“Yes, our secret. No one else’s. Especially not Peter.”

Remus nodded. He didn’t want to tell Peter either. Or James, really. “Revere the closet…”

Simeon gave him an odd look, like he was puzzled but still amused, and finally nodded. “You always were funny,” he said, before hugging Remus and finishing with a quick peck on the cheek. “I’m gonna now. Shouldn’t leave Hugh to wonder, he’s a fretter. But remember, Remus—it’s our secret.”

“Our secret!”

Simeon waved him off, and then he was gone again, and Remus was as high as ever.

That was a development, the voice said, as he stumbled back toward the pool. It felt closer when he was stoned, like a real voice whispering in his ear rather than just his head. Remus swatted at the air over his shoulders.

Go away, Remus replied, stopping to lean on the side of the pool shed.

And where would I go?

I hate you.

I am you.

Suddenly he was itchy all over again. Remus regretted drinking from that blue cup. He’d heard Tomny say it before—bad trip. The moment when the good drug turns on you and everything becomes ten times as shitty as when you’d been sober. Tomny was the best at those, he’d experienced every bad trip in the book, and one time, when Remus was fourteen and had gotten fucked out of his head on mushrooms, it’d been Tomny who’d kept him grounded. He’d watched over him. It was just how it was. Now Remus was watching others, except he wasn’t any good at it. He didn’t know how to guide them through their downs, or even cheer them on during their highs. He was too miserable. He wanted Tomny.

Tomny.

“Tom.”

Tomny.

“Oi, Tom!”

Remus pushed the hallucination away. It was the voice again, taunting him with the one thing he couldn’t have. “Shut up, leave me alone,” he moaned, slamming his fist on the shed’s metal wall.

“Pfft. Skaghead,” a voice muttered disdainfully, passing him from behind. “Tom!” The guy barked. “Time tah go. Got the rich twat’s dosh so we’re outta ‘ere.”

“Yeah, yeah, hold on. Gonna find me that girl from before.”

“Plonker, as if that blue-blood bitch’s gonna want anythin' tah do wiff you.”

“Just admit ya don’t have any game and lighten up, alright Brecker?”

It was the ‘r’… The ‘r’ in Brecker. That’s what really gave him away. It was that touch of intonation, the hint of a Scottish drawl he’d all but lost since childhood.

Remus looked up. He thought he might vomit. There he was. Just… right there, a mere few feet in front of him.

Tomny.

“Diddya even see where she went?” Brecker asked, scanning the pool. His head was shaved nearly to the skin, and he had a nasty look about him. But not Tomny; Tomny looked the exact same. Same dirty-blonde fringe, always dipping down into his eyes. Same dimples, same sea-glass eyes. Remus imagined if he were closer, he could’ve spotted that little scar on his upper lip.

“Nah, but I’ve an eye for things like these,” Tomny said, smirking devilishly.

It was as though Remus had forgotten how to breathe again. He used the shed’s wall to drag himself closer, repeating the name in his head in hopes that just one of them would reach his lips. Tomny. Tomny. Tomny.

“C’mon,” Brecker said, nudging Tomny’s arm; “I’m tired of these rich prigs and I don' need Lee takin' off wiff the car.”

Lee!

"I told you we should've left 'im back at my place," Tomny said.

Oh god—Lee and Tomny. The flat! He must've been dreaming. But Remus was so close; he reached out.

Brecker spotted him first. Spinning around, he deflected Remus’ hand and scoffed. “Piss off, we don’t got no more, you zombie. Find your fix sumwhere else.”

Tomny began to turn. “C’mon, Brek, now that’s jus' bad business—” He froze. Remus couldn’t believe it. He saw him. He saw him.

“Christ…”

“Tom,” Remus whined.

“You know this guy?” Brecker demanded sharply. He looked Remus up and down, the same way someone like Lyall might had he seen Brecker on the street in all of his skinhead glory. Apprehension. Disgust.

“I…” Tomny shook his head in disbelief. “Lu… what are you fucking doing here?!”

Lu. Remus almost forgot how it felt to be called that. Relief surged over him like water, and he could finally speak again.

“S'a party,” he garbled; “I wassss invited. What'rrre youuu doin' 'ere?”

“It’s a job,” Brecker answered first. Tomny snapped his gaze to him, pressing his lips into a thin line.

“Brek, why don’t you jus' let me handle this one. I’ll... meet ya back at the car.”

Brecker looked like he wanted to argue, but no matter how much time had passed or where he’d gone, Tomny had always been a leader. It seemed that it still rang true now. After another suspicious glance at Remus, Brecker shambled off, hands in his pockets. Remus, who still hadn’t moved from the shed wall, leaned his forehead against it in attempts to ground himself. Everything was so muddled, and he wanted desperately to see Tomny clearly. To know that he wasn’t just seeing things.

“Are you really 'ere right now?” He whimpered, appreciating the touch of cool metal against his skin.

Tomny looked at him with sympathy—or pity, maybe. “Here, Lu,” he said, grasping Remus gently by the arms. “Let’s getchu sat down.”

He guided him back to the pool, to the very same spot Remus had been lying not ten minutes before. It was fate then, he decided. Mean, ironic fate. Remus looked around for his friends, but they’d gone. To where, he wasn’t sure, but somehow it fit. Thonas Armstrong simply did not exist in the same dimension as Sirius Black and James Potter.

“Feelin' any better?” Tomny asked, kneeling before him and eyeing Remus warily.

Remus ignored the question; “What arrrre... What are youuuu doin' ‘ere...?”

“Sellin' drugs to posh prats with money to burn,” Tomny said blandly. “Never thought I’d see you 'ere though… Never thought I’d see you again at all, actually.”

The comment stung a part of him that Remus couldn’t put words to. “I missed you,” he said.

“You’re drunk,” Tomny responded, “or high. Possibly both. Did ya take it on yer own or did someone dope ya?”

“I miss you,” Remus said again, pathetically. “I miss all of you guys. M'sorrrrry.”

Tomny turned a bit ashen. “C’mon, don’t… don’t say that.”

“Whatever I’ve done, m'sorryyyy.”

“Stop it, Lu.”

“M'sorry I lied to ev’ryone! I’ll—I'll tell the truth, all of it! Ngh… About my family and school and—”

“Stop!”

Remus held his tongue. Still kneeling, Tomny hung his head and then ran a hand across his face. “Look, I can’nah really do this right now,” he sighed. He stood then, biting his lip and looking at Remus like he were an injured puppy he’d picked up off the side of the road. And really, that was exactly what Remus was.

“I have to go,” Tomny said. “Don’t feel sorry, jus’… take care of yerself, Lu.”

Remus felt like crying. Maybe he already was.

“… Okay, Tom.”

Looking almost pained, Tomny raised a hand like he might pat him on the arm, but then he thought better of it. Instead he turned, and Remus had to watch his back as he crossed the courtyard and passed out of sight.

So close, and yet so far, vicious Moony said. Tell me, did you think he would just take you back? You knew he didn’t want you.

“No…”

Don’t be sad, darling, said Hope. Shall Mummy sing to you? Oh, where have you been…

Remus covered his ears. “Noooo…”

Who would want you back? said Tomny. You’re a liar. You loved my girlfriend, you didn’t love me.

“It ain’t true…”

No, he’s right, you even lie to yourself, said Sirius. I mean really, Remus Dean? Yeah right. You don’t know how to be honest. You’re bad, Moony. Bad to your core.

“Please… Please just stop…”

You want everything, said Lily. You have everything and you still want more. You’re selfish.

Where do you belong, Moony? said Peter. Do you belong anywhere? Anywhere at all?

“Stop it…”

‘Stop it, stop it’—just listen to him whine, said Marlene. It’s so hard when we refuse to get better. Why can’t you just get better, Remus?!

It’s ‘cause he’d rather run from it, said James. Are you fast enough, Moony? Better run—RUN!

“Stop it!”

He won’t run. He’s a quitter, said Lyall. He’s nameless. He’s a child. He doesn’t care.

And where have you been, my darling young one?

“STOP IT!”

“MOONY!”

Remus opened his eyes. Sirius was before him, kneeling in the same spot that Tomny had been. He was wet, with his dark hair curling around his forehead. He had both of Remus’ wrists in his hands, a look of concern stamped across his features.

“Moony, what’s goin' on? What's a’matter?”

Remus’ mouth opened, but no sound came out. I saw Tomny, he wanted to say. Tomny was here, and now he’s gone.

Sirius moved his hands—first to Remus’ cheeks, then his forehead. “Blimey, you’re soaked. Is this all sweat? Here, lie down.” Slowly, he manoeuvred Remus back onto the deck chair. Remus wanted to ask how he was so coherent, but the blinking stars were back with a vengeance, and it hurt just to keep his eyes open.

“I–I think m’havin’ a b-bad trip, Siri… uss...”

“O-Okay…” Sirius managed; “You jus' stay right here then. M'gonna go find Simeon.”

Sirius left him, racing off into the dark, and it occurred to Remus that Simeon might be rather tied up at the moment. Our little secret.

Remus had a secret. Secret–sss. Oh lord, did he have secrets.

“Sirius…” he moaned. “Sirius…”

He wished they’d never left the estate. He wished they’d run off just like Sirius had wanted; found a flat and played music for pennies. He wished he’d never seen Tomny. He wished he could see him again. He wished, he wished, he wished…

But wishes were for children, and Remus hadn’t been a child for a long time.





* * *





It was official.

Remus Lupin was lost.

He’d really only meant to go a short ways, just enough to punish his father. He’d thought that running away from the car when Lyall had stepped out for a quick meeting and Giles had been distracted by the paper would be a great idea. Maybe then his father would pay attention. Maybe then he’d yell at him, instead of just pretending he wasn’t there.

But now he was lost. He didn’t recognise any of the streets, and people gave him weird stares when he passed. A woman had even tried to talk to him, but she’d been wearing dirty clothes and had pigeons all over her, so Remus had fled in the other direction. That had gotten him even more lost, and he’d ended up wandering until he found a park with a play area. At least, Remus thought it was a play area. All of the bars were rusted or missing completely, and the metal slide had a hole in its middle as if it’d been melted right though. Only one swing remained and when Remus sat on it, tired from walking, he grasped the chain link and pinched the skin between his thumb and palm so badly that it immediately turned purple.

Cradling his hand to his chest, Remus felt like crying. He wished now that he hadn’t run. He wished Giles would just show up to take him home in the car, even if it earned him a week’s worth of punishments. He wished his father would come looking. He wished there was someone else left to miss him.

“Are you cryin’?”

Remus whipped his head up. A boy had appeared, obviously older than him, with a mop of shaggy blonde hair and an open cut on his top lip. He was wearing a dirty white shirt and jeans with a hole in each knee, and he was smoking. Remus was amazed. He’d never seen a kid smoke so openly before. At school, the other boys who were always smuggling their parents cigarettes in with them had to sneak around the back gym so they wouldn’t get caught by any of the teachers or nuns. They’d offered him one once, but the smoke had stung his eyes and made him cough terribly. Not this boy though, he wasn’t coughing. He took a drag on the cigarette and exhaled, like he’d been doing it all his life.

“Well?” He said again. “Are you cryin’ or not?”

“No!” Remus replied, embarrassed. He wiped his face. “M’not crying…”

“Are you lost?”

“No.”

“You look lost.”

Remus clutched the swing’s chains, ignoring the sting in his palm. “I’m not!”

“Orright, so you’re not lost. What you doin’ ‘ere then?”

“I… I went for a walk!” Not a total lie.

“Bad place for a walk,” the boy said, bringing the cigarette to his lips again. “ ‘specially lookin’ like you. Kids like you get picked up round ‘ere. Big bad men come and take ‘em away and they never see their mummies and daddies again!”

“I don’t have a mummy,” Remus said, because he thought it might make him sound brave. “She died.”

“Mine too.”

“… Really?”

“Nah, I lied,” the boy said, smiling inexplicably. “Sorta wish she’d died though.”

Remus’ eyes widened. He’d never met such a boy.

“How old are you?”

“Almost twelve,” Remus answered. “How old are you?”

“Almos' sixteen.”

Wow, a teenager. Remus didn’t know any teenagers, that was unless you were counting that pair of nasty brothers, Jacob and Henry, which he didn’t. Remus hated those brothers. They only came over when their father organised meetings with Lyall and they always took his things, or made fun of his teeth, or called him names like ‘beanstalk’ and ‘nancy boy’. Last time they’d even held Remus down and marked up his copy of Magical Mystery Tour with a pocketknife. Giles had bought him a new one straight away, but Remus still hated them.

“What’s yer name?” The teenager asked.

“Remus.”

He snorted rudely. “What sorta name is that?”

Remus bristled. He hated when people made fun of his name. Especially mannerless boys like this one. “It’s my name,” he said. “What’s yours?”

“Tomny.”

“Tomny? And what sort of name is that?”

Tomny smiled, then he answered; “You’re posh.”

“Am not!”

“Sure are.”

Remus stood up from his swing. He wished he could hit Tomny. He’d done it once before—two months ago when Sidney Donahue had called him pitiful for only having one parent at home and using his driver like a second mum. It’d hurt his hand at the time, and Sidney had cried, but Remus had felt better.

“Are you gonna hit me, Remus?” Tomny asked, as if he could read his mind. “If yer gonna hit me, best be ready tah get hit back.”

“If I did, you’d deserve it. Now I want you to leave,” Remus said, thinking it was best to at least give the other boy a way out.

Tomny rubbed at his eye indifferently. “Nah, don’t think I will.”

“I was here first!”

“No, ye weren’t. I’ve been sittin’ ‘ere all this time, you jus’ didn’t notice me. Easy for people like you, always overlookin' people like us.”

Remus didn’t like what the boy was implying. That they were somehow different, that Remus was bad.

“Leave!” He barked.

“No.”

“I said leave!”

Tomny leaned in very close. “And I said—no.”

Remus couldn’t help it; all of his anger toward his father and his desperation over being lost bubbled to the surface at once. He brought up his fist, clipping Tomny on the edge of his jaw. Only, where Sidney had gone down immediately, Tomny simply glanced sideways, absorbing the punch. Then he lifted his own hand—the one without the cigarette—and hit Remus square in the cheek.

Remus went down onto his backside like a sack of bricks, shocked and bruised. Now he really wanted to cry.

“Yer lucky, that was my left,” Tomny said, rubbing his knuckles. Then he did something even more unexpected than the punch, he offered Remus his hand.

Remus stared at it, at the faint scars on his knuckles, the fingernails with dirt beneath them. He wondered if anyone had ever made Tomny wash his hands before he ate.

“Well, m'on then,” Tomny said, “don’t ‘ave all day.”

Shocked at himself, Remus slowly peeled his hand away from his swollen cheek and took Tomny’s. It was warm, and Tomny immediately pulled him to his feet, even helping to dust off Remus’ trousers.

“There, now the li'tel master’s all spick 'n span.” Smiling, Tomny bent down and picked up his cigarette, which he’d dropped. It was little more than a stub, but he re-lit it anyway using a cheap plastic lighter he pulled from his pocket. Then offered the cigarette to Remus too.

“Wanna try?”

Remus stared at it. Tomny had already socked him one, he didn’t want him to think he was frightened by a little smoking too, that would be lame. Readying himself, he took the cigarette and pinched it between two fingers, sucking in very sharply. The effect was an immediate burning sensation in his throat and chest. He began to hack and cough as Tomny plucked the cigarette from his fingers and finished it off.

“That was my las' one,” Tomny said, flicking the butt away as Remus continued to splutter. “Wanna go get sum more?”

When he could finally breathe again, Remus wiped the corner of his eyes. “You mean… with you?”

“Yeah! … Unless yer not finished with your walk, that is.”

Embarrassed again, Remus looked around. He was still lost, and certainly didn’t want to remain at the poor excuse for a play park.

“Okay,” he said.

Grinning, and revealing two deep-set dimples, Tomny turned and ushered him on. “You can call me Tom,” he said. “You got a nickname?”

Following, Remus shook his head.

“That’s rubbish, everyone’s got a nickname.”

“Not me.”

“Well, ya can’t go round 'ere callin’ yerself ‘Remus’, no one’ll take ya seriously. You need a tough name, one that says ‘don’t mess wiff me’.” Tomny began to stroke his chin. “Hmm… m’not really a fan of ‘Rem’. You?”

Remus shook his head. “Not ‘Rem’.”

“Orright. How ‘bout somethin' different then? I once knew a guy who called ‘imself ‘Bones’. You like that?”

Remus shook his head again. Tomny frowned. He probably thought Bones sounded very cool.

“Got a surname then?”

“Lupin.”

“Heh. Funny name.” Tomny snapped his fingers. “Oh, I know! M’gonna call you ‘Lu’, okay?”

‘Lu’. Loo… Wow.

“You like that?”

He nodded.

“Champ! Now lets getta move on,” Tomny called, already five paces ahead. “Find ourselves somethin' cool to do. Ever shoot bottle rockets at cars? It’s wicked fun.”

Remus didn’t know what a bottle rocket was, or where they might find such a thing, but his heart felt lighter somehow. He didn’t even care that Tomny had made fun of his name again. Tomny was nice, and not fake nice like everyone that visited the estate. Tomny was real. Remus hoped it made him real too.

“C’mon, Lu, this way!”

Remus glanced back at the dilapidated park. Suddenly it didn’t look so bad. His cheek no longer ached, and he didn’t even feel like crying anymore.

“… I’m coming! Wait for me, Tom!”



Chapter End Notes

Chapter title comes from the Scottish idiom "If wishes were horses, beggars might ride..." just in case you weren't sad enough already :^) Also, apologies to any Welsh readers for the sheep comment, lol.

'Hoover' is a vacuum.

'The Beeb' is slang for the BBC or 'British Broadcasting Corporation'.

'Offie' is slang for 'off license' or liquor store.

Calling 'bagsy' is same thing as calling shot-gun.

Woolworths was a supermarket chain.

'Cost a bomb' is an idiom for expensive.

'Molly' is slang for ecstasy and 'barbs' is slang for barbiturates.

'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds' is a ref to the Beatles song.

'Skaghead' is a derogatory term for anyone who abuses drugs; typically heroin though. 'Zombie' is the same.

I took inspo for the 'queer book' Remus reads from a real academic article published in a journal of psychology in 1975. It was very grim, but a strong window in on the societal thoughts of the past. I'm proud of how far we've come since. Let me know if you want the article's citation.

I realise the topics within this chapter may be triggering for some so in case you were looking for support, here is link to the Stonewall's list of international LGBT+ resources. Please reach out if you need it. https://www.stonewall.org.uk/our-work/international/international-resources

See you next chapter! (Final part of summer 1977.)





Chapter 71: The Boys at the End


Chapter Summary

End of summer, 1977. Remus leaves behind the Potters, among a few other things. Hawkings welcomes him back with an unexpected surprise.



Chapter Notes

C/W: Brief reference to self-harm (but NO actual self-harm, just a misunderstanding), and [unnamed] methods of conversion therapy. Also drug-use and subsequent withdrawal from it, homophobic language, and knives.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Though I know I’ll never lose affection,

For people and things that went before;

I know I’ll often stop and think about them,

In my life, I love you more…

- “In My Life” The Beatles, 1965



Waking up always sucked more when you couldn’t remember falling asleep, except in Remus’ case, he couldn’t even remember getting back to the Potters’. He learnt later that Sirius had in fact found Simeon—innocently drinking among a group of friends—and that Simeon had hailed them a cab. Only the two of them had left first; Peter had still been whacked off his arse and there was no way they could’ve taken him back home to his parents in such a state. He and James hung back with Simeon and followed later, but it’d been Sirius who’d dragged Remus across the Potters’ threshold, complaining of too much to drink, and then hauled him up to the bathroom where he'd promptly puked his guts out.

"You’re mental," Sirius had said while Remus hugged the toilet bowl. "My mental Moony." Then Remus could've sworn he'd heard the words, love you.

It could’ve been part of the dreams. Or the drugs. Or both, really. Getting high was the only way that the dreams would ever come out; the nights were colourless, while days remained all too exhaustive. It was like he was backwards. Wrong in all the right places.

When he could prise his eyes open, he found that the curtains in his room were still drawn, but Mrs. Potter had left his breakfast on his side table. Along with the tray was a note from Giles that said to call him the moment Remus was feeling human again so he could come retrieve him in time for school.

Ugh, school…

Remus supposed he had to be grateful. Neither Mr. or Mrs. Potter had mentioned what had transpired during the phone call with Sirius’ parents, but it was clear they weren’t going to allow Sirius not to return to Hawkings. Sirius wasn’t about to complain either; it wasn’t like he didn’t want to go back to school, he just wanted someone to care whether he did or not.

Unable to stomach the thought of eating, Remus drank greedily from the class of water Effie had left and turned back over in bed. He was alone for a while longer, gaze lost on the intricately carved wardrobe of peacock feathers. He'd expected Sirius to come knocking eventually but surprisingly, it was James who came to him first.

“Moony?” Peeking his head in, James knocked gently on the open door. “You feeling alright, mate?”

Remus grunted at him. His mouth tasted vile and his breath was probably worse, but he didn’t feel hungover in a sick sort of way, just drained mentally. LSD did that to you, left you feeling fleshly and benign, like a conscious tumour. There was a reason people lost themselves in it, even Remus felt tempted at times. But the trip had been bad, he knew that now. At least most of the energy and jitters from the night before had melted away, and the hallucinations had stopped. Thankfully.

“Not hungry?” James asked, coming in and surveying his untouched breakfast.

Remus sat up, holding his head. “No… feel like shit. You?”

James shrugged. "Feels sorta weird, like I'm still moving in slow motion, but Mum and Dad haven't really noticed. I did wake up absolutely famished though.” Sitting down on the edge of the bed, James illustrated this by picking up a piece of cold bacon from Remus' plate and gobbling it down. “Di’h yooh read yer no'h?” He asked over a full mouth.

Remus nodded, plucking the note from the bedside and ripping it into little pieces to keep his hands busy. “How mad was Giles?”

“Duh'no.” James swallowed. “But Mum said he was perfectly pleasant. Guess we’ll see when he comes to get you. If I were you, I’d give him the bell soon though.”

“Right.” That meant a stern lecture was in the cards, at minimum.

“Sirius said you got pretty out of it last night,” James said, speaking carefully like Remus was an eggshell he was trying not to crack. “What happened?”

“Bad trip, I'll wager.”

“What'd it feel like?" James asked, not unkindly, just more curious than anything. "Did you see things?”

Yes. And I heard them. Heard you—all of you.

“Well, it was acid, Prongs.”

James just laughed. “For me it was dancing zebras. They were everywhere. Then I met a wizard with this long white beard, and he offered me three wishes.”

“Isn’t that a genie?”

“Oi, it was my acid trip!”

Remus smiled. “What'd you wish for?”

“First, that Arsenal win the next Cup, then I think it was socks with my face on it—”

“You want to wear socks with your own face on it?”

“They were gonna be for you guys, obviously. Don’t really remember the third wish, but I think it involved less zebras.”

“Wish I’d met a wizard. I’d love to abracadabra some ‘a my problems away,” Remus sighed, then; “Is Sirius alright? He… hasn’t come to see me.”

“Only just got up, I think. Said he was gonna take a shower. You probably should too, by the way. There’s vomit on your shirt.”

Remus looked down at himself. “Ugh. Right…”

Nicking Remus’ second piece of bacon for good measure, James stood up from the bed and wiped his mouth. “I’ll leave a fresh shirt outside your door. Come down whenever you want.”

After his friend left him to clean himself up, Remus peeled off his dirty clothes and shoved them into the bottom of his bag. He didn’t want any more reminders of last night. Not the drugs, not what happened with Simeon (had it been Guy or Hugh? … Dammit.) and especially not of Tomny.

I can’t do this right now, Tomny had said. At the time it’d felt heartbreaking, but now Remus had the good and bitter sense to be angry. Why did Tomny always get the last word? Why did he always get to decide what was best? Remus might’ve been stoned out of his gourd, but he was still a person! He deserved to be heard… and now he almost regretted not forcing Tomny to listen.

Nudging open the bedroom door, Remus trudged down the hallway to the guest bathroom in just his trousers. He couldn’t hear the shower when he approached, but when he tried the door handle he found it locked.

“Sirius, are you in there?” He knocked. “Just need my toothbrush.”

There was a short clatter, followed by a hissed bout of cursing.

Remus raised a brow. “Sirius, you good?”

“Y-Yeah!” Sirius answered. “One sec…”

He waited, but the bathroom had fallen steadily quiet, and after several seconds Remus pressed his ear to the door.

“… Shit…”

“Sirius!” He called again. “Sirius, open up.”

No answer.

Swallowing, Remus forced the panic down and knocked twice; I’m okay, but again there was no answer. He knocked again; silence.

“Sirius,” he ordered in a stern voice, “if you don’t respond I’m going to have to knock the door down and bury you in white roses. Now I don’t care if you’re in the middle of pissing—open up.”

There was some shuffling and after a long, reluctant moment Sirius unlocked the door, peering out through the crack. He was dressed, with his leather jacket on and everything. “Red roses,” he murmured.

“Huh?”

“Bury me in red roses. I’m a traditionalist.”

Remus scoffed. “Bury yourself, ya bastard. Now what’s going on, you weren't really taking a leak, were you?”

“Moony, you’re indecent,” Sirius said, changing the subject. He reached one hand out to poke Remus in the centre of the chest, and Remus batted him away.

“Buzz off. My shirt was…” Remus tailed off. He’d glanced over Sirius’ shoulder and managed to catch sight of a green bag with a white cross on it sitting on the edge of the sink. “What’s that? Did you hurt yourself?”

Sirius whipped his hand back, squeezing the door shut even more. “It’s just a little cut, don’t worry about it.”

“Let me see.”

“No."

"Don't be a tosser, let me see."

Sirius scowled lightly. "I thought Prongs was supposed to be the mother hen?”

Remus ignored him; “Are you gonna let me in, or do I actually have to knock the door down?”

Looking reluctant, Sirius finally opened the door and allowed him inside. The guest bath was tinier than the others, painted sky-blue with a tiled ceiling and bearing a beach theme. A small basket of sea-shell shaped soaps sat on top of the toilet and a framed photo of the Potters’ beach house in Devon hung on the wall. The wallpaper had sailboats on it, and the shower curtain matched. It all felt so mundane, so expectedly homely. There was no way Lyall Lupin would’ve permitted such a room in his house. Sirius’ parents neither, Remus suspected.

“Okay, show me,” Remus said, eyeing the first aid kit. There were gauze pads in the sink, stained faintly with blood. Not enough to be alarming, but still not good. He faced Sirius, who’d shut the door and was leaning up against it with a grumpy frown.

“It’s not that big ‘a deal,” Sirius pouted.

“Why’d you let me inside then? Why'd you hide it?”

“Because you’re impossible.”

“Good. Anything to get you to listen. Now where’s this 'no big deal' of a cut?”

Grumbling a bit, Sirius sloughed off his jacket, revealing a red David Bowie t-shirt (a gift from the Potters) and a large bandage wrapped haphazardly around his arm. It stretched almost the entire length of his forearm and was wound so tightly that the skin on either side was pinched white.

“Jesus,” Remus swore, taking Sirius’ arm in his hand.

“It’s not that bad,” Sirius assured him, “I just suck at this stuff. Must’ve nicked myself last night, but I can’t really remember. Woke up with it.”

“You swear?”

Sirius gave him a funny look. “Well, I didn’t do it to myself, now did I?”

They just looked at each other, and Sirius’ expression changed.

“I didn’t,” he promised. “Swears.”

Remus licked his lips. “Okay,” he said. “Here, sit.”

Sirius did as he was bid, dropping down onto the toilet seat as Remus crouched in front of him and got to unwinding the bandage from his arm. Sirius exhaled as he did, and Remus shook his head.

“You are shite at this,” he taunted. He let the wrap flutter to the floor, before gently peeling back the layer of gauze beneath. Sirius had been right, the cut wasn’t too nasty, mostly a surface graze, but it ran from the tip of his elbow to his wrist and had obviously dried messily overnight. When Remus prodded the skin around it, Sirius winced.

"Reckon it was that gate," he said. "The metal one, on our way out. Probably caught it when I was guiding you out."

Remus bit his lip. "Thanks for that, by the way..."

"Don't need to thank me, you just had a bad trip, that's all," Sirius said softly. "I mean, what else are friends for besides picking each other up when we're tossed as a salad?"

I love you, Remus thought intrusively. It wasn't a 'friendly' thought, it was something else. Sirius had saved him, in more ways than one, and Remus loved him for it. He wished he could tell him just how much.

“Doesn’t look like it’ll need stitches, but you should've cleaned it better. It could get infected," Remus chastised, scooping up the extra gauze and throwing it in the bin. "You can show Mrs. Potter later if it still hurts, just keep pressure on it for now.” Popping up to wash his hands, he quickly dried them on a towel embroidered with smiling starfish, and began rifling around through the first aid kit.

"School in a few days..." Sirius said, like he couldn't think of anything else to talk about.

"Yup..."

"Going back to your place today then?"

"Mhm. Gonna call Giles after this."

Sirius nodded silently, and Remus knelt back down before him. Using an alcohol swab, he began cleaning the area while Sirius squirmed on the toilet seat, hissing through his teeth.

“Ugh, burns so good.”

“Don’t make it weird.”

“It’s not weird. You’re tending to my wounds like some soldier fresh from battle, it’s sexy.”

Remus glanced up, ripping into a fresh pack of gauze with his teeth. “Shuddup.”

“Knew you thought so too,” Sirius smirked.

Pressing the gauze to the newly-cleaned wound, Remus began wrapping the bandage around Sirius’ arm once more. “You’re an idiot, Sirius Black.”

“I love hearing you say my name.”

“You would.”

“Not like that,” Sirius scoffed. “It’s different with you. It’s like… you say it and it sounds completely different. No one says my name like you.”

Their eyes met again and Sirius held the gaze for a moment, before his eyes widened and he seemed to realise what he’d just said. “So,” he cleared his throat; “since when did you know so much about tending wounds of the flesh anyway?”

“I don’t, really,” Remus surmised, tucking the end of the bandage in by Sirius' wrist; “But I used to know this kid… Flacky. He was always getting himself into one mess or another. Even put his foot through a window this one time. I just cleaned him up a few times, s’all.”

“And who cleaned your wounds?”

Hm… Remus looked down.

“Aw shit,” Sirius sighed. “I… ignore me.”

Just tell him, Remus thought. Tell him so it doesn’t become another fucking secret.

“I saw Tomny yesterday.”

Sirius’ mouth dropped open, then he closed it. “Nah, now you're having me on.”

“I’m not. I saw him.”

“Actually?! Where—At the football game?”

“No, at the party. He was there.”

“What? What would he be doing there?”

“ … Selling drugs.”

Sirius raised both eyebrows, and Remus immediately regretted telling the truth. How could he not get the wrong idea about Tomny now? Then again, what even was the right idea? They both seemed so different now, Tomny and him.

“You know, you got down pretty bad yesterday,” Sirius said quietly. “You were rambling a lot. Are you sure you’re remembering things right?”

Remus didn’t miss his meaning. “Reckon it was drugs, do ya? That he wasn’t really there at all, and I just dreamed the whole thing up?”

“No! S’just…” Biting his lip, Sirius leaned in. “M-Maybe you didn’t actually see him, maybe you just thought you did. There was a lot of people around after all, and we were all pretty fucked up, right?”

“I didn’t imagine him,” Remus replied sharply. “He was there. Right there in front of me. I talked to him—he… He was there, Sirius.”

“Alright, I believe you." Sirius picked at his bandage sorely. "But what are you gonna do about it?”

Remus sat back, stretching out until his back met the bathroom wall. “Nothing, I guess. It wasn’t like he suddenly wanted me back. Didn’t even know I was gonna be there so…”

Sirius moved on from the bandage and began rubbing his fingers together, in that fidgeting way of his that meant something was wrong. “Well… perhaps it’s a good thing? Like maybe now you can put it all behind you. Focus on the good things—the stuff that matters!”

He’s saying you’re a shit friend, the vicious Moony suggested, none-too-kindly; Imagine if he was always going on about Miles, would that not smart some, Moooooony?

“Yeah,” Remus mumbled; “You’re right… probably time to put it to rest anyway.”

Sirius nodded eagerly, coming down from the toilet to join Remus on the bathroom floor. “Yeah! And then maybe that way we could…” He trailed off, looking uncomfortable. “Aw fuck, I can’t do this anymore… I’m sorry, Moony.”

“For what?” Remus felt his heart quicken. It was too like Tomny. Too similar to what he’d said. Was Sirius about to break up with him? Could you even break up if you weren't dating in the first place?

“I messed up,” Sirius said solemnly. “You asked me to do something and I bungled it all and… I’m just really bloody sorry.”

“I don’t understand.”

Looking straight pained now, Sirius reached for his jacket, drawing it into his lap. “I never really did tell you everything about that school in Belgium.”

Suddenly, Remus’ stomach plummeted.

“It wasn’t exactly a normal school,” Sirius said grimly. “They called it ‘therapy’. You see, before they sent me there, Mum and I had this huge fight. She’d gone through my room, and she found some stuff. Mostly cigarettes, a few records… and uh…” Sirius licked his lips; “a dirty magazine or two.”

“Bet she loved that,” Remus replied, humourlessly.

“Yeah well, I'll wager she might’ve actually preferred it if it were only tits and snatch.”

“You mean it was…” Realisation dawned upon Remus. “Oh.”

“The magazines were old as dust anyway,” Sirius scoffed half-heartedly. “I found ‘em when I was a kid, in one of the maid’s rooms, and I dunno… I guess I just kept them. I wasn't all stupid though, knew enough to know that looking at guys like that was generally frowned upon by society, so I hid ‘em under a loose floorboard in the corner of my room. It was the only hiding place she’d never found, but this time I forgot to put the board back all the way. Rookie fucking mistake. She’s got a nose like one of your dad’s hounds, right, so of course she found it. She demanded the truth and I… Fuck, I dunno—I told her? ... I think I just wanted to shock her. But hey, it worked. She smacked me, which meant I got what I wanted, and then there I was—off to that fucking school a few days later…Just one and done…”

“What was it like?” Remus asked after a long moment. "If you... want to talk about it, that is." A part of him was afraid of the answer, but he had to know, and Sirius deserved to let it out if he wanted to.

Looking indifferent, Sirius busied himself by picking at a crack in his jacket’s leather sleeve. “Well, apparently Belgium’s supposed to be pretty progressive, but I suppose there’s always gonna be a few cracks in the system. The school was run by some Evangelical from Merseyside anyway. He preached for hours about how ‘God still loves us’ and ‘we’re not broken, we’re just lost on the path to righteousness’. I mean fuck, it was like talking to Father Minsin if he was secretly a bloody poof. I figure most priests are, like you’d have to be, to be that horny for Jesus, but still.”

Remus suddenly felt like he were splintering inside. He couldn’t even imagine how Sirius felt. “Are you okay?” He asked, another stupid question.

“I’m fine,” Sirius replied. “Honestly, I think I got off easy. This other kid I met there, Jeremy, he’d been to three different places before that one. Said they beat you and starve you elsewhere, until you so gone and mental that you're writing bible verses on the wall—total mind-fuck stuff. This place just made us go to church all hours and locked us in our rooms like little kiddies if we were bad.” He rubbed his nose. “I thought it might be harder once I broke out, but you came and I was… I was alright again. Really, I was. I just wish I’d run earlier, so that none of it would’ve happened.”

Remus shook his head. “Don’t think like that. It wasn’t your fault.”

Sirius shrugged. “This wasn’t my first time running away, ya know.”

“You mean when you came to the Potters’.”

“Yeah, got a real beating for that one, but that wasn’t even the first either. Once when I was twelve I got as far as Chippenham, but I had no idea what I was doing. I’d run away after some dinner where Mum had yelled at me in front of the whole family—didn’t even bring a bag. Eventually I just turned around… stupid… And then when I was fourteen I stowed away on this lorry all the way to Newbury, right? Well, the guy found me when he stopped at a petrol station and made me call my parents from the payphone. I didn’t even fight him, I just did it. Sucks now… but you know, every time it happened I sorta thought to myself, ‘this is it, I’m finally gonna get out’ and then things would start to feel real again and I always went back. Hard not to think that if I’d been braver maybe I could’ve actually changed some of it.”

“No,” Remus said firmly; “Just because you turned around doesn’t mean you weren’t brave. If anything, I think going back took more bravery than leaving.”

“How is it you always know just the right thing to say?” Sirius asked sadly.

“I don’t,” he confessed. “I’m only trying the best I can, just like everyone else.”

Leaning towards him, Sirius pressed a gentle kiss against Remus’ lips and pulled back, stroking his cheek. “You should put that into a song,” he said.

“I’m sure somebody already has.”

“No.” Sirius shook his head. “Not the way you’d write it. I want to hear Remus Lupin’s songs.”

Remus kissed him back. “Only if I get to hear yours too.”

Sirius cracked a smile, before his eyes dropped and he pulled away. “There’s... There is something else, Moony.” Slowly, Sirius slowly began palming his jacket again, turning it over in his lap. “I really am sorry,” he whispered, reaching into the inner pocket. A moment later he withdrew a rumpled piece of paper, the same one James had found in his jean pocket the day before. Up close, Remus could see that not only was it worn and tattered, but also been charred on one end, like someone had tossed it into a bonfire and thought to save it at the last second.

“I’d hid it under the floorboard,” Sirius blubbered, more emotional than ever. “I thought I’d hidden everything well enough a’course, but she still found it and she—she threw it into… Oh god, I’m so sorry.”

Looking into his face, Remus then realised what exactly it was. Instantly numb all over, he reached out and slowly took from Sirius the blackened remains of Tonya’s letter. Unfolding it carefully, he saw that the top half was completely ruined, charred and unreadable.

“I almost told you that day on the roof,” Sirius said, “and I… I knew I should’ve given it back to you or even James before we left school! But I was worried he’d read it and misunderstand or—or that you’d make yourself sick obsessing over it all the time, so I thought it best to… but I was wrong. It was the only thing I managed to smuggle with me to Belgium—I’d never give it to her—but it got even more ruined and I’m… I’m so sorry.”

Trying his best to stave off the despair suddenly clouding every thought, Remus clutched the letter. The top may be gone, but he could just make out the end. Smoothing out the paper’s rumpled edges, he read it over.



Don’t let Tomny stay angry, it read; I love him too. I loved him enough to stay but I love him even enough to leave. And I’m sorry I couldn’t give him anything. It’s just just not how we work. He’ll understand what I mean.

I have to go now, sweet love. Be safe, be healthy, and please be happy, whatever that means. And don’t ever anyone—ever—tell you what that means.

Love forever,

Tonya.



Remus lowered the letter.

“Now that’s… just bad luck.”

“Fuck, Moony!” Sirius moaned. “Don’t do that! Don’t be so good! Yell at me—hit me—do something!”

“I’m not going to hit you, Sirius,” Remus replied sadly.

“Why not?” He demanded. “You trusted me with this one thing—one thing—and I let it get ruined! It was your last bit of her and I wasn’t even man enough to tell you when you came and saved my sorry arse, so why won’t you do anything?”

“Because I’m sad. And because I’m sorry too.”

“Moony—”

“—I’m sorry that I never told you how much I love you.”

The barest breath of a gasp left Sirius’ lips. Again, Remus felt like throwing up. Baring your soul was so hard, but…

“You make me so happy, Sirius,” he said. “You have a light inside you that makes everything sing. Your family may not see it, but I do—so do the Potters. It's like... if James is colour, then you’re sound. And I want to listen to you forever. Every soul-crushing pun or joke at my own bloody expense. All of them. You see, this—” he held up the ruined letter; “This is a memory. It’s not me. You’re me—you are. No one has ever made me feel like you do. Not Tonya… not even Tomny. And god… I like you so much.”

Sirius was looking at him with a wet, glassy stare. A bit of his newly-sheared fringe fell across his eyes and he sniffed as he pushed it away. “Dammit, Moony…”

“I can’t promise that I’m not gonna absolutely bollix everything up, because I probably will—I have been,” Remus said; “but I had to let you know. Had to. It's the truth, and the rest of it is this: I’m not good, Sirius, not good by half, but you make me better. And I want to be with you, I do. Even if I'm a coward who can't tell anyone, I want you. “You deserved to know. I'm sorry.”

"No," Sirius said, smiling through whatever sadness. “Don't say you're sorry—say it again."

"Say..." Remus opened his mouth, and then closed it again. "That I'm in love with you?"

Sirius smacked him in the arm. "Don't make it a question this time around, you shithead! I mean, really—I’m sound? What the fuck, you romantic bastard, how am I supposed to follow that?!”

As he continued swearing like a sailor, Remus caught Sirius by the arm, pulling him in for a desperate kiss. “Tell me whatever you want,” he murmured against his lips. “Tell me the truth.”

“The truth?” Sirius pulled away, wiping under his eyes. “The truth is that I don’t half bloody like you, Moons... I love you.”

Please be happy, Tonya had written. And don’t ever anyone—ever—tell you what that means.

Okay, Ton, Remus thought; I’m happy. Hope you are too.

And because he was happy, Remus took a breath, then another. Then he balled up Tonya’s letter, reached across the bathroom, threw it into the toilet, and flushed it away.

“MOONS!” Sirius barked, scrambling to reach the toilet bowl. “What are you doing?!”

Inexplicably, Remus laughed. “Unless you’re going to throw-up, stop hugging the bog. That’s nasty.”

Still horrified, Sirius spun round and smacked him in the arm, this time much more forcefully.

“OW!” Remus winced. “What happened to loving me?”

“How could you do that? It was your letter! She—She was—!”

“It’s only a letter,” Remus sighed, slouching back against the wall. “Just because it’s gone, doesn’t mean I’m going to suddenly forget what it meant to me. If things were that easy, I would’ve burned every record I’ve ever owned by now.”

Sirius came away, and joined Remus with his back to the wall. “You won’t regret it?” He asked.

“Maybe one day,” he shrugged, “but right now I think I feel just fine.”

Sirius leaned his head against Remus' shoulder. "This is crazy, you know that? Us liking each other... Absolutely mental."

"You know me, 'Mental Moony'."

A dry chuckle; “I just mean, are you sure this is such a good idea? Like, I’ve got a lot of baggage.”

“And you’re talkin’ to the king of baggage.”

“Oh? Allow me to help lighten the load then.” Cheekily, Sirius slid his hand beneath Remus’ interlocking their fingers. Remus, unable to help himself, lifted his arm up and kissed the back of Sirius’ knuckles. Sirius watched him, and Remus let himself believe it was real yearning in his eyes.

Remus stroked the back of his hand with his thumb. “Won’t be for long. Three days. You guys follow on the first.”

“Oh.” Guys, as in—more than one. The dorm would be just as much James and Peter’s as theirs, which meant no more laze-about days in bed, snogging through breakfast. They’d be lucky to get away with holding hands under the table.

“Things are gonna be such shit at school,” Sirius grumbled.

“Can’t hide in the toilet forever.”

“Nope.”

“And I suppose it wouldn’t be smart to tell people.”

Remus looked away, too guilty to meet his lover's eye. He knew it wasn't what Sirius truly wanted—the hiding—but but he couldn't bring himself to say that everything would just be okay. He wasn't sure he'd be able to handle it; the extra voices in his head that would tell him all of the nasty things people would be thinking should they know the truth. He just... couldn't.

Right! Right, right, right...

“Exactly,” Remus said, relieved that the two of them were finally on the same page.
