Chapter 72: Eight Days a Week


Chapter Summary

The beginnings of the lads' final year at school, and things are... complicated.



Chapter Notes

A/N: This chapter picks up almost straight after the end of the last. Maybe re-read the final scene if it'll help you remember where we're at.

C/W: 'F' slur used in a smoking context.

Note for future of this fic: As the first chapter of year 13, I felt the need to inform you that this year goes heavily into Remus' experiences not just as a queer person but as someone who struggles with mental health. I hope it'll come across clearly, but in a thoughtful way, that Remus is bipolar and experiences symptoms of BPD (Borderline Personality Disorder). I don't really expect this to come as a shock, considering how I've built him/his experiences/his reactions until this point, but maybe it is if you're not as familiar with the signs and symptoms of either disorder. Going forward (and in the past) it'll become obvious that Remus experiences a lot of the same symptoms of Bipolar II disorder (though type 1 & 2 were not differentiated until the 90s). As a seventeen year-old who uses substances as a vice, it's not uncommon for Remus' mental health to take a turn during this point in his life. For anyone wary, I am taking this seriously, but please do not expect this to be an over-consuming part of the storyline. It is a part of Remus, it is not him entirely. There is no one "right way" to have a mental illness, and all experiences are valid.

Honestly I feel a little nervous putting this out there, since I don't want anyone to think I just 'threw it in for the drama'. Remus has been, and always will be this character, so please don't hesitate to send me any messages or ask questions in the comments. I look forward to the open discussion should there be one. Cheers, and enjoy!



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Oh! Darling, if you leave me,

I’ll never make it alone;

Believe me when I tell you,

I’ll never do you no harm;

Believe me darling…

- “Oh! Darling” The Beatles, 1969



Things literally couldn’t have been worse.

Initially, Remus had thought that his final year at school would be a quiet one. He’d certainly thrown a spanner into the works by kissing Tomny, but he’d yet to decide whether that really counted as cheating. He and Sirius hadn’t exactly ‘defined the relationship’, but they’d confessed. Was it emotional cheating then? Was that even a thing? He could’ve asked one of the girls, except that would entail an explanation, and he certainly didn’t have one of those. Remus tried reasoning with himself that the kiss with Tomny hadn’t meant anything—not really. It was more like a pile-up of emotions, like when you filled your teacup too full and a little spilled over the edge as you went to add the milk. It was a stupid analogy, but it was about all he could come up with, what with everything else going on.

First and foremost, there was Jillian. She'd insisted on sticking around, and with her came a gaggle of other prefects Remus had otherwise had very little interaction with beforehand. It turned out that, awkward wire braces or no, Jillian was the sort of popular that occurred in those kind of tight-knit, academically-driven circles. She seemed to have both a personal vendetta and admiration for Lily, for her academic skill and ability to corral even the worst botched jobs. Remus had already heard word of her success in subduing the likes of ‘James Potter and those other messers’ pittering through the other prefects, though news of this tended to grow quieter whenever they realised he was within ear-shot. Now this year, without Lily around, Jillian was free to take on full authority of the prefects. She stepped in like McGonagall had actually crowned her Head Girl, and no one seemed interested in fighting her on it, aside from Remus’ own prefect partner, that was.

“You don’t get to just switch the schedules around,” Regulus told her, after Jillian had tried to trade Remus’ timetable with another twelfth year so they’d be together during library duties.

“It’s not like it’s that big of a deal,” Jillian retorted. “You and Remus will just take the library rounds every other month, with me and Trish.”

“Professor McGonagall didn’t give you leave to do that,” Regulus scowled, snatching back the schedule and shoving it into Remus’ hands. Jillian appeared upset, but as she turned to complain of the younger boy’s rudeness to her friends, Remus made to catch up with him.

“Hey, thanks for that. Dunno what I’d do if I got stuck—”

“Don’t talk to me,” Regulus snapped, stomping off and bringing the conversation to an abrupt end.

That evening, as the prefects all gathered around the dining hall tables for supper, Remus reluctantly took up a spot at Jillian’s table. There was apparently some dull tradition about spending the first night getting to know your new partner, but he doubted he and Regulus were about to break away from the group to shoot the shit over a friendly game of cribbage. Or whatever Regulus did in his spare time. He had no idea.

“I feel for you, Remus, I really do,” Jillian said from her seat at his side. “He’s just so rude. I would’ve thought at least one Black brother would make it out with some manners.”

“Sirius has manners,” another prefect named Tracey said. “And he’s funny... handsome too.”

“Ooh, Trace, does this mean you’re really interested?”

Tracey blushed terribly. “I’m not! Besides, Sirius probably already has someone...”

“No way. He never dates anyone over the summers, right, Remus?”

"Hm."

“I’m sure Remus could give us the scoop," Jillian continued. "I mean, it’s not like Sirius is all that hard to come by, right? Nothing like his little brother. I’m not even sure Regulus had ever spoken to a girl—nicely, that is.”

Tracey giggled, but it was Trish who answered.

“I think yer being a bit quick to judge, meself,” she said, picking her teeth with a toothpick. “Regulus isnae that bad.”

A part of Remus was almost thankful for her support. It wasn’t like he wanted to comfort Regulus, but he couldn’t bring himself to participate in Jillian’s subterfuge, lest she begin to think he was interested in anything else she had to offer.

“Does that mean you’re interested in Regulus too, Trishy?” Jillian teased.

“Nah, I just ken when yer being a bitch.”

The look on Jillian’s face was priceless, and Remus almost broke, but as Trish began innocently sifting around in her pockets he managed to swallow his laughter with a bite of roasted ham. As he did, he glanced back at Regulus’ table. The other boy wasn’t looking at him, but Remus figured that if he had been, he’d just as readily draw a thumb across his neck in threat.

“Either o’ ye have a lighter?” Trish asked.

“No,” Jillian replied, scathingly.

“You, Looper?”

It took Remus a few seconds to realise she was talking to him. “Me?” He flubbed.

“Aye, you.”

“Uh…?”

“Do–you–have–a–lighter, my dear gowk?” Trish said again.

“Oh.” Reaching into his pocket, Remus passed the zippo over without a second thought. It wasn’t until Trish saluted him and left the table that he realised it was his good lighter, the engraved one Sirius and James had gifted him for his birthday. Hoping she could be trusted to return it, he pat his other pocket and was relieved to find that he still had the one Tomny had given him that morning for luck. Not that it’d been much help so far.

“Bit rude herself, that one is,” Tracey said.

Jillian huffed. “Don’t even try complaining. At least you don’t have to be her partner for the rest of the year.”

Trish’s balls of steel aside, Remus was almost jealous. He would’ve let Trish call him ‘gowk’ or ‘bawbag’ or whatever other Scottish jargon she wanted if it had meant that he could just switch partners. So far he’d yet to try anything so drastic, but as fate would have it, Professor McGonagall came strolling out of the kitchens, busy talking with one of the head cooks.

“Reckon we’ll get any new professors this year?” Tracey was saying. “I keep hoping Binns’ll finally retire. I can not sit through another year of his droning.”

“It’s Dr. Becker for me,” Jillian said. “He’s just so creepy. Darcy swore she caught him looking down her shirt once.” Sniggering, she tilted her head so she was back in Remus’ view. “Remus, you’re coming back to Byron after supper, yeah? We prefects always head there first night to catch up. We’ve got some booze too—Suzie nicked some of her dad’s sherry.”

“And Dustin’s even got some weed,” Tracey added, the picture of scandal.

Remus stood up from the table. “Be right back,” he muttered, before taking off after the Headmistress. He managed to catch up to her and the cook in the hallway, a large knot of dread forming in his stomach.

“Professor! Professor, I’m sorry, can I talk to you for a moment?”

Pausing to finish her conversation with the cook, Professor McGonagall then turned around and raised her head to him. “Hello, Mr. Lupin. What can I do for you?”

“It’s about our assignments,” Remus said, trying his best not to sound ungrateful. “I just think that it might be better if we—”

“Switched partners?” She interrupted, surreptitiously.

Since she was so clearly keen on the subject, Remus cut straight to the chase; “Regulus hates me,” he said. “In fact, I think he’d rather it be anyone other than me.”

“Mr. Lupin,” the Headmistress started, “what would you say if I told you that Mr. Black had already come to me confirming your suspicions?”

“You mean he actually admitted to hating me?”

McGonagall gave him a knowing smile. “I think this will be a valuable lesson for you both. Far too often, students at this school simply complain and get their way, but the two of you…” She tilted her head down to gaze at him over her spectacles; “I have real hope for.”

Remus felt like telling the Headmistress how seldom it was that he actually got his way, but he wasn’t quite at the level of grovelling just yet.

“So you’re not going to let us switch partners?”

McGonagall straightened up. “No, I don’t think I will. Now is there anything else?”

Remus ground his teeth together, and through them managed; “No… thank you, Professor.”

Because he couldn’t bring himself to walk back into the dining hall and face Jillian and Tracey, Remus made his way outside. He was hoping to find Trish and retrieve his lighter, but as he made his way out onto the pavement he found her long gone. Probably the smart thing too; Remus had already decided that the prefects were a bit too cliquey for his taste. So with nothing else to do, he walked. Doing so aimlessly brought back memories of his first year at Hawkings, when he’d walked and walked just to avoid having to return to his own dorm room. Remus imagined that if he’d gone back in time and told himself that he’d one day be in love with that stupid roommate of his, that his fifteen year-old self would’ve said to fuck right off. How could he be in love with such an intolerable bastard? Someone who played music at full-volume all hours and insisted on calling him names like ‘wolf-boy’ and ‘Moony’. But that was the reality of it; the Remus from back then and the Remus that was now were just separate enough to want different things.

And what is it you want now? Vicious Moony asked.

Sirius. Only Sirius.

But you kissed Tomny.

Remus stopped walking. He’d made it all the way to the library. It was going to be daylight for some time still, but he almost wished it were night. Night made confessions easier somehow.

I’m going to tell him, he decided, as he pulled open the library’s doors and slipped inside.

And if he hates you for it?

He won’t, was Remus’ first inclination, but really, who could know for sure?

The Hawkings library was quiet on an average day, thanks to its loyal librarian’s continued effort to oppose any and all tom-foolery within its sacred halls, but without any students mulling around, the hall was as silent as a grave. Ms. Pince was perhaps the only person the Marauders were actually afraid to cross. Her library had been unofficially declared off-limits ever since a seventh-year James and Sirius had thought it hilarious to release several jars of crickets into the romance section. They were lucky that McGonagall didn’t allow for corporal punishment, or Pince might’ve force-fed the tiny insects back to them.

“Made prefect this year, did you Mr. Lupin?” The librarian observed, after spotting him on his way in. Remus nodded, and after he declined her offer to help him find a book, Pince waved her hand in the direction of a cart of unshelved books. “Might as well make yourself useful then. Those are the new books purchased for this term. Put them away for me and I might just let you take one out a day early.”

He wasn’t all that tempted by the offer, but with nothing better to do and no desire to attend Jillian’s prefect party, Remus took the cart and began wheeling it off. Most of new texts and didn’t interest him, but he did come across a few feminist manifestos that Lily or Marlene might’ve found interesting. He was actually enjoying the mindless work, the up-and-down pacing of the aisles, until he’d neared the end and reached for the cart’s bottom shelf. Bending down, he retrieved what he assumed to be another mundane text full of haphazard facts and citations, but when he turned the book over, the words The History of Sexuality stared back at him.

Remus fumbled the book. It landed face down on the library floor with a thump and for several long seconds he couldn’t even move. It was like he was back in that bookstore in Fitzrovia, holding a queer book with a queer look on his face and being stared at by a man who knew nothing about him, and yet decided to judge anyway.

Fuck you, Remus wished he’d said. You don’t know me, fuck you!

Suddenly angry, Remus scooped up the book and shoved it onto a random shelf, spine facing in. He never wanted to see it again, never wanted to think about effeminate tendencies, or issues with temperament, or familial despondency ever again. Wasn’t it enough to just like someone? To make it through everything life threw at you and still be whole enough to love? It should be.

Pushing his cart away, Remus paused at the end of the aisle to collect himself. He could hear shuffling a row over and the last thing he needed was Ms. Pince to think that he’d been crying in the reference section. When he was suitably calm again, he rounded the corner and cleared his throat.

“I’ve finished with the—”

“JESUS F. CHOP—!” Sheila threw her arms up, scattering several books about the aisle. “Remus,” she wheezed, one hand pressed to her heart; “You nearly scared the daylights out of me!”

“Sorry,” he croaked, just as surprised to find her there. “Thought you were Ms. Pince.”

“You too,” she nodded. “I’m avoiding her actually, I’ve had these books out since May and she’s likely to have me drawn and quartered if I don't return them before term starts. Her wrath is not just reserved for students, you know.”

Almost smiling, Remus picked up one of the books that had slid toward his feet, The Memoirs of Hector Berlioz, and passed it over. The rest of the novels she carried were much the same; Living with Bach, Chopin’s Letters, Conversations with Camille Saint-Saëns.

“You’re in the wrong section,” he told her. “This is philosophy. Memoirs and biographies would be two rows over.”

“Explains so much. Couldn’t find ‘Vivaldi’ anywhere,” Sheila sighed. “I managed to swipe their record cards, but this bloody Dewey Decimal System still confounds me. Will you show me?”

He nodded and began backing up the aisle, leading the way.

“Did you have a good summer?” Sheila asked as they walked.

“Yeah,” Remus said, “I did. Got to spend it with Sirius, actually.”

“Ah, yes. I hear he’s living with the Potters now, right?”

Remus nodded. “His parents, well—uhm… I guess I’ll let him tell you, if he wants.”

“That’s probably best,” Sheila smiled.

“Was your summer good?”

“Yes, actually. It was very nice. Colin and I got away to the sea for a bit. It’s the only place that seems to make him feel better.”

“Is he sick...?”

Sheila nodded slowly, dark eyes scanning the shelves of books. “Quite so. He has something called Huntington’s disease. Have you ever heard of it?”

Remus shook his head, suddenly regretting that he’d asked.

“It attacks the nerves in the brain. In Colin’s case, he has to use a wheelchair, and it’s hard for him to… remember certain things. He was diagnosed several years ago, when you would’ve been very small. I used to take care of him myself, but this job offered the best benefits and insurance and Professor McGonagall allows me to visit him often. The hospice takes good care of him too, of course.”

“That’s, uh… good? I mean—”

Sheila chuckled, stopping alongside him at the end of the proper aisle. “No, no, Remus, I apologise. It must sound terribly dreary, but you should know that this is entirely normal for me. A disease like this, well, you just find a way to live with it. That’s what love is after all.”

Remus licked his lips. Right…

No one bothered them as they busied themselves with re-shelving the books. Sheila hadn’t mentioned the paper stitches on his cheek, though he could tell she’d noticed, and he had no trouble reaching the highest shelves. When all the books were returned to their rightful places, Sheila dusted her hands on a pair of daisy-embroidered dungarees. “You were very helpful today, Mr. Prefect,” she declared. “If there’s anything I can do to repay you, you need only ask.”

It was a jest, but Remus’ mind automatically shifted to his most recent problem.

“Actually…”

To her credit, Sheila did listen intently. After leaving the library behind, Remus ended up following her back toward the Bellchant building, ranting the entire way about the unfortunate circumstance of having Regulus Black for a partner.

“I’m telling you, it has to be a mistake! Some—Some sort of sick joke!”

“I’m not so sure Professor McGonagall makes mistakes,” Sheila hummed. “Now sick jokes, on the other hand…”

Remus frowned deeply. He hoped he looked pitiful, at least that way she might feel more inclined to sympathy and get him out of this mess.

“But why Regulus?”

Sheila smiled like she knew something he didn’t. “Why not?”

Teachers! He thought; Devils! All of them!

“I would’ve thought that you and Regulus would have plenty in common,” Sheila said, admiring the sun as it got ready to set over the horizon. “You’re both very talented musically, you both like to read, and of course there’s a one Mr. Black… is that not enough to simply remain cordial?”

Remus squeezed his eyes shut. How could he explain to his teacher that Sirius was exactly the reason they couldn’t be cordial?

“I’m sorry, Remus,” she said as they neared the music building, “but if you’ve already talked to Professor McGonagall and she’s said no, then I’m not sure I’d be of much help.”

He suppressed an eye-roll. “Yeah… I figured.”

“If I were you, I’d try focusing less on the things you can’t do, and more on those you can. If Regulus needs a partner, then be that partner. If he needs someone to ignore, be that too. And if he just needs a friend… well, I assume you know where I’m going with this.”

“And what if Regulus doesn’t need me at all?”

“Everyone needs someone,” Sheila replied. “As Schumann once said, ‘to send light into the darkness of men’s hearts, such is the duty of the artist’. Is there no one who inspires you?”

Remus looked away, defeated and comforted all at once. It was startling how she was able to do that, more startling still when he remembered how much he’d missed it.

“Wait right here,” Sheila told him, “I think I’ve just the thing to lift your spirits.”

Slipping a jangle of keys from her pocket, she disappeared into a back door of the music building, leaving Remus to kick the toe of his trainer against the pavement while he waited. When she returned, just as bright and smiley as before, she presented him with a large leather case, and the accompanying ‘64 Fender Jazz Bass it carried.

“Call it an early gift for the school year,” Sheila said, as Remus practically whooped at the sight of it. Taking the leather case from her, he set it down immediately and flipped the top, running his hands over the lovely sunburst pattern of it. The entire thing was just the right weight, the strings just the right thickness. Oh how he’d missed this.

“Thank you,” Remus said, honestly.

“Don’t waste it,” Sheila smiled, before shutting the door. As Remus locked the case and turned for home, it occurred to him that perhaps she wasn’t talking about the bass guitar.

Thursday 1 st September 1977





“Regulus, do you have that list of names N to S?”

“…”

“Regulus, did you hear me? I need the list.”

Remus turned around, in search of his partner, but Regulus just strode further away, white-knuckling his clipboard with fervent displeasure.

Glaring after him, Remus apologised to the tiny seventh year girl before stomping across the lawn in pursuit. “Look, I know you don’t like this any more than I do, but we’re supposed to be doing a job,” he lashed, weaving between kids as they filed off their buses and flew into the arms of friends they hadn’t seen for nine weeks. “Regulus!” He shouted again, easily catching up with him through the crowd. “We can try fighting McGonagall over the pairing again later, but for right now we just have to—”

“Piss off,” Regulus hissed.

Remus scoffed; “Now that’s not very eloquent. Sirius would’ve told me to go suck an egg or something.”

It was the wrong thing to say, but he wanted to say it anyway and he got the reaction he’d anticipated when Regulus spun around and snarled at him.

“Get fucked.”

Remus almost laughed. Maybe he and Sirius were related after all.

“At least give me the bloody list!” He barked, as Regulus scowled and stomped off again. Sighing, Remus reached up and pinched the bridge of his nose. Starting off term with a headache of such magnitude had really set the tone, but it was nothing compared to how it felt to hear Lily Evans shout his name from across the berm.

“Remus!” She called happily; “Hey, Remus!”

He spun about-face just in time to spot Lily and Marlene as they rushed towards him, trunks bungling along against their shins. Seeing his friend again looking so eager and spritely only served to ignite his past answer.

“Lily!” He cried, making her entire face light up. “LILY, HOW COULD YOU DO THIS TO ME?!”

Both girls hit the brakes only a few feet from him, but Remus was not deterred. He surged forward, leaning in until he and Lily were nearly nose-to-nose. “WHY?” He wailed. “WHY DO YOU HATE ME SO MUCH?!”

Her face split into a puzzled smile, which only drove Remus crazier. “What are you talking about?” She snorted. “And what happened to your f—”

“YOU’RE NOT A PREFECT!”

Lily blinked and sudden realisation came over her face. “Oh, Remus…”

Tuesday 13 th September 1977 – Two Weeks Later...





Remus was trying. He really was, but being partners with Regulus Black was like being partners with a brick wall. A brick wall that hated your guts, that was. The two of them had had their first real on-duty session as prefects just barely two weeks into term, and while they’d been given the job of organising and shredding all of the student records from the previous year’s outgoing alumni, Remus had been confined to a single corner of the room, where he was not permitted to touch so much as a stapler.

“I can help,” he said to Regulus.

“Piss off,” Regulus told him.

And so the hours passed, and by the time he was making his way back across campus for supper, Remus had gnawed his nails down to the quick out of boredom. Because that wasn’t enough, on his way into the dining hall he was pulled aside by a small group of prefect girls. Not Jillian, thankfully, but three eleventh years with hopefully looks on their faces.

“Do you know if Sirius has invited anyone to the village?” The mousy one in front asked.

Dear fucking lord, could he not catch a break for five minutes?!

“Sirius isn’t looking to date right now,” he told the girls, before leaving them distraught and bleary-eyed by the front doors.

Already annoyed and not all that interested in playing nice, Remus tried sitting diagonally from Lily at their usual dining table, budging in next to a very bewildered-looking Peter. Lily made a face when she noticed, which he ignored, and after calling his name—which he also ignored—she finally got up with her tray and moved directly across from him, forcing James out of his seat and onto Peter’s other side.

“Oi, enough with the musical chairs, some of us are trying to eat,” Peter complained.

“Blame Remus,” Lily huffed. “I can’t believe you’re still mad at me.”

“Of course I’m still mad at you,” Remus replied.

“Well, what can I do to make it up to you?”

“Have you got a time machine?”

Lily frowned deeply. “I’d do it with you if I could, you know I would! But I’ve got an extra seminar three days a week and I’m still taking Advanced Maths.”

“Is that supposed to make me feel better?”

“You’re really making Evans feel the burn today, aren’t you, Moons?” Sirius snarked from his seat beside him.

“Yeah,” James cooed; “Can’t you see how sorry she is?”

“Butt out,” he told them.

“I understand why you’re upset,” Lily said; “This is on me! I didn’t realise I hadn’t told you my plans. End of term felt so crazy last year, but if there’s anything I can do…?”

Giving her nothing, Remus went back to shredding his chicken piccata to bits. He understood better than anyone just how mental the last few weeks of school had been, but in between pranking and kissing his best friend, he’d still managed to let everyone know his plans for the following term. Surely Lily Evans deserved some punishment.

Before Lily could begin to whine some more, Jillian appeared at the end of their table, showing off her new lack of braces with a bright smile. “Remus,” she said, poking him, “are you almost ready to walk back to the dorms together?”

Remus dropped his fork, and both Peter and James made this sort of garbled noise of surprise as they chewed. The question was so bold, and she’d asked in front of an entire audience.

“Walk... together?” He squeaked. “Like the two of us?”

“Mhm! You said it’d be a great idea this morning.”

Remus wracked his brain. It was true—he had spoken to Jillian the morning, but she’d waylaid him during his free period, just as he was on his way to meet Sirius. He would’ve probably said yes to her hand in marriage if it’d gotten her to go away.

“I’m so sorry, Jill,” Lily cut-in, graciously, “but Remus agreed to help quiz me after supper, so I’m going to have to borrow him tonight. I hope you don’t mind.”

“Oh… No, not at all.” Jillian gave her a tight smile. “Next time then.”

Trying not to look too disappointed, she flashed all of them a small wave and quickly scuttled away.

“You’re welcome,” Lily said smugly.

“Uh-huh, sure. Next you’re gonna be dodging proposals.”

And if he doesn’t want the title then fine, we’ll take care of him, won’t we?”

Remus pressed his lips into a thin line. “Yeah, you’re both right.”

“It’s okay to be sorry,” James told him, reaching to pat Remus on the shoulder, “but those two have had plenty of spats. This ain’t the first and it won’t be the last, just sucks that you’re in the middle.”

As they all gathered their trays and returned them to the rubbish bins at the back of the room, Remus’ head began to throb. It hadn’t even occurred to him that he was in the middle. Regulus had just as much reason to hate him as he did his brother, though he was hardly Remus’ favourite person either. But James was right, they had to be loyal to Sirius. Regulus was never going to be their friend anyway.

“I’ll wait for Sirius,” Remus said, as they stopped outside the hallway toilet. The other two nodded him on, and as they left for the dorm, Remus leaned back against the wall. Peter’s words from earlier were nagging at him; it would be smartest to squash the Jillian problem before the trip into Craigtyre, but more than that, Remus was lagging behind on his promise. He’d meant to tell Sirius about the Tomny kiss ages ago, but the timing had never felt right.

“I’ll tell him tonight…” Remus mumbled to himself. And he would, he promised.

“You’re in the way.”

Remus looked up. Instantly he wanted to shout; first Barty and now Snape. The miserable boy was glaring scornfully at him with his arms crossed over his chest. It seemed like Snape had also grown over the summer, but included in that was his nose, which remained about two sizes too big for his face.

“Then go around me,” Remus snarled, indicating to the bathroom door with a jut of his head.

“Do you make it a habit to hang out around men’s toilets, Lupin?”

“Do you make it a habit of being such a twat?”

Snape started to sneer again, but before he could say anything, Remus remembered his newfound power.

“Detention,” he said.

Some of the colour drained from Snape’s face. “Since when—”

“Detention,” Remus said again, feeling his inside jacket pocket for the little pad of pink slips, “for harassing an on-duty prefect.”

“You’re—You’re not on duty!” Snape spluttered.

“You don’t know that. Now piss off before I make it two.” Whipping the pad out, Remus clicked his pen and quickly scribbled down over the top slip. As he tore it off and held it out to him, Snape flushed.

“Fuck you,” he snarled, snatching the paper. “It was a mistake making you a prefect.”

“Don’t I know it. Now shall I give you another?”

Snape lunged forward slightly like he might try something, but Remus only raised his pen in threat and he was forced to storm around him, straight into the bathroom. Feeling smug, Remus almost relaxed, until he remembered what he was doing outside the toilet in the first place.

“HEY!” He heard Snape scream, along with a severe banging noise. “You can’t smoke in here!”

“Shit,” Remus grunted, streaking inside. There he found Snape hammering his fist on one of the cubicle doors.

“Who’s in there?!” He demanded. “Get out here now!”

“Piss off!” The occupant called. Sirius.

“Dammit, Snape, why can’t you just stop bloody bothering people?” Remus demanded, marching up and getting between Snape and the bathroom stall.

“Ha!” Snape scoffed, leaping away from Remus like he had some sort of disease. “Alright sure, come on over now, Lupin! Let’s see you hand this crackhead idiot a pink slip!”

“Just get out!” Remus barked. “Or I’ll make sure you’re in detention until July!”

“You’re gonna regret this.”

“OUT!”

Scowling, Snape turned and retreated from the bathroom, leaving the air thick with cigarette smoke and unuttered insults. Remus let out a heavy sigh when he’d gone, and turned to gently rap his knuckles against the stall’s door twice.

“I’m okay,” Sirius answered, before opening the door a crack. “Just needed a break. Figures Snivelly would come knocking.”

“Can I come in?”

Sirius peered at him, before opening the door the rest of the way. It was tight inside the stall with the two of them, and the light overhead was busted, leaving them in an overcast blue-toned dimness. Sirius offered him his cigarette and Remus took it, breathing in deeply.

“Love you,” he said on the exhale.

In answer, Sirius arched a brow and Remus knew he was in trouble.

“You’re… upset about Jillian, aren’t you?”

“Wow. Am I that transparent?”

“I’ve tried talking to her.” He handed the cigarette back. “It’s the same for you, y’know. I keep having to deter girls who are losing their bloody minds over your new haircut.”

Sirius swept his fringe out of his eyes pointedly. “Okay sure, but it’s different with you.”

“How could it be different? I’ve always had to watch you with girls.”

“Those girls just like the idea of me. What I can give them, or how I’d make them look. Stewart and the rest—they actually like you.”

"That's not true."

"That’s love. At least that's how I see it."

“That’s a horrible way to think about love,” Remus frowned. “Do you think I like you like that?”

“Obviously not, since you’ve told exactly zero people.”

Remus reached up to rub the back of his neck. “That’s… probably not all true…”

Sirius pulled the cigarette away from his lips. “What? You mean you actually told one of the others?”

“Not exactly.”

“Then who?”

“I didn’t say anything about us really, but…” Remus dropped his arm. The toilet’s low lighting had made him think it’d be a good idea to say it there, but he and Sirius were nearly chest to chest. Barely enough space to breathe.

Sirius arched a single brow, impatient. “Are you waiting for an audience reaction or…?”

“I didn’t want to do this here,” Remus said, “and now you’re mad at me, so this probably isn’t the greatest idea in the first place, but yeah... I have something to tell you."

“Then stop beating around the bush and bloody tell me.”

“It—” he winced; “It might affect how you feel, y’know, about me… I wouldn’t even blame ya none if it did.”

“Spit it out, Moony, you’re making me nervous.”

Alright.

“I kissed Tomny.”

Sirius gave real pause. Then his eyebrows knit together in their centre, as though Remus were speaking a language he didn’t understand.

“What?”

“It wasn’t a real kiss,” Remus started, shaking his head so vigorously he banged it on the bathroom stall behind him. “Augh—Fuck! … Or I mean, it was a kiss, but it was different from how I kiss you.”

“Different kissing? How’s that?” Sirius demanded, biting anger seeping into his tone. “Do you measure it by the tongue’s depth? Or is there some richter scale for the ferocity with which you swap spit that I don’t know about?”

“It’s not like that—”

“Why wouldn’t you just tell me that you kissed him at that fucking party?! Why make me worry that you were losing your goddamn mind when really you were just happy to get your rocks off?”

“It wasn’t at the party!”

Sirius drew back, as much as he could in the tight space. “You kissed him when you went back there?”

“Yes,” Remus frowned. “But nothing happened, I swear. Will you let me start over so I can explain myself?”

Sirius crossed his arms, unusually calm. “Fine. Go on then, spin your tale.”

And so he did. He told Sirius everything, right there in that shitty student bathroom. From the trip home with Giles, to Lee and his dead brother—to Tomny in the churchyard and then all the way back to school again where he found out he’d be stuck with Regulus as a prefect partner for the foreseeable future. They were lucky supper had ended and no one was around to interrupt. Sirius never stopped him either, instead he’d clambered up onto the back of the toilet, boots perched on its seat as he leaned his chin on his hands and stared at the floor, the ceiling, the door—anywhere but at Remus.

“So it was an impulse?” He’d asked, when Remus had finally finished.

“Yeah.”

“Gotta be honest, not sure if that’s worse than if you’d actually meant it.”

“Yeah…”

Sirius began sucking on his bottom lip. “Do you love him?”

“No, not like that.”

“But you love me?”

“I do, I know I do,” Remus said truthfully. “I just made a mistake. It was like I was feeling everything all at once and I… Look, Sirius, I don’t know how to tell you how sorry I am.”

“Sure you do, you’ve been doing it for the last half an hour.”

“I need you to know that I mean it though,” he pushed, “and I know it might not make you feel any better, but Tomny didn’t kiss me back.”

“You’re right, that doesn’t make me feel better at all,” Sirius replied staunchly. “I’d rather he be madly gone for you, and know that you’d still pick me in the end—that’s Shakespeare! But how do I know any of that’s the truth? How do I know that if he hadn’t refused you, that you’d still be here with me?”

Remus frowned. “Because I… I love you.”

“Right.” Sirius sniffed, then wiped his nose. “Well, I’m gonna need a little while, I think. Sort myself out and all that. I'll wager you should probably do the same.”

“I don’t understand what you mean. Time for what?”

“Christ, I mean time to think—figure it out. Decide what it is we want.”

“But I want you.”

The answer felt so blatantly obvious that Remus found himself surprised when Sirius didn’t automatically reply with the same thing.

“Do you not want me?” He asked, terrified.

“Didn’t say that,” Sirius mumbled. “Just said I needed some time…”

Sirius stood up then, manoeuvring past Remus and unlocking the stall door. They’d been in there for so long that the sky outside had gone dark, dimming the room enough to leave shadows on their faces.

"For how long?" He asked, following Sirius out of the stall.

"I don't know. A while."

"Sure," he nodded quickly. “A little while then, s’not a problem. I’ll sort out all of the Jillian stuff too—for real. I just… Can you tell me long you need?”

“For fuck’s sake, Moony, I don’t know! There isn’t exactly a statute of limitations for this sort of shit…” Sirius began backing away slowly. “Just give me some space to think, alright?”

“Okay.” He said in a tight voice. “Sure, take—take your space. I’ll be here. Or—not like ‘here’ here, just… you know.”

Sirius looked him up and down, like he was trying to burn the sight of him into his memory. The he turned away.

The door squeaked as it swung closed after him.

It’ll be okay, Remus thought. He just needs time. It’ll be alright… It’ll be just fine…

He expected the voice to come to him, to provide some sort of jaded dialogue he could fight back against with his own feeble hope, but there was nothing. Just him and an empty bathroom.

Remus looked up at the bathroom window. The sky was still dark. He could not see the stars beyond the clouds, and as he craned his head to search for a hint of them, an insurmountable loneliness washed over him like a chill.

It’ll be alright...

Right?

Alone in the bathroom, Remus Lupin hugged himself tight.
