Chapter 73: On Dating


Chapter Summary

Stupid fucking idiots. Discoveries are afoot.



Chapter Notes

Don't lie, I know you're loving the drama ;)

CW: References to homosexuality (argument), vomit, & smoking.

Also, because I forgot last chapter: here's the Spotify playlist for Year 13. Enjoy!



See the end of the chapter for more notes



So messed up, I want you here,

In my room, I want you here;

Now we’re gonna be face-to-face,

And I’ll lay right down in my favourite place;

Now I wanna be your dog…

- “I Wanna Be Your Dog” The Stooges, 1969



Friday 16th September 1977





It was official then, Sirius was angry. Maybe livid, even. Aside from the fact that he was clearly keeping Remus at an arm’s length, Sirius had hardly spoken to him at all in the past few days. Remus tried telling himself that it was normal—whenever they’d fought in the past, they’d always needed space apart to find their way back together again. But as the hours turned into days and Sirius showed no inclination of returning to his side, Remus began to grow antsy.

“I hope the weather holds out for tomorrow, it’d be such a shame to get washed out during our first trip off campus,” Mary said, holding a hand over her eyes as she surveyed the dark grey clouds looming outside the common room window.

“Wear a mac and some boots, you’ll stay dry enough,” Marlene said blithely, her legs kicked up over the arm of a Rowena-blue armchair.

Mary spun around and seized the book she was reading, only to start fanning herself with its cover. “A mac and a pair of wellies do not make for a cute date ensemble, Marlene.”

“Give that back! Who even says it has to be a date anyway?”

“Uh—everyone? That’s literally what these weekends off in the village are for. In fact I wouldn’t be surprised if a group of parents banded together originally and commissioned them. How else are they supposed to ensure that their kiddies find themselves a fruitful match?”

“You’re insane.”

“And you’re naive. C’mon, you tell her, Remus.”

Remus looked up at the pair, only half listening. “Uh?”

“Tell Marls that one cannot look cute with their hair smashed beneath a rain bonnet.”

Remus just blinked, and Marlene reached over the back of her chair to snatch the book back. “Bring an umbrella then, you drama queen.”

As Mary primped her hair, smiling like a cat, Lily reached over and tapped Remus’ notebook with her pencil. “Remus, that one’s incorrect.”

“What? Oh.” He looked down and sighed. All afternoon he’d spent in the girls’ common room—just one of his new perks as a prefect—working on homework, and yet he’d barely made a dent in any of his assignments. But really, how could he be expected to focus on school when Sirius hated him?

He doesn’t hate you, Remus reminded himself; He just hates what you did. Give him time.

He’d been recounting similar thoughts ever since Tuesday, since their conversation in the bathroom. Before then he’d stupidly assumed that they were on the same wavelength, that they were both in love but acting consciously to ensure that no one ever came close to figuring it out . Now it was clear that Sirius expected more. He expected Remus to want whatever it was they had just as much as he—and Remus did! He just didn’t know how to prove it.

Am I not enough for you? He also wanted to demand of Sirius; Is it not enough to just have me? Is this love not enough?

God, how Remus was starting to hate love; it was the excruciating polarity of it all. Love made everything more complicated, it made you miss people, even when they were standing right next to you. It was like an endless sea, and he was the inexperienced sailor, adrift blindly amongst its waves. He didn’t have enough luck to bet on calm waters. He might’ve, except real luck didn’t favour selfish people.

And Remus was selfish. So horribly selfish that if someone were to cut him open, his bones might’ve been blacked with the sin of it. He’d always known he wasn’t a saint, but being with Sirius made him realise he was a worse person than he'd thought. He was selfish and greedy because he wanted all of it—he wanted the freedom to have Sirius with him, but also the secrecy of no one else knowing. He wanted that one more a million times over. He would’ve been willing to do almost anything to get it, except perhaps tell the truth.

I like you so much, but there’s always a limit, ain’t there?

It made him feel guilty, and the guilt made looking at Sirius hard, but it shouldn’t be hard for normal friends to look at one another, so Remus forced himself to do that too. That left him tired and depleted, like a skipping record. James had noticed—James, the real saint—and more than once during that first week of classes, he’d leaned across a desk or table and asked Remus if he were alright. Remus always appreciated the quiet tone in which James asked, and sometimes he even imagined telling him the truth;

No, I’m not alright. I’m not alright because I’m in love with my best friend—no not you, James—Sirius. I’m in love with Sirius Black and I can hardly bring myself to say it out loud when it’s just the two of us, so how could I say it in front of anyone else?

“I’m fine, just tired,” Remus would answer instead.

Lily noticed too—effervescently stubborn Lily—though she seemed to chalk it up to his general distaste of being a prefect and therefore current distaste of her. As she leaned back from Remus’ notebook, her expression read as worried. It’d been her idea to study together, and Remus had accepted because he couldn’t stand another afternoon of returning to his dorm room and not speaking to Sirius—but now he was starting to regret it. Lily fretted like Mrs. Potter, and yet somehow remained twice as overbearing.

“Are you sure you’re feeling alright?” She pressed, as Remus scratched out the incorrect answer and accidentally ripped a hole in the centre of his paper.

“Fine,” he grunted.

“I hope you’re not still angry with me over the prefect thing. You're not, right? What if I were to do all of your essays until Christmas?”

“I already told you, I’m not mad anymore,” he said tiredly. “You don’t have anything to make up for, Evans.”

“Liar!” Lily practically shrieked. “You’ve been sulking ever since we got back, so just let me do your essays and then you can call me ‘Lils’ again and everything’ll be fine!”

“I like doing my essays.”

“Ooooh! You—You’re Satan incarnate, Remus John Lupin!”

Maybe. But he doubted even Satan was as greedy as he was.

Obviously enjoying the show, Mary strolled up from behind and leaned down over Lily to hand her a tissue. “I thought you already solved his Jillian problem?”

Still pouting, Lily swatted at the tissue, not really needing it. “I didn’t work.”

“Well, what did you do?”

“Just never you mind.”

Mary shrugged, pulling out a chair at their table and sitting down. “Whatever. Do you want my advice?”

“ ‘No’,” all three of them answered at once.

“Rude. I was only going to suggest that if Remus really wanted the girl to leave him alone, he should try actually finding himself a girlfriend. I’d do it—for a little while, that is—except I just agreed to go to Craigtyre with Petyr Tarnowski, and I'd hate to double-book myself.”

“Because Petyr’s such a great catch,” Marlene mumbled from her chair.

Mary laughed; “Ha! Bitch—love you. But really, I do know a few girls who’d be interested. None of them are as crazy as Jillian either. Just say the word, Remus.”

“No thanks, Mary.”

She shrugged once more. “Suit yourself. I’m going to go find something less boring to do. Not that watching you lot do your homework isn’t terribly thrilling. C’mon, Marls.”

“But I’m reading.”

“And I’m a leo. So glad we had this conversation. Now, chop-chop!” Forcibly hauling Marlene to her feet, Mary beamed as she laced their arms together and led her best friend from the common room. Lily turned to watch them go, before glancing at the chalky grey sky outside.

“Mary’s right, I hope it doesn’t storm. We deserve a nice day in the village.”

Remus grunted, eyes busy boring a hole through his notebook.

“Have you given any thought to what you’d like to do tomorrow? Craigtyre’s pretty nice in the daylight too, you know.”

Another grunt.

“You could always come with James and me. He’s been talking about Madam Puddifoot’s, it’s this little tea shop. Of course there’s also Broomsticks. Some kids take boats out onto the local pond as well, and there’s shopping and—”

A sudden rapping came on the window next to their table, and both Remus and Lily looked up to find James standing outside with a goofy grin on his face. He was wearing his running clothes, with a thick red sweatband around his forehead.

“Speak of the devil,” Lily said, slipping out of her chair and unlatching the window. “Aren’t you freezing? Where’s your coat?”

“Nah, just about to go for a run, thought I’d check in on you two first,” James said. “Alright there, Moons?”

Remus waved him off, still scribbling down his notes.

“I was just inviting Remus to the village with us,” Lily professed loudly; “Isn’t that a fine idea, Potter?”

“Oh, sure!” James trilled. “ ‘Course you should come, Moony, with you there we can make it a real party. You, me, Lily, Peter, Moira, Sirius, and Nydia.”

That got Remus to look up.

“Nydia?” Lily echoed for him.

“Yeah, you know—Nydia Burke. She runs the theatre club? Her dad owns that crazy chain of bookstores based out of London. Anyway, she asked Sirius to go to the village with her this morning, so guess she’ll be tagging along too.” James craned his head to see past her. “Ain’t that great, Moons?”

Remus could only gape at him. “I–I…”

“At least we know Sirius is finally back to normal,” James kept on; “I was starting to worry about him—what with all this shit with his parents, and how often he’s been skiving off with you. Speaking ‘a you, is there anyone you got your eye on, Moons? Or are you flying solo again?”

Remus stood up from the table. “I have to use the toilet.”

He left before either of his friends could start asking questions, abandoning his school things and taking the back door out of the dorm. The wind nipped icily at the back of his neck in just his school jumper, but Remus barely noticed it. His mind was operating at warp speed, and he was dangerously close to crashing. Sirius said yes to Nydia? He actually agreed to a date with her? But he’s—? And we’re—!

Remus forced himself to take a breath. Maybe he was reading too much into it… Maybe it wasn’t a date at all! James had called it a group thing—but everyone else going was dating someone, weren’t they? No—yes? Fuck. He needed to hear it from Sirius. Even if they hadn’t talked probably in days—he would force the truth from his very lips if he had to.

Taking the back path to Godric, Remus stumbled into the dorm, trousers wet to the kneecaps from navigating through the tall grass. The stairs he took two at a time, only slipping once, and when he reached dorm 4A he fought to free his keys from his pocket and shove them home in the door’s lock.

“Sirius?!” He cried when he was finally dashing inside.

“Nope, just me,” Peter called, as the door fell shut with a decisive click. He sat up on his bed, setting a comic book aside, but when he took in the state of Remus, his eyes widened slightly. “Boy, you sure look wild. What’d you do to your trousers?”

“Have you seen Sirius?” Remus demanded, still breathless from the stairs.

“No, but I expect he’ll be back soon.” Peter checked his watch. “He’s gonna meet us for dinner. You’re coming right? James says you can’t survive on cigarettes and tea, you know.”

Remus spun away, too frantic to entertain Peter’s weak wit. Fully intent to storm the rest of the school until he found Sirius or even Nydia herself, Remus reached for the door, but before his palm could meet it, it swung open on its own to reveal Sirius Black stranding in the doorway.

“Ah!” Sirius gasped, surprised to find Remus standing so close. “Fuck, what are you doing, Moony?”

“I need to talk to you,” Remus said. “Now.”

In that great big brain of his, Sirius must’ve understood. His eyes flitted to Peter and he cleared his throat. “Uh... hey, Wormy? I think Moira’s downstairs looking for you.”

“She is? What for? I just saw her.”

“I dunno, but she seemed pretty mad. Something about a forgotten anniversary? I’d get a move on if I were you.”

"What anniversary?!" Already alarmed, Peter threw himself off his bed and was out the door without even grabbing his shoes. Sirius shut it after him and then turned to Remus, looking hapless.

“That should give us a few minutes,” he said. “What do you want to talk about?”

Remus threw his arms out. “Just… Nydia?!”

Sirius’ eyes slid away. “Oh. That.” He moved around Remus then, shrugging off his jacket and tossing it across his bed. “What’d you wanna know?”

“How ‘bout—what the actual fuck?”

He heard Sirius snort. “Still Moony…”

“Don’t gimme that shit,” Remus lashed. “Turn around and tell me the truth!”

Sirius spun around in front of the stereo. “What truth?”

“I don’t know! Maybe an explanation—a bloody excuse?!”

“I don’t have any excuses,” Sirius replied, in that same cutting tone he’d used in the bathroom. “Why would I need them? S’not like you and I are dating.”

“Dating—?!” Remus stopped himself. If he exploded now there’d be no calming down. “Alright,” he managed; “Why then? Why do this—why do it this way? Are you trying to punish me or something?”

“It’s not always about you.”

“Do you think this is gonna make it better? You just going out and snog—”

“I haven’t snogged anyone,” Sirius seethed. “You did.”

"It was a kiss!" Remus cried. "One kiss! And I fucked up royally, I know! But it didn’t mean anything! I just needed someone, and he was there.”

“And I was there—that very fucking morning!”

“I’m sorry!”

“No, you’re not!” Sirius said. “You’re… You’re ashamed of me.”

Remus’ eyes bulged. “What?”

“You’re ashamed to be seen with me.”

“Sirius, I’m seen with you every day!”

“Not like that!” Sirius threw his arms out, like he wanted to hit something but nothing would satisfy. “You know what I mean, you’re just playing thick ‘cause you want to be the victim here. You’d rather hold my hand under the bleedin’ table than let anyone know that you’re even slightly different!”

The words cut deep, possibly even more so because they were true. Remus swallowed his guilt. He was selfish, after all.

“Are you in love with her then—Nydia?”

“No, I’m not in love with her! But unlike you, she actually wants to be seen with me. She wants to hold my hand in public!”

“She’s a girl! She’s a girl and you said that you weren't even—”

“Oh, are you really the one to be policing my sexuality? Mr. ‘I like you but not like that’? You're such a bloody hypocrite. Since when does gender have anything to do with wanting to really be with someone anyway?”

“Since always!” Remus shouted. “Since forever. Since they sent Oscar fucking Wilde to the slammer for writing poetry to another man! I’m not embarrassed to be seen with you, I’m just a guy! I thought we’d agreed that that was enough? That it was what we both wanted?”

“You agreed,” Sirius retorted, “I just went along with it.”

It hurt, but Remus still fumed. How easy it was for Sirius to put all of the blame on him.

“This is so typical for you! ‘Moony, I did it for you’—‘Moony, we did it for you’!”

“Yeah well, this time I’m pretty sure you asked me for it!”

“So what now? We’re just over? You're gonna go off and date Nydia because I won't admit to being something I'm not?"

Sirius threw up an arm in exasperation, pointing at Remus viciously. “You know, that’s exactly what’s wrong with you! You say we, but really it's 'I'. 'I, me, mine'—Remus Lupin! It's like this every day, there never even was a ‘we’, not really! It was always 'us' and 'them'. Well, I'm fucking tired of it! I get to be 'them', as much as the next guy!"

"Who is them?!"

"Them—everyone! Everything you're afraid of! You can't admit what it is you really are, and now that I’ve branched out you act like you’re losing something!”

“I would say going out with someone else is a lot more than just ‘branching out’!”

“Call it what you want then, but remember, I asked you! I asked you if this is what you really wanted, and you said yes!”

“I said yes to you dating other girls?!”

“No! You said yes to keeping us a secret, and I said alright. You said we wouldn’t be boyfriends—I said alright! But I never said I’d just be okay with sitting back and being another one of your dirty little secrets! Shutting up and living blind and silent while you go crazy in your own bloody head!”

“Alright, sure,” Remus said, voice cracking slightly; “Go ahead, keep telling me everything that’s wrong with me. But remember, I also said that I loved you—and you said it back.”

“Yes, except you can’t even kiss me without looking over your shoulder first.”

“You want me to tell people, is that it? You want me to shout about us from the bloody rooftops?”

“I want you to want to!” Sirius cried, like a deep wound was opening within him. “That’s the difference, isn’t it?! I never expected you to just start coming out to everyone and their mother, but you’re ashamed of me! You’re no different from Miles!”

“Stop comparing me to him!” Remus wailed. “You do it constantly! Maybe not always out loud, but in your head—I can see it! You compare me to this guy that I don’t even know, and that you haven’t known since you were basically a fucking child! So tell me, Sirius, how can I live up to your imaginary idea of the ‘perfect man’—HOW?!”

“Don’t be a fucking coward for starters!”

Remus pressed a hand to his forehead. He was so tired, he hadn’t slept well the night before and shouting with Sirius always left him feeling like he had a gaping hole in his centre.

“Tell me you don’t want me to go out with Nydia,” Sirius said lowly. “Tell me, like you couldn’t with Kimmy. Or Stacy. Or Viv. Or Chas—”

“I’m sorry, if you could refrain from listing off all of your conquests, I actually have things to do between now and next Tuesday.”

“Fuck you,” Sirius spat. “I’m tired of you putting all your damage on me. I’ve got enough of my own.”

“That much is clear.”

Sirius waved him off angrily, snatching his jacket up from the bed. “Fine. Whatever, be miserable—keep your fucking secrets, but do it on your own.”

“Oh, I will!” Remus shouted, as Sirius marched around him toward the door. “And I hope you and Nydia have tons of fun together tomorrow!”

Sirius grabbed the door handle. “We will!” Then he slammed it, and Remus was alone again.

Because he couldn’t think of anything else to do, Remus padded into the bathroom and slammed the door himself. For a split second he thought he might be alright, but then it was like someone had taken a shovel to his insides, impaling him and bringing it all to the surface. Stomach heaving, he bent over the open toilet and expelled everything. It was disgusting. He couldn't tell if his eyes were watering or if he were actually crying. His ears burned, his entire face felt tight, and he was gripping the toilet bowl hard enough to chip fingernails.

When it was finally over, Remus sat back and breathed. Stomach acid still burned the back of his throat, and his nose was suddenly clogged. He didn't want to come apart right there on the bathroom floor, next to a bowl of his own vomit, and so he hauled himself up to the porcelain sink, where he tipped his head beneath the faucet and chugged deeply, desperate to rid himself of the taste. Afterwards, as he huffed, he splashed water on his face and neck. It didn’t soothe him, only made him wet, and as he leaned across the taps to stare at his own reflection in the mirror, Remus began to count. It was an old technique a school nurse had once advised when he’d have one of his outbursts; make a list of things that might calm him. It felt stupid but there was really nothing else to do, and his stomach was already empty.

One… Sirius Black. There would only ever be one Sirius Black.

Two… I love you’s. Two I love you’s whispered in the dark.

Three… moles. Three moles behind Sirius’ left ear.

Four… calls. Four calls he’d ignored from Giles, worried they’d be from his father.

Five… weeks. Five weeks they’d spent at each other’s side.

Six… friends. Six friends they’d been missing.

Seven… braids. Seven times he’d braided Sirius’ beautiful hair.

Eight… days a week. I ain’t got nothing but love, babe… Sirius had sung it to him days ago. Did he remember?

Nine—

Come now, is this not getting rather pathetic?

Remus slammed his fist into the mirror. It cracked along the edge. Go away! He told the voice. Just fuck off!

Now that’s fine manners. You talk to your mother with that mouth?

Nearly undone, Remus glared at his reflection. “You aren’t real,” he gasped. “You’re just inside my head. No one else can hear you.”

Of course I’m inside your head, but why should that mean I’m not real? Remus Lupin, Remus Dean, Moony, we’re all real. In fact, it’s getting a bit crowded in here… Might want to empty some of us out soon…

Remus splashed water over himself again. It did not help. He was tired, and wet, and he didn’t want to think of Sirius or Nydia or anyone else anymore... but it was impossible. The longer he stayed in that room, the worse the thoughts seemed to get.

And so he walked.

Aimlessly.

People called out to him, asked him where he was going. Remus didn’t have an answer. He only wanted to be angry. Angry at Sirius whom he loved, at Nydia who did nothing, at Tomny for being so far away, at Lyall for marrying someone else—at his father for not knowing him! … And his mother who knew both and had left them all.

Remus Lupin was angry at the world. He had been for a long time. He hadn’t been raised like James, to know anger and also forgiveness, or Sirius who felt anger and knew to demand retribution. He knew only how to be angry, and anger made for stupid lovers. Jealous, bitter lovers. And that was entirely the reason why he called out to her from across the berm.

“Hey, Jill… do you have a moment?”





* * *





Saturday 17th September 1977





It felt a bit like being back on acid. He was drifting, physically there but mentally somewhere else. He imagined he was back at the estate. It was early August, James and Peter were still away on holiday and Giles had taken Lyall and Sandra out on some day trip. The staff had the day off. It was Sunday. Their day. Remus was burning the eggs, Sirius was flicking through the radio. It was Sunday.

“You could’ve come inside, you’re a prefect now,” Jillian said to him, as she appeared out of the front door of Bronte House in a pretty blue peacoat.

“Oh. Forgot.”

She took his arm. “Don’t worry. Now you’ll know for next time.”

Remus swallowed. Somehow next time wasn’t as appealing as one more.

They started up the lane together, following a train of other upper-sixths, all on their way to make the buses that would carry them down to the village. It was cold—a storm was bound to be rolling in, but none of their classmates had been deterred anyway. A pair of Rowena girls whipped past, jostling Remus accidentally and stopped just long enough to apologise before giggling and moving on.

“Will we be seeing your friends today?” Jillian asked, once they’d made it to Castle Hall, where a string of yellow buses were lining the curb.

Remus shook his head. They’d asked him to join them, of course, but he’d declined on precedent. He already refused to be within ten feet of Sirius within their own dorm, no way he was going to share a table with him at some stupid teashop. It was Saturday.

“No, they’re… doing their own thing.”

“Oh, too bad.”

If he’d been paying attention, Remus might’ve noticed the look of satisfaction on Jillian’s face, but the crowd had him distracted. Professor McGonagall was at the head of it all, checking names, while younger prefects mulled about, trying desperately to keep the excited bunch of sixth formers in order. Skirting the edges of it all was a very gleeful-looking Mr. Filch, who’d already apprehended Barty Crouch and Aaron Travers for trying to stowaway on one of the buses. As Filch dragged the moaning boys away by the ear, Jillian tapped him on the shoulder.

“I’m gonna chat up Tracey for just a sec, can you check us in?”

He nodded and she pressed up on her toes—simultaneously yanking Remus down by the shoulder—to kiss him on the cheek.

“Be right back,” she cooed.

As Jillian slipped away, Remus cursed himself. It’d been an impulse to ask her to the village—one he should’ve ignored. After all, since when had his impulses ever panned out the way he’d wanted?

“Lupin and Stewart,” Remus grunted, after fighting his way to the front of the mob surrounding the nearest prefect with a clipboard. At his words, she turned around and he realised then that it was Trish.

“You’re off yer head, Remington,” she exclaimed. “Dinnae tell me you actually asked Jillian out?”

Remus scowled. “Why don’t you say it louder, don’t think she heard you.”

“Tis your funeral,” she sniggered, checking their names off the list. “Bus three. Now who’s next?”

As other kids shoved forward to get their names down, Remus went back around to the correct bus. He was glancing around for his date when Peter appeared with Moira, and that quickly multiplied into the two of them plus James and Lily.

“Moony, you’re coming after all!” Peter said.

“Uh, yeah,” Remus said awkwardly. “Thought I’d give it a go.”

“That’s great, I can’t wait to see everything,” Lily smiled, grabbing his coat sleeve. “C’mon! Our bus is this way, you can ride with us.”

He followed her obediently, and was fine with the situation until James and Lily took it upon themselves to link their arms through his.

“So, Moony… are you and Black fighting again?” James asked.

“Yeah, he’s been weird all morning,” Peter called.

Lily scoffed; “What those two are trying to say is, are you alright? You and Sirius aren’t talking, and we’ve sort of noticed.”

"Definitely noticed," Peter added.

“It’s fine,” Remus insisted, pulling away from all of them. “We’ve just had a little spat.”

“You mean a big spat?” James echoed.

“No! Just—ugh… Just let me deal with it, alright?”

“Okay,” Lily said, taking his hand again. “But if you need a lawyer, don’t call Potter. He’s failing criminal court already and it’s only week two.”

“That is a grievous falsehood, Evans. I could sue you for slander.”

“You’d have to be able to understand the paperwork first,” she teased.

“Moony!” James rounded on him. “Who’d you rather have defending you? Me or Lily?”

“Of course he’d pick Lily,” Moria said, making Peter snort. “Any sane person would.”

“Moira, you wound me so,” James moaned. “I’ll have you lot know that I am planning to ace our next test in—”

Just then Jillian reappeared, stepping between Remus and Lily and taking his arm fondly. “Thanks for checking us in,” she said sweetly, then; “Hey, guys.”

Lily snatched her hand back. The last time Remus had seen that look on her face was when Sirius had showed up with Chastity on their way to the village the very first time.

“Oh. Hi, Jill,” she chirped. “Are you two… together?”

Remus hated how Lily had asked the question, but Jillian only seemed to glow. “Yes, Remus asked me to go to the village with him.”

James reached across his girlfriend, gently knocking a fist against Remus’ shoulder as a friendly rapport. “Way to go, man,” he said. "Knew you had it in you."

“Are you two coming on our bus?” Moira asked, absentmindedly picking a stray pine needle from Peter’s hair. Though Peter had insisted hand over fist that he’d grown over the summer, Remus suspected it was only a half inch at most. Conversely, Moira had grown. She was still sporting her same straight-across fringe, but she’d gained at least an inch and a half on her boyfriend in the last year, maybe two. If Peter had noticed, he’d made no mention of it to his friends.

“No!” Remus answered quickly. “Or—What bus are you guys taking?”

“Three,” Lily replied.

“We’re four.”

Peter glanced around. “But there’s only three buses.”

“—I meant two!”

“Shame,” James said. “I’m sure we could squeeze you in.”

“No… we—”

“POTTER!”

They all turned. Sirius was waving his arms from outside the doors of the very last bus, trying hard to get their attention. Next to him stood Nydia Burke, looking very pretty with her hair arranged neatly over one shoulder. She wore a white wool overcoat that seemed to make her brown skin glow, and was standing very close to Sirius, as if leaving too much room would prevent people from understanding that she was the lucky winner of his undivided attention for the day.

“Impatient, that one,” James chuckled, waving back and already steering Lily and the others towards him. “See you in the village, Lupin?”

“Yup,” Remus answered, as Jillian took his arm and did the same.

“I could tell you were lying,” she said, as they neared the front doors of the bus. “You don’t want to be around your friends.”

“It’s not like that…”

“No, it’s okay! I get it. It’s sort of sweet—how you want us to be all alone. I never would have pegged you as such a romantic, Remus.”

Resisting the urge to correct her, Remus glanced back over his shoulder. Through the small crowd he could just make out a head of midnight-black hair. It occurred to him that he didn’t want to want Sirius to turn around, but perhaps if he thought hard enough…

Come back… Turn around. Come back.

But Sirius Black did not turn around. Rather, he stepped back the gentlemen he was to allow Nydia to board the bus ahead of him, and then he climbed its steps, and Remus could stare no longer.

Jillian was nudging him. “Remus? Remus, are you listening?”

“Uh, sorry, what were you saying?”

“I was asking you what you’d like to do today.”

“Oh. Well, Lily mentioned there was a bookshop.”

“Bookshop it is,” she agreed. “And afterwards we can get a spot of lunch. It’ll be fabulous.”

Yeah… fabulous…

So the day went on. And on. And as tumultuous as Remus felt inside, it was admittedly not entirely terrible. Lily had been right, Craigtyre was charming in the daytime. Its roads were cobbled and windy, boarded on either side by rows and rows of look-alike cottages. Every yard had a garden and every garden had a fence, though most were made of stone and covered in soft cushions of moss. Street lamps lined the busier roads, all of them leading into the centre of town like a bead of rain running across a spider’s web. The heart of the village held most of the shops and much of the comings and goings were centred around there, along with the main road in and out, where the buses had dropped them.

As baffling as Jillian was most moments, Remus found himself grateful for her unwavering ability to chatter on. She literally never ran out of things to say, but never complained when Remus’ attention wandered or when he thought to distract himself with a fag or otherwise. And she didn’t insist on having tea in that ridiculous Madam Puddifoot’s, an immense relief. They’d walked past the shop earlier in the day and the sight of all those tacky frills along with the overpowering smell of potpourri was enough to turn Remus’ stomach for the second day in a row.

“That girl, Lily Evans?” Jillian said, as though she didn’t already have every facet of Lily’s life recorded to memory; “She tried telling me the most egregious story about you the other day.”

Remus pulled his cigarette from his lips. “She did?”

“Yes! She said that… Well, it’s hardly worth repeating, it was so silly. I think you might need to check in with your James friend though, she might have a crush on you. Wouldn’t want that now, would we?”

She hugged his arm again, which was really starting to wear out its welcome. Remus thought he might have bruises around his elbow by the end of the day.

“Look, Remus, I’ve found your bookshop.”

Jillian kindly pointed across the street, to a small line of shops all brightly decorated. Remus lit up when he saw it. There was indeed a bookshop, but that wasn’t what had caught his attention. The building that adjoined the bookshop on the left-hand side was painted all over in rich colours of navy and plum. It had a sign that bore the words Dervish and Bangers! Records & Tapes and its windows were plastered with posters advertising the latest album releases. He could hardly believe it—a record shop, right there in Craigtyre! It was positively mouth-watering.

“Blimey! I didn’t know they had a music shop here!” Remus gasped, already dashing across the street. Jillian came with, only because she’d refused to release his arm, though the noise she made as they stumbled across the street was less than impressed.

“Appears it’s new,” Jillian said when they’d reached the front windows. She pointed at a flyer taped to the glass, advertising the shop’s grand opening, and as they stared the door opened towards them and a small group of their classmates shuffled out, each clutching different LPs to their chests and chattering excitedly.

“Hey Jill!” A few of the girls trilled, sizing Remus up as they passed by. He barely noticed, itching to get inside.

“You coming?”

“I’ll be right there,” Jillian said, waving at the giggling girls. “I’m just gonna catch up with Donna and Sandy first.”

Not about to complain over the sudden offer of privacy, Remus pulled away from her and slipped into the shop. It was small inside, but warm enough, with each wall painted a different neon colour and decorated with posters and thin shelves displaying various albums. On the floor in-between were rows and rows of vinyl records and tapes, each of them stacked together and just waiting to be sifted through. Music was playing, naturally, and apart from a few other browsers, the only other person inside was a young guy busy organising a milk crate of dingy LPs behind the shop counter. It reminded Remus of summer, when he and Sirius had wasted away hours wondering through the shops around Camden and Carnaby. And as soon as he thought about summer, he began to miss Sirius all over again.

On the upside, without Jillian around to bother him, Remus was able to spend some time sorting through the rows like he did in the shops back home. The shop attendant never really paid him much mind, he was too busy bobbing his head along to the music as he price-stickered each record. It was a folk song, which didn’t appeal much to Remus, but he wasn’t used to a music store being so quiet. The guys in London were always trying to upsell you some newest release.

“Who’s the band?” He asked, making the shop attendant perk up.

“Oh, uh—” He spun around, picking up the album cover. “New group—husband and wife duo, looks like. ‘The Long… bottoms’. Hm.”

Remus nodded—the name was definitely folky enough—and suddenly a knock came on the window behind him. Jillain was outside, waving like she expected him to come outside and join her. She had a group of her girlfriends with her too, each of them looking keen.

Come on! Jillian mouthed through the glass. She gestured to the girls, clearly wanting Remus to make an entrance.

Pulling a random record off the shelf, Remus raised it like he’d yet to pay. Jillian crossed her arms, but motioned for him to go on and Remus slunk back toward the pay counter, sheepishly dropping the album down in front of the seller.

“KC and the Sunshine Band, eh?” The guy said, turning the record over.

“Er—no, s'a mistake,” Remus said quickly. “Do you have any Sex Pistols?”

He nodded, and turned around to shuffle through a pile of albums on the back counter. “Aye, yer in luck. Just got a fresh shipment in yesterday. Still going through it, in fact. But those Sex Pistols—hard tae come by.”

“I’ll take whatever you’ve got,” Remus said, watching patiently as the guy sorted through. He wanted to celebrate when the stack finally revealed the band’s single, Anarchy in the U.K., but what came after just about made Remus’ eyes roll out of his head.

“That the new Bowie release?!” He asked breathlessly, pointing at the album, which was still fresh and untouched in its plastic. Across its front read, Restricted release for promotional use only. Not for sale.

“Mhm, a pal ‘a mines helped me get my hands on a merchant copy,” The guy picked it up, passing it over to Remus to let him run his hands across it. Heroes, it was titled. Remus could hardly believe it.

“Will you sell it to me?”

The guy shook his head. “Na, can’t sell it. Against the rules. This baby won’t hit shelves for an’nur month or sae. Check back then.”

Remus did the math in his head. Sirius was quite possibly more livid with him than he’d ever been. It wouldn’t negate the seriousness of what was done, but showing up with a fresh-off-the-presses Bowie album just might soften the blow.

“I’ll pay double for it!”

“Sorry, pal. Cannae do it.”

Jillian knocked on the window again, looking impatient.

“Please! I'll do anything! I'll... well, next time I’m in I’ll sort five crates of stock for free! You’re a brand-new shop, I’ll bet you’re busy enough without having to sort through a million copies of KC and the Sunshine Band.”

The guy squinted at him, before smirking slyly. “Ten crates.”

“Seven.”

“Eight.”

“Deal.”

He emerged on the street with both albums, feeling victorious, but with little time to reveal in the glow of the still plastic-wrapped LP. Jillian was waiting for him, arms crossed and tapping her foot like a scolding professor. Luckily her friends had gone.

“Sorry, I had to haggle with the guy,” he supplied meekly. Jillian looked him up and down, then swept her hair out of her eyes.

“That’s alright. I wanted to introduce you a bit more, but girls had a reservation at Madam Puddifoots.”

“Next time?” He winced.

She nodded. “What’d you get then?”

He showed her.

“Bowie? Never much cared for him.”

“He’s great once you get used to him.”

“Really? I always thought he was a bit too ostentatious. Overzealous, maybe.”

“Oh, he totally is, but he’s also pretty… uhm…” He trailed off. Suddenly Remus didn’t feel much like talking about music. “Lunch then?”

Jillian beamed.

They took tea in some random café just off the main drag, and throughout the meal Jillian continued peppering him with questions about his life and growing up in the city. She never forgot to interject with bits of herself though.

“My mum’s family is from London, but we never see them,” she sighed, sipping from her Coca-Cola. “I hate spending the summers in Chippenham, it’s so boring. It’s like, you grow up there and the only other people around for miles are those with babies and their grandparents.”

“Chippenham, that’s close to Bath, innit?”

“Yeah! Have you been?”

He quickly changed the subject; “Do you read much?”

Jillian sat up straighter, apparently pleased that he’d finally contributed to the conversation some. “Not really, I love the theatre though. My favourite is ‘My Fair Lady’. It’s a musical. Have you seen it?”

“Er—no.”

“That’s too bad! I saw it first in London actually, and I loved it so much that I went to see it again when I was in New York. Only then I realised that it wasn’t actually ‘My Fair Lady’, but the original play it was based on. ‘Pygmalion’, or something.”

“Oh yeah,” Remus said, his memory jogged; “Like that guy in Ovid.”

“In what?”

“The Greek figure? Ovid writes about him in… y’know what, never mind.”

Jillian propped her chin up on one hand and grinned at him. “You're so funny, Remus."

"Nah, not really."

"You are," she insisted. "And you have such handsome curls.”

“... Thanks.” Oh god, was he supposed to compliment her back now? “You’ve got nice hair too. Very... a nice colour."

Despite the lame attempt, Jillian laughed. Maybe he was funny. Then she reached across the table, thumbing a piece of his hair, which had fallen down over his temple. “So soft too,” she praised, before gently running her thumbnail down the side of his cheek.

Remus immediately shivered. He couldn’t do it anymore. He shouldn’t want to. He was in love with Sirius, even if Sirius was off with Nydia.

“Jill—”

Perhaps it was women’s tuition. Before Remus could even get the words out, Jillian was popping up from her chair. “Look at us—we’re wasting the day,” she declared, grabbing her handbag. “Don’t worry, this one is on me.”

She left their table to pay, and Remus was left dejected and disappointed. He wondered where Sirius had taken Nydia. To the Three Broomsticks, maybe? Where they could get a booth along the back so that no one might interrupt? Or maybe he’d taken her to the joke shop James had been chittering on about—the one that supplied gag toys and rubber snakes-galore. Was he telling her of their band, their plans for the future? Was he complimenting her beautiful brown skin, or singing to her, or talking about flats and Jagger and his lovely new life at the Potters?

Was he calling her the sky?

You could almost be considered a masochist at this point, what with all the emotional turmoil you churn out, Vicious Moony said. Are you sure you’re a seventeen year-old boy? Sounds more like a lonely housewife to me… Shall I fetch you an apron?

You’re not fucking funny.

I think our audience would disagree.

“Ready?” Jillian asked, reappearing beside the table.

They walked around the village some more, even stopping in to the local confectionery to line their pockets with various sweets. Remus looked everywhere for Sirius—a hint of him among the village’s passersby—but never spotted him.

“Oh, Remus! We should take a boat out!” Jillian said, as they crossed into the eastern half of the village. The crowds were less dense there, mostly because of the small lake that took up all of the space on the edge of the nearest neighbourhood. It was nothing compared to Lake Dubh, if anything it was more of a large pond, but there were tiny fishing boats left along the shore by the local authority and they had leave as Hawkings students to use them as they pleased. No one was out on the lake today though, which was a good thing. The weather had turned again and it was clear that a usual Scottish storm was on its way.

“I dunno, Jill,” Remus said, surveying the sky. “Looks like it’ll rain soon.”

“I’ve brought my brolly,” she said, pulling a small telescopic umbrella from her bag. “C’mon, it’ll be fun. I won’t even make you paddle the entire time.”

And that was how they ended up floating across the tiny loch in a wooden dinghy. The water was pitch black and the entire thing swayed precariously in the shifting breeze, but Jillian only appeared ecstatic. “You can swim, right?” She’d asked him, as they drifted further from shore. He could, but the water was already icy despite being only September, and Remus didn’t much fancy a dip.

"James and Sirius seem funny," Jillian said, while Remus rowed and she sat across from him. It wasn’t raining yet, but she kept her umbrella balanced carefully on one shoulder as though it were a parasol and they were two amorous lovers who’d only just escaped the prying eyes of their snub-nosed rivals. Staring at her, Remus wondered what the probability was that she’d be struck by lightning before they returned to shore.

"They are."

"I've known them both for a while, obviously." She eyed him, like a cobra sizing up a meal. "But you don't seem to have much in common."

Remus tried not to appear affronted. "We have a lot in common. We all like music."

"Oh, but I didn't really mean interests. It was more like, they're... active, and you're reactive."

He didn't understand her meaning, and wasn't entirely sure he wanted to, so Remus just focused on paddling. "They're best friends. Bound to be alike, I guess."

“And is Peter your best friend then?”

“He’s one of them,” he answered sharply. “James too.”

“But you just said that James is Sirius’ best friend.”

The comment made Remus grumpy; as if he and Peter were the leftover Marauders, and must’ve been closer because of it. The things that I know—that I’ve seen—that James Potter hasn’t.

“There’s also Lily,” he said; “and Marlene.”

“Your ex-girlfriend?”

“She’s just a friend now.”

Jillian nodded quickly. “Of course. I didn’t mean to insinuate otherwise.” She bit her lip. “Oh, look at that, it’s starting to rain!”

Despite not having an umbrella of his own, Remus had yet to feel a single drop, but that didn’t stop Jillian as she quickly scrambled across the dinghy to take a seat next to him. With all of their weight now transferred to the back, the boat lurched dangerously and Remus clung to its edge, trying to keep it from overturning and dropping one of his oars in the process.

“Uhh—Jill, I don’t think we’re properly balanced anymore!”

“It’s rude to comment on a lady’s weight, Remus,” Jillian teased, snuggling in close. Eventually the boat stopped rocking, though they were tipped precariously to one end. As Jillian coddled him, Remus peered miserably over the water’s surface, mourning the loss of his oar. At least it floated; he could see it several yards away, bobbing aimlessly like a taunt. What else have you lost? It seemed to say; Let us count the ways. You’ve lost your friends, your mind, your boyfriend, your self-resp—

Boyfriend...?

Boyfriend?!

“Remus.”

He looked back, and Jillian was right there. She was looking up at him, their faces only mere inches apart. It was almost dark under the umbrella, he doubted any rival could’ve seen them even if they were trying to spy.

“I really like you, Remus,” Jillian confessed abruptly. How easy it was for her to say such things. He might’ve commented on it, wryly—as if to defuse some of the sudden tension—but before he could she was stretching her face up toward him.

Oh god. She was going to kiss him!

He pulled back sharply, his only thought being—Sirius! And as he did so, his hand missed the edge of the dinghy and fell onto empty air. There was a sudden shriek—Jillian—then a splash, and just like that Remus Lupin was in the lake.



* * *





It would be funny later when he was looking back on it, but in the moment, Remus was nothing other than humiliated. Jillian seemed equally so—her face was splotchy and red the entire row back and she didn’t say a word, but she had helped him clamber back into the boat so that was something.

“I’m s-sorry,” he told her, as he stood shivering on the shore.

Jillian didn’t meet his gaze. Her peacoat was stained with lake water, and she was fiddling with the strap of her umbrella. “It’s alright,” she murmured.

“I didn’t m-mean to of-f-fend you,” Remus said, already working on his incoming cliché. “And it’s n-not even you, it’s j-just that… there’s s-someone else.”

Jillian’s meek look turned into a deep, frustrated frown. “Oh Jesus—I knew that.”

For a moment Remus stopped shivering. “You did?”

“Yes!” She huffed. “If you must know, Lily told me. I thought it was just her way of keeping you to herself at first… but I guess now I know she was telling the truth.”

Remus couldn’t believe it. It felt as though the entire world was caving in. How could Lily have possibly found out? And how could she have told Jillian?!

“I… Jill, we—!”

“Yes, yes, I understand.” She glanced bitterly at the lake. “Family matters, and all that. So rare that these things turn out, but you can’t help who you like, even if they’re French.”

“I—” Remus drew up short once again. “French?”

“Lily told me all of the details.”

She didn't tell me the details! Remus scrambled to make sense of what she was saying. He was French? That’s what she was focussed on? What did Sirius being French have anything to do with it? He would’ve thought she'd be more caught up over the fact that they both had a—

“You can tell Ms. Farrah that I’m not going to try and steal her fiancé,” Jillian said. “Now that I know she’s actually real. Though if I were her, I would’ve never let you come back here without me. Too many girls, too few eligible boys.”

Jillian began wiping off her coat, while Remus ran circles in his head. “Farrah?”

“She must be pretty beautiful,” she said, “to make a guy stay so faithful when another girl is openly trying to kiss him. I understand why you hid it though—the fact that you're engaged and have an actual fiancée. I mean, we’re only seventeen and it is 1977. I wouldn’t want to be engaged this early, no offence.”

Suddenly the dots were starting to connect. “Farrah…” he mumbled. Lily… Lily and her egregious story… oh—

“OH!” He cried. “That fiancée.”

Jillian rolled her eyes, like his unanticipated dip in the lake had turned him daft. “No need to play dumb anymore, Remus. I get it. You were actually pretty decent, all things considered. I’ve heard that I can be sort of… overbearing.”

“Heh, you? Nah…”

It began to rain, spattering them with fat raindrops and further darkening Jillian’s sky-blue coat. “I do wish you’d have told me before I refused Roy Nilssen’s invitation to the village,” she drawled, opening her umbrella. “Why did you ask me anyway?”

Remus licked his frozen lips. Lily’s lie was already spun and Jillian was believing it; there was no need to tell her that he’d done it only to make the best friend he was simultaneously sleeping with jealous.

“Well, I was hoping that we could… still be friends?”

She gave him another hopeless look. “Of course we can still be friends.” She pat him on the arm, and Remus got the sense that it was more of a pity-offer than anything else. “I’m gonna go now, I think, see if I can catch up with Roy before we have to get the bus. You going to be okay on your own?”

He nodded, lake water still dripping off the tips of his hair. “I’ll be fine, don’t worry about me. And I’ll pay you back for lunch too.”

“Keep your money,” she said kindly, as she passed him back his records. “Spend it on your fiancée in Paris. Bring me back a croissant or whatever.”

She left him there on the edge of the Scottish loch, and despite the fact that he was sopping wet and had most definitely ruined the fresh package of cigarettes in his pocket, Remus had never felt more relieved.

Lily Evans, you are forgiven and then some! He promised, as he made his way back up the rain-covered cobbled streets with a new spring in each squelching step. He’d just turned onto the village’s main thoroughfare when a voice called out to him, and he turned to find Marlene standing beneath the awning of the same cafe he and Jillian had eaten at earlier. She was bundled up against the weather in her oversized leather coat, but her hair was spiked up with gel and she was without her stockings, instead having traded them for thick black knee socks and heavy workmen boots. Perhaps even more surprisingly, she held a cigarette between two fingers.

“What the fuck happened to you?” Marlene asked, looking him up and down. “Why're you all wet?”

“Marlene,” Remus said, equally unable to believe his eyes, “are you smoking?”

Like she were embarrassed, Marlene straightened up and flicked the cigarette away. “As if you can talk,” she mumbled, casting a worried glance at the cafe behind her.

“Waiting for someone?” Remus asked.

“No!” She answered very quickly, coming forward. She took his arm, despite the fact that he was still wet, and began steering him away. “C’mon, I was just about to head back. You’ll catch a cold if you stay like this.”

“I’m looking for Sirius,” Remus said as she led him; “Have you seen him?”

“Mhm, a while ago though. Think he went to Broomsticks with the others.”

Remus nodded thoughtfully. He didn’t want to make a scene in front of all of their friends—certainly not Nydia. He could wait, clean himself up, and then maybe he’d have a chance to make all of it right again.

“You sure you want to go back so early?” He asked Marlene, as they made it to one of the waiting buses.

“Yeah,” she said, pushing him aboard. “Wasn’t having much fun anyway…”

They sat, and the doors closed as the driver—Stan, the young guy with all the acne who’d driven them to their very first live gig in year eleven—pulled away from the curb. The weather was terrible, a real storm had begun to lash at the bus’s windows, but Remus felt hopeful for the first time in days.

“Marlene,” he said.

She looked up from her seat across the aisle. She’d been drawing on her boot with a pen and had the cap tucked between her teeth. “Eh?”

“Just wanted to say... that you’re pretty.”

She stared at him, then capped the pen. “Delirious already. Right, that’s it—straight into the bath with you.”

Back at the dorm, he took a shower to warm his frozen skin—because a bath would’ve wasted more time—and hightailed it back to Castle Hall with his hair still damp, where he waited in the rain to apologise to Sirius. Each returning bus might as well have been a ship pulling in harbour, but when their passengers piled off and none of his friends were among them, Remus always felt a pang of disappointment.

“Has Sirius Black returned yet?” He eventually asked the waiting prefect—not Trish, thankfully. The boy glanced over his clipboard and shook his head, and so Remus waited. It was nigh seven o’clock when he checked his watch to find that supper had come and gone without him. His legs and arse were aching after spending so long leaning against the cement retaining wall alongside the road, but just as he was considering giving up, another bus pulled up the lane. Among the exiting students were James and Lily, and they spotted him immediately.

“Remus!” Lily declared, rushing over and stepping beneath his umbrella. “Did you have a nice day?”

“Yes,” Remus told her, before all but dropping the umbrella and pulling Lily into a tight hug. “You’re insane, Lily Evans, but you’re also a genius!”

“What did I do?” She asked, voice muffled by his shoulder.

Suddenly another pair of arms enveloped them.

“I’m not sure why we’re hugging,” James said, “but cheers!”

“It’s Jillian,” Remus said, when they’d finished. “She’s done with me. And all because someone told her I was already engaged.”

“You’re engaged?! Oh my god… Can I be best man?” James gasped, while Lily whipped him playfully on the arm.

“He’s not really engaged,” she said quietly. “I just told Jillian he was so that she’d leave him alone. I can’t believe it worked, she so totally didn’t believe me before!”

Remus shifted from one foot to another. “Yeah, well… she definitely does now.”

“This is too funny,” James chittered. “Black! Come and get a load ‘a this!”

At James’ call, Remus shot upright, spraying Lily with the rain that had collected on top of his umbrella. He hadn’t seen Sirius get off the bus, but now that he were paying attention, he could see Sirius across the berm, standing next to Nydia.

Sirius threw a hand up in answer, and paused slightly when he noticed that it was Remus James were standing next to. Remus thought about throwing up a friendly hand of his own, but then Nydia tapped Sirius on the shoulder and said something into his ear that had him turning into her. He smiled, that amused smirk of his, and Remus felt his heart plummet.

“They certainly look like they had a good time…”

“Right?” James trilled. “I was gettin’ a bit worried about him—always spending all his time with you.” He elbowed Remus lightly in the stomach. “Guess we know he’s back to normal after all.”

“You’re always encouraging him,” Lily scoffed, as Nydia placed a peck on Sirius’ cheek and strolled away. “Just watch as he breaks her heart.”

“Nah, he won’t break it,” James said, “Nydia’s tougher than that. It’s why he said yes to her in the first place.”

Remus bit down on his thumbnail. Dammit.

“Can’t have five minutes without you interrupting,” Sirius said, as he wandered over. There, he looked Remus over. “Get caught in the rain, Lupin?”

“Fell in the lake, actually.”

The barest shadow of a smile crossed Sirius’ face, almost giving Remus hope, but it vanished by the time Lily was rounding on him.

“You fell in the lake?!”

“It’s not that big of a deal…” he murmured, suddenly more shy.

“Go on, tell him the good news, Moony!” James prodded. Sirius eyed them both.

“What news?”

Suddenly very nervous, Remus baulked, and it was Lily who stepped in.

“Remus is finally free of any and all persistent admirers!” She announced.

Sirius raised a brow. “You mean Stewart?” He said, and Lily nodded.

“You heard me, Jillian Stewart is no more! Remus is much too busy with Farrah to be bothered with silly school-girl crushes.”

“And by Farrah, you mean…?”

“His beautiful French fiancée, of course!" She chittered. "But be careful, she’s a secret. Wouldn’t want to embarrass him.”

“I’d say that ship’s sailed,” Remus muttered.

Raising his chin, Sirius slipped both hands in his pockets. “Great. Happy for you.”

“Me too,” James agreed, clapping a hand on both of their shoulders. As he did so, Remus nearly fumbled his albums, which he’d been keeping tucked under one arm.

“Got these in the village,” Remus said, passing the first record onto James and Lily to get a look.

“Sex Pistols—nice!” James declared. “Bet they’d be just mental to see live.”

“Yeah…” Sirius answered, keeping his hands in his pockets but peering over as though he didn’t want to appear too interested.

“Might be a bit wet,” Remus said. “But there’s also this.”

Trying to keep his fingers from trembling, he raised the other album, and Sirius’ eyes expanded to twice their usual size.

“Holy shit,” James gasped for him; “Is that a new Bowie record? Black, you think you would’ve told me it’d come out.”

“It hasn’t,” Sirius echoed. “Not until the end of next month.”

“Convinced the guy to give me his merchant’s copy,” Remus said, eagerly holding out. Sirius took the album and flipped it over, taking in Bowie’s black and white image.

“Fucking hell…”

“You’re still so full of surprises, Remus,” Lily giggled.

“Really is,” Sirius agreed quietly.

Trying not to let the comment get his hopes up, Remus cleared his throat. “Practically sold myself into servitude to get that, but you can call it an early birthday present.”

“You mean you got it for me?”

“Well, I didn’t get it for myself, did I? Figure you’re the only one in all of Scotland with a copy.”

“I…” Sirius bit his lip. “I can’t accept.”

“Sure you can, we keep our records in the same place anyway.”

Sirius looked like he wanted to argue, but if there was anything in the world he liked more than attention, it was Bowie.

“Thanks,” he said. “This is pretty fucking rad.”

“Don’t mention it.” Remus smiled, and Sirius returned the look. It was a chastened smile, but Remus took it as a good sign. Perhaps they weren’t entirely down the tubes then. If Sirius could forgive him for Tomny and he could overlook Nydia then maybe they—

“Sirius, darling,” Nydia called; “we’re heading back to the common room now. Are you coming?”

Sirius raised his chin. “Yeah, be right there,” he told her. “Catch you guys back at the dorm.”

“Don’t stay out all night, tiger,” James laughed, slapping Sirius on the behind as he turned away. Sirius scoffed at him, before raising the record in Remus’ direction.

“Thanks again, Moons. Super cool.”

And just like that he was gone. Remus wanted to scream.

“Don’t be too disappointed, Moons,” James told him, as they headed back to Godric with Lily in tow. “It was good on you for trying. Black’ll come around, you’ll see.”

“And if he doesn’t, then we’ll just sue,” Lily added fondly.

His friends’ lighthearted sympathy aside, Remus was still lost. He’d known that things between him and Sirius weren’t just going to magically heal themselves after Jillian’s departure, but he’d been anticipating that it would at least make it easier to talk about. Judging from Sirius’ reaction though, it’d been a false hope.

“Did ya make a mistake, Lu?” Tomny asked later, when Remus had plucked up the courage to phone him. He'd been nervous ever since Tomny had seen him off at the station, like seeing him slip out of sight had been some great goodbye. He'd even avoided calling, afraid the line would come up dead again, but now Remus felt stupid. Tomny had picked up on the third ring, and he'd been the same as always. Friendly, kind. Just so Tom.

“… Yeah, I made a big fucking mistake..." Remus murmured. He heard Tomny sniff, then chuckle lightly.

“Little sop. Don't cry."

"I'm not crying!"

"Right, right. But all 'ah this is about that friend of yours, yeah? The tall glass ‘a water yer always goin’ on about… Sirius?”

Involves you too, he wanted to say. When he didn’t, Remus began to gnaw on the inside of his cheek. He knew Tomny had a vague idea of what he meant by the relationship, but so far he’d been tip-toeing around actually calling it what was. He supposed the kiss had been evidence enough.

“Yeah, that’s him.”

“Orright then, so whatchu gonna do to fix it?” It was such a Tom answer; you break it, you fix it.

“I dunno. Doesn’t really feel like a ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ thing.”

“Those are ‘ard, them.” Tomny stopped to cough. “But nah’ impossible. S’like when yer feelin’ down, and you want to feel up again, right? But ya’ve mixed up all yer pills—just gotta figure out which one’s which. Trial ‘n error, ‘n all that jazz.”

“I feel like I’ve just been ‘erroring’.”

“That’s ‘cause yer ‘ere, whingin’ to me. You should be out there—whingin’ to ‘im.”

“You saying you don’t want to talk to me?”

“Nice try, ya plonker. I’m just no good wiff love advice.”

The comment made Remus spin around to make sure he was alone in the hallway. He was; everyone else was taking up space in the common room, or else had moved on upstairs for the night.

Remus exhaled, jaw trembling. “You know I’m not gay, right, Tom? I’m just sorta… queer for him…” He laughed suddenly, ashamed. “Does that even make any sense?”

Tomny was quiet for a moment, then; “Well, who am I to tell ya what you are and what you aren’t? S’long as yer you, I’m satisfied.”

Like with so much of Tomny, Remus carried the conversation with him as he laid down in bed that night. Sirius had always loved him for who he was, he knew that, but as he stared up at the roof of his four-poster, he began to recall all the times he couldn’t. Couldn’t love Sirius as he was, or more properly, couldn’t himself as he loved Sirius. Over and over again it went;

Sirius, I can’t do that.

Sirius, I can’t be that.

But what could he do—who could he be? It made him wonder if Sirius had ever asked himself the same things.

The next morning, Remus approached Sirius in the common room. He had an entire spiel prepared, but Sirius had always been quicker to the mark. Before Remus could even begin to explain himself, Sirius was charging on ahead.

“Haven’t seen my light, have you?” He asked. He was busy rooting through the cushions of every sofa in the room. He’d already amassed an impressive collection of shrapnel, lint, and the odd calcified biscuit or two.

“Here, use mine.” Remus felt for his pockets. He had a lighter, but realised at the last second that it was the one Tomny had given him. Somehow it felt like a faux pas. “Er… never mind, I don’t have one after all.”

“S’fine. I’ll ask James for his.” Sirius piled the cushions back into place and moved to go around him. Seeing his chance slip away before his eyes, Remus grabbed his wrist. He dropped it quickly, too conscious of any prying stares and how Sirius might react to their first touch in days.

“Can I talk to you?” He murmured.

Sirius looked at his hand, the one he’d used to grab him, and then shrugged. “I dunno, can you?”

Remus didn’t even have time to read too far into the hostility; James and Peter appeared in the room’s doorway and called them away to breakfast, and the opportunity was gone.

In the breakfast line up, Marlene fell into step with him.

“You look terrible,” she said.

“Love ya too, Cherry.”

“Did you get any sleep at all?”

“Not really.”

“What's a'matter then? Nightmares keeping you up?”

“No. I don't—"

"Right, right. Forgot—you don't dream. Guess that extends to nightmares too. How lucky."

"It’s a small mercy in a world so cruel.”

Marlene smirked at his sarcasm and reached for a bowl. “Fry-ups again,” she complained, as Remus loaded his plate with bacon and sausages galore.

“Since when do you not like back bacon?” He sneered, tucking a piece between his teeth as he moved up the line. Marlene followed, grimacing and pinching him on the side for good measure.

“For your information, I’ve gone green,” she said.

“As in vegetarian?”

“Yes!” She illustrated by ladling her bowl full of over-ripe fruit salad. “It’s so much better for the environment. You’d switch over too if you paid any attention to the abysmal conditions that our country’s livestock suffer. I learned about it in Morocco, their traditional farming habits are so much more sustainable than ours, though they are driven mostly by exports. But did you know that pigs here—just like the one on your plate—have been genetically altered to such a degree that they reach slaughtering age before they’re even six months old?”

Remus swallowed his bacon. “Ohhh-kay… and you enjoy those strawberries picked by five year-olds in Peru.”

“You just pulled that out of your arse,” Marlene grumbled. She might’ve said more on the matter, had Chastity Bell not cut between them in the line. The sight alone had Remus backing away, but it wasn’t him she’d come for. Chastity stepped right up to Marlene, tossing her long brown hair over one shoulder, one hand on her hip.

“You’re a real bitch, you know that?”

“Good morning to you too,” Marlene replied, dully.

“ ‘Good morning’?” Chastity echoed, furious. “How dare you—what the actual fuck was that yesterday? You just left me there! What—thought it would be funny to walk away without saying anything?”

“You didn’t seem all that bothered when you were making eyes at Chris Lambert from across the room.”

“Oh? So that’s what this is about?!”

Remus was flummoxed. He didn’t think Marlene and Chastity had ever said a willing word to one another. Their conversation wasn’t exactly friendly, but it implied a little more than passing gestures. As he stared, along with several other kids just waiting to collect their breakfasts, Marlene caught his eye and quickly cleared her throat.

“Could you go?” She asked Chastity boldly. “You’re causing a scene.”

“Oh, I’m causing a scene?”

“Yes, as per usual, and I… Well, I don’t much feel like arguing about some dumb group project in the breakfast line either.”

Chastity’s eyes doubled in size. “Group project? Ugh. Grow up, Marlene.”

She stalked off, and Remus thought it was lucky that Marlene hadn’t ended up wearing her tea. “What was that about?” He asked.

“You heard—class project,” Marlene mumbled, budging him further up the line. “She wanted me to do all the work. I told her tough. Just forget about it.”

“Alright…” Remus turned back to his tray, picking an apple off the buffet table. “Look, I’m green,” he said, mostly trying to cheer her up. He took a bite and she smiled at him.

“Do you want to hang out today?” She asked. “It feels like it’s been so long since it was just the two of us.”

“Uhm, sure. What do you want to do?”

“Anything. We can even skip mass.”

“Skip mass?” Remus gaped. “Who are you and what have you done with Marlene McKinnon?”

“Sorry to surprise you,” Marlene giggled. “The world is a very vast place, Remus. You learn things when you venture out, sometimes even become anew.”

“Only seventeen, and yet so wise.” Remus glanced across the hall, to where James, Sirius, and Peter were sitting at their usual table. They were currently using the back of Barty Crouch’s head for target practice, firing bits of cereal across the room with plastic forks while Lily groaned and Lottie reapplied mascara in her favourite compact mirror.

“They’ll never change, will they?” Marlene sighed, after following his gaze.

Setting the apple down on his tray, Remus turned to her. “You’re right, it has been a while. C’mon, let’s you and me hang out.”

The grin that split her face was warmer than the sun.

With the late-September storm still beating their windows and nothing else to do on a Sunday other than skip communion and be irresponsible, Remus and Marlene packed up their things and made the trek across campus to their old spot.

“I don’t want to stay at the dorm,” Marlene explained, shouting over the noise of the rain. “Mary’s bringing Petyr back and I can’t stand the guy.”

“Does that mean the two of you fought?” He called back.

“Only a little.” She raised the umbrella so he could keep dry. “Did you and Sirius have a row? Things have felt a little tense between the two of you.”

“They’re fine,” he’d said, steering her inside.

Tucked up on their little window seat, legs all a-jumble, Remus stared out at the storm. The flower gardens they overlooked had been battered to a muddy pulp, but such was the way in Scotland.

“Alright!” Marlene announced with a tired sigh, as she snapped her book shut. “Twenty words or less—go.”

“Nah, you first,” he insisted, having been waiting for her to finish. “I wanna hear this.”

Setting aside the book he’d leant her, Marlene rolled her eyes and held up her hands to count. “Alright, let’s see then… Gonzo eats entire sheet of acid. Stupidly tries to electrocute himself… uh…”

“Careful, you only have nine words left,” he teased.

“Shaddup… Erm… Oh! Threatens Duke guy with knife. Passes out in catatonic despair.”

“That was twenty-one words!”

“Eh, I’m pretty sure it was twenty.”

Remus laughed. “ ‘Catatonic despair’?”

“It’s your book!” Marlene raised it like it were a dead rat she’d found drowned in the eaves gutter. “ ‘Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas’,” she scoffed; “What in God’s name would’ve made you want to buy this book?”

“I enjoy fear and loathing, it’s very relatable.”

“Mhm, sure.”

“You said you liked the last chapter.”

“I did like it—because I heard only twenty words of it.”

He chuckled while reaching into the bag of crisps Marlene had brought with them. Dusting his hands off after, he said; “Alright, my turn then. Let’s hear what your chosen pinnacle of literary genius had to offer.”

As Marlene sat up in earnest, Remus cleared his throat; “Ahem!” He began flipping through the pages, before becoming suddenly nervous; “Erm… so this chapter, it…”

“Are you counting those as part of your twenty?”

“No! It’s just…” He stared at the page. “It’s talking about how aliens shag.”

Marlene laughed at him. “It’s science fiction, Remus. These aren’t real people.”

“I know! But it was like…” he scanned the words; psychosexual, ambisexual, manwoman; “reading an essay on mating rituals.”

“That’s exactly what it was,” Marlene said, before sighing and taking the book. “This chapter was like an excerpt to help us understand why the Gethenians are the way they are. In their alien society, anyone can have children, therefore no one is a ‘man’ or a ‘woman’. They simply exist as they are, all equal.”

“But the author uses ‘he’ for all of them.”

“It doesn’t matter, the Gethenians are genderless. See here—‘the Gethenians are not ‘it’, they are potentials’, as in ‘endless potential’. We’re just seeing them through the narrator’s eyes, and he’s a human and clearly a misogynist, so you see, the entire thing is about unpacking our own biases.”

“... You’ve read this before, haven’t you?”

She gave him an impish look, bending the worn-down spine between her hands. “A few times, yeah.”

“I love it,” Remus said, because he could tell she did too. “Read the next chapter and tell me what it’s about?”

She smiled. “Alright, but only for you.”

Remus took his own book back, flipping to the correct page. He’d just set eyes on the first paragraph when Marlene spoke again, calling him back;

“Remus, do you remember what you told me last year—before Christmas?”

He shook his head.

“You said that you should like someone as a person first. Do you still believe that?”

Remus considered; he’d been sixteen then, stupid and naive, and mostly pissed off over Sirius’ ever-rotating train of paramours. He hadn’t really liked any of the girls he’d seen over the summer either, had hardly known anything about them. But he liked Marlene, and Tomny, and Sirius. Oh how he liked them.

“I suppose there are some exceptions, but yeah, I still think it’s true.”

Marlene nodded thoughtfully, and then returned to her book.

They read on like that for much of the day, and into the afternoon and early evening. When they’d both learned a considerable amount of alien politics and the effects of LSD and other methamphetamines on the so-called American Dream, they left their little perch and retreated back into the reality of everyday life.

“I wanted to stop by the library on my way back, do you want to come?” Marlene offered, as they donned their jackets and wellies.

He went with her, because there really wasn’t anything better to do other than return and play hopscotch around his and Sirius’ broken feelings. While Marlene was off in search of some book on Advanced Theology, he meandered toward the reference section, innocently curious about some of the words he’d seen in the sexy, not-so-sexy alien book. It wasn’t a queer thing, he told himself, it was a literature thing. And there was no reason to be afraid of a dictionary.

The first entry, ‘psychosexual’, led him to a lengthy definition coined by Freud that he had no real interest in further extrapolating upon, but the second word, ‘ambisexual’ did not seem to exist in the dictionary at all.

Returning the dusty tome to the shelf, Remus flicked his finger down the line of books until he found a dictionary that seemed more modern. Inside, he carefully scanned each page but again came up empty. Thinking that it was simply a word the author had come up with herself, he gave a last-ditch effort and flipped further back, to ‘S’. There he found what he was looking for.





Sexuality /sekSHo͞oˈalədē/ n. (pl. -ities) 1. the quality or state of being sexual. 2. identity in relation to the gender or genders of which they are typically attracted to; sexual orientation. (See also: heterosexuality, homosexuality, bisexuality.)





Remus gave pause. He read the definition over, then over again, until the thump of his heart in his ears had drowned out the rough purring of the library’s overhead vents.

Gender or genders.

As in… more than one.

Slowly he began to to turn the page, then faster, until he’d dropped to his knees on the carpeted aisle and pinned the book to the floor. There he all but tore the feather-light pages from the spine, furiously trying to find it.

And then, like a lightbulb turning on, there it was.





Bisexual /bīˈsekSH(o͞o)əl/ ajd. (pl. -s) 1. being sexually attracted to both men and women. (Compare: heterosexuality, homosexuality.)





Remus couldn’t breathe, but at the same time, he could. He was finally breathing. Bisexual—not straight, not gay, but somewhere in the middle... an option he'd never known he could have. It was like waking up after a coma and being told the meaning of life. Suddenly he had all the answers, and right there on that mulish grey library carpet, Remus felt more like himself than he ever had before.

Finally, an answer. Something to give people when they asked—if they asked—but more importantly, something to give to himself.

“What are you doing on the floor?”

Marlene had reappeared at the end of the aisle, clutching a fresh book to her chest. Remus looked up at her, alive and breathing and no longer a nameless thing. Glorious.

“Marls, have I ever told you how much I love you?”

She gave him a funny look. “Weirdo. C’mon, they’re serving chocolate cake for afters.”

I personally prefer Bowie's live version of "I Wanna Be Your Dog" over the original, but that's just me, lol.

A 'mac' is a raincoat.

A 'brolly' is an umbrella.

'Wellies' are rain boots.

'Shrapnel' is loose change.

‘Afters’ is dessert.

The book Marlene is reading is "The Left Hand of Darkness" (1969) by Ursula K. Le Guin. It's a science fiction novel that paved the way for many women writers. 100% would recommend to anyone interested in the genre.

Also, the actual definition of ‘ambisexual’ varies, but it would be either a subset of bisexual or defined even as ‘of indeterminate gender; androgynous’.

Chapter 74: Up and Down, Interrupted


Chapter Summary

Chapter 74, in which Remus discovers that Snape makes a GREAT wingman.



Chapter Notes

Dedicating this chapter to Becca, who can always be counted upon to answer even my dumbest questions <3

CW: Lots of emotions in this one. Allusions to mental illness and neglect. Sexual content (non-descriptive).

Also, Remus alludes to his BPD without really having a word to call it what it is. I've had a few people ask me if Remus will ever fully 'know' about his disorders (as in a diagnosis) and yes, he will, but not for a while. If this is at all upsetting to you, I've placed '>>>' to mark the beginning of the conversation and '<<<' for the end portion for you to skip over. It's a very short portion, but I hope this helps.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Well, I’m sorry for the things that I told you,

But words only go so far;

And if I had my way,

I would reach into heaven,

And I’d pull you down a star, for a present;

And I’d make you a chain out of diamonds,

And pearls from a summer sea;

But all I can give you is a kiss in the morning,

And a sweet apology…

- “Tomorrow’s Gonna Be a Brighter Day” Jim Croce, 1972



Monday 19th September 1977





This was it, he'd decided—this was the upswing. Remus Lupin was finally going to get his life together. He woke up the morning more sure of anything he’d ever known; this was it! He was going to make up with Sirius, prove that that the only person he was truly gone for was him and finally things would start to fall into place. He’d even taken the dictionary out of the library, which Ms. Pince only let him do because he was a prefect. He had everything now, everything to explain himself and what he’d been feeling. He still had to own up to the Tomny kiss, but he’d do it. He’d do it as many times as Sirius needed him to, because Sirius was worth every word.
