Chapter 78: Champions, Heroes, and Everyone In Between


Chapter Summary

It's Sirius' eighteenth birthday, and Remus has a surprise.



Chapter Notes

Okay uhhhhmmmm sooooo today is actually the fic's 1 year anniversary on Ao3, and some lovely anons/friends on tumblr convinced me to post this week's chapter early. I don't feel all that bad, since it's more of a short and sweet thing, but I really hope you enjoy. Thank you for all of the love and care you've shown me and this fic for the last year. Your kindness means the world.

Here's to one amazing year, and hopefully the next <3



See the end of the chapter for more notes



If I was a sculptor, ha,

But then again, no,

Or a man who makes potions in a travelling show;

I know it’s not much, but it’s the best I can do,

My gift is my song, and this one’s for you…

- “Your Song” Elton John, 1970



On the morning of his eighteen birthday, Sirius got two phone calls. One from Mr. Potter’s lawyer (until then Remus hadn’t been fully aware that lawyers needed their own lawyers in the first place) and one from his parents. Relief came when he picked up the receiver and found that it was not the stern, haunting voices of Walburga and Orion Black, but rather, the warm, jewel-toned accents of the Potters, calling to wish their second son the bestest of birthdays.

Sirius did not bother to hide his tears this time.

Really, they should’ve known when the call came straight to the dormitory that evening. The Blacks never called their line directly. Remus let Sirius have his moment with his family—joined by James as they shouted happily into the phone loud enough that they could be heard all the way in the common room. The rest of their friends were slouched around on the couches in front of the fire, sharing popcorn while Peter tried his best to sort out the TV James had managed to nick as dorm head for the special occasion. They had to negotiate terms outlining the sworn lack of alcohol just to get it, but considering most of the school was still reeling from Halloween, nobody seemed to mind much.

“Blasted piece of—” Peter grunted, smacking the top of the telly as it continued to fizzle with static. “Knew we should’ve grabbed the other HMV model.”

“What time is the show supposed to be on?” Lottie asked over a yawn.

“Seven,” Remus answered, slouched down very comfortably between Mary and Marlene. He was excited—they never got to watch the Pops on the night it showed, since televisions weren’t allowed in the dorms on school nights. Better yet, every single one of them had a hat to throw into the ring; Queen was showing it’s newest single, leaving Remus positively giddy in his seat, and ABBA and Bowie were playing as well. It was sure to be a stacked performance.

“Should you be smoking that inside? You’re still a prefect during off-hours, you know,” Lily said from a couch over, glancing pointedly at the cigarette in Remus’ hand.

“Unless you’re trading places with me tomorrow as Regulus Black’s baby-sitter, you can sit with the smoke, Evans.”

“You’ll never get over that.”

“It’s training for the future. I’m practising holding a grudge.”

“You’re practising being a nob.”

Remus smiled to himself and took another drag before Mary leaned over to pluck it from his fingers.

“Speaking of Regulus,” she started, taking a drag; “I wonder how he’s taking all of this. Sirius being practically adopted by the Potters and all that.”

They all looked at Remus pointedly.

“I don’t know, okay?” He huffed. “We only have to do prefects’ stuff alone together a few times a month and he usually just refuses to speak to me.”

“What is it you’re doing tomorrow?” Marlene asked, tucking her toes up under his thigh. Marlene’s feet were always as cold as Lake Dubh.

“Music class,” Remus answered, unenthusiastically.

“Like teach?”

“Mhm. Primary music teacher took ill, and Sheila’s got choir practice. She asked if Regulus and I would do it instead. It was either that or gym class with the sixth years.”

“That’s brilliant though!” Lily applauded. “I bet you’ll be a great teacher.”

Remus didn’t bother discouraging her, but it was hard not to think about the sour face Regulus had put on when they’d been asked to step in. So far neither of them had managed to say a kind word to one another, though Remus hardly thought it his fault. He'd tried apologising to Regulus, but the younger boy stood firm in his resentment. Remus had even tried putting himself into his shoes for a bit—even if he and Sirius were constant adversaries, he couldn't imagine losing your only brother to some other family felt very nice—but Regulus wouldn't have it.

Just keep your big nose out of my business, he'd said, the last time they'd been paired up for duties. And Remus had immediately resolved himself to do just that. If Regulus was going to stay such a sour sod, then he could do it on his own.

“I hope we’re not late!” Sirius cried, appearing behind the rest of them. James followed a second laster, drumming his hands along the sofa back on either side of Remus’ head in excitement. Sirius was still sniffling a bit, but he quickly wiped his cheeks and no one tried shaming him for it.

“How’d it go then?” Mary asked happily. “You filthy rich again?”

“Positively mucky,” Sirius teased. Remus went to grab his cigarette back from Mary, but Sirius swung in, stealing it first.

“Monty’s lawyer said I could access the funds as soon as we get back to London," he said. "It's all mine baby. Full pay-out."

"And what is the first thing you're going to buy, now that you're rolling in it?" Asked Lottie.

"I know," Remus replied snidely, but Sirius had already given him a knowing look.

"The first thing I’m gonna do when we leave school is buy us a great big flat in the middle of the city, that way we can peddle our music all day and all night. And then, I'm upgrading the stereo—and then! ... A motorbike.”

"A motorbike?" Marlene exclaimed.

"Not this again," Peter groaned, still buried amongst the telly's wiring.

"He's been obsessed for weeks," Remus surmised, when the girls all turn to look at him. "Ever since Effie sent him that copy of the NME with a photo of Marc Bolan on the cover, riding some fancy bike."

"It was a Benelli seven-fifty, Moons! That's six-cylinders!"

"Marc Bolan," Mary echoed; "Ain't that the singer that just died?"

"No!" Sirius barked, waving his arms around. "I'll have no talk of Marc Bolan's death on my birthday! I'd much rather imagine him alive and poncy, as per usual—with me, myself, and I happy in my brand new flat, thank you very much."

"Good luck with that," Lily sniggered. "With the way you play music, I'll bet you'll have neighbours pounding on your front door within hours."

"I welcome the challenge! Perhaps they'll learn to appreciate the music of our generation," Sirius said, giving James a high-five of camaraderie.

“And what if they just complain?” Lottie sneered.

“Then I’ll buy their flat too. Then you girls can move in!”

“In that case I’ll be the one complaining,” Marlene said, just as Peter gave a great ‘A-HA!’ and the television’s screen cleared to reveal The Top of the Pops’ logo.

“It’s starting!” Lottie trilled, as Peter dove into the cushions in front, nearly upsetting one of the bowls of popcorn.

“Oh, shit—Moons!” James called right after. He jut his finger toward the dorm’s hallway. “Almost forgot, a call’s waiting for you.”

“Tomny?” He asked, suddenly hopeful.

“Uh-uh. Giles, I think.”

Remus settled back into the couch. “Oh, well don’t worry about it.”

“Shouldn’t you get it?” Marlene asked him.

“Nah, not interested. Been avoiding their calls. It’s just Dad wanting to preach about my marks anyway.”

“Smart move,” Sirius said, as James came around the side of the sofa and slid in next to Lily. Playfully, she reached up and twirled the strip of blonde in James’ hair around her finger, giggling when he kissed her wrist. James, ever the most-gracious prankster, had been the first to admit that he’d come around to the skunk-like appearance, even if his mum was likely to flay his arse when he got home. He was less impressed by Remus' new tattoo, but that could be said for most of them. Only Sirius had been excited by it—Sirius, who felt the need to drown himself in every societal-taboo he could get his hands on. Between talk of motorbikes and tattoos, Remus was starting to wonder what the odds were of Sirius moving to London and joining a gang, same as Tom.

Taking a moment to streak forward and toss the smoked cigarette into one of the other fireplaces, Sirius returned to the sofa and leaned over its back, trying to squeeze his arms in between Mary and Remus’ shoulders.

"C'moooan, Macdonald, budge up a bit!”

“You budge up, I'm comfortable,” Mary grumbled, busy watching the show’s host.

“It’s my birthday, you heartless hag.”

“Then sit in Remus’ lap or something.”

Appearing enticed by the idea, Sirius shot Remus a cheeky look before leaning forward, scooping Mary up around the middle and manoeuvring her onto his own lap as she shrieked in surprise. It was enough room for all of them that way, and Remus could feel Sirius pressed up against him from ankle to shoulder. If their friends weren't so close by, he'd have been tempted to do something about it.

“You’re impossibly cheeky,” Mary chastised, flicking Sirius in the nose as he kept hold of her around the waist.

“It’s why you love me,” Sirius said smugly, settling back into the sofa. As Mary shook her head and reached over to the popcorn bowl in James’ lap, Remus spared a glance to his right, gingerly, and found Sirius watching him.

"What?"

The show’s credits rolled and the girls all began to cheer at the flash of ABBA’s name. Still looking cheeky, Sirius leaned in.

“You haven’t given me anything for my birthday,” he whispered playfully.

“Gotta be alone first."

Sirius’ eyes flashed hungrily. ‘You’re filthy’ he mouthed, making Remus raise his eyebrows suggestively.

Suddenly a face appeared between them—Davey Gudgeon—and Remus nearly leapt a foot off the couch.

“Wicked! You guys got the telly in. Who they showing tonight?” The other boy asked, elbows propped up on the couch back.

“No one you—” James started, before Lily shoved a fistful of popcorn into his mouth.

“Queen, Bowie, ELO, Smokie,” Remus recited.

“And ABBA,” Lottie added.

“Champ!” Davey declared, before smacking Sirius on the shoulder. "Hey, heard it was your birthday, mate! Your guys' show on Halloween was ace too, by the way. Even you, Potter. Didn't know you and Pettigrew joined the group."

"Thanks, Gudgeon," James replied dully, mouth still full of popcorn.

In the end, Davey's entrance marked the first of many, and by the time they got to Queen’s promo, they’d been joined by a small army of kids. Word tended to get around fast when there was a telly available outside of weekends, and plenty of technologically-starved students from other Houses piled in, practically sitting on top of one another just for a chance to get a glimpse at the tiny screen. When Mercury’s eyeliner-clad image appeared, Sirius grabbed Remus around the shoulders and shook him in glee as everyone cheered and sang along.

“Turn it up, Pete!” Sirius cried.

The song was brilliant—a real stadium anthem. It touched that part of Remus deep inside that felt just like that little washout from Blackheath, the one desperate to fit in wherever he could. He wasn't sure how he felt about Mercury's choice of spandex, but it was cool enough to leave Sirius enraptured.

"Just look how his mouth moves!" he crowed. "Man, if I could sing like that..."

Remus didn't say it, at the risk of embarrassment, but he thought that if Sirius wanted to, he could've sung just like that. And apparently he wasn't the only one. All around them kids leaned in to smack Sirius on the shoulders in eager praise, joining in when he began to belt out the lyrics with soppy dedication.

“We are the champions! We are the champiooons! No time for looosers—! ‘Cause we are the champioooons—! Of the woooorld!”

It was pure adrenaline—it was why Remus loved Queen. And then Bowie came on, and he knew instantly why Sirius loved him. It was the title track from his latest album, Heroes, which they must have listened to half a million times already, but seeing it performed live—there was nothing like it. As the Starman's gentle tenor spread out from the telly's speakers, James hushed the common room. Instantly every kid became slack-jawed with awe, and Sirius went instantly still. He was gone for it, a total fan. Watching him watch Bowie was like watching an artist marvel at his favourite masterpiece, and when Bowie hit his falsetto Remus was rewarded for his dedication when he felt Sirius shiver against his shoulder.





‘And the shame was on the other side,

Oh, we can beat them forever and ever,

Then we could be heroes just for one day!’





Heroes. He liked the song. It was his favourite, he decided. But compared to the thrill he got from watching Sirius, it was all rather null. Slipping his hand down between them and the couch, Remus chanced the moment where he could hold Sirius’ hand and feel the strength of his emotions in the gentle tremor of his fingers. This was what they were, what they were determined to be.

Champions and Heroes.

“I wonder what that felt like,” Sirius whispered, turning his face into Remus’ shoulder so his lips brushed him as he spoke; “To be there. To sing like that.”

As the song came to a close, replaced by the loud bleating of Showaddywaddy and the other kids around the common room, Remus leaned into Sirius’ ear, hidden out of sight by the high-backed sofa and Mary’s hair.

“You’ll know,” he told him, “one day.”

He left the barest breath of a kiss on Sirius' cheek and very quickly pulled back, refusing to meet his gaze for the rest of the song. It was embarrassment, but Sirius quelled all of it when licked his finger and stuck it in his ear in retaliation.

“I can’t believe that’s the single they chose to show on television,” Sirius said, once they’d all sat through ABBA’s promo and the show had ended. “ ‘What’s the name of the game?’ Try, ‘he’s just not that interested, doll’.”

Mary spun around in Sirius’ lap and smacked his shoulder. “I swear, you’re the most unromantic musician I’ve ever met.”

“You say that as if you’ve actually met other musicians.”

She hit him again.

James hopped up from the couch. “Can you stop being a tosser long enough to sing or are we gonna have to start recruiting?”

A gasp went up from all of the girls, as well as several others.

“You mean you’re singing tonight?” Lily asked.

Sirius glanced at Remus and gave a nonchalant shrug. “We got to talking yesterday—as we were cleaning up our dorm room, I might add—thought it was kind of a shame we didn’t end up singing any of our own songs at the party.”

“Nooo—actually?” Mary spun around on Sirius’ lap again, nearly falling off the couch. “You mean you’re finally going to play something original?”

“Just one song,” Remus interjected sheepishly. “It’s Sirius’ birthday, so Sirius’ song.”

“I think you’ll like it,” Peter promised, hopping up and scuttling over the corner of the common room. Everyone turned around to watch as he dragged the sheet off of his drum kit, which they’d neglected to drag back to the music room for that very reason.

"Pardon me, love," Sirius said, before promptly flipping Mary off of his lap. She didn't even complain—too excited—and as the girls turned around on the sofa to watch, the four of them piled onto their instruments, flicking on the amps and testing each cord. It was a small crowd, made up of mostly Godric boys, but it was enough to leave Sirius looking giddy as he took up his microphone.

" 'ello, 'ello," he murmured, tapping the head until feedback echoed throughout the room.

"Yes, who's is it?" One of the boys chanted back, making everyone laugh. Sirius too, until he was practically shouting into the mike again.

“Oh, I almost forgot! Evans, you brought that camera 'a yours, right?”

Perking up, Lily nodded and reached over the side of the sofa for her bag. From there Remus got to watch as she pulled out her polaroid camera, cradled in its dingy leather case that was peeling at the corners. A hand-me-down from Petunia, she'd once told him.

“You want me to take photos while you play?” She offered, checking the film.

“Yes," Sirius drawled; "but I figured that now that I’m officially rolling in it on my own, I should send word back to Bath. Mum and Dad ought to know I'm doing alright for myself, yeah?”

“You mean to your parents-parents?” Remus asked gingerly.

“Precisely.” With a devious grin, Sirius grasped the mike and leaned in toward Lily as she held her camera up to her eye. “ ‘Toujours pur’ this, bitch,” he said, before licking the microphone and flipping the camera the bird. The entire room sniggered, and even Lily smirked as she snapped the photo.

“Like a real rock star,” Mary laughed.

“You’re cleaning that microphone,” Peter called after.

Sirius grinned, taking the photo from Lily and pocketing it. “Whatever you say, Wormy. Now you lot ready?”

The room cheered; ‘Yeah!’

“You don’t sound ready! I said—Are you ready?!”

“YEAH!”

“Alright then! This one’s called—”

James interrupted Sirius with a cheeky lick on the guitar, ripping up and down the strings and making everyone grin excitedly. “This is ‘Downtown Girls’!” He shouted.

“What the tosser said,” Sirius grinned. “Pete, be a dear and count us in.”





* * *





They were true to their word and only played the one song—except the girls liked it so much that they demanded that they play it twice more. They sounded better sober, but it wore on the nerves a lot more. By the end Remus’ fingers were tingling. Playing in front of others always brought a rush, but even he had to admit that there was just something about listening to people cheer for their own music. Lyrics and notes they’d created out of thin air—their art! It was validating somehow, like; Yeah, I did that! I did it with my friends—my band. Together.

A part of him wished he’d had enough courage to play the song he’d written for Sirius in front of everyone, but he hated his singing voice and was too worried about tripping up around the guitar. So he waited until late that night, when everyone else had gone to bed. By the time he was creeping back across their bedroom it was nearly midnight, a few precious minutes until it wasn’t Sirius’ birthday at all anymore. He wasn’t the least bit tired, and he knew Sirius wouldn’t be either, not after the looks they’d been giving each other all evening.

Sirius was slipping out from behind his curtains before Remus even made it to the foot of the bed, smile glowing in the blue light of the moon. While he grabbed a spare blanket, Remus nabbed Andy’s guitar case, enjoying the look of confusion that flitted across Sirius’ features. Together they slipped out of their bedroom, back down to the abandoned common room, where Sirius could finally moan and groan without anyone around to overhear.

“Fuck winter,” he hissed, shivering in front of the hearth as he prodded the fire back to life. Once they had a decent flame going, he joined Remus back on the couch, draping a wool blanket across their laps for extra warmth. Remus sighed happily, busy tracing patterns along Sirius’ ankle beneath the blanket. He’d left enough space between them just in case anyone wandered downstairs for a midnight snack, but their legs were tangled together, filling the space between them.

“This is nice,” he said.

“Mhm. You sure you’re not too tired though?” Sirius asked teasingly. “I know you have to be up early tomorrow.”

“It’s music class with a bunch of nine year-olds, not exams. I’ll be fine.”

“I meant spending time with my brother,” Sirius snorted. “Takes years off your life, that one.”

“Regulus is bearable,” Remus said, rubbing Sirius’ ankle beneath the blanket. “Have you thought about trying to talk to him at all?”

“He wouldn’t give me the time of day anyway.”

“Won’t know unless you try.”

Sirius nodded glumly. “Probably my job, right? Being the older brother and all that. I think I’m just bitter. It’s like—I see him and all I can think about is the damage. How fucked up we both are. And then he talks like he hates me and I know that the damage doesn’t even mean anything. It just means we’re wrecked. That we've lost.”

“Not lost," Remus said. "Maybe it just means that you could be better.”

Sirius’ eyes flickered to him, glowing in the light of the fire. “I think about him. I do—all of the time... but I don’t know how to talk to him.”

“Start with that then. Just be honest. Whenever you’re ready.”

Sirius took a deep breath. “Thanks, Moons. You always know just what to say. And you’re there for me, I don't think I've ever told you what that means.”

“You don't have to. I know."

They shared a small smile, and the tension broke a moment later, when Sirius sat up straighter on the couch and clapped his hands together. “Alright. You gonna tell me what this ‘surprise’ is now, or am I gonna have to guess? Because I’m guessing that it has something to do with Andy’s Gibson.”

“You’d be guessing right,” Remus said, glancing at the guitar they’d left sitting on the floor.

“Alright.” Sirius leaned down to pick up the acoustic. “What am I playing?”

“Well, actually…” Smiling shyly, Remus reached across the sofa and plucked the guitar from his boyfriend’s hands, setting it across his own lap.

“No way,” Sirius laughed. “You? Really?”

Remus shrugged. “I might’ve been doing some practising with James.”

“Colour me bloody… For me?”

He nodded, sheepish.

“Wow,” Sirius breathed. “What a great gift—never thought you’d look so sexy holding my guitar. Like a naked chick on a motorbike.”

“You’re so stupid.”

Sirius clapped his hands together once more in glee. “Well, fine then—go on! Don’t make me wait all night!”

Clearing his throat, Remus set his fingers on the strings. He hesitated, wondering why it was harder to play in front of Sirius than an entire common room of kids, and Sirius reached across and slid a comforting hand across his arm.

“Hey, it’s just me.”

Sirius’ touch gave Remus goosebumps, which he had to shake off to keep going. “Alright,” he said; “but remember, I’m not a singer.”

Sirius only smiled at him.

Straightening up, Remus took a deep breath and began to play. It was a slow melody, one of the ballads Sirius was always saying he’d be famous for one day, but he was too nervous to play any faster anyway.

Just do it, he told himself; Over the waterfall.





“Hey, I bet you’ve heard the rumours,

You can only guess which ones of them are true;

But I’ve always liked how you talk of future

Yeah, I’d go anywhere if you asked me to.”





He hit the bridge, and sparing a glance up at Sirius’ handsome face, Remus found a grin waiting for him.

“Beautiful,” Sirius gasped. "Christ..."

Keep going, he thought to himself. Don't stop now.





“You say want a nice place with enough space,

So we can sit and watch the sun rise and fall;

And talk about what comes next,

With you I’d do it all.”





Sirius’ lips parted. It was awe. Remus had to look down at the guitar to keep playing.





“And there’s that future, always haunting,

Hangin’ just out of our reach;

But if you had told me that you saw it,

I wouldn’t second guess your speech;

And I can only have you if you love me,

So tell me now, please don’t taunt me;

‘Cause I won’t reach for that future,

If it don’t include you and me;

How nice a future like that could be…”





He looked up again, voice filtering out; “How nice it could be…” and all it took was Sirius’ grey eyes, ignited orange by the fireside for his fingers to slip clumsily on the strings. Slouching forward with relief, Remus laughed inexplicably. He was almost wheezing, and when his nose whistled with a snort, Sirius laughed along with him.

“There’s more,” he fumbled, “but that’s the first bit. It'll probably sound better when you sing it.”

“No, it’s brilliant,” Sirius told him. “Brilliant like you.”

Sirius leaned in to kiss him, and Remus glanced at the doorway, just in case. Cheekily, Sirius pinched his chin in one hand.

“If you’re that worried, we could always go back into the cupboard.”

Remus sagged again, exasperated and in love, and took Sirius’ hand, placing a kiss on his palm before yanking the woollen blanket up over their heads. Hidden away, he could still see the glow of the fire peeking through the holes in its weaving, scattering little stars of orange light across Sirius’ face. It reminded him instantly of that final day in his bedroom on the Lupin Estate, where he got to watch the sun rise and fall on Sirius.

"I want to hear the rest," Sirius told him. "When you’re ready."

Oh yes.

“So bring me back to July,” Remus murmured; “Warm and rich with soft orange skies…”

Sirius began tracing a finger along Remus’ jaw. “Is that the next line?”

“No, it’s something else,” he whispered, closing the space between them and kissing his love tenderly.

“Happy birthday, Sirius.”





* * *





Friday 4th November 1977





Remus wasn’t used to arriving first. Normally, Regulus was on the premises ages before he’d even considered how long it was going to take him to walk from point A to point B. This time though, Remus found himself waiting for his partner outside the colourful Hufflepuff building, fingers itching for a smoke. The eastern half of campus, kept for the primaries, was completely akin to its western brick and mortar counterpart, except that the pavement was constantly covered in colourful chalk drawings and everything was built to be no higher than Remus’ shoulder.

He was starting to wonder if he’d finally reached the day that Regulus Black had skived off from his prefect duties when the youngest Black brother came stomping up the pavement, his violin case tucked under one arm and a stack of music sheets held precariously in the other.

“Unlike you to be running late,” Remus teased lightly. “Class doesn’t start for another ten minutes.”

“Photocopier jammed,” Regulus huffed, missing the joke.

Adjusting Sirius’ acoustic on his shoulder, Remus opened the door for him and eyed the sheet music as Regulus passed. The staves looked a lot like what James would call “mouse tracks”, endless signatures, ties, and looping notes.

“You’re not gonna try and teach them that, are you?” He asked warily, following the other boy down the hall.

“It’s only the chorus portion of ‘Für Elise’. Some of Beethoven’s simplest stuff.”

“They’re nine.”

“I was playing this at five.”

“Do you know how insufferable you sound?”

Regulus rolled his eyes. “We’re here to teach them, aren’t we? We don’t even need a piano for this.”

Remus gestured about the hallway, at its array of colourful student cubbies and the tiny wellies that sat beneath each. “Yes well, I don’t know about you, but I don’t exactly see many Stradivarius violas sitting around. We’re just supposed to be supervising the class—you know, let them bang their drums for an hour and then go home.”

“You mean you’re okay with just making noise and leaving it at that? Some musician.”

“Whatever,” Remus scoffed. “Do what you want, I’m not going to fight with you.”

Regulus turned his nose up. “Suits me just fine, you can sit in the corner and watch. Maybe you’ll actually learn something.”

Remus didn’t get the chance to fire back a retort; ahead of them, a door opened and a stout woman slipped out, slamming the door after herself. She straightened up when she spotted them, adjusting her blouse. There was a smear of paint on her cheek.

“Ah! Are you two the prefect students they sent over for music period?”

“Yes…?” Remus answered, regretfully.

“Oh good!” She plastered a smile on her face and surged towards them, blazing right past. “I’m just the secretary—and you’re just in time for my tea break. The kids have been darling angels today. They’ve already got their instruments out—I’m sure a few stern words will have them in tip-top shape. Have fun with the lesson, see you in an hour!”

Before they could so much as say something, the secretary was halfway down the hall, waving as she turned a corner and disappeared out of sight.

“Is she allowed to do that?” Remus asked. "Just... leave?"

“C’mon,” Regulus just grumbled; “Before they set the curtains on fire or something.”

Following each other down the hall, they opened the door and strode inside. The kids were clearly surprised to see them; as the chatter came to an abrupt halt, twenty pairs of eyes turned on them in question, various instruments and noise-makers already in hand. No sooner had Remus shut the door behind himself did he have a child before him. The boy was rather chubby around the middle, with a whip of wheat-blonde hair on top of his head, and he was looking at Remus like he'd just arrived on a spaceship and demanded to be taken to his 'leader'.

“Er—hey man.”

“You’re not Mrs. Bean,” the boy said indignantly.

“Nope, I’m not.”

“Where’s Mrs. Bean?”

“Off for the day,” Regulus answered cuttingly. Holding his violin aloft as though afraid their tiny hands might obliterate it with the slightest touch, he weaved through the kids’ seats until he’d made it to the front band stand of the music classroom.

“I’m Mr. Bl—” Regulus flinched as one of the kids blew horribly on a recorder. He glared at the boy until he looked next to tears, and then cleared his throat again. “I’m Mr. Black. Lupin here, and I have been appointed as your music instructors for the afternoon.”

“You’re really tall,” a girl up the front shouted at Remus.

“Do you talk out of turn in front of Mrs. Bean?” Regulus asked her.

“You’re really short,” the girl shot back, making Remus snort and therefore allowing the entire class to descend into a furious giggle-fit.

"Five-foot-nine is not short."

Remus resisted the urge to burst out laughing. If only Sirius could hear how alike they truly sounded.

“Rich kids, eh, Reg? Can’t live with ‘em, can’t teach ‘em.”

Regulus ignored him, clearing his throat furiously and holding up his stack of music sheets, which he kept rearranging into different orders. “We’re here to learn. I’ve brought with me a piece even a stray dog could learn to play. Now does anyone recognise these staves?”

A paper ball flew through the air and smacked Regulus in the side of the head. His eyes widened, and Remus watched as his face turned a raging red.

“Who threw that?”

The kids burst into laughter.

Before Regulus could lose his mind entirely, Remus intercepted, stepping in front of the band stand and leaning over it. “Reg, they’re kids. I'm pretty sure they can smell fear. Don’t let them get to you.”

“They aren’t!”

“Then maybe try levelling-out some, okay?” Gingerly, Remus took a step back and faced the class, awkwardly clearing his own throat. “Okay, well, can anyone tell me what you were last practising with Mrs. Bean?”

One of the girls held up a hand, her clarinet balanced precariously in her lap; “We were practising ‘Daisies in the Meadow’.”

“Christ,” Regulus said under his breath.

“ ‘Daisies in the Meadow’,” Remus mused, slouching back on an empty desk in the corner of the classroom, “sounds quite captivating, don’t you agree, Mr. Black?”

Regulus gave him a sharp side-eye and came around the front of the band stand. “Alright, fine. Who’s got the sheet music?”

There was a bit of rustling, and one of the kids from the flutes section handed him a doodle-encrusted paper. The song was apparently not up to par with Regulus’ expectations, as his shoulders sank in disappointment while he passed the tablature back to the fifth year.

“Fine, whatever, let’s hear it then. Trumpets, give me an E flat.”

Rather than the correct note, Regulus was promptly answered when one of the students gave a horrible fart, letting it rip across the classroom as all the kids shrieked in horror and delight.

“Sounded more like a low-G to me,” Remus cackled.

Regulus rounded on him. “You’re supposed to be helping me!”

“I’m sitting in the corner like you told me to! Maybe if you asked nicely…”

“Not on your life, Loony.”

Remus shrugged and leaned down, popping the clasps on Andy’s guitar case and pulling out the beaten-up acoustic. It was certainly well-loved (Sirius had let Peter sketch flowers along the side of his body ages ago and the strap was fraying at both ends) but Remus set it across his lap anyway and tucked a pick between his teeth as he fiddled with the tuning. When he looked up he found nearly every set of eyes on him, kids craning their necks to get a look at the guitar. Even Regulus had paused, eyeing the instrument the way he always did when Remus brought it around. It was hard sometimes to remember that he was Andy’s cousin too.

Remus pulled the pick from his lips and scanned the room. “How long have you guys been practising ‘Daisies in the Meadow’?”

“Since September,” one of the kids called.

“Bloody hell,” Regulus muttered.

“He said a bad word!”

Remus stood up from his corner desk, throwing the guitar strap over his shoulder. “Okay, who here actually likes ‘Daisies in the Meadow’?”

None of the kids raised their hands.

“Well, who likes listening to music?”

Hands shot skyward.

“That’s what I thought. See, Mr. Black and I really love music, and if you keep up with it long enough, one day you’ll be able to play whatever you want, whenever you want. Like—” He hit the first several notes of “Smoke On the Water”, because he knew it would make Regulus pucker, and not a single laugh or childish shriek interrupted him; “Like that. But really, I’m just an amateur—you should hear Mr. Black. He's practically a virtuoso.”

Remus looked back at Regulus, who suddenly appeared rather nervous to be put on the spot. The kids leaned forward in their seats, utterly hooked.

"It's nothing," Regulus stammered. "Anyone can play a few basic notes."

“Really? Hm. Well, no need to be humble now.” Smirking, Remus stood up and addressed the room. “I want to hear Mr. Black play, how ‘bout you guys?”

The nods were slower, but eventually kids were calling out faintly. Remus thought of Sirius, who would never have accepted such a lacklustre response. “I can’t really hear you,” he started again, “I said, I want to hear Mr. Black play, now how about you?!”

The chorus came more fervently, and Regulus looked about ready to cave in on himself.

“Well, Reg? You heard ‘em,” Remus smiled.

Tapping his fingers against his palms nervously, Regulus finally relented. He reached for his violin case, withdrawing a beautiful violin the colour of mahogany wood and burnt sugar. It was a magnificent instrument; it would’ve been such a shame to have ended up at the bottom of the lake. When he pulled out the matching bow, a little girl from the brass section held up her hand.

“Er—yes, what’s your name?” Remus asked.

“Charlotte."

“One of my best friends is named Charlotte," Remus said. "What’s your question?”

“It’s not a question,” the girl murmured. "I just wanted to know if Mr. Black knew ‘Swan Lake’.”

He turned to Regulus. “Do you?”

“Obviously,” Regulus said flatly. He might’ve called it too simple, or too beneath his station, had Charlotte not been instantly smiling from ear-to-ear.

Pushing his dark hair out of his face, Regulus took up his spot at the front of the class, carefully tucking his violin beneath that primly-chiselled chin. When he set his bow against the strings, it became clear that all of the nerves had drained from him. When he played his eyes were closed; drifting. Remus wondered what he pictured.

The piece was perfection, naturally. Regulus played the theme’s introduction with flawless precision, stopping just before the crescendo as though he knew the exact way to edge his desperate audience into needing more. None of the kids booed him, they were too much in awe. Remus too.

“Fantastic,” he smiled, clapping and earning Regulus an ovation he sheepishly accepted. “Wouldn’t it be cool to just be able to do that?” Remus asked the class. “Should we do that—just pick a song and play it?”

There was a rallying cry of agreement and he wracked his brain for something age-appropriate to play. It had to be easy, since they had no time and no sheet music, but when the idea came to him, it was brilliant.

As Regulus set his violin down, Remus leaned in, whispering his idea into his ear.

“How is that any better than bloody ‘Daisies in the Meadow’?” Regulus demanded immediately.

“It’s fun, Reg. It’s a song they’ll know, and we only have to do the chorus.”

“Go on then. Since you’re so clearly enjoying yourself.”

Remus couldn’t deny it. He’d scoffed at Lily when she’d said he would make a good teacher, having no real experience with kids, but it’d been a while since he’d felt so needlessly silly, and he wanted to make the most of it. The kids would like it, he was sure, but he still needed Regulus’ help.

“C’mon, you’re the protégé—I know you know how to play more that just that violin. And you know how to translate all the notes! I can’t do it without you...”

Regulus’ steel-grey eyes widened a bit, and he looked back to his violin. “Do you at least know how to play it on that dingy guitar of yours? I'm not teaching you too.”

“Hell yeah, I do,” Remus grinned, before grabbing a scrap piece of paper off the teacher’s podium and hastily scribbling out a stave of notes for Regulus to see. He sighed, grumpy for the sake of being grumpy, but took the sheet and turned around to tackle the task at hand. After that it was easy. Remus took the percussion section, while Regulus weaved between the rows of kids, correcting the way they held their instruments and helping them fumble through the correct notes. They’d toned the level of difficulty down a bit more—until it was only the most basic sounds—but eventually after much squeaking and squawking, they had music.

“Okay!” Remus declared, clapping his hands to draw the kids’ attention back to the front of the room. “I actually feel really confident about this, how ‘bout you, Mr. Black?”

“Time will tell, I guess,” Regulus answered, picking up the conductor’s baton.

Remus turned back to the class. “Remember, we don’t need it to be perfect. Noise—music—it’s all a matter of opinion.”

“Or taste,” Regulus muttered.

A girl named Angeline raised his hand. “Can we sing along?”

“Of course! In fact I expect it—from you too, Mr. Black!”

“Yeah, fat chance.”

The kids laughed, and Remus did too, but Regulus just rapped the baton against the podium, clearing his throat.

“And a one, and a two—”

The rallying noise that exploded was nothing like the song they’d just spent the better half of the hour practising. Regulus shivered all over in revulsion, and instantly Remus held up a hand, half-laughing as the hooting trumpets and blaring trombones came to a shrieking halt.

“Maybe we shouldn’t count in,” he offered.

Instead of fighting him, Regulus nodded. “Anything’s better than that.”

“But it was a great start!” Remus trilled quickly, as all the kids stared up at them. “How about we try something else?” Slowly, he started snapping his fingers along with the beat, humming as well. Twenty tiny heads bobbed after him, fingers twitching around their instruments.

“Add in the timpani,” Regulus advised.

Remus nodded, and pointed to the percussion section. “Douglas, he means the really big drum just there. Can you beat it along with my snapping, like we practised?”

The nine year-old nodded and took up his mallet, banging along spectacularly.

“Now cymbals on count four,” Regulus said. “You there—”

“Marley,” Remus offered.

“Marley,” Regulus tried again, “use your pedals to—”

Before he’d even finished, the little girl was clapping away, a huge smile on her face.

“There, that sounds great!” Remus cried.

Regulus had placed a hand over his mouth thoughtfully, staring down the expectant class like Sheila during one of their own lessons. “I want to hear clarinets now, four G notes, high-A, and four D.”

There were only two clarinets in the class, and both tripped up their high-A, but Remus high-fived the kids when they were finished. One by one they went through every section as a class, adding them together until finally they had something that was more akin to music than noise.

“This is fantastic,” he said when they’d finished, eagerly scooping up his guitar and standing at the front of the class. “What do you guys say we run through it together?”

As the kids trilled enthusiastically, Remus elbowed Regulus. “You gonna play with us? Only if it’s not too hard for you, that is.”

Arching a brow, Regulus picked up his violin, and together they faced the class.

“I hope those of you who can will sing with me,” Remus said, before smiling. “One, two, three—Weeeeee… all live in a yellow submarine! A yellow submarine, yellow submarine!”

And just like that the class was playing. Those who could sing, did, and Remus wasn’t the least bit ashamed. He spent so much of his time playing the pessimistic, hesitant asshole, that right then it didn’t matter if he was embarrassed or not. He was just an idiot making noise.

“We all live in a yellow submarine! A yellow submarine, yellow submarine!”

The cymbals clashed until their ears twinged—the drums drummed until the floor shook. There was more squeaking and squawking than ever but they were all squeaking and squawking together. It wasn’t magnificent—wasn’t even that good, but they were nine and happy and making noise; what else could you ask from such small, eager musicians?

“This is going to be stuck in my head until I’m ninety!” Regulus shouted at him without missing a beat.

“Then you’ll have lived a full life!” Remus added; “—A yellow submarine, yellow submarine…!”

They played and played until the secretary finally reappeared, looking distinctly less rumpled but exceedingly shocked to find that they’d managed to get the kids to sit still long enough for an entire lesson.

“Well, aren’t I just chuffed to bits!” She preened. “You two are miracle workers! They should have you back here every week.”

Remus laughed nervously and quickly tucked Andy’s guitar away as the secretary began setting the kids to clean-up. Taking a moment to watch them stack chairs and band stands, he crept over to Regulus’ side as he gathered the music sheets he’d brought with him back into a pile. “Sorry we never got to play any Beethoven, but you have to admit, it was pretty brilliant.”

“It was terrible,” Regulus answered lightly.

“Okay, we’ll compromise—it was ‘brilliantly terrible’.”

He might’ve been seeing things—a side effect of staying up the entire night before with Sirius—but for the briefest moment Regulus actually smiled, dropping his head down and shaking it lightly. Not a dismissal—a friendly exasperation. Somehow, it was refreshing to see.

As Regulus tried to hide his pleased indifference, Charlotte appeared beside him, tugging on his Salazar-green jumper and making him whirl around to face her.

“Is it hard to play the violin?” She asked, all big brown eyes.

“Of cour—” Regulus caught himself, swallowing tensely. “Not… if you’re willing to put the work in. It’s hard work.”

“If I work hard, will you come teach us again?”

Regulus didn’t seem to know what to say to that. It took him several moments to manage; “Uhm… sure.”

Charlotte nodded eagerly and spun on her heel to join her classmates, while Remus just watched in amusement, slinging his guitar up over his shoulder. Regulus caught the look grimly.

“Shut up.”

“I didn’t say anything!”

“You were thinking it!”

“A violin master and a mind reader—is there anything you can’t do?”

Scoffing—albeit more light-heartedly—Regulus picked up his violin and together they said goodbye to the class and the secretary, making their way out into the hall.

“You talk differently with children,” Regulus said eventually, as they passed row after row of colourful cubbies.

“Yeah well, kids can be trusted. They’re honest, and you never have to wonder what they’re thinking. They’re better people than most adults.”

Regulus was quiet, and eventually they emerged on the outside of the building, both blinded by the light of the midday sun. Remus had assumed that with the lesson over, Regulus would leave him there without so much as a goodbye, but he was surprised when he looked back to find him standing there, nervously digging the toe of his shoe into the pavement.

"That was... fun, right?"

Regulus grunted back, still not looking at him. Remus squinted his eyes, considering his options. He could just leave, but then...

Goddammit.

“Reg, if I were to ask you if you actually liked music, what would you say?”

“That I do,” Regulus replied, snapping his head up without a hint's hesitation.

“Alright, why?”

“Why do you?”

“Because it’s something I can do with my friends," he answered. "And because it helps turn everything else off.”

Regulus made a face, and Remus rushed to extrapolate;

“I just mean that when I’m playing, I don’t have to worry about anything else.”

“You’re not worried about sounding awful?”

“Oh, I’m worried,” he laughed; “but there are worse things than sounding awful.”

Regulus paused and then stepped past him. He strode forward a bit, like he meant to leave him there after all, before turning around abruptly and giving Remus a hard look.

“I like jazz.”

The confession surprised Remus, to say the least. “I like jazz too. Do you have a favourite?”

“Miles Davis.”

“He’s amazing. You have good taste. Is there… anything else you want me to know about you?”

Regulus hesitated, but then; “I don’t like being called ‘Reg’.”

Remus’ lips parted for a moment, before he nodded. “Okay, what do you want me to call you then?”

“Just Regulus.”

“Well, alright then. It’s a pleasure to meet you, Regulus Black." Feeling a bit stupid, he held out his hand. "I’m Remus."

He'd really only expected Regulus to scoff and turn away, but Remus should've known better.

Never underestimate a Black.

He watched as Regulus came forward, tucking his sheet music under one arm and taking a deep breath. Then he reached out and took Remus' hand, and giving it the barest squeeze.

“Pleasure to meet you too, Remus Lupin.”

Happily, Remus squeezed back.



Chapter End Notes

Songs: "We Are the Champions" by Queen, 1977 & "Heroes" by David Bowie, 1977. Both are links to 'Top of the Pops' videos that would've been shown on Sirius' actual eighteenth birthday <3

Chapter 79: The Long Week


Chapter Summary

Mid-November, and it's as though the entire school is in a tizzy. Remus assumes he's made it through relatively unscathed, but life has a way of keeping things interesting.



Chapter Notes

CW: Fat chapter, with smoking and brief allusions to violence and sexual content.

So... got this out a bit late, but better late than never. Also, some of you will see that I did let "Almost Famous" inspire me a little bit with that one 'Rolling Stone' scene, hehe. Happy reading x



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Vicious,

You want me to hit you with a stick,

But all I’ve got’s a guitar pick;

Huh, baby, you’re so vicious…

- “Vicious” Lou Reed, 1972



Tuesday 14th November 1977





“It’s no use! Mock exams are right around the corner and I can’t retain any of it! I might as well give up now…” With a heavy moan, Lily pressed her forehead onto her open law textbook, stifling all chances of studying. Another library goer shushed her, and she lifted her head just long enough to shoot them a nasty glare.

“Five minutes ago you were just lecturing us on the importance of flash cards,” Marlene replied dully. Across the table, Remus cracked a small smile. Lily’s habit of switching between stark reinforcement and utter despair was entertaining to say the least.

“Seven years,” the red-head whimpered; “Seven years at this godforsaken school and I haven’t learned enough to fill a thimble!”

“It’s only November,” Remus reminded her. “I’m sure you’ll reach thimble capacity before uni applications are due.”

“No!” She practically shrieked. “Applications have to be in before Christmas. Otherwise, you might as well throw them in the bin! We’re already considered too far away to attend interviews—we have to impress on paper or we haven’t got a chance.”

“If you actually plan to apply, that is,” Marlene remarked, eyeing Remus pointedly.

She was right of course. As busy as he was between their exams, musical affairs, and Sirius affairs, Remus was not worried. He had no plans to apply for university. He was going to be in a band.

“Shhhh!”

Madam Pince appeared next to their table, scowling venomously, and all three of them cowered until she’d finally moved on.

“I’ve only got practice until six,” Marlene whispered. “We could study again afterwards. Lupin, you want in?”

Remus shook his head. “Can't, got plans. Band stuff.”

It wasn’t a total lie. The night before, all four Marauders had agreed that it was finally time to nail down exactly what it was they were going to say to get their families to agree to a life of pursuing music. James planned on pitching the idea as a gap year; they’d take a single year off and if nothing came of Marauders, then he’d go to uni and make something out of himself. Remus had initially thought it a bit of a gamble—a year was mere plonk change in the record industry—but James didn’t appear worried. In fact, out of all of them, Peter’s parents seemed to be the hardest sell. Mr. Pettigrew was a working man through and through, and although he’d been behind a desk at his newspaper company for many years now, he’d been preaching the value of a hard day’s work for as long as his children could remember.

Sirius had it a bit easier. Though he'd received no word as to whether or not he'd been officially disowned by his family, he still wanted to appease the Potters—but then again, no one was going to blame him for following music. He was a prodigy. And as for Remus, well… he was never going to accomplish what Lyall Lupin wanted of him anyway. He just hoped Giles took the news alright. It was enough for Remus just to lounge around in surreptitious bliss, which he did on the floor of their dorm room, gorging on tarts sent by Effie and listening to Dr. Hook play off the stereo.





‘We take all kinds of pills, that give us all kind of thrills,

But the thrill we’ve never known;

Is the thrill that’ll getcha when you get your picture,

On the cover of the Rollin’ Stone…’





Next to him, Remus watched as Peter licked the jam from his fingers while pouring over his open notebook. Homework aside, the other boy had written and rewritten his 'gap year' pitch about twelve times, though Remus doubted it was bound to get any better. If they didn't have this in the bag by now, then Marauders wasn't going to get anywhere.

“You’re so lucky, Remus,” Peter said, when he'd caught him staring.

“He’s lucky his dad don’t give a shit about him?” Sirius replied dryly, trying and failing to roll a spliff on the back of his Latin text.

“No! He’s lucky he don’t have to hear him bleat about it at all hours. My dad’s called three times this week just to ask me about my maths.”

“Mine did too,” Remus said, taking the spliff from Sirius and easily finishing up the sides for him. “I just never picked up.”

James nudged Peter with his foot. “I guess that’s the difference, hey Pete?”

“Go on, yack it up. Not all of us can play the delinquent where our parents are concerned. I stop picking up and the next thing I know, Dad’ll have me pulling twelve hour shifts in the printer’s basement!”

“Could be worse,” Sirius reasoned, taking back the finished spliff; “You could be designated mail room bitch.”

They all shared a shameless chuckle, while Peter huffed and reached for another tart.

“Just you wait,” Sirius urged him; “this is gonna be fucking brilliant. A whole year off, with nothing to do but make music! And then once we've cut a demo, we can send it out to all the biggest reps in the country and wait for the offers to start pouring in.”

"Come on," James said, "that's a bit far-fetched, even for you."

"Yeah, no way it's gonna be that easy," Peter chipped in. "Besides, most of us are still learning our damn instruments."

"Who gives a shit about that? None of the Pistols could play their instruments, and they got a deal before they'd even added 'Sex' to the name!"

Remus, already rolling a second spliff for himself, shot Sirius a brazen look. "Yeah, well I don't want to be like the Sex Pistols," he said. "I want to be better."

"Obviously!" Sirius crooned. "We're gonna blow that prissy 'New Wave British Heavy Metal' out of the water! I'm talking billboards as big as the buildings they're printed on! Our faces plastered along Piccadilly Circus and Times Square! ‘Top of the Pops’, ‘American Bandstand’, and then some!"

"And what shall we do in-between all of that?" James asked. "Toothpaste adverts?"

"If it fits your fancy." Smirking, Sirius raised the spliff to his lips but paused at the last second and reached for the stereo’s volume dial. The next thing they knew, the speakers were blaring, and he was singing along.

“ ‘We got all the friends that money can buy, so we never have to be alone. And we keep gettin' richer but we can't get our picture—!'”

Unable to help himself, Remus belted out; “ ‘On the cover of the Rollin' Stone!’”

"Fuck yeah!" Sirius cried. "That's it!"

A second later and James and Peter had jumped to their feet. “Wanna see my picture on the cover!'”

Sirius joined them; “ ‘Wanna buy five copies for my mother!'”

“ ‘Wanna see my smilin’ face—ON THE COVER OF THE ROLLIN’ STONE!' ”

They all laughed and shoved each other, which was just brotherhood for love and endearment, and just like that it wasn’t about exams or parents or money anymore, it was just about the music. As the song ended and James went to change the tape, Sirius crouched down ahead of Remus and set the spliff between his lips.

“Whaddya say, Moons?” He mumbled around the filter; “Feel like being on the cover of ‘Rolling Stone’?”

Remus raised his zippo, lighting the tip of Sirius’ spliff and grinning at him over the flame.

“Sounds good to me.”

Sirius breathed in, and when he was done, turned the joint around for Remus to smoke right off of his fingers. And Remus did so, wishing horribly that it were Sirius’ lips he were feeling instead.

They’d been better lately, about including their friends in whatever relationship they sought to maintain. Every secret escapade was strategically planned, and they’d learned not to be greedy. James was showing no further signs of jealousy and Peter seemed to be blissfully unaware, as per usual, but aside from that, their continued efforts had resulted in a growing lack of sleep. Remus had always been a shit sleeper, but now that things were good again, he and Sirius were spending all of their late hours sneaking into each other’s beds—anything just to have a moment alone. When he did manage some shut-eye, Remus practically slept with his songbook under his pillow—poised for any idea that might happen to come along at the most inopportune moment. Though, it had the added benefit of keeping any and all sticky fingers at bay. Sirius was a real curtain twitcher when it came to songwriting, and despite serenading him on his birthday, Remus wasn't sure he was quite ready to give up all of his secrets just yet.

Perhaps the lack of personal time might've been cause for alarm once, but now that they were all well and truly on the same page (or as close as they could get whilst remaining in the closet—revere the closet) Remus wasn’t all that worried. If the youngest Black brother’s recent lack of total aversion for him was anything to go by, then he’d even managed to make a breakthrough where Regulus was concerned. Yes, life was good. Not even Snape had come within twenty feet of them since the bucket incident, which left only one visible downside.

It was time to say goodbye to the East End. For good. There was no place for him there anymore, save maybe Tomny's love. Remus had realised it sometime in early November, after another chat with his oldest friend had taken a glum turn. They hadn’t fought or anything of the like, but he could tell by the way Tomny talked that things were still not ideal. And it was the same thing later that night. After the spliffs and jam tarts, Remus had slunk down to the ground floor to ring him, and was greeted with a Tomny that sounded as ragged and worn as an old tire.

“Things are jus’ busy nowadays,” he said. “And you know me—hate the cold. Can't never stop fuckin' coughin'. But don’t worry yerself, Lu. S'normal!”

“And Lee? How's he?” Remus had asked, once he’d plucked up the courage to say his name.

“Lee is… Well. Lee’s Lee. You know ‘im.”

Not anymore.

He told himself to get over it. Remus had never had a brother, but he had Tomny. And that was enough. He just hoped that Lee and the other boys would find some way to be happy.

“It won’t last,” Sirius told him afterwards. He'd taken up a spot on the bottom of the stairs, but they were alone in the hallway, and rather than being annoyed that Sirius had followed him downstairs despite his wishes, Remus found that he was grateful. He glanced back at his boyfriend, setting the phone back on its hook.

“What won’t?”

“The feeling… like they’re forgetting you. It’ll fade. I promise.”

“And if it don’t?”

Sirius stood, smiling quietly. He pattered over in naught but his socks and grabbed Remus by the belt loops, tugging them together.

“You worry too much.”

Remus arched a brow. “And you don’t worry enough.”

“Yeah, you’re right. But that's what makes us work. We balance each other. Like a jack and coke.”

“You couldn't have tried for a music reference? Lennon and McCartney...?”

“Mm… in that case, I’d say more like Jagger and Richards.” Sirius smirked, and then glanced around to make sure they were really alone. He kissed him then, briskly and with that perfect Sirius mouth that Remus dreamed of every night. It was almost funny—the idea that something as tumultuous as their relationship could bring balance. He loved all parts of Sirius, even the insane, unreasonable half of him that was always getting them into trouble. He never knew what to expect or when he should be expecting it, but that was half the fun; if not all the more reason to worry.

Hard to worry when you were dead asleep, though.

BEEP—BEEP—BEEP!

Morning had come, and Remus lifted a heavy eyelid, letting out a long groan.He could still feel the faint effects of the whisky bottle James had unceremoniously opened upon his and Sirius’ return to the dorm room. Things often went that way whenever one of them was feeling sorry for themselves.

BEEP—BEEP—BEEP!

“Potteeeer!” He moaned through his bed curtains; “Turn off the bleedin’ alarm, you great git! Not everyone likes goes for five-AM runs…”

“It’s six-thirty,” James fired back, before the alarm was mercifully silenced.

Like most mornings, Remus turned over and collapsed back into his pillow for a few more precious moments of sleep. Distantly, past the cover of his bed curtains, he could hear the sounds of his friend as he puttered about the room. Remus could picture it perfectly; a creature of habit, James would first pop his joints with a stretch, then put on his glasses and head into the bathroom. (He also kissed the photo of Lily good morning too, but they weren’t supposed to talk about that.)

Once he’d pretend to run a comb through his hair, James would reappear and stop to open Peter’s curtains the tiniest bit, cooing a gentle good morning at him. (He never tried this with Remus, for good reason.) He would end his rounds with Sirius, though his greeting was usually more along the lines of ‘up and at ‘em, you handsome prig’ and not at all like—

“I’m sure he tells you enough.”

Remus scratched the side of his head, reminded of the reason why so many of Sirius’ relatives went into politics. They certainly had the tongue for it.

Then an idea hit him.

“Hey, Regulus, do you want to come home with us for Christmas?”

Regulus’ eyes shot wide. “Excuse me?”

“We’re going back to James’. You could come too.”

“You want me to follow you back to… to Potters’ house?!”

“Why not?”

“I could give you a thousand reasons why not.”

“Okay… but isn’t there at least one reason to come? You could get away for a while. See what it’s like to be happy for a change.”

If he was more sober, Remus might’ve realised that this was not the thing to say.

“You’re all the same,” Regulus said, picking up an armful of leaves. “You think anyone who’s not you must be miserable. But I don’t need to be like my brother. I know Sirius, and the phrase ‘blood is thicker than water’ only applies when he wants it to. Now do us all a favour and stop meddling.”

Remus was at a loss. He said nothing more as Regulus strolled away from him—just watched as he tossed the leaves onto their large pile.

“Where’s MacDuff?” Regulus demanded.

Jillian hid a giggle behind her hand. “I dunno.”

“She was just here! We still have half a lawn left to rake.”

“Maybe she needed to use the lav.”

Regulus scoffed, probably well on his way to chastising his classmate for skiving off, when Trish suddenly burst forth from the pile—scattering leaves everywhere and screaming blue murder. The fright was enough to leave Regulus gasping for breath, but by then Trish was already bent over and laughing herself to tears.

“Your face!” She howled. “You should’ve seen your face!”

“You—! How dare you!"

“ ‘How dare I’? Crivvens, who are you, my gran?”

“I’m the only sane one here apparently!” Regulus shouted back. “God, it’s like taking care of children! Can’t you people do anything right?!”

“You’d be surprised, o’ m’laird,” Trish replied, crossing her arms over her chest. “Maybe if you came down from yer high horse every now ‘n then you’d see the world like us wee folk do.”

“And I suppose you think that’s rather smart of you!”

“Tis certainly getting under your skin well enough.”

Regulus fumed. “Why anyone would ever like you, I’ll never understand!”

“Oi, oi,” Remus called, stepping in between them. “C’mon, Reg. That’s a bit uncalled for, don’t you think?”

He hadn’t expected the shove, but it came anyway and Remus had to stumble to avoid crashing straight into Trish.

“MY NAME IS REGULUS!”

The shout cut deep, and Remus was instantly sorry, but Regulus didn’t give him time to apologise. He turned, kicking his rake out of his path, and tore off across the lawn in a fit.

“Bleedin’ Christ, he’s really unhinged, isn’t he?” Jillian said after. “Are you alright, Remus?”

“Yeah, no harm, no foul,” he huffed, stepping out of the pile of foliage and dusting the leaves off of his trousers.

“And you?” Jillian asked, wrapping an arm around Trish’s shoulders. The younger girl leaned into her friend, her usual vigour depleted to nothing.

“Didnae mean to make him so mad… Sorry, guys, now we’ve gotta rake the rest of this ourselves.”

Jillian pat her partner’s head softly, like a big sister might. “Don’t worry, Trishy. Regulus Black is just an old sour puss. Who’d want to be liked by a boy like him anyway?”

Remus didn’t say it, but the look on Trish’s face did not seem very comforted.





* * *





Friday 18th November 1977 – The Day Following…





It was only lunchtime, and Remus Lupin was not in a good mood.

Not only had Peter neglected to return his poem on time, but that morning he’d gotten roped into his second prefect project of the week. Sheila had come to him at the last second and requested that he and Regulus cover the fifth years’ music class again. If it’d been anyone else he might’ve said no, but Sheila had probably known that, so that’s why she’d asked him. On his way over to the primary campus, Remus had been sceptical of seeing Regulus so soon after their spat. He’d considered how he might go about apologising for stepping so far over the line, but apparently he’d worried for nothing.

Regulus had not shown.

“Blimey, you look… well, fucking terrible actually,” Sirius said, when Remus reappeared for lunch, indeed looking haggard and grumpy. He sat, groaning as he attempted to stretch the kinks from his neck. Luckily, James was well versed in muscle tension. He leaned over and began working the knots from Remus’ shoulders with those magic fingers of his.

“Ah, thanks,” Remus sighed. “Lifesaver.”

James waved him off kindly, and Lily slid a cup of tea toward him. “Are you really okay, Remus? Sirius is right, you look awful.”

“Do I? No wonder, I’ve been run ragged by a bunch of nine year-olds all morning. Now does anyone else care to tell me how bad I look?”

“Could be worse,” James offered; “You could be tutoring them in maths.”

“Oh yes, that’s what I did,” Lily finished, smiling brightly.

“Thank god for the little things…”

“Hi, Remus.”

Remus turned around. The table behind theirs held a large group of girls, all of whom were looking at him with curious grins on their faces. He couldn’t tell which of them had called out to him, but they seemed to be waiting for something. Bewildered, Remus flashed them a meek wave, and suddenly all of the girls squealed a bit before turning back to one another, heads tucked tightly together.

“What was that about?” Sirius murmured.

“Dunno…”

“Maybe you’re getting a fan club,” James teased. As he did, another girl passed by behind him.

“Hey, Remus,” she called, brushing her long hair off one shoulder.

“Er… Hi.”

She didn’t stop, just carried on with a sly look on her face, but Sirius looked after her.

“That was Pepper Doyle,” he said with an air of surprise. “What’s Pepper Doyle doing saying hi to you?”

“I don’t know!” Remus insisted. “Did you guys do something while I was with the primaries?”

All of them shook their heads.

“Tell the truth!”

“They didn’t do anything,” Lily swore. “Potter was with me in Politics and… well, I can’t say for Sirius.”

Sirius scoffed; “I actually went to class today, thank you very much. Had a Latin quiz and everything. Aced it.”

“Does that mean, you carpe diem-ed the day?” James snorted.

Sirius opened his mouth to answer, but all that came out was;

“Hi, Remus.”

This time they didn’t even know which direction the hello had come from, but as they all whipped their heads around to check, Remus suddenly realised that they’d amassed an audience. Girls had crowded in like a swarm of crows—even some guys were craning their necks to get a look. Before Remus could question it, he felt a tap on his shoulder. It was Andrea Sapsford. She and Remus had History together, though Andrea made a point of sitting near the front of the classroom so they’d rarely ever talked. Now she was standing beside his table, clutching a piece of paper across her stomach so tightly it looked about ready to tear in half.

“H–Hi, Remus,” she said nervously.

“Hi, Andrea. Is… that today’s homework or something?”

“Oh no, it’s…” She bit her lip, and Remus could sense all of his friends leaning in—Sirius most of all. “Well, I figured that I just had to say something. What you did was so nice and all.”

Remus looked at Sirius. He had no idea what he could’ve ever done to Andrea Sapsford to be considered 'nice'.

“You know I’m actually sort of seeing Oliver Paice right now,” she continued, “but if you’re interested then maybe we could hang out as friends and… oh," she giggled nervously; "I dunno... See where it goes?”

She smiled after, and Remus blinked very quickly.

“I’m sorry?”

Andrea glanced down at the paper, biting her lip. “Maybe I’m jumping the gun, but no girl could resist such a sweet gesture.”

Sirius was on his feet in a second, snatching the notepaper from Andrea and looking down at it. For a moment nothing was said, but Remus knew he was in trouble the moment Sirius’ eyes widened.

“… Holy shit.”

“What?” He clambered after him. “Sirius, what is it?”

“Er—” Sirius shook his head frantically. “No... don’t think you want to see this, Moons.”

Remus felt dread wash over him. “Give it here!” He cried, as Sirius ducked around the other side of the table. On the way, James managed to snatch the paper from him and turned it over, eyes turning to saucers in shock.

“Bloody hell. Is this what I think it is?”

“Can I have that back please?” Andrea shrieked.

“Oi!” Someone else called. This time it was a guy. Remus didn't even know his name, but that didn't stop him from storming up with a paper of his own and waving it beneath his nose.

“Lupin!" He cried. "What d’you think you’re doing giving something like this to my girl?”

“Wha... What girl?”

“My girl! You trying to sweep her out from under me, you thick nob?”

“Huh?”

Andrea stepped up. “Remus, you mean you gave it to someone else too?”

“Gave what?!”

“Moons—” Sirius got between him and the angry boy. “Moons, something’s happened. It's your poem, I think it might’ve…”

Remus gaped. “My poem?”

“Are you dating someone else or are you not, Remus?” Andrea demanded.

“Yes—I mean, no!”

“Then who was this poem meant for?”

He hadn’t the time to answer; just then Mary and Lottie rushed the table. “Remus!” Mary gasped; “You must tell us—did you actually write this?”

Remus threw his arms out. “WRITE WHAT?!”

“The poem!” Lottie gushed. “It’s so beautiful! Like, I might actually have to fall in love with you after all!”

This got Sirius’ attention. He snatched Angry Boyfriend's paper and dashed toward the girls, taking the one from Lottie so he could compare.

“It’s the same! It’s the same, and…” a smile split Sirius’ face; “Oh Moons, I knew you could write poetry!”

Remus did not wait for permission. Horrified, he all but launched himself across the dining table and snatched the first paper from James’ hands, turning it over. What stared back at him was the single most embarrassing piece of work he’d ever created—his own love poem. And the words were not just hand-written in pencil anymore, they’d been transformed into ink. Solid, permanent, unerasable ink.

Someone had copied his poem.

No, no, no, no, no—NO!

“Fuck!” Remus cried. “Mary, where did you get this?!”

She looked affronted. “Rochelle from history gave it to me.”

“Where did she get it?”

“I don’t know! But tons of girls had a copy, I assumed you gave it to them.”

“Are you insane? Why would I give this to anyone?!”

As Mary baulked, Remus put his head in his hands. Shit! Shit! Fucking shit!

Across from them, Sirius covered his mouth as though he were afraid Remus might catch him laughing. “It’s not that bad, Moons,” he reasoned. “Really, it’s a good poem! A new classic, even.”

“You!” Remus lashed, seeing red. “You did this!”

Sirius dropped his arm. “Me?”

“YES! You fucking did this, didn’t you!”

“How could I have done it? You wouldn’t even let me see it until now!”

“It had to be you! It had to be because it’s always you, and you were the one who—!” Suddenly Remus broke off. No, it couldn’t have been Sirius, because Sirius wasn’t the one who… blithering fuck.

“Where is he?!” Remus barked, furiously scanning the room.

“ ‘Who’?!” Everyone asked at once.

“PETER! PETER PETTIGREW, WHERE ARE YOU?!”

“I’m here!” Peter strolled leisurely up to the table, lunch tray in hand. “What’s everyone shouting about?”

He glanced around, but upon finding no smiles to greet him, Peter’s good mood quickly vanished. All he needed was to see the look on Remus’ face and the paper in his hands to connect the dots.

“… Oh shit.”

“YOU!”

Remus was throwing himself on Peter in a second. The poor boy didn’t even have time to put his tray down before the entire thing plummeted to the linoleum after Remus had tackled him round his middle and sent them both flying.

“YOU TOLD ME YOU WOULDN’T GIVE IT TO ANYONE!”

“I DIDN’T!” Peter shrieked. “I DIDN’T!”

“THEN HOW THE FUCK DID IT END UP WITH ROCHELLE FROM HISTORY?!”

“Lupin! Lupin, that’s enough!” James barked, grappling Remus around the middle and trying to haul him off. He hadn’t hit Peter yet, but they’d wrestled a good ways across the floor, drawing a crowd of at least two dozen students, all of them cradling their books and bags as they stared on in sick fascination. Beyond them, the girls urged him to stop, but Remus’ anger had tapped into an unknown strength. Shoving James off, he used his legs to pin Peter in place before bending over him like an animal readying itself for the kill.

“WHO’D YOU GIVE IT TO?!”

“No one!” Peter wailed. “I swear!”

“THEN HOW’D IT GET OUT?!”

“Someone stole it from his bag!”

The cry came from Moira, who pushed through the crowd to come to her boyfriend’s aid. She started by batting Remus with her English text, looking even more furious than he was.

“He didn’t hand out your shitty poem—someone took it!” She spat. “Now get off him, you bloody brute!”

Remus acquiesced, albeit reluctantly, and Peter slowly staggered back to his feet.

“I was gonna give it back to you, honest!” He insisted; “But then I went to check my bag this morning and it wasn’t there! I thought I’d lost it so I started tearing our room apart—but I swear, Moony, someone must’ve taken it and given it away!”

“Who would give away a fucking poem, Peter?!”

“Hah! I wonder!"

The single laugh cut through the dining hall like a knife. Remus knew who it was instantly. All he had to do was turn, and the crowd parted around Barty like the Red Sea.

“Gotta be honest,” the nasty boy sneered, “didn’t think a single piece ‘a paper would get you so rattled, but I guess obsessing over girly stuff like this just comes with the territory, Loony.”

Remus was moving again. This was it—he was finally going to kill Barty Crouch.

“Woah, there!” Sirius grunted, grabbing a hold of Remus’ arm just as he raised it to give Barty the beating of his life. “Save it for the ring, big guy!”

"Get out of my way, Sirius!"

Somewhere further off, a few kids had begun chanting.

'Fight! Fight!'

"What's a'matter, Looooony?" Barty sang; "Getting a bit slow?"

Remus raged, as James grabbed his other arm and Lily even came between them.

“Remus, don’t!”

”Ooh, I’m so scared! Someone call for a teacher, Lupin’s gone rogue!”

“I’m going to murder you, you little shit!”

“Nice talk coming from a prefect!” Snape heckled, appearing on the sidelines like a leech.

“PISS OFF!”

“Remus, please calm down!” Lily begged. “It’s just one poem! I’ll bet nobody’s even seen it!”

“Don’t be too sure about that, charity girl,” Barty sniggered. The little coward had slipped several arm’s lengths away as if he could still remember the sting of Remus’ fist from the last time they’d gone toe to toe. “That bird from your piddly history class might’ve been one of the first to receive her letter, but she wasn’t the last. I should feel more at loss—best revenge ever and it wasn’t even my idea!”

Remus couldn’t believe his ears. He thought about ripping his friends off just to try and trounce Barty again, but reality had already sunk in. All around them kids were holding books and homework papers—except they weren’t papers at all. They were poems—his poem. At least thirty people were standing right there, reading his love poem right in front of him. And he couldn’t do a thing to stop it.

“Don’t read that!” Marlene said, coming to her senses first and ripping a paper out of the hands of the girl closest to her. Her gesture seemed to bring all of his friends to life at the same time, and the girls and Peter went about the room, taking back every copy of the poem they could get their hands on. It still wasn’t enough. The dining hall was one room out of hundreds, and they numbered just eight. Remus wasn’t even done processing Barty’s words. Not my idea. Not my idea.

But whose?!

And then it hit him. Of course. Naturally. A long game—just like the girls on Halloween. Perhaps one that had never stopped.

Not my idea.

Remus turned. He found him sitting in the same spot, but this time when he looked, Regulus looked back. This time, Regulus Black set down his fork and folded his hands neatly in his lap, mouth forming just a single word.

Checkmate.
