Chapter 85: Moony &amp; Lu


Chapter Summary

Going home is always hard, especially when Lily Evans has put a hit out on you.



Chapter Notes

Note: See the end notes for an alternate POV of the final scene in this chapter.

No specific trigger warnings for this chapter, but the boys go back and forth a lot, and it carries some underlying issues with their families as well as internalized homophobia. You can tell they're hurting. But it's got its moments, I swear!



See the end of the chapter for more notes



I, I will be king,

And you, you will be queen;

Though nothing will drive them away,

We can beat them, just for one day,

We can be Heroes, just for one day...



Saturday 31st December 1977





"This ain't goodbye."

"I know."

"Then stop looking at me like I'm about to head into the trenches."

"I'm not!" Remus scowled. "If anyone's headed for the gallows it's me. I'm the one going home..."

"Ah, yes. I'm sure facing down the likes of potpourri and a nice home-cooked meal does have its downsides."

"You've clearly never met Lily."

Tomny smiled at him, the distant shriek of train whistles and car announcements echoing down the Tube behind him. "When do you leave for school then?"

"The third. We head out of King's Cross on the first train like last time," Remus said, still wondering how he was going to last at the Potters until then. And there was still Giles to contend with as well... shit.

"You know you can call me if things get really unbearable," Tomny offered. "Like if they forget to put out them little finger sandwiches. Or the champagne's flat."

"Prick." He shoved his hands into his jacket pockets, only to pull them out again when Tomny raised his arms for a hug. They embraced right there on the station platform, while other commuters swerved around them, occasionally tossing them a dirty or otherwise bewildered look as they rushed to catch their train home for the final holiday of the year. Remus hardly cared; they'd agreed to part on good terms, him and Tom. And so he clung on, not wanting to let go. His lips brushed the worn leather of Tomny’s jacket, and it was cold.

"Stop trying to drink yourself to death," he said.

"Stop trying to smoke yerself stupid," Tomny replied.

"Stop fighting with drug dealers."

"Stop fighting the world."

"Stop... Stop taking so many drugs!"

"Stop making everyone fall in love with you!"

They pulled apart.

"Though, suppose that's asking for the impossible, innit."

Remus felt his chest tighten, like a breath he'd been holding onto for too long. "Promise!" He insisted, knocking his fist against his friend's shoulder. "Promise you're gonna straighten your shit out."

Tomny jabbed him in the chest. "I'll promise if you promise!"

"... Promise."

"Then we're agreed. Shit shall be straightened. Now is there anythin' else you'd like to demand of me before ya go?"

"Yeah, just one more thing. Don't disappear."

"Aw." Tomny pat his cheek fondly. “I already told you, didn’t I? I’m not going anywhere. Still need my Lu.”

Good terms, Remus had promised himself, not soppy, weepy messes.

They hugged once more, and then Tomny handed him the clunky Fender Twin amplifier and began backing up toward the stairs.

"Better hurry along then, don't want to get caught in the rain. I'll see you on the third."

Remus blinked. "The third...? What—"

"Oh, and if your lover-boy is really that bothered, just tell 'im we shagged with the lights on. And that we saw God. See what he has to say about that."

It was horrid—completely cheeky, but before Remus could so much as utter a response, Tomny had hopped the turnstiles and vanished up the Tube steps. He was almost tempted to follow him until a train attendant appeared on the other side of the stalls, shooting an irritated look in Tomny’s direction. Rather than being hounded for the ticket he didn’t pay for, Remus picked up his bass guitar and skirted further down the platform, jumping the first train back to East Finchley. As he rode it was hard not to wonder what he was walking into, harder still not to succumb to the urge to flee whenever the train doors slid open. But he'd agreed to go back. He wanted to go back. He owed his friends an explanation for running off, and the Potters an apology for taking their kindness for granted. You just gotta own up to it, Tomny had told him. Be a man.

A man like who? Tomny? Lyall? Remus wasn't sure. He’d wanted to be better, and they’d all wanted it for him too. Only he'd bottled it, just like Lyall said he would. They'd warned him—Grow up! Tell us what's going on! Don’t be a shit friend!—but he'd never listened, and running away in the middle of Leicester Square didn’t exactly scream ‘mate of the year’ either. He had nothing with him aside from the second-hand Teisco and the clothes on his back, and up until that second it'd felt like enough. But when had nothing ever been enough?

A short ride later, he got off at the same station he and Sirius had travelled to on their way to the Potters' last summer. He'd felt out of place then, and he felt out of place now. James’ neighbourhood was not the sort one traipsed along in bearing unwashed clothes and morning-after-beer-breath. Overhead the sky turned to rapid grey while December wind licked up his back, and still Remus marched. He passed countless cottages and terrace houses done up in all of their festive glory, the words ‘upper middle class’ all but stamped on their welcome mats. After his visit in the End, he felt the same way he had on that very first day he’d arrived at Hawkings—a yob in a sea of shining gentry. A faker. It made him want to hurry, which he regretted the instant he appeared in front of the Potters’ noble, three-floor abode. It was New Year’s Eve, which meant he’d been gone for nearly a week. Hadn’t said where he was going, hadn’t called, hadn’t delivered so much as a bloody carrier pigeon. He was in deep shit.

Don’t be a shit friend.

Remus' hands flexed around the amp's handle. I won't. I'll go in. Beg for mercy if I have to.

Aw, and what will you do next? Get down on your knees and kiss their boots? Beg Sirius to take you back?

It's not about that. We're still friends.

Friends don't treat friends like rubbish.

Enough! No more. You ruin everything, and I'm going to feel guilty anymore. I'm not crazy, and I won't let you turn me crazy, so just piss OFF—

“Moony?!”

There was a loud clatter, like the breaking of glass on stone, and Remus whipped around to find Sirius standing a ways down the pavement. He had oven mitts on either hand and seemed to be torn between gaping at Remus, and frowning down at the smashed platter of food he'd apparently been carrying.

"Shit!" Sirius cursed. He knelt down on the icy sidewalk to fret over the steaming glass, but by then Remus had already abandoned the amp and Teisco and dashed to his side.

"Effie's gonna kill me... I was supposed to be bringing this plate of bread sauce over from Pete's mum."

"It was an accident. I'm sure she'll understand."

Sirius whipped his head up, as if he only just remembered who he was talking to. "You! What the fuck are you doing here?!"

"I—I..."

Sirius stood then, whipping off the oven mitts with a sharp tug. He seemed to be waiting for something—an explanation probably. Remus wished he'd have seen him first coming up the adjoining path from Peter’s house. Maybe then he'd have managed to find the right words to apologise; he’d been struggling with it the entire train over. It hadn’t been enough! Now he was left standing before the gates of Potter Cottage, tongue thick in his mouth.

Oh god—say something, you idiot! He’s staring right at you!

“I'm back."

"Back?"

He swallowed. "Yep... And I'm sorry I ever left."

Sirius' lips parted, and Remus imagined them contorting to fit all sorts of nasty replies. The worst of them being that he hadn't wanted him to come back at all. But Sirius didn't say that, and when he raised his arms Remus told himself to be ready for a fine wallop he absolutely deserved.

And that didn't come.

Rather than beat him into the mud, Sirius’ arms came up and wrapped around Remus' neck so tightly that he was yanked down to his level. With a little gasp, Remus allowed it and found himself frozen all over again. He and Sirius had barely said a handful of words to each other in weeks, and now there they were—hugging.

“You fucking idiot! You sorry excuse for an absolute—!” Sirius drew up short, pulling away all at once. “What d’you think you were on about, huh?! Freaking us out like that? Did you know we had to practically bend over backward covering for you? Effie almost went to the police! Then she straight tore a right strip off of Giles when he came by to talk her out of it. 'Does this all the time'—what fucking rubbish! Do you have any idea how bloody worried everyone was?!"

Remus swallowed thickly. He'd been expecting a tongue-lashing from Lily, maybe James and Marlene, but from Sirius?

“You were worried about me?”

“Of course I was, you great idiot!"

Something inside of Remus' chest fluttered. He searched Sirius' face for a hint of reciprocation, and that was when he noticed the grey beneath his eyes, the haggard look. Remus felt more stupid than he'd ever been in his life. Of course Sirius had been worried for him. He was heartbroken, not heartless. His own anger had blinded him. Blinded the both of them.

"I'm sorry. I didn't mean to ruin everyone's Christmas."

"Bit bold of you to assume you ruined fucking Christmas," Sirius lashed, though the strain in his voice gave him away. "You went to the End, didn't you? You went and saw Tomny."

Remus squared his shoulders a bit, aware of the incoming fight. "I did."

"You couldn't have called?"

"I didn't think you'd want to talk."

"Fuck off. Why's it so hard for you to believe that people care about you?"

"It isn't."

"Then why didn't you call!?"

"I was afraid."

Sirius looked away, glaring down at the mess of bread sauce on the pavement, already turned cold. He seemed to be at a loss, and when he looked up again he had to wipe his cheek on his shoulder.

“What’s that then?” He asked, gesturing to the abandoned amp and guitar case. Remus was grateful for the distraction.

“Oh. It’s a bass... Long story.”

“Did you steal it?”

“No, I didn’t steal it!”

“Can’t blame me for checking.” Sirius looked him up and down, deflating slightly as his anger morphed into something more frustrated. Hurt, maybe. “Why’d you do that, eh? Why would you just up and leave without saying anything? Andy came over to say hello, and you'd just vanished!"

"Didn't realise she was coming over to the house."

"She didn't come over to the house! Dora's sick with a cold so Ted's mum was watching her for the night. But you could've stayed! What, you hate me so much that you couldn't stand waiting five minutes just to say hello after the movie?"

Remus felt like someone had just hit him over the head with a hammer.

"What movie?"

"The fucking space movie, you prick! With the laser swords and strange, weird bear thing that made all the funny noises! Blahh!"

"Andy was there?"

"Yeah! Didn't you see us talking?"

He wracked his brain. All he could remember was a girl. A girl in a hat and a long coat—and Sirius talking to her, smiling! At the time it'd made Remus sick to his stomach. He must've been iller than he'd thought, straight delusional actually. Andy! The girl had been Andy! Remus wanted to top himself.

"I must've gotten confused," he confessed. "I thought she was just a random... That you..."

Sirius frowned deeply. "That I what? Was trying to get back at you by flirting with some girl I don't care about?"

"Wouldn't be the first time."

"Oh. Fine then," Sirius snarled, throwing down the oven mitts. "Think what you want. Hope you at least have the decency to tell the others your alive. I ain't doing it for you this time."

He made to go around him, but Remus reached out at the last second and caught his arm.

"Sirius, wait. I didn't mean that. And I didn't mean to take off out of the blue either, I just needed to be away for a while... Figure some stuff out.”

Sirius looked back at him sharply. “And?”

And I still love you.

“And I’m sorry. Truly.”

Sirius puckered, the way he always did when he was rearing up for a fight. “I hate this, you know. I hate that you left. And I hate that it took for you to chat up your precious Tomny to come back. Why can't we just talk to each other?”

Slowly, Remus released his arm. "I don't know."

For a moment they were both quiet. For such a solemn conversation, it struck Remus as odd that it wasn't raining. Then, as if on cue, he heard the distant sound of thunder rumbling. The storm came in quickly as it often did the more one thought about it, and as the clouds began to churn above them, Remus felt tiny raindrops began to patter down onto the tops of his shoulders.

“Look, I’m sorry for not telling you about my dad,” he called, voice raw on the wind. “I'd never told anyone. Not even Tomny. I hated thinking about it, and the thought of telling someone, it... I still can't. When I was a kid I sorta thought that if I pretended not to know, then he'd forget. And he'd j-just become my real dad anyway. Want me... But it doesn’t work like that. Even if I really was his kid, I don't think he'd ever have wanted me. Not with who I am... And not the way I wanted him to want me."

Sirius was still looking back at him, eyes dark like the storm clouds. Remus knew he was crying, that'd he'd made himself cry, but he hoped the rain disguised it.

"I'm sorry I never told you, Sirius. And I’m sorry for using it as a punishment when I did.”

At his words, Sirius almost began to flounder. He shifted his weight, chin buried down in the collar of his jacket as though he were trying to make himself disappear.

“Fuck,” he huffed finally. "I really liked you, you know. Then I went and bottled it, didn't I?"

"Yeah... me too."

Sirius dropped his chin again. "So yeah, I didn’t know about your dad. But... Fuck! I’m sorry too. What I did... What I tried to do—” He scoffed and wiped his face; “I was so pissed off at you, and it's like I don't even remember why now! That's almost the worst part... But what I did, it was foul. You shouldn’t forgive me for it.”

“I do, though.”

“McKinnon sure don’t. You should’ve heard the way she shouted at me when you ran off. Thought she was likely to kill me right then and there—dump my body in the Thames. Evans along with her, though I confess she's probably been waiting since year seven. When James and I stole her swimming costume and ran it up the school's flag pole."

"In that case I'm with the girls. You'd deserve it."

"It was kinda cute. Had little polka dots and everything."

They both laughed, quietly, and wiped their faces as the rain started down harder. Silence almost lapsed again, until Remus couldn't take it anymore.

"Can we just agree to be sorry then? Nothing else, just... I can't hate you, Padfoot."

"I can't hate you either, Moons."

Good. "Friends again then?"

It felt stupid—how could they ever be friends again?—but if the choice was between having Sirius this much, and not having him at all, Remus would take friends every time.

Sirius nodded, and bent down to pick up Effie's oven mitts, now soaked from the rain. “So that stuff about your dad," he asked meekly; "Is it all true?”

“That I’m a bastard? Yeah, it’s true.”

“Well, I already knew that.” Sirius cracked a wry grin—a small one—and it was like a flash of hope. “But you really… All this time?"

"Mhm."

"Then do you know who…”

“Yeah, I know who my real dad is.”

“You’ve met him?”

“No, got a picture. Sheila gave it to me.”

“Sheila?”

He nodded. “She knew my mum. They all went to school together.”

“Holy. That mean your dad—he… wow.”

"Would you like to see?"

“Y-Yeah!" Sirius sputtered. "I mean, only if you want me to...”

In that moment, Remus couldn’t have wanted anything other than to fall onto Sirius and expel every last secret. No more, he silently promised, I’m done keeping secrets from you.

"Hold on, got it right here." Squinting through the rain, he began patting his pockets before straightening up. "Oh, forgot. Left it in my—shit!"

He bolted past Sirius, to where he'd left the Teisco and the tiny Fender amp sitting idly on the pavement. Both were sopping now, but the guitar had its case at least.

"Here!" Sirius called, appearing beside him to help. He grabbed the amp and together they scarpered through the front gate, all the way up the massive drive to where they finally found cover beneath the front porch. Soaked through and sighing, Sirius fell into the family porch swing and Remus automatically slumped down next to him. When he glanced sideways at Sirius, he could see his dark hair as it curled at the bottom around his ears, dripping tiny droplets of rain onto his cheeks and neck. Prompted by their close proximity, Remus felt his hand drift upwards, fingers nearly touching...

"Hope this thing still works," Sirius said, snapping Remus from his daze. He gestured to the sad little amp sitting next to them, and Remus nodded.

"Should probably test it before I plug the guitar in. Don't want to roast my fingers."

"Good idea." Sirius flashed him a winning grin, and Remus almost regretted not taking his hand. It’d become a habit when they were alone, he realised.

“What’s his name?” Sirius asked suddenly. “Your real dad, I mean.”

“Thaddeus.”

“Thaddeus? Are you for real? And I thought ‘Sirius’ was bad.”

“No one called him that anyway! Sheila said he told everyone to call him Tad.”

"Did he and your mum used to date then?"

"Dunno. Don't know anything else about him. Not where he was born, or what he did after school, or if he's... still alive."

"Shit. Haven't you tried asking Sheila?"

"Er... No. She mostly talks about my mum, and it's always a bit—y’know.”

"Weird."

"Yeah..."

"Well, I could ask her if you want. Then you could ask me and I'd only tell you the things you wanted to know. Remove the middle man, and all that. Or I suppose, it's adding a middle man... Anyway, I'd promise to never tell anyone else. I'd take it to my grave, if you asked me to."

Remus smiled shyly. "I'm grateful, but right now, I think I'm sorta alright not knowing. Figure it's better than being disappointed."

"Yeah, alright."

They shared a glance, so close their shoulders were pressed up against one another, and Remus watched as a single raindrop raced down the tip of Sirius' nose. He was still watching it when he felt a finger trace the back of his hand, and for a moment he almost let himself believe that maybe...

But then the front door flew open, and Remus knew he instantly that was in for it.

"Oh bollocks."

“REMUS JOHN LUPIN!” Lily roared, rushing out onto the front mat in her house slippers. "I'm going to MURDER YOUUUUU!”





* * *





And you, you can be mean,

And I, I’ll drink all the time;

‘Cause we’re lovers, and that is a fact,

Yes we’re lovers, and that is that...



Though nothing will keep us together,

We could steal time just for one day;

We can be heroes for ever and ever,

What d’you say?



They weren’t miraculously back together, but the apology with Sirius had gone well enough. He could tell there were still plenty of things left to be said, but there was no time to be alone, and Remus knew from experience that privacy was hard to come during a Potter holiday. He considered asking Sirius to step out with him for a while; pop off to the shops before they closed or some other excuse, but he was busy—very busy, peeling enough potatoes to get an entire Irish village through the winter. After that he was to scrub every pot and pan that'd gone into their festive supper. And then he would salt the drive, and fold the washing, and dust the parlour, and kiss Lily’s feet, probably. Perhaps finally then she would forgive him for being such a massive nob.

Remus was disappointed, but didn’t object. He'd already traded the front porch for the back and was now bent over a tub of soapy water, a stack of dirty dishes half the size of himself beside him. He could handle a bit of humiliation, and if he was lucky, he’d finish his chores with enough time to join his friends in one final practice before the Pettigrews’ legendary New Year’s party was set to commence. It pleased him to hear that the Marauders were still set to make an appearance even after his decided dis-appearance. He’d taken enough from his friends, no reason they should avoid showing off their hard-earned talent.

As the rain continued to pour, Remus kept scrubbing. He’d just started on a pot big enough to cook a small child in when Mrs. Potter stuck her head out the door.

“Not too chilly out here, are you, Remus?”

“Oh, no. Water’s still warm too.”

She smiled and untucked a blanket from her arms, settling it down over his shoulders anyway. “Dinner's in an hour. And I’m glad to see your aunt helped you kick that cold.”

He glanced up, nearly losing his grip on the pot. “Sorry?”

“Your aunt? The one the boys said you’d gone to stay with?”

“Oh. That aunt.”

“Yes, now where is it she lives again?”

“Er… Ealing?”

“Ealing, is it? Funny, I think I remember James saying that it was Merton.”

“That’s my… other aunt.”

Mrs. Potter smiled and he knew he was caught, but all she did was shake her head lightly. “You should know that I rang Giles, and he is very disappointed in you.”

“Don’t worry, that’s just Giles for ‘I love you—see you at Easter'.”

She laughed heartily, but did not bother correcting him.

“It’s nice to have you back, beta. Come inside when you’re finished with those dishes, hm? I have some cakes that need frosting.”

“Yes, ma’am.”

Giving him a gentle smile, she bent down and planted a kiss atop his head before stepping back into the house. With his insides now properly squirmy, Remus pulled the blanket tightly around himself and did not feel the cold at all.

“I don’t have to go on with you,” he insisted later as they all filed into Peter’s parlour, where their instruments were ready and waiting for them. “I wouldn’t be offended if you’re still too mad at me.”

James whipped around. “If you don’t go on with us, I’ll let Lily throttle you.”

“At least it’ll be a quiet death. She’s still not talking to me.”

“Honestly I’m not sure I want to be talking to you either.” James pulled his guitar strap up over his head. Next to him, Sirius smacked one of Peter’s cymbals with a thick smirk.

“Lay off, Potter, he’s had enough punishment. He folded your sock drawer after all.”

“I don’t care. He still hasn’t said where it was that he went!”

“He went to the East End, ya dolt. Go on—tell him, Moony.”

Remus nodded at James, who did not look pleased to hear it.

“You couldn’t have given us the address?” He demanded. “Called—anything?!”

“I’m sorry, Prongs.”

“Yeah, yeah,” James huffed. “At least you’re safe. You are safe, right?”

“Yeah. Swears.”

He didn’t look like he believed him, but Peter was already dropping down behind his drum kit, sticks in hand.

“You can grill him later, James, for now let’s just get on with practice. Mum said people’ll start arriving soon.”

So… they weren’t exactly Led Zeppelin reborn. Two rough-hewn acoustic guitars, one on-offer electric bass with a shitty amp for company (at least it wasn't water-logged anymore) and a set of drums that had been barely broken-in didn’t make for many grand concerts, but it was hardly about that anyway. Mrs. Pettigrew had granted them full rights to her vast front parlour to practice. It meant that come showtime, it would be as easy as throwing the doors open and allowing anyone who was nearby to have a listen. Even if they did end up sounding like a patchwork disaster, no one would care, not with the the party's open bottle service.

“Starting with an Elvis number will definitely go over well, ‘cept my cousin Caroline is bound to cry, she’s hardly stopped since the guy bought it—but mum still thinks we should do at least one Christmas song,” Peter said, after they’d run through their planned set list for the dozenth time.

Sirius mimed retching. “No way. If they wanted carols they should’ve called the happy-clappy brigade—not Marauders.”

“You mean you have no plans to release a Christmas album one day?” James asked. “You could call it ‘Black Christmas’.”

“Funny. But I still say no. Not in front of people.”

“It’s just our families,” Peter scoffed.

“Exactly. Your family.” He raised his eyebrows and Remus caught on.

“Oh—Simeon! He’s back now then?”

Peter immediately rolled his eyes. “It’s been five days and you lot are still acting like I’ve got Lou Reed hidden in the guest room.”

“Simeon’s way cooler than Lou Reed,” Sirius said, then; “Fuck Pete! That nearly took my eye out!” As Peter threw a drumstick at him.

“Stop fantasizing about my brother!”

“Fanta—? ... C’mere, you cheeky shit!”

“Watch the drinks!” James wailed, making a dive for the tea tray

As the pair scuffled and James played referee, Remus slouched onto the arm of the sofa, fiddling with the Teisco’s tuning. He didn’t remember much from their summer party, but the last time he’d seen Simeon they’d both had their trousers around their ankles. He wondered if it wasn’t too late to back out, but then the sound of the front door opening echoed from out in the hall, along with a familiar holler;

“Muuum! We’re back! Got those dinner rolls you wanted!”

“There you go—that’s just brilliant! You’ve bloody conjured him!” Peter moaned, brandishing his drum stool like a shield to keep Sirius away.

There was a gentle knock on the parlour’s glass doors and Simeon stuck his head inside. He looked the same—stunning baby blue eyes and dimples on each cheek, which he used to grin down at the sight laid out before him; four stupid boys and their instruments amongst a sea of festive tinsel.

“I don’t hear very much practising going on, lads. Thought I told you this morning that I expected a full rockfest when I returned?”

“Maybe stop bothering us and we’d actually get some work done!” Peter snapped.

Simeon leaned casually on the door handle, still glancing around musingly. It was obvious he only meant to antagonize Peter, but he did a double-take when he spotted Remus and came into the room further. Only slightly spooked, Remus stood up from the sofa arm and took a quick step back.

“Oh hey, you," Simeon grinned. "Word on the street was that you were gonna be a no-show. What, stop by just to see me?”

Remus opened his mouth but no sound came out. Not that it mattered. Simeon had already plunged on, patting Remus on the shoulder fondly as he peeled out of his winter coat and revealed the handsome Aran jumper and dark brown trousers underneath.

"You look like you're having fun at least. Is this what rockstars are wearing these days?" He asked, gesturing to James' brown cardigan, Sirius' dark turtleneck.

“Says you," Sirius replied. "Nice jumper, Oxbridge boy."

Simeon smirked at him, holding Sirius' gaze for a long while. He looked away first, which was to be expected—Sirius never broke eye contact first—and looked Remus up and down.

“Christ, I think you’ve bloody grown again, Lupin.” He nodded to James. “And here I was thinking you’d end up being the tallest mate.”

“There’s no competing with this one, he’s like a weed,” James replied; “Grows only two ways—up and stubborn.”

Broken from his trance, Remus shot his friend a light glare before looking back at Simeon. “Hey, Sim—er… How’s school?”

Simeon shrugged. “It’s Oxford, which is code for lots of crusty old geezers and entire lecture halls full of sods who think they’re the smartest person in the room. Which is impossible, of course.”

“Why, ‘cause you’re already the smartest?”

“And the funniest.” Simeon winked and Remus’ stomach did flips.

A throw pillow hit the parlour door next to Simeon’s head and Peter flopped down onto his stool. “Sim—goooooo! We’re busy!”

“You can get your knickers out of a twist, Petey, I only wanted to say hello. Speaking of which—Phae, come here and meet the gang.”

Another face peeked around the doorway, joined quickly by the petite body of a pretty girl with honey-brown hair and huge silver hoops in her ears. “Hello," she smiled. "Are you boys still at it then?”

“Remus—this is Phaedra, my girlfriend,” Simeon said.

Remus almost started. Girlfriend? Like, for real?!

“Pleased to meet you,” Phaedra said, waving sweetly. “You’re one of Peter’s friends then?”

Remus didn’t even get the chance to answer; not that he could’ve. Instead Peter thumped his bass drum several times, glaring at them both.

“SIM—OUT!”

“Alright, we’re going,” Simeon blagged, snaking an arm across his girlfriend’s shoulders and backing her out of the room. “This concert of yours better be good!”

He shut the parlour door before Peter could resort to more drumstick tossing and James turned to smirk at him. “If you’re worried we’re going to replace you with Sim or something you can relax, Pete.”

“I’m not worried—”

“ ‘Cause I already asked, and Simeon can’t play the drums.”

“I hate you.”

This time it was James’ turn to scuffle. He grabbed Peter in a friendly headlock and while he was avoiding taking a drumstick to the eye, Sirius crossed the room and flicked a guitar pick at Remus’ cheek.

“You’re mooning, Moony.”

“I am not," he grumbled, flicking his own pick at him. “Sod off."

“I never noticed—have you always drooled this much over Sim?”

“I wasn’t drooling.”

“Sure you were. Could’ve solved the drought in Africa on your own.”

“Well, what about you? One step away from openly declaring your love for the cheeky git, you were. 'Nice jumper'. I mean, really."

"I was clearly teasing."

"Only 'cause you like him so much. You wish he'd tease you back."

“Fuck off, Moony.”

“Make me.”

Sirius’ eyes flashed and Remus clamped his mouth shut, looking away quickly. Luckily Sirius didn’t seem much interested in purposeful arguing or accidental flirting; he moved past him, mumbling something about the toilet, and Remus was left to slump back against the sofa.

Less than an hour or so later, people had begun arriving in droves. They brought with them spare Christmas presents and cling-wrapped dishes that left the dining room piled high with all sorts of sweet and savoury treats. Remus had missed the Potters' infamous Christmas party, which meant that everywhere he turned there was someone new to be introduced to. The Pettigrews were a small family when compared to the Potter clan, but they had friends all over. Remus spent twenty minutes just listening to some guy done on about the likelihood of the labour party taking back majority government before realising that it was local MP. He made a swift enough exit, only to be swept up into another conversation over the extended construction on the M25, and the Underground Fleet line, and the new NatWest Tower. It struck Remus how all adults seemed to do was complain, but despite the awkwardness and the overwhelming amount of people, he was glad to be back with his friends.

They escaped up to Lottie's childhood bedroom eventually, where Peter broke out a round of Chartbuster. It was mostly just an excuse to sit around and chug the bottle of vodka Lottie had smuggled upstairs, but Remus was winning so he had very few complaints.

“Kids, it’s time to come down and greet the rest of our guests!” Mrs. Pettigrew called, practically wailing on Lottie’s bedroom door to get them to come out.

“We’ll be down in a second, Mum!” Lottie hollered back, before downing her share of the booze and passing it along to James.

“I still don't know how you thought this would be a good idea,” Lily moaned, covering her mouth with the back of her hand. Equally as unsettled, James lowered the bottle from his lips and heaved slightly.

“I think I’m going to be sick.”

“If you so much as drool on my new rug I’ll boil you in great aunt Frida’s hot cider,” Lottie threatened. She tossed the empty bottle into the bin before checking the hallway—no mother—and began to herd them all out of her bedroom one by one. Remus waited obediently in the hall, but nearly fell over when the door he'd been leaning against opened behind him.

“I hope you at least divided the swill fairly,” Simeon said, coming out to leer at them. His collar was misbuttoned, and Remus realised why when Phaedra emerged, dabbing at her smudged lipstick and gently combing through her fingers through her hair.

“Phae and I popped off to the off-license earlier, so if you’re good I've got some rum with your names on it," Simeon offered. Immediately Peter pushed forward, waving a finger at him.

“We don’t—” He cut himself off with a hiccup; “We don’t need you to get alcohol for us anymore. Sirius’s eighteen now!”

“Which means I’m mature enough not to turn down free booze when it’s offered!” Sirius declared promptly.

“What’s that about free booze?” One of Peter’s uncles slurred, appearing out of the upstairs bathroom and adding to the already crowded hallway. As Sirius made a humble excuse and Simeon began ushering them down the stairs for a hasty exit, Remus hung back in the bedroom with Lily, who’d stopped to watch Lottie reapply her lipstick in her vanity mirror.

“I see Peter’s still running with his ‘anti-Simeon’ dogma,” Lily sighed.

“Ugh, it’s been awful, he never stops whinging.”

“What’s with that by the way?” Remus asked. “It’s never been this bad.”

“Mhm, well—” Lottie smacked her lips together; “You know how Petey's always been a bit shite at getting what he wants? Well, it was Sim who convinced our parents to get him that silly drum kit in the first place, and I guess Petey’s never quite gotten over it. Couldn't tell you why, it’s not like Sim lords it over him. If anything you’d think he'd be grateful. Mum and Dad never would've gone for it had Sim not been the one to convince them. Anyway, looks like it’s happening again with this gap year rubbish. Petey brought it up over dinner the other night and Daddy blew a gasket.”

"You mean they're not gonna go for it?" Remus winced.

"No, they will. But only because Sim told them about this friend of his who took a year off and now runs his family's entire leather-making business up in Birmingham. They ate it up. You should've seen Petey’s face."

"Was he not pleased?" Lily asked.

"Not even close. He went red from top to bottom, but couldn't very well say anything without upsetting our Dad again. Now I guess he’s right pissed off. Won’t stop taking shots at Sim—keeps calling him hen-pecked by Phaedra. The hippocrite. I quite like the girl, myself. She’s chill. And it's not like Petey’s anything but whipped for Moira anyway.”

"That's too bad."

"Eh, he'll get over it." Finished with the mirror, Lottie turned back to Lily and snapped her fingers. “Lils, c’mere and let me fix your eyeliner.”

“You already spent hours on it,” Lily moaned dramatically, letting Lottie drag her over anyway.

“Want me to do you too, Remus?” She asked after.

“Oh, no—”

“You should, Remus!” Lily preened. “For your show! It’s a holiday anyway—no one’ll care. It might even impress Sirius.”

“Why would I want to impress Sirius?”

Without answering, both girls grabbed him by the wrist and tugged him over, forcing him down onto the vanity stool while Lottie raised her eyeliner pen, which was a regrettable electric blue colour.

“Ow—fuck, Lot! You sure you haven’t had too much to drink? You know you’re not supposed to operate heavy machinery while under the influence…”

“It’s an eyeliner pen, you twee idiot. Now quit faffing around and hold still!”

Sirius appeared in the bedroom doorway. “Moony! Something's wrong with your amp. It keeps buzzing and—oh! Lot, be a doll and do me next!”

Finished being painted, Remus stood up and quickly switched places with Sirius, blinking excessively as his eyes watered. He reached for them, but Lily appeared at his side and batted his hands away.

“Don’t. It looks good and you’ll only ruin it."

"I suppose I'll just blink through the pain then."

"Good. Because I think ‘Mediterranean Breeze’ might just be your colour.”

He resisted the urge to rub the makeup away and turned to squint at her. “Glad to see you’re talking to me again. I missed the only other sound voice of reason around here.”

“It’s a holiday,” Lily reasoned. “And I missed you too. Even if you are an absolute spanner. I should be giving you the royal silence treatment, shouldn’t I?”

“You could always start now. At least that way I wouldn’t have to hear you rag on me for not doing my winter homework.”

Lily gasped playfully, and snatched up one of the throw pillows from Lottie’s bed to smack him with it. Remus laughed, pleased that she had forgiven him, despite the fact that he most certainly didn’t deserve it.

“We were so worried,” she said afterwards, voice soft and reluctant. “Especially Sirius.”

Remus glanced over at the boy in question. He was sitting obediently on Lottie’s plush pink stool, smiling with his eyes closed. His hair had finally grown back some, and was now just curling around the ridges of his jaw. And his mouth… Christ. Devastatingly handsome, Sirius was. There was no other way to describe it. One look and you were just done for.

“We apologised, sort of,” he said to Lily. “We’re… friends again.”

She smiled, entirely relieved, but Remus found no comfort in it. He didn’t want to be friends with Sirius—or even bandmates. He wanted to be his sky.

“And—voila! All finished,” Lottie declared, stepping back so that Sirius could pop up from the stool and admire her handiwork.

“Looks great, Lot! We should get Potter and Pete up here too—paint up the entire band.”

“In that case, sit down. I’m adding blusher.”

“And that’s my cue,” Remus said, promptly backing out of the room.

Really, he should’ve accepted the blusher. Not five minutes after arriving downstairs, Remus found himself accosted by several aunties, all of them chittering away with a glass of sherry in their hand. One even tried to pinch his cheek, but he was tall enough to swerve her hand and pass it off as a neck cramp.

“You know, I have a daughter about your age."

“Oh Doris, don’t tease the poor boy!”

“I’m not! I only asked if he was on the market."

"Do ignore her, Remus, she's already had far too much to drink."

"Don't belittle me, Gladys, you're just as bad. But what was I saying, Remus? Oh yes—Phillipa. She attends St. Margaret’s Ladies’ College in Heathrow. Darling thing—loves horses. She was awarded first in Dressage at her last competition. Oh, I know—the two of you should meet! I could arrange the whole thing!”

Remus glanced across the salon, desperate for an escape. He could see Phaedra talking to Mrs. Pettigrew, but no Simeon. Then a flash of dark hair as Sirius descended the main staircase and slipped into the parlour.

Doris leaned in. “What is it you said your father did again?”

“Dunno, never met the guy. If you’ll excuse me.”

Remus turned and fled the circle of women, squeezing through the crowd of bodies until he finally reached the glass doors and yanked them open. Inside the parlour, some of the noise and clamour was drowned out and he found Sirius next to Peter’s drum kit, fiddling with the cheap microphone Simeon had brought out from the garage.

“New rule—when we start throwing our own parties, no one over twenty-five’s allowed past the front door."

“What happens when we pass twenty-five?” Sirius asked casually.

“We start keeping a guest list.”

Sirius popped up from his squat, swinging the microphone around on its cord. When he walked he sauntered, and when he smiled he bit his lip, the corners of his mouth curled upwards cheekily. It was unbearable.

“So? How’d Lottie do?”

Skipping forward, he closed his eyes so Remus could see the fierce electric blue that was now rimming his lashes. A bit had smudged at the outer corners, but the makeup suited him—looked like a night already lived.

“You look good,” Remus said, truthfully. “You always look good.”

Sirius gave him a long look and swung the microphone around once more before catching it out of the air. “Well… you don’t look so bad yourself, rockstar.”

Fuck.

“You can’t do that.”

“Do what?”

Remus swallowed. “You know what.”

Before Sirius could offer another rebuttal, James and Peter appeared through the doors, both sporting eyeliner of their own and big grins.

“So, lads?” James started; “Shall we get this show on the road?”

While they were busy doing their final checks, fingers buzzing from nervousness, Lottie came downstairs to join them along her newest beau, the infamous Roger. The investment firm high-flyer came dressed up in a full suit, which would’ve been fine had it not made him look forty. Lottie had already sworn up and down that he wasn’t a day over twenty-seven, but Remus wasn’t entirely sure he believed her. At least he wasn’t balding, and Lottie seemed happy enough. She was showing off her new diamond bracelet to anyone who cared enough to ask—a Christmas gift from the man on her arm.

“So… where did the two of you meet again?” Sirius asked sceptically.

“Roger was visiting daddy’s office and I just happened to be bringing his lunch,” Lottie recited. “We reconnected when all of us came back for holiday. It was fate.”

“She’s hard to say no to,” Roger surmised.

“I see. Does that mean you’ve already rung Clyde and let him know the good news, Lot?”

“Sirius—shut your mouth.”

Sirius immediately held up both hands in surrender, but Roger remained unfazed. “So why ‘Marauders’?” He asked.

“It’s a concept,” James said, busy pouring them all a final shot of whisky for good luck.

“A concept of what?”

“Er… don’t worry about it.”

The parlour door flew open and Lily stuck her head in. “Are you guys ready? Everyone’s waiting.”

James waved her over and all of them, including Lottie and Roger, raised their glasses. “To good times—” He glanced pointedly at Remus; “and to better friends.”

“To all of you tossers!” Lily cried.

“And to rock and roll!” Sirius finished, as they all knocked their rims together and downed the whisky. “WHOO!” Sirius gasped. “Oh yeah, showtime, baby.”

As they hid the leftover booze bottles behind the sofa and took up their instruments, the girls opened the parlour doors and eager party-goers flooded into the room. Family, friends, colleagues, and coworkers—all of them were interested. It was Halloween two-fold, and Remus just hoped they could play loud enough to be heard over the chatter.

“Welcome and happy New Year!” Sirius called, playing at being pragmatic. “We’re gonna be your house band for the night. You have a one, Jannet Pettigrew, to thank for that—which means that any and all complaints can be directed to her immediately following the show!”

Everyone laughed, and Remus couldn’t tear his eyes away. Sirius was such a natural with people and crowds; he spun about with confidence oozing from every pore. Remus would’ve been a wreck were he in his shoes, but Sirius was in his element. Eyes on me, it seemed to say; Don’t you dare look away. I’m here. I’m here.

“We do take requests,” Sirius mused; “Provided said request comes with a tenner—nah, only joking. Though if you see a hat going ‘round I hear it’s poor taste at these things to keep your wallets in your pockets.” More laughter. “Listen to me ramble—you came for a show! Right—right?”

More cheering, this time with hearty laughter and accompanying applause, and Sirius grinned.

“Well, alright then. That’s James, Remus, and Pete, and I’m Sirius. And this… is ‘Jailhouse Rock’.”





* * *





I, I wish you could swim,

Like the dolphins, like dolphins can swim;

Though nothing, nothing will keep us together,

We can beat them, for ever and ever,

Oh we can be Heroes, just for one day...





A rather sozzled crowd of middle-aged aunties and a few busted strings later, they’d given two encores and everyone was left smiling ear to ear. It was a rush, Remus could still feel the ring of Elvis in his ears. This was what it was to really love music—no matter how imperfect the performance, they’d just kept playing. And the entire time, he couldn’t take his eyes off Sirius.

“Weren’t they just wonderful?” Mrs. Pettigrew declared, borrowing the microphone to shout at the crowd; “Yes! Well you all know what time it is—half-hour until midnight!”

As the party began to disperse again, Lily shot forward and threw her arms around James’ neck. “That was so fun! You were amazing—even better than last time!"

“It was, wasn't it?” Sirius concurred, hugging them both.

“But we got all muddled up in the middle,” Peter said irritably. “I thought we agreed ‘Paperback Writer’ and then ‘Metal Guru’?”

“Who cares,” Remus said happily, “we got through it.”

“It was brilliant,” Lily said again, kissing James several times on the cheek and mouth, leaving him a smiling mess.

“Good show, boys,” Mr. Potter called, as he and wife approached. “Your dedication has clearly paid off. Though I did think it was all over after James snapped that string on his finger.”

“That shit hurt for reals, dad,” James said.

"No swearing around your mother," Mr. Potter warned, before leaning in. "Save that for the after-party."

"Monty!" Mrs. Potter sighed, before brushing a hand across the back of Sirius' head fondly. “You boys really were wonderful. It’s so good to see you all together again.”

"Feels good," Sirius replied, looking straight at Remus.

He’d thought it before, but Mrs. Potter was never subtle, Sirius even less so. Excusing himself quietly, Remus returned to the kitchen, desperate for a glass of water. He had to accept several rounds of praise before he got it but luckily Sirius had followed and they were able to seclude themselves on a corner bench, where the chatter and radio music were less noisy.

"So how was your Christmas anyway?" Sirius asked. He’d somehow ended up with a glass of sherry and several lipstick marks on his cheeks, both of which had to be courtesy of some aunty.

"It was alright. Was mostly just Tomny and I."

"Still on the outs with the rest of your friends?"

"That's over with now. Can't go back."

"That sucks."

"Mm."

Sirius began twiddling his thumbs. "So are you gonna tell me what happened with Tomny or what?"

"Nothing happened. I just went to see him."

"And what... played jacks all day?"

Remus gut twisted painfully. "Why don't you just ask what you really want to ask. We've been up and down all day and I'm tired of trying to keep up."

"Don't talk to me like that. I'm not Jillian Stewart. I was your boyfriend."

"Was?"

Sirius looked away, wiping beneath his eyes. "Bloody makeup... So what do you think of Roger?”

"Ha. Classic Sirius..."

"What was that?"

"I don't think anything of Roger."

"No? You don't think he's too old?"

"I guess, but Lottie likes him.”

Sirius nodded thoughtfully. “I think he’s gay.”

“Don’t be so horrible.”

“I’m not! We shook hands just now, and he’s got skin softer than a baby’s bottom. Then he asked me what shampoo I use.”

“That doesn’t mean that he’s—that he’s into guys!”

Sirius smirked bitterly. “Well, I can actually see Lottie marrying a bender. Kind of fits, right? They can share outfits.”

“How is it you find it so easy to slander your own sexuality?”

“Everyone else does it, why should I hold back just because I'm a poofter?”

Remus pressed his fingers into his eyes. “You’re impossible. And a nasty drunk.”

“Maybe.” Sirius paused to sip his drink. “But I've been thinking, if we’re talking statistics, then there’s bound be a few more of us hanging around school. Can’t just be me, McKinnon, and… you. I mean, there’s obviously Barty but he might as well be a sea sponge for all the tits and ass he’s getting.”

“You’re saying Barty’s gay now too?”

“He’s right obsessed with you, ain't he? Not that I blame him.” Sirius cast him a sideways glance before polishing off the sherry. “So, who’s your bet? I'm thinking Freddie Thomas—he’s on the football team with James. That’d be a win, right? At least he’s somewhat fit. And that Darcy Williams girl—Mary said once that she was always staring at other girls in the changing room.”

“This is a sad game. And I don't want to play.”

“Why? Because we’re sad? Pitiable? In that case I’m gonna need vodka—you want one?”

“No, think I’m gonna step out for a smoke actually.”

“Fine. See you later then.”

Sirius stood up from the bench and drifted off through the crowd, not looking back. It was almost startling how quickly they could go from being on top of the world to fighting. It worried Remus, but he was drunk too and really did need a cigarette.

Shrugging on his jacket, Remus stepped out onto the back porch and braced himself against the cold. It'd stopped pouring sometime in the early evening, but the cold kept everything wet and icy. He moved away from the other men standing in a circle and puffing on their rich cigars and ended up around the side of the grand house, smoking alone in the dark. A part of him was angry, but he wanted so badly to move past it. He wanted to know if Sirius had told James he were gay like he’d said he would. He wanted to know if there was a chance at mending things at all. And god, did he want to put Sirius Black’s handsome face through a window.

“I already told you—you can’t be here.”

Remus snapped his head around. He was alone, save for the distant party chatter drifting out from some open window, but the voice had been closer. It cut through the darkness in a harsh whisper, followed by another, this one louder.

“You promised you’d come and see me. You said we could talk!”

“We broke up! What is there to talk about?”

Too curious for his own good, Remus crept around the corner and found himself at the top of the Pettigrews’ driveway. He had to be careful to avoid slipping on the icy pavement, but when he peered around the side of Mr. Pettigrew's Oldsmobile, he spotted the pair arguing and he nearly did a double-take. It was Simeon, standing next to a stranger amongst the sea of parked vehicles. They were squared up to to one another like brick walls, though all Remus could make out of the other guy was a head of dark hair and a large nose that might’ve been handsome.

“I didn’t want to break up,” the stranger said.

"That's funny considering you dumped me," Simeon shot back.

"It was a misunderstanding. You know how much pressure my dad was putting on. I just needed some time."

"Yeah, well maybe I needed time too."

Suddenly, Remus couldn't breathe. Just needed some time, hadn't he said near-on the exact same words to Sirius?

"You can't just decide it's over like that!" The stranger keened. "I deserve another shot!"

“Who says?" Simeon snapped. “Christ—we weren’t bloody married! You're the one who called it quits. What you think I would do, just wait around until you got over yourself?”

“I thought you'd wait at least a few weeks at least! Guy's already told me you've found someone else."

"Maybe I have! Butt out!"

"Who is it? It better not be that slag Lorelei. You know she's just using you.”

“I'm not seeing Lorelei!"

"Who then? Angus? If it's him I'll pound his face into the—"

"It's none of your business who I date, Hugh! We’re not together anymore!”

Remus covered his mouth. The guy was Hugh then, the one he'd caught Simeon with last summer. Holy shit.

“I love you," Hugh said. "And I know you love me too."

“No, I don't."

"Yes, you do. I can tell."

Sirius clung to him, fisting that little silver chain round his neck.

“Oh, how I fucking missed you.”

Tuesday 3rd January 1978





They reached King’s Cross at half-past nine, and despite the fact that they were running slightly behind schedule, Giles refused to miss his chance to pull Remus aside and berate him for every stunt he'd pulled since he was seven.

“You cheeky little blighter!"

"I'm sorry, Gil."

"What were you thinking?!"

"I wasn't, Gil."

"That was very disrespectful, what you did!"

"I know, Gil."

The old driver fisted both hands in front of him.

"The Potters are good people, Remus, and you had Effie near-on in hysterics! Is it really that hard to tell someone where you’re going? To realise that others might worry? People care about you! Do you understand what that means? It means that whenever you go off somewhere on your own, people get concerned! And you don’t get to decide that—you don’t get to decide who cares about you! That ain’t how it works, do you hear me?”

“I hear you," Remus said.

"Are you sure? I don't think you do! Must still have cotton in your ears!"

"I don't," he swore. "I hear you, really. I'll never do it again."

"Never?"

"Never-ever. I give you my word."

Giles huffed very sternly, then tugged the cap from his head and pressed a hand to his forehead, as if struggling to stay angry with him. He realised why right after.

"Remus, I know things with your father are complicated. I had no idea you'd known for so long, and I'm sorry I never told you. For a long time I was just the driver. Didn't feel like my place. But you're important to me, I've watched you grow—known you all your life. So whatever you need, you only need to call. Alright?"

"Alright," Remus said, before chancing his best bet. "Will you tell me one thing then, Gil?"

"What is it?"

"My dad. The real one. Do you know if he's alive?"

Giles sighed then, and glanced up, as if cursing the clouds. "Last I heard he was living somewhere in America."

"America?"

"Yes, sir. New York, if I remember right. But that was going on, six... seven years ago now. I'm sorry, son, but I don't know anything else."

Remus nodded, trying his best to find a way to compartmentalize the information without letting it uproot every other modicum of his life.

"Thanks for telling me, Gil."

"Don't go running off to America now. You do, and I'll ground you for life. No more cigarettes and books until you're eighty."

"Your age then?"

"Oi. What'd I say about that cheek?"

Remus did his best to smile, for Giles, and nodded again. "I won't run off. Promise."

The driver let out a sigh of relief, returning his hat to the top of his head. "Right. Do have all your school things then?”

“Yeah. It’s all in my trunk. Left my amp at James'. I'll just use the one at school.”

"And you're sure you have everything?"

"Mhm."

“Well, I would check again."

As Remus stood on the curb, wondering what it was he could've possibly forgotten, Giles turned and fit his upper body back into the boot of the car. From inside, he hauled out a small white trunk with brass fastenings. Hope’s trunk.

“Felt a shame to get rid of it. Tried fixing it up instead. No more loose handle, see?”

He shook it pointedly before handing it over. With the trunk in his hands again, Remus felt a bit forlorn.

"S’just an old trunk…”

"Old is alright. Old makes memories. And memories are important."

He trailed his fingers along the corner edge. "Yeah, I suppose you're right."

“I'm always right. And it’s good to have more than one case. Keeps things organised. You'll see I tucked some extra things inside it too. New gloves—I know it's cold up there. Some books, and school things too. Only what's useful, of course... You can repay me with good marks, and better attendance. Now get along, don't want to miss your train.”

Remus let the trunk hang down by his side. It didn't quite feel like his but he was grateful for the gesture, and as he turned away to rejoin his friends, a strange feeling of homesickness came over him. Without stopping to think too hard, he spun back around and threw his arms around the old driver instead.

“Thank you for everything, Gil. You've been like a dad to me.”

Giles hesitated, as was to be expected, but finally wrapped his thick, barrel arms around him in return. “Well, I—er… Had to raise you right! No blighter ‘a mine gonna go off to school with a bad attitude.”

They came apart then, and Giles ushered him ahead, eyes turned glassy.

"Best get going then. Your friends are waiting."

He went, and after they’d all said their goodbyes, the six of them made their way onto the train platform, trunks and instruments bungling against their knees with every step. “This is it, lads!” James cried as they approached the train. “Last time we’ll be boarding the ol’ railway north. S’almost enough to make one emotional.”

With a tiny smile, Sirius grabbed his trunk and hauled it up behind him, already moving on down toward their friends' compartment. Remus watched him, wondering just how he was supposed to feel. Two down… Two down… Well, maybe it didn’t sound so bad after all.

“Yeah.” Two down. “I’m coming.”

Chapter 86: January, 1978


Chapter Summary

Another January at Hawkings, and Remus isn't the only one taking charge of his life.

Later, on the train...





Remus had always liked lists. Lists helped keep things tidy, and tidy kept said things from going missing. It also kept one from bollixing up their entire life; who knew what, who went where, who liked who—that was messy, no way around it. Keeping tidy lies prevented the inevitably messy from getting even messier. It also helped keep peace of mind.

Marlene. Tomny. Regulus. Simeon. Lottie—today's list. Everyone he'd told (inadvertently or otherwise) about his and Sirius' secret relationship. It felt like a tidy record, until he thought more on it and realised that people had lists of their own. Marlene knew and was gay herself, which consequently meant that her girlfriend Nicole knew as well. And Tomny knew, because Tomny knew everything, which must've meant that Tonya had known, even if she'd guessed it on her own. Regulus had sworn up and down that he'd told no one about Sirius, but it wasn't enough. His parents had realised it anyway the day Walburga Black found those dirty magazines beneath the floorboards of Sirius' bedroom, and no matter how badly he fretted, Remus would never know the full extent of who knew. How many? How many other family members or evil doctors or nasty psychologists knew about Sirius' shameful little secret?

At least the Blacks were far away, he reasoned. One could hardly add names to a list without knowing them in the first place. But what about the problems closer to home? What about Lottie, the self-proclaimed queen of gossip—could she really be trusted to keep such juicy news to herself?

Suddenly it was starting to feel like Remus' tidy list had gone out the window. He spent most of the never-ending train ride back to school with his nose in a book, eyes glued to the page but hardly absorbing a word. He felt the fizzy-drink feeling return, like he was a rocket ready to launch right off the compartment bench. His more reckless side kept telling him he should just do it—whip his head up and announce it to everyone.

I'M GAY!

Or well...

Not exactly gay.

More like half and half.

I still like girls. Girls are great—Women! I meant women, Mary. What? No, we always meant to tell you! Y-Yeah, Sirius too. And we're sorta... No, Lily, it isn't like that! We wanted to wait until we were sure we could trust—er, no sorry, wrong choice of words. Huh...? NO! We do trust you, but there's always... And we weren't fighting! Or, I mean we kind of were, but we're better now and—no, Lottie, I've never thought of Mick Jagger naked, but Sirius—no, Peter, I've never thought about YOU naked either. And Tomny isn't—BUTT STUFF?! ... ohmygod.

Then again—not a chance. Maybe in another life he'd have allowed the reckless abandon to truly take over rather than just get muddled in his head, but not this Remus Lupin. Not when he had no guarantee of the outcome. He'd rather it happen slowly, one at a time. Like writing a song. First the melody, then the bridge... First James, then Lily... Peter, Mary... Lily sat beside James, red hair wild and windblown from having just transferred over from Doncaster. Not long after the trip into Craigtyre, Remus told Marlene everything. About Lily and James, how they’d taken the news and the wonderful way they’d accepted it without question. A part of him had been almost afraid to tell her; he’d wrapped up his story with the assurance that there was no need for her to do the same, and that neither he nor Sirius had told them anything about her and Nicole.

Afterwards Marlene was quiet for a long time. Remus sat quietly too, waiting for her to process it all, and eventually he felt the gentle nudge of Marlene’s pinky finger against his own.

“Tell me again?” She asked, her voice barely a whisper. “Tell me again what they said?”

Chapter 88: Reunion


Chapter Summary

Sirius has always enjoyed putting on a show. Turns out it's a family trait.



Chapter Notes

The song at the beginning of this chapter wasn't actually released until October of 1978 but I couldn't resist so meh to the details.

CW for this chapter:

Intense references to child abuse, including physical but mostly emotional/psychological as well as strong references to homophobia.

This chapter's got some solid hurt/comfort, so please be mindful of these content warnings. They all go through it, but come out on the other side stronger.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



I don't need you to worry for me 'cause I'm alright,

I don't want you to tell me it's time to come home;

I don't care what you say anymore this is my life,

“Looks like he’s finally developed a sense of humour at least,” Sirius gripped, taking back the card and turning it over in his hands several times. Remus had already mapped the route; if they borrowed the money for the train from their friends they could be there and back in three days. It was a Tuesday. Remus only remembered because he taught music to the fifth years that day. Things had been tough going without Regulus there to help, and his acting replacement, Anton, was positively useless when it came to all things music and children.

"Finally! I thought it'd never end," he groaned, digging the foam plugs from his ears. He insisted on wearing them to every lesson, and though Remus doubted they did much against a nine year-old and a tuba, he wasn't interested enough to ask.

"New assignments from McGonagall today, eh?" Anton said, as they said goodbye to the kiddies and made their way back toward their half of campus. "Hope I get something easy, like office duty. No one cares if you slack off there, all you've got to do is show up! How 'bout you, Lupin?"

"Don't matter to me." As long as it's away from you.

Outside the building, pulled straight up front was a sleek black Bentley car, complete with the flashy hood ornament. He glared at them, then gave a sharp flick of the pipe he was smoking, indicating that they should move on.

"Who do you think that beauty belongs to, Lupin?"

"Maybe the Queen's come to visit," Remus replied snidely, not really interested.

Still rushing, they went up the front stairs together only to come upon a cluster of other prefects on the ground floor, all mulling around like nervous sheep. Remus let her go. The stairs he took two at a time until he'd emerged on the third floor landing. It was less stifling so high up and hardly crowded, and yet Remus couldn't get a breath in. It was like a stone had lodged itself in the middle of his chest. Sirius, he thought cowardly, I can't do this, maybe we should get Sirius!

But he didn't want to risk it. Regulus was back now, but how long until his mother decided it was all a mistake and took him away again? How would he ever be able to face Sirius knowing he'd let his little brother slip right through his fingers?

Don't be a bloody pansy, she's a woman not the devil!

He wasn't sure how much of that was true, but he approached the Headmistress's office anyway. He'd just about grasped that heavy golden knocker when a sharp, reedy voice cut through the quiet.

"I cannot believe you let that filth back in here. This is why we thought to keep our son home, do you even realise the damage I could do to this school's reputation with a single phone call?"

The voice was coming from inside the Headmistress’s office. He was sure he'd never heard it before, but somehow it was still familiar. It was every sordid creak of the Shrieking Shack, every shrill piano note in the late-night horror films, every ghastly screech in his nightmares. But there was something else too; a certain hitch in the consonants, and the way she seemed to hold her breath before certain words—as though she knew exactly what would create the deepest and most efficient cut.

It was a woman, and she was angry. She wasn’t even yelling at him—there was an entire door between them—and yet Remus felt it in his bones. It was like being thrust back in time. In all of his memories, he could only recall one time Hope had really yelled at him. It was after he’d overheard a few of the house staff gossiping; deranged, they'd called her, raving mad, likely to cave her own head in. And those pills, someone ought to flush them away, save us the trouble.

So he did. He thought he was helping, and she never bothered to keep them out of reach anyway. He realised his mistake only when she found him with the empty bottle in his hand.

REMUS! OH—What have you done? What have you DONE?! Those were important, darling! We talked about—oh my… Bad! You are so bad, Remus! You’re a BAD boy! I needed those! Where am I going to get them now? Are YOU going to get them for me? ARE YOU?!

Remus felt ill. He couldn't breathe. Then he heard McGonagall's voice, and he was no longer six years-old and hiding beneath his mother's bed.

"Mrs. Black, you should know that we here at Hawkings treat all students equally, regardless of background or extenuating circumstances."

A sharp sound, like a smack.

Remus would've recognised her anywhere, she had the same black and grey colouring as each of her sons, but where Sirius' eyes were captivating like a live thunderstorm, hers were cold and shadowed. The woman’s like five foot nothing, Sirius' voice echoed in his head; You see her and think 'a swift breeze could knock her over', but I swear, when she’s angry... It’s like watching that kid from the fucking Exorcist. Nothing can stop her.

She hadn't tried throwing him out a window yet, but the expression on her face didn't feel so far off.

Inexplicably, Remus had almost missed him. He'd been sitting apart, looking almost bored, but when he stood up from one of the velvet armchairs ahead of the fireplace, there was no mistaking him as Sirius' father. Regulus looked away, and Remus knew it was shame. Don't look at me.

I can't. What have they done to you?

"Remus, I'll have to ask you to wait downstairs with the other prefects."

Professor McGonagall began backing him out the door, but Remus couldn't tear his eyes away.

Regulus.

Don't look at me.

"Are you a child or a mongrel? Get!"

"Remus, please."

She shut the door, and there was more ranting, but Remus could barely understand it. His mind was racing a mile a minute. He had to see Sirius, had to get him before anyone else did—had to warn him! He couldn't let Trish bring him there, he'd be done for. She'd ruin him.

He must've flown down the staircase, it was a miracle he didn't stumble. The other prefects were still piddling about the ground floor, irritated and tired of waiting. Several of them made noises of discontent when he shoved them aside, but there was no waiting to be polite. Outside the cold air seized in his lungs. Remus only got a few feet before he finally skidded on one of the slick steps. Thankfully someone was there to catch him.

"Woah! Where's the fire, Moony?"

It was James. He caught him near the bottom of the stairs, which was terrible of course because where there was a James, there was always a—

Sirius grabbed his sleeve.

"You saw him then?" He demanded. "Is he still inside?"

Remus looked at Sirius desperately, then at Trish who stood behind him.

"You actually brought him here?!"

"It's his brother!"

"No, Sirius, don't—"

The front doors opened, and three figures clad in black strode out. They looked out of place at their school, like nightmares come to life.

"Stand up straight, Regulus! I thought I already told you to stand up straight."

They were getting closer. Remus felt his breath hitch. Five feet, four feet, three!

They passed by.

"And your hair is far too long. You must get it cut if you're to stay at all. I won't have you running around looking like some woe-begone queer. Are you listening, Regulus?"

"Into the car, Walburga. It's time to go."

Remus stared in disbelief. They were only standing a few feet off to the side, and yet they hadn't even noticed them. As the family approached the lush car, their driver hopped-to, opening first the far side for Mr. Black, then the curb-facing for his wife. Mr. Black was first to pull Regulus aside, and after whispering something into his ear, he stepped round the car and ducked inside. Then it was Walburga's turn.

"You remember what I told you," she hissed, grasping Regulus by the elbow like her were a scolded child. "One toe out of line, and you will never see this place again. It would be like nothing. One call, Regulus. One."

“Yes, mother.”

"Remember what you agreed to. Mind your lessons, and do not disappoint us. This is a gift. You should be grateful. Now... kiss me goodbye.”

“That fucking bitch...” Sirius started forward, hands fisted at his side, but James got in front of him first.

“Mate, you don’t wanna do this."

“Get out of my way, James."

"But they’re leaving!”

"I don't care! I’m not gonna let her talk like that. Not—Not here!”

And for all his wild and irrational nature, it almost made sense. Sirius loved the Potters, loved even more guessing what their life could be one day, but for the last thirteen years Hawkings had been his home, and one did not let others lay waste to that which they loved.

Ripping free of James, Sirius cut down the final set of steps.

"Oi! Oi, hey, Mum!"

It was crude, but that was the point. When Walburga heard the unrefined shouting she instantly recoiled like a spider. Her spindly fingers formed tight fists across her stomach as she set eyes upon them, her face forming the most unsettling scowl. She was like every angry teacher, tutor, and housemaid Remus had ever had, all rolled up into one—and yet somehow still worse.

“You. I knew you'd be here."

“And where else would I be—Belgium?”

For the not the first time, Remus thought Sirius would've made a wonderful actor. Like the flick of a switch his tone became boorish and disinterested, until the ten feet between them might as well have been ten miles.

"Been a while since you made the big trip up north, did you enjoy the sights? Hope the refreshments were up to your standards. I know you prefer your blood fresh, ya old vampire."

"Orion!" Walburga screeched. "Get out here this instant!”

There was a moment of hostile silence, and then a click as the back door opened and Orion Black stepped back out in his sweeping winter coat. He shut the door with a sharp flick of his wrist and rounded the car, stopping only at his wife’s side.

“Hey Dad,” Sirius sneered. “Lookin’ stellar. Absolutely mint. How’s the heart condition treating ya? Guess Mum hasn't completely written you off yet, otherwise who would be left to listen to her shriek about the neighbours?”
