Mr. Black set a hand on his wife's shoulder, temporarily silencing her shrieking. Next to him, Regulus still hadn't raised his gaze from the pavement. Perhaps it was because he felt so many eyes on him; he couldn't stop shifting his weight, hands tapping rhythmically at his sides the way they always did when he was nervous. No doubt drawn by Mrs. Black's cries, a small circle of prefects had emerged from the Hall and stood looming on the stairs above, like vultures to a fresh carcass. It was the perfect feast, with the perfect cast; they waited to see who would draw first blood. Remus could only hope one of them had the sense to send for McGonagall.

"Sirius," Mr. Black started, with a voice like rolling thunder, "you should know better than to test your mother.”

“Yeah, well… You know how it is. I get so choked up at family visits. And I'm the only one who can get under that scaly skin of hers, why deny myself such simple pleasures?"

Sirius tucked his hands up behind his head casually, but no one looked impressed. Remus could feel the sweat on his palms while James' dread was pouring off him in rivets.

"Sirius..."

“Enough," Walburga hissed. "I’ll say this only once. All of you—stay away from our son.”

Sirius slapped his hands to his heart. "Who? Me?"

"You are not our son. You are nothing but a mistake."

It was dismissive. It was cruel. It was everything Remus had imagined of the Blacks. Superior, brutal, unyielding. There was no room for argument; Regulus was their son, and Sirius was, well…

Sirius smiled, lifelessly, and Remus imagined he could see the energy seep out of him like blood from a wound. Then he surprised all of them. Instead of rising to the obvious bait, Sirius looked away from his mother—dismissing her—and faced his brother.

“Are you okay, Reg?”

Walburga swept in almost before Sirius could get the words out; “Don’t you dare speak to him,” she snarled, while Regulus looked on, shoulders caved in on themselves like an animal bound for slaughter.

“He’s my brother,” Sirius said through his teeth. "Piss off."

A short gasp went up from the other prefects. Trish covered her mouth.

Wow, did you hear that? He told her to piss off...

Ha, look at her face!

"You pathetic little welp..."

With eyes like fire, Walburga Black raised her hand. She might've hit him, right there on the school's front steps, but luckily for them not everyone was as interested in making a scene.

"Walburga!"

Mr. Black had his wife by the wrist instantly. Meanwhile, James and Remus had their friend by either elbow, yanking him backward to keep some space between them. It was protective, but Sirius fought it every step of the way.

"You can't do this forever! We're not your little puppets!"

Walburga began to laugh. A deep, manic, belly-driven laugh. It cut into everyone watching like a knife; surely used the madness, Mr. Black threw down her arm and stomped back toward the car.

"Oh, Sirius, you aren't our anything. You aren't even a part of this family... You're nothing, really."

"You think I wanted to be a part of this family? This isn't a family, it's a curse!"

"Oh, you should be so ungrateful. I didn't curse you, brat, I gave you a gift! It was me who made you, who sat your miserable little behind in front of that bloody piano. I gave you everything, even though I knew—I knew you’d come out wrong the moment you opened those dirty eyes and looked at me. It's you—you're the curse. I couldn't so much as comb your hair without seeing it."

“You never combed my hair! Not once!”

“Oh don’t whine, Sirius. It is so unbecoming."

"I hate you," he moaned. "I wish you'd die already, both of you! I hate you!"

"Is that really the best you can do?" She smiled wickedly, and then clicked her tongue in disappointment. "Just one little bit of hatred?"

I would’ve expected more from you.

I would've expected more.

Expected more.

More.

It was a waterfall. Remus didn't remember letting go of Sirius' arm, of getting in between them. All he saw was her shocked expression, the indifferent face of his father, and that horrible landscape painting that hung on the wall. Hurt me, not him. I'll kill you if you hurt him.

"Moony!"

There was a hand on the back of his neck, another on the side of his face—Sirius. When Remus came back to himself they were nearly nose to nose, Sirius holding him back like a grounding rod in a rabid storm. Everyone was watching but it hardly mattered, the Blacks were already getting back into their car, and Regulus was gone.

"I do hope you can make Alphard's money last, Sirius," Walburga called, eyes wide like she too had been spooked by Remus' sudden threat. "I knew letting that man near my family was a mistake, and look, here's the proof."

"Walburga, get in the car."

With a sharp glance her husband's way, Mrs. Black folded herself into the back seat, pausing long enough to smile at them once more.

"Goodbye. We won't be seeing each other again."

The driver shut the door, and the vile face of Walburga Black disappeared behind tinted windows.

“Yeah, go!” Sirius cried, wrenching himself free of James and rushing the car’s boot. He placed a sharp kick on its back tire and continued until the expensive lift was pulling away from the curb. “GO!" He shouted, wrenching up piles of snow and throwing it at the back window. "Get out of here! Get out of this place!”

A sudden slamming came from the top of the stairs as Professor McGonagall burst through the doors, scattering a row of gawking prefects. Someone must've fetched her then, or she'd overheard the shouting all the way from the third floor.

"What the devil is going on here? Speak now, somebody!"

A few kids pointed, and McGonagall's eyes found them in a second.

“Sirius! Sirius Black, come up here this instant!”

It was Trish who moved first. “Go!” She urged, shoving Sirius from behind. “Regulus went toward the dorms, I bet if you cut through the trees you’ll be able to head him off! I’ll distract McGonagall.”

Shooting her a grateful look, James grabbed Sirius by the arm again. "C'mon, before she hauls you in for questioning or therapy. Moony, hurry up!"

Taking the shortcut had been a good idea in theory. On good days they shaved off at least a few minutes but come winter the forest paths were scattered with snow and various tree debris. They had to slough through ice and mud, and even then they only emerged with seconds to spare. Already Regulus was cutting across Salazar's front lawn, face red like he'd been sprinting.

"Reg!" Sirius hollered. "Reg, stop!"

"Don't come near me! I don't want to see you!"

"I said stop, you bloody twat!" Then Sirius picked up a snowball the size of his fist and hurled it right against the back of his brother's head. Regulus went down hard on impact, spooking a group of boys who'd just made their way out of the dorm. When he stood up again, Regulus' entire front was covered in snow. He gaped like he couldn't believe it, and rounded on Sirius viciously.

"I hate you! You ruin everything!"

"Yeah, well I hate you too!" Sirius fired back. "You're a boring, skittish little prude, and all you do is rag on me! Ever since we were kids, it's always whinge, whinge, whinge! And I listened to it because—because DAMMIT—you're my brother!"

With a great wail, Regulus picked up a snowball of his own to throw. Sirius was already so close, it should've hit him dead-on, but his pitch went wide and he missed, nearly toppling back down to his knees. Luckily, Sirius was there to catch him.

“It’s not my fault!” Regulus cried. “I told them not to come—It isn’t my fault!”

“I know."

"You ruin everything!"

"I know."

Regulus pushed—pulled—anything to get Sirius to let go, but he clung on.

“I know,” he kept saying. I know. I know. I know.

Beyond them, James and Remus could do nothing. Faces were peeking out of painted green windows; soon news of the brawl would be everywhere. Everyone would finally know the Black family legacy, and how it all culminated in two traumatised boys. Perhaps it'd always been building to this, perhaps this was the give.

"You're a bad brother," Regulus wheezed. "I hate you."

"I know."

"I want to hate you!"

"I know."

The dorms to Salazar opened and Barty Crouch spilled out, along with Yaxley and Travers. All three boys looked shocked to see Regulus, even more so to find him grappling his brother.

“Regulus? ... Reg?"

It could've been a trick of the light, or maybe Remus was just going snow-blind, but the concern on Barty's face almost looked real. His brow was deeply creased, and he realised it was concern; concern for a friend that he'd always assumed was one of convenience. It was enough to shake Regulus back to his conceited senses though, and immediately he was thrashing against his brother.

“Let—Let go of me!”

“No.”

Sirius kept his hold, locking arms behind Regulus' back like shackles in the gallows.

“Get off—get off! GET OFF OF ME!”

“No!”

Denied freedom, Regulus’ writhing eventually turned to fists and he began to beat Sirius wherever he could; in the sides, on the back, even the head when he could reach it. James started forward in his defense, but Sirius just let loose a ferocious 'DON'T!' and it was enough to ward all of them off. Soon enough both brothers lost their footing, and together they rolled like crocodiles across the snow. Regulus spat as he struggled, gleaning a particularly nasty shot off of Sirius' ribs.

“I HATE YOU!” He raged, voice cracking. “I WANT YOU GONE!”

“I KNOW!” Sirius bellowed back.

“LET GO!”

“I WON’T!”

Before he knew it, Remus had intercepted him. "Don't interfere, Crouch.”

“I ain't afraid of you, Loony! Get your bonkers mate and get the fuck off our lawn!”

“No, you’re not stopping this,” James added severely, appearing at Remus’ side. Barty faltered at that, and ultimately glanced back to where Regulus was still screaming, flopping back and forth with Sirius pinning him in an iron-clad embrace.

It took a while for the struggling to cease, but once Regulus had finally managed to tire himself out, both he and Sirius sagged back against the ground, heaving and covered head-to-toe in snow. No one knew what to say, so no one said anything at all, and eventually Regulus wiped his sleeve over his eyes and sat up.

"I never want to see you again," he said bitterly.

"Well then, Reggie... you're just gonna have to learn to live with your eyes shut. 'Cause I ain't leaving ya... Not this time..."

With a conflicted expression, Regulus pushed himself to his feet and turned back to his dorm. He stepped forward and stumbled, but Barty was at his side immediately, grabbing his friend by the arm and leading him away. No one stopped them, and James was already back at Sirius’ side, helping him to his feet.

“Are you alright, Pads?” He murmured, while Remus gave all their on-lookers a nasty glare and even nastier gesture.

"PISS OFF! SHOW'S OVER!" He looked back to Sirius, and darted over. "Sirius...?"

"I'm alright," Sirius croaked robotically. "Just... gon' take a walk, I think. You two can go find Pete, or whatever..."

“It's okay, mate," James told him; "we'll fill Pete in later. Let's go on your walk.”

Sirius exhaled like he wanted to fight them too, but only nodded. With one last look at his brother's dorm, he turned and limped his way toward the nearby pavement. Remus, and James too probably, had expected Sirius to turn away from the dorms and head toward the main campus, or maybe the music room. He'd always gone that way when he needed to be alone. Now instead he carried on up the lane, silently moving ahead of them like a leaf on the wind.

The chapel was an unexpected end to their journey. Sirius was a self-proclaimed agnostic, and the church held very few good memories for any of them. Of course there was the odd prank or two—even the failed ones could be remembered fondly, but not fondly enough to bring actual comfort. At least the place was empty, Remus told himself. They were able to walk right in, past the confessionals, beneath the organ balcony, and right into the very heart of the building. They stopped only when they'd reached the first pew, and there Sirius finally collapsed, bent over with his head between his knees.

Wordlessly, James and Remus took up their seats alongside him, waiting for something—anything—to happen. It almost felt odd for them. Them, who'd never waited for anything but rather, made anything happen.

When Sirius sat up again it was like they all let out a collective breath. He sniffled only once, before squinting up at the large statue of Christ that hung at the head of the church. It'd been there all year, hanging above them with it's tortured expression. Remus felt no love from it.

“The Blacks paid for that statue, you know,” Sirius said, almost musingly.

“We know, Sirius,” James answered, in a gentle voice. Sirius responded with a humourless chuckle and pressed a finger beneath his nose, which was bleeding slightly.

“Blimey, that little blighter got me good. Look, Prongs—real blood.” He held his hand out to James, who just looked uncomfortable, before bursting into sudden laughter. “It’s almost funny, ya know! They come all the way here… just—just to be angry. Just to poison everything. When I was a kid I thought that maybe if they were to just get out of the house for a bit they might finally be happy. I mean, I was happy here and dad had that bird in London he was fucking so I couldn’t have been all wrong, right? Ha… I was left-handed as a kid, wasn’t I, Prongs?”

“Yes, Sirius…”

“Yeah, and she used to order my tutors to smack me on the hand every time I reached for a pencil with my left, remember that? Broke me of the habit... Then there was this one summer when I was seven, she wanted to make sure we were learning useful things, like our languages. So she refused to let us speak English the whole time. Reg was only six—six! Can you believe that, Moony? Well, this one day it was Italian, and I couldn’t remember how to ask to go to the bathroom at dinner. So she made me sit in it. In front of everyone… I just… sat there…”

Remus was biting down hard on his knuckle. He could feel the pain in his bone, and wondered briefly how much more pressure was needed to break skin. He had no words, nothing that could make any of it better. He and James sat in the same silence they’d walked in with. They didn't know what to do, how to help.

Suddenly Sirius leapt up from the pew. “Fuck you!” He hollered, pointing a vicious finger at the statue. “Fuck you and your money! And your house! And your bloody religion and stupid shitty pride! Fuck your parents—and your parents’ parents! I can’t wait to drag your name through the fucking mud! Fuck you! FUCK YOU! FUCK YOU!”

Sirius turned and reached for the nearest bible, ripping it up from the pew across the aisle and sending it flying through the air. It barely brushed the statue’s foot and fell with an unceremonious thud against the choir stands, but by then Sirius already had another in hand. He threw it too, getting closer to the statue this time but still missing its mark.

“FUCK!” He roared, throwing a third and then a fourth, their pages whipping through the air like flightless birds.

“Sirius…” James stood up from the pew, following his friend down the aisle as he came apart in pieces.

“They ruin everything, James! They’ve fucked me up forever! I’m gonna be like this—FOREVER!”

Remus came too, desperate to soothe him, but there was nothing to be done. Sirius kicked the baseboards at the foot of the chancel and shoved aside a large golden candlestick, shattering the wax into pieces on the marble floor.

"Sirius." James reached for him. "Sirius, please. It'll be alright, I promise!"

"Get away!" Sirius howled, stepping away and not hearing any of it. "It's you, too! You think so too!"

"No, never."

"You do! She said I came out wrong, do you know what that means? It means it's my fault! He got sent away and it's MY FAULT!"

"Who?" James pleaded.

"Miles," he whined, like a kicked dog. "It was my letters they found, mine! I'm the reason his grandparents found out, I'm the reason they took him out of school, and you won't even say his fucking name anymore!"

Sirius might as well have punched him. James looked at Remus, astounded, and shook his head stiffly.

"I—I don't... But it upsets you, Sirius! I mean, what if he'd died or something? It's not your fault he got sick."

“Jesus Christ, he wasn’t sick, James—he was gay!” Slamming his hands on the chancel bench, Sirius turned and knocked over another candle holder. "He was a fucking queer, just like me, and I liked him!"

It was as though all the fight left Sirius at once. He staggered before that great statue of Christ, breaths turned raspy while James slumped down on the end of a pew. Remus half expected God Himself to appear and strike them down for such sins, or at least send Father Minsin to do it for him, but there was nothing. Just the hollow silence of the church.

“And you wanna know the sickest part?" Sirius whimpered finally. "I’m thankful... Yeah, I’m glad Miles is gone, 'cause otherwise, we might not have known Moony, and I can’t imagine not knowing Moony. So yeah, I am the curse. I got my best friend pulled from school, and I’m fucking glad for it.”

James had gone silent, and Remus felt the sharp sting of his nails as they dug themselves into the palms of his hands. Sirius had quieted too, but Remus could tell the rage hadn't gone; it'd simply seeped back under his skin like oil in a desert. And he was angry too. Not at Sirius, at the world. At fate for being so graciously ironic. To have him Sirius had had to give up Miles, and it'd carved a wound in him so deep that only his greatest undoer, his mother, had been able to dredge it up again.

It wasn't fair.

Glaring down at the floor, Remus spotted one of the bibles Sirius had thrown lying at the foot of the chancel. Silently, he moved forward and picked it up, before wrenching his arm behind his head and whipping the heavy book directly at the statue. It hit Christ just off the forehead, and the top heavy statue teetered for just a moment before settling.

"Fuck you," Remus told it. Then he picked up another bible, and offered it to Sirius. "Fuck them."

Sirius stared.

He took the book.

Pages tore as it ripped through the air.

"Fuck you!"

"Yeah!" James shouted, picking up a bible of his own. "Fuck you!"

They beat the statue into submission, until each of them were shaking and heaving with the effort of their rage. The stone Christ remained upright, but Remus imagined it was as close as they were going to get to smiting God on a Tuesday.

"Kay..." James panted. "No one tell Marlene."

It must've been the right thing to say, as Sirius snorted and clapped his hands over his face.

"Eugh... fucking hate crying... You bastards, why'd you let me cry?"

"As if we could stop you from doing anything, Padfoot," Remus teased meekly. Sirius dropped his hands to look at him, and a shade of doubt passed over his face.

"Moons..."

"Don't be sorry," Remus told him, firmly. "I'm only glad you're alright."

He gathered Sirius against him and kissed him once on the cheek, twice on the lips. It didn't matter if Sirius was thinking of Miles while he did it, for once Remus did not feel jealous. If this was Sirius' pain, then he would bear it too.

"Hey," Remus said, when they broke apart. "Is that my jumper?"

Sirius glanced down at the school vest, which was clearly too baggy in the chest.

“Oh, is it?”

“Yes, it is.”

Sirius smirked, pushing up the oversized sleeves for good measure. "Wondered why I liked it so much."

They kissed again, until Sirius snapped his face away.

“Potter, stop staring!”

Across the aisle, James’ mouth dropped open in mild offence. “I’m not staring, you two just happen to be kissing right in front of me!”

“Avert your eyes then, Peeping Tom.”

James scoffed, but obediently clapped a hand over his eyes. Sirius chuffed then, while Remus glanced around them at the mess.

"We should probably go anyway, before someone catches us."

"You two aren't planning on heading back to the room for a shag, are you?" James called, eyes still covered. "Because I'm suddenly in need of a kip."

Sirius kicked a bible toward him and tackled his friend.

"Some ally!" He cried, while James laughed and wrestled him into a headlock. Remus followed them down the centre aisle, before a flash of gold caught his eye. Along the far wall, sitting on an altar, was a row of communion chalices, probably left out to be polished after that morning's mass. Remus went to them, and picked up one of the heavy metal cups, before returning to Sirius and offering it to him.

“Whaddya say, Pads, one more round?"

Sirius looked up, and quickly unravelled himself from James' headlock. When he snatched the cup to race back to the head of the church, he was grinning.

“I used to think he was the bad influence on you," James said. "Now I know better. You're an enabler, Moons."

"We enable each other," Remus smirked. "It's a symbiotic relationship."

"More like neurotic."

"Semantics."

James shook his head. "Look, there he goes."

Up ahead, Sirius raised the chalice into the air.

“FUCK—” He grunted; “YOU!”

The dish soared, arching through the air like a single golden star—and smacked Christ square in the face. With a violent clang, loud enough to make all of them flinch, it bounced off the statue and clattered back to the chancel floor. Again Remus waited for the smiting, but nothing happened, and eventually Sirius turned back around.

“There! Feels good… Now we can go—”

There was a low cracking sound—smite!—and Christ’s nose snapped clean off, crumbling to the floor with a dull thump.

"Uh... Whoops."

“I think that means it's time to go!" James bleated, already sprinting for the doors. He ditched Remus, who was fully frozen until Sirius took him by the hand, laughing while tugging him down the aisle.

"C'mon, Moons, leg it!"

Outside the sun was warm. Remus stared at the back of Sirius' head and breathed a sigh of relief.

Justice .



* * *





The statue had been discovered by the following morning, sans a nose, and promptly covered up. By dinner rumours had already begun to swirl, but neither Marauder was quick to claim credit. They took up their usual seats in the dining hall with stubborn silence, pretending as though they didn't notice the swirling rumours surrounding the Blacks, as well as Sirius and Regulus’ fight in front of Salazar. Thankfully none of the girls had attempted to pry into what had happened, which was a relief, but Peter insisted on knowing the whole story.

"It's not my fault I missed it," he said, when Sirius dismissed the interest. "I had AV Club..."

Sirius didn't condemn him at least, but Remus knew he felt embarrassed, perhaps even more so over his outburst in the church afterwards. In the end they told Peter what was necessary, and dropped it. Other kids steered clear, afraid of being called out by James' protective wrath. Not even Barty said anything, though that was to be expected.

Across the dining hall, no one had attempted to approach Regulus. The amount of eyes on him doubled when he and his roommates sat down for breakfast. He didn’t look any better than the day before, but he wasn't entirely withdrawn. Every now and then Barty or one of the others would lean over and whisper something, to which Regulus would nod or shake his head.

“You think I fucked up?” Sirius asked quietly, drawing Remus’ attention back from the table.

“No,” he answered. “He needed to know someone cared.”

“Guess I’m not the only one. Don't look now, but Penny Prefect's on the move.”

For a moment Remus assumed that Sirius had meant him, but then Sirius jutted his chin back toward his brother, and he turned to look. Trish was standing next to Regulus’ table, a cup of tea in her hand. She smiled and set it down next to him, but Regulus never met her gaze. He appeared nervous, embarrassed maybe. He kept nodding along to whatever it was she was saying. Barty and the rest of his roommates shared perturbed looks but none of them rebuffed her, and in the end Trish stepped back from the table and retreated to her own. On the way she caught Remus’ eye and gave him a small wave.

“I swear to god,” Sirius mumbled, “if he turns into a lady killer…”

“There's potential," Remus smirked. "Maybe."

He got a sharp elbow to the ribs for it, but they stopped obsessing after that, and returned to their dinner and shared talk of Marlene’s latest social justice plight; the amount of meat and animal byproduct served at meals.

“I just think that if God meant for us to be herbivores, he wouldn't have given us kebabs," Mary reasoned, waving her chicken döner ahead of her nose.

"Are you Buddhist or Catholic, make up your mind!"

Mary giggled and bit into the kebab, while Sirius did the same.

"I'm with Snatchy. McKinnon, you’ve been resisting your nature for the last six months, but we can't all be so resilient. We’re meant to be carnivores, we need the protein, otherwise how could we ever expect to stay on top of the food chain?”

“Humans are omnivores,” Marlene shot back. “And we’re not actually at the top of the food chain, that’s an outdated expression. It’s more of a circle, but if there was going to be a top it’d be animals like polar bears and killer whales—actual apex predators. If anything, we’re more similar to pigs.”

Sirius chewed on the kebab, before pushing his nose up. “Oink! Oink!”

"Ooh, go do one, Sirius Black."

“Maybe you should go into public office, Marlene,” Lottie offered. “I mean, you have so many opinions on everything. That’s what politicians need, right?”

”Yeah, I’d off myself before ever considering a career in politics. No, I think I might try and go back to Africa after we finish school. Somewhere like Mali or Burkina Faso.”

“I can’t visit you in Mali or Burkina Faso,” Mary complained. “Do they even have phone service?”

“Of course. In the cities.”

“Why can’t you ever volunteer somewhere nice? Like Austria or Portugal or... Latvia?”

It was a quarrel they had often, but Marlene just smiled and nudged Mary fondly. In return Mary gave her a long look before ultimately sighing and bringing her tea cup to her lips.

“Honestly, there’s no winning with you.” She set the teacup down. "Well, it's not Burkina Faso, but I might as well tell you guys before word gets out. I've decided to go on to university."

"Were you not going to before?" Lily asked, alarmed.

"I considered taking a year off, my cousins in Montpellier even invited me to come stay with them, but I've decided against it. I've been talking to Mrs. Buchanan, and she's helping me apply. French, with a focus on vocal arts on the side."

Sirius nearly spat his tea. “Vocal arts? Since when has singing appealed to you, Macdonald?"

“Since I started voice lessons with Mrs. Buchanan last year, thank you very much. Sorry if you've only just noticed."

“And what does your family say?” Peter asked, mouth agape like the rest of them.

“Daddy doesn’t care, as long as I'm doing something with my life. Honestly he’d probably rather I just get married, but that sounds like a horrible waste of time if you ask me. Men are only nice to wake up to when you know they're leaving after breakfast. I'm sure you'd agree, right Lottie?”

Lottie sneered. “There’s nothing wrong with wanting to get married. Love is the most powerful emotion in the world. It can save lives, even.”

“Or ruin them,” Sirius answered, hopefully thinking of his parents and not Remus. “You really want to be a singer, Macdonald?”

Mary shrugged indifferently. “Dunno. Maybe. But not everyone has to be as loud about their dreams as you, Black.”

The table's mood felt more thoughtful after that, and Remus got the sense that each of their friends were imagining their own incoming futures; who and what they wanted to be, where they might end up. Would it bring fame or fortune, maybe love? Ideally it would be all three but if Remus had to choose, he knew which one he would rather have. Lily may have still been waiting on an Oxbridge acceptance letter, but school didn’t interest him. As long as he and his friends could stay together in whatever capacity, he’d be happy.

“Hey.”

All eight of them glanced up to find Regulus standing at the end of the table, staring at Sirius with his hands tightly at his sides. Regulus wasn't the type to pick a fight first, and though a second round of their brawl seemed unlikely, the rest of them were instantly put on edge.

“H-Hey,” Sirius answered. “How… are you?”

Regulus tensed up, like just speaking to them was causing physical pain.

“Fine. Do you have a few minutes?”

A beat passed, and Sirius glanced around dubiously.

“You mean... Me?”

“Yes, you. Idiot.”

Remus had to bite his lip to hide his amusement, but Sirius remained stunned. It took him a few moments to get moving, but once he’d recovered he stood up from the table.

“Er—yeah. Yeah, totally.” He cleared his throat. “Lead the way.”

Not needing to be told twice, Regulus turned and began striding off. Sirius rushed to follow, but turned back around one final time to flash the rest of his friends an excited thumbs-up.

Mary started; “Did he just…?”

“I think so…” Marlene finished.

Peter looked at Remus. "What happened to never wanting to see him again?"

"Dunno... but suppose miracles happen every day, Wormy."

“Nah, no way,” James chuckled. “Five pounds Regulus means to drown him in the lake.”

“Potter!” Lily smacked him in the arm, but they all laughed anyway and returned to their meals. As it turned out, Sirius did not return for the rest of supper, and eventually it was time to retire to the dorms. Remus almost wondered if Regulus had managed to drown him in the lake after all, but his worries were satiated just before curfew, when Sirius stepped through the door looking weary, but content.

“You're back!” James cried, shooting upright on his bed. "Well, how'd it go?"

“Alright, I think. We went for a walk."

Peter raised a brow. “Did he try to drown you in the lake?"

“No, we just walked,” Sirius said, dropping his boots by the door with a thud. He paused for a moment, before dissolving into a fit of overtired sniggering. “Shit, all we did was argue! About the house, our parents, school—all of it.”

“But it was still good, yeah?” Remus asked gently.

Sirius nodded. “I think we might understand each other a bit better now. Neither of us is gonna win ‘best brother of year award’, but… It was something at least.”

"Well, he didn't murder you, I call that a win." Peter flopped back into his pillows, comic book hanging low over his nose. Then he perked up; "Oh and James, you owe me five pounds."





* * *





Tuesday 28th February 1978 – One week later…





Sirius and Regulus had a lot more meetings after that. Some days Sirius would return elated and high off life, others grumbling and irritated, but he always went. It meant they were trying, which was all anyone could hope for really.

“He’s pretty smart, that Regulus,” Sirius would sometimes say; “I mean I always knew he was smart, but he’s like—actually clever. Proper funny too, when he’s not in one of his little moods.”

“You are related,” Remus would say back. Early on he'd gotten the feeling that it was the first time Sirius had been happy about anything regarding his family. They weren't kidding themselves—the two still fought like scrapping rhinos—but if Regulus had chosen to rebel against their parents by seeing his brother, then Sirius wasn't likely to complain.

“I think he’s got potential. Who knows, maybe he’ll make a good roadie someday.”

“I’d keep that comment to myself if I were you, Padfoot.”

“Heh. You’re probably right.”

Sirius wasn’t the only one happy about Regulus’ return either. That morning, while Remus was on his way to the elementary campus to teach his bi-weekly music class, Trish skived off her chemistry class to join him. Now normally Remus did his best to stay out of other people’s romantic business (whether that worked or not was generally not up to him) but Trish’s interest had become so obvious that it hurt. She walked alongside him, chattering happily away about Regulus’ first week back and how he ‘already seemed so much better’.

“And it’s partly cheers to you too,” she beamed. “You’re the one wha' got through to him first.”

“We were just prefect partners.”

“But Reginald talked to you! And he never talked tae anyone save Crouch, not really.”

“He’s talking to Sirius now.”

“I heard. Sorta thought the two of them were a lost cause, what wi'h the way they were always going after each other. But well, I’m just glad he came back. Er—glad for him, I mean.”

Remus couldn’t help teasing her; “Sure, Trish. Whatever you say.”

They stopped outside the elementary building and Trish nailed him in the arm. “You watch your mouth or I’ll feed you your guitar or something."

Remus quickly pulled Sirius’ acoustic out of her reach, but Trish only sighed happily.

“You know, Remington, you should have a bit more confidence in yourself. You’re really very good.”

“Good at what?”

“At whatever you want to be.” Then, without another word, Trish spun around and drifted back up the lane, humming loudly to herself. Remus watched her go, before turning back to the door. He’d just gotten it open when someone rounded the far side of the building, carrying a violin case.

"Regulus?"

Regulus raised a brow, marching straight up to him. “Aren't you going inside?” He asked, completely blasé.

“Are you going inside?”

“We have a music lesson to teach, don’t we?”

Remus just about started. “I—I just assumed that you weren’t doing prefect stuff anymore.”

“Does that mean you're going to tell my parents?"

"No," Remus said, before a smile took over his entire face. "Wow! This is great. The kids totally missed you, you know.”

“I doubt that.”

“No, they did. Really!”

Puckering a bit, Regulus looked away shyly. “Fine, but can we go in already? I'd like to get this over with.”

Remus yanked the door open. "After you."

They made their way down the familiar hallway, passing row after row of colourful cubbies and racks filled with tiny boots. The closer they got to the classroom, the happier Remus began to feel. Maybe Trish was right after all.

“Wait!" Remus called when Regulus stopped outside the correct door. "Don't move!"

"What is it now?"

“Please, let me just do this one thing.”

With a vexed look, Regulus gestured for him to go on and Remus stuck his head inside the classroom. There he found twenty kids all pittering around, blowing their flutes and banging their drums. The sight had once made him sick to his stomach with nerves, but not anymore. Now he looked forward to those few precious hours a week he spent teaching music, and clearly Regulus did too.

“Hey everyone!” Remus called. “I've got a surprise for you!”

There was an instant chorus of 'WHAT?' and 'SURPRISE?!', but when Remus stepped aside to reveal their second teacher, looking rather embarrassed himself, the kids began to shriek in delight. They rushed the door, and Remus had to tug Regulus inside to avoid letting him bolt. He might've still tried, if one of the girls—Charlotte—hadn't caught him around the waist in a great hug.

“I thought you were never coming back!” She wailed. “You promised to teach me the violin!”

“I-I didn’t...”

“See?" Remus grinned. "Told you they missed you."

“Shut up, Lupin.”

"MR. BLACK SAID A BAD WORD!"

More shrieking, and Regulus had freed himself from Charlotte's clutches. "Yes!" He cried. "And I'll say more unless you all get back to your seats!"

“You heard him!” Remus ordered straight away; “Back to our seats so we can show Mr. Black what we’ve been practising.”

The kids needed no further encouragement. Charlotte rushed back to the tiny strings section, taking up her violin and practically vibrating out of excitement. They all knew what was happening—Remus had planned it in case Regulus ever returned. A big surprise.

“Everyone find your songs! Come on, you know the one."

There was a flurry of paper shuffling, and Regulus stepped up to his side, almost suspicious. “What have you planned now, Lupin?”

“Oh, it’s just a little something we’ve been working on. Now stand back and prepare to be amazed.” He ushered him off, and Regulus reluctantly obeyed while Remus took up his spot at the front of the class, hands extended to lead them. “Alright. On my count—and a one, and a two—!”

The clamour started instantly, several instruments just pounding right over one another with little regard for real rhythm or beat. The notes were nearly correct, but everything else was terrible. The violins squeaked enough to make one cringe, and the trumpets sounded like balloons losing their air. Already appalled, Regulus watched from the front of the room and when the piece finally came to a staggering end (they really only knew about six bars), the kids all lowered their instruments and turned to him gladly.

"Well?" Remus asked. "What'd you think?"

“Was that… supposed to be ‘Für Elise’?”

“Oh, good you got it!"

Regulus gaped at them. “Holy shit.”

“YOU SAID A BAD WORD!" Came the entire class. "BAD WORD! BAD WORD!"

“Oi, enough of that!” Remus called, trying not to sound too amused. “Let the man think! We just rattled him to his core, didn’t we? You alright there, Mr. Black?”

“That was, uhm… it... Well, it was terrible really.”

For a second the room was deadly quiet. Remus had just begun to wonder how he was supposed to comfort twenty sobbing nine year-olds when, quite inexplicably, Regulus began to laugh.

"Terrible!" He crowed. "Oh my god, my ears! What have you been teaching them while I was gone, Lupin?”

The kids shrieked in delight, all giggling and pointing fingers at Remus while Regulus practically split himself at the seams.

“What? I taught them ‘Für Elise’!” Remus shot back, while every kid giggled horrendously. “I thought we sounded quite good! Didn’t you guys?”

“NOOOO!” The kids all bellowed.

“Looks like I have my work cut out for me,” Regulus said, wiping the tears from the corners of his eyes. “Starting with strings, you guys were just—yeesh. I mean really, Lupin.”

“They need a teacher! They need you.”

That seemed to do it. Regulus peered down thoughtfully, before opening his violin case. “You’ll take the brass section, then?”

Remus winked. “You got it.”

They weren't exactly the London Philharmonic Orchestra by the time the lesson was done, but Remus was sure he’d never seen Regulus smile so much. After he’d assured them that they'd both be returning next class, they sent the fifth years on to lunch and went about the room, collecting chairs and sheet music.

“This one wrote ‘Beethoven sucks’," Regulus said, picking the page up off the music stand; "Only they mispelt ‘Beethoven’. And ‘sucks’.”

Remus set down a stack of chairs with a grunt. “They’re kids, what can you expect?”

Regulus tucked the stack of music sheets under one arm and carried a chair over to add to Remus’ pile. “You did good with them these last couple months. They sound better, truly.”

“I must be hearing things. Did Regulus Black just give me a compliment?”

“Don’t get used to it.”

Remus shrugged, stopping to return Sirius’ guitar to its case. “I’m glad you’re back. It was shit to have to teach them on my own... and I’m even more glad that you and Sirius have made up.”

“We haven’t made up,” Regulus said quickly.

“Right, sorry. I’m glad you’re talking to one another.”

“Mostly we just talk about you, actually.”

“You do?”

“Don't get excited, it’s all Sirius. He really likes you. No idea why, of course."

Remus chuckled. “Regulus, can I ask, how long have you known about us?"

Regulus shifted uncomfortably. “Since last year...”

“But Sirius and I weren’t together last year.”

“Are you sure about that?"

"Uh..."

Regulus smirked very briefly. "Well, whatever. Like I said, I’m not gonna tell anyone. It’s your business, as long as you don’t go flaunting it in everyone’s faces.”

Unsure of how to feel, Remus slowly closed the case’s lid and let the clasps snap shut. He recalled his list and began counting the names off in his head. They'd probably have to tell Peter soon, only seemed fair. Fair... oh christ.

“Lupin? ... Lupin!"

“Yes!” Remus spun around, back snapping straight up. He’d expected more questions, maybe even some teasing, but Regulus had crawled in on himself too, it seemed. He was white-knuckling his violin case.

“How do you do it?” Regulus asked quietly.

"Do what?"

"Talk to people, make them see you... I mean, really see you.”

This made Remus soften. He stopped wringing out his fingers and relaxed, letting out a long breath. “Do you think people don’t see you, Regulus?”

“I don’t mean it literally. I mean… Well, I’m not what other people think I am.”

“I know that. And Sirius knows that. Others might too, if you took the time to actually see them back."

Clearly it wasn't the answer Regulus was looking for. He seemed to pout, but Remus kept pushing.

"People aren’t just going to be able to know you right away, Regulus," he told him. "You have to talk to them, try to understand them, and tell them things.”

“Like what?”

“Like anything. Like what you like, and don’t like. What you think about things and how they make you feel. Not what others expect you to say, but how you actually feel.”

“And what if I’m not sure how I feel?”

“Then you tell them that too.” Remus licked his lips. “I’ve spent way too much time worrying about what others think of me—I was doing it just now. But like you said, Sirius likes me, and I like him too. That’s what’s important.”

Regulus regarded him for a moment longer, before nodding his head. “He’s kinda stupid, you know. My brother... He really is a bit of an idiot.”

"Funny though, right?"

Regulus smiled faintly. "Sometimes."

Just then, the classroom door opened and James stuck his head in. “Oi, Moony, let’s get a move on! Remember, we said we'd all practice for that quiz in music tomorrow—oh hey, Reg!”

Regulus averted his gaze, mumbling; "Hey, Potter."

"Good music class?"

"Terrible, actually."

"Right..." James gave Remus an uneasy smile, and Remus nodded.

“Be right out, Prongs.”

"Kay!"

Before James could shut the door, a thought suddenly occurred to Remus.

“Oi, James!"

“Mm?”

“One more thing, Regulus doesn’t like to be called ‘Reg’.”

“Oh.” James paused to consider. “Well alright, my bad. See you later then, Regulus.”

Nearly speechless, Regulus sputtered a moment before finally managing a; “Y-You too, Potter.”

Smiling at him, James bobbed his head genially and slipped out. Remus paused, before picking up his guitar case and glancing back at Regulus, who was—if he wasn’t mistaken—blushing.

“See?” He grinned. “It’s that easy, mate.”
