Chapter 89: Eighteen


Chapter Summary

Haven't we all wanted to date Remus Lupin once or twice?



Chapter Notes

No CW's for this chapter, apart from some general cringe-worthy embarrassment. Edit: There are some intrusive thoughts toward the very end of the chapter that could be read as upsetting.

& btw, THAT scene with Sirius and James (you'll know it when you see it) is 100% inspired by THAT scene from Gilmore Girls, lmfao.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Hello, I love you, won't you tell me your name?

Hello, I love you, let me jump in your game,

Hello, I love you, won't you tell me your name?

Hello, I love you, let me jump in your game...

- “Hello, I Love You” The Doors, 1968



When it came to rock and roll, chaos was pretty much a given. An occupational hazard, the less creative writers might call it. A de facto dream-state one regrets come morning only to crave desperately at night, so say the more clever ones. And say they did! The people needed answers after all—what car does he drive, which obnoxious radio DJ can't he stand, what was he thinking when he wrote that one specific line in that one specific song?! ... It was miracle work, it was. A reputation pieced together until there was enough he said, she said to make it worth reading. Rock and roll was life written on the backs of cigarette foils and train tickets, petrol receipts and takeaway menus—anything one happened to have on them when he began talking about one specific line in that one specific song! ... And he never made things easy either; for a breed that made their living off of such rhetoric, rock stars sure seemed to hate microphones. Or maybe they just hated reporters.

We know what he's doing now, they'd say; We wanna know what he did before!

Easier said than done. The subject in question was locked up tighter than a nun's legs on Sunday, hadn't gone on record in years. Anything before 1980 was a mystery.

“I’ve got a source that says he was seeing some girl named Wendy back then,” one would say.

“Nah, the girl’s name was Cathy,” another would chime in.

"I heard it was Tannice. Tannice Wiggs."

"The one from Wimbledon?"

"No, Bermondsey. Wimbledon was the twin sisters."

“Bleeding Christ, someone call Rita bloody Skeeter already. We need the real scoop!”

Those poor sods, they’d never get it right. It was too messy and there were far too many different accounts. By that time daughters would be discovering their mothers’ old diaries in the attic and wondering why the name ‘Remus Lupin’ sounded so familiar. Eventually they’d connect the dots when an old song came on the radio, or Pops showed a throw-back special from the early 80s. He looked better then—shinier and brimming with hope and promise. Handsome even, in a ‘he snogged my mum’ sort of way.

“Mum, you really dated a rock star?” They’d ask.

“For a day,” she’d reply, if she felt like being honest.





* * *





Thursday 9th March 1978





The problem started with an innocent trip to the library. He was just one day shy of turning eighteen, but seemed to be doing a well enough job of dissuading his friends from any and all birthday celebrations. Sirius acquiesced only after Remus threatened to end all mid-morning snogging sessions for the foreseeable future, and James and Peter couldn't very well continue with only two-fourths a marauder. This left the girls, though luckily they were still jaded from their failed attempt the year before and didn't seem all that interested in forcing Remus into another party he did not want. In fact, since the fiasco on Valentine's, no one seemed to have 'Remus' on the brain at all, and so when he'd agreed to meet Amelia Hodgkins in front of the library that morning, the last thing he'd been expecting was a love confession.

"But I don't understand," Amelia whined, "Mary said you weren't dating anyone."

"I'm not, but... Look, Amelia, I'm really sorry."

The girl looked up at him with glassy eyes, her face flushed with embarrassment. If there was one thing he had to give the Hawkings girls credit for, they were certainly bold. It'd taken him months to pluck up the courage to say anything to Sirius—though that was a slightly more fearsome beast to tackle—and try as he might, Remus couldn't recall how he'd ended up in such a mess. He and Amelia had been paired off in history, and for the last three weeks the two of them had been meeting up during whatever free periods to work on the project. They'd presented it in class the day before and everything had gone off without a hitch. Afterwards Remus had assumed that would be the end of it. Stupid fool...

"There is someone else, isn't there?" Amelia whimpered, reading him the way a woman only could.

"No, really. I'm just not looking for a relationship right now. And besides, I think you'll find you'd be disappointed with me."

"Oh, Remus… You are so thick!"

She fled back in the direction of the dorms, leaving him to dawdle awkwardly by the front doors of the library. He knew he'd lingered a moment too long when none other than Severus Snape slipped out behind him.

"Lupin. I'd wondered how the school's biggest basket case was doing these days. Now I see you're breaking hearts as well as mirrors."

"Figures you'd be eavesdropping," Remus snarled. "Don't you have some seventh year chemistry class to torture?"

"Why would I bother with them when you're so intent on airing your dirty laundry right where anyone could see?"

"Piss off." Remus turned to march away, already intent to drown his sorrows in leftover gin and whatever Sirius had on the turntable, when Snape skipped to catch up with him.

"Come now, Loony. Where are you off to in such a hurry?"

"I'm going to see my friends. Sorry you can't say the same."

"Suppose you'll be filling them in on your little fling with Hodgkins then."

"None of your fucking business."

"Oh, what's wrong? Don't tell me you're embarrassed. You're not the one who ran off with tears streaming down their face. Really, I almost feel sorry for the girl."

"A new experience for you, I'm sure."

Snape chuckled, and it struck Remus how cheery it sounded. Too cheery to mean anything good, surely. "I wouldn't worry too much about Hodgkins if I were you," he said. "She'll get over it. As I hear it, the girl's been around the block more times than the local trolley."

"No one asked what you've heard, you slimy git!" Remus bellowed. "Now you'll stop following me if you know what's good for you!"

It was enough to give Snape pause. He flinched when Remus rounded on him, and Remus felt that familiar twinge of satisfaction. He'd just stepped away again when Snape yelled after him; the nail in the coffin.

"Careful, Loony! Spend any more time with those friends of yours and people are gonna start wondering if you're a ponce!"

He could've just given him another detention, slap his wrists with a pink slip and be done with it. But as it was, Remus had never been much inclined to settle things the 'prefectly' way. Before Snape even had time to cackle, Remus had turned round and grabbed him by the front of his school coat. He thrust him against the side of the library, pressing on his chest hard enough to force out a pathetic little wheeze.

"This is your last warning, Snivelly. You leave me and my friends alone, or you're gonna be coughing up teeth for a week. Capeesh?"

He didn't nod in understanding, that would be too much satisfaction for a single interaction, but the look on Snape's face told Remus he'd spooked him well enough. With another sharp shove to the chest, Remus tossed the miserable boy aside and threw himself back down the pavement. This time, Snape knew better than to call after him.

"I can't believe it," Sirius said when he'd arrived on time for their music lesson and told him. "You actually said the word 'capeesh'? Oh god, Moony, that's so lame!"

"Snape didn't seem to think so when he was pissing his pants outside the library."

"I would've paid to see it."

As enthralled as Sirius was with the whole story, Remus remained uneasy. Snape may have just been looking for the easiest way to get under his skin, but if he'd noticed anything going on between them, then...

"You don't think he actually knows, do you?"

"That we're shagging under the covers? No, I don't. I think if he did the entire world would know by now. Snape's just being a git, per usual."

"Do you ever think what would happen if it got out?"

Sirius shrugged. "Can't be disowned twice. Might make our plan for world domination a bit harder though. Maybe if we went to a school of nobodies it wouldn't matter as much."

Remus bit his lip, thinking of his list. "A lot more people know about us now. You aren't worried they'll say something on accident?"

"Are you?"

Instantly Remus felt bad. They were his friends. And Regulus, though a part of him still held out hope there as well.

"Sorry," Sirius answered first, nudging him softly with his elbow. "Stupid question. We just won't tell anyone else then. Keep it contained, so we know who to put a hit on if it ever gets out."

"What about Peter?"

At that, Sirius looked uneasy. "Pete's never been able to keep a secret. Remember our first year together when he let slip to Snape about my birthday? He lets slip about this and we'll have a lot more than detention to worry about... 'Sides, doubt he'd appreciate knowing that he lives with a couple 'a poofters anyway."

He wasn't sure it was fair to Peter, but who was he to tell Sirius off for not coming out? He had been acting a bit odd ever since Valentine's, but no... Remus forced the idea away. Best not press their luck, not with Snape breathing down their necks anyway.

"Maybe we should plan a prank," Sirius said.

"What's this I hear about a prank?" James called, arriving just in time to take up the empty chair on Sirius' other side. Peter followed, a single drumstick already in hand. He sat on the stands next to Remus and pulled his bag strap over his shoulder with a giddy smile.

"Hey, Lupin! Look what I finally figured out how to do this morning!" He proceeded to demonstrate an impressive little manoeuvre, twirling the drumstick around multiple fingers like the blades of a propeller. It was a pretty nifty trick for a guy who couldn't tie his own shoes until he was thirteen, and Remus nodded appreciatively.

"Neat trick, Pete. Where's your other stick?"

Peter caught the drumstick out of the air. "Dr. Becker confiscated it. I was practising in maths."

"Ah."

"I'll just get another one from Buchanan. Oh, also I can do this now!"

"If you're quite finished," Sirius interjected, silencing Peter just as he was about to twirl the drumstick in his opposite hand; "I was trying to say, Moony doesn't want a birthday party, but we can't just do nothing. We should celebrate another way—a better way—with a prank."

"Who's getting pranked?" James asked.

"Snivellus. Stupid git deserves it, he tried coming after Moons this morning."

"It was nothing," Remus surmised. "Just a sorry loser talking out his arse."

"Can't have that," James mused, "imagine the stink."

There was no culling it after that. All through the lesson, every time Sheila had her back turned, one of them was whispering some inane idea to get back at the sworn enemy.

“Think he has a diary? Bet he has a diary… We could steal it and make copies to post all over school. Just like Reg did with your poem!”

“I’m not laughing, Sirius.”

“Maybe we should get Lily to ask him on a date,” Peter suggested. James looked at him, utterly appalled, and he blanched. “Not for real, obviously! As a joke.”

“Evans’ll never do it,” Sirius sniggered. "I think a part of her still holds out hope that Snivelly will magically turn out to be a good person."

“Or maybe Lily’s just a good person,” Remus added.

“S’a good idea though… Hm…”

“Boys, since you’re all so intent on gabbing through the lesson, how about we start this week’s listening quiz with you.”

“Aw. C’mon, Sheila…”

After they’d finished and the bell had rung, Sheila pulled him aside. Worried he’d somehow bollixed up his test, Remus followed her into the office only to be presented with a guitar case sitting atop her desk. He recognised it without question; it was the shiny Martin acoustic she’d let him play before Christmas.

“A little birdy told me it was your birthday tomorrow,” Sheila smiled. “Thought you should have something nice to celebrate.”

Remus’ mouth fell open.

“This?”

“I changed the strings yesterday,” Sheila said quickly, popping the case’s lid to reveal the pristine guitar lying within. “Personally, I love the timbre that comes with old strings, but she needed a good clean and I worried about what they would eventually do to the fretboard. I did keep them though, just in case you liked the sound.”

Remus was speechless, as he often was in the face of Sheila’s kindness. He’d felt terrible when Tomny bought the Teisco for him, but this—this was a work of art.

“I can’t take this,” he babbled. “I-It’s not even my birthday yet.”

“I know, but we don’t have class together tomorrow, and I wanted to make sure I got it to you before I left for the weekend. Call it an advance.”

“Oh.”

She smiled, guilty. “Not what you were expecting?”

He hadn’t been expecting anything at all, but saying that would’ve sounded ungrateful, surely.

“Are you sure you’re allowed to give away the school’s instruments?”

“Oh! You don’t have to worry about that, this one doesn’t belong to the school. It was mine actually, when I was your age. My parents gifted it to me for my eighteenth birthday as well. Now giving you a hand-me-down almost feels like a slight faux pas, but no one’s played it in so long. It saddened me to see her just collecting dust.”

A faux pas?! Remus looked down at the guitar again. It was beautiful, probably worth a pretty penny. And she was giving it to him?

“Mrs. Buchanan… I really can’t take this.” Couldn’t even touch it.

“Nonsense.” She bent down and pulled the instrument from its case, practically pressing it into his hands herself. Remus’ thumb brushed the strings and a rich sound rang out, perfectly tuned.

“It would make me happy to know you have it,” Sheila said. “A musician should have all the resources available to them, right?”

Remus’ hold tightened around the neck as he bit his lip. He couldn’t bring himself to admit it, but he wanted the guitar—badly.

“Do you do this for all of your students?”

The question seemed to catch her off guard. She blinked at him, chuckling once. “You’re not just my student, you’re my…”

“Your dead friend’s kid,” he finished for her.

She frowned, then smiled sadly, which was somehow even worse. “You don’t have to take it, but it’s yours if you want it.”

There was a bad feeling. Where’s the catch? There’s always a catch!

Remus looked down at the guitar. He imagined it were being held by David Gilmour of Pink Floyd and not some scrawny kid from south London and that made things a bit easier.

“Thank you, Mrs. Buchanan.”

“You’re welcome, Remus.”





* * *



“Happy birthday to you! Happy birthday to you! Happy birthday to Remus, happy birthday to youuuuu!”

He blew out the candles, all two dozen of them, and Hope and Giles and the entire household staff clapped their hands together in celebration.

“I can’t believe it, my little baby’s already seven years-old!” Hope squealed, pulling him into an iron-clad hug. Behind them, Giles chuckled as he gripped the back of Remus’ chair proudly. His hair was more red than white back then, but he still had the telltale lines on his forehead carved by eyebrows that raised up with every sardonic smile.

“Yes, sir. He’ll be a man soon enough.”

“No, I simply won’t allow it!”

“Muuuuum, gerroff!”

Hope gave a great sigh and pulled back, pushing the hair out of her son’s face. “You’re growing up too fast. It’s like I blink and you’re suddenly an entire year older. I can still remember when you were small enough to fit in the palms of my hands.”

“I was never that small,” he protested, looking past her and eyeing the tiered cake greedily. Their head chef, Rosel, had made it specially for him, though she’d only let him put one finger in the icing bowl the night before.

“Of course you were,” Hope cried; “ask Giles.”

“Your mother’s right. When you came home from the hospital you were no bigger than the teddy bear waiting for you.”

Remus raised his arm, showing off the stuffed toy with floppy ears. “Seabiscuit’s a dog.”

Giles ruffled his hair. “Dog, then.”

“Would you like to try your cake, darling?” Hope asked, while Rosel began plating up the dessert on expensive china plates. They set a slice down in front of him and Remus picked up his fork, getting ready to stab into it—then the other side of the table caught his eye. The chair was empty, without a place setting.

“Remus? Don’t you want to try your cake?”

“When’s daddy coming home?”

Hope blinked her pretty blue eyes. “I’m not sure, darling,” then; “Tomorrow.”

“You said that yesterday.”

“Your father had to head up to Manchester this week, son,” Giles said. “He’ll be back soon.”

Remus wasn’t satisfied. He was seven and nature demanded stubbornness. He wanted his father.

“I want him here now.”

“Mummy’s here,” Hope smiled, spreading her red lips. “Didn’t we agree that Mummy was enough?”

“I want Daddy. It’s my birthday.”

There was a passing beat, and Hope drew herself up with a deep breath. “Remus John Lupin, you’re going to hurt your friends’ feelings. They all gathered to celebrate your birthday.”

He looked around. The maid behind him had slapped his fingers that morning for mixing potions in the bathroom with all the nice smelling soaps. And that butler was new. He’d never said a word to Remus before.

“I want Daddy,” Remus said again. “Can I call him on the telephone?”

Hope balled up the napkin in her lap. “If you’re not going to eat the cake Rosel stayed up all night to make you, then you’ll have to go to your room. Ungrateful boys don’t get birthday parties.”

“I don’t want a birthday party. I want daddy.”

“Fine then.” She began pulling the plate away, and Remus grabbed her arm.

“No! I’ll eat it…”

“Apologise to Rosel first.”

“Sorry, Rosel.”

Hope let go and Remus pulled the plate back toward himself, quickly stuffing a bite of cake into his mouth. It was delicious, so sweet it stung his tongue.

His mother smiled again, leaning in close. She kissed his cheek and it hurt. She’d burned him with her kiss, and when she drew away again she’d changed. Her blue eyes had gone dark, her teeth had grown long and sharp. Red lipstick dripped from her chin.

“Shall we open your gifts afterwards, darling?”

“No!” He wailed. “No, stop! I want Daddy!”

“Darling, we agreed.” She raised a clawed hand. Behind her the maid was a devil with a snake’s tongue and the butler was engulfed in flames. He smiled as he set Giles alight, and no one seemed to notice the old man’s screams.

“I want Daddy!”

“MUMMY IS ENOUGH!”

Remus awoke with a start. There were no forked tongues or flame-clad men, just a dorm room with three snoring friends. It was his birthday today, he was eighteen, and yet all he could think was how long it’d been since he’d seen that stuffed dog.





* * *





Friday 10th March 1978





His friends may have relented to no parties, but that did not mean they weren’t going to let the entire world know that it was Remus’ birthday. That morning when they arrived for breakfast, Remus had to endure a full rendition of ‘Happy Birthday’ courtesy of half of Hawkings’ student body. Even Barty joined in, though it was undoubtedly just so he could replace ‘Remus’ with ‘Loony’. Remus was still embarrassed, and spent the remainder of breakfast pelting Sirius with bits of cereal, and when he really deserved it—entire slices of toast.

“Count your lucky stars, Moons!” James cheered. “You and Snivellus got out of an entire day of pranking.”

“Only ‘cause you guys couldn’t come up with anything decent in time.”

“Oh yeah? That’s what you think…”

Remus nearly asked, but just then Sirius started up another round of ‘Happy Birthday’, this time in Italian. Or at least, he thought it was Italian. He found out later that it was really Pig Latin.

“This isn’t even going to be the most embarrassing part of your day!” Sirius cackled, using his school bag as a shield while he made a beeline for the door. “See you in class, Moony!”

“Or before, you never know!” James added, following him out.

He let them go, telling himself he didn’t care enough to worry about it. There was only two of them, how clever could they be?

“Pete, are you ready for English?”

Peter nodded, staunchly. He’d said very little apart from singing “Happy Birthday”, and now appeared to be going slightly purple in the face.

“Pete?”

“He’s not talking to you,” Lottie explained from across the table. “Doesn’t want to ruin the surprise.”

“Christ.”

“It isn’t a party,” Mary insisted. “But you’re going to wish it was.”

“When I told everyone that I didn’t want a fuss, I meant it.”

“Mm, yes. Too bad we don’t believe you. In fact, I’m starting to wonder if it isn’t just a vain attempt to get even more attention.”

“I assure you, it’s not.”

She shrugged, looking coy. “Happy birthday, Remus.”

“Happy birthday, Remus!”

“Happy birthday, Lupin!”

“Lupin, it’s your birthday ain’t it?”

“Happy birthday, big man!”

They followed him everywhere. Kids he’d never even spoken to strode right up as if they’d been waiting in a queue. Every now and then he spotted what he thought could be a flash of dark hair and glasses, but every one of his well-wishers was adamant; no one had put them up to it at all.

On their way to English, Remus reamed into Peter.

“Do they think it’s funny? Does it look like I’m laughing?!”

Peter kept his lips clamped shut, and just as Remus considered reaching over and wrenching his mouth open himself, a foot appeared in his path and sent him sprawling. Barty and his cronies stood off to the side, laughing at him as he stumbled on the slick tile.

“Happy birthday, Loony!” Each of them chittered, making their escape before Remus could even consider retaliating.

It’s just one day, he told himself, just get through today.

“I heard it was your birthday today, Mr. Lupin,” Professor Flitwick said as he handed out that day’s assignment. “Good show!”

Remus languished. He’d never considered himself all that difficult to embarrass, but James and Sirius were turning it into a fool’s errand and it was only ten o’clock. If only he knew what was coming.

As Flitwick lectured, Remus kept his chin propped up on his arms, already zoning out on a crack in the chalkboard hovering just over the stubby professor’s head. Two seats ahead, Peter had spent the entire period with his head down into his lap. He seemed to be worrying about something, but Remus wasn’t close enough to enquire what it was without being overheard.

Halfway through class, Jodie, the girl who sat in front of him, turned around in her chair.

“Are you alright, Remus? You look as though you just watched a puppy get run over.”

Remus never got to answer. At the same moment the classroom’s door flew open—WHAM!—and none other than Sirius Black stood in its doorway. He looked distraught, distinctly un-Sirius-like as he slammed the door shut behind himself and tore into the classroom with frantic urgency.

“Excuse me! I’m sorry, Professor, but I’ll only need a moment.”

Professor Flitwick leaned over his podium, nearly toppling off the stepping stool he used to reach it. “Mr. Black, we are in the middle of a lesson—”

“Yeah, I know, Flitty. But this can’t wait!”

“M–Mr. Black!”

Sirius ignored the spluttering teacher, and instead began strutting straight between the rows of desks. Various kids wrenched their heads around to get a better look as he stopped before Remus’ desk and slammed his hands down on its surface, going as far as to topple Remus’ neat stack of books. Remus might’ve rebuffed him, were Sirius not already clearing his throat.

“Moony, my Moony, in vain I have struggled! These last few months have been a torture, and I can suppress my feelings no longer! I cannot tolerate these foul rumours being spread—I will not share you!”

Ahead of them, Jodie Gagnon’s mouth fell open. Peter looked mortified, but not entirely surprised, and Professor Flitwick had practically climbed across the top of his podium.

“S–Sirius Black, I cannot condone—”

“Doubt truth to be a liar,” Sirius wailed, “but never doubt, I love! You must, Moony! You must! I simply cannot take it if you won’t! And so I ask you now, how? How could you do this to me?!”

This is the part where I kill Sirius Black, Remus thought blithely. He was doing a stellar job of not breaking character, but whereas Sirius was going for tragic romance, the class was roaring like a comedy. Remus could see it now—Snape would be spreading his poncy agenda by midday, and then there’d be no use in hiding it.

“Sirius—”

“How could you do that to me?!”

“DO WHAT?!”

The class erupted back into laughter, and a shadow of a smirk fell across Sirius’ lips. He recovered quickly though, and launched back into his undoubtedly well-rehearsed monologue.

“After everything we’ve been through!” He moaned, smacking the desk again. “You tell me all those things—those sweet, sweet things, and then you just leave? Don’t even wait for me to wake up, you just sneak away like a coward out the back door?! Leave me out to dry like I’m some old sock that’s finally got too many holes in it—but you’re the one who wore the holes in me, Moony—you!”

“I’m going to wear a lot more into you if you don’t bugger off!”

“You cold, heartless fiend!”

“That is quite enough, Mr. Black!”

Professor Flitwick had finally come down from his podium. He strode toward Remus’ desk with purpose, flapping his stout arms about as though it might subdue the rollicking class.

“You’ll have to leave this instant, else it’ll be two weeks detention.”

“But Professor, would you give in so easily had you’d been so terribly wounded by the object of your deepest affections?”

“Sirius, go!”

Sirius spun round. “I will not! Give me detention, I don’t care. None of it’s worth anything if you don’t love me back! And I love you, you hear me, Moony? Dammit, just talk to me!”

“Mr. Black, OUT! Right now, before I have to call—”

“BLACK!”

It was James. He burst into the room with an even louder bang than Sirius had, and for a single foolish moment, Remus almost thought he was saved. Surely James, in all his emphatic pandering, would know exactly the sort of disaster this spelt. Surely he would solve all their—

“I told you already, Moony’s with me now! All the bleeding poetry in the world won’t save your fractured heart!”

A holler went up, mostly from the girls, and Sirius pointed a vicious finger at his best friend.

“You stay out of this, Potter! You’ve been jealous ever since you found out the truth, but I won’t sit back as you try to steal away the only thing that’s ever made me happy in this godforsaken world!”

“This is getting pathetic. Let it go, man! ”

“I will not let it go!” Sirius rounded on Remus again and bent down until they were nearly nose-to-nose over the desk. “Moony, I can’t keep going around pretending like nothing’s happening between us, I have to say something! People have got to know that what we have between us is real! As real as this blood as it courses through my flesh!”

He grabbed Remus by the wrist and pressed his hand over his own heart, a move that shocked Remus so badly he wrenched his entire arm back and fell from his chair.

“Mr. Lupin!” Flitwick shrieked.

“Moony!”

“Now you’ve gone and done it!” James stalked forward, giving Sirius a sharp shove to the shoulder. “Give it up, Black! You knew it was never gonna work. I already told you, damn it—he doesn’t want you, Remus is with me now!”

Remus whipped his head up. “Remus is what?!”

The laughter was rapturous, as loud and as delighted as the smile Sirius kept forcing from his face. James was no different.

“Hear that, Black? He doesn’t love you, he doesn’t even know you! You’re a joke!”

“You’ve always been jealous of what we had! Lupin’s the moon and I’m his stars—what are you? A bulky, ginger-worshipping arse!”

“Don’t get petty just ‘cause you know Lupin prefers my arse to yours.”

Another kid hooted from across the room; Ow-ow! but Sirius remained undeterred.

“Potter! Everything was fine until you came along and started objectifying my Moony with that wanton gaze of yours. You think I’ll hand over Lupin’s heart so easily?”

“Hard to give something you never had in the first place.”

“Oooh! Keep it up, I’ll kill you.”

“I’d like to see you try!”

Sirius squared up instantly and James practically toppled poor Jodie’s desk as he leapt forward to get at him. As the two idiots collided in the middle of the aisle, mostly a rumple of limbs, Remus got to his feet and could only watch. All around them kids were gasping and shouting in glee.

“Pin him, Potter!”

“Go for the eyes, Black!”

“Right hook—right hook!”

“You and I are best mates no longer!” Sirius grunted, rolling James into another desk with a loud clatter. “I hate your guts, Potter!”

“The feeling’s—” James shoved him back; “MUTUAL!”

Boys pumped their arms, girls gathered together to shriek and yelp. A right hook from James, a jab to the jaw from Sirius. Poor Professor Flitwick looked about ready to pass out.

And then Peter stood up from his chair.

“Y–You’re all wrong! R–Remus’ heart is m–mine!”

Remus covered his face with his hands.

“Enough! That is enough!” Professor Flitwick howled. “Stop this nonsense this instant or I’ll have you both in detention for the rest of the year!”

No one listened, and Sirius delivered another spectacular blow to his friend’s abdomen. James retaliated by practically picking him up from the floor and throwing him over some poor girl’s desk in the second row, pumping his arms in victory until suddenly—a prefect’s whistle cut through the air, and Jillian Stewart appeared in the doorway.

“I heard there was a fight going on! Professor McGonagall sent me to break it up!”

Professor Flitwick gestured desperately the boys, who were still rolling around on the ground with two stupid grins on their faces. Huffing, Jillian came forward and grabbed them both by the collars, hauling them to their feet and facing the class. “You great idiots,” she sighed. “Now what’s this all about?”

“I’m dating Remus Lupin!” Sirius shouted indignantly.

“No, I am!” James replied.

Jillian shook her head as though it were a lost cause. “Remus Lupin,” she announced, turning every head in the room back Remus’ way; “I told you to keep your personal problems in the bedroom.”

“Fuck off.”

“MR. LUPIN!”

Remus rolled his eyes at the scorned professor, but at least the laughs were his own this time. With a heavy shake of her head, Jillian turned a rather sorry-looking James and Sirius toward the door and marched them out.

“Really, it’s pathetic!” She said, loudly enough to be heard from out in the hall. “You two—best friends—so obsessed with one person that you’re fighting. I mean, come on, we all know who Remus is really going out with anyway.”

At the last second, Jillian’s face reappeared in the doorway and she blew a kiss and a wink in Remus’ direction.

“I’ll see you at dinner, darling. Kisses!”

“Stewart!” Sirius’ voice wailed. “Not you too!”

A few people began to clap, while Remus just pressed his fingers deep into his eye sockets. He helped Jodie right her desk, and in return she gathered a few of his scattered books for him, only to pass them over with a wary look.

“You sure are popular, Remus.”

Remus was about to spurn her—if this is popularity, please take it from me—when Flitwick appeared in the aisle between them, looking eerily calm despite the hairs that had come askew in his moustache.

“To be quite frank, I’m not entirely sure what just happened,” the Professor said; “but since you seem to be the common denominator, Mr. Lupin…”

Without another word, Flitwick placed a detention slip on the corner of his desk and returned to the front of the classroom. Remus couldn’t even object.

After class, he collected his things and spurned a very guilty-looking Peter before stalking out into the hall. Sniggers followed him the entire way; he figured he had about ten minutes of peace before word of James and Sirius’ passionate confessions made their way into common knowledge and the teasing became incessant, but of course he didn’t even get that. When he emerged Sirius was waiting for him, leaning back against a row of lockers with an unlit cigarette balanced between his lips. Fit bastard.

“Good lesson, Moons?”

With a huff, Remus walked straight up to him and snatched the cigarette from his mouth, tucking it behind his own ear. Then he smacked the detention slip against Sirius’ forehead.

“You got me detention, you git.”

Wincing, Sirius peeled the slip from his forehead and looked it over, completely chuffed. “Er… Happy birthday?”

Remus scoffed and kept on down the hall. Sirius followed, naturally, and got in front of him, so he was walking backwards. “Hey, don’t be mad. We had to do something for your birthday. It was either this or publicly ask out McGonagall on your behalf.”

“Why would it be between that and asking out the Headmistress?!”

“For the drama, duh.”

“You’re a cunt.”

“Aw, don’t tell me you’re mad? You’re all the school’s gonna be talking about for weeks!”

“ ‘Cause that’s been my goal from the very beginning.”

Sirius smirked wryly. “We were only trying to show you our love. And now Snape can’t say shit. We owned it. Now it’s our joke, not his.”

Remus laughed incredulously. “You wanted to keep Snape from calling us ponces so you do it for him?”

“Yes, that’s it exactly!” Sirius preened, closing the distance between them and pressing his fingertips against Remus’ chest. “Plain sight, Moony. If we hide out in the open, no one’ll suspect anything. And as a little added bonus… I finally get to tell the truth. I’m dating Remus Lupin.”

“Were you dropped on your head as a baby?”

“Probably. But at least I’m good-looking, right?”

Unimpressed, Remus made to go around him and Sirius grabbed him by the tie, pulling him back. “Moony, Moony, Moony… You’re not seeing the full picture here. Do you really think I’d just openly declare myself a poofter without a contingency plan? The day is young, and as far as anyone else is concerned, you’re Hawkings’ most eligible bachelor. Though, not for long I suspect.”

“Oh no—no more of this, I’ve had enough!”

“Don’t be such a wet blanket, love. You think everyone wants to sleep with you now, but if you can’t handle a few school-yard crushes, how are you doing to handle the masses when we’re rich and famous?”

“Sirius, what have you done?”

Instead of answering him, Sirius smirked and came forward, fixing Remus’ tie with long, meticulous fingers. “Figured I should make that incessant lovability of yours work for me for a change. But I should go… From what I’ve heard, you’ve got quite the busy schedule. See you later, birthday boy.”

He should’ve chased him down and beat the truth from him, or at least skived off the rest of the day. Either would’ve saved him from his friends’ carefully curated torture. In his second class, Professor Binns’ stirring lecture on Roman restoration was interrupted at least a dozen times when nearly every member of the Hawkings football team showed up with a rose with his name on it. They made no effort to introduce themselves, simply crashed into the room and threw the flower onto his desk, escaping with a great hoot. Some of the more bolder lads even opted to try for a cheeky snog, which had everyone in stitches. By the seventh rose, Mary and her other girlfriends were killing themselves in the last row, and Remus was picking petals from his hair.

After class he gave the flowers away to the girls, who were all much more keen on receiving them than he was. Apparently it earned him a few more points, as they started going around telling everyone that he was giving roses away to all of the prettiest girls, though this one got old rather quickly when others started realising that they had not received a rose themselves.

He would’ve assumed the Marauders’ reach had ended with the football team, but he was proved wrong when the tenth year girls’ choir met him outside of class and promptly launched into every annoying love song in their arsenal.

“I didn't know just what to do, so I whispered ‘I love you’! And he said that he loved me too—and then he kissed meeeeee!”

Torture, actually. The girls followed him all the way to the library like a travelling band, by which time they’d mowed their way through most of Dusty Springfield’s discrography as well as several agonising canticles. Thankfully Ms. Pince took one look at them and promptly chased the girls off for disturbing the peace. If he’d had a shred of patience left, Remus might’ve been impressed; whatever James and Sirius had told them, it’d certainly taken some serious coordination.

The library was supposed to be a safe haven. Remus secluded himself amongst the stacks as he so often did, but he should’ve known better. Sirius knew all of his hiding spots, and within the hour he’d suffered through no less than seven very public marriage proposals, three declarations that he was in fact a cheating bastard, and four offers to sneak away for a rather cheeky pint at the Three Broomsticks. Even Audriana made an appearance. She was flanked by two of her closest girlfriends, but at least she’d brought a present.

“I hope you like chocolate.”

“No eating in the LIBRARY!” Ms. Pince screeched, before promptly ejecting all of them from the building.

By lunch, Remus was sure he’d lost ten years off his life. He took a seat at the table furthest from the dining hall’s doors, but he was spotted anyway. First by Peter, then Lily and Lottie, all of whom didn’t seem all that interested in the pranks. Well, almost. The girls couldn’t help smirking at him and Peter was still clearly embarrassed in his delayed contribution to James and Sirius’ row.

“Sirius told me to say it!” He insisted. “I thought it was rubbish.”

“I heard it was hilarious,” Lottie assured. “Remus, when you and your many, many, many lovers marry, can I be a bridesmaid?”

“Ooh! Ooh! Can I walk you down the aisle?” Lily giggled.

Remus dropped his head down on the table with a groan.

“Poor Remus,” Lottie cooed. “Would a kiss make you feel better?”

“Oi, lips to yourself, Lot,” Sirius said, arriving at the table with James in tow. “That’s my man you’re trying to snog.”

“I’ll fight you for him.”

“Alright, but I warn you, I play dirty.”

“Oh trust me, I know.”

James and Sirius shared a matching grin. They sat down and Remus had to resist the urge to stab them both with his fork.

“Now that doesn’t look like the face of the man who’s just gotten engaged twelve times,” James said, as he slid in between Lily and Peter at the table.

“Piss off,” Remus grunted, before his curiosity got the better of him; “How’d you do it? How’d you get so many people to go along with this idiotic plan of yours?”

“Pure animal magnetism,” Sirius declared, grabbing him by shoulders and rolling his tongue in his ear. Immediately, Remus seized up and shoved him away, grumbling.

“You’re not funny.”

Sirius stuck his tongue out.

“You should tone it down, Sirius,” Peter said. “People are gonna get the wrong idea.”

“What wrong idea?” Sirius sneered; “Really, I should be so humbled to think that anyone would actually believe Moony and I are dating. You hear that world? I’M DATING REMUS LUPIN!”

A cheer of camaraderie went up from several other tables. A wolf whistle, and several more declarations of love came rolling in.

“ME TOO!”

“HE’S MINE!”

“GET YOUR OWN!”

Sirius spun around, practically vibrating in his seat. “I’m dating Remus Lupin,” he chittered. And for all the embarrassment and torture he’d been put through, Remus couldn’t find it in him to be angry.

“I hate you,” he mumbled, leaning his chin into his hand to hide his smile. Perfectly pleased, Sirius simply blew him a kiss.

There was a clatter as Mary and Marlene arrived at the table with their lunch trays, completing their group.

“Why are we sitting all the way back here?” Mary frowned, before flipping her hair over her shoulder. “Whatever. Helloooo, Remus, dear.”

She slid into the table next to him, sidling up close enough that both their thighs and shoulders were touching. It might’ve been alright, had she not budged in front of Marlene to snag it. Marlene frowned as Mary shoved her lunch tray aside and replaced it with her own, and Remus looked between them, entirely bewildered. Surely they couldn’t be back to fighting already?

“Mary, you took my seat.”

“Go sit by Lily,” Mary replied dismissively, batting her eyelashes at Remus while he stuffed several bites of sandwich into his mouth.

Marlene crossed her arms. “But I always sit by Remus.”

“You don’t always sit by Remus. What an absurd thing to say.”

“What’s absurd is your sudden fascination with him. You never cared about getting Remus’ attention before. What’s changed? Run out of boys with an IQ below eighty?”

“Don’t be jealous, Marls,” Mary replied. “It gives you wrinkles.”

“And what does being a slag get you? Venereal diseases?”

Remus choked on his food. He might’ve thought it was more serious, had Mary not burst into laughter and stood up from the table.

“There!” She said, thrusting a finger toward Marlene’s brow. “I can see one forming right now. The Mariana Trench of foreheads!”

Marlene swatted her hand away. “Get out of my seat.”

“Make me.”

Sirius whistled. “Cat fight!”

It was like lighting a beacon fire. Kids were craning their heads immediately, ready for round two, and Mary was about to deliver.

“You're calling me a slag, Marls, but all I see is a frigid little church girl. Why don’t you go back to saving yourself for Jesus. Remus is a man, he deserves a woman.”

“And what you deserve is a good kick up the arse!”

Mary turned and shook her skirt at her. “Only if you kiss it first.”

Marlene raised her hands, clamping them over Mary’s head and shaking her vigorously. Mary screeched—“Not the hair!”—and the girls fell backwards, bowling straight into Remus and Sirius and shoving them down to the edge of the bench.

“Jesus Christ!” Remus grunted, crushed beneath Mary’s back. “Can’t you all just give it a rest already?!”

“All’s fair in love and war. Maybe you should just pick one of ‘em,” Sirius sniggered, before taking an elbow to the temple.

“Neither!” Remus wailed. “I pick neither, now get off!”

Mary and Marlene both gasped, shooting upright on the dinner bench.

“Remus, what are you saying?”

“I—”

“Are you breaking up with us?”

“We never dated!”

“Liar!” Mary moaned. “You told me I was your one and only! Right after I let you eat me out on the common room fl—”

Nearly screaming, Remus clamped a hand over Mary’s mouth himself. “Cut it out!” He wailed. “We. Are. In. PUBLIC!”

“I don’t care!” She declared, ripping his hand free. “I’m not afraid of my love. Even if you are a selfish lover. I can change you!”

“Eat yourself, Mary!” Remus hissed, at his utter wit’s end. He might’ve launched himself up from the table altogether had Sirius not pressed in on him from behind, pinning him in place.

“What’s ‘a matter, Moony? Wouldn’t that story only be embarrassing if it were true?”

Across from them, James slammed his fist on the tabletop. “Moony, you two-timer!”

“Technically he’s at least a four-timer,” Lottie pointed out, popping a grape into her mouth as though it were popcorn at the cinema.

Mary burst into tears.

“REEEMUS! YOU CHEATING BASTARD!”

There were whistles from at least two tables down, as well as jeering, shouting, and several rounds of “Lupin, you dog!” Mary continued to cry, putting on a spectacular show of it while Marlene stomped her foot like a scorned child.

“Mary, stop crying! You’re embarrassing my Remus!”

“Your Remus?” Sirius echoed.

“Yes! My Remus!”

“Oh look, there’s Moira,” Peter said, taking his tray and leaving the table.

“Peter, wait!” Remus begged, still locked between Mary and Sirius. If Sirius noticed his distress, he didn’t seem to care, instead he only thrust a nasty finger at Marlene.

“You had your shot, McKinnon, now back off! I’ll fight for my man if I have to!”

“Oh yeah? Square up then, pretty boy! You may be able to go toe-to-toe with Potter, but I think you’ll find me a much nastier row.”

Releasing hold of Remus, Sirius leapt up from the table and Marlene gave him several weak pops to the jaw with her closed fist, both of them grinning. Taking his opportunity, Remus went to flee, only to have Lily reach across the table and snatch his sleeve.

“Remus, are we still on for that date tomorrow?”

“Date?!” James demanded.

“You’re not invited.”

James sputtered indignantly.

“Hope everyone’s hungry,” Lottie observed calmly, “ ‘cause here comes cake.”

Horror-stricken, Remus looked up to see a group of girls carrying a large sheet-cake across the dining hall, candles already lit. Across the middle, he could just make out the words ‘We ♡ Remus’ written in red icing. The stuff of nightmares.

Wrenching his arm back, Remus grabbed his bag and fled. He would’ve hopped the window if he could, but instead he ran around the outside of the dining hall to avoid the leering crowds, earning himself a spectacular round of whooping applause. Screw the rest of his lessons, there was only so much embarrassment one fool could take.

Fully prepared to return to his dorm room and never reemerge, Remus passed the first outdoor courtyard, busy with coming and going students, and instead made his way toward one of the dining hall’s grassy quadrangles. He was surprised to find it empty save for a single person—even more surprised to find that that person was Regulus Black.

Ever since his return, Barty and the others had been surrounding their friend like a pack of antsy guard dogs, almost never letting Regulus out of their sight. Seeing him alone almost made Remus wonder if maybe something was wrong, but when he approached and asked if he could sit, Regulus squinted at him in distaste.

“No.”

“Would you let me sit if I said it was my birthday?”

Regulus glared at him.

“… If you’re quiet.”

Happily, Remus took up the spot opposite to him at the bench, and they sat in silence for a long while. Regulus didn’t so much as look at him; he had a book open in his lap and his lunch remained untouched on its tray. It made Remus’ stomach rumble a bit—he’d barely had time to touch his own—but there was no way he was going back inside. He’d starve first.

“You’re all by yourself today,” Remus said eventually.

“Keenly observed,” Regulus replied, not bothering to raise his head.

“Did you fight with your friends or something?”

“No, I just wanted a bit of peace. Got a bit rowdy inside.”

“Oh… heh… Heard some of that, did you?”

“Depends. Do you mean the part where my brother openly declared his love for you, or the bit where you and that Macdonald girl shagged in public?”

“So you heard all of it,” he snorted. “That’s funny. I didn’t think you knew what the word ‘shagged’ meant.”

“You don’t know a lot of things about me.”

A smile tugged at the corner of Remus’ mouth. “Touché.”

“Don’t think you can hang around and cause trouble. I’m not interested in watching your stupid friends lose their minds over you, and I’m not about to fight valiantly for your heart either so if that’s what you were expecting you can forget it.”

“You mean Regulus Black isn’t in love with me? How will I ever go on.”

Rolling his eyes, Regulus turned back to his book, and Remus mourned the fact that he hadn’t deigned to bring one for himself.

“Nice courtyard…” He murmured. “Not too chilly out today either… Hm… Good place to read, really.”

“Do you know what ‘quiet’ means, Lupin?”

“Yes, but you’re the only one I can count on to always be in a worse mood than I am. Makes me feel a bit better about myself.”

Another eye roll.

“What is it you’re reading?” Remus asked.

“ ‘The History of Jazz’.”

“Oh… Good read?”

“A bit dry actually.”

“So you wouldn’t recommend it?”

“Not to you.”

“Hey, I like jazz,” Remus insisted. “Rock was built on jazz.”

“Something tells me the members of Black Sabbath aren’t that familiar with scalar improvisation.”

Remus thought he must be hearing things.

“… You listen to Black Sabbath?”

“I wouldn’t go that far.”

“You do!” He exclaimed. “My god, what’s your favourite song?”

“I don’t have one.”

“Mine’s ‘N.I.B.’.”

“Mediocre, at best.”

“You did not just call their best song mediocre.”

“Everyone likes ‘N.I.B.’, it was their debut. They didn’t care if it was perfect, they just wanted to shock their hippy neighbours. ‘Paranoid’ blows the whole thing out of the water.”

Remus was flabbergasted. “How do you know all of this?”

At the question, Regulus grew flustered. “Sirius… may have misplaced a tape or two over the years.”

“You little thief.”

“I’ll deny it if you say anything. I’ll take your thumbs too.”

“Alright, alright, Mr. Dramatic,” Remus cooed. “It can stay our little secret if that’s what you want. But you should know that Sirius would go insane if he knew.”

“He’s already insane. Thought you would’ve figured it out by now, you’re the one dating him.”

Suddenly a bit shy, Remus glanced down at his lap and smiled to himself. Yeah. Yeah, I am.

“Does this mean we can teach the kids ‘War Pigs’ next?”

“Don’t push it.”

“We can censor the words!” Remus urged. “Call it ‘Party Pigs’, imagine them ripping into—oh hey, Trish.”

Regulus jumped, fumbling the heavy book. It landed with a thud next to the table and Trish stopped to pick it up, having arrived while they were having their little back and forth.

“Hello, you two,” she smiled. “Lupin, what’s this—date number seventeen today?”

Regulus’ eyes bulged. “It’s not a date! Just because Lupin’s insatiable doesn’t mean everyone wants to be the apple of his fucking eye.”

“Calm down, Reginald, I was only joking,” Trish sniggered. “But I was looking for you. Your parents called Professor McGonagall’s office. She sent me to fetch ye.”

“Got it. Thanks, MacDuff.”

She nodded and glanced between them expectantly when Regulus made no indication that he was going anywhere. “Did you… forget the way?”

“No, I just thought I’d make them wait a bit longer.”

Trish smiled and passed his book back over. “Well, guess I’ll be seeing ye then.”

“Uh-huh.”

Lingering a bit longer, Trish smiled and flashed Remus a quick wave before turning and skipping away with her hands clasped behind her back. Regulus watched her go, probably not even realising he was doing it.

“You’re staaariiiing,” Remus said, sing-song.

Regulus snapped to attention. “I am not!”

“Did something happen between you two?”

“No. There is absolutely nothing going on between me and MacDuff.”

“Oh? Can I call you Reginald too then?”

“Shut it. I already told you, if you can't be quiet, you can’t stay.”

Throwing up his hands, Remus sat back on his bench and swallowed a smile as Regulus bitterly opened his book once more. He was considering his chances of survival should he try teasing him again when his stomach rumbled loudly and he clasped a hand over it. Regulus glanced up sharply, and Remus gave him a sheepish look.

“Sorry, just my stomach. I’ll be quiet now, promise.”

And he was, apart from the incessant rumbling in his gut. On the third growl, Regulus scoffed and slid his untouched lunch across the table.

“Just eat it.”

“But it’s your lunch.”

“And your stomach’s like listening to a chainsaw. It’ll be a relief.”

Remus smiled. He picked up the sandwich and ate.

“Mhm… Tea’s gone cold.”

“Thin ice, Lupin. Thin. Ice.”

Later that day…





‘—FINISHED WITH MY WOMAN ‘CAUSE SHE COULDN’T HELP ME WITH MY MIND! PEOPLE THINK I’M INSANE BECAUSE I AM FROWNING ALL THE TIME!’

“Moony!”

‘ALL DAY LONG I THINK OF THINGS—'

"Moony!"

'—BUT NOTHING SEEMS TO SATISFY! THINK I’LL LOSE MY MIND IF I DON’T FIND SOMETHING TO PACIFY!’

“MOOOOOONY!”

Remus turned the hi-fi down. “I’m sorry, did you say something?”

“Yeah, I said—”

‘—OCCUPY MY BRAIN!’

“Sorry, what was that?”

“I was saying—”

‘—OH YEAH!’

“Oh, real mature!”

Sirius stomped over, punching the red ‘stop’ button on the stereo and snatching out the tape to dangle it in front of his face. Remus tsked, tucking himself further onto James’ bed with Sheila’s guitar in his lap.

“I’ve been looking for you, you know,” Sirius grumbled. “We had an entire interpretive dance planned for the middle of Classics but you skived off! We were gonna laugh at that little vein that bulges in Bilshin’s forehead whenever he gets slightly irked!”

“Funnily enough, I’m not sorry.”

Sirius smirked, and then finally noticed the guitar. “Holy shit, where’d you get that?”

Remus raised the guitar up from his lap meekly. “Birthday present.”

“From who? From… From your dad?”

“Yeah, as if. It’s from Sheila actually. She gave it to me yesterday.”

“No shit? Told you she liked you best. Between her and Tomny, you’re on your way to a whole collection.”

“She said it was hers from when she was our age. I tried telling her it was too much.”

“Maybe for someone else, but not for you.” Sirius looked up at him, and leaned in to kiss him over the guitar.

“Nice try,” Remus scoffed, turning his face away. “I’m still mad at you.”

“You sure?” Sirius captured his chin. “What if I do this?” He left a gentle peck on his jaw. “And this?” On his neck. “And this…?”

Sirius kept on going down, leaving longer and longer kisses in each new spot. Remus, as weak as he was, couldn’t help but enjoy it. He let it go on for a little while longer before turning and biting Sirius on the earlobe.

“Ow!” Sirius clapped a hand over his ear. “I’m all for a bit of roughness here and there but you should probably warn a guy first.”

“Stupid.” Remus kissed him on the cheek. “Now gimme my tape back.”

“In a second. I have something for you too. It's a surprise. Was gonna save it for later, but I reckon now’s as good a time as any.”

“If it's another interpretive dance, can you at least save it for when I’m drunk?”

Sirius laughed, and slipped over to his own bedside table to rifle around within it. Figuring that there was no way he could fit an entire ‘We ♡ Remus’ cake in his drawer, Remus set the Martin aside and began sorting through his own pocket. He’d just pulled out a cigarette and set it between his teeth when Sirius turned around, hands hidden behind his back.

“Close your eyes.”

Remus did so.

“Now choose a hand.”

A sigh. “Your… left.”

"Ooh, good guess."

There was a wet feeling—Sirius had licked his finger and shoved it in his ear.

“EUGH!” Remus bat his hand away, eyes flying open. “Have you not had enough?! I mean, really—!”

“Happy birthday, Moons!”

Remus’ breath lodged itself in his throat. Sirius was crouched low beside the bed, a single silver ring pinched between two fingers. He bit his lip over a smile, and urged Remus to take it.

“Well…? Don’t you like it?”

A laugh slipped out, and the cigarette dropped into his lap. “Sirius, if you wanted to ask me to marry you, you picked the wrong day. I’ve already had about nine different proposals, and I think the charm’s worn off a bit.”

“This isn’t an engagement ring!” Sirius yelped. “It’s a posey ring.”

“What the hell is a posey ring?”

“You’d know if you hadn’t spent all Christmas crying into Tomny’s couch.”

Remus scowled, and Sirius shook his head very quickly.

“It was Evans. She dragged us to this museum while you were gone, made us spend hours looking at old dead things, or things that used to belong to old dead things. Apparently lovers used to give each other these rings as a sort of promise, or something. They’d sometimes inscribe words or little messages on them too. I dunno, I guess I just saw it and thought… Well… Anyway, go on. Check it out.”

Sirius held the ring closer, and after tucking the cigarette back into his mouth, Remus slowly reached out to take it. It was thick in the band, not as round as a traditional wedding ring but rather more rough-hewn, like it’d been pulled directly from the fire and set on display. And right there on the inside he could make out the small engraving, clear as day; RJL.

Remus John Lupin.

“Moons, you’re not saying anything…”

“Oh!” Remus pulled the cigarette from his mouth again and cleared his throat “Sorry, I was just… Wow. It’s—uhm… It’s… beautiful.”

Sirius frowned. “You don’t like it.”

“No! No, I—I’m just shocked, is all. Ninth proposal, remember…”

“I told you, it’s not a proposal,” Sirius said. “I find those things reeking in heterosexual undertone. This is a promise.”

“A promise of what?”

“That we’ll always have each other. No matter what.”

“… No matter what.”

Sirius nodded. “But if you kiss Tomny again I’ll break your face.”

A warm feeling had suddenly burst across Remus’ chest. Quickly, he slid forward on James’ bed and took the ring from Sirius, slipping it over his fingertip. Tragically, the band never made it over his knuckle.

“Uh… Sirius, I’m sorry, but it doesn’t quite fit.”

Sirius’ face split into an audacious grin. “That’s ‘cause that one’s mine.”

“Huh?”

“You don’t think I’d give you a ring with your name on it, do you?”

Cheekily, Sirius pulled the band from his finger and slipped it onto the ring finger of his right hand. A perfect fit. Then he reached into his other pocket and withdrew a second ring, its twin in every way.

“Here, this one’s yours. We don’t have to wear them on our left hands or anything. It’d be enough if you just wore it at all.”

Remus bit his lip. He didn’t have to wonder what inscription he’d find on the inside of his ring. It could only be one thing; SOB.

Sirius Orion Black.

“You know your initials spell out ‘son of a bitch’, right?”

“No, tell me again.”

“Tsk… Son of a bitch.”

Sirius slipped the ring onto his finger and kissed his knuckles. “There. Now we match. I’m glad I got silver, the gold seemed a bit tacky.”

Remus looked down at them, and practically melted. He held his own hand up, pressing it to Sirius’ and letting their fingers slip together and intertwine. Somehow the metal of the bands were already warm. It felt so right; so Sirius. He wasn’t sure his heart had ever felt so full.

“Dunno what I did to deserve such expensive gifts,” Remus hummed.

“Who gives a shite about that, you’re priceless.”

Oh…

Sirius smirked. “I suppose this means you like the gift then?”

“Yes… Oh, yes.”

“Good. Now take off those trousers—your birthday ain’t over yet, rock star.”

What a drag it is getting old…

- “Mother’s Little Helper” The Rolling Stones, 1966



Tuesday 21st March 1978





Turns out, it was a good birthday. It was a good March, so far. It reminded Remus what they were looking forward to—what life together could be. Plans were being laid, universities applied to, songs written; it was all so good. He nearly forgot what it was to feel bad. Nearly. Apparently all of the professors had come together and decided that their workload that term had been far too light, and as a result, had piled on the assignments just as everyone was about to depart on holiday.

After an early supper, Remus and his friends congregated on the floor of the girls’ bedroom, determined to finish the rest of their assignments, overdue or otherwise. The only ones who weren’t drowning in homework were Sirius and Lily; Sirius because he didn’t plan on finishing any of it in the first place, and Lily because she already had. While Sirius poured over a battered copy of last week’s newspaper—paying special attention to the ‘properties for rent’ section—Lily had since moved on to one of her many university entrance essays, leaving them all in the dust. She’d may have been “conditional’ed” from Oxford, but that didn’t mean she wasn’t going to try for any other university that was worth its salt.

“Find anything in there yet?” Mary asked, sneaking over to Sirius and all but ignoring her unfinished essay. “You’ve been looking for ages.”

Sirius rolled over so his head was resting against Remus’ thigh. He straightened the paper and hummed lightly. “Dunno… There’s this place in Lambeth that seems to have promise, but it’s awfully close to the river, and I’m not sure how I’d feel waking up to the smell of rotting sushi every morning.”

“The smell isn’t that bad,” Remus reasoned.

“Yes, but with our luck we’d move in one day and have a second coming of the Great Stink the next.” Sirius shook his head, flapping his paper again. “I’m still looking.”

“If you’re so picky, then maybe you should just go see some of these places in person,” Lottie suggested. “At least that way you could scope out the area.”

Sirius glanced up at Remus. “You didn’t tell them?”

“Tell us what?” Echoed Peter.

“Sirius and I are staying at school for Easter,” Remus said, not looking up from his work.

James all but shot up from the floor. “You are?! Why?”

“Why not?” Sirius shot defensively. “Mary’s going to Paris, you’re both going to your girlfriends’ houses. You think Moony and I like going home? No, might as well stay and have some peace from you lot.”

“Ah, yes, peace from us,” Lily sneered.

“It doesn’t matter, he’s just gonna be catching up on the homework he’s refused to do before now,” Remus said.

“No, I’m not.”

“Yes, you are.”

Sirius made a displeased noise.

“I see, so it’ll just be the two of you?” Marlene pondered innocently.

Remus gave her a small smirk. “Leave it, Cherry.”

She appeared much less innocent after that.

“Right, I’ve had enough.” Sirius tossed the newspaper aside and sat up.

“You haven’t even done anything,” Lily blagged.

“I meant I’ve had enough of waiting on you people,” he huffed, before turning on James. “C’mon, you said we’d practise tonight. I want to show you that new riff.”

James frowned, looking down at all of his unfinished work. “Sorry, mate, don’t think I can swing it today. Got two days to finish this or Loughty’ll have my head.”

“Wormy?”

Peter sighed. “Can’t… got maths.”

“I’ll go with you, Pads,” Remus said, before Sirius could start pouting. They got up together and whilst they were slipping out the girls’ window, Mary whistled.

“Have fun, you two.”

“But not too much fun!” Marlene added.

“Bugger off,” Remus said, before noticing an odd look on Peter’s face; like he knew he was out on the joke but couldn’t quite figure out what it was. He nudged Lottie, and the two of them had one of their silent twin-telepathy moments. In the end all Lottie did was shake her head and feign indifference, but it was enough to make Remus regretful. He supposed that ‘two of his best mates buggering each other’ wasn’t high on Peter’s list of possibilities, but still, should probably say something.

Maybe after Easter…

Bidding Rowena House adieu, he and Sirius stopped by their own dorm to drop off and collect their things before heading on to the Bellchant building. It was dark, so Remus took Sirius’ hand in a brief bout of boldness. Sirius squeezed back, and he felt their twin rings click together. Sometimes, on the days he was feeling most daring, Remus wore the ring on his left.

They found her in the dining hall, calmly sipping her morning tea with a rather unimpressed expression on her face.

“Ohhh no,” Mary objected quickly; “Did you forget about our bet? Tomorrow you two are all mine. And I do hope you remembered to bring your dancing shoes to school, Black, because I’m going to waltz you for all you’re worth.”

Ba-dum-tss!

“Going to the library two days in a row won’t kill you, Padfoot.”

Remus huffed sharply, unimpressed. He was standing in the middle of the common room’s threshold, doing up his coat. Mary had already returned to her room earlier that morning, complaining about the state of her hair after falling asleep without her bonnet for the second night in a row, while his boyfriend remained obstinate, still lazily rolling around the floor-bound couch cushions in his pyjamas. They'd slept there last night, under a hastily-built blanket fort of Sirius' making.

“C'mon, Moony,” he whined. “Macdonald kept me up for hours with that stupid dance of hers, and I was good, so don't I deserve a little lie-in? Come back to bed, Moons... I’ll even let you be the little spoon.”

On his own then, Remus made his way across campus to the empty library. Inside, only a few tables were occupied, almost all of them by other year 13 students pouring over their texts. You could’ve heard a pin drop, but Remus had always had keen eyes. He spotted Regulus Black at one of the tables near the far back of the room, set up facing the rows of massive crystalline windows the library was famous for. The windows overlooked the southern half of Lake Dubh, and the stunning view nearly distracted him as he made his way toward the table.

“I hope you’re here to study,” Regulus said, without looking up from his textbook.

“Of course."

“Good. Because you if you can’t be quiet then you—”

“Can’t stay,” Remus finished. Really, those Black brothers were so predictable.

Regulus rolled his eyes but indicated to the chair opposite to him and Remus took it, silently thankful. Most of his homework for the week was mere busy work, which he didn’t mind so much, but when he went to pull out his copy of Brave New World to begin working on the paper he had due for Flitwick, it came with one of Mr. Pettigrew's newspapers. The paper must've ended up in his bag by mistake; already he could see evidence that Sirius had had his hands on it. There were several addresses for rent already circled in red pen as well as a few accidental cigarette burns and devil horns drawn onto the Queen's portrait in the upper right hand corner. The first address he'd circled was a tiny three-bedroom in Chiswick, but it boasted a ‘third floor private entrance’ which most likely meant a three-floor walk-up on some rickety fire escape. The next was advertised as a ‘spacious flat in West Brompton’, but the rent was suspiciously low. Either the nearest tube station was thirty kilometres away, or someone had died in it recently and the owners were looking for a quick lease. He'd circled more, though when Remus compared the addresses he found all of them to be rather suburban and quiet.

It was almost surprising. When he’d first pictured Sirius living in London, Remus had imagined a flat overlooking the bustling streets of Soho and Carnaby—somewhere the city never slept. All Sirius talked about was living the high life, making noise and not caring what anyone thought of them. Perhaps he was pulling back a bit then, considering how it might feel to try sleeping with the background noise of a city when all one was used to was the serene emptiness of the Scottish Highlands.
