Everyday, it's a-gettin' closer,

Goin' faster than a roller coaster;

Love like yours will surely come my way,

A-hey, a-hey, hey;

Love like yours will surely come my way...

- “Everyday” Buddy Holly, 1957





Remus had forgotten what it was like to have a mother. He'd witnessed bits of it, through Effie and Mrs. Pettigrew—even a few of the more overbearing ladies in the estate's kitchens—but Sheila was something else entirely. It wasn’t as though she was suddenly bursting into his room every Sunday morning, screeching for the laundry or pestering him about how a cup of coffee did not qualify as a meal in itself. (He had James for that.) Rather, she told him things. Gave him her opinion, offered advice, shared memories from when she was a girl. Memories of himself, and his family. Before it had irked him, knowing that a stranger might remember more of his own past than he did, but Sheila wasn't a stranger.

She was something else.

He wasn't sure he'd ever be able to forgive her for walking away during the penultimate years of his life, but maybe he didn't have to. Maybe it was enough just to let her in at all.

“I think you should be glad to be named Remus," she'd told him once. "You were almost Rodney.”

“And then on your first Halloween, Hope dressed you up like a little dalmatian," came another; "A bit on the nose, maybe, but the photos she sent of you with the dogs were so cute.”

“The first time you met your grandmother you spit up right in her face. Hope and I laughed for hours. She really was a nasty woman, that Alys Howell. You're lucky, Hope was nothing like her.”

Every memory, Remus drank in desperately. It was as though he’d lived his entire life on a desert island, and was only now just getting his first taste of water.

“Do you remember the first song you ever heard, Remus?” Sheila asked.

He shook his head.

“I do. I was there actually. But of course you wouldn't remember... it was the first time you and I had ever met, after all. Hope had just brought you home from the hospital. Such a tiny thing—Lyall barely had you through the doors by the time I came whipping up the road. But I was so excited. I'd made your mother promise that I could play you your first ever song."

"You?" Remus echoed. "You played me my first song?"

"Not myself," she laughed; "Doubt I could've gotten through a single verse on my own, no matter the instrument. I'd already mucked up the whole thing, you see. When I arrived at the house, I'd meant to play you a Bobby Darin record, only I was so nervous that I'd grabbed Bobby Day instead. Not that it mattered much, you loved it. I can remember the way your pudgy little face just lit up! I swore up and down that you'd be a music lover, and you proved me right straight away. Playing that record was the only thing that could get you to sleep. I'm almost sure that Lyall and Hope were cursing me to my back—they must've had 'Rockin' Robin' stuck in their heads for months."

It was amazing. Like a golden ticket—the perfect flick of ash off the end of a cigarette. As long as she had it in her to keep going, Remus would listen.

"Hope and I would sing to you for hours, you know,” Sheila said proudly that same evening, after he’d finished the day's lessons and snuck away to her office for the fourth time that week. It wasn't a secret where it was going, but Sirius and James knew better than to try and tag along. Remus needed this, even if hearing some of her stories made the knots in the pit of his stomach twist uncomfortably; he wanted to know.

"Your mother had decent enough taste when it came to music," Sheila went on; "Though, it was all thanks to me, of course."

"Yeah?"

She nodded, smiling. “But not everyone's perfect. Did you know that when we were growing up, all she would listen to was American pop music? Yes, she was convinced she was going to turn eighteen, move to California, and marry Guy Mitchell—kept a poster up in her room that she’d kiss goodnight and everything. Personally, I didn't get the appeal. He was so soppy.”

“I’ve never even heard of him,” Remus smiled, eager for more.

“He was a bit before your time, I think. Though I should have one of his albums around here somewhere...” Popping up from her desk chair, Sheila began digging through the many storage boxes that lined the office walls while Remus sat back with his tea, occasionally munching on the biscuits she’d set out for them.

“Ah! Found it!”

Practically tossing the record sleeve over her shoulder, she set the vinyl disc up on the turntable that took up most of the space in the office’s tiny corner. He listened earnestly at first, but there was no arguing that Sheila was right, it was soppy.





‘My heart cries for you,

Sighs for you, dies for you;

And my arms long for you,

Please come back to me…’





“She never told me it was this bad,” Remus said. “She always said she grew up on rock and skiffle. Like Chuck Berry and the Beatles.”

“Ha! As if... No, Hope was a good girl. Our parents would’ve had our guts for garters had they known we were listening to that stuff. Besides, by the time we’d left school John Lennon and Paul McCartney were still playing their banjos around Liverpool as the Quarrymen.” Pausing to sip her tea, Sheila promptly ripped Guy Mitchell up from the turntable mid-wallow and tossed the entire record lazily over one shoulder to join its sleeve on the floor.

“Now this,” she said, setting down the teacup; “was my American standard.”

Pulling out a simple little 45 LP, Sheila handed him the sleeve and set the record up to play. Remus turned the cover over in his hands.

“Little Richard?”

“Oh yes,” she grinned, “they don’t call him the ‘architect of rock and roll’ for nothing.”



‘Gonna tell Aunt Mary ‘bout Uncle John!

He claims he has the misery,

But he havin’ a lot of fun!

Oh, baby, yeah, baby!

Whoooo! Baby, havin’ me some fun tonight, yeah!’





As the song continued to play, Sheila strolled back to her chair and sat. “Little Richard inspired the Beatles, right. They even covered this song ten years later. Can you imagine—inspiring the Beatles? I don’t like giving those Yanks all the credit, but they did have some good‘uns.”

“Does that mean you don’t like Elvis?”

“Pfft. Elvis—overrated.” She winked at him, then pointed to the LP's sleeve. “You can keep that if you’d like, and the Guy Mitchell. That is, if you can find it...” Raising her hands hopelessly, she glanced around the cluttered office, which was still perfectly curated in its own chaos. Not that Remus minded. He polished off his tea while glancing over the LP's b-side, and when Little Richard's song ended Sheila flipped the record and went to fix him a second cup, humming the tune under her breath. Watching her, Remus began fidgeting.

“You've probably already heard about the band… o-or, our band...”

“Oh, you mean ‘The Marauders’? Yes, I think Mr. Black has filled me in once or twice.”

Damn you, Sirius.

"It's just 'Marauders' actually..." Remus cleared his throat. “We—uhm… We’re all gonna move back to London after school’s done. Live in a flat and see if we can actually do something with it—the band, that is..."

“Really?” Sheila’s eyes seemed to twinkle. “That’s wonderful, I hope I’ll get to see you in a show some day. Maybe at Wembley, hey?”

"Wembley? Are you joking?"

"Oh, c'mon, Remus. It's Wembley, not the moon."

This made Remus awfully embarrassed. Wembley Stadium might as well have been on the moon. Aiming to play there was like fetching a bingo card and expecting to win the lotto; a one in a million shot. Even with all four of their luck combined, it was statistically impossible. Still, it felt rather good to hear Sheila say it.

"We’re actually looking to record some of our own stuff," he boasted meekly. "Sirius writes a bit, and I—well, we'd like to put together a demo. Just don’t have the proper equipment for it yet.”

"Well, I’m sure I could dig something up around here if you’d like. Or there's the radio room! There must be something in there.”

Remus picked at his thumbnail, before letting out a long sigh. "Aren’t you going to tell me that it’s absolutely mental?”

“What do you mean?”

“I mean—us. Thinking that out of everyone who has this exact same dream—that we could make it.”

Humming thoughtfully, Sheila lifted a biscuit to her lips and took a bite. Then she crossed her arms, and shrugged very simply.

“Why not you?"

It stumped him for a moment, but then Remus remembered who he was. Why not him.

“Look at me," he said, "I’m not exactly John Lennon."

"Of course not. You're much more handsome."

"No! I mean, I can't do that. I can't inspire people... I'm only me. And you!? Shouldn't you be telling me that I should pick something more useful? A career that actually has a chance of making me a living wage?"

"Why would I ever tell you that?"

"I dunno, because you're the adult? The sensible one?"

She squinted at him and Remus felt his heart lurch. He quickly reigned the feeling in as she polished off the biscuit and dusted her hands, all the while looking him straight in the eye.

"Remus, I have lived my life being entirely too sensible, and you know what it's gotten me?"

"A roof over your head and a stable career?"

"Bored."

She winked again.

"Be a dreamer, Remus. I think you'll find that they have more fun."

It felt heavy, almost reminiscent of a conversation he and Lyall had had ages ago; but still different, enough so that he shied a bit, peering down at his shoes. Not that Sheila was ever much deterred by shyness. Still smiling, she reached across the table with the plate of fudge biscuits and offered him another as her show of support. Remus accepted with a simple nod, and though her confidence in him hadn't served as some awe-inspiring moment of clarity, it did strike him then just how much he was going to miss her.

Friday 5th May 1978





With April officially come and gone, the only thing left for the Marauders to worry about was their end-of-term exams. Or, that was how things should've been. Remus was still picking bits of flour off of his jumpers, but that was nothing compared to the silent war that had been raging in their bedroom for over a week. Peter was still reasonably angry with them, and any attempt to talk to him had so far ended in a cold shoulder or rapid-fire shouting match. It made James uncomfortable, though not uncomfortable enough to pick a side.

"You three have to sort this out between yourselves," he'd said, "I'm not your mother."

It seemed a bit ironic that he'd chosen now to rein in his motherly tendencies, but Remus kept the thought to himself for fear of losing yet another friend. Without a drummer, all Marauders' band practices had been drawn to an immediate halt, and anytime Sirius suggested the three of them go it alone, James would make the excuse of having to meet Lily and the girls for study. This made for long hours in the library and a generally sour-Sirius, not that he wasn't also in attendance. The self-proclaimed 'King of Self-Study', ran the risk of having Lily bludgeon him with one of her textbooks every time he tagged along, and had eventually resorted to bringing a pillow with him just to catch up on his sleep. This lasted for about two days.

“This is such shite," Sirius complained over a yawn. "It's a Friday, and we've been here for hours! You can't possibly fit any more knowledge into those fat heads."

"Why don't you go back to sleep, you arse?" Marlene offered, already sporting deep purple bags beneath her eyes. Sirius might've, had Ms. Pince not confiscated his pillow that same morning. He'd already resorted to using James’ collection of textbooks as a pillow instead, which was proving annoying for James, who was forced to trade him books every time he switched subjects.

“A-Levels are important. Even for someone like you,” Lily said, not even looking up from her notes. It was no question who the 'you' was for, but Sirius only yawned again.

“Why? It’s not like I have any plans to go to uni. Honestly, I could probably skive them off altogether. I’d still pass.”

Sirius rolled his head up, so he was just resting on his chin on the texts. “Ah, but you see, that in itself is still an ‘achievement’.”

“I didn’t want to bring these out while everyone’s around because they might not think it fair, but look what I found you!” She threw her arms out over her desk, where a machine about half the size of Sirius’ stereo was sitting, a single microphone connected to its side.

“It’s a tape machine!” She beamed. “For your band—so you can record yourselves!"

"Oh."

She must've read his expression as being unimpressed, as she rushed to clarify;

"Now, I know it's nothing fancy, but it's something, right? And I’ve found you a whole box of blank tapes as well. The machine belongs to the school, so I can’t just give it to you, but I don’t think it would be a problem if you took it back to your dorm until the end of the year. Provided you take care of it, that is?”

He didn’t have the heart to tell her that there might be very little ‘band’ comings and goings without their drummer, so instead he just nodded and smiled.

“Thank you. Mrs. Buchanan.”

Remus could tell Sirius was thrilled by the prospect of finally getting to record their own songs, but it was obvious that he was holding back his excitement to appease James. After class the other boy regarded the tape machine with little more than a glower, and finally he turned and grabbed both of them by the arm, dragging them from the room.

“Wha—?" Sirius baulked. "What about the tapes? A-And our instruments?”

“Just shut up and come with me,” James growled.

He marched them across campus to the Agrippan Block and straight up to the second floor, where he dropped them in the first empty classroom and ordered that they sit.

“None of us have class in this building,” Sirius rebuffed. “And it’ll be dinner soon.”

James turned on him fiercely. “Don’t. Move.”

Without another word, he swept from the classroom, leaving them both on their own.

“I don’t think he wants us to move, Padfoot,” Remus said, while Sirius sighed and took a seat at one of the desks in the front row.

“He’s meddling—which is worse than your meddling because it means that he’s also going to nag me.”

“I think you need a bit of nagging,” Remus said, sitting down across from him.

Smirking, Sirius hopped up and leaned down over Remus’ chair, effectively blocking all means of escape. “Was that an innuendo, Mr. Lupin?”

“No.”

"Oh. Well, could it be?"

"... Maybe."

Sirius smirked and leaned in until their faces were but a mere hair’s breadth away, but just then the door opened. They were caught in the act by Peter, who was standing awkwardly in the doorway, clearly just as surprised to see the two of them. He went to turn around, but just as quickly—James was there, backing him into the classroom without a stern look on his face.

“In,” he ordered. “And sit down.”

Without room to argue, Peter gave in and ultimately took a seat at one of the desks several rows over from the rest of them. Taking his time, James shut the door behind himself before calmly proceeding to the professor’s desk and lifting himself up until he was sitting on top. Sirius had already opened his mouth to offer complaint, but James simply raised a stern hand and silenced him instantly.

“I think we all know why I've brought you here. And just let it be known, how disappointed I am—in all of you."

Both Peter and Sirius began to speak at the same time; “No way, I—!” and; “But he—!”

“QUIET!”

The boys slumped back into their respective chairs, and James hopped down from the professor’s desk, body as taut as a string. “Especially you two!" He hollered. "You are best friends for Christ’s sake! How could you say such things to each other?”

Before any of them could respond, James threw out his arms again.

“No! In fact, ignore that! I’m the one who’s gonna talk now, and you’re gonna listen. Years of friendship aside, we agreed to do this together! We became Marauders together, and that’s not gonna change, not as far as I see it! If any of us wants out then that’s their decision, but we do NOT turn our backs on our friends. We do not intentionally hurt them—no matter how angry we are! I don’t believe anything any of you have said or done deserves the kind of hatred you spewed at one another, and I want it to end here. Today—right now. So go on, let’s have it out. Say what you want—resolve it—and leave it at the door. Because we’re friends first.”

There was a beat of silence, and then another. James looked to Sirius, who only glanced down at his fingernails, uninterested. Similarly, Peter crossed his arms and also refused to speak. Finally, James turned on Remus.

"Moony...?"

Remus couldn’t handle it anymore.

“I was the one who asked Sirius not to tell anyone about us,” he admitted. "I asked him to keep it a secret. From everyone. And he did it for me."

Sirius threw an arm out. "Moony, you don't have to explain—”

"I want to!" Remus said. “When things started between Sirius and I last summer, I wasn’t ready to come out. I didn't even have a word for it. I thought we had to be friends first, and that whatever it was I was feeling, wasn't real. But it was—it was real. And it scared me. I didn't want you to see us any different, for anything to change..."

At his words, Sirius turned his face into his shoulder. Still, Remus plunged on.

"We fought because I was scared, and because I was being selfish. I wanted everything at once, but I wasn't willing to risk what I already had... It was the same at Christmas. And I'm sorry that the rest of you had to deal with it, even though you didn't know what was going on. I didn't know what it was that I wanted then, but I do now, and now all I want is for us to leave school and still be together. Even if it isn’t as a band... or in London… It's like, I found out recently that I have a fucking godmother, but even if I hadn’t I would still be okay, because I have you guys. You’re my family... All of you.”

James glanced at Peter, who didn't return the look, but eased the tenseness in his shoulders.

“Pete?”

Peter continued glaring at the floor, and then finally threw his arms down. “Fine! Yes, I understand. But it's not my fault you decided to like each other…”

“That’s not what this is about, Pete,” James said, then, more cautious; "Is it...?”

“No.” Peter raised his eyes to Remus'. “You say you didn't tell people, but you did! You just didn’t tell me. Even Lottie knew, only I was singled out! But that’s how it always is, isn't it? I don't care who you're buggering, but christ—I thought it would be different when Miles left! Then you came and it was the same thing all over again... Do you even know why I like Moira? ‘Cause she makes me feel like a person! You guys make me feel like crap.”

“This isn’t some polygamist cult, Pettigrew,” Sirius said. “Not including you in mine and Moony’s relationship isn’t exactly uncommon! We had to know we could trust you first!”

“Trust me?!” Peter exclaimed. “What happened to being family?!”

“You can’t keep a secret!”

“And my sister can?”

Sirius sat up. “Your sister did! For months—she didn’t breathe word of it to anyone! You drop your spoon at lunch and you make sure the whole world knows it!”

“Piss off!”

“Stop!” James ordered. “We’re not just gonna shout. We’re here to work this out, because the way I see it, none of us are gonna move forward with any of our relationships as long as it’s an issue. Now, Moony, why’d you decide not to tell Pete about you and Sirius?”

Remus felt at a loss. “It just… never came up.”

Peter scoffed. “Right.”

“Not even when you were telling Lily and me?”

“It’s not that simple,” Sirius cut-in. “Telling one person doesn’t mean you’ve suddenly got the confidence to shout it to the entire world. We had no idea how you and Evans were gonna react—it’s not like we were telling you our bloody shoe size had changed. It's like Moony said, it was about how you saw us. What you thought later and forever. Because it matters.”

“And I don’t, I suppose,” Peter shot back.

“You do, Pete,” Remus insisted, “but it was harder than that. And thinking about how we wanted to do this band… Be rock stars. One word to the wrong person could ruin everything.”

Peter slammed his hands on the desktop. “Fuck's sake, it’s always gotta be about the bloody band with you!”

“Lay off him!” Sirius snapped. “He just means we had to know you were serious.”

“Serious?” Peter echoed. “SERIOUS?! Try seriously pissed off!”

“Right, we got that part.”

“Oh, you think you’re so smart!” Peter hissed. “But how smart could you be if this mythical band’s all you’ve got going for you!”

“What did you say?”

“That’s right! You’re so desperately clinging to this idea of being rock stars because you’ve got nothing else going for you! Me and James have shit—he could take over his dad’s firm in an instant, or be a sports star if he really wanted! And I’ve still got options with my brother—no matter how pathetic you may think it is, I have people who want me! James and I could make something of ourselves, it’s you two who have nothing other than this fucking band!”

“I knew it!” Sirius howled, launching himself up to his feet. “It was never about me or Moony, it was always about following James! Of breaking us up so that he could be as pitiful as you! Some artist—just say you’re a coward and get out!”

This time Remus did not have to get in front of Sirius—James did it for him, using all his full height to walk Sirius back to his desk.

“Sirius, sit down.”

Remus couldn’t see with James’ back turned, but something about his expression must’ve made Sirius think twice. Slowly, he lowered himself back down into the desk, kicking the closest chair to him away for good measure.

"This is not how I wanted this to go," James said. "We were supposed to be making up!"

"Guess that's what happens when you try and force people to get along," Peter glowered. Sirius returned the look, and James' hands became fists at his sides. For a moment it looked as though he might actually hit something, but then he shut his eyes and let out a long breath and just like that he'd relaxed again.

"Fine," he said, leaning back against the professor’s desk. “If that's the case, then I wanna take a poll. No shame, no pressure, just answer honestly—all of you. But either in or out, I want us to promise right now that we’ll still be friends after.”

He cast his gaze over all of them, and one by one, they all managed a nod.

“Okay. Now who actually wants to be in a band? Not, ‘it’d be cool to do that for six months and then piss off’, but actually. Who wants this?”

Sirius’ hand went up without hesitation, and Remus’ too, a few moments later. James did not vote right away, instead he looked to Peter, who was picking at his desk with a fingernail.

“Pete, now’s the time to be honest, mate. No judgement, just honesty.”

Slowly, Peter looked up until he was able to look James in the eye. And then he raised one hand. At that moment, Remus wasn’t sure if he should be upset or relieved—and because it would’ve terrified James to know which, he pushed the thought away.

“Good.” James raised his hand too. “All four of us want this then. And we want it together, how it should be. But we have to know we can trust each other too.”

“Yeah,” Peter said. “How do we know that this won’t all go to shit if the two of them suddenly break up?”

Sirius turned sharply as though he were ready to stand again, but stopped when Remus grabbed his arm. “He has a point,” Remus said.

“We’re not breaking up,” Sirius said firmly. “Maybe this is all news to the rest of you, but I’ve loved Moony since—” he stopped short, and scratched his nose to cover it; “since… a while. Now we’ve sorted out our shit. We’re happy.”

“So you say now,” Peter said, “but your track record’s against you.”

This time it was Remus’ turn to spin around. “Pete, don’t be an asshole.”

“Me?”

“Yeah. We wanna do this with you, but not if you’re just gonna be a prick about it.”

“Well, I may be a prick but at least I’m not shagging one.”

“Pete!” James snapped. “What did we talk about this morning?”

Scowling, Peter leaned back in his chair and crossed his arms, but said nothing else. Remus eyed him grimly for a few moments and then turned back around in his chair. Sirius was covering his mouth next to him, and when he pulled his hand away Remus expected to find a frown—only it was a smile. He looked from Peter, back to Remus, and then inexplicably, Sirius began to laugh.

“Ha… mhm… ‘not shagging one’…” he mumbled; “s’a good joke almost…”

“Sirius, are you actually laughing?” Asked James.

Sirius shook his head, even covering his mouth again. He held out for a good few seconds before sputtering through his hand and breaking down entirely. “He got you, Moons,” he cackled. “You are indeed shaggin’ a prick! HA!”

“And an idiot, apparently," Remus half-moaned, covering his eyes. Across the room, he heard James give a chortle.

"Is it a tiny prick, Padfoot?"

"No, massive. Right, Wormtail?"

"Yeah, well he is a massive prick..."

"HA!"

More laughed, and Remus finally removed his hands to find that all three of them had joined in, even Peter. It was ridiculous how easy it suddenly felt. All of that, and now this.

Infected by the sudden lift in mood, Remus began to laugh too, letting all of the pressure and anxiety seep from his bones. Sirius laughed until he was practically crying, and while he was wiping the tears from his eyes, Peter cleared his throat.

“Look, I don’t care that you’re gay—”

“Moony’s bisexual,” James and Sirius said together.

“What… So like, both?”

Remus shook his head. “Doesn’t matter. As you were saying, Pete?”

“I’m not gonna tell anyone," Peter said. "I want to be in the band too, and as much as I hate saying it, you're right... I don’t think the world is ready for a gay rock star, even if he is as fabulous as Sirius.”

Sirius smirked, and then shrugged amicably. "Wouldn't want to steal the spotlight off of the rest of you that much anyway. Sounds like a lot of work, that."

They shared another chuckle, and finally James clapped his hands together. "Glad that's over. I hate fighting, so if there's anything else the lot of you want to say, now's the time to do it."

Remus and Sirius both shook their heads, but three out of four wasn't a whole, and so finally they all found themselves looking back at Peter.

"Pete?" James said anxiously. "Come on, mate."

"I want this," Peter nodded. "But I need to know, what's gonna happen if the two of you break up?"

Sirius frowned, and Remus could tell he was trying to keep his anger in check.

"We won't."

"That's not good enough."

The hackles went up again, but luckily James was there to soothe it once more.

“Hey. I understand where Pete’s coming from, and it's not an insult, Padfoot."

"Easy for you to say. What if he'd just asked whether yours and Evans' relationship had an expiry date?"

"It'd suck, but it wouldn't have anything to do with the band."

The frown became another scowl, and Remus reached out to take his hand. "Say what you want to say then," he told the other two. "We'll hear you out."

"You gotta swear this isn't just for you," Peter said. "That this whole band thing, leaving school to live like bums—that isn't just a part of some crazy romanticised idea. That it isn't just for you."

"I see four people here," Sirius echoed; "Just because it was our idea doesn't mean you don't have an equal stake."

"But you could make or break it, Sirius," James finished. "Pete's right. I know you might not mean for it that way, but things like this can get warped. You… You—I dunno—Maybe you just have to swear that this whole thing—taking a year off, working for the band—that it's more than what we see. That it's not just for you guys, because it can't be. It has to be all of us, together, like you said—four. I love you both, really, but you have to be real about this, 'cause this is real life, ain't it? And if anything’s gonna come of it you have to put this first, or at least make it the same.”

Unsure of how to answer such a thing, Remus wiped his face. Opposite to him, Sirius leaned back in his chair and looked up at the ceiling.

“Put it first, huh?”

Or the same, Remus thought sorely.

“I just mean we have to be friends first, don’t we?" James winced. "That’s how this whole thing started anyway. Like, if we can’t be friends before bandmates and whatever else, then… Pete’s right, how could it ever work?”

“I agree,” Remus said, though he didn't want to. “We started this as friends, I think we should finish it... as friends.”

Obviously relieved, James nodded. “Okay. And what say you, Padfoot?”

Sirius sighed, and dropped his eyes from the roof. “I say yes, I suppose. Marauders weren’t meant to walk alone anyway.”

“ 'One for all, and all for one’, right?"

"Right." Standing, Sirius took James' hand and clapped his shoulder in a friendly hug. “Pete,” he called afterwards, “I didn’t mean what I said earlier, I was just angry. My bad, won’t happen again.”

Remus thought that it wasn’t exactly an apology, but Peter didn’t seem to notice. He stood up too, and nodded in return.

“I hate fighting. It’s so much easier to just let James boss us around.”

James pulled a face. “Oi, I’m not bossy. Sirius, am I bossy?”

“Only as bossy as Moony.”

"I am not bossy,” Remus scoffed, “you just need a twenty-four-seven babysitter.”

“Eh, boyfriend—babysitter. You’re all the same. Sarcastic arseholes with a pretty face.”

Remus grabbed Sirius by the jaw, squishing his lips together with a grin. “Says you.”

“Is this what they’re like when they flirt?” Peter asked James.

“Pretty much.”

“Ah, so not that different from usual then.”

Remus smiled back at them as Sirius pulled his face free. “I think we need to do something,” he said keenly. “Something to make up—make us not so foul anymore. We’re leaving school soon and everyone’s gotten weepy, but I’m excited! Shove the exams, let’s do something to celebrate! Something cool, so that when we leave we'll have no regrets.”

“You mean like a prank?” Asked Peter.

“Yes… or, that too anyway. Suppose there's gotta be more than one way to have 'em remember us.”

James tilted his head, clearly intrigued. “What are you getting at, Padfoot?”

“I was thinking we could make a time capsule, actually.”

“Like the one Filch dug up last term?”

"Yeah!"

Peter scratched his head. “What would we put in it?”

“Anything—everything. Whatever we wanted! Put in James’ rank football boots for all I care.”

“But we’re not important. Who wants to dig up a time capsule full of our crap?”

“Yet, Wormy,” Sirius said, “we’re not important yet.”

“I think it’s a great idea,” said James. “We could get the girls in on it. Let McKinnon try out a time capsule of her own.”

“You’re so nice,” Sirius teased, knocking him gently in the shoulder. “But yeah, the girls too. Now whaddya say, Moons?”

They all looked at him, and Remus smiled.

“I think it’s about the lamest thing you’ve ever suggested."

"Oh? Really."

"Yeah... And I know exactly what we should put in it.”

Chapter 94: Glory Days


Chapter Summary

The Marauders get ready to leave school while juggling exams, football, and an unfortunate lack of pranking ideas.

For once in my life, I won’t let sorrow hurt me,

Not like it’s hurt me before;

For once, I have something I know won’t desert me,

I’m not alone anymore;

For once I can say, “This is mine, you can’t take it!”

As long as I know I have love, I can make it;

For once in my life, I have someone who needs me…

- “For Once in My Life” Stevie Wonder, 1968



Wednesday 31st May 1978





Remus clenched the post card tightly between his fingers. It was wrinkled as though it'd been dropped in a puddle and only had a few sparse words, but the excitement it carried was astronomical.





Imming was bust. Found a group and we’re moving on. Phone me at the Roadman’s Pub in Ipswich. Wrote the number down below. Luv Tom.





He took the stairs down two at a time, and was punching numbers into the closest telephone line before he’d even stopped to catch his breath. The phone rang for a moment, before it clicked on and an old, breathy voice shouted down the line.

“ ‘Ello, Judy? Is that you?”

“Eh… No… it’s Remus…”

“What’d you say, Judy? Come now, speak up you old bat, you know my ears ain’t naught but whistles in the wind nowadays.”

“Sorry, wrong number!”

He slammed the receiver down, stopping just long enough to laugh at himself as he dialled the number again—more slowly this time. It took longer this time around for the call to cross the miles between them, but when the line finally connected, he was met with the rumbling drawl of another stranger.

“Roadman’s pub 'n inn, how may I direct ya?”

He told the man on the end of the line who he was looking for, and then there was a clatter as the phone was set down. In the background he could hear an entire rabble, most likely working men just got off from a hard day’s work. There was shouting, laughter, the occasional sound of a smashing glass. Remus imagined Tomny was fitting right in.

There was another clatter as the phone was picked up, and then his friend was shouting down the line;

“Oioi! Whatchu want—who’s this?”

“Got that many people calling you at some dingy pub, you slag?”

“LU! Oh baby, I missed you!”

Remus’ heart leapt in his chest. He could barely hear Tomny over all the noise, but he was smiling ear-to-ear anyway.

“Honestly, Tomny, the things I do for you—”

“What? Sorry’s, love, can you speak up a bit?”

“I was only saying!” Remus shouted into the phone; “That I just dialled the wrong number. Instead of the pub I just got some old bint yelling her head off and calling me Judy.”

“Eh, s’not a terrible nickname,” Tomny said. “Though, I do prefer mine. How’s it do, Lu?”

“Life’s good, Tom. Got your letter. I see your penmanship’s gotten better.”

“Oi. Just 'cause I dropped out at thirteen don’t mean I’m a total thickhead. Burrin’s had me copying out his bookie notes since before I could see over the counter.”

“Mhm, sure. So what the hell happened in Imming? Why're you in Ipswich?”

“Oh." Tomny made a sound of discontent and sighed into the phone. “Eh, bit boring really. Eventually every'fin just went tits-up and no one was gettin’ paid anymore, so a few of us packed our bags and skipped town, s'all. Place is too cold to be a summer home anyway.”

“That’s shite.”

“Eh, easy when you only got one bag. We managed to snag a ride on the railway but got kicked off near Leicester when the poncy conductor found us hiding out in one of the sleepers. From there it was shanks’ pony all the way to Peterborough, but managed to bum a ride from there. But I got another gig down at the port out by Felixstowe! We're all heading over there tomorrow actually. Me and the guys are gonna live together down by the ports."

"Do you know them?"

"We're comfortable. Better than living in a dosshouse. And it’s honest work—port’s massive, way bigger than Imming. The boys thought a bit of a celebration was in order though, so we're's just having ourselves a bit of a piss-up now." In another, another shattering glass echoed in the background, followed by a round of hearty laughter. Tomny joined in, before shouting into the phone again; "But what about'chu?! How long ‘til yer done wiff school?”

“Few weeks."

Tomny whistled. "Then what?”

“Then I’m back home, s'pose. The lads and I are gonna get a flat—find work ourselves. Maybe a shitty pub to peddle our band in.”

“Ah yes, the band,” Tomny mused. “You’re not goin’ back to yer dad’s then?”

“No. Nothing there for me anyway.”

“Too right. Get this though, Burrin knows the guy who runs the racket in the yard round 'ere, says he's gonna set me up too."

"Doing what, something illegal?"

"S'only illegal if you get caught."

"Wonder how many felons have said that."

"Cheeky. Give me six months, I'll have the entire place eatin' out of the palm of my hand."

It was jest—probably an exaggeration at best, but Remus couldn't help the way his stomach seemed to plummet toward his feet.

"Six months...?"

"Ah." Tomny clicked his tongue, and Remus' fist tightened over the postcard.

“Tom, is this your way of telling me you’re not coming back to London?”

"Now hold on, I never said—" Suddenly Tomny went silent, and Remus had to press the receiver more tightly to his ear just to make out the voices over the noise.

"Piss off, m'on the phone, ya prick!"

"C'mon, Tim-Tom, don't be stingy. I just wan' say hello to your pretty bird from back home."

"Oh, fuck you, Harv."

The tussle went on for a few more seconds until eventually Remus was answered with a new voice. This 'Harv' was clearly drunk, and had a deep Black Country accent that was impossible to miss. He laughed down the line at first, and Remus felt his patience wither.

"Ow do, luv?" He drawled. "You one 'ah the girls our Tim-Tom's always chatting up from back home?"

"Shut up, Harv!" Tomny called; "It's my fuckin' brother, orright? Now give me the bloody phone!"

Another clamorous scuffle began, and distantly Remus heard the barman from before warn the two about messing around in his pub. In the end it was Tomny who won, shooing his friend off as he sighed into the phone.

"Sorry 'bout that... S'just Harv. Pretty sure he took one too many hits to the skull as a kid and it's left him a moron."

"No, it's my bad. Didn't realise I was clogging up the line," Remus scoffed. "I should let you go, let the 'pretty birds' have their turn."

"The git's lying! I barely have a second to myself, ain't no time leftover to flirt."

"Sure, Tim-Tom."

"Okay, I'd say your cheek's hit full for one phone call, don't cha think?"

Unable to help himself, Remus smirked and began absentmindedly twirling the phone cord around his wrist. "You called me your brother."

"Yeah, and?"

Remus' smile widened.

"I am coming back, y'know," Tomny said eventually. "Can't stand coming home every day stinkin' 'ah fish guts and oil forever. M'just... Well, I'm just gonna see how this works out first. But I'll be back. One of us still owes the other a warm meal, innit.”

Remus sighed. "Yeah, alright."

"So you gonna finally tell me what's new or am I to stand here listening to you mope forever?"

"I found out I have a godmother.”

"No shit?"

“And she’s my teacher.”

“Fuckin' 'ell!" Tomny exclaimed. "Your life sometimes, I swear... Are you happy about it?”

“Yeah, sorta. But it’s still confusing, mostly.”

“Family always is. I only ever had mum, and she was more than enough to deal with. I used to think she was a bit daft, but she was just some girl, and ya don’t get fancy things like ‘godparents’ when yer born a low-rent. Now how’d you find out about this god-mum of yours?”

“It’s a long story.”

“Maybe you tell me when I see you next then. Since you’re moving back for good?”

Remus brightened a bit. “Yeah, definitely! I can't wait for you to meet the others, properly this time. And you should meet Mary and Marlene too. They all know about Sirius and me now, all of them.”

“It’s a date,” Tomny agreed, then; “And you can tell lover-boy I said so."

"You shouldn't tease him."

"Why not? It's a big brother's job—giving the new boyfriend a hard time."

"Yeah, okay. I'll see you when we're both back then?"

“You know it. Make sure you give me the bell once you’re settled in. I'd like to pop by and catch one of your little shows.”

"They won’t be little forever. Who knows, maybe one day I'll be inviting you to Wembley.”

"As long as you'll be there. Now I'll be seeing you, Lu. Stay safe, enjoy yourself. You've earned it, posh-boy."

When Tomny hung up, all the sounds of his rowdy pub fell away and Remus was left alone in the quiet hallway of his school dorm. Nearby the common room was flush with groups of kids trying to enjoy what was left of their evening. No one noticed, but Remus' cheeks had started to burn even before he hung the phone back onto its hook. A part of him wished he hadn't mentioned Wembley Stadium in the first place; he blamed Sheila for ever putting the thought in his head—Me? Play Wembley? As if—but then again, Tomny had never been the sort to trample on other people's dreams. All Remus could do now was trust his word; that Tomny would be back as soon as he could, and everything would be alright again. And so he resolved himself to push the entire thing from his mind, at least until they were all back in London and ready to do something about it.

Turning to face the front doors, Remus picked up the Fender’s case from its spot along the wall and pulled up the collar of his jacket as he walked out into the crisp night air. There was no time to fret over Tomny anyway.

He was late for band practice.





* * *





Monday 5th June 1978





Lily stood in the doorway of their dorm room, squinting down at the tape recorder Sirius had just unceremoniously dropped into her arms. She and Marlene had really only come over to get their notebooks back after James and Peter had borrowed them for self-study, but Sirius had been quick to waylay them before departure with talk of their latest bright idea.

“I don’t understand…” Lily said; “You want us to do what with it?”

“Pick a song—one that really means something to you—and record it on this here tape. It’s set up for you already,” Sirius instructed, scooting in closer. “This is the record button, and there’s the stop button—basic stuff. Just hit the record, play your song off whatever radio, and then hit stop again. Easy-peasy.”

“But why?” Marlene asked, peering over Lily’s shoulder.

“It’s for the time capsule,” Remus said.

Both girls stared back in surprise. “You’re making a time capsule?”

James’ voice carried from inside the bathroom; “It was Sirius’ idea!”

“But Moony thought of the tape!” Sirius added excitedly. “We’re gonna put everything into a capsule of our own and bury it—right here on campus! Then, in twenty years when we’re either rich and successful or fat and balding, we can come back and dig it up again. Relive our glory days, as it goes.”

“Wouldn’t it make more sense for you guys to record your own songs?” Marlene asked, reaching over Lily’s shoulder and tapping a fingernail along the tape recorder’s keys sceptically. In answer, Sirius and Remus exchanged a smug look.

“We already did.”

The girls’ jaws dropped. “You did?”

“Finished it this morning in fact,” Sirius beamed proudly. “Wormy’s over in the AV room right now, getting those lads to piece it together for us. It's not perfect, but when he’s done we’ll have our very first amateur demo.”

“So this is what you’ve been doing with all of your time for the last month!” Lily huffed. “ ‘Studying’ my arse—you four were just shut up in that bloody music room, working on your riffs instead of working on your marks!”

“Don’t worry, we're still passed all our exams,” Sirius preened. “Some with flying colours, I hear.” He glanced coquettishly at Remus, who had already done more than his fair share of bragging; which was of course only well-deserved. Their final reports had come back the day before, and he’d been very pleased to find that he’d made top marks in not only English but Classics as well. He tried not to gloat, but even Professor Bilshin had praised his work, and it was a well-known fact that that old sour-puss had never praised anyone.

“Well,” Lily breathed eventually, “this is all brilliant then. When should we expect to hear this ‘demo’ of yours?”

“You won’t,” Remus said, leaning against the open door shyly. “We swore we wouldn’t listen to it until 1998.”

“1998?" Marlene gasped; "But that’s twenty years from now!”

“We know. It’s going in the capsule.”

“And there will be room for you and yours,” Sirius assured them, “just pick a song—get Mary and Lottie in on it too. It’s an eight-track tape, and there’s eight of us. Honestly, I couldn’t think of anything more perfect.”

Lily and Marlene smiled, obviously softened by Sirius’ show of inclusion, and nodded their heads in agreement. “Alright,” Lily said, “but you’re not allowed to make fun of our choices.”

Sirius put a hand over his heart. “I solemnly swear to not make fun of the songs you ladies choose… Even if they are absolutely grating on the ears.”

Contented, Marlene reached out and pinched Sirius on the cheek, before both girls turned to go.

“Make sure you give it back soon,” he called down the hall after them. “We’re gonna bury it after the tournament!”

Once they’d gone and Sirius had come back inside, Remus shut the door and raised his arms up in a stretch. “You think it’s silly?” He asked. “The tape idea?”

“Of course not,” Sirius smiled. “I can't think of anything better. The rest of you might be embarrassed of your music taste in twenty years, but not me. Bowie’ll always be timeless.”

“So you picked a Bowie song? I should’ve known.”

“Practice what you preach, right?"

"Right."

"What song did you pick then? You never said.”

“Sorry, not telling.”

"Uh-huh, nice try," Sirius scoffed. “No go on, fess up!”

“You're the one who said it should be a secret."

“Yeah, but it’s me!”

“Even more reason not to tell,” Remus said snidely, “you know far too many of my secrets already.”

“Ugh. You're no fun.” Stopping long enough to stick out tongue as a show of opposition, Sirius crossed the room to the bathroom door and promptly banged his fist on the wood. “Dammit, Prongs! How long you gonna be in there for? The rest of us need to piss every once in a while too, ya know.”

“Do you mind? I’m shaving!” James called back. “Call me when you get more than two hairs on your chin!”

Sirius kicked the door. “Wanker.”

Disinterested, Remus returned to his corner of the room. He had Hope’s white trunk open on his bed, which he’d been slowly filling as the days went by. It was mostly books, spare socks, the odd essay he’d thought worth keeping, but there were also a handful of photographs, courtesy of Lily. She’d given them to him in an envelope only a few weeks before, and when he peered into the collection of polaroid photos he’d found more than he’d thought he would. Apart from a few chance moments, he could scarcely remember Lily toting the camera around with her at all, and yet the evidence was right there, dated and captioned just for him.

Some of them were priceless, like the ones of all four of them on Sirius' seventeenth birthday, standing in naught but their pants at the very end of the dock. Even now Remus could still recall the cold. Then there was Peter missing an eyebrow, and Sirius in Mary's tube tup at the end of twelfth year, and James on his birthday with that stupid party hat they'd made him wear. Those ones were definitely worth a good laugh, but there were also simpler ones;

Mary and Marlene cuddling each other on the sofa; a concentrated Peter in art class; Lottie waving in front of the Three Broomsticks; James and Sirius smiling for the camera, a tight-lipped Professor McGonagall standing between them; and finally four girlish faces squeezed into a single frame and an unsuspecting Remus passed out in the background. If he squinted hard, he could just make out the fresh tattoo on his chest.

They’d really had so much fun at school.

Each photograph had unlocked a memory for Remus that he'd almost thought forgotten, but it was the one of him and Sirius in the common room that had really gotten him. It was dated as March 24th, 1977, just a few days before James' birthday. Sirius had Andy's guitar in his lap, his eyes shut as though he were lost in the song. And Remus... God. He was smiling like a sop, wasn't he? Staring at Sirius as though the sun rose and set on him. He supposed it did. For whatever love he'd had for Sirius in that moment, it had only tripled since.

“I don’t know why you’re packing now. We don’t leave for another week and half,” Sirius said, appearing over Remus’ shoulder and glancing down at the trunk. With a soft smile, Remus tucked the photographs away and turned to him.

“Your hair’s finally grown back," he said, tucking a lock of it behind Sirius' ear for him. "It looks like it did before.”

“Does it?” Sirius thumbed his fringe. “Doesn’t feel like it.”

“You could probably even braid it again.”

“Would you do it for me?”

“If you wanted me to.”

"And if I wanted you to do... other things?"

Remus tongued the inside of his cheek. "Now that would have to be negotiated."

"I think you'd find it to be a waste of time," Sirius tsked. "After all, I always get what I want. In the end..."

"Do you now?" Remus arched a brow. "Why don't you prove it."

For a moment it appeared as though Sirius might rise to the bait. He smirked at him, even grinned and ran the tip of his tongue across his teeth to tease. And Remus might've been satisfied with just that, but then Sirius sighed and turned away, as though the game did not interest him in the slightest. Remus didn't even think; it was instinct to reach out and grab him, haul Sirius back with every finger hingeing in the waistband of his trousers—and Remus got his due the moment he spun Sirius back around and spotted that smug look on his face.

"See?" Sirius purred. "Want you? Got you." Then he grabbed Remus round the jaw and kissed him hard on the mouth. It was something Remus never got tired of. Sirius was a bombshell—a firecracker come to life. He made everything exciting, no matter how many times they did it. The idea of one day having to share him with the rest of the world made him endlessly nervous, but Sirius was too big a star to ever be contained. They'd see him, they'd love him, but never like this. This belonged to Remus alone.

"I want this," Sirius murmured, kissing Remus' mouth; "and this—" his cheek; "and this—" his eyes; "and this—" his neck; "All of it."

"All of it?"

"All of it."

They ended up on Remus' bed, Sirius straddling him as Remus slid his hands up beneath his shirt. He'd just made it to the top of his ribs when Sirius grabbed one wrist and brought Remus' hand up toward his face. Instantly Remus thought to grasp his neck and bring their mouths back together and—kiss, kiss, kiss—but then Sirius was sucking a finger into his mouth, biting him round the first knuckle.

"Careful," Remus moaned. "Much more of that and I'll—"

Before he could finish his eyes fell sideways, right over Sirius' shoulder, to where James was stood frozen next to his own bed in little more than his sport shorts. Remus screamed—"AUGH!"—and shot upright, just as Sirius was leaning back down to kiss him. Their foreheads collided with a dull thump and instantly Sirius had collapsed back on the bed.

"Fucking—CHRIST!" He groaned, as the two of them writhed on the bed, clutching their newly-formed bruises. "Moons, what the hell?!" Sirius rolled over, and Remus knew he'd spotted James as well when his arm shot out.

"YOU!"

James laughed once, and gave an awkward wave. "Sorry... Didn't mean to interrupt."

"It's always fucking you!" Sirius howled, snatching up a pillow in one hand and sending it soaring across the room to smack James upside the head.

"I was trying to get by without you noticing!" He wailed back, fixing his glasses. "But the bloody door's between your beds! What was I supposed to do?"

"You were supposed to stay in the fucking toilet!"

"That's not fair. How should I know that the two of you were out here eating each other's faces off?"

"Oh, I'm sorry! Next time we'll moan louder!"

"Yeah, yeah," James scoffed, pulling on his t-shirt. "Give it a few weeks, we'll all be out on our own... No more sharing a room then."

Still clutching his forehead, Sirius looked to Remus, who shrugged haplessly, rubbing his own.

"Fine," Sirius huffed, clambering off the bed; "Suppose the mood's gone anyway… Anyone feel like music?"

"Anything to drown out the sound of you sticking your tongue down Moony's throat."

"Don't be jealous, Potter. Macdonald says it gives you wrinkles."

As Sirius crossed back to his own bed, Remus stood and righted his mother's trunk, which had ended up on the floor in their haste to make room on the tiny four-poster. By the time he'd picked all his things up off the floor, Sirius had a Bad Company album playing and was lying upside down on his bed, tossing a tiny rubber ball up in the air.

"Big game's coming up, Potter," he said. James didn't reply at first, and Remus glanced over to find him lying back on his own bed, hands clasped over his chest and staring up at the ceiling as though he were lost in thought.

"Potter?"

"Huh? Oh... Yeah, it is."

Sirius tossed the ball up again. "You and McKinnon decide what it is you're doing for the tournament yet?"

"Sorta."

"Alright, be stingy then." Another toss, and another, and then; "Blimey, where is Pete? It's just one tape, can't be that hard—"

James sat up on his bed; "When you two kiss each other, do you ever think about how you're kissing another bloke?"

This time Sirius missed the ball. It hit him square between the eyes before bouncing off and rolling across the room and beneath Peter's bed. By then James had earned himself an incredulous look from both of them and Sirius had sat up so quickly he'd nearly taken a spill off of his covers.

"Pardon me?"

"Like, does it feel different from kissing a girl?"

Sirius made a small choking sound in the back of his throat. "From a girl—why yes, I expect it's a bit different!"

"Better different...?"

"That's probably up to the person, Prongs," Remus said, while Sirius leapt up from the bed and pointed yet another finger at his best friend.

"You been kissing other blokes, Potter?!"

"What? No!"

"Then why the sudden interest?"

"I was just curious!"

Remus suspected that if James could've blushed easily he would've been red from top to bottom. As it was, he merely let out a nervous huff and began organising his already-spotless bedside. "I've just been thinking about it, that's all," he babbled, tossing his arms out and rubbing the back of his neck simultaneously. "A lot's happened since you told us! Like—Like the shit with Pete, and—and Marlene! She's a lesbian, you know."

"Yes," Sirius scoffed; "We know."

"Well, I... I've been talking to her about it."

"That'll get you every time," Remus mumbled. It made Sirius smirk a bit, but James didn't seem to notice.

"She said she's always known," he continued; "That she—you know, liked girls. And I was just wondering... was it the same for you guys? You know, since you... 'like guys'."

He used air quotes, and Remus' jaw just about fell off his face.

"James, could you... I mean, do you think you could like—"

"Men?"

James looked up when he said it, and both Remus and Sirius seemed to be gripping the edge of their seats, but in the end James only laughed.

"Ha, no! Don't be stupid, you two, I have Lily."

"What does that have to do with anything?" Sirius demanded.

"Well, I have a girlfriend."

"Moony's had girlfriends!"

"So has Sirius."

James shook his head. "No. No, you're wrong. It's nothing personal, I'm just... you know, not. Like, when Padfoot and I kissed I didn't feel anything at all."

Sirius made a retching sound. "Please, don't ever bring that up again. I have nightmares about that day."

James rolled his eyes, and Remus came across the room to lean gently against one of the posts of his bed.

"You know, Prongs, having a girlfriend doesn't much have to do with your sexuality. You could still... 'like' people."

"I like Lily," James replied staunchly. "I wanna be with her forever."

"O-Okay."

James glanced between the two of them; Remus who kept rubbing his neck, and Sirius who wouldn't meet his eye. "I shouldn't have said anything," he chuckled, the humour not meeting his eyes. "Things are just different now, is all. Exams are pretty well finished, we're all about to leave school... It's just curiosity, right?"

"It's alright to be curious," said Remus.

"Yeah," Sirius shrugged. "Like, if you really wanted to know what it's like to kiss Moony you could've just asked."

"Really?"

"No!"

James grinned, then stood up from his bed. "Aw, Pads, no need to be jealous. You want a kiss too? C'mere, I'll make it up to you!"

"Piss off!"

But James didn't. He sprung forward like a cat, grappling Sirius even as he was playfully beaten and slapped. When he failed to reach his lips, James turned and hugged Remus instead, which only made Sirius want to pry him off even more.

“Don't be stingy, Padfoot! I want some boyfriend love too."

“Too bad! This one’s mine, go find your own!”

Sirius shoved him, and Remus was unable to stop it as they all fell back onto James' bed in a tangle of limbs. By then James was laughing—that great infectious guffaw of his that always brought a smile to each of their faces. Sirius laughed, then Remus too, and they were all done for. The laughter was still going even several moments later when their bedroom door opened and Peter strolled in.

“It's done, lads!" He cried. "Tape’s all fin—Oh, Jesus fuck... If this is your way of telling me that you’re really a part of some homoerotic triad I might actually have to kill myself.”

Sirius flung James’ arm off and sat up. “Nah, we wouldn't leave you out, Wormy! Here, let Daddy Padfoot give you a big ol' smooch.”

The next day, as they made their way down to the church for that morning’s communion, Remus kept the small tape clutched tightly in the palms of his hands. He hadn’t let the thing out of his sight since Peter had finished it, it was too valuable. They’d actually done it—it was real!

Their very first demo.

When Remus had first suggested they record a demo of themselves that day in the classroom, he had no idea just how good it would be for the four of them. It was the perfect way to reconcile after the Peter fight—instantly nothing mattered more than the music. Not relationships, not A-Levels, not even sleep—only the band.

And it was exactly what they’d promised! Each of them put in their fair share of long hours at the music room, perfecting every lyric and every melody until Filch was all but chasing them out with a pitchfork, and even then, they never fought once. It was almost a miracle. Figuring out the recording bit had been tricky—there was only so much room on the tape and more than once they'd ended up taping right over their already finished work—but after finally getting the hang of it, things had just come together. The demo had a little piece of all of them—Sirius’ bombastic ‘Downtown Girls’, James’ incessantly cheesy ‘Letter to a Lily’, even an entire three-minute drum-solo spearheaded by Peter.

Initially Remus had been a bit hesitant, but the tape's final draft also included ‘Tonya’s Song’, though... only as an instrumental. He quite couldn't bring himself to sing the words, and though Sirius had offered, it just felt better this way. Tonya was a plaster he still wasn't quite ready to rip off, but thankfully his friends’ intrepid love and talent made up for it.

“Almost seems a shame, leaving it in a box for twenty years,” James yawned, stretching his arms up over his head as they filed into the pew. For the most part the church was empty; they’d made the mistake of coming down to the church early after James had forgotten to do headcount the night before. He'd spent all morning rushing around, ensuring that all of the Godric boys were alive and counted for. Watching him almost made Remus feel sorry for every dorm monitor that'd had to put up with the likes of them over the years. They'd probably given poor Kenny a few premature greys.

“We’ll make another one,” Sirius vowed, taking a seat between James and Remus. “Next one'll be even better than the last, you'll see. We can rent a real studio! In London, even.”

“Are you sure?" Asked Peter. "I find it hard to believe that just anyone can waltz in off the street like that."

“You can if you have the cash.”

“Dad’ll kill us if we just buy our way up, you know. He says—" James stopped for another yawn. "He says it’s not how it’s done."

“Only because rock stars so often start out as dirt poor,” Sirius drawled, “but yeah sure, we’ll ‘work our way up’.”

“With what job?" Remus asked, tucking the tape away. "Gotta get one first. And you're about as work-hardy as a spring daisy.”

“Look, it's a bloody job, okay? I'll get one—work at a pub or something. How hard can it be to pour a pint for a couple ‘a old codgers.”

“Mum’s got a friend who runs this real fancy restaurant in the city!" James said. "She figures she could get me a gig waiting tables. Want me to ask for you as well?”

Sirius made a face, then shivered. “Thanks, Prongs, but no thanks, I got cousins in the city, Andy’s family. And I’d rather spend the entire night scraping gum off bar stools in Hackney than risk having to fetch them their 'lemon water, no ice'.”

“He says, having never done a day of work in his life.” James craned his head. “Moony, how ‘bout you?”

“Uh…”

“Nah, no way!” Sirius cried, grabbing Remus by the shoulders. “Hundred pounds says this guy’s gonna end up working at some twee little bookshop. ‘Pardon me, son, have you seen any copies of “Das Kapital” sitting around by chance?’—‘Oh, yes sir! That’ll be aisle twelve! And if you’re looking for some nice, light reading, may I suggest “Mein Kampf”? Very inspirational, that’.”

"You are an idiot," said Remus.

“Swotsaidwhat?"

Remus hit him with a bible, and James laughed as he watched Sirius bitterly rub his shoulder.

"What about you, Pete?" Remus asked, turning to his other side. "Got any plans?”

“Yeah, wanna work at a fine London bistro together?” James offered enthusiastically, pushing Sirius' head out of the way. Down the row, Peter looked away, mumbling under his breath;

“Erm… Yeah well, about that… Dad called yesterday actually. Called it an 'ultimatum'. Says if I’m not going to school, then I have to work with him at the press.”

"What crap!" Sirius cried, before raising his arms up behind his head and slumping down in the pew. “Sounds like he’s trying to bloody indoctrinate you.”

“I thought he was fine with you taking a year off?” Remus asked.

“He was, but guess he decided he doesn't want me slumming around and doing nothing.”

“Music’s not nothing,” Sirius tsked.

“You try telling him that.”

“S’alright, work the job, Wormtail,” James said. “Show him you're dedicated. We can make the band work on the weekends.”

It wasn’t the news that they’d wanted, but Sirius managed to keep his mouth shut and no one said anything more on the subject. Eventually a swirl of chatter began filling the air as more and more students arrived to find their seats. Next to him in the pew, Remus felt Sirius begin to wiggle as though he couldn’t get comfortable. He turned to him and raised a brow in question, and Sirius just shrugged half-heartedly before gesturing to the front of the church.

“You’d think they’d have taken it down by now," he muttered. "It’s such an eye-sore.”

The eye-sore in question was the large statue of Christ, still hung up at the front of the church but now covered from view. It’d been several months since Sirius' outburst—the only that had left the statue without a nose. They'd all been hoping the school would remove it, but instead a while sheet had been draped over top of the statue and was to remain until term ended and the God-son's nose could be repaired.

“At least you don’t have to stare at it anymore?” Remus offered.

Sirius shrugged grumpily. “Wonder if Reg knows I did it.” He nodded his head to a busy pew a few rows ahead, where Regulus was sitting with Barty. It was with great pleasure that Remus spotted Trish on his opposite side, their shoulders nearly touching. As he watched, Barty reached around Regulus and yanked a fistful of Trish’s hair. It would’ve given Remus cause enough to intervene, had Trish not immediately retaliated by scooping up one of the bibles and thumping Barty over the head with it. He could see Regulus snapping at the both of them afterwards, probably telling them to act their age, which they'd both refuse—snidely.

“Imagine you hid someone behind it,” Remus mused, pointing to the sheet and attempting to improve Sirius’ mood. “And then the priests go to take off the tarp and end up scared shitless.”

The corner of Sirius’ mouth tweaked upwards. "You could jump out in the middle of the service."

"Wearing a robe and wig."

"Or naked."

Remus laughed, and imagined Regulus telling them to act their age. Then he laughed harder.

"You look as though you're having a good morning," Lily smiled, as she and the girls appeared in the row behind them. She kissed the top of James' hair before sitting, and Sirius immediately swivelled around in his pew to face them.

“Evans, McKinnon! You two tell them about the tape yet?”

“Let us wake up a bit first, Black,” Marlene said, still rubbing her eyes; “Yes, we told them.”

“Brilliant idea, right?” James grinned.

“Uh-huh, I love it,” said Lottie. “Our own time capsule! One to replace the shitty one they unearthed last term, right Marls?”

Marlene nodded in agreement.

“I think the tape’s a cute idea too,” Mary agreed. “I’m still undecided on a song though. Like, do I want to go with the expected choice, which would be amazing regardless, or should I try for something more interesting—more éblouissant? Which would also be amazing too. Obviously. Hm... Maybe I should compile a list.”

“Pick whatever song you want, just don’t tell us what it is,” Sirius said.

“Why not?” Lottie asked. “I thought we were putting it on the same tape.”

“We are, but it’s supposed to be a secret. At least until we play it.”

“Which will only be twenty years from now,” Marlene scoffed.

“Exactly! Now you’re getting it, McKinnon.”

Still stroking James' wild hair, Lily smiled and sat back in her pew. “Seems a bit silly, why wouldn’t we just play it together now? I want to know what you chose.”

“Have faith, Evans,” Sirius smirked, giving her a final wink.

The Marauders’ plans became reasonably predictable after that. They kept up with their band practices, and Remus continued to meet with Sheila on the regular. She was ecstatic when he told her that they’d actually managed to piece together their own tape, but when she asked to hear it, Remus had to stupidly refuse. He did consider sneaking it away just for her, but the demo had already proved to be too much of a temptation. For days they went back and forth over whether or not to listen to it, torn between pride over something they created and also entirely too nervous that even a single listen would point out all of their mistakes. They'd never listened to a recording of themselves before; and so, to settle the debate, Sirius had taped the demo to the ceiling of their bedroom, where it might be seen at all times and they could each hold the other accountable. In the very least, it was certainly one of their most questionable decor choices yet.

With their demo done and summer growing ever nearer, most students found themselves free to do as they pleased. Even the teachers seemed to have already checked out for the holiday, but Hawkings itself was in a tizzy preparing for the hosting of the final football tournament. Meanwhile rumours of parties and celebration swirled about campus, egged on by the idea that Remus and his friends had yet to unveil some grand plot that would put all of their previous marauder-ing to shame. Though whenever asked, all four Marauders appeared to playing dumb. Firstly because they didn't want their plans to be foiled before being brought to fruition, but also because they'd yet to make any. Sirius had claimed that a regular old leavers party would be boring and not in line with their usual end-of-term tomfoolery at all, but so far none of them had been able to come up with anything better than the usual 'chickens in the dorm room' gag.

While they hummed and hawed, the days passed until there were hardly any left. The tournament would be on them before they knew it, and there wasn't much else to do aside from look forward to whatever was coming next. It felt odd that none of them would be returning in the following autumn, but it didn't mean there wasn't any excitement in the air. Remus and Sirius would be returning to the Potters' until the four of them could find a place big enough on their own, and come September Lily would be joining them as well. While they worked and peddled their band, Lily would be starting a criminal justice degree at the University College of London, where she hoped to one day earn herself a spot in their faculty of law.

To no one's surprise, Mary had decided to study French at a London university as well, where she would be living separately from her family and taking voice lessons at a local conservatory on the side. She had tried to convince Marlene to move in with her, but the flat Mary had her eye on was in South Kensington, and the weekly rent alone would've been more than Mr. McKinnon made in a month. Lottie, meanwhile, would be returning home to live with her parents for the first time since she was a little girl. Her boyfriend Roger had been overseeing his father's holding company out in Reading for several months and was expected to remain until the following year, and so Lottie had made plans to attend a women's bookkeeping course in the city for a few days during the week, so that she might be able to take the train and see him on weekends. Marlene still maintained loose plans to throw her lot in with various charities and not-for-profit programs, though more recently it had come out just how badly her parents disapproved. Their wish for Marlene was that she attend a women's college closer to home, but when Marlene refused over Easter, the family's relationship with their only daughter had begun to deteriorate. Apparently rumours had started swirling at the McKinnon's church ever since it'd come out what sort of charity programs Marlene had been looking into. Most of them focused on helping young women and single mothers, but others had to do with more... social issues. Racial empowerment and queer rights were among the most condemned.

After that Marlene had decided that she would be moving out of her parents' house and into a shared living space in Southeast London. The flat itself was already being rented out by a few of the people who'd helped organise her trip to Morocco, and Marlene seemed excited for the change, despite her family's disapproval. Mrs. McKinnon threw a terrible fit when she heard, distraught over the soiled state of daughter's chastity and mortal soul. She began calling Marlene every night in a desperate attempt to get her to reconsider, but Marlene was resolute. “Hevershire College,” James answered, eyes closed and head still tucked in Lily’s lap. “But they’re not that good, so should be a shoo-in. They’ll still place as though they beat us because of the tournament’s barmy rules, but we’ll get to be the ones in the final game tomorrow.”

“And who do you think you’ll be facing?”

“Brentford, definitely. They’re tough, but I reckon that if we keep on like we have been we’ll have a real chance!”

“Can’t be that tough,” Remus muttered, munching on his egg and cress sandwich. “Their captain’s a bit of a tosspot.”

“He is not,” Sirius sniggered into the grass. “You just didn't like him. Not that I care, I love jealous Moony—ohhh! Yeah, right there, Lot!”

“You’ve met him? Is he proper fit?” Marlene taunted.

“Ixnay on the aptin-cay,” Remus shushed. “Just make sure you beat them tomorrow, okay, Potter?”

James saluted. “Aye-aye."

Everyone giggled, and as Lottie finished with her massage, Sirius rolled over, stretching and popping everything back into place. His face-paint was so smeared now that he looked as though he’d been hit with a red and gold glitter bomb. It made Remus nervous to think what his own cheeks looked like.

“I mean it Lot,” he sighed, “you’re like a magician. A wizard.”

Looking well-pleased, Lottie checked her nails. “Comes in handy with Roger too.”

“You do know you’ve only seen him in person like ten times,” Peter chirped. “That’s like once for every year he was alive before we were even born!”

“Some of us mature more rapidly than others, Petey.”

“Yeah, right. You just want to be his trophy wife. You know, I'm not even sure your relationship is legal.”

“Are you quite finished?" Lottie snapped. "Because you’re boring me.”

“Speaking of finished…” Sirius sat up, cracking his neck once more. “Don’t forget the tape. It’s going in the time capsule tomorrow after the game.”

“Already done," Mary announced. "I’ll give it to you at supper."

“Let me guess—ABBA?”

“You can find out in twenty years.”

Sirius smiled and reached over to kick the bottom of James’ football boot. “I suppose all that’s left is for you guys to kick ass in this tournament. Do try your best, I’d rather you not be mopey during our last day.”

“Oh, we’ll win alright,” Marlene answered for him, “gotta put Remus’ new arch-nemesis in his place, after all.”

“He’s not my arch-nemesis,” Remus grumbled, patting his pockets for his cigs and a light. He’d just gotten one of the fags lit when Sirius scooted up to his side, reaching and grabbing him by the chain necklace he wore around his throat. Using it as leverage, Sirius pulled Remus in close and leaned into the cigarette, taking a long drag right off of his fingers. When he was finished, he mouthed the words ‘I love you’ and then exhaled the rest of the smoke with a silly grin.

It was enough to leave Remus blushing for the rest of the afternoon.

When lunch was over they all headed back over to the pitch to watch the final match. The rest of them got first dibs in the stands when James and Marlene went to warm up, and it was clear not even ten minutes into the game that Hawkings would take it. To be polite, Remus waited until half-time to split off to the loo, and on his way back, spotted little Sam Sheridan sitting beneath the stands on his own. He had a book with him, as Sam often did, and feeling rather candid, Remus ducked low beneath the metal bars to join him.

"Hey, Sam. What're you doing under here?"

Sam glanced up from his book, pushing his glasses up his nose. "Hiding," he said.

" 'Hiding'?" Remus licked his lips to cover a laugh. "From who?"

"From Fiona," Sam replied grimly.

"Ah, I remember her. She invited you to that dance on Valentine's, didn't she? I'm guessing it didn't go well?"

"It went terrible. She thinks I'm her boyfriend now."

"Are you?"

"No! It's mental, I don't want to be her boyfriend!"

"Have you tried telling her that?"

"Yes! ... Or, no." Sam sighed and Remus got a distinct feeling of déjà vu. "I tried staying in my room, but our dorm monitor wouldn't let anyone younger than sixteen stay behind on their own, and I hate playing sports—or watching them. So I hid here..."

Chuckling, Remus took a seat across from the other boy, stretching out his long legs amongst the weeds. "I'm not much one for sports either. You live in Piaget House, right?"

Sam nodded. "And you're best friends with our school's team captain, aren't you?"

"Yeah, that's James. He's playing now actually."

"He's nice. Last year some kids stole my glasses at lunch... He got them back."

"Sounds like James," Remus smiled, before nudging the toe of Sam's trainer. "What's that you're reading?"

Suddenly Sam grew very nervous. He snapped the book closed, then flipped it over in his lap so Remus couldn't see. Unfortunately for him, Remus had spent his fair share in the library, hunting for answers to a very queer set of questions. He recognised the back cover as well, and the writing on the spine; Maurice.

Suddenly Remus felt terrible. Sam was biting his thumbnail, face an angry red like he'd been caught doing something he shouldn't. He stood up, like he was going to run away, and Remus reached for him.

"Sam, it's alright."

"I-I don't want to talk to you anymore," Sam stammered. "We—We're not f-friends."

"Well, that's a shame. Since I sort of hoped we were."

Sam softened then, and Remus gave him what he hoped was a comforting smile. "I like 'Maurice'," he said. "It's a good book."

"You've read it?"

"Yeah. Twice, actually."

Sam's mouth opened in shock, and Remus beckoned for him to sit.

"It's alright to be nervous, you know. Or afraid," he told him, when Sam was back to nibbling his thumbnail in the dirt. "I'd say it's normal, even. People can be mean and they don't always understand."

"My dad thinks people like... Like Maurice are disgusting. He spat on a man once because he saw him holding hands with another man."

"I'm sorry that happened," Remus said. "But not everyone's like that, I promise."

"Do you think I'm a queer?" Sam murmured.

Remus smiled softly. "Do you think I'm a queer?"

He stared at him, with those big brown eyes, and ever-so-slightly, nodded.

"And do you think I'm disgusting?"

This time Sam shook his head. Suddenly Remus felt very light.

"Sam, how would you like to come watch the rest of the game with me and my friends? I know you don't really like football, and I can't really guarantee Fiona won't be there..."

"I'll come!" Sam chirped, already shoving the copy of Maurice into his bag. Grinning, Remus stood up and together they crawled back out from beneath the stands. Sam got a good laugh after Remus narrowly avoided smacking his head against one of the beams, but by then the game's second half had already kicked off.

As they rounded the end of the stands that faced toward the great green pitch, Remus slid an arm around his young friend's shoulders.

"Hey, Sam, have you ever heard of Queen?"
