"And the others?"

"James can't sit still long enough to focus on a page. Peter... Well, Peter paints."

Tomny nodded approvingly, moving on to stare appraisingly at one of Lily's plants; a Christmas cactus she'd lovingly named 'Mary'. Watching him, Remus suddenly felt nervous. Tomny was in his flat, his home. It’d never happened before... It wasn’t as though he were suddenly worried about the nicks in the furniture, or that suspicious stain on the corner of the rug—after all, Tomny's flat had never exactly been tidy—but he wanted to impress him. He wanted Tomny to know that he’d done well for himself, and that he was happy and healthy too.

“You said you got back into town last week?" Remus asked, gingerly licking his lips. "What's kept you 'til now?”

“I’m a busy man. Hedge fund won’t run itself.” Smirking, Tomny came away from the bookshelf to join Remus on the sofa. “This s’a nice place. Nice neighbourhood. Didn’t even have to check my pockets on the way over.”

“Sirius found it. Used some of the money his uncle left him for the deposit. We all split the rent.”

"You working then?"

Remus nodded. "At a music shop over near Soho."

"Right." Tomny gestured playfully toward the stacks of records piled up around the stereo. “And your band? How're things going?”

“S'great!" Remus replied, perhaps a bit too enthusiastically. "We actually just got a residency out in South Bank right now—means we play there every week. It’s a local pub. You should drop by sometime, see us play. Bet you'd like it.”

“Bet I would.”

“You said you had something to tell me?" Remus asked, suddenly more nervous about all the talk had been of him. "Is it to do with Ipswich?"

Tomny licked his lips pensively. "It... started there, I s'pose."

"You're not going back there, are you?"

"What? Nah, don't worry. Couldn't pay me to go back to smelling like fish all day."

"Were the docks really that bad?"

"Nah, I'm just whinging." Tomny shook his head. "We mostly handled cargo, used to get boxes from countries I hadn't even heard of. A dock’s a dock, but I finally got paid summick reasonable down there, innit. Legal work even. You'd be proud, I managed to save up a bit too.”

“Save up for what?”

Tomny considered, drumming his hands lightly on his thighs. “Looking to get my driving licence actually. See about getting a car after that. I keep telling myself I’d go out and visit Doss on his little farm—his girl’s up the duff again."

"Again?"

"Yeah, but her dad's passed now so Doss's taken over everything. Bet he's going mental, what with another baby on the way and only a wife and sheep to talk to. I just reckoned that if I go out and visit enough, he'll name the baby after me.”

"Piss off," Remus snorted. "You don't want a fucking baby named after you. That's like... Well, s'like one step away from a bloody godfather."

Tomny's expression shifted, like thinly-veiled surprise, but it was gone a second later as he slumped back into the sofa with a hapless shrug. "I don't think being a godfather would be all that bad," he said, once again leaving Remus astonished.

"Shut up! Since when have you given two shits about children? No, I tell you, who are you and what have you done with Tomny?"

"I'm still the same ol' me, ya cheeky fucker. I'm jus' saying—a baby? Now that's like... gotta be some sort of miracle."

"If a baby's a miracle then a fart's a sign from the Almighty."

"So you have no interest?"

Remus scoffed; "Say some barmy idiot does name you godfather to their child—what happens if they just up and kick the bucket? Are you gonna raise 'em?"

Tomny crossed his arms. "You saying I couldn't do it?"

"No, I'm saying why the hell would you want to?"

Tomny didn't answer. Instead he turned his head to face the kitchen, the tendons of his neck strained with unease.

"Lu, I have something to tell you."

He was leaning forward to look Tomny in the eye when he realised it, and instantly Remus was abhorred.

"No," he moaned. "Please say you didn't do it."

Tomny spun around; "Now Lu, I—"

"Doss asked you to be godfather, didn't he? And you fucking went and said yes."

"Wha—? No!"

"You big idiot, Tom! Doss' parents are dead, and now according to you, so are his girl's. What happens if something happens to them? You're roped in for life now. Supporting a baby and a candy habit at the same can't be good for anyone's formative year—"

"Will you just fucking shut up?" Tomny snapped. "Doss didn't ask me to be the kid's godfather—I'm trying to tell you that I met someone!"

Remus felt like he'd been punched in the throat. For a while, no words came.

"Y... You...?"

"Her name's Skylar. She's living wiv' me, back at the flat now."

"She... Skylar..."

As if taking his stunned yammering as permission to continue, Tomny sat himself up on the couch and reached forward until he'd placed a hand over Remus' forearm. Remus watched it from far away, feeling foolish. There had always been a train of girls that followed Tomny, especially when they were younger. He was as handsome as handsome came, even compared to those who'd grown up west of Aldgate. Much to the other boys' chagrin, he had even managed to catch the eye of a few upmarket girls over the years; but the shock of hearing that he'd gotten serious—that someone else had moved in with him? It rattled that empty space in the middle of Remus' chest, the one that’d been missing its matching piece for a while.

“We's met when I was over in Felixstowe," Tomny explained, smiling in what was probably supposed to be encouragement. "She was working at one of the pubs and we sorta... got on. She’s a nice girl—think you’d like ‘er.”

Like her? How could I ever like her, she’s not—

Remus stifled the thought.

“So, she… She likes you?” He tried. Tried.

"What, like it's so hard?” Tomny grinned, squeezing Remus' arm as a comfort. "I'm only taking the piss," he said. "But yeah, she likes me. When we met she’d never even been further than Ipswich… but she ain’t thick! Lush enough to be in the pictures, innit.”

He’s bragging, Remus thought; He’s bragging because he’s proud of her.

Maybe that was what stung the most. He’d always known that Tomny would move on and find someone else, but the hole in his chest still rang hollow. It stung. Ached. Over a year it’d been, and though he'd forgotten some things, the memory was still raw. He still missed Tonya.

"And, uh, Lu...? There's one more thing."

Remus looked down again, at the hand Tomny kept clasped around his wrist. His grip was even tighter now, as though letting go might mean an escape. It was then that Remus finally grasped what Tomny had been trying to tell him all along.

Oh no.

“It's Skylar."

Please, he silently begged; Please, please don’t say it.

“She’s preg—”

“God-FUCKING-dammit, Tomny!”

Remus threw himself up from the sofa instantly, about ready to run the length of the room. Maybe the entire flat. When that didn't happen he put his head in his hands and squeezed, hoping it might wake him up from the horrible nightmare he was having, or at least pop his eardrums so he wouldn't have to hear any more. It was insanity. Tomny—with a kid?!

“You’ve got to be joking me!” Remus cried. “PREGNANT?! You went and got a girl pregnant? Are you insane?!”

Tomny quickly scooted to the edge of the sofa, holding out an arm as if he could calm him. “Hold on there, Lu. This wasn’t exactly planned, orright?”

“Yeah, that’s pretty fucking clear! Honestly, how hard is it to use a fucking condom?!”

“Fancy that. I’m ‘ere having a kid, and yet yer the one losing his shit.”

“Of course I’m losing it—you’re not responsible enough to be a father!"

"Shit, thanks for that."

"You're not old enough!"

“Not according to biology.”

“And what the hell would you know about biology, huh?" Remus spat. "I mean, christ—how long have you even known the girl?”

“We met when I got into Felixstowe.”

“That’s less than five months, you lunatic!”

“Wow—really? Didn’t realise that, since I'm clearly too thick to count!”

“CLEARLY!”

Tomny scowled then, falling back into the sofa cushions with a nasty scoff. “Whatever. Keep barking yer head off if it makes you feel better, but there ain’t nothing left for you to shout about that I ain’t already said to meself. The baby’s coming, Lu."

"Okay, so why're you here?" Remus demanded. "Why are you with me and not home with her—picking out bassinets and rubbing her feet?"

“Reckon it’s cause yer important to me,” Tomny shouted. “You fuckin’ knob!”

It took the wind out of his sails considerably, though Remus had always been a poor fighter when it came to his friends. He felt his anger crumble away, replaced by the guilt of lashing out so badly. Tomny clearly needed someone, and he’d come to him. Remus should’ve been grateful.

“Have you told anyone else?” He asked, face hot with shame.

“No,” Tomny replied, no longer looking at him. “Just you. I wanted you to hear it from me. I wanted... Well, guess it don't matter now.”

He'd ruined it then. Utterly fucking bollixed. Looking at Tomny, Remus was reminded of all the reasons why he never wanted to be a parent. After so many years of friendship, he'd just figured they were the same.

Slowly, Remus eased himself back down onto the sofa.

"I'm sorry."

Tomny grunted.

“I am. You said she…" Ugh. "So how far along…?”

Tomny spoke into his hand; “Baby’s due in April.”

“Oh... Shit.”

“Whaddya think,” Tomny murmured; "Girl or boy? Betting on a boy meself, but I hope s’a girl… Yeah, a girl would be nice.”

Remus hung his head. He wished he'd had something to drink, but Sirius wasn’t back with the beers yet—thank fuck—and so he settled for the pack of cigarettes he or one of the others must have left lying atop of the stereo. After fitting one between his teeth, he turned to Tomny and offered him his own. It took a second, but eventually Tomny turned back to him, accepting the cigarette as well as the flame Remus offered to light it. Only when the air was thick with familiar smoke, did Remus feel himself begin to ease. The fight had left him, though now he felt a bit like crying. Frustration, he realised.

“I used to think I was the one keeping you on your toes."

“You were," said Tomny glumly. "Pretty sure I have heart problems thanks to you.”

“Nah, that’ll be all the snow.”

Tomny shrugged, unable to argue.

Thumbing the cigarette filter, Remus took a deep breath. “I don’t see you for almost a year, and then you show up and drop this fucking bomb on me.”

A chuckle. “Nah, it was a bomb for me. For you... more like one 'a them cherry bombs Seesaw used to cook up in his dad's garage. He's got a job now. Working up in the Midlands in some mine."

Remus forced a smile, but it fell a second later when he turned to face Tomny for answers.

“But I thought you didn’t want kids.”

Now, Tomny turned to look at him.

“Now when did I ever say that?”

Despite expecting it, the question still caught Remus off guard.

"I just thought that..."

A beat passed, as Tomny nodded like he understood. "You're half right," he confessed, reaching forward to tap his cigarette along the ashtray sitting on the coffee table. “Maybe I didn’t picture it happening like this, but never? Nah. 'Sides, how else would I avenge them if not this way?"

"I don't understand," Remus replied; "Avenge who?"

"Us. Kids like us, anyway. Kids who—who grew up without a sod's chance in hell, because their parents had already given up."

It felt good to hear Tomny speak about them as though they were the same, but the guilt was already too heavy. Lee had made it clear the last time he'd seen him; we are not the same.

"Tom, you know you and I didn't grow up the same. Me? I don't have any right to complain. Not when you—"

"I ain't talking about fucking money," Tomny sighed. "Money may make the world go 'round, but it ain't what makes you a good dad, or a good mum. Now I know the odds aren't exactly stacked in my favour, but I figure that if I'm willing to try, then at least my kid won't be starting from nothin'. That they... Well, that they'll be better off than me."

It was an admirable thing, one that—if he were being honest—made Remus' heart twinge with envy.

"You're right," he breathed, almost a whisper. "They won't have nothing, not if they have you. You're worth more than..." Remus trailed off then, and picked up the only way he knew how; "You're my best friend, Tom. My brother."

It was as though all the anger and apprehension left Tomny all at once. His shoulders slumped, and after a sigh of relief, he leaned forward and wrapped his arms around Remus in comfort. "Oh, how I missed ya, Lu," he said, rotating between clapping and rubbing Remus' back. "I'm gon' make this work, you'll see. M’gonna get clean. No kid of mine's gonna be cleaning up after their shit-stinkin' father. And I’m gon' get my licence and join Burrin in the bookie league."

"Gambling?" Remus said over his shoulder. "You're sure that's legal?"

"Legal enough, innit. Gonna be a mess for a while—the lads are gonna be straight pissed—but my kid deserves more than a dad dealing dope out the back door. I’m just so glad I've got you on my side, Lu.”

“I’m always gonna be on your side, Tom.”

“Good.”

They held on for a while longer, simply taking it all in at their own pace. Then a thought occurred to Remus.

“Fucking wanker!" He shoved Tomny away, playfully, and then reached for his cigarettes. Grinding out the first in the ashtray, he reached for a second, and offered it to Tomny first. "What d'you think you're even playing at anyway, Doss naming his kid after you? You’re having a kid of your own, bloody name that one after yourself.”

Tomny grinned as he lit the end of his cigarette off his own lighter. “Ah," he hummed, breathing out his first puff; "but I think the world deserves a few more ‘Tomnys’, don’t chu?”

They shared another laugh, this one more genuine, and afterwards Remus bit his lip.

“Now don't go crying on me, but I just wanna say... I'm happy for you, Tom—truly. You’re going to be a great dad.”

Tomny softened then, like he’d been waiting ages just to hear those words from someone. He probably had.

“Aw," he moaned, "that's it! Come ‘ere, you!”

There was a second hug, this one much tighter than the last. As Remus struggled to keep from dropping his cigarette, he heard Tomny's words rumble happily in his ear;

"And to think, I almost asked you to be the little sprog's godfather."

Remus dropped the cigarette. It burst with orange sparks against the couch cushion before rolling off the edge and onto the floor, where it was chased by the both of them, Remus with his hands, Tomny his boot. Remus got there first, but unfortunately for him, Tomny wasn't much slower; his boot came down hard, squishing both finger and ash against the wooden floor.

"Shit, sorry!" Tomny yelped, as Remus brought a sore finger back to his mouth. He wasn't bothered; he was too distracted. And rightly so.

"Me?" Remus echoed. "You wanted me to be the godfather?"

"Well, yeah," Tomny blanched, "but now that I know how you feel about it, I wouldn't ask that—"

"You don't know how I feel."

"Uh, yeah... I think I do," Tomny said, squinting at him. "Or was your entire rant earlier just some sort of figment of my imagination? Hard sell, that. Have'na done a line in two days."

"I-I know what I said before," Remus admitted, "but what if I changed my mind?"

"You've changed your mind?"

"I dunno. You haven't asked me!"

Tomny laughed, nodding brazenly at Remus as though he couldn't decide whether he wanted to hug him a third time or bash him upside the head. Finally setting his cigarette down in the ashtray ahead of him, he scooted forward on the sofa once more, both hands clasped together in anxious enthusiasm.

"Lu, would you consider being my kid’s godfather?"

"I... Well, I'll think about it."

Tomny faltered for a moment, as though he'd been expecting a different answer and had to reel his excitement back in. To his credit, the smile never disappeared, and instead he nodded at Remus in understanding. "That's fair," he said. "I didn't think you'd give me an answer straight out anyway. You just think about it then. Reckon you got about five months."

"This is a bit mental, you know," Remus told him; "I find out I have a secret godmother and my best friend asks me to become a godfather myself all in the same year."

"Sounds like to me that yer on a roll."

"Suppose that's true too."

Tomny moved on from the baby stuff faster than Remus had expected. He regaled him with everything that had happened since they'd last seen each other. From Immingham up to Sunderland and back, it'd seemed as though Tomny had scoured half of the country's entire eastern coastline. He boasted sometimes;

"The sea was nice," he said. "You ever camped out by the sea before?"

Remus shook his head. "I've never been." Aside from that time he'd driven to Dover to rescue Sirius, that was.

"Really? Well, I'll take you. We can camp out on the sand, have ourselves a fire. You gotta be careful picking the spot though, once me and the boys had a bit too much and we's woke up with the tide lapping at our ankles."

"Only you, Tom."

And sometimes he complained;

“Bloody reeked in the mornings, before the tide came in,” he would say, “but then you started work and everything else just fell to the wayside. They use these huge cranes to get the cargo on and off the ships. By the end I was operating ‘em all on my own, and my boss? He even got me connected with a guy here in the city. Said he could get me set up with another gig soon, that’ll be great, eh?”

Remus kept on nodding, listening intently but also not at all. He was so happy to see Tomny again, but he couldn't help the fact that his brain was still wheeling.

Godfather. He could hardly believe it. It was not something he'd ever aspired to be, especially at eighteen, and especially not after discovering that he had a godparent of his own a few short months ago.

But it was Tomny, and Tomny had asked him! He'd asked Remus because there was no one else he wanted as his family's side than him. And after all that time spent wondering if he’d have just one more summer, one more day to be near him, suddenly the idea didn’t sound so bad...

The afternoon had become an early evening by the time Tomny stood up from the sofa and said that he should be getting back. Sirius was still gone, off on whatever shopping venture, and as he saw Tomny off from the door, Remus felt a sudden surge of adrenaline. The sane part of him knew that Tomny was a man of his word, and that if he said he was back for good then he meant it; yet still, Remus couldn't help the feeling. He was afraid that if he let Tomny walk out that door now, it'd be a long time before he ever saw him again.

“Hey Lu, I think you should meet Skylar,” said Tomny as he stepped out into the damp and chilly street. Pausing on the third stair, he turned back around and pulled a toothpick from behind one ear. Remus wanted to say that he was surprised by the request, but after today, he didn't think he was capable of being shocked anymore.

"You do?"

"Yeah. Like I said, she's a nice girl. And I'd like you to meet her... If yer willing."

"I'm willing," Remus nodded. "We'll get lunch. It'll be your treat."

Tomny chuffed, and fit the toothpick into one corner of his mouth. "Yeah, orright—my treat." He turned away, scooting down the last few steps. "I'll call ya then, princess! See if we's can't make a date around yer severely busy rock star schedule."

"I ain't a rock star yet!"

"Only a matter of time then!" Tomny called, saluting him as he walked backward toward the street. "Be seeing ya, Lu."

Remus almost let him go, but then a sharp wind came out of nowhere and licked up the back of his neck, and whatever metaphorical tightrope he'd been teetering on snapped.

"Tom?! One more thing..."

"Eh?"

"Yes."

Tomny squinted at him in the evening's dull light. "Yes, what?"

"I'll be godfather."

A car whipped past, cutting through a particularly nasty puddle and threatening to all but soak the back of Tomny's trousers. And it would've, had Tomny not already launched himself back up the stairs.

“Holy shit—Lu! I fucking love you!”

Spitting out the toothpick, Tomny slapped his hands around Remus' face and left a fat smooch on either cheek. He might’ve done more—like lift Remus' entire body up over his head in victory—had Remus not pushed him off first.

"I don't want you to think I'm making this decision on an impulse," he said.

"Who gives a shit about impulse?!" Tomny whooped, clapping him around the shoulders. “You said YES! Oh man—my sprog’s gonna be set for life!”

"You dick—"

"I love you," Tomny said, kissing him once more on the forehead, this time with an exaggerated mwah! "You're amazing. Bloody amazing."

Afterwards, Tomny pitched himself down the front steps, still singing Remus' praises and punching the air.

“Let’s just start with lunch,” Remus called after him. “I mean it, your treat!”

“Fucking—lunch! Yeah, orright!”

“And don’t get lost on your way home!”

"I love you! I love—you!"

"I..." Remus sighed. "I love you too."

He watched Tomny all the way to the corner, the kid about to be a dad, and when Remus finally shut the front door to the flat, he sagged against it. Bands, demos—now children?! What a fucking laugh his life was turning out to be.

Back in the kitchen, Remus drifted. He washed the leftover coffee mugs, dried them, and put them away. Then he scrubbed the sink, and after that he swept the floors, dusted every surface. He would’ve mopped, except they were out of detergent. Instead he dug around in the drawer, designated for miscellaneous rubbish and managed to find a can of 3-in-One to fix the squeaky hinge that had been plaguing one of the cupboards since they’d moved in. Afterwards he tested it, opening and closing the cupboard until the squeak inevitably faded. It felt slightly insane—manic—but he needed to be doing something. Finally Remus threw the cupboard shut; slamming the door with all of his strength. The dishes inside gave a rattle, and he swallowed the scream that was building up his throat. Tomny had only just gone, and he’d been happy for him! So why did he suddenly feel so hopeless?

Trudging back into the living room, he went first to the radio, yanking on the dial and watching as it scanned through each channel. Aside from a few comedy shows and the occasional radio personality caught mid-rave, all that was playing was the daily news summary and Radio 1’s Top 40. Remus tried to stomach it, but the national radio had been his enemy ever since he’d discovered that they limited decent music to John Peel’s late night sessions and Tommy Vance’s Friday Rock Show.

“And now it’s number thirty on—RADIO ONE, the new top forty!”

He’d turned on the radio to drown out any silence; and now to drown out the radio, Remus turned on the television. There was an advert for Pebble Mill, then some rubbish programme on cotton farming. With both noise-boxes going, he could hardly tell which was worse. X-Ray Spex or BBC1.

‘I know you’re antiseptic, your deodorant smells nice!’

“And now onto… Ajay P. Taylor looks at cotton—the fabric of an age.”

‘—I’d like to get to know you, but you’re deep frozen like the ice!’

The answer was that they were both intolerable. Curling in on himself, Remus tucked his head into the corner of the sofa and tried to let the noise sweep him away. Yet for all of Poly Styrene’s incessant bleating, he could not stop thinking about Tomny, Skylar, and the baby. Imagining the three of them living in the flat he'd once lived in with Tonya felt a lot like how it’d been to think of Sandra living at the estate. But that was stupid of course, since Sandra was his step-mother and had no babies and Tonya had only been his best friend’s girlfriend.

Remus punched the sofa cushion—Dammit! It was pathetic. Tomny had caught him by surprise, but how could this be such a problem? It wasn’t as though Remus was the one who’d run the girl up the pole. So why did it hurt so badly?





‘He’s a germ free adolescent,

Cleanliness is her obsession—

Cleans her teeth ten times a day,

Scrub away, scrub away, scrub awayyyyy!’





Curse the Queen Mother and her fucking BeeBeeCee.

There was a clatter as the front door opened, and Remus was on his feet in a second. He swung out into the hall, Sirius’ name already forming between his lips, but rather than his boyfriend, he found three girls making their way inside, nearly tripping over one another to get their shoes off.

“Hiya, Remus,” Mary said, shrugging out of a fabulous leather trench. “What’s all that noise now?”

“Nothing,” he flubbed. “I was… cleaning. Kitchen needed a scrub.”

“Did it ever,” Lily agreed, slipping past. She brought with her a large paper bag, which she set down on the dining room table. A second later the radio clicked off, and Marlene came forward with an armful of her own, this one in the form of a cardboard box. She set it aside to greet him, kissing his cheek warmly.

“No Lottie?” Asked Remus.

“Nah. She’s skipped town again to see Roger.” Marlene looked him in the eye then, and he knew she was reading his expression like a picture book. “Are you alright?”

“Fine. Had a long day.”

“Me too,” Mary interjected. “I swear this bitch of a professor at the conservatory has it in for me. Keeps singling me out in Diction lessons. Try telling her that ‘Rubber Baby Buggy Bumpers’ sounds vaguely dirty one time and it's like I’m on the bloody blacklist…”

"Mary's voice lessons aren't exactly shaping up to what she'd hoped," Marlene explained quietly.

Mary huffed; "Whatever. I'm only doing it to piss Daddy off. He's still hung up on me taking French." Without any more complaining, she flounced past the pair of them and into the living room with a box of her own. Now Remus was starting to get suspicious.

“What are those?” He asked Marlene, as she picked up her own box and carried it inside.

“Just a few things for the flat—Mary’s idea.”

“It’s just so drab in here!” Mary called, as she set her box down on the coffee table. Shrinking at the noise, she snatched up the television remote and flicked it off, clapping it into her palm as she surveyed the room. “Ugh. I knew we should’ve brought paint. This beige is simply vomit-inducing.”

“I told you, no painting. We still want our deposit back later,” Lily said, opening a third box of her own. Thankfully this one was filled with take-away.

“I thought we were going to the cinema, not redecorating,” Remus said, shutting off the radio with a flick of his hand. To him, the flat was perfect; the downstairs made up of a simple living and dining combo with wood floors and two front windows, short only a pair of curtains. Their furniture consisted of a table with six chairs, a sofa and a two-seater, along with the bookshelves, telly, and radio—plus enough albums to last them a decade. Lily’s plants had taken up most other surfaces and they’d even wrangled a dart board onto the wall that James had rescued from the local rubbish tip. Remus wasn’t sure what else there was to want.

“We’re just looking to spice the place up a bit,” Mary said, opening her box and withdrawing several plush throw-pillows. “My driver Henry will be over later with more if you’d like to help us drag them inside.”

He didn’t, only because he was in a bad mood, and so Remus plodded back over to the sofa, where he collapsed on top of Mary’s new periwinkle pillows. They didn’t match the sofa by any means, but he could already see her pulling out fabric swatches to compare.

“James is supposed to be back before five,” Lily said, while she and Marlene arranged the take-away boxes across the table. “Remus, can you go fetch Sirius?”

“Can’t. He’s gone out to the shops.”

“Oh. Any idea when he’ll be back?”

“Nope.”

“Remus, what do you think?” Mary held up her sofa swatches. “Leather or synthetic?”

He shrugged, not caring, and Mary frowned, before setting both hands on her waist.

“Oh no, you’re upset.” She tipped her head back. “Ladies, we’ve a crisis on our hands. Remus is in distress.”

“I’m not in distress,” he grumbled.

“What’s the matter?” Lily called. "Remus, what's wrong?"

“Nothing’s wrong!”

“That’s a lie,” Mary persisted. “Poor baby Remus. Having a bad day, are we?”

“Mary.” Coming forward, Marlene tossed a glare in her best friend’s direction, before gently prodding Remus’ arm. “Is there really nothing bothering you?”

“No, it’s fine. I’m totally—”

“You can tell us, you know,” Lily piped up. “Whatever it is, we won’t be upset.”

“I don’t know what you’d have to be upset about!” He snapped. “You’re not the one having the baby…”

A collective gasp went up around the room, and the girls were on him in a second—their faces pressed so close to his that Remus felt himself go cross-eyed.

“Remus, you got a girl pregnant?!”

“You cheated on Sirius?!”

“What were you THINKING?!”

“Not me!” He wailed, throwing his arms up to ward them off. “It's Tomny!”

The girls eased immediately, their expressions stunned nonetheless.

“I thought you said that he was still in Ipswich,” Lily prodded gently.

“Well, I thought he was,” Remus amended. “He came over today—said he met someone… Now I guess the girl’s pregnant.”

“Shit,” Marlene winced. “Are they gonna keep it?”

“Guess so.”

The girls exchanged a look and even began whispering to one another in hush, while Remus began bitterly picking at a hangnail on his thumb. He didn’t feel like going mental over the kitchen cupboards anymore at least, but then again, he didn’t want the girls feeling sorry for him either.

“Look, it isn't like I’m just gonna fall to... What's that look for?"

All three girls were staring at each other. Remus recognised it instantly; they were having a telepathic moment, the kind only other girls could understand. He'd seen it enough times back at school, but then he usually had one of the other lads to back him up. Now he was outnumbered.

"Mary," Lily nodded, "go get it."

With a little giggle, Mary shot across the room toward the stereo.

"Wait—what’re you doing?” Remus demanded, as the other two took his arms.

“Just come on!” Lily grinned, while she and Marlene hauled him to his feet. Across the room, Mary was rapidly flicking through the collection of LPs. When she found what she was looking for, she slipped the vinyl disc from its sheath and tossed the remaining cover across the living room with a happy shout. The cover was a diamond blue blur in the air, but Remus still understood.

Oh no...

"We know exactly what'll make you feel better, Remus," Marlene told him.

"No, please—mercy."

"This is mercy!" Lily laughed. "How can you be sad when you're dancing with your friends?"

“That's right," Mary shrieked happily, as she bent over the turntable with the record in hand; "Remember, Remus, there's an ABBA song for everything!”

“Aw, for Christ’s sake—”

"Come on, Remus, dance with us!"

"Yes, dance with us, Remus!"

He probably could’ve said no if he'd really wanted to, but they were looking at him with those big doe eyes, and the sound of Lily’s new ABBA record was already sailing out across the room from the stereo’s speakers. First the Spanish guitar, followed by rapid piano. Then the sheer embarrassment.





‘Chiquitita, tell me what’s wrong,

You’re enchained by your own sorrow;

In your eyes, there is no hope for tomorrow…’





Remus groaned, and still the girls pulled him into the middle of the living room—Marlene pushing the coffee table aside for even more space. By the next verse they were singing, and though he longed to push them away, they were smiling too big for him to bear it.





“Chiquitita, tell me the truuuuth,

I’m a shoulder you can cry on,

Yoooour best friend—I’m the one you must rely on…”





“Guys, this is embarrassing!”

“Just let it happen, Remus!”





"You were always sure of yourself,

Now I see you've broken a feather. "





Marlene grinned, and Remus shook his head adamantly.

"No, no—I can't!"

“Yes, you can! Dance with us, Remus!”

“Yes, Remus—dance!” Mary declared, returning to her box of treasures and pulling out a vibrant feather boa of all things. Remus thought himself safe when she wrapped it around her own neck, but then she pulled out a second. He all but gaped at her, and as the chorus began, she simply spun round and tossed it over his shoulders. Lily squealed, clearly ecstatic, and by then they were done for.





“Chiquitita, you and I knoooow!

How the heartaches come and they go—

And the scars they’re leaving!

You’ll be dancing once again,

And the pain will end,

You will have no time for grieving!”





They swung him about the room, feathers flying, and while Remus mourned his pride, he did not stop them. Lily held one hand, throwing it skyward, and after she swung into his chest, demanding he dip her. Remus did—and then Marlene dipped him.





“Chiquitita, you and I cryyyyy!

But the sun is still in the sky—

And shining above you!

Let me hear you sing once more,

Like you did before,

Sing a new song, Chiquitita…”





Laughter. They were laughing. It was contagious, and it went on again for an entire second verse. By the time they’d made it to the end, Remus was out of breath from letting Mary lead him around by the boa, dodging the girls’ impressive swings and kicks. He tried to sit, but they pulled him in for the final verse, draping themselves across his arms and back as though their legs had all suddenly given out.





“Tryyyy once moooore, like you diiiid befooooore!

Sing a new song, Chiquititaaaa…”





Just as he was threatening to collapse under their combined weight, the girls let out a tremendous giggle and shot upright. Holding him by the boa, they spun around some more as the music slowly filtered out. Every step and skip remained on beat, even as the front door opened and the sound of James’ warm tenor cut through the music.

“Evening, ladies! Guess who I ran into on the way home.”

“Moony, I remembered the sugar!”

A second later, James and Sirius rounded the corner, muttering something about the smell of Chinese. They stopped on the threshold, clearly surprised by the show, and while James opened his mouth to laugh, Sirius crossed his arms and sagged sulkily against the doorway.

“No fair. Why’s he always get to have all the fun?”





* * *





Later that night…





The week before, following an argument with Peter over the evening’s radio channel, Remus had gone out and spent his entire paycheque on a second radio. Sirius had had no qualms—he installed the device in their own bedroom, knocking aside one of the lamps just to fit it on their bedside. Nowadays the room was almost never silent. If one of them was home, the noise was on. Blondie, the Clash, German synth—none of it mattered, so long as it kept the quiet away. And while Remus listened to his radio, Sirius sat across the room on the cosy sofa chair they’d left in the corner, quietly plucking away at Sheila’s guitar. Working at the pub had turned him into even more of a night owl, and he claimed his best work was now written alongside the burning midnight oil. Not that Remus ever minded.

Reaching over to the radio, he turned up the volume;

“—And for those folks who are just now tuning in, that was XTC with their new single ‘Are You Receiving Me?’” The disc jockey droned; “In proper news, I see the Nipple Erectors have transmogrified themselves into simply, ‘The Nips’. I assume it’s some sort of attempt to win over the playlist committee. This device will not—I think—work, but perhaps it will get them a few more plays on the ol' airways. Before that though, we interviewed legendary producer Gaz Spectre in our studio earlier this week. Now we bring you that brief recorded clip."

Remus brought his cigarette to his lips, listening as the DJ's single voice became two;

"Now Gaz, we've talked for a while about your signed acts, but what about the future? Can you tell me, what is it Spectre Records is looking for in a fresh band?"

"Well, you know I ain't looking for any old act, John. Any plod off the street can pick up a guitar and play, what I'm looking for is a phenomenon. Someone who can just up on that stage, and make it their own. It's my job to make the music sell, anything less ain't worth my time."

"You heard it here first, folks—Gaz Spectre doesn't sign bands, he signs phenomena."

As the DJ switched back over from the record to live feed, Remus shook his head. Phenomena—what a load of shit.

"There's nothing I love more than getting legends in my studio seat," the DJ announced. "Now I'm wondering, will the Nips be that phenomena Gaz is looking for? I'll leave that up to you to decide, dear listener. The Nips, ‘All the Time in the World’, coming at 'chu next.”

Polishing off his cigarette, Remus ground the stub into the ashtray next to the bulky radio set-up and lit another, before dropping back into his pillows. Outside, the nightly rain pattered their bedroom windows while the remnants of punk shot out from the radio speakers at a moderate volume.





‘Now it’s all over, I’m sorry baby, my brains are in my pants,

You know I’ve got my eyes on you, I’m looking for a chance!

All the time—all the time!’





A baby, he kept thinking. Tomny is having a fucking baby.



‘So lie on your back and think of England, and I’ll put my hands on you,

I’ve been dreaming on your picture, baby, creaming over you!

All the time—all the time!’





“I like this one,” Sirius said. “ ‘Cream all over you’? Now that’s modern romance.”

Setting the guitar aside, he came forward, sliding onto his side of the bed like a cat. When he was close enough to reach, Remus pulled Sirius into his chest until he was spooning him from behind.

“Did you finish your song?” He murmured.

“Nah. Couldn’t quite work out the bridge.”

“I’ll help you tomorrow.”

“Mm.” Sirius grabbed his wrist, tucking the end of Remus’ cigarette between his lips and taking a long draw. He let it go a second later, and Remus watched the smoke drift up toward the ceiling and disappear.

“Got the fright of your life today, didn’t cha?” Sirius said. Not seeing a point in hiding it, Remus had since told him everything. The others as well.

“I dunno… you turning up on my doorstep last summer might still take the cake.”

“Hey, at least I called first.”

Remus smiled, and relaxed into the pillow again. Sirius took another drag, and then left tiny smoke-caressed kisses along the inside of his wrist.

“I just thought we’d have more time,” Remus said. “You know… to be kids. Yobs. I just wanted to have fun. But he’s living in another world. Always has.”

“Just because he’s growing up, doesn’t mean we have to. We’ve still got plenty of time to be yobs.”

“You’ll never be a yob, Sirius.”

“Now that’s pure classism.”

They both laughed, quietly, and Remus buried his nose in the back of Sirius’ hair.

“Guess I should get over it now. How long until you figure James and Lily are up the duff?”

“Not long at all, considering we keep nicking the condoms from their toilet.”

“You told me that you bought those!”

“It’s November—practically freezing out! You really want me to pop off to Boots’ every time you’re feeling a little bit randy?”

Remus shook his head. “You’re hopeless.”

“Probably.”

Behind them, the radio kept going.





‘ It don’t really matter what you wanna say, ‘cause I know that I’ve got—

All the time—all the time in the world to make you mine!

All the time—all the time in the world to make you mine!’





Only half-listening, Remus spared a peek downwards at Sirius. He’d stolen his cigarette now, and was smoking it quietly in the dim-lit room while Remus simply watched him, eyes trained on the trio of moles behind his ear. Just below that, the neckline of Sirius’ t-shirt had been stretched badly, revealing the cut of his collarbone. Carefully, Remus let the hand he had wrapped around Sirius’ middle trail downwards, until his fingers had slipped just beneath the shirt, brushing against his abdomen.

“Guess this means you’re not exactly feeling tired yet,” Sirius said. Remus heard the smirk in his voice.

“Are you?”

A pause for consideration, and then Sirius was flipping himself around—bringing one leg up on Remus’ other side until he was straddling him. He pushed his hair back, sucking on the end of the cigarette.

“Go on then. Take off your shirt, rock star. If you're good I'll cream all over you too.”

"Wow. How did I ever get so lucky?"





* * *

Only hours before they’d been having mind-blowing sex to the soundtrack of X-Ray Spex, and even had a gig at the Shoestring to look forward to later that evening. Aside from that, all Remus had planned for the day was a great sack of nothing. Though apparently no one had thought to tell Peter that. “Peter’s always been mouthy,” Remus replied. “You just gotta shut up every once in a while to hear him.”

Sirius opened one eye to glare at him, and then cracked a smile. “Aw Moons, I think you were drooling in your sleep again.”

He touched one finger to the corner of Remus’ mouth and Remus quickly knocked his hand away.

“You snore.”

“I do not.”

“Mhm. You snore like Mary.”

“I’m going to tell her you said that. See if she won’t claw your pretty eyes out for me.”

Remus snorted and pulled back the covers, swinging his legs over the side of the bed. He was naked save only his pants, though he hardly had to worry about that anymore. They did, but not any longer than necessary.

“Right, so what’s this about not having the van anymore?” Sirius called as they emerged on the downstairs landing. He was still pulling his shirt down over his head, but James and the others were already dressed, busy shoving pieces of toast into their mouths. Lily had about half a dozen textbooks open on the kitchen table, but she still waved good morning as they came in and offered Remus a cup of coffee.

“Dad called,” Peter said, attempting to fix his tie in the hall mirror. He never got it quite right. “He said that they’re expanding the printer’s workshop into a second location and they need the extra car to cart the supplies back and forth.”

“Marlene said she might know someone we can borrow off of,” Lily said, handing Remus his coffee. “But it’s not a for sure.”

“Guess we’re taking it on the tube,” Remus sighed. It was a sarcastic quip at best. No way they’d be able to lug all of the amps and instruments over to South Bank on foot. They’d probably be mugged before they even made it across the river.

“We could just cancel,” Peter said, having given up on the tie. “It’s only one gig.”

“No way!” Sirius whipped his head around to look at each of them. “I work at the Shoe, I know how it goes! Ray's old Saturday night group have already found themselves a new drummer now they're looking to get their spot back. We give it up and they could sweep our residency right out from under us like we did them.”

Peter sighed in relief as Lily came to his rescue, righting his tie and kissing him on the cheek. Afterwards he rounded on Sirius again, looking a lot like a bank teller in navy and white.

“Do you have any other suggestions then? Or maybe you’ve been keeping a four-wheeler tucked up in that bedroom of yours that none of us know about?”

“Aw, what? Is wittle Moony afraid of the big, bad car salesmen?”

"That's light?" James asked, glancing at the stack of texts.

Remus smiled at her, and Sirius clapped his hands together in approval.

“There then. Evans and Moony’ll go, and then you two’ll be back just in time to help ‘em shove the gear into our new set ‘a wheels.”

Sirius smirked. All ready to go, he kissed Remus goodbye and muttered a quick ‘Ta!’ slipping out the front door. Remus had already turned away when Sirius stuck his head back inside, grinning keenly.

“Oh, and Moons—make sure you get us something cool.”

"Think we should get some lunch on the way?" Lily asked. "I’m starving,"
