“Yup.”

“So how’s your brother, Remus?”

Admittedly, most days Remus forgot to give Lottie credit for her own cleverness. She had a subtle way of prying the truth from you that he’d never witnessed in anyone else. You never expected her to be listening, and yet she always was; it was exactly how she’d guessed the truth about him and Sirius in the first place. Now, over a year later, her question hit him like a train going a hundred kilometres per hour. It took all his concentration just to fasten the last button, and when he was finished she turned around again, staring at him with those big blue eyes.

“Remus, you know Petey and I fight all the time. Like, all of the time—sometimes I could bash his face into the pavement! … But he’s my brother, and I love him. I know you and Tomny are still on the outs—Lily's been keeping me up to date, you see. But seeing Regulus here with Sirius tonight, it occurred to me what a miracle that was! Like, I never thought I’d see the day when those two could reconcile their differences."

"It didn't happen overnight," Remus griped. Lottie smiled at him for it, and it was sad.

"I know you and I haven’t really spoken since Christmas," she said softly, "but I don't think you're giving yourself enough credit, love. And I just think that if Regulus could forgive his brother, and Sirius could forgive him back, then there's got to be hope for you and Tomny too.”

His first instinct was to be angry with her. Angry at her bold assumptions, at the way she so easily pried her way into his life, despite the fact that they’d only ever been friends by association in the first place. I don’t have a brother, he’d shout; You don’t know what you’re talking about! If he was really my brother he would’ve come for me by now! He would’ve picked up the phone!

But then he remembered what he’d done, and all Remus felt was shame.

“Don’t be sad, darling,” Lottie told him, reaching up to cup his cheeks. “Maybe it's the married woman in me, but it could just be time to forgive and forget.”

He refused to let her see him cry, but he did let her hug him. All five feet of her—more if you counted the hair. By the time Sirius appeared, strolling down the hallway behind them with a glass of champagne in either hand, Remus was past the threat of tears.

“LLLLLLLottie! … You still trying to steal my man? Don’t make me tell Roger…”

Remus straightened up, while Lottie placed one hand on her hip.

“Sirius Black, I do believe you’re drunk.”

“I’m not drunk, you’re just sober,” Sirius said, passing them both a champagne flute. “Why is that, by the way? It’s your wedding night—shouldn’t you be getting absolutely pissed?”

“I can’t get pissed tonight,” Lottie retorted. “It’s mine and Roger’s first night tonight together, I have to take care of myself if I don’t want to look completely revolting.”

Sirius’ mouth dropped open. “No way. You mean you and Roger have really never…?”

“Not all of us have to rely on our bodies to attract potential mates, Black.”

“Is that what you were doing then? Attracting my mate with your body?”

“Don’t be jealous.” Lottie crossed her arms, looking snidely up at Remus. “I was only showing Remus everything he’s missing.”

“Har-har,” Sirius drawled, sucking his teeth as he took back the champagne. “In that case you should know that dear Roger and all his groomsmen were talking about taking a dip in that pond out front—y’know, the one with the golf balls and all the duck shit? Yeah, suh’spect it was those six bottles of Jack that did ‘em in.”

With a huff and a curse, Lottie picked up the hem of her dress and began marching back down the hallway. Far below in the ballroom, the music had begun to slow, effectively clearing the dance floor of everyone save the more romantic couples. Remus recognised the song, probably thanks to Marlene; Bloody Bee Gees.





‘I know your eyes in the morning sun,

I feel you touch me in the pouring rain;

And the moment that you wander far from me,

I wanna feel you in my arms again…’





Sirius raised a hand, looking at him slyly. “Nice try. You still owe me that dance, Moons.”

Remus looked around. They were alone on the balcony, too high up for anyone below them to have any hope of spying.

"Might as well."

After tipping back the champagne and finishing it in a single go, Remus set the glass aside. Then he took Sirius’ hands, smiling quietly as the two of them began to sway in the middle of the hallway. He let Sirius lead, same as every other time, and the two of them stayed like that for a long while.

“Who would’a thought it, huh?” Sirius mumbled after a while. “Lottie, a born-again virgin. Not slut-shaming! I’ve always admired that tenacity of hers...”

“Love makes you do crazy things, I suppose.”

Sirius hummed, his arms tightening around Remus’ waist.





‘Cause we're living in a world of fools,

Breaking us down when they all should let us be;

We belong to you and me…’





“Have you ever thought about it… Getting married?”

Sirius’ voice was small, almost a whisper. Remus leaned his chin against his hair.

“Not really… Have you?”

“Only when I’m feeling sorry for myself.”

It surprised him for some reason. Perhaps because they’d never really talked about such a thing. They had their rings... each other. Why should some stingy official have to declare them wed for them to mean something? For Remus, it was enough to just get to stay by Sirius’ side.

“Would you want to?” He asked, a part of him reluctant. “If we could…?”

Sirius didn’t answer at first.





‘And you may not think I care for you,

When you know down inside that I really do;

And it’s me you need to show—

How deep is your love?’





“Maybe,” he said again, “if I didn’t have such a shit example of what marriage should look like.”

“And if we weren’t both men?”

“Ha. Yeah, that too...”

Remus squeezed him tighter, and they kept swaying like that for some time. Sirius smelt of alcohol, of James’ Farrah Fawcett hairspray and his own musky aftershave. He imagined them living in some house in the country, married and growing old, arguing over the television channels and whether or not they should spend Christmas at home that year or travel somewhere warmer. The picture fell apart when he began to consider kids—they were two men, and neither of them had any confidence as a father. But that was what people got married for right? To settle down, have a family… Surely the tax incentives weren’t that good.

“What’re you thinking about, Moons?”

Remus responded to the mumble with a kiss on the hair.

“You, mostly. And… something Lottie said.”

Sirius raised his head in question, and Remus knew there was no use in backpedalling.

“Do you think I should’ve tried harder to make up with Tomny?”

Clearly the question was not one Sirius had been expecting. He didn’t let go of Remus, but he stopped swaying, straightening up a bit so they could look each other in the eye.

“Do you want make up with Tomny?”

That’s the big question, innit?

“I don’t want us to hate each other forever.”

“Then I guess you have your answer.”

Well, shit.

“Maybe it’s a good thing,” Sirius said after a moment. “He asked you to be godfather, and the kid’s gonna be born this month, isn’t it?”

“Surprised you remembered.”

“Why? I have a good memory.” He smirked. “I remember everything about you.”

“Oh yeah? And what’s my favourite colour?”

“Blue, of course. Give me some credit.”

Remus smiled then, a quiet, knowing one, and then kissed Sirius deeply. By the time they’d parted, the two of them were swaying to the music again.





‘How deep is your love, how deep is your love?

I really mean to learn…’





“I don’t think I’d make a good godfather,” Remus told him. “Or husband…”

Sirius shook his head; “Moony, you great fool…”

The music filtered off, but instead of getting upset, Sirius' eyes began to tighten at the corners, in that wry, wry way of his.

“Come on then. Don't forget, you still owe me another song.”

The Next Morning…





It was only half past eight by the time Remus was awoken by the sound of someone pounding on their front door. Turning over, he nudged Sirius, who only groaned and shoved him off.

"Sirius, the door."

"Ngh... tell'm to pishh off..."

The pounding continued, and finally Remus dragged himself out of bed. They were the only ones around after James and Lily had gone home with the Potters and Peter had hopped a very expensive taxi back to Moira’s place in Stratford.

Thud! Thud! Thud! Thud!

The pounding on the door had gotten worse in the time it'd taken for Remus to get down the rickety staircase that led up to their room. Rubbing his face grumpily, he took a moment to glance about the landing. He could distinctly remember leaving the wedding at around half-past two in the morning, but after that everything was a blur. Now the flat was a mess; Regulus’ powder blue suit jacket was still lying at the base of the stairs along with several pairs of shoes and bits of a ruined bouquet. When Remus stuck his head into the living room he found the privacy sheet they’d hung for Regulus in a pile on the floor. Regulus himself was passed out on the sofa, his limbs half-dangling off of the cushions.

“Couldn’t manage the door, Edge?”

There was a grumble that sounded a lot like ‘fuck you, Lupin’ and Regulus turned over and buried himself deeper into his blankets.

THUD! THUD! THUD!

“Fucking… Christ, hold your bloody horses… I’m coming.”

Almost tripping over a stray slipper, Remus stumbled toward the door. His hangover throbbed in the centre of his forehead, and the light temporarily blinded him as it came through the textured glass. The fist pounding on the front door had quickened even more, to the point that Remus had begun to wonder if it was the London Metropolitan Police he’d be facing down.

“Whatever it was, we didn’t steal it,” he muttered to himself, before yanking the door open.

It was not the police.

“WHERE IS HE?” Patricia MacDuff hollered as she barged past Remus, straight across the entryway. “That jobby-flavoured bawbag of a wankstain—WHERE IS HE!?”

Remus almost thought he was still dreaming, but then Trish turned around and sucker-punched him in the arm and he knew he must’ve been awake.

“Where—Where is who?!”

“REGULUS!” She roared, the picture of every Scot's fury. “REGULUS BLACK, YOU SON OF PISH-HEADED ARSEPIECE—GET OUT HERE RIGHT NOW!”

“She’s been like that since Glasgow.”

Remus whirled around to find none other than Barty Crouch standing in his doorway. He looked tired and unimpressed, and was still wearing his Hawkings-regulated school coat, but before Remus could begin to wonder what the fuck Barty Crouch was doing standing on his London doorstep, Trish had stormed into the living room. A second later, Remus heard it.

“YOU!”

Sliding around the corner behind her, Remus was rewarded with just enough time to watch as Regulus shot up on the sofa, a look of utter horror in his eyes.

“Oh shit.”

“You stay there!” Trish told him. “Stay right there so I can fucking feed ye yer own lying tongue!”

It was like watching a pair of alley cats go at one another. Trish charged in, but Regulus had already leapt up from the sofa and launched himself over its armrest. They used the coffee table to incite a great game of keep-away, which would’ve been amusing had Trish not been aiming for more than a cheeky ‘you’re it’.

“You fucking cunt!” She snarled. “You absolute waste of a man! Couldn’t say nothing, could ye? Nae a word—not even a note! Just pissing off in th’ middle of the night like a fart in th’ wind!”

“I told Barty where I was going!”

“You told me you were going to a funeral,” Barty cut-in, casually coming around Remus’ side with his hands in his pockets. “Not that you were running away to join the circus.”

“How’d you even know where we live?” Remus demanded.

“Sirius writes a lot of letters,” Barty shrugged. “Followed the return address. How else were we supposed to find him?”

Gaping at the obvious betrayal, Regulus straightened up like he was going to give Barty a piece of his own mind. Too bad for him, Trish got there first.

“You jackass!” She howled, shoving him back into the sofa and promptly smacking the living shite out of him. “Do ye even ken how worried we’ve been? I should drown you in that filthy river, ye fucking bampot! M’on then, tadger! I’ll pound yer stupid face in!”

Every insult came with a fresh slap, until Remus was almost impressed with her stamina. He’d never seen anyone talk to Regulus like that before, but if anyone was going to do it, it made sense that it would be Trish.

“Moony? What’s all that bloody shouting?”

Never one to miss a dramatic moment, Sirius had appeared at the base of the stairs, his hair tangled from sleep and wearing naught but his pants. He shivered in the draft let in by Trish and Barty’s arrival and struggled for a moment while fitting one of Remus’ buttoned shirts around his shoulders. His jaw dropped when he realised what was going on, but that didn’t stop him from giving his twopence.

“Alright, what in the devil’s sweet fuck is going on down here? Someone wanna tell me what Barty Crouch is doing standing in my entryway?”

“Believe me, Black, it ain’t my choice. You think I wanted to spend my school holiday looking at your pale arse?”

“Still as unclever as ever, I see. Go on then, Crouch, maybe you’ll feel better if you kiss it.”

Sirius was puckering up when suddenly the phone began to ring, driving yet another ice-pick into Remus’ temple and igniting the beginnings of what was absolutely going to be a prime hangover. As Trish continued to take swipes at Regulus from across the couch and Sirius and Barty took turns insulting each other in the doorway, Remus slipped over to the kitchen nook and picked up the receiver. He was hoping it’d be James or Lily with a possible solution, but it wasn’t.

“Remus? Remus, is that you? It’s Sheila.”

Remus resisted the urge to groan. Just what he needed—Trish and Barty, and now his godmother come to nag. He was starting to think they’d planned this.

“Uh, hey, Sheila. Sorry, but now’s really not the best time—”

There was a crash as Trish whipped one of the couch pillows at Regulus’ head, missing by a quarter of an inch and taking out a stack of records that’d been sitting on top of the stereo.

“Those were first pressings!” Sirius wailed.

“Now what was that noise?” Asked Sheila. “Oh, never mind. Now Remus, you know I care about you, but you’ve been dragging this nonsense out for far too long and I really think that it’s time to—”

“—YOU STUPID—LOLLY-HEADED—SON OF AN ARSE-LICKER—”

“Stop fucking throwing shit at me, you loon—and stop yelling!”

CRASH!

“I AM NOT YELLING!”

Now it was Remus’ turn to duck as several magazines came whipping over his head, narrowly avoiding a cup of day-old coffee someone had left on the kitchen nook counter. He heard Sheila in his ear—"Remus, is there something you’d like to tell me?”—and just like that the words slipped out before he could stop them;

“It’s just Trish and Regulus, they—”

“A-HA!”

Oh, the irony. Remus bit down on the phone cord in exasperation as Sheila began bleating in his ear about how she knew he’d been lying the entire time.

“Is he safe?” She shrieked. “Is he healthy?! Remus, put Regulus on the phone!”

“You’re not my bloody baby-sitter!” Regulus snapped, though he’d barely gotten his words out before Trish full-body tackled him into the sofa. Behind them, Barty was making a show of wiping his dirty shoes on the rug and Sirius was caught between telling him off and egging Trish on.

“Go on, MacDuff!—Oh, piss off, would'ya, Crouch!—Atta girl, right hook! Right hook!”

“I should’ve been born an only child!” Regulus hollered, words choking off as Trish wrapped her bicep around his throat.

Then the doorbell rang.

“Remus, do you hear me?! Put Regulus on the phone this instant—”

“SORRY SHEILA, GOTTA GO!”

He slammed the receiver down, feeling like he’d run a marathon. It was obvious Trish was merely playing with Regulus now—an angry cat and her mouthy ball of a yarn—but Barty and Sirius didn’t seem to be paying attention anymore.

“I wonder who’s at the door!” Barty cackled. Sirius went to chase him, but Barty merely picked up one of Trish’s stray pillows and threw it, catching Sirius upside the head in a daze. A second later and the two had passed out of sight, veering into the entryway.

“Come on, MacDuff,” Remus sighed, reaching a hand out in an attempt to peel Trish off of Regulus before she did any real damage.

“Get her off, get her off!” Regulus was shouting. Then a yelp; “OW! Did you just bite me?!”

“You deserved it, twat-face!”

Remus stopped, his head pounding. A part of him wondered if he were to just give up, maybe he’d wake up in his bed with the realisation that it was all just a bad dream. But then Sirius yelped from the entryway and he knew it wasn’t a dream at all.

“Moony, crazy bird number two incoming!”

On cue, she came peeling around the corner into the living room with a look of pure fury on her face. Remus couldn’t believe it.

“Oh, you’ve got to be fucking joking me…”

“Where is he?!”

It was Skylar. She stormed into the living room with her blonde hair frazzled, screaming her head off and looking about nine months pregnant. Startlingly, Remus realised that she was nine months pregnant. It was April, which meant the baby should’ve been due any day—so why was she at their flat?

“Where is he?” Skylar snarled again, tearing across the living room to throw a pile of blankets off the far couch, as if whoever she was looking for might be hiding underneath. “Where is that fucking asshole?”

Even Trish and Regulus had stopped fighting. They stared at her, crammed onto the same loveseat, and Skylar paid them no mind as she went instead to the kitchen pantry, throwing the door open.

“This happen to you guys a lot?” Barty mused. Sirius scowled at him for the sarcasm and began picking his way across the living room, holding a pillow over his crotch to hide the fact that he was still half naked.

“Moony,” he hissed, “is that really—”

“Skylar.”

Remus said her name like a call and she turned on them sharply, her eyes wet and an angry red. Sirius flinched in response, but if he was expecting her leap forward and tear their throats out like an angry lioness, he’d be disappointed.

“Where is he?” She asked, her voice much smaller now. “Where is Tomny?”

Remus shook his head; “I–I don’t…”

There wasn’t time to explain further. Before anyone else could say anything, Skylar burst into tears.

Chapter 104: Noise


Chapter Summary

“You’re not worried about sounding awful?”

“Oh, I’m worried, but there are worse things than sounding awful.”



Chapter Notes

CW for this chapter: violence including threats and knives, but also a lot of general tomfoolery. The word "ponce" is repeatedly used. Remus is sorta sad, then really happy (!!!), then sorta sad again, lol.

Also, for those of you more interested in the music aspect of this fic (that being following along with the "vibes" of certain musical scenes) you're probably going to want to play THIS when Rat Scabies starts asking for a 'sacrifice'. It's personally one of my fav live versions of the song xoxo

We met when we were in school,

Never took no shit from no one, we weren’t fools;

The teacher says we’re dumb,

We’re only having fun;

You know, we piss on everyone,

In the classroom…

- “Stay Free” The Clash, 1978



Back when they were young and decidedly less queer, Remus had attended an Easter supper at Marlene’s house as her boyfriend. Marlene’s eldest brother John had been newly married and was just expecting his first child. Remus had only met the McKinnons the one time, but he remembered John’s small wife—her stomach ballooned to the point of obvious discomfort. She’d looked positively ill that day, like the smallest breeze might topple her. Marlene had talked his ear off beforehand about how pregnant women experienced a variety of horrific symptoms, including the type of hormones that tended to cause wild mood swings. At the risk of sounding like a misogynist, Remus had simply nodded along with little fuss, but now he wished he’d asked a few more questions. Namely, what to do when your ex-best friend’s girlfriend shows up on your doorstep nine months pregnant and won’t stop sniffling into her tea.

It took several minutes for him to become convinced that Skylar was not, in fact, at risk of having a "stress baby" on his living room floor. Sirius and the others had already cleared out, and the two of them were able to sit down on the ratty sofa seats to talk. Remus almost felt like pinching himself. After their first disastrous meeting in Whitechapel he’d been pretty sure that he would never be seeing Skylar again. But then again, fate had always been a bit ironic like that.

“It’s been five days,” Skylar said, her voice more than a little raspy from crying. “How could ‘e not come home? My due date’s in less than two weeks, and this arsehole ‘finks it’s alright for ‘im to go on a bloody bender.” She rubbed her face with one hand, moaning in frustration. Meanwhile Remus had never felt more awkward in his life. A part of him wished Sirius had stayed behind to play mediator, but between Trish and Regulus’ spat and the hangovers they’d both woken up with, he and others had peeled out of the flat so quickly Remus wouldn’t be surprised if they’d left skid marks on the front rug.

“So when you saw him last, Skylar—”

“Call me Sky, right,” she whined, pathetically blowing her nose into a kitchen flannel.

“Right… Sky…” Remus took a deep breath. “When you last saw Tomny, was he using?”

She shook her head no, then her face twisted in pain again. She shrugged miserably. “Oh, I dunno! We fought so much about it I ‘fink he just started to hide it. But he’d been clean for two months before all ‘a this.”

Remus scratched awkwardly at the side of his neck. Clean or not, Tomny’s entire life had been uprooted. He’d given up his work, the money, friends… Everyone needed a vice, and Remus was hardly the one to judge.

“Did he say he was leaving? Going somewhere, maybe?”

“No, 'e just left. We had a fight, sumfink about work—and he stormed out.”

“Well, Tomny’s got a lot of friends, you know. He could’ve easily gone to theirs to cool off. He used to do that a lot, back when we were younger, right? Sometimes he’d get drunk and just go home with other people. You know, crash at theirs.”

“For five days?”

“Well, if it was a girl—”

“Yer saying Tomny’s off in some uvv’er girl’s bed?”

Remus winced, pinching the bridge of his nose. “No… No, he’s not like that.”

“I just don’t get why this’s so hard for ‘im,” Skylar went on. “I had ter give up drinking—and smoking! My entire body’s been fucked over by this, and all he’s got to do is be there. Why's that so hard?”

Now Remus really wished the others hadn’t left. He let her go on for a bit longer, and when it was clear she’d run out of steam, he offered her a real tissue. Skylar mumbled her thanks.

“You look nice,” he said instead, trying not to stare too long at her stomach. “Is the... baby healthy then?”

“For the most part.” Skylar glanced down at her stomach, stroking it gently. “Had a few rough months wiv’ the morning sickness but Tomny took me in for all them scans, right, ‘n’ the doctor said everything looked awright. He missed the last appointment though. Now I’m just ready for all of it to be over.”

Remus nodded, then; “Skylar, how did you know where I lived?”

She sipped her tea, eyes dry for the time being. “Tomny thought it would be smart to keep a list of emergency numbers on the fridge. O’course, it’s only got yers, un'all. I know you two haven’t been talkin' but I figured that if he was going to hide out anywhere it’d be ‘ere.”

Her words were like a stone sinking in his gut. It made Remus look down at his hands, and as he did so Skylar clutched her baby belly tightly.

“You don’t ‘fink sumfink’s happened to him, do you?”

“What? No way.”

"—'Cause I’ve literally been going out ‘a me mind."

Remus shook his head, adamant. “Tomny’s resourceful. I’ll bet… Well, I’ll bet he’s just too ashamed to face you right now. He’s probably out there beating himself up over it.”

Skylar scowled like she’d like to have seen it for herself, but Remus' palms were already sweating. He thought that when he’d finally be doing this, that the one he’d be facing down would be Tomny, but as it was Tomny was nowhere to be found, and he owed Skylar an apology.

“Skylar.”

She raised her head.

“I just wanted to say that I’m sorry for… For what I said in the cafe. It was completely out of line. I–I don’t know why I acted like that, I just… Shit, I…”

“Tomny said that youse were different. Not like, different–weird, but that you didn’t judge, d’you know what I mean?” She pursed her mouth, looking toward Sirius’ stack of toppled records. “He wouldn’t talk to me about it afterwards, but I know he felt judged. I ‘fink you let ‘im down. Slated, innit.”

Remus nodded mutely, biting down on his bottom lip to keep it from shaking.

“I think something’s wrong with me,” he said eventually. “I think something was wrong with me that day, and I… Well, I took it out on you and Tomny.”

“Ain’t that the wey.”

Neither of them said anything more for a while, and Remus got the feeling that Skylar wasn’t all that interested in comforting him. Fair enough, he thought; he probably wouldn’t have felt like comforting him either. As he went on quietly moping, Skylar wrapped an arm around her stomach and winced.

"D'you mind?" She gestured to the room. "Walking's easier on my back. O'course if it ain't my back it's my feet..."

Remus beckoned her on, and she hauled her large stomach up from the chair and began wandering about the room. Perhaps this was just her way of snooping, Remus didn't care. He was busy racking his brain for anywhere Tomny may have gone. Doss was living in Cardiff now, and as far as Remus knew, Seesaw was still in the Midlands. If Lee was to be believed, then Tomny had quit the gang, which meant those bridges were all ash and dust now. Shit... Vint? Donna or Cheryl maybe? No—no way Tomny was prick enough to go back to an ex-girlfriend with Skylar in such a state. Maybe he'd gone to Burrin then. He was his full-time boss now, but Tomny had never even let Remus meet the guy, let alone tell him where he lived. Suddenly it was looking like finding Tomny was going to be about as easy as finding a chipped brick in a council flat.

Dammit, Tom...

“I know that one.”

It took Remus a few seconds to catch on. At that point Skylar was already setting her cup of tea aside and picking up one of the albums Sirius had left in a cluttered pile next to the radio. Harvest, by Neil Young.

“My dad used to play this for me when I was little. This one—" She pointed to the track list; "He'd sing it for me 'n me mum."

Remus got up from his chair. “It belongs to my friend James,” he explained. “His dad likes Neil Young too... Would—Would you like me to put it on?”

She considered, then nodded and passed it along to him. Slipping the record from its sleeve, Remus had just about set up the needle when Skylar gave a short groan and bent over at the middle. Instantly Remus was panicking.

“A-Are you okay? Should I call an ambulance?” He’d dropped the needle’s arm in his surprise, causing a harsh scratch and effectively starting the album mid-song.

“No, no, ya melt, m'fine,” Skylar grumbled. “Baby’s just kickin’… Ugh, I swear, the bleedin’ wee shits know exactly where your kidneys are. Bloody ‘ave to piss ev’ry five minutes. Ain’t it enough that I’m riskin’ being ripped ass to twat?”

Remus looked away, trying not to grimace. Several deep breaths later, Skylar had righted herself and was running her hands along her stomach soothingly.

“Tomny always jokes that the kid’s gonna be some pro-wrestler or sumfink. Should’a seen him the first time ‘e felt the babe kick.”

Just please don’t ask me to feel your stomach, Remus thought drearily. Luckily Skylar didn’t seem to have any interest. They stood next to each other for a while, listening to the song. It was a nice one. Eventually Skylar began to hum along.





‘I’ve been to Hollywood,

I’ve been to Redwood;

I crossed the ocean,

For a heart of gold…’





“Say, Remus?”

“Yeah?”

“You should know that your ‘ouse is a bit of a mess.”

“Oh, well, we weren’t exactly expecting guests.” Remus glanced around at the cluttered living room, then down again, to where Skylar was still stroking her belly.

“More tea, Sky?”

“Ah nah, whisky on th’ rocks for me, thanks.”

She smiled, and Remus finally began to feel himself relax.

A short while later the record had run out and Tomny had still not shown up, and so Skylar took that as her cue to leave. Remus had managed to flag down a taxi for her and even held her hand as she hobbled down the front steps of their townhouse. After helping her into the back of the cab, Remus handed the driver a few quid for the ride and stepped back to her door, peering in on her anxiously.

“You’ll call me if he turns up, right?”

She nodded. “Cross me heart.”

He thought he should say something that might comfort her in return, and so while white-knuckling the edge of the open taxi window, Remus did his best to smile.

“I wouldn’t worry much, Sky. Tom can’t keep away from home long anyway. Likes his flat too much.”

“The flat? No, didn’t you know, we—” She caught herself. “Oh, that’s right, you wouldn’t have known.”

His expression must’ve given away his unease, because Skylar rushed to console him.

“We moved, Remus. Back in January. We’re up in Hackney Wick now… But it’s a nice place. Tomny didn’t want to go too far, and I couldn’t very well force him to leave outright. He takes the car out to the track at Kempton Park for work. At least he was… Anyway, there’s a lot of young families in our building.”

“Have you been back to the flat then? Maybe he went there.”

“O’course I went to the flat,” she replied, sounding irritated now. “Tomny told me ‘e passed the lease along to a friend after we moved out, but no one ever answered the door.”

Remus swallowed. Tomny may have been a better guy than most but even he wasn't above lying. He could've easily passed the lease on to someone he knew like he'd told Skylar, or he could've been using the flat as a place to hide out. It worried him, but Skylar was nine months pregnant. She shouldn't have to be wandering around dodgy East London council estates looking for her missing boyfriend.

“I’ll go. Maybe they just weren’t home.”

“You’d do that?”

“For Tomny? Anything.”

She cupped his cheek. Her hand was warm.

“You know, I wasn’t sure at first, but I think Tomny just might have been right for asking you to be godfa’vver.”

His breath caught, but she’d already released him. Slowly Remus stepped back onto the curb. “Make sure she gets home alright," he told the driver, who honked his horn while pulling away. At the last second, Skylar stuck her head out the window.

“Remus, if you see Tomny, you send him home!”

“I will," he called. "Call if you need anything, Sky. I-I mean it!"

She smiled, blonde hair whipping around her face.

“By the way, it’s a girl!”

She was still waving by the time the cab rounded the street corner and disappeared, leaving Remus stunned and speechless on the curb. It seemed Skylar was getting quite good at that.

A girl… It's a bloody girl!

His palms had begun to sweat again by the time a series of loud honks were echoing up the street. It was Sirius driving their beloved purple Minnie-van. He pulled the VW up to the curb and jammed the gear stick into park.

“So that was Skylar then?” He called, rolling down the passenger’s side window so that Remus could hang his arms inside. “Seems like a nice girl. And you were so nasty to her. Tsk—tsk, Moony.”

“Call me an arse,” Remus sighed. “ ‘Least I got to apologise.”

“Yeah? So you mean she didn’t totally bite your head off?”

“More of a light nibble really. No less than I deserved...” Remus watched as Sirius scooped up a packet of cigarettes from the centre console. “Where’d you get off to?”

“Oh, only took these wankers for a little joyride. Managed to pick up a few things too.”

Just then the van’s side door opened and Trish stuck her head out, clutching a fat spliff between two fingers. “Look, Loonarny! Real London-grown weed!”

He heard Regulus groan—“Bloody hell, MacDuff!”—and Trish was unceremoniously dragged back into the van before anyone off the street could see or smell her.

“Say,” Sirius smirked, lighting his infinitely more legal cigarette, “I was thinking—we could take these kiddos somewhere fun and normal like, oh, I dunno—back to Portobello Road and the like. Or... we could show ‘em what the real London underbelly looks like.”

“You don’t know what the ‘real London underbelly’ looks like, you toff.”

“I know enough, inn–it,” Sirius said, teasing. Remus leaned his chin on the edge of the van’s window.

“What’d you have in mind?”

“Saw in the paper that The Damned are doing a show over in Camden tonight. S’not too far outta the way. I already rang Prongs and Wormtail and they’re in, and MacDuff over there seems eager enough too, so whatcha you think? Crouch and shithead can wait outside if they’re not interested.”

A cry came from the back seat; “Fuck off, Black! We ain't waiting outside for your freak show to be over!”

"Zip it, Crouch, or I'll drive you over to Whitehall and dump your miserable arse. See if Crouch Sr. is looking for a visit."

At Sirius' threat, Barty flipped him the bird but did begrudgingly sit back in his seat, both arms crossed in defiance. Next to him, Regulus appeared unbothered, slowly flipping through one of Sirius' old NME magazines. Dave Vanian of The Damned was on the cover, rubbing a piece of raw meat into his eye.

"So, what d'ya think?" Sirius pulled a pair of sunglasses down from the van's visor. "I know them 'no wave' folk dress a bit like if your gran started snorting heroin through a chimney pipe but if we can handle the Sex Pistols then I reckon we can stand embracing some of their nihilism for a single evening. You?"

Remus shrugged meekly. “Yeah, Sirius sounds fun… but first, I—uhm…”

“Aw no,” Sirius sighed, tipping his head back against the seat. “I know that look. You’re about to do something stupid, aren’t you?”

“And just how is it you always know when I’m about to do something stupid?”

“I just do. You get this depressed little line in the middle of your forehead.”

“I do not.”

“Sure, you do. I can see it right now.”

Sirius flicked his cigarette carton at him, effectively knocking Remus upside the head with it. Remus chuckled, though it fell off toward the end, growing rather unenthused. Afterwards he picked up the cigarettes and began tapping one loose while Sirius smiled at him, knowingly.

“What’s going on, Moons?”

“If…" Remus gnawed on the end of the cigarette; "If I said you were right, and told you that I did want to do something completely stupid, what would you say?”

Sirius paused to consider. “Can we still go to the concert later?”

“If I survive, sure.”

“Right. In that case, I’m driving.”

"... Really?"

"Why not? It's like I already said—nihilists for an evening, yeah? And if life's already meaningless then I suppose there's no point in worrying how badly you're about to fuck ours up."

Remus reached for the van’s door handle. "Christ." Thank god for Sirius Bl—

“Black, can we hurry up with this stupid venture of yours?” Barty called from the back of the van. He’d pulled a stray beer can out from beneath his seat and was dangling it in front of his nose like a dead rat. “This car of yours—if you can even call it a car—is foul. I mean, where did you find it? A scrapheap?”

“Got it from your mum actually, Crouch,” Sirius drawled, adjusting the rear-view mirror. “Shall I tell you what I did to pay for it?”

Barty sneered, sticking his tongue out whilst tossing the can over his shoulder. “Still smells like ass back here.”

“That’s ‘cause you’re sitting in the same place Moony and I had sex last week.”

“Is that right?” Barty turned to Regulus, clearly delighted. “Shit, Regulus—you never told me your brother’s a poof!”

“You never asked.”

Whatever comeback Barty was expecting to give died before it even reached his lips. He glanced at Sirius—smug—then back at Regulus, who was still ignoring him in favour of his magazine. It took a cheeky brow-raise from Trish for realisation to begin dawning on Barty's face.

“You… You mean you and—you and… huh? ”

“Cat got yer tongue, bawbag?” Trish sniggered.

“You—and-and him—and—HUH?”

“Don’t tell me you’re prejudiced, Barty,” Sirius asked innocently. "Not after crushing on Lupin for all these years."

“Fuck off, I ain’t prejudiced, I just hate you! And you—” He pointed at Remus; "You—You fuck off too!"

Remus put his hands up. "What'd I say?"

"Is it true, bawbag?" Trish gaped at Barty.

"No! Now everyone just fuck off!"

"Tsk. He must be prejudiced."

"I ain't!" Huffing and red-faced, Barty gave Regulus a nervous glance. “I-I ain’t! Ugh… stupid—ngh... Fucking tosser...”

“Well." Sirius paused for a moment to yawn and stretch dramatically in the front seat; "Glad we’ve got that sorted. Now if you guys don’t mind, I prefer a bit of music while I drive.”

He began punching several dials on the radio, and suddenly Radio One’s top hits were pouring out of the speakers.





'You disturb my natural emotions,

You make me feel like dirt and I'm hurt...'





“That’s one way to tell someone you’re fucking your best friend,” Remus mumbled over the music, sliding into the passenger’s seat and shutting the door after himself.

“What can I say? I like being efficient.”

"I don't remember you being so 'efficient' when we were telling James."

"Hm, really? Don't recall. Must've been some other totally gorgeous knockout with black hair."

"Riiiiight."





'And if I start a commotion,

I'll only end up losing you and that's worse...'





Sirius dropped the pair of sunglasses down over his eyes before putting the van into gear. “Best put on those seat belts, kiddies," he said, "I’ve been known to be a bit of a wild card behind the wheel. Just ask, Moony.”

"Aye. Seems like there's a few things I'd like to ask him," observed Trish keenly.

Jamming on the horn a few times for good measure, Sirius grinned as he peeled back out into the motorway. In the backseat, Remus overhead Trish offer Barty a hit of her spliff, which he almost dropped into his lap upon realising;

“Wait… you... YOU MEAN YOU REALLY DID IT BACK HERE?!”





'Ever fallen in love with someone—

Ever fallen in love, in love with someone?

Ever fallen in love, in love with someone—

You shouldn't have fallen in love with?!'





As Sirius drove, Remus imagined all the ways what he was about to do could go terribly wrong. If, by some miracle, he did manage to find Tomny at the flat, what would he even say? I’m sorry, obviously, but then what? Go home? Cut the shit? Be the dad you promised you were gonna be? Remus wasn’t sure he had the right to say any of it. Where had he been these last months—not with Tomny. Tomny could sock him in the face and slam the door and Remus would still deserve it. But at least this way he could tell Skylar he'd tried. And fuck—that her boyfriend was bloody alive.

They were passing through Spitalfields, the radio’s usual midday disc jockey droning on, when Barty thrust his finger against the van window in awe.

“Oh man, look there! Manky old bloke's passed out on the pavement. Reckon he’s dead?”

“Have some respect, Crouch,” Trish snapped.

“Alright, if you’re so genuine why don’t you hop out and go help him? I’m sure he’d just love gutting a little girl.”

“I’ll gut ye, bawbag, if you don’t shut it!”

“Enough,” Remus called. “None of you are getting out. You’re staying right here.”

“What? You mean you drag us all the way to scrub-central and we’re not even allowed to leave the car?”

“That’s right, Crouch,” Sirius said, adjusting the radio’s volume. “Your boney arse isn’t leaving that seat, ‘least not until Lupin’s finished whatever business he's got with that big brother of his.” He glanced sideways to give Remus a wink, before turning the van onto Whitechapel’s Commercial Road. From there Remus had to give him directions. When Sirius finally pulled the purple VW van up to the curb, Remus felt his heart lodge itself in his throat. Of course nothing about the building had changed; still the same scuffed white brick, single-paned windows, rusted gate barely hanging onto its hinges.

“This is where your brother lives?”

“Bawbag, what’d I just say!”

There was a hiss as Barty took another one of Trish’s smacks to the shoulder, but by then Sirius was already undoing his seatbelt.

“Right. You twats stay here, Moony and I are gonna get this done and be right back. If you’re good, I might even say yes to a stop at Wimpy’s on the way home.”

Sirius blew the three seventeen year-olds a kiss as he opened his driver’s side door, but by then Remus was already gripping him by the elbow.

“What're you doing?”

“I'm coming with you, obviously," Sirius scoffed.

"No way."

"Yes way—you can't go alone. Don’t worry, I won’t crowd you while you’re talking to Tomny. I just wanna see inside.”

Quickly, Remus reached past Sirius to tug his door shut.

“Sirius, stay in the car.”

His tone ignited a fierce stare off, the kind that Sirius’ natural-born stubbornness usually won him, but Remus was unyielding. If coming there was only going to blow up in his face, then he didn't want Sirius to be anywhere near the blast radius.

“I won’t be gone long,” he told the others as he got out. “Just keep an eye out, and make sure you lock the doors and all that.”

“Don’t forget to watch the mirrors too,” Barty added snidely; “Don’t want anyone syphoning our petrol.”

The gate creaked as Remus pushed it open. There was a woman sitting on her ground floor balcony as he approached the intercom, smoking a cigarette and peering at him over the top of her newspaper. When Remus pressed the buzzer there was no sound.

“Squawk-box’s busted, lad,” said the old woman. “Door’s open, 'ead on in.”

“Thanks,” replied Remus, nodding his head at her kindness. He found the building’s door left ajar just as she’d said, propped open with a small brick. It let in a terrible draft, though upon reflecting the building had never been particularly well insulted in the first place.

Tomny’s place was on the second floor, flat 3. The door had once borne a brass plate indicating it as such, but now—like the VW’s missing hood ornament—all that was left was a faded outline of where the numbers used to be. The door was locked.

“Tom…?” Remus knocked lightly, his stomach in knots. “Tom, are you there? Is anyone…" Fucking hell. "It’s Remus. Tom, if you’re there, let me in.”

There was no answer, and after several long seconds of silence, Remus considered turning away.

Then he heard it; a soft creak of a floorboard.

Someone was inside.

“Tom!” He began battering the door with his fist. “Wake up! Tomny, I don’t care how pissed off you are at me—did you know I saw Skylar? Yeah, she came to mind, you bloody oaf! Open the door and I’ll explain everything. You—You know I can pop the lock... Oi, tosser! Don’t make me force my way in!”

Again, no answer. He was starting to get frustrated. Surely if it was some stranger they’d have told him to piss off already.

With nothing else to do, Remus began rifling through his pockets for something to use on the lock. Before he'd even finished a thought occurred to him, and against all hope he reached his hands up to the top of the door frame. He didn’t even know if they would still be there; it’d been Doss’ idea to leave them behind. He’d placed them there for safe keeping. Remus had been too short to reach then.

He wasn't too short now.

Ting! T-Ting!

The paperclips hit the tips of his fingers and bounced off the frame’s edge and onto the floor. Both were rather rusty, the steel corroded from years of disuse, but when Remus tested their strength against the pads of his thumbs, the metal held.

“I’m coming in, Tom!” He hollered, already pinching them into shape with his teeth. It was like muscle memory now—the first lock he’d ever popped. It took less than thirty seconds.

Remus pushed the door open.

“Tomny? I know you're here..."

He was still hopeful when he found the lights on, but walking inside—there was no one. All the usual stuff was there; the dingy couch, Tomny’s recliner, even the telly. It was dirtier now than it had been when half a dozen guys had been living there, but at least Remus figured that the old furniture meant that at least someone familiar was still around.

He regretted being right the moment the door shut behind him.

“I told you that if you ever came back here I’d kill you.”

The door bolt slid home with a deafening click. The feeling of hungry eyes on his back—yeah, Remus imagined this was what it felt like to be hunted. When he turned around he did so slowly, hands raised to show him that they were empty. Unfortunately for him, Lee’s were not.

“I warned you,” Lee said, his voice reedy and thin. He had a small knife trained on the middle of Remus’ chest and was using his free hand to steady his dominant arm as it trembled in mid-air. The blade was shorter than his thumb, but long enough to do some damage, though the look on his face was twisted in pain.

"Lee—"

Lee thrust the blade forward threateningly.

“Have to hand it to ya, Lu, you always were a stubborn cunt.”

“I wouldn’t have come back if it weren’t important,” Remus said, slowly licking his lips. “I’m only looking for—”

“Tomny, I know,” spat Lee. “You think I didn’t hear you screaming yer head off in the hall? Fucking bastard… It’s always Tomny wiff you, innit. You’re like a bloody parrot the way you get on. S'always Tomny this, Tomny that—Tomny, Tomny, Tomny, Tomny!”

Lee moved sporadically, ambling forward several paces and slicing the knife through the air with short jerky motions as if he were punctuating every word. It didn't feel totally intentional, but Remus did have to jump backward to avoid letting the last one slicing through his chest. By then he’d been driven back far enough that his legs hit the coffee table, rattling a large crystal ashtray that looked as though it’d been lifted from one of those fancy cigar bars in Fitzrovia.

It was hard not to panic. Lee was blocking the door and the only other escape route was the balcony—and that was only if Lee didn’t catch him first. Even if he did manage to make it there; even if the door was unlocked, they were on the second floor! At best he’d scratch himself to ribbons on whatever dead bramble bushes grew beneath the balcony—at worst he’d break both ankles, possibly his neck. Though, Lee would’ve probably found that quite agreeable right about now.

“Are you even listening to me?” He wailed, swiping at the air with his knife, barely an arm’s length between them now. “God, you never fuckin’ listen!”

“Lee, put the knife down. You—You don't mean this."

"Shaddup! You ain't gonna tell me what it is I mean! You think just 'cause it's us two that I won't do it? Fucking toff—I warned you!"

"I know," Remus said, struggling to keep his breath even, "but I swear, Lee... If you let me go now, you’ll never have to see me again. I’ll never come back here, I’ll disappear.”

“As if I’d believe a liar! As if I’d believe someone who only ever lied to me!”

Desperate, Remus glanced around for another exit—another chance. All he found was a filthy living room and empty beer bottles. Lee had a cut on his cheek that had healed badly, no doubt the result of a fight. Seeing the cut and how its scabbed surface pulled at the skin, Remus was reminded of his own run-in with trouble, all those summers ago.

"Alright," he gulped, "so don't believe me now—I know you can't, that's fine. Don't believe the things I told you—believe the things you know!" Remus touched the side of his nose, where he knew his faded scar still split his face like a crack in the pavement. "You knew me when I got this. You knew me! I was fifteen and we were friends—you were my friend, Lee. I loved you, and I loved Tomny and he loved us both... And you—you and me? I would've followed you anywhere, mate!"

"You're not my mate!"

"No, but I'm still your Lu!"

For a split-second, Lee's knife dropped. Remus felt it in his bones.

"Please, Lee."

"I didn't ask you to beg."

"I'm doing it anyway."

The knife fell another several centimetres, and slowly Lee straightened up. He was glaring at something—his scar, Remus realised.

"You say you're my Lu? But who's that, huh? I dunno a Lu... All's I know s'a lying bastard named Remus Lupin."

"No—"

"You're a liar. There never was a Lu. Not really."

Remus shut his eyes. He felt like he'd been cleaved in two.

"I loved you, Lee."

"Liar."

"—I lied, but I still loved you. I swear, I did. I made you feel sorry for me so that you’d let me into the group, and I went on letting you believe it because… well, ‘cause it was easier than admitting that I was any different.”

"You're not 'different'," Lee hissed. "Different’s growing up sleeping in front of the oven ‘cause your piece of shit dad gambled away that month’s electric money! Nah, yer a fucking prick—you only ever been mollycoddled! You don't know what it's like to be different!”

Remus grit his teeth. “You’re right… but for what it’s worth, I’m sorry anyway.”

A hand shot forward, fisting the front of his jacket viciously.

"Don't you get it?!" Lee screamed. "I don't want your sorry! You can't just make up for your lies by being fucking sorry!"

Remus had nothing to say. Lee was right. He'd lied, and these were the consequences.

For a while Lee’s expression was no more than fury. He was breathing hard enough that shoulders drooped by several inches each time he exhaled and spit covered his cracked lips from all the swearing. Remus wasn’t fool enough to think he was safe, but when Lee finally released his shirt, he felt his chest give a lurch of relief.

“You say yer lookin’ for Tom?” Lee asked, sucking his teeth. “Well, he ain’t ‘ere. Ran out on us jus’ like you did, innit. Wanted a better life for him and that stupid girl of his.”

“Skylar’s pregnant. He only meant to—”

“Don’t care. ‘Cause you see, this—” and he raised his arms, indicating to the rest of the flat; “this s’as good as it gets fur’ the rest ‘a us. Every’fin rots in the End.”

He wanted to deny it, but Lee had never been the kind to look outside of his own means. He felt safe in the familiar and had clearly made a name for himself the same way Tomny had. Reality was that he didn’t want anything Remus could offer, he was just a sad boy mourning the things he'd lost. At least there, Remus could relate.

“I’m sorry, Lee,” Remus said stupidly, feeling a lump form in his throat. “I’m sorry everything’s gone.”

For a moment it almost appeared as though he’d gotten through to him. Lee stared back at him and for a moment his eyes were clear again; but quick as the change came, it was gone. Lee tipped his head forward, and this time when he raised the blade he pressed it to Remus’ throat.

It hit like a train—I’m a ponce—and like a vicious reminder, the knife stung his throat.

“Go on, Lu, say it!”

I’m a ponce.

“Would you rather me gut you? Is that it?”

"No."

I’m not a—

I said, I'm not a—

Remus had felt the words leave his mouth. When they did, Lee's face turned to stone.

The knife bit deeper.

I'm—

I'm King of the Dock.

It was like Lee’s eyes had glazed over. Maybe it was relief.

“Ya hear that? Them’s my mates. They're 'ere, looking out. Whatchu think—I give you tah them? There won’t be enough left for yer boys to bury.”

Just a little more—

So close—

The guys outside were pounding on the door now. In a few seconds they’d be throwing their entire weight against it and it'd be game over for Remus. Nearby Lee was on his knees, clutching his head in both hands. He was bleeding.

“Moony, what the hell are you doing?!”

It was Sirius again. He stood in the middle of the front garden, waving his hands erratically.

"It was Lee!" Remus shouted back. "Tomny isn't here."

"I figured when I saw those skinheads go inside." Sirius shielded his eyes with one hand. “You should jump!” He shouted. “Go on, I’ll catch you!”

There was no time to argue. As the balcony door strained, Remus went to the railing and leaned over. He was fifteen—maybe twenty feet off the ground. If he managed to get himself over the railing and dangle from the bottom then he might’ve been able to half that—except Lee's mates didn’t seem all that interested in waiting. So, Remus did what any reasonable eighteen year-old facing certain death would do.

He jumped.

Someone must’ve been watering the bramble bushes; they weren’t nearly as thorny as he was expecting when he landed. In fact, they were more like shrubs than anything, but that didn’t stop Remus from flattening them as his entire body came crashing down from above. Sirius was on him in a second, peeling his battered body out of the foliage with a single sharp tug.

Remus hissed in pain. “Shit! What happened to fucking catching me?”

“I panicked!”

“Bloody f—uuuuuck!”

“Quick, before those new friends of yours start thinking they can survive a jump like that too.”

With Sirius’ help, Remus began hobbling his way across the lawn. The old woman from earlier was gone, but the front gate was open. As they neared it, the van’s side door slid open and Trish and Barty leapt out, urging them onwards with frantic arms.

“Hurry! Hurry! The damn lunatic’s right behind you!”

It was like Remus’ stomach had shot back into his throat. Behind them, Lee had flown out the flat’s front door like an animal. Practically foaming at the mouth, his shirt was stained with blood and a vein bulged intensely in his forehead.

“LUUUUPIN!" He howled, brandishing his knife; "I’M GONNA KILL YOU!”

“Fuck this!” Sirius yelped, practically dragging Remus toward the gate himself. “Reg, start the bloody car!”

There was no time to be astonished. Sirius’ grip on his arm was like a vice, and Remus could feel Lee at their backs even as they ran. Ahead of them, Trish and Barty scrambled back inside the van, reaching for anything they might be able to use as a weapon. When they'd reappeared, Barty had an empty beer can in either hand while Trish weilded the end of a broken mike stand.

“RUN!” They shouted, clearly terrified. "RUN, LUPIN—RUN!"

Even injured, Remus was quick. He and Sirius made it to the gate before Lee had time to reach them and—bursting through it, had only a few more steps of precious pavement left between them and safety.

Then Remus felt a hand on the back of his jacket.

"I've got you!"

“Lupin!” Barty shouted; “DUCK!”

Thankfully, Sirius’ instincts hadn’t been dulled by a twenty-foot drop. He pushed Remus forward, nearly driving him face-first into the floor of the van, and Barty let the beer can he was holding fly. His aim was true, and they watched as the can smacked Lee dead in the face and—miraculously not empty at all—exploded with all the glorious force of a stale lager.

The show was over for Remus before Lee could hit the ground a second time. As the other skinheads appeared on the flat's porch, Sirius shoved the rest of Remus into the van and hauled the door shut behind them. He gave Trish a nod and she turned to Regulus, who'd already leapt into the front seat;

“Drive!”

With a nasty screech off the transmission, Regulus shoved the gear stick all the way into fifth gear and the van shot forward into the street. He did nearly drive them into a line of parked cars, but eventually they'd levelled out, with Regulus’ elbows locked straighter than an arrow as he struggled to keep the steering wheel from wobbling in his hands.

Lying next to Sirius on the floor of the van, it was all Remus could do to breathe. So far none of them had said anything, and instead the radio prattled on, serenading them with a Village People's song. A second later, and Trish peeked over the edge of her seat.

"You okay there, Loonarny...?"

Remus shrugged, the tiny movement alone drawing a deep groan from deep down inside of him. Hiding her mouth behind one hand, Trish slowly began to titter;

“W-Wow…hah-ha... Heh–he–ha! Boy, Loonarny—when you said to watch out for the locals, ye really meant it.”

Unable to help himself, Remus began to laugh as well. It hurt, but he finished with a groan anyway after Sirius had turned over and smacked him in the centre of his chest.

“You bloody idiot—do you ALWAYS have to throw yourself into every near-death experience?!”

“Ngh… Huh-ha! Shit, Padfoot... How else do you get any character development around here?”

“Character—?!” Sirius finished with another slap, but the sounds of Remus’ pain were drowned out by Barty as he leapt up on his seat.

“Did you see that? Did you see when I threw that can of beer at his face?! HA—it fucking exploded!”

“ ‘Twas a good shot,” Trish agreed. “He’s gonnae be nursing that lump for a while. Here’s hoping he forgets ye exist, huh, Loonarny?”

Unsure whether he wanted to laugh or cry, Remus waved her off, lips pressed tightly together as he cradled an arm across his stomach. When he opened his eyes again, Sirius was still peering down over him.

“I’m guessing you didn’t find who you were looking for,” he said quietly.

The fact alone hurt more than his injuries. Sirius must’ve read the answer in his eyes; he reached out and carded his fingers through Remus’ fringe, his mouth forming a sympathetic smile.

“Don’t worry, I’m sure he’s alright.”

I hope so, Remus thought.

Up ahead in the driver’s seat, Regulus was still white knuckling the steering wheel. “Great!" He shouted. "Now that we’ve established that everyone’s all well and alive, I feel this is a great time to remind you that—I don’t know how to drive!”

Friggin’ in the riggin’
