Chapter 107: Son


Chapter Summary

Well folks, we're ending like we began.

With a series of goodbyes.



Chapter Notes

C/W for this chapter: Discussions of past childhood trauma. It's a hard convo, but it's for the better.



See the end of the chapter for more notes



Down at the Astoria the scene was changing,

Bingo and rock were pushing out x-rating;

We were the first band to vomit in the bar,

And find the distance to the stage too far;

Meanwhile it’s getting late at ten o’clock,

Rock is dead they say—

Long live rock!

- “Long Live Rock” The Who, 1974



Friday June 22nd 1979





“Moony! Oi, Moony…? Hell, you even up there?”

Remus grunted back;

“Be down in a sec.”

There was no need. Sirius came swinging around the bedroom doorway a second later, looking rather outrageous in a velvet-collared frock coat. Seeing him, Remus chuffed lightly.

"You know, most people wait until they've gotten a couple albums out before they start dressing like a gender-queer pirate."

"Is that so? Well, then I feel the need to inform you that most people also wait until their late sixties to start wearing those jumpers with the patches 'round the elbows."

Remus looked down at himself. "Lily said it looked smart. For the party."

"You can take advice from Evans on many things," Sirius sighed, "but fashion is not one of them."

Because he couldn't be bothered, Remus returned his gaze to what he'd been looking at, while Sirius flounced further into the room. “Are you coming then?” He asked, busy fiddling with the cuffs. “Effie’s gonna have our necks if we’re late to our own going away party.”

“Yeah, m'coming…”

Sirius turned his nose up, curious. “Go on then. What’s it you’re looking at?”

There was no need to feel shy. It was only Sirius.

Remus held out the photograph. It was the same one Sandra had given him at the start of last summer; the black and white picture of himself and Hope sitting together on the estate’s parlour floor. The memory had been standing idle on the top of their wardrobe for months now, and Remus had never paid it much attention. Like the old white trunk he'd hauled to school every year, it was enough to just have her nearby. Now that they were going away, his mind had begun to wander.

"I get nervous when you act sentimental," Sirius said. "Usually it means you've done something wrong."

"That is a gross exaggeration."

The corners of Sirius' mouth quirked up and he came to sit next to Remus on their bed. Without asking, he draped both legs over Remus’ lap, sitting upright so that he could meticulously pick a finger through the curls in Remus’ fringe.

“It’s a good photo,” he hummed, peering down at it kindly. “Your mum was proper lush, yeah?”

“Shut up.”

"What?"

"That's my mum."

"Yeah? Well, I’d have still chatted her up. Bet Potter would too… If she were ginger, that is.”

Remus turned to him, nose scrunched. “That’s enough out of you.”

"Shut me up for real then."

Remus didn't need to. Before he could say anything else, Sirius was leaning in to kiss him. It lasted a good while, with Sirius' hands clasped tightly around the sides of his neck, fingers tangled in that silver chain. It was ironic; in every other sense Sirius was electric. He could light up a room with less than a smile—shock you like the unexpected flash of lightning—and yet most of the time, it felt like he was the only thing keeping Remus grounded on earth. He was that rod that kept the rest of him from just... burning up. If it weren't for Sirius, Remus Lupin would've gone up in smoke ages ago. There'd be nothing left save for maybe a few scorch marks on a chair.

"Oh, Moony," Sirius whispered as he stroked his face and hair, "Moony, Moony, my mooning Moony... What's got you feeling so melancholy then, hey? Is it the tour... Mhm... We leave in a few days. Thought you’d be excited.”

Leaning away, Remus paused to pick a hair from his mouth—Sirius'.

“It’s not that," he mumbled, flicking it away. "Was just thinking."

"Aw. Don't leave us in suspense."

He shook his head. "It's stupid. I was only wondering if… Well, if she’d ever left the country before. Or, hell—been on a plane.”

“You mean you don’t know?”

The question came out deadpan, and Sirius winced in apology;

"Sorry, dumb question.” He cleared his throat. “Couldn’t you just—I dunno, ask Giles or something?”

Remus set the photograph back on their set of drawers. He was embarrassed and so he began picking at a hangnail. “Nah, not really. He’s sorta weird about it... Reckon he thinks talking about her will upset me. He’s probably just afraid I’ll turn out like her or something.”

“Lush?”

Remus gave him a stern look. “Crazy.”

“Oh. Well, I can deal with crazy,” Sirius said, matter-of-factly. “Just don’t start pulling out all your teeth or anything. A guy's got his limits.”

Scoffing, Remus shoved Sirius’ legs off so he could turn himself over, and just like that—had him pressed against the bed. Sirius laughed when his head hit the pillows, and Remus bore down on him with a hand on either side of his head.

“You're saying you wouldn’t love me without teeth, Padfoot?”

“Don’t get all offended, Moons. I wouldn’t love me without teeth.” Sirius smiled and traced his tongue across his front teeth for emphasis.

"And just what happens when we’re old then? When everything starts falling out on its own?”

“I’ll expect you to glue them back in.”

"Right. 'Course."

The bed creaked as Sirius raised both legs and wrapped them around Remus' middle. Remus took hold of a large chunk of Sirius' hair, pinning it to the pillow as if to say, what do you think you're doing? Clearly unbothered, Sirius squeezed with either thigh while simultaneously tracing a hand up the side of Remus' neck. He finally stopped with one thumb pressed against his bottom lip, and Remus felt a breath lodge itself in his throat.

Sirius licked his lips. “God, you’re lush too, aren’t you?”

“Enough. Say ‘lush’ one more time and I’ll—”

“Hush,” he cooed, already pressing the thumb past Remus' lips, laying it against the flat of his tongue. “Keep it a surprise. You know I just love surprises.”

Remus bit down on Sirius’ knuckle, before pulling back and kissing along the inside of his wrist.

“You… You drive me mad, Sirius Black.”

Sirius' lips parted. "Well, in that case..." There was a sudden series of grunts—mostly from Remus—as Sirius pushed up by the shoulders and flipped them over so that he was on top. “—Let's drive to Fiji! Screw the tour, we'll just tell he others to fuck off."

There was no time to formulate a plan of escape. The two had only just begun kissing again when a knock echoed from the corner of the room. The bedroom door was still ajar but rather than walking straight in unannounced, a hand waved itself through the open doorway like a white flag of surrender.

James Potter, it seemed, was finally learning.

“Not that I don’t totally love that cheeky feeling of deja vu, but it’s almost seven o’clock, so could you two please get those randy arses of yours in the car? We're going to be late...”

An hour later, they pulled up to Potter Cottage to find a small line of parked cars waiting out front. Every light in the house was on, and Mr. Potter's front garden was in full bloom. They were met at the door by Mrs. Potter, who smiled as she kissed James and Sirius on either cheek.

“Arey, Remus, beta, you get taller every time I see you," she said, after settling on a warm hug. "Oh, Lily—come here, darling… And Peterbird, you’ve brought Moira! Welcome, welcome. Jai shri Krishna. Come inside, all of you. Everyone’s waiting… And we have such wonderful news to celebrate!”

Fashionably late for their own party, the Marauders walked inside to find a sea of family and friends waiting for them. Marlene and Dorcas were there, along with Lottie and Roger, fresh off their Spanish honeymoon. Simeon was even chatting up Mary in the salon; only Mr. Pettigrew had stayed away, leaving his wife to make excuses for how he was needed in the office that evening. No one bought it, but Peter had put on a brave face anyway, somehow determined to make the most of his good news despite his father’s disapproval.

Effie had pulled out all the stops in her cooking, having converted the dining room into a massive buffet-style spread of all the quintessentially British foods they'd be missing while abroad. "I hope you boys brought your appetites," she said, while loading Remus' plate up with several layers of wellington and chicken biryani. "Mind the raita now, and make sure you leave space for pudding! Jenny's made Banoffee pie."

It was grand. Not to be outdone, Lottie had even found the time to have shirts made, which the girls and Mr. Potter sported around the house gladly. On their front was a large red ‘M’ surrounded in the same tiny footprints Peter had hidden in their band poster, and on the back—Marauders’ first American (back up) Tour ‘79.

“Kinda bummed I didn’t get one,” Simeon said, observing the girls from his spot along the parlour wall. Remus was with him, having stuffed himself to the bursting point with supper. Now he was just trying not to feel nauseous every time he glanced at the heaping trays of canapés still scattered about the room.

“Lottie did say that she had a few more in the boot of Roger’s car," he said, after burping quietly into his fist.

“Did she? I’ll have to snag Rog’s keys.” Simeon smirked into his glass of champagne. "All packed then, Lupin?"

"Mostly. I don't have a lot of clothes. Probably for the best... Sirius keeps sneaking things into my bag."

"Ah. And I suppose this means you officially don't have any plans for university then?"

"Not in this lifetime."

"You sound smug."

Remus shrugged, swallowing the nausea and feeling smug indeed. "This your attempt to talk us out of it then?"

"Me? Never." Simeon finished his champagne, 'ah-ing' the way people often did when they were working themselves up for some big reveal. "Don’t tell Peter, but you four have got me feeling particularly inspired these recent months."

"What's that supposed to mean?"

"It means..." And Simeon tilted his face toward Remus'. "That I'm dropping out."

'Surprised' wasn't quite the word to describe it.

“You’re dropping out of Oxford?” Remus echoed, careful not to let anyone overhear; “Christ—why?”

“Didn't I just say? 'Cause of you." Smirking, Simeon set his glass down on an empty canapé plate. "I haven't told anyone apart from you, to be honest. Might just not... I'm sure my parents would prefer thinking I was living neat out in Oxfordshire anyway, going to school like a good little boy."

"And where is it you'll really be?"

"Just New York."

"Wow."

He shrugged like it was nothing. "A friend of mine's a photographer. Anyway, he knows a guy who works for some fancy scouting agency over in America. He sent him my photos, and now his boss wants me to meet them in New York.”

"To what, like—be a model or something?"

"Think I couldn't?"

Remus looked him up and down, skeptical, then; "Er... Never mind."

“Ah, Lupin, you always were a charmer. Here, hold on.” Slipping away for just a moment, Simeon returned with two beers; one he handed to Remus before knocking their rims together. "You can blame Sirius," he said, going in for a swig. "He gave me the idea actually—something he mentioned at the wedding. Figured he was taking the piss, but since he usually has such great ideas, I just thought that—well.”

“You think your parents are gonna like it?”

“Oh, not a chance! But they’ve got Lottie, she’ll make ‘em proud. And hey, Petey will too, in his own way… I’m glad he’s blazing a trail with you though. Makes me feel a bit braver.” Simeon leaned back into the wall, his blonde hair offsetting the dark wallpaper. "I dunno, Lupin... It’s like, I used to think that it was enough to just be clever, right? By an average bloke’s standards, a clever mouth might as well make you extraordinary. But here I am, all clever mouth and still just... ordinary."

"We never thought you were ordinary," Remus said. "Not for a second."

"Aw. That's sweet."

"Dick." Remus kicked him lightly on the shin, and Simeon's eyes began to wander.

"Hey, Sim?"

"Mm?"

"You should know that Peter—" Remus hesitated, before sighing. "Look, I know he's never really said it or anything, and the two of you have this—I dunno, weird brotherly-rivalry thing going on that I'll never understand, but he looks up to you, Sim—really."

"You think?"

Remus shrugged. "Well... Yeah. Reckon all he's ever wanted was to be you actually."

Simeon chuckled. "And look at us now, Lupin."

Together, the pair of them glanced across the room in the direction of where Peter and Moira were sitting tight on one of the lounges. It felt wistful, maybe, but at least Simeon smiled, and afterwards knocked the tip of his shoe into Remus' ankle.

“Thank you by the way, Lupin. For always keeping my secrets.”

Remus clinked their beers together.

“Anytime, Sim.”

Not long after Simeon’s confession, Remus found themselves busy relaying the tour schedule to Mrs. Pettigrew, who insisted on repeating everything he said with an air of surprise—“Twelve weeks? Twenty-five cities? Over forty shows?! Oh my…”—when they all overheard the doorbell ring. Like a good host, Mr. Potter went to get up from his sofa chair to fetch it, only to be rebuffed by James.

"Nah, don't worry, Dad. I got it."

"Who could that be?" Peter asked, just before James returned with a giddy smile on his face.

“Moony! Oi, Moony, you’ll never guess…”

But Remus didn’t have to guess. He’d invited them after all.

“Take this, would ya?” Tomny said, tossing the nappy bag at him as he tugged his boots off. He’d gotten good at balancing the baby carrier in one hand while he did so, a talent that less than year ago would’ve had Remus falling over in shock.

“Hello, luv’,” Skylar said, pecking Remus on the cheek as she shrugged off her coat. Remus barely had time to return the hello; before he knew it, the Potters had emerged from the parlour with James and Lily close on their heels.

“You must be Tomny,” Mrs. Potter said, “and Skylar! Welcome, welcome—you are most welcome. I hope you found the house alright.”

“Hard to miss, innit?” Tomny said cheekily, but his smile said everything. He carefully handed Remus the baby carrier and shook James and Mr. Potter’s hands before allowing Mrs. Potter to pull him into a hug as though they were old friends. Over her shoulder, he winked at Remus, then pointed toward the carrier.

“Best watch out, Lu. Little bugger’s only jus’ stopped crying.”

Remus looked down. Emma was sucking on a dummy, staring around the new place with big brown eyes. They’d been blue like Tomny’s when she was born, but now at nearly eight weeks, her eyes were as dark as shoe leather. It was not the first time the two of them were being introduced; Remus had been there for the christening, just like Tomny and Skylar had wanted. He signed his name on the baptism certificate, and afterwards Tomny gave him Emma to hold. She was so small, Remus had been afraid of hurting her, and most of the photos had him looking like he was one small jostle away from throwing up all over the church floor.

"Remus," Lily chided, "won't you invite your friends inside?"

"They want to see the baby," James clarified, looking to Tomny.

"Have at 'er, mate. I'd keep edgy if I were you, though. One 'a her farts sure can clear a room."

After guiding Tomny and Skylar into the parlour, the Potters celebrated their new arrivals with another grand round of introductions. The girls were instantly enamoured with Emma and sat cooing around her carrycot while Mr. Potter broke out several fresh bottles of wine. He offered the first glass to Skylar, who appeared happy enough to indulge in a glass after nine months of forced sobriety. Tomny, however, abstained, citing a need to drive at the end of the night. Secretly, Remus was proud of him.

"Should probably step outside for one of these though," Tomny said, raising his cigarettes. Mr. Potter stopped him.

"Good idea, son. Smoke's no good for the baby, but I only wondered if I could tempt you..."

Mr. Potter offered a box of his Cuban-leaf cigars, to which Tomny answered with an impressed arch of his brow.

"Shit. Don't mind if I do."

“Oh, aren’t you just the cutest thing?” Mary moaned, as she leaned down over Emma's carrycot. Marlene and Dorcas stood behind her, each of them sporting a beer and a red ‘Marauders’ t-shirt of their own.

“Thought you hated babies, Macdonald?” Dorcas asked sceptically.

“Only when I have to take care of them.” She glanced up at Skylar. “May I?”

Skylar waved her on. “Let me know if she needs a nappy change.”

“Aw no,” Mary went on cooing, as she scooped the baby up. “You’re just darling, aren’t you?”

Just then Lottie appeared in the parlour doorway, having stepped out to powder her nose. "No one told me there was a baby!" She shrieked, rushing forward to tug pointedly on Mary's sleeve. “Go on, Mary, hand the pwecious wittle thing over.”

“Wait your turn, Lot. I only just got her, and just because you went and got yourself hitched doesn’t mean you get to call bags on every toddler from here to Andalusia.”

Lottie pouted, but eventually got her turn and one-by-one the girls passed the baby around for a cuddle each. Emma was patient with them for the most part, sucking happily on her dummy and only grabbing hold of a fistful of Mary’s hair when one of her curls fell into her face.

"Yeah, she's a bit grabby," Skylar said, helping untangle Emma's fingers as Mary moaned; ow, ow, ow! "Doctor's saying she's advanced for her age. Most kids don't even start grabbing things 'til twelve weeks."

Already on her second turn with the baby, Lottie wasted no time in beckoning her husband over.

"Rog! Rog, come here! Come see how adorable she is."

Roger, who'd been previously engrossed in a work-related conversation with Mr. Potter, sighed as he meandered over.

"Yes, very cute."

"Here, try holding her."

Roger didn't appear all that eager, and had to be reminded to mind the baby's head on two separate occasions. To her credit, Emma did not immediately begin to cry, however it only took a few seconds for her to decide that she was done being held, and subsequently spit up all over the front of Roger's fine grey suit.

"Oh, shit—sorry!" Skylar rushed forward, while Roger began to gag into the palm of his hand. The room erupted into giggles despite of this, and Mrs. Potter was kind enough to come forward with a towel to help clean the big-shot up.

"Now, now. No use in getting all fussy, Roger Penrose," she chided. "You're going to have to get used to this, you know."

"Lottie," Mrs. Pettigrew interrupted, "take Roger next door to ours, he can borrow one of your father's suits for the meantime."

As Lottie herded her disgruntled husband out, Remus overheard Peter mutter something to Moira about how if Lottie was smart she'd put off having kids until she was thirty. Moira didn't reply, and eventually Mr. Potter stood up to break the tension;

"Anyone feel like some music?"

He put on a folk album, to which Skylar happily announced that she knew. Humming along, she kept her daughter balanced in one arm while she sipped from her beer, content enough until Lily offered to take Emma off her hands so she could finish her drink.

"N-No, it's alright," Skylar replied, looking suddenly worried.

"You're sure? I really don't mind."

Skylar glanced between her daughter and the beer, before nodding pensively.

"Well, just for a little bit then..."

A 'little bit' turned into a good half-hour, with Lily rocking Emma right to sleep on one of the Potters' fancy ottomans. James had sat down behind her and was whispering things into Lily's ear to make her laugh. Remus could hear it now;

Whaddya think, 'Prongs Jr' for the middle name?

As if, Potter.

“There you are," Tomny called, sauntering up to Remus in the corner of the room. He had a Coke in one hand, courtesy of Mrs. Potter, which he sipped from generously. It was probably a very difficult thing—being sober in a room full of people who had never had to think about where their next drink was coming from, much less all the things they'd do to get it.

"How was your cigar?" Remus asked.

Tomny mimed sucking one back. "Rich. I forgot you aren't supposed to suck 'em into yer lungs. Spent all of ten minutes coughing into the pavement."

"Idiot."

"Met one of those friends 'a yers though. Simeon? He's... posh."

Remus grinned. "Yeah, well, you missed all the fun in here. Your daughter threw up all over Roger. I'll wager he's bent over the pavement right about now too."

"Ah." Tomny sipped from his Coke, looking pleased. "I guess you finally found someone who’s more popular with the ladies than you."

"You mean Emma? Yeah, you should talk, wanker. But I still remember Cheryl, and Donna." He began counting them off on his fingers; "And Tracey, and Libby, and Veronica—”

“Alright, alright—not so loud. I’m a committed man now, I’ll have ya know. Though… suppose you are too, seeing as how Lover-boy hasn’t stopped glaring at me since we got ‘ere.”

Remus glanced across the room, to where Sirius was sitting with Peter and Moira, presumably trying to play nice. It would’ve been more effective had he been actually listening to whatever Moira was going on about and not turned halfway around in his seat to stare pointedly in Tomny’s general direction.

“What can I say, he’s cute when he’s jealous,” Remus replied smugly. He watched as Tomny gave a cheeky wave, and Sirius responded by not-so-subtly scratching his nose with his middle finger.

Remus nudged his friend. “Thanks for coming, Tom.”

“Any time. That Simeon bloke sure had a lot to say about you. Is there anyone here you haven't kissed?"

"You—? Simeon and I never kissed!"

"But you wanted to, didn't you?"

"Ha. Prick!"

Tomny laughed, nudging Remus with his shoulder. "Right, my bad. But I am glad we came. Honestly it was just a relief to get out of the house for a while. Don’t tell her I said so, but I think Sky was going a bit stir-crazy. Emma cries a lot.”

“Aren’t babies supposed to cry?”

“Sure, but Emma cries all the time. We thought she had colic, but the doctor just thinks she's fussy. Mostly it's whenever—"

On cue, Emma gave a wail loud enough to drown out Mr. Potter's second folk album. She was being held by Dorcas, who was quick to pass her back to Skylar, but even as her mother cooed little assurances to her, Emma kept on balling.

“Maybe her godfather should have a go,” Lily suggested, already standing at the ready with her camera. Remus highly suspected she’d conspired with Emma to plan it.

“Aw-right! Can’t wait to get a load 'a this,” Tomny said, as Skylar stepped up and practically dumped her daughter into Remus’ arms. Emma blinked twice, another wail hovering on the tip of her tongue, and then—

Nothing.

“Fuckin' hell,” Peter said, before covering his mouth for the curse; “Sorry. Only meant—she stopped crying.”

“Always does wiff ‘im,” Tomny said, jutting a thumb in Remus’ direction. “I call it blatant favourtism.”

“Who would’a thought it,” Marlene sniggered; “Remus Lupin, the baby whisperer.”

“What? No, I only—” Remus glanced down at Emma, who’d started playing with the chain necklace around his throat, her eyes still damp with tears. For someone who barely had control over her own tongue, she was mighty quick to ham-fist the plastic guitar pick hanging on its very end and shove it into her gummy mouth.

“Oi, don’t swallow it.”

Nearby, Lily raised her camera. “Look here, Emma, darling. Smiiiile, Remus.”

KA-CHSSH!





‘She ain’t got no money,

Her clothes are kinda funny,

Her hair is kinda wild and free!

Oh, but love grows where my Rosemary goes—

And nobody knows like me!’





Once everyone had gobbled down their share of salty canapés and fizzy champagne, and Emma had wowed everyone by blowing a snot-rocket onto Remus’ shoulder, Mr. Potter turned down the music and invited the room to share in a toast.

“I have to be honest, boys,” he started, “when James came to us and said that he was going to give this band stuff a try instead of going off to university—well, a part of me thought it was a mistake. I was worried for your futures, all of you. But you made a promise and kept to your word, and for that alone, we could never be more proud. So to James, Peter, Sirius, and Remus—I only have one thing to say, and that’s cheers to you.”

Everyone raised their glass;

“ ‘CHEERS!’”

“I have some good news of my own too!” James added keenly. “Lily is—”

“OHMYGOD—She's pregnant!” Mary burst out. Turning beet-red, Lily smacked her with one of the sofa pillows as she fumed;

“No, Mary! God, you are so full of it!”

“Geez, alright. One of these days I’m gonna be right though...”

Only looking slightly frazzled, James tossed a sincere look at his mother before clearing his throat;

“What I meant to say… is that Lily’ll be joining us on tour! Once she finishes her term in June, of course.”

The girls gasped in delight, and Roger—donned in a fresh suit—leaned over to smack Peter keenly on the shoulder. “Brilliant! And Moira too, I’ll expect?”

The chatter died a bit.

“Actually I’ll be spending the summer in the Isle of Skye,” Moira answered stiffly. “My grandparents have a house there."

No one said anything, and Moira rushed to clarify;

"But they’ve said that Petey’ll be able to call me from the road. Isn't that right, Petey?”

Peter sipped his beer, nodding firmly. Meanwhile Roger turned to Sirius and gave him a fond shove on the shoulder.

“Suppose you two lads’ll be having the time of your life then,” he said, gesturing to Remus. “You know, plenty of American girls to go around and all that.”

Barely a second had passed before the entire room had burst into laughter.

“Oh yeah, birds aplenty!”

“Getting it in every night!”

“Proper menaces, they’ll be!”

Simeon dropped a hand on his brother-in-law’s shoulder while Lottie pinched her forehead, leaving Roger to look around himself in bewilderment.

“What? Lottie, what’d I say?”

Everyone was still caught mid-guffaw by the time Sirius stood up. “Moony and I appreciate the vote of confidence, Rog,” he said humbly, while reaching into the inside pocket of his oversized leather jacket. “Luckily for us, you’re not the only one who expects big things.”

Withdrawing his hand, Sirius held up a small paper album sleeve, which happened to hold a single red-pressed vinyl EP. It was titled Marauders, and it was their very first.

“Got this from Spectre,” he told everyone. “It’s one of the ones he’s gonna distribute to the radio stations during our tour. But I got him to make an extra, just in case we fail terribly."

"Which you're not gonna!" Said Marlene.

"Of course not! But we all thought to ourselves, who better to have it than the fools who believed in us. So, Mum—Dad… this is for you.”

With a flourish, Sirius dropped down onto one knee and presented the vinyl disc to Effie, who accepted with happy tears in her eyes. Remus watched on proudly, smiling until Emma tried to shove a fist into his mouth.

Eventually the parlour got to be too stifling, even with the windows open, and Mr. Potter opened up the patio doors so that the party could migrate out into the back garden and appreciate the early-evening air. The music carried through the open windows, and Mary had managed to convince Marlene and Dorcas to dance despite not being nearly drunk enough. It was mostly disco, that was until Sirius boldly put on their own EP. Even more shocking—they knew the words.



" 'Hey, have you seen my friends around?

Oh, I swear they’re pretty hard to miss!

One’s yay-high with flowers in her hair—

And the other you’d likely kiss'!"



"Are you ever going to tell Mary you wrote this song for her?" Peter asked.

"Not me," Remus replied. "This one was all Sirius."

Moira took Peter's arm. "Come on, Petey, let's dance."

There was no arguing with her, and so Peter went, and on and on they danced. Even Tomny was up there, Skylar's arms wrapped around his neck as they swayed. It was a bit of a mind-fuck to see them dance along to “Midnight Dancer”, but Remus told himself that it was enough for just to see them enjoy it. This one was his, after all. And he wanted them to be happy.

“You’re so lucky, you know,” he whispered to Emma, as he rocked her on one of the Potters’ wicker garden benches. She blinked at him for a while, and finally answered by knocking the dummy from her mouth with her tongue. Remus was just fitting the rubber nipple back into her mouth when Sirius dropped down beside him.

“Still stuck on baby-duty, huh?"

"Yup."

"And here I was about to ask you to dance. Should we offer Lottie another turn?”

“Can’t. She cries whenever I put her down.”

Sirius narrowed his eyes. “That sounds like a lie.”

“Oh? Shall we test it then?” Remus held the baby out to him, and Sirius instantly veered away. Emma’s chubby legs had only been hovering in the air for a moment before she started to gurgle and whine.

“Take it back—take it back!”

“Told you.” Remus settled the baby back into his lap, adjusting her rubber dummy while Sirius looked on contemptuously.

“Eugh—must mean she just likes you.” He pointed a finger softly at Emma’s nose. “Don’t think I’m not watching you, girl. I know your game. Just ‘cause you think you’re so cute…”

“You’re jealous of a baby now, Pads?”

“For your information, it’s called being smart.” Sirius tapped his head; “Women always have good intuition—even as babies.”

In answer, Emma made a little hiccuping noise that might've been a laugh were she not so fresh out the womb. Then she reached out and grasped Sirius' finger with her tiny hand, and Remus knew it was purposeful.

“Ugh—don’t do that,” Sirius scoffed. “Don’t act cute. You and me—we ain’t friends. You’re only here to take my man away, I know it.”

Emma pushed the dummy out of her mouth, coming as close to a smile as a seven-week-old human could. Sirius kept squinting at her, but did not pull his finger away.

“Have you spoken to Regulus at all?” Remus asked, watching as James spun Lily around the patio like a music box ballerina.

“A bit. He's agreed to watch the flat while we’re gone.”

"Cool. Guess that means he doesn't have any plans to go back to your parents' place then?"

At that, Sirius matched Emma's smile.

"He said he wanted to work. How did he put it... To 'do something for himself for a change'. I think he's just rebelling, myself.”

"About time."

They shared a laugh, and Remus knocked him fondly with his knee.

“That’s good, Sirius. Really.”

Sirius nodded, gently rocking his finger as Emma clung to it. “You all ready for America then? … Flight’s in a few days. I dunno—maybe it’s just me looking into things, but you seem sorta… off.”

“And if I say it is just you?”

“Fine, I know it’s not me. You’ve been… quiet, Moons. Like this morning when you—”

"Yeah, I know," Remus said, finishing Sirius' sentence for him. He took a moment to fit the dummy back into Emma’s mouth again—baby tongues, weird—before nodding. “I’ve just been doing a lot of thinking lately.”

“Ohhhh no.” Sirius leaned down toward Emma. “Watch this, kid—this is the part where he does something stupid.”

“Yeah, you would call it stupid…”

After making a few friendly fish-faces at the baby, Sirius sighed and straightened up again.

“Alright, what is it then? Is it redemption? Are we asking Lee to be our roadie or something? Personally I don’t think he’ll accept but if you’re looking for someone to get you in shape for the tour then I’m sure he wouldn’t mind going for a few rounds in the boxing ring.”

“It’s not Lee,” Remus replied grimly. “But it is a redemption of sorts."

"Wanna spell it out for me then? I don't actually know what it is you're thinking all the time, you know."

Remus swallowed thickly.

"I just think it’s time I go home, Sirius.”

“Home like… the flat home?”

“No.”

“Oh, good. ‘Cause I sorta promised Mary I’d let her show me that eyeliner trick before we leave on tour.”

“Sirius—”

“Fine—I asked her if she’d show me. But if you’re really tired then I’m sure Effie wouldn’t mind if we—”

“Not the flat.” Remus took a deep breath. “I mean, I think it’s time I go speak with my father.”

“... Oh.”

“I keep thinking that I should say something to him before I up and leave the country. And there's Giles... Guess, I’ve got a few people to visit.”

“Right.”

Remus looked down at Emma, ashamed. “You think it’s a bad idea.”

“No! S’just… ugh.” Sirius reached a hand up to the side of his neck, rubbing it like it was giving him grief. “I just didn’t think there was all that much to say to the guy. It’s not like his opinion matters.”

“Yeah, but he was still my dad for seventeen years.”

Sirius pressed his tongue to the inside of his cheek, looking forlorn and distraught. That, perhaps, was the one way they differed when it came to their own respective parental troubles. Sirius wanted to let go—to throw it all away and be done with it. For Remus, hating something had always felt better than hating nothing.

"If you think it's stupid then I'll—"

"No—no. You’re right, I get it,” Sirius said, dropping the arm from his neck. “To be honest, Moons, I’ve been thinking about it a lot too. Going home, I mean.”

“You mean you...?”

“Not literally.” Sirius gave a dry chuckle. “Shit, I ain’t ever doing that again… No, it was the safe actually. You know, the one in my father’s office. It opened when I put in my birthday—not Reg’s, mine—and I dunno. I just couldn’t stop thinking about it. Dad and I never got along, see? Even without Mum. So like, did he really mean to do that? To remind himself of me every time he… Or shit. Could he just not be bothered to change the fucking code?”

“I wish I had an answer for you.”

“Yeah, me too.” Sirius looked up at him, smiling haggardly. “It’s stupid anyway. I'm not ever gonna know now, so what point is there in killing myself over it?"

Remus nodded.

"But I suppose… that it’s not too late for you to get some answers.”

It took a moment for Remus to understand what Sirius had meant. Was that he wanted then—answers? He imagined it was hard to get answers without any real questions, but still—if this was supposed to be their new life, then he supposed making peace with his old one was the best way to go. And if not peace, then at least remission.

“So you’ll go with me then?”

“You mean to do this one last entirely stupid thing that might not make any difference in the long run anyway?” Sirius shrugged. “Hey, you know me—I’ll get the keys.”

Feeling comforted, Remus leaned down to kiss the top of Emma’s head. Across the patio, his friends were still swaying; Tomny and Skylar were holding each other close, mouths pressed to each other’s ears as they giggled and shared whispers.

Remus smiled into the wisps of Emma’s hair.

“Thank you, Sirius," he said. "For everything.”

Next to him, Sirius took his hand.

“You’re welcome, Moons.”

There are places I remember,

All my life though some have changed;

Some forever, not for better,

Some have gone and some remain;

All these places have their moments,

With lovers and friends I still can recall;

Some are dead and some are living,

In my life I’ve loved them all…





* * *





In the twenty-six minutes that it took them to get from Victoria to Blackheath Hill, Remus had almost asked Sirius to turn the car around three separate times. He was sitting in the passenger’s seat, ripping the skin around his nails to shreds while the radio played its Top Hits. Eventually Sirius reached over and clasped one of Remus’ hands in his to help ease the worst of it, but the thoughtful show of devotion did little to quell the apprehension brewing in Remus’ gut.

He couldn’t help but feel like he was making a mistake.

Perhaps it would’ve been better to just disappear into obscurity, as he’d been doing all year. Let whatever relationship he and his father had fizzle out to nothing. But he was going away. This tour could very well be the first of many nights spent away from London, and he knew that saying nothing would hurt Giles—especially after so many months of silence. Shit... Remus knew what he had to do. If he was going to accept Spectre’s offer of a lifetime, then it was probably time to face his demons head-on.

“Are you sure you don’t want me to come with you?” Sirius asked when they’d pulled to the top of the estate’s long driveway.

Remus didn’t answer at first. He couldn’t stop picturing the surprise on the gateman’s face. He’d done a double-take when they’d pulled up in their rusty purple Volkswagen—a few more months and he might not have recognised him at all. Would he still be Lyall Lupin’s son then?

“No,” he answered eventually. “I think this is something I have to do on my own.”

Sirius tapped his hands along the steering wheel. “Alright. But I’ll be right here when you’re finished.”

Turning around, Remus leaned and left a gentle kiss on the very corner of Sirius’ mouth.

“Be right back.”

He slammed the car door shut just as Sirius was lifting the sunglasses from his eyes.

“Oi! I love you—you hear me?”

Remus smiled, waving as he started up the estate’s steps. A high-pitched honk followed him, and for a second he felt hopeful. But that all fell away when he was faced with the towering front doors of the Lupin estate. There was a tremor in Remus’ hand when he knocked, but he was thankful for the familiar face that answered. It was Giles, a little more creased at the edges, but still wearing his favourite waistcoat and cap.

“Hi, Gil.”

The old driver looked torn. He probably didn’t know whether to embrace him or put him over his knee. In the end he opted for a scolding.

“You—You cheeky—! Do you even know how long it’s been?!”

“A while. Give or take a few days.”

Giles’ nostrils flared the way they always did when he was full of rage. Then he swallowed it. “You… You look different,” he grunted stiffly. “You’re taller. More—More… Well, you look like a man.”

Remus’ chin dipped, suddenly bashful. It made Giles chuff lightly, and he grasped Remus around both shoulders as if to admire him.

“Christ—you look like a rock star! You’ve grown… Oh. My little bugger.”

Remus smiled back at him, feeling a sting in the corners of his eyes.

“Speaking of grown, has your nose gotten bigger by any chance?”

Giles clapped him upside the head. “Watch your mouth,” he warned, before taking a deep breath. “Look at me pissing about—come in. We’ll get you settled in for a drink and you can tell us all it is that you’ve been doing this long while.”

Remus was grateful. He knew coming back would be difficult, but he’d underestimated just how happy he'd be to see his old friend again. The house still felt empty; the ceilings too high—the rooms too big. The vastness made him feel small, like he was nine years-old again and being sent to his room on Christmas morning.

After following Giles into the parlour, Remus sat down and allowed the driver to pour him a glass of whatever Spanish brandy he had on hand.

“Here. Since you’re such a big ‘man’ now.”

Remus thanked him. “I shouldn’t stay long though, I’ve got a friend waiting in the car.”

“The dark-haired one. I recognise him."

Remus nodded.

"His hair looks better long," Giles said as he handed him a glass of brandy. "Not all short like it was the first time you brought him here."

It took a second.

"The first time?"

"You remember. That summer you smuggled him into your bedroom."

Remus nearly dropped his brandy. "Giles, you knew?"

"Of course I knew. You may be sneaky, but I'm the one who raised you. I know all your tricks, bugger—there ain't a single thing you can hide from me."

It was humbling, surely, and Remus ran a hand through his hair as he raised his glass. "Fuck—cheers, I guess."

The brandy was foul. It tasted like the stuff Peter used to lift from his parents’ liquor cupboard during their Christmas holidays. They used to choke the stuff down in James’ bedroom, telling themselves that it was all worth it for the buzz.

“Glad to know you’re not fully grown yet,” Giles remarked after watching him grimace. He took a seat in his old armchair before starting; “So! Where is it you’ve been all this time?”

Remus traced the edge of his brandy glass.

“Oh, you know… around.”

“Likely story."

"We rented a flat. We... we work."

"Fine. And where is it you’re hoping to go next?”

“That’s what I’ve come to tell you actually.”

Giles began to stroke his stubbly chin, and Remus knew there was no point in beating around the bush anymore. Sitting forward in the chair, he readied himself for the grand reveal.

“I’m going to America, Gil.”

Instantly Giles’ entire body fell slack. If he had anything to say, he never got the chance. Before either of them knew it, a loud bark echoed through the parlour, and the door was nosed open by a single scruffy, speckled hound. If Remus had been standing, he would’ve barrelled him over, but as it was, all Dusty could do was fling his entire body up into his lap.

“Oh f—DUSTY! Jesus—down, boy! Down!”

“Looks like I ain’t the only one who’s been wondering where you’ve been,” Giles called. Dusty continued to bowl into Remus, pinning him to the sofa chair as he slobbered kisses up and down his face and neck. As jarring as it was, Remus was no less than delighted. It was Dusty, his oldest friend.

“I’m sorry, Dusty,” he said, making sure to hug the dog tight. “I’m sorry.”

“He’s been waiting for you,” Giles said, however fondly. “You should be glad you came. Had a bit of a scare a few months back, but the doc’s said he’s in the clear now. ‘Course he’s never slowed down… Wilder than a march hare, that one. Your influence, I expect.”

Capturing the coonhound’s long face in his hands, Remus held their heads together, staring into his dog’s deep brown eyes.

“You good, boy?” He whispered. “You alright? I’m so sorry I made you wait.”

Dusty threw his hands off, and celebrated with another frothy kiss. It took a while for Remus to get him off the chair, and afterwards the happy dog laid down by his feet, panting with his tongue out and accepting no less than many—many, head scratches. With his free hand, Remus wiped beneath his nose, sniffling.

“I’d like to take him with me, if I can. I know our place isn’t exactly ideal—it’s got a busy road and a shit garden, but there’s room. I already talked to the landlady. And... well, I’d feel bad leaving him here again.”

“Of course you should take him,” said the old driver sceptically, “but I’m not sure how well a dog like Dusty would do on a plane to America.”

“I can sort it,” he said earnestly. There was Regulus or Mary—and it was just for the summer! But… “Unless you think he’d be happier here with the other dogs…”

Giles shook his head. “Nah, he’s your dog. About time you took responsibility anyway—you know I was just looking out for him while you were gone. And home is where the heart is. It’s why I understand why you’re going off to America in the first place. I’m sorry, Remus, I didn’t realise you’d found him.”

It was like piecing together a puzzle without knowing what the picture was first. It took a while, in which Dusty barked several times and began gnawing on his shoe, but then Remus remembered what Giles had told him while standing on the pavement outside King’s Cross Station.

America—home—found him.

Giles thought he meant he was going to his father. His real father.

“It’s not that, Gil,” Remus said earnestly. “It’s my band—we got a deal. Or—we got this opportunity anyway. There’s a producer. We met with him and he’s agreed to put us up as an opening act for some other band. We’re going to tour America and play our music. We… We leave next week. I'm not just chasing false hopes.”

Giles slouched back into his chair. “Well, I’ll be…”

“I know it sounds crazy, but it’s real, I swear. We’ll be in San Antonio starting next week, and who knows—if we do good on this, maybe next it could be us touring the country on our own.”

“And just who’s driving?”

“Well, I… we’ll be on a tour bus, I reckon.”

Giles nodded thoughtfully. “And I expect you’ll be enjoying yourself on the road?”

“What d’you mean?”

“I’m old—I ain’t ancient! I know what those rock stars get up to in their spare time. All the drinkin’ and the drugs and the women. I’ll bet you’re just sooo excited to get up there and have those girls throw themselves at ‘chu.”

Apparently there were some secrets he could hide from Giles.

"Why does everybody keep saying that?”

“Remus John Lupin, if you dare get a girl pregnant out of wedlock—”

Remus threw both hands up; “Gil—trust me, you have quite literally nothing to worry about.”

“Taken a vow of chastity, have you?”

“Something like that.”

“Huh. I always knew that religious school was gonna be a good influence.”

Remus couldn’t help it; he broke down laughing until he’d fallen back into his chair and Dusty was nosing about to get into his lap again. Just then the parlour door opened for a second time and a man wearing a dark suit and a business-style tie poked his head in.

“Bloody dog,” he was grumbling, “Dusty—here! Heel!”

Remus sat up, holding his dog close by the collar. The man noticed him straight away, and jumped in surprise.

“Giles?”

The driver said nothing in reply, and quickly the butler stepped out.

“That’d be Carsten,” observed Giles gratingly.

“I remember him.”

“He’ll be going straight for your father to tell him you’re here now.”

“That’s alright. Dad and I have some unfinished business. I only came back because I couldn’t go away knowing how we’d left things. And to sort out my responsibilities, I guess...”

He'd started patting Dusty on the head. Across from him, Giles lifted his brandy glass, pointing it in Remus’ direction.

“Careful, you’re almost starting to sound like a man too.”

Remus tipped his chin down again, and went on patting Dusty’s ears.

Not five minutes later, Giles had walked him over to the west wing, where he knew he’d find his father’s office waiting at the very end of the hall.

“Behave,” Giles told him, “and if you can’t behave then—”

“Be good, I know. I remember.”

He left him with a warning smile, tottering off with Dusty in tow.

Remus hoped Sirius wasn’t boiling himself alive in the car. It was getting warmer these days—supposed to be even hotter in America. Peter had already spent days talking their ear off about that one time he’d visited New York with his family, (Remus still hadn’t told them about Simeon,) and James was excited to see the Grand Canyon. It’s almost two thousand miles long! He’d said. According to Sirius, a big hole in the ground wasn’t all that much to sneeze at. The real prize was Los Angeles, where one could surf and play and party from sunrise to sunset. Remus wasn’t sure what he was most excited for. The music probably. He wanted to see some phenomena.

At the end of the hall, the office opened and Sandra stepped out in a sleek white pantsuit. Remus wasn’t surprised; he’d been expecting her, and tried not to react when she dropped the door handle and rushed toward him.

“Remus! Oh, I’m so glad you came. Look at you, you’re so…” She sighed, squeezing his shoulders. “How have you been? You look healthy. How are your friends?”

“Send him in, Sandra.”

It was his father, for once saving him from having to reply. At the sound of her husband’s voice coming through the crack in the door, Sandra looked up and gave Remus a warm smile.

“We’ll talk after,” she cooed, petting his hand. “Go ahead. He’s waiting for you.”

Remus was half-sure he’d rather hear her say that he was clear to join a bomb disposal squad than know that Lyall fucking Lupin was ready to see him. Still, he picked up what was left of his courage and trudged on. He hoped all the pain was in the anticipation—like ripping off a plaster. But of course, Remus knew better than to count on a hope.

It was bright inside the office with all the curtains open, and there he found his father waiting for him behind his heavy desk. He’d been scribbling something in a leather day-timer and went on with his scribbling even as Remus thudded over the expensive carpet in his heavy boots.

“Remus.” Lyall turned the page in the day-timer. “I didn’t realise you were coming.”

Opposite to him, Remus fit his hands into his pockets stubbornly. “Yeah. Just wanted to drop in… See Giles, y’know.”

A moment passed, and Lyall slowly set the pen down, snapping the day-timer shut. “I’m glad you did,” he replied stiffly. “It’s been too long, son.”

And then Lyall Lupin did something Remus was not expecting; he came out from behind his imposing desk and set a hand on either of his son’s shoulders.

“You’ve grown.”

Like Giles, Remus didn’t get the feeling he meant ‘you got taller’. Unsure of what to say, he ground the tip of his boot into the floor until Lyall inevitably cleared his throat and drew away.

“Can I offer you a drink?”

“No, I’m not staying long.”

Lyall set out two glasses anyway, surprising Remus again when he loosened his tie and casually leaned back against the front of the desk. He’d left the whisky next to him like an offering, but Remus could still taste the brandy and he felt ill.

“So what is it you’re doing now? Are you working?”

“I was,” Remus replied, unwilling to admit to having been fired from his minimum wage job at the music shop. “I’m taking some time off now. Me and the guys—we’re going away for a while.”

“Is that so?” Lyall sipped his whisky. “And where is it you’re going?”

“To America.”

Whatever recollection he’d missed in Giles’ expression, he now saw reflected back at him in Lyall’s. He considered letting him believe it, but in the end his pride won out.

“It’s for my band. We got offered a contract—er, sorta. But now we’re gonna be touring the states. We… Well, shit—we did it.”

It should’ve felt gratifying. We did it—all of it—without you. Except his father wasn’t looking at him. Instead Lyall had wandered over to the window, one hand tucked into his trouser pocket while he absentmindedly swirled his whisky tumbler and stared out over the back garden. Remus kept expecting to hear a dog bark, but there was nothing. They were alone.

“I wish you luck then.”

Remus scoffed, torn between anger and disbelief.

“ ‘Wish me luck’—that’s all you have to say?”

“I’m being pragmatic. Would you rather me jump for joy?”

Maybe I would, thought Remus bitterly. Or maybe he just wanted him to be angry, to start going on about how he was throwing his life away. It’d certainly have made it easier to shout and scream like he was used to.

“I’m going to America,” Remus repeated, as though his father hadn’t heard him properly the first time. “We’re all but signed to one of the biggest agencies in the country—the Potters threw James a bloody party!”

“And is that what you’d like, Remus?” Lyall turned around. “A party? Here I was, under the impression you didn’t enjoy such frivolous things.”

"What would you know about the things I enjoy?"

Lyall didn't answer, and Remus felt his fists clench at his sides. He would not break.

“I’d be enough just to hear that you’re proud of me. I mean, honestly—couldn’t you have ever told me just once, ‘good job, son’, or ‘I’m proud of you, son.’ Was nothing I ever did worth that much?”

“Remus, You’re only eighteen—”

“Nineteen.”

His father faltered then, and Remus might as well have been a starving hound suddenly presented with a steak dinner.

“Remus, I am proud of y—”

“Oh, come on! You just stand there and lie to my face now? Say what you really mean."

Pinching the bridge of his nose in exasperation, Lyall crossed back to his desk, where he picked up his pen and began scratching more notes into the old leather day-timer. It felt like a dismissal, even as he mumbled under his breath;

“You know nothing, you don’t understand.”

“No,” Remus growled. “What I don’t understand is why we can’t ever talk about it. It’s always the same—I’m going to walk out that door with nothing. Only this time, I’m not coming back. You’re lucky you have Sandra now, because otherwise you’d be alone and that’s on you! So just tell me… Tell me the truth, Dad!”

Lyall sagged back into his desk chair, looking haggard as he squeezed his fist around the gold-plated pen. “You won’t be satisfied.”

“You think I came here to be satisfied? Man, I’m giving you one chance to set all this straight. If you don’t want it, then tell me to piss off and let’s be done with it.”

But despite all the anger and animosity they’d hurled at each other over the years, Lyall did not tell him to go. Instead he set the pen down and clasped his hands over his stomach.

“You have to understand. I cared about your mother—”

“Yeah, I’m sure you did.”

“Do you even want to hear this?”

Remus clenched his jaw to avoid a reply, and returned to grinding the toe of his boot into the rug. Lyall watched him for a moment, but must’ve decided it wasn’t worth the effort.

“Your mother was eleven years younger than me when we got married,” he started. “She left her parents in Saint Asaph and came to live with me here. I knew she had no one, but thought she got on well enough. We never really had that much in common, but she was… vibrant. I could hardly keep up. Some days it was like living with two different people. For a while I thought to myself, ‘this is just how she is—get used to it’. I had no idea what it actually meant. Her mind, she...”

“Bet you blamed her for it.”

“I never blamed her—not once. Not in the beginning.”

“Did you know then?” Asked Remus. “That she was in love with someone else?”

“I knew before we’d even met. At the time it hardly mattered. I needed a wife, and she needed a husband her parents approved of.”

Remus almost asked what about Tad could’ve been so appalling that his grandparents wouldn’t approve, but in the end, he held his tongue—too worried it might derail whatever truth Lyall was finally permitting him.

“I discovered your mother was having an affair a year before you were born,” he went on, turning back to the day-timer with that bloody pen. “She used to take trips out to see her best friend from school—I believe you know the one.”

“Sheila.”

Lyall hummed—scritch, scritch. “Eventually I began to get suspicious, so I hired a private investigator to follow her. You can imagine my surprise when she did not board a train to Glasgow. Instead she took a car to Notting Hill.”

“Why didn’t you do something about it?” Remus demanded. “Why didn’t you just divorce her?”

“It was too late. By the time I was considering the option, Hope was already pregnant.”

It was not the answer he’d wanted.

“That tells me nothing!”

“I would’ve assumed it made perfect sense.”

“But you knew! Even then—you knew I wasn’t yours!”

Lyall stood up from the desk; “Is that right?”

“Yes, of course you knew! You wouldn’t hate me so much if you didn’t.”

“I never asked Hope for a paternity test.”

“Why not?”

There was no reply. Lyall had returned to the liquor cabinet, where he uncapped the decanter and poured himself a second glass. After tipping that back, he poured a third.

“Remus, you’ve no idea what you’re talking about.”

“Oh, I think I do. You did it to save face, didn’t you?”

He stoppered the decanter sharply. Remus seethed.

“You couldn’t stand the idea that someone else had gone under your nose! That your own wife loved someone else in a way she could never love you. Admit it, you wanted to divorce her but you couldn’t stand the idea because the truth is, you’re too afraid to be alone—”

Lyall spun around.

“I didn’t divorce your mother because SHE ASKED ME NOT TO!”

His chest heaved, and Lyall sipped the whisky with shaking hands;

"She asked me not to..."

“How could you expect me to believe that?" Remus threw a hand up. "You fought all the time—I heard you!”

“Believe what you want, but I am telling you now, whatever you think you know about that man is wrong. This is not some fairytale—your mother was delusional! She threw her fits and made me into the bad guy because I’m the one who was here. And when he found out about you, it was over. Just like that—gone!”

“But he sent me Christmas presents.”

“And I suppose that would make him father of the year?”

Remus turned his face away, torn between shame and his own ego.

“You have no idea what it was like,” Lyall spat; “dealing with her.” He paused again to sip from the whisky, still breathing hard. “I told her I would agree to the divorce if it was what she wanted, but that she could not keep you from me.”

“So that’s it—you held me hostage.”

“I kept my family together! I kept Hope safe—me! Even during all the times she’d deluded herself into thinking that a relationship with that bastard would ever work. He couldn’t take care of her, and you were too young, and so I stayed. I stayed because she was my wife, and because you are my son!”

“Then why did you do it?” Remus wailed. “Why did you keep me from going to her funeral—why did you push me away at every possible moment? Was it because I looked like her? Or because I look like him?”

“You are my son,” Lyall repeated, “you will always be my son.”

“Ain’t that the fucking miserable truth.”

Neither of them said any more after that. More-so out of spite, Remus finally picked up the glass Lyall had set out for him and downed it for all that it was worth. He slammed the cup down;

“I have spent so much of my life being angry with you. Even when I’d thought I’d let it go, it was always there—burning me from the inside out. But not anymore… No, ‘cause I have everything now—everything! And after today, I’m going to walk out that door and I won't be angry anymore, do you hear me? Not because I’ve somehow found it in my heart to forgive you, or because your story made any difference, but because I forgive myself. So yeah, Dad… I love my life—and maybe I love it because of some of the things you gave me, but it’s mine. And I’m going to start living it for me, and I don’t care if you think that’s selfish.”

“It is all I’ve ever wanted for you, Remus.”

Liar.

Liar—liar—liar!

You don’t care—you don’t care!

Remus clutched at his head. Not now—christ, not now! It’d been ages since he’d felt himself slipping back into the old habits—the meltdowns. The thoughts and memories always came like lightning, but stuck around for hours like tape caught on a loop. He’d been doing good for so long. His friends’ influence, probably. And Sirius… always Sirius. That’s who he thought of now.

I love you.

Oi! I love you—you hear me?

Eventually Remus was wiping the sweat from his palms on his trousers. Lyall had been very quiet, studying him nervously out of the corner of his eye. Remus knew what he saw.

“Don’t,” he said, “I’m not broken.”

Lyall’s mouth opened, but with nothing to say that would change things, it eventually fell shut again. And so Remus figured he'd gotten what he wanted—answers to the questions he didn’t know he’d had.

“I leave for America next week,” he said to his father. “Just wanted to let you know.”

There was no objection as he turned to leave, but when Remus’ hand came to rest on the office door handle, Lyall Lupin spoke once more.

“Remus."

He stopped.

"You should know that I loved your mother."

He waited for it—the liar!

"Very much."

It did not come.

“Good.”

The door shut behind him with a soft click.





* * *





Sandra was waiting for him by the front door, along with Giles and a woman Remus assumed must’ve worked in the kitchens. They stood close together, acting fond, while Giles kept hold of Dusty’s leash and wrung his cap in both hands. Of them, it was Sandra who approached him first, looking cheerful despite her nerves.

“Giles filled me in,” she whispered kindly. “America—how wonderful. I’ll bet you’re excited.”

“It’ll be interesting, for sure.”

“You’ll make sure to be careful? It's a big place.”

“I'll be careful.”

“Well, at least you’ll have Dusty to take care of you now.” After glancing at the dog, she smiled and quickly kissed Remus on the cheek. “And Remus, you know that you will always have a home here if you want it.”

He nodded, but got the distinct feeling she already knew how this would go. With a tight squeeze, Sandra released his hands and Remus was free to make his way along to Giles.

“Suspect you’ll be needing some of this,” the driver said, gesturing to a large bag of dog feed at his feet. “And Gladys here, fixed you up some leftovers to take with you, as I’m assuming you’re still not much of a cook.”

Remus rolled his eyes, but thanked Gladys as she handed him the food in a paper bag. Afterwards Giles passed him Dusty’s leash, finishing by poking him in the nose.

“Take care of yourself, son. And don’t you be smoking so much.”

“How do you know I still smoke?” Remus queried. “I could’ve quit.”

“Yeah, and I’m the Queen of Sheba.”

They shared a matching grin.

When it was time to go, Dusty was the first out—yanking Remus down the stairs as he struggled not to lose hold of the heavy bag of dog kibble. There they found Sirius, casually leaning up against the side of the van with that morning’s crossword in hand.

“You made it out alive,” he cheered, tucking the paper under one arm and the pen behind his ear. He raised his sunglasses up onto the top of his head next, making Remus’ heart give a little jump. Sometimes it actually escaped him just how devastatingly handsome Sirius was.

“You ready to go, Moons?”

Remus nodded; “I’m ready.”

Sirius stared at him a moment, and then glanced up at the house and gave his arm a little touch—as if to say I’m here.

It was enough.

After Remus had loaded Dusty inside, Sirius smacked the body of the van and ran around to the driver’s seat. “You’re gonna love Reg, boy!” He said to the over-sized dog. “He’s house-sitting the whole summer, and he just looooves dogs.”

Dusty barked as Remus clicked his seatbelt into place. Up above, he could see Giles and Gladys standing arm in arm, waving them off as Sandra blew a kiss. Remus waved too, and didn’t feel the least bit bad about it.

“Music?” Sirius offered. “I’m thinking music.”

He flicked the radio on before throwing the van into reverse. There was a crunch as the tires ground across gravel and stone, and just as Sirius began to veer back down the driveway, Remus spotted a person standing in one of the windows that ran along the side of the house. Again, he didn’t feel bad, more like… at peace. Lighter.

Bye, Dad.

Sirius was speeding already—the gateman had just enough time to haul the gates back before they were flying through, the windows down and warm summer air whipping at their faces.

“I’m proud of you, you know!” Sirius hollered. “Now you can be whatever you want to be!”

“You mean that?”

“Sure!”

Remus paused.

“And what if I just want to be your Moony?”

Sirius bit his lip over a smile. He noticed the radio at the same time, and shouted ecstatically;

“Ooh, I love this one!"

"Not exactly hard rock, is it?"

"Who cares? Just turn it up, Moons!”

He did.





‘Little darlin’, the smile’s returning to their faces,

Little darlin’, it seems like years since it’s been here;

Here comes the sun, doo-doo-doo-doo,

Here comes the sun, and I say,

It’s alright…’





“Have you given any thought to it at all?” Sirius yammered on. “Like, what happens if this tour doesn’t work out, and we all gotta go back to being like one of those regular cogs in society’s system?”

“No. You’re far too mental to be a society cog.”

“And just what’s that supposed to mean?”

Remus shrugged. “You’ve said it yourself, Padfoot. Mental makes art.”

“Oh, shit! Heh—I’m a fucking genius. You could put that in a song, you know! Might have to kick it up a notch though. More like… mental makes love? Nah, needs an 'm'... More like... mental makes magic? Oh shit—yeah, that's it!”

“No way, that’s so cheesy.”

“Wha—? Nah. Dusty don’t think so, do ya boy?”

‘Woof!’

“Told ya.” Sirius leaned over, shoving him fondly. There was sun in his hair, turning it a shimmering shade of silver. “Hey, Moons?”

“Mm?”

“Nothing. Just—love you.”

Sirius winked at him, before dropping the sunglasses back down over his eyes. Already grinning into his palm, Remus mouthed the words back.

Love you.

“What was that? Didn’t quite hear you.”

Remus turned his smile to the window.

“Eyes on the road, Sirius.”

We’ve tackled so much in this story and seeing the characters grow as they have has been such a life-changing experience. Really.

For those of you curious about the fate of Part 2, I still fully plan on writing it. However, I have no idea when that will begin, so I’m kindly requesting that you to refrain from asking ‘when’. I have other projects I’m going to be working on before I start writing Part 2, so if you’re interested those, please feel free to subscribe to my ao3 page.

I also am going to ask that you don’t ask me about the ships of Part 2. Like Cadence, it’ll be told entirely through Remus’ POV and will be a central wolfstar fic. (Other questions/curiosities are totally welcome!)

Someone on Tumblr asked me to compile a list of the songs I have written for the fic so here it is. Some are unfinished and will probably stay that way. I’m still really proud of them.

I have one last epilogue chapter to post and that will be happening this Friday, Feb 24th. This chapter is the END of Cadence, but I couldn’t leave a few precious questions unanswered. I’m not going to say anything else about it, except for the fact that the chapter is not told through Remus’ POV.

So that’s it for now. Hope this was an ending you can cherish. Thank you for all of the comments, kudos, and messages you’ve sent over these past two years. I couldn’t even come close to replaying all the love you’ve given me, but please know that I’m thankful for every single one of you.

Until next time x

I debated for a long time whether to include this chapter as an epilogue or a b-side, but in the end decided that it was better off here. She was the heart of the story for a long time. And that'll never stop being true.



Chapter Notes

This chapter includes strong references to: attempted sexual assault [not shown], child abuse [including neglect], domestic abuse [not shown], age gaps, under age sex [not shown], drug use/addiction and [minimal] withdrawal, and the mention of bulimia [in a character off-screen].

Please do NOT read if any of this is at all triggering to you. This epilogue is not central to the understanding of Cadence's ending, it’s simply for those who fell in love with her the same way Remus did.
